strInstructions:
Boil the potatoes until tender, then slice.
Blanch the cabbage, bean sprouts, and green beans separately until just cooked but still crisp.
Boil the eggs, then peel and halve them.
Fry the tofu and tempeh until golden, then cut into cubes.
Make the peanut sauce: blend fried peanuts, garlic, chili, palm sugar, tamarind water, and salt, then thin with warm water to a thick, pourable sauce.
Arrange the vegetables, tofu, tempeh, egg, and sliced cucumber on a plate.
Pour the peanut sauce generously over the top.
Garnish with fried shallots and prawn crackers before serving.

Boil the whole chicken with water, lemongrass, bay leaves, and lime leaves until cooked, then remove and shred the meat; reserve the broth.
Blend shallots, garlic, ginger, turmeric, and candlenuts into a smooth paste.
Saute the spice paste in oil until fragrant.
Add the paste to the reserved broth and simmer for 20 minutes, seasoning with salt and pepper.
Cook the glass noodles and bean sprouts separately until just tender.
In a bowl, layer noodles, bean sprouts, shredded chicken, and boiled egg.
Ladle the hot broth over the top.
Garnish with fried shallots, celery leaves, and a squeeze of lime; serve with sambal on the side.

Blend garlic, shallots, coriander seeds, turmeric, and salt into a paste.
Rub the paste over the chicken pieces and marinate for at least 30 minutes.
Simmer the marinated chicken in a pot with a little water, bay leaves, and lime leaves until the chicken is cooked and the liquid has mostly reduced.
Heat oil in a pan or deep fryer.
Fry the chicken pieces until golden brown and crispy on the outside.
Drain on paper towels.
Serve hot with steamed rice, fresh cucumber and tomato slices, and sambal.

Cook steamed white rice as the base.
Prepare several side dishes separately: fry chicken pieces marinated in turmeric and garlic until golden, simmer beef in sweet soy sauce (semur), and saute long beans or spinach with garlic and chili.
Boil an egg and slice it, or fry it into a crispy telur balado.
Fry tempeh and tofu until crisp.
Make a simple sambal by blending chili, shallot, garlic, and a little shrimp paste, then frying briefly in oil.
Arrange the rice in the center of a plate.
Surround the rice with small portions of each side dish.
Top with a spoonful of sambal and a sprinkle of fried shallots before serving.

Wash the rice and place it in a pot with coconut milk, water, lemongrass, bay leaves, and salt.
Cook over low heat, stirring occasionally, until the liquid is absorbed and the rice is tender and fragrant, similar to cooking regular coconut rice.
Separately, simmer shredded chicken in a seasoned broth with garlic, shallot, coriander, and galangal until flavorful.
Prepare a side of labu siam (chayote) cooked in coconut milk with the same spice base.
Boil eggs and halve them.
Serve the rice warm, topped with shredded chicken, a piece of egg, the chayote side dish, and a drizzle of the chicken broth.
Garnish with fried shallots.

Simmer beef shank and tendon in water with ginger and bay leaves for a couple of hours until tender; reserve the broth.
Slice the cooked beef and tendon thinly.
Blend garlic and shallot into a paste and saute until fragrant, then stir into the broth along with salt and pepper to season.
Blanch fresh yellow egg noodles and bean sprouts until just tender.
Place noodles and bean sprouts in a bowl.
Add the sliced beef and tendon on top.
Ladle the hot broth over everything.
Garnish with chopped celery, fried shallots, and a squeeze of lime; serve with sambal on the side.

Blend shallots, garlic, candlenuts, coriander, and a little ginger into a smooth spice paste.
Saute the paste in oil along with bay leaves and galangal until fragrant.
Add goat or mutton pieces and stir until the meat is coated and slightly browned.
Pour in coconut milk and a little water, then simmer until the meat is tender.
Stir in sweet soy sauce, sliced tomato, and shredded cabbage.
Simmer for a few more minutes until the cabbage softens slightly but still has some bite.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve hot with steamed rice, garnished with fried shallots.

Simmer chicken or beef in water with lemongrass, bay leaves, and lime leaves until cooked; reserve the broth and shred or slice the meat.
Blend shallots, garlic, ginger, turmeric, and candlenuts into a smooth spice paste.
Saute the paste until fragrant, then add it to the broth and simmer for 15-20 minutes, seasoning with salt and pepper.
Cook glass noodles or rice vermicelli separately until tender.
Assemble a bowl with noodles, shredded meat, and bean sprouts.
Pour the hot broth over the top.
Garnish with fried shallots, celery leaves, and a wedge of lime, and serve with sambal and crackers on the side.

Combine ground beef with tapioca starch, garlic, salt, and pepper, mixing until a smooth, slightly sticky paste forms.
Shape the mixture into small round balls.
Bring a pot of water to a gentle simmer and drop the meatballs in, cooking until they float and are cooked through.
Prepare a separate light beef broth seasoned with garlic, fried shallots, and white pepper.
Cook thin rice noodles or vermicelli until tender.
Assemble a bowl with noodles, a few meatballs, and optionally sliced tofu or wontons.
Ladle the hot broth over the top.
Garnish with chopped celery, fried shallots, and crispy shallot oil; serve with sambal, sweet soy sauce, and crackers on the side.

Blend shallots, garlic, candlenuts, turmeric, ginger, and coriander into a smooth spice paste.
Saute the paste in oil with bay leaves, lemongrass, and lime leaves until fragrant.
Add the meat (beef, chicken, or goat) and stir until coated and lightly browned.
Pour in coconut milk and enough water to just cover the meat.
Simmer gently, stirring occasionally, until the meat is tender and the gravy has thickened slightly.
Season with salt to taste.
Serve hot with steamed rice or ketupat.

Fry cubes of firm tofu until golden and slightly crisp on the outside.
Boil potatoes until tender, then cube them.
Make the peanut sauce by blending fried peanuts, garlic, chili, sweet soy sauce, tamarind water, and a little salt with warm water until smooth and pourable.
Prepare fried lontong or rice cakes if using, and cut into cubes.
Arrange the fried tofu, potato, and rice cakes on a plate along with bean sprouts and sliced cucumber.
Pour the peanut sauce generously over the top.
Top with a few crispy crackers and fried shallots before serving.

Wash the woven palm-leaf ketupat pouches (or purchase pre-made ones) and rinse the rice used to fill them.
Fill each pouch about two-thirds full with uncooked rice, leaving room for expansion.
Boil the filled pouches in a large pot of water for several hours, topping up water as needed, until the rice inside is fully cooked and compacted.
Remove the ketupat and let them cool completely.
Cut open the pouch and slice the compressed rice cake into cubes or wedges.
Serve as a side alongside dishes like opor ayam, rendang, or satay with peanut sauce.

Blend shallots, garlic, candlenuts, coriander, and turmeric into a smooth spice paste.
Saute the paste until fragrant, then simmer the chicken pieces in it with coconut milk, sweet soy sauce, and a little water until the chicken is tender and the sauce has reduced and thickened.
Remove the chicken and let it cool slightly.
Grill the chicken over medium-high heat, basting frequently with the remaining thickened sauce, until charred and caramelized on the outside.
Serve hot with steamed rice, fresh cucumber and tomato, and sambal on the side.

Marinate chicken pieces briefly with a little salt and turmeric, then shallow-fry until golden but not fully cooked through; set aside.
Blend shallots, garlic, ginger, dried chilies, and tomatoes into a smooth paste.
Saute the paste in oil with a cinnamon stick and star anise until fragrant and the oil separates.
Stir in tomato sauce, a little sugar, and salt, then add a splash of water to loosen the sauce.
Return the fried chicken to the pan and simmer until the chicken is cooked through and coated in the thick red sauce.
Stir in a small amount of evaporated milk or coconut milk for richness, if desired.
Serve hot with steamed rice.

Clean the catfish and score the sides lightly.
Rub the fish with a paste of garlic, turmeric, coriander, and salt, then let it marinate for about 15 minutes.
Deep-fry the catfish in hot oil until golden brown and crispy on the outside.
Make a sambal by grinding red chilies, bird's eye chilies, garlic, shallot, tomato, and a little shrimp paste, then briefly frying it or serving it raw depending on preference.
Prepare a plate of raw vegetables (lalapan) such as cucumber, cabbage, and basil leaves.
Plate the fried catfish alongside steamed rice, the sambal, and the raw vegetables.

Cut chicken, beef, or lamb into bite-sized cubes.
Marinate the meat with a mixture of ground coriander, turmeric, garlic, sweet soy sauce, and a little oil for at least 30 minutes.
Thread the marinated meat onto bamboo skewers.
Grill the skewers over hot charcoal or a grill pan, turning frequently and basting with more marinade, until cooked through and slightly charred.
Make the peanut sauce by blending fried peanuts, garlic, chili, palm sugar, and tamarind water, then thinning it with warm water to a thick, pourable consistency.
Serve the grilled skewers with the peanut sauce, a side of ketupat or rice, and pickled cucumber and shallot (acar).

Blanch the water spinach (kangkung) briefly in boiling water until just wilted, then set aside.
Boil fresh yellow egg noodles until tender, then drain.
Saute garlic and shallot in oil until fragrant, then add a little soy sauce, oyster sauce, and a splash of chicken or fish stock to make a light gravy.
Add the blanched kangkung and cooked noodles to the pan and toss well to coat evenly.
Optionally add sliced fish balls, shrimp, or a fried egg for extra protein.
Season with a dash of white pepper.
Serve hot with a side of chili sauce or sambal.

Blend shallots, garlic, ginger, turmeric, and dried or fresh chilies into a smooth paste.
Saute the paste in oil with lemongrass and torch ginger flower (if available) until fragrant.
Add tamarind water and enough water to make a broth, then bring to a simmer.
Season with salt and a little sugar to balance the sourness.
Gently add fish steaks (such as mackerel or red snapper) to the simmering broth.
Cook until the fish is just done and the broth has thickened slightly, being careful not to overcook the fish.
Serve hot with steamed rice.

Cut firm tofu into cubes or triangles.
Heat oil and deep-fry the tofu pieces until golden brown and crisp on the outside.
Make a dipping sauce by mixing sweet soy sauce with sliced bird's eye chili, a little chopped shallot, and a squeeze of lime.
Alternatively, make a peanut sauce by blending fried peanuts, garlic, chili, and palm sugar with warm water until smooth.
Drain the fried tofu on paper towels.
Serve the tofu hot with the dipping sauce of choice on the side.

Blend shallots, garlic, candlenuts, and a little galangal into a smooth paste.
Saute the paste with bay leaves and lemongrass in oil until fragrant.
Add coconut milk and water, then bring to a gentle simmer.
Add chopped vegetables such as young jackfruit, eggplant, long beans, and chayote, along with cubes of tofu and tempeh.
Simmer until the vegetables are tender and the broth has thickened slightly.
Season with salt and a little sugar to taste.
Serve hot with steamed rice or ketupat.

Simmer beef and beef tendon in water with garlic, ginger, and bay leaves until tender; reserve the broth and slice the beef.
Saute a paste of shallot, garlic, and candlenuts until fragrant, then stir into the broth and season with salt and pepper.
Boil fresh yellow noodles until tender.
Slice fried spring rolls (lumpia) or risoles into pieces.
In a bowl, combine noodles, sliced beef, tendon, sliced tomato, and shredded cabbage.
Ladle the hot broth over the top.
Top with the sliced spring rolls, fried shallots, celery, and a squeeze of lime; serve with sambal.

Simmer beef and beef offal (such as tripe or lung) in water with bay leaves and lemongrass until tender; reserve the broth.
Blend shallots, garlic, candlenuts, coriander, turmeric, and ginger into a smooth spice paste.
Saute the paste until fragrant, then add it to the broth along with coconut milk.
Simmer gently until the broth turns rich and slightly thickened, seasoning with salt to taste.
Slice the cooked beef and offal into bite-sized pieces and return to the broth.
Serve hot over sliced lontong or with steamed rice, topped with fried shallots and a sprinkle of chili powder, with extra sweet soy sauce on the side.

Clean the whole fish and score the sides.
Rub the fish with a mixture of turmeric, garlic, ginger, and salt, then let it marinate for about 15-20 minutes.
Heat oil in a pan or deep fryer until hot.
Fry the fish until golden brown and crispy on both sides and cooked through.
Drain on paper towels.
Serve hot with steamed rice, sambal, and fresh raw vegetables such as cucumber and basil leaves.

strMeal: Nasi Pecel Sambal Tumpang Khas Solo
strInstructions:
Prepare the ingredients. Bring water to a boil, then boil the tempeh pieces together with the curly chilies, shallots, kencur, kaffir lime leaves, bay leaves, and galangal. Boil until cooked.
Remove the chilies, shallots, kencur and galangal. Grind finely, then return to the tempeh cooking water.
Remove the tempeh and grind it coarsely. Return it to the cooking water.
Lower the heat. Add the coconut milk and seasoning. Stir well. Add the whole bird's eye chilies and cook, stirring occasionally, until it boils and the broth reduces slightly so the flavors soak in. Check the taste and turn off the heat.
Prepare the vegetables.
To serve: put a plate of rice, add the vegetables, and pour the tumpang sauce over it. Ready to eat with assorted fritters. Here I used fried tofu, according to what I had at home.
strIngredient1: Semangit tempeh (very ripe tempeh), cut into large cubes
strIngredient3: Red bird's eye chilies, left whole
strIngredient18: Helai kacang panjang , potong dan rebus
strIngredient22: Wortel , potong korek api dan rebus
strIngredient23: Helai sawi hijau , potong dan rebus

strInstructions:
Tumpang sauce: boil/steam the tempeh and all the spices except the kaffir lime leaves, galangal, bay leaves, kencur powder and candlenuts. Don't discard the cooking water!
Blend all the boiled spices, add the candlenuts and kencur powder, and blend until smooth.
Add the blended spices to the tempeh cooking water, add the crushed galangal, kaffir lime leaves and bay leaves, boil again and add the Kara coconut milk, salt, sugar and stock powder. Stir well, cook until boiling, adjust the taste, and set aside.
Boiled vegetables: boil the vegetables one at a time, starting with the long beans. Once the color changes, remove and set aside. Then the spinach: boil until the color changes, remove and set aside. Then the napa cabbage: boil until the color changes, remove and set aside. Lastly the bean sprouts: boil only briefly, remove and set aside.
Serving: arrange rice on a plate lined with banana leaf, put the boiled vegetables beside it, pour the tumpang sauce over, and add crackers and serundeng chicken on the side. And voilà... ready to serve 🤗💞

Boil the medem tempeh and the regular tempeh.
Mash the tempeh and set aside.
Grind ingredients B and mix them in with the tempeh.
Add enough water and bring to a boil.
Once it boils, add ingredients C except the tapioca flour.
Next, dissolve 1 tbsp of tapioca flour in water, stir slowly, and add it to the tumpang vegetable mixture. Adjust the thickness to your own taste.

Mix the glutinous rice and the regular rice, wash, then soak for 1 hour... After 1 hour, steam until soft. If it's still hard, sprinkle with hot water and cover again.
Once the rice is soft and still hot... add it to the coconut milk and stir until evenly mixed. Let it sit until absorbed, then steam again until cooked.
Combine all of ingredients B and cook until boiling and fragrant.

Prepare the rice, tumpang sauce, vegetables and lalapan (fresh raw vegetables).
Because the vegetables ran out, they can be replaced with a mix of papaya, carrot and moringa leaves. Boil the moringa leaves for only 10 minutes, then remove and drain.
Steam the carrots, sliced lengthwise, and the coarsely grated papaya. Steam for 20 minutes.
Prepare the side dishes. It goes well with rempeyek.
Assemble the tumpang rice: rice, vegetables, sauce, lalapan and side dishes. Enjoy ❤️ Thank you 👏
strIngredient3: Pecel tumpang sauce 200. pecel tumpang sauce

strInstructions:
Boil the vegetables and make the pecel sauce (see reference) Complete Nasi Pecel.
Make the side dishes (see reference) Bali-spiced eggs and tofu.
Make the tumpang sauce (see reference) Kediri-style Sambal Tumpang.
Make the pincuk from a banana leaf with the ends folded and pinned with a skewer.
Arrange on the pincuk: rice, boiled vegetables and side dishes, then pour over the pecel sauce and tumpang sauce. Serve with peanut peyek (sorry, the peyek isn't in the photo; by the time I realized, it was already gone 🙊🙊)
strIngredient2: Side dish ingredients, Bali-spiced eggs and tofu
strIngredient3: Sambal tumpang ingredients, Kediri-style sambal tumpang

strInstructions:
Boil all the vegetables, and prepare the peanut peyek and tumpang sauce. Put terok rice on a plate.
Then arrange the vegetables on the plate, pour the tumpang sauce over, sprinkle with fried shallots, and finally top with the peanut peyek.
The dish is ready to serve.

Boil the spinach, bean sprouts and carrot for the urap.
Make the urap seasoning: grind the garlic, shallots, chilies, kaffir lime leaves, shrimp paste, kencur and palm sugar, add salt, and mix with grated coconut. Taste and adjust to your liking.
Make the tumpang vegetable dish by first boiling the tempeh, cut into pieces, in boiling water. Then remove it and grind coarsely.
Also boil the spices to be ground (garlic, shallots, chilies, candlenuts) in boiling water. Then grind until smooth. Don't discard the remaining water; it's used for the broth.
Once the spices are ground, sauté them in a little oil until fragrant. Add the bay leaves, kaffir lime leaves, galangal, salt and palm sugar. Add the water the spices were boiled in plus enough fresh water to your liking.
Once the water boils, add the coarsely ground tempeh and the sliced tofu skin. Add salt, pepper and salt.
Add the coconut milk and check the taste. If it doesn't taste rich enough, add a little granulated sugar and Totole (mushroom seasoning).
Solo-style tumpang vegetable rice is ready to be served with a boiled egg.
strIngredient16: Papan tempe ukuran kecil yg masih seger
strIngredient17: Sedikit tempe yg udah mateng banget

strInstructions:
Fill a pot with water and boil the shallots, garlic, curly chilies, bird's eye chilies, kencur, and 3 kaffir lime leaves. Drain.
Grind the ground spices (ingredients 2) and set aside.
Then grind the semanggit tempeh (overripe tempeh). Set aside.
Also grind the regular tempeh coarsely. Set aside.
Bring the water used for boiling the tempeh back to a boil.
Put into the pot the ground tempeh, ground spices, kaffir lime leaves, bay leaves, galangal, salt, mushroom stock powder, sliced palm sugar, and coriander. Stir evenly and cook until the broth thickens slightly.
Pour in the Kara coconut milk. Let it come to a boil while stirring.
Lastly, add 2 tbsp of rese/urang dawu (small dried shrimp). Stir, adjust the taste, and remove from the heat.
Prepare a pincuk, add rice and vegetables, drench with the tumpang sauce, and add fried tempeh and peanut rempeyek. Serve.
strIngredient8: Small dried shrimp / urang dawu / rese

strInstructions:
Prepare all the ingredients according to the recipe measurements.
Boil all the spices except the bird's eye chilies.
Also boil the accompanying ingredients and set aside.
Grind the tempeh and the boiled spices.
Add the spices, tempeh and tofu to the spice cooking water. Boil until it boils.
Add the coconut milk, bird's eye chilies, petai (stink beans), sugar and salt.
Cook until boiling, stirring occasionally. Taste test.

strMeal: Nasi Pecel Sambal Tumpang Asli Kediri
strInstructions:
Prepare all the ingredients.
Boil all those ingredients except the coconut milk, salt, sugar and stock.
After boiling until tender, remove everything from the pot. Grind the spices first and set the tempeh aside. Don't throw away the cooking water, okay..
Once the spices are smooth, it's the tempeh's turn to be ground. Once everything is smooth, put it all into the cooking water from before and boil again along with the galangal & bay leaves.
When it's almost boiling, add the coconut milk, mushroom stock, and salt and sugar to taste.
Stir well while tasting. Once it has thickened slightly and the taste is right, turn off the heat.
Ready to serve with boiled vegetables, side dishes, pecel sauce & crackers / rempeyek.
Good luck trying it and enjoy, okay.. Don't forget to give it a love and recook, momsis 😘👌

strMeal: Nasi Jagung Kuah Sambel Tumpang Ikan Asin Dan Sayur
strInstructions:
First, steam the corn rice for 10 minutes,,,, after 10 minutes, remove and sprinkle with a little water bit by bit, then steam again for 10 minutes over medium heat,,
While waiting for the corn rice to cook, prepare the spices for the tumpang sauce (garlic and shallots, chilies, kencur, rotten tempeh, candlenuts), pounded coarsely,, cut the tofu as you like (you can add meat trimmings if you like).
Heat oil,,, once hot, sauté the spices until fragrant and add the bay leaves until wilted,,, then add the tofu and enough water,,, let it sit for 5-7 minutes,,,
While waiting for the rice and tumpang sauce to cook, we fry the salted fish and the leafy vegetables until cooked.
After the tumpang sauce has sat for 5-7 minutes, add the coconut milk and wait until it boils.. Remove the corn rice,, once the tumpang sauce has boiled, turn off the heat..
Ready to serve.. thank you, happy trying

Wash the rice as usual.
Fill plastic bags with 100 mg (weigh it).
Seal the plastic by burning it with a candle (make sure it's tight) so the rice doesn't come out.
Pierce the rice-filled plastic with a pin so that water can get into the rice.
Bring water to a boil in a large pot.
Once it boils, add the rice in plastic.
Boil for 4 hours over a wood fire.
If the water level drops (the lontong is no longer submerged), add boiling water (cooked in another pot).
Remove after 4 hours.

strMeal: Lontong Lodeh Tahu Tempe Cecek 100 Porsi
strInstructions:
Boil the cecek (cow skin) together with bay leaves and lemongrass.
Fry the tofu and tempeh.
Blend the ground spices.
As in normal cooking, after the spices are sautéed, I add the Ale green chilies and sauté until fragrant. I mix it with the tofu, tempeh and cecek....
And I mix it with thin coconut milk. Wait until it boils, add the washed rebon (tiny dried shrimp) along with seasoning, and add thick coconut milk. Once it has boiled, taste test.
strIngredient8: Shallots (the remainder after blending was only 750 g)

strInstructions:
Grind the shallots, garlic, candlenuts, ginger, turmeric, and red chilies.
Sauté the ground spices together with the galangal, kaffir lime leaves, and bay leaves until fragrant.
Add water and the chicken, and cook until the chicken is done.
Add the coconut milk and the cut-up tofu.
Cook until boiling, add flavor enhancer, then serve.

Prepare the ingredients. Grind the spices. Boil the chicken until just cooked.
Sauté the ground spices and the whole ("cemplung") spices until fragrant. On another stove, boil water until boiling. Pour the sautéed spices into the pot, then add the boiled chicken.
Pour the coconut milk into the pot. Add salt, sugar and mushroom stock. Adjust the taste. Turn off the heat.
Arrange the lontong and chicken, pour the broth over, then sprinkle with fried shallots. Serve.
strIngredient3: Whole setan bird's eye chilies (extra hot)
strIngredient22: Secukupnya bawang merah goreng taburan bawang merah goreng

strInstructions:
Prepare the ingredients.
Sauté the ground spices and the whole ("cemplung") spices until fragrant. Add the chicken eggs, boiled chicken and thick coconut milk. Add salt and palm sugar.
Cook until boiling. Turn off the heat. Serve.
Serve the lontong opor with potato sambal goreng and shrimp crackers. Sambal Goreng Kentang (potato sambal goreng).

Wash the rice thoroughly, then cook it until half done (aron). Divide it into 2 containers. Mix one container with dragon fruit (blended and strained) and add a little salt. The other stays white, also mixed with a little salt. Stir each until evenly mixed.
Take a leaf, put 2-3 tbsp of aron rice on it, then roll it up and pin it with a skewer. Tidy up the ends of the leaf with scissors (repeat until the rice is used up).
Bring water to a boil in a steamer pot, add the lontong until submerged, and boil for ±2 hours.
After 2 hours, remove, let cool, and serve with your favorite dish.
strIngredient5: Banana leaves, wilted over the stove flame

strInstructions:
Wash the rice, then cook it with coconut milk, adding salt and bay leaves. Stir periodically so the dense porridge doesn't burn. Once the coconut milk has reduced, turn off the heat. Let it cool slightly so it can be wrapped in banana leaf.
While waiting for the dense porridge to cool a bit, make the filling first. Fry the tempeh briefly, not too dry, then smash it and stir-fry with the listed spices, adjusting to taste.
Once the filling is done, wrap the dense porridge in banana leaf, about 65 g per lontong with 1 tsp of stir-fried tempeh filling.
Once done, steam for 45 minutes to 1 hour. Good luck 🤗

Prepare the ingredients.
Fry the tofu until it forms a skin, then drain. Briefly fry the garlic and chilies.
Grind the chilies, garlic, salt, sugar, MSG (Asatu Rose Brand) and peanuts, then add enough warm water and sweet soy sauce, and adjust the taste.
Arrange the lontong, bean sprouts, tofu and celery leaves, then pour the peanut sauce over and sprinkle with fried shallots.
Serve.

~ Peel the chayote and cut as desired, and prepare the other ingredients
~ Prepare the spices and grind them, sauté the ground and aromatic spices until fragrant, add the chayote and chilies and cook until wilted
~ Add the tofu and enough water, stir well, add the coconut milk, sugar and salt as needed, stir well and taste
~ Cook until the spices have soaked in, then turn off the heat
~ Take a serving plate, add enough lontong, and add the lodeh vegetables and fried shallots
~ Serve
strIngredient7: A handful of whole bird's eye chilies

strInstructions:
Prepare the ingredients and grind the spices.
Heat the ground and aromatic spices until the water is gone, add oil and sauté until cooked.
Add the chicken and quail eggs. Once the chicken changes color, add water.
Add seasoning and continue to simmer.
Once the chicken is tender, add the instant coconut milk.
Cook, stirring occasionally, until it's cooked down, and adjust the taste. When the taste is right, turn off the heat.
Accompaniments.
Serve the chicken and quail egg opor with lontong and its accompaniments.

Arrange the lontong, tofu and egg together with the cabbage and bean sprouts on a plate.
Grind all the sauce ingredients except the sambal lime.
Add water little by little to adjust to the desired thickness, and taste.
Squeeze in the sambal lime for freshness.
Pour the peanut sauce over the arranged lontong, tofu, egg, and vegetables. Sprinkle with celery and fried shallots. Ready to serve.
strIngredient3: Tofu, fried then sliced without cutting all the way through
strIngredient12: Bird's eye chilies, add more if you like it spicy

strInstructions:
Prepare leftover rice from last night and put it in a wok/pot. Add hot water, then cook it half-done (aron) over the heat while stirring so there is no scorched rice at the bottom. Once the water has evaporated, turn off the heat.
Prepare a container lined with banana leaf and rub it with oil so it doesn't stick. Pour the rice into the container and press it down with the banana leaf. Compact it and cover the top with another banana leaf.
Close with the container's lid and keep it in the refrigerator so the lontong becomes firmer. If you'll use it soon, keep the lontong in the refrigerator for about 1 hour. If you'll use it later, it's fine to keep it in the refrigerator until needed. But don't store it for too long (just a few days).
When ready to use, take it out of the container and cut it into pieces. Ready to serve.

Crumble the oncom by squeezing it into small pieces with your hands. Set aside.
Grind the shallots, garlic and chilies. Cut the spring onions into small cubes.
Sauté the ground spices. Once the spices smell fragrant, add the spring onions and stir, then finally add the oncom and salt. Cook until done.
Wash the rice until clean. Then add water, salt, and bay leaves. Cook over medium heat while stirring constantly until steam bubbles pop up. Cover the pot and let it sit for 5 minutes.
Prepare a pestle/wooden pounder covered with plastic so the aron rice doesn't stick when pounded. Pound the rice until soft enough to make lontong.
Using plastic gloves, take some of the soft rice, sized to the lontong you want. Make a hole in the middle to form a bowl, then fill it with 1 tbsp of oncom. Close it again and wrap with banana leaf.
Arrange the lontong standing upright in the steamer. Then steam for 30 - 45 minutes.
Remove and arrange the lontong 1 minute after it's done on a perforated container/tray. Cool it outdoors so it cools down quickly. Serve with peanut sambal and fritters.

Prepare the rice. Take a container (I used a brownie pan), line it with banana leaf, then add the hot rice and press it down until compact. Arrange meat floss on top.
Cover again with rice and press to compact it. Cut into several pieces, take 1 piece, then tidy up its shape by molding it. Place it on plastic, you can add more floss filling, then roll it round. Take a width the size of the lontong, then roll it up. Arrange on the steamer. Steam for 10 minutes. Wait until cool.
Fold it back and pin it into the fold. I stuck on a sticker so it wouldn't come undone. Serve.
Take a square leaf and place it at the corner of the lontong roll. Then roll it up to 2/3 of the leaf's width. Fold the left and right sides forward.

Wash the rice thoroughly, then drain until completely dry.
Tear the banana leaf to a width of ±35-30 cm, then lay a banana midrib on top leaving ±10 cm at the top, then roll it up.
Fold it and pin a skewer at the end, then remove the banana midrib, fill with ±3 tbsp of rice, fold the end, then pin it with a toothpick.
Put all the lontong into a pressure cooker, fill with hot water until all the lontong are submerged and the water is 1 cm above the pot's rack. Cover with the pot's rack and weigh it down with a stone so the lontong don't float.
Close with the pressure cooker lid. Pressure cook ±15 minutes over high heat (counting from the first time it hisses), then continue for 15 minutes over medium heat.
After 30 minutes, release the steam, open the pressure cooker lid, then take out the lontong. Wait until completely cool and cut into pieces as you like. Enjoooy ❤️❤️❤️

Prepare a pot/wok and add the water, coconut milk, salt and pandan leaf.
Add the glutinous rice, then turn on the stove and cook while stirring until the coconut milk is absorbed. Then turn off the stove and let it cool.
Take a banana leaf, place the glutinous rice in the middle, then roll it up and pin a skewer at both ends of the roll. Do this until the glutinous rice is used up. Then boil in boiling water (add green food coloring if you like) for 45 minutes (until cooked).
Make the sugar syrup: boil the water, sugar, salt and pandan leaf until boiling and thick.
Steam the grated coconut that has been salted.
Then, once drained and cooled, cut into pieces as you like, arrange on a plate, add the coconut and sugar syrup, and serve. Enjoy😍

strMeal: Lontong Lodeh Labu Siam Wortel Dan Tempe
strInstructions:
Peel the carrot and chayote and cut into matchsticks or shred them with a potato shredder, wash clean, set aside.
Grind the two kinds of chili, two kinds of onion, dried rebon shrimp, turmeric, ginger and galangal, and sauté in hot oil together with the bay leaf and kaffir lime leaves until fragrant.
Once the spices are fragrant, add the chayote and carrot and stir evenly.
Add the coconut milk, tempeh, salt, granulated sugar and mushroom stock, and cook, stirring occasionally, until boiling and the vegetables are cooked. Check the taste and remove from the heat.
Arrange the lontong on a serving plate, add the chayote lodeh, carrots and tempeh, plus a boiled egg. Alhamdulillah..... Let's eat....

Cut the banana leaves as needed. Wash the banana leaves clean, dry them, then toast them over the stove so they wilt and are easy to use for wrapping 🤗
Bring 750 ml of water to a boil, wash the rice and add it to the water, add the salt, and cook while stirring until the water reduces. Let it cool slightly, then mash it with a pestle or the base of a drinking bottle covered with plastic. Divide into 5, then roll each portion in plastic into an oval shape.
Prepare 1 wide banana leaf and layer a smaller banana leaf on top of it with the green side up. Take 1 oval-shaped portion of rice, wrap it, and pin the ends with a skewer. Bring water to a boil in a slow cooker, then boil the lontong on the auto setting for 5 hours.
Remove the lontong, drain, cut as you like, and serve with lontong broth, shrimp and potato sambal, and egg. Happy Eid 🥳

Make the lontong rice: wash the rice, bay leaves and lemongrass clean. Then add enough water (like cooking rice), cook until boiling and add salt.
When it boils, stir the aron rice so the bottom doesn't form a crust, add oil and stir again, cook until the water is absorbed. Then cover the aron rice and wait until warm.
Once warm, pound the aron rice.
Cook the filling: sauté the garlic and shallots until fragrant.
Add water, add the potatoes and carrots, and stir evenly. Cook until half done, then add the shredded chicken, stir evenly, and add salt, pepper and seasoning as needed. Taste to get the flavor right. Cook until done and the water is absorbed, set aside.
Prepare the banana leaves and toast them over the flame so they wilt.
Take the aron rice (I weighed 50 g), flatten it on the banana leaf, then add the filling, and close it tightly.
Wrap it and fold both ends.
Do this until finished. Because I'm making these for the freezer, this is as far as I go. Then put them in plastic and into the freezer. When ready to steam, take them out, wait until no longer frozen, and steam for 45 minutes. Remove and wait until cooled. Ready to serve 😋

Wash the rice until clean, then drain.
Prepare banana leaves that have been sun-dried so they wilt and are easy to shape. Cut the leaf to about 2 hand-spans. Roll the leaf with the green side on the inside so the lontong color is greener, then fill it with rice up to 1/2 full and pin a toothpick or skewer at the end.
Prepare a pot and boil water until hot & boiling. Cook the lontong for 3 hours with the pot covered, or use the 5-30-7 method. If the water reduces during cooking, add more hot water (up to 3 times).
Once the lontong is cooked, remove it and drain the water. Once cool, cut the lontong into pieces as needed. Serve the lontong with chicken opor / lontong vegetable soup.

Prepare the rice and banana leaves. Wipe the banana leaves with a clean cloth and tear them to a width roughly enough to wrap the lontong later.
After washing the rice clean, put it in the rice cooker bowl and pour in water at 2x the amount used when cooking regular rice in a rice cooker. Then press the cook button. Once the rice is cooked, stir it briefly, then take some and arrange it on 1 banana leaf. Shape it into a neat long form.
Once neat, roll up the banana leaf while pressing, the same way as rolling a roll cake. Then staple both ends of the lontong. Do this until all the rice is wrapped. Then steam for 15 minutes so it cooks through and sets.
Once done, take the lontong out of the steamer. Wait until cool before cutting into pieces so the texture is firm and neat.

Prepare the ingredients needed
Heat the water, and once it boils, add the rice. Cook until the rice is cooked through and the water reduces.
Once it has reduced, turn off the heat. Let it cool slightly, then wrap the aron rice in banana leaf.
Do this until all the ingredients are used up.
Tidy up the bundles by pinning them with toothpicks.
Boil the lontong for about 30 minutes.
Once done, remove the lontong and drain. Once cool, it's ready to serve.

Wash the rice until clean, then cook it in a rice cooker like regular rice at a ratio of 1:3 (1 rice : 3 water), adding a little salt.
Once cooked, press the rice until smooth.
While waiting for the rice to cook, dip/boil the banana leaves briefly in boiling water, then drain (this is so the leaves wilt a little so they're easy to use and don't tear easily).
Prepare a leaf, take enough rice (this time my rice wasn't mashed fine enough 🫣), then roll it up (press it tightly so it comes out pretty), then pin each end with a toothpick.
Do this until all is used up, then steam for 15-20 minutes. Quick and easy lontong rice, ready to use.

Wash the rice clean, then soak for about 1 hour.
Pour the evaporated milk into a container, then add the pandan leaf and the salt.
Drain the rice with a strainer. Then put it into the rice cooker pot. Don't forget to press the button. This cooking process takes about 45 minutes.
Once the rice is cooked, stir it evenly. Prepare a baking pan and line it with banana leaf. Put the rice in, then pound it with a pestle covered in plastic.
Because the pan I used first was too big and wouldn't fit in the steamer pot, I switched pans. Prepare an 18 * 18 pan, then line it with banana leaf, and don't forget to press the lontong into the pan (compact it).
Cover again with banana leaf. As for the leftover crusty rice, don't mix it in.
Heat the steamer pot. Put the pan in once there is plenty of steam. Then steam for about 1 hour.
When it's cooked, you can open the banana leaf.
Ready to serve with a soupy vegetable dish.

Wash the rice clean.
Add the water, salt and oil. Stir evenly.
Press the cook button. Let it go until the water in the rice cooker boils. Then open the rice cooker lid and stir gently. Close it again. Continue cooking until the cook light turns off and the warm light comes on. Once cooked, leave it for 10 minutes without opening the rice cooker lid, letting the mixture set first.
Once the mixture has set, stir it while mashing it until completely smooth. I just used the rice cooker's own scoop.
Once smooth, transfer it to a container that has been lightly greased with oil. Press it down until even, then lightly brush the surface with oil so it doesn't dry out. Let it cool and the lontong will set. If making it at night, let it set at room temperature. If making it during the day to eat tomorrow, after it sets you can put it in the refrigerator. Make sure the surface is covered so it doesn't dry out.
Once cooled and set, cut into pieces as you like. Serve with your favorite vegetable dish.

Wash the rice 2x, then add water to about 1 segment (finger joint) above the rice.
Cook the rice half-done (aron) until the water reduces.
Wilt the banana leaves.
Wrap the rice without overfilling, then roll it up.
Cook the lontong over medium heat; the lontong must be submerged in water. Cover the pot and cook until done, about 3 hours.

Prepare the rice cooker bowl, put in the rice, bay leaf, lemongrass, pandan leaf, salt and water, then put it into the rice cooker and cook until it switches to warm or is done. Once cooked, transfer it to a container or wrap it in banana leaf brushed with vegetable oil. Let it cool for 2-4 hours. Then steam for 15 minutes. And let it cool again. (It can be kept in the refrigerator for 3 days and is still good.)
SAMBAL BAWANG (SHALLOT SAMBAL): HEAT A WOK, ADD VEGETABLE OIL, FRY THE SLICED SHALLOTS UNTIL BROWNISH, THEN ADD WATER, SALT, FLAVOR ENHANCER AND CHILI POWDER, STIR UNTIL THE WATER BOILS, THEN ADD WHEAT FLOUR, STIR SLOWLY UNTIL IT THICKENS, THEN TURN OFF THE STOVE. ADD THE MARGARINE. THE SHALLOT SAMBAL IS READY TO SERVE.
strIngredient4: Glutinous rice flour / rice flour, if available

strMeal: Opor Pedas Ayam Suwir (Untuk Nasi Bogana)
strInstructions:
Rub the chicken with lime juice. Let it sit for about 15 minutes, then simmer the chicken in water until it makes a stock. Turn off the heat first.
Sauté the ground spices and whole spices until fragrant.
Pour the sautéed spices into the chicken broth. Add the coconut milk, salt, stock powder, granulated sugar and tamarind water. Stir evenly. Cook until the broth reduces and thickens. Adjust the taste.
Remove the chicken pieces, then shred them and arrange in a container/plate. Pour the broth over. Serve sprinkled with fried shallots.
strIngredient4: Packet of Masako chicken / stock powder

strInstructions:
Grind the spices, then sauté until fragrant, add the lemongrass, kaffir lime leaves and bay leaves, stir evenly
Add the coconut milk, then immediately I divide it into 2 in 2 woks. First wok: add the chicken
Add the grated coconut, salt and mushroom stock, cook until done (use low heat). While waiting for the chicken to cook, pour the rice into the 2nd wok, stir until evenly mixed, add turmeric powder so the color is more vivid. Keep stirring until even, add a little salt, then turn off the stove
Stir the chicken stew, cook until the liquid reduces, then turn off the stove. Take a tumpeng mold, then pour in the yellow rice while pressing it down so it's compact and doesn't fall apart
Then turn it out onto a prepared plate/tray, then arrange the accompanying side dishes.. Bogana rice tumpeng is ready to be served
strIngredient20: Sambel goreng kentang sambel goreng kentang ati ampela
strIngredient21: Bihun goreng bihun goreng sayur sehat

strInstructions:
Boil water and cook the eggs until done, soak in cold water, peel, set aside.
Sauté the ground spices until the raw smell is gone, add the water, salt, sugar and eggs, stir evenly, check the taste, remove.
Sauté the ground spices, kaffir lime leaves, bay leaves, galangal and lemongrass until cooked, add the chicken, stir until it changes color, add the grated coconut and stir evenly.
Add water until submerged, season with a rather generous amount of salt so the rice isn't bland, and sugar, and cook until the chicken is done. Then take out the large chicken pieces and some of the seasoning, set aside. Add the rice, stir until evenly mixed, check the taste, remove.
Then steam the rice for 30 minutes so it cooks through better, remove and let it cool.
Then shape it into a tumpeng using banana leaf, and serve with accompaniments.

SAVORY RICE (NASI GURIH): Mix all the ingredients. Stir evenly. Cook until done like cooking regular rice (cooked 2x)
SPICY CHICKEN OPOR: Rub the chicken with lime juice. Let it sit for 15 minutes, then boil with 300 ml of water until it makes a stock, turn off the heat first. Sauté the ground spices, lemongrass, galangal and kaffir lime leaves until fragrant. Pour the sautéed spices into the chicken broth. Add the instant coconut milk, salt, stock powder and granulated sugar. Cook until the broth reduces and the spices have soaked in. Adjust the taste, remove the chicken and shred it. Ready to serve with the broth poured over
PINDANG EGGS: Mix all the egg ingredients. Boil for 10 minutes, then remove and tap until cracked. Boil again briefly and turn off the heat. Leave the eggs submerged until the water is cool, then remove. Peel the eggs and cut in 2
STIR-FRIED LONG BEANS: Sauté the dried rebon shrimp until fragrant. Add the shallots, garlic and chilies. Sauté again until fragrant and cooked. Add the long beans, then pour in water. Add salt, stock powder and granulated sugar. Cook until the beans are tender and the spices have soaked in. Adjust the taste and it's ready to serve
COCONUT SERUNDENG: Mix all the serundeng ingredients. Dry-roast until dry while stirring constantly. The serundeng is ready to serve
STIR-FRIED SHALLOT SAMBAL: Sauté the ground spices until fragrant. Add the palm sugar, salt, stock powder and granulated sugar. Cook until cooked through/oily. Adjust the taste. The sambal is ready to serve
SERVING: Serve the rice together with the dishes
strIngredient2: Rice (for the rice cooker), washed clean
strIngredient7: Large (1.3 kg) chicken breast, washed clean
strIngredient14: Packet of Masako chicken / stock powder
strIngredient18: Bumbu halus opor : blender jadi satu
strIngredient27: Air asam jawa (3 mata asam + air)
strIngredient38: Kacang panjang , cuci bersih lalu potong-potong
strIngredient49: Kaldu udang bubuk homemade (boleh diskip) kaldu udang bubuk (dari ampas petis)
strIngredient51: Bumbu halus serundeng : blender jadi satu
strIngredient61: Air asam jawa (5 mata asam + air)
strIngredient68: Bumbu halus sambal : blender dengan sedikit air

strInstructions:
RICE: > Mix all the rice ingredients, then stir evenly > Cook until done like cooking regular rice in a rice cooker > Let it sit for about 15 minutes > Once it's cooked through, stir it evenly and it's ready to serve
CHICKEN GULAI: > Heat the cooking oil > Sauté the shallots, garlic, cardamom, gulai spices, star anise, cinnamon, cloves, lemongrass and kaffir lime leaves until fragrant and cooked through/oily
> Add the chicken, salt and palm sugar > Stir evenly and cook until the chicken changes color
> Pour in the water, then stir evenly > Cover the wok and cook over rather low heat until the chicken is done > Stir occasionally
> Add the coconut milk and green chilies > Cook until the chicken is tender and the spices have soaked in > Adjust the taste and it's ready to serve
PICKLES (ACAR): > Wash the cucumber, carrot and onion clean > Remove the seeds from the cucumber, then cut into matchsticks > Cut the carrot into matchsticks > Slice the shallots
> Put all the pickle ingredients in a container/bowl > Stir evenly and let sit for a while until everything is absorbed > The pickles are ready to serve
Serve the express nasi dagang together with the chicken gulai and pickles
strIngredient11: Large chicken, washed clean and drained
strIngredient13: Heaping (12.5 g) instant gulai spice mix

strInstructions:
Wash the rice clean, then soak for 1-2 hours.
Put the thick coconut milk, water, salt and sugar into a pot and cook until boiling while stirring constantly so the coconut milk doesn't split. After that add the fenugreek, ginger, garlic and shallots. Stir evenly, then turn off the heat.
Prepare a container or basin and put in the thin coconut milk. This is for the first pour over the rice.
Steam or cook the rice that has been soaked for 2 hours, using the method of poking a hole in the middle so the hot steam rises quickly and the rice cooks quickly.
Once the rice is nearly half cooked, remove it and transfer it to a container, then pour the thin coconut milk over it while stirring constantly until evenly mixed.
Steam or cook the rice again until fully cooked. Still using the method of poking a hole in the middle. Then remove it again and pour over the 2nd thick coconut milk that was cooked with the fenugreek, shallots, garlic and ginger earlier. Pour while stirring until evenly mixed. Then steam again only briefly, no need for long.
The nasi dagang is ready to be served with tuna gulai and pickles 😁 Tuna Gulai Nasi Dagang
strIngredient6: Coconut milk, separate the thick and thin milk

strInstructions:
Clean the tuna first, then cut it in half or into small pieces as you like. Boil the tuna until cooked; it tastes better if boiled a day ahead. Remove the fish meat. Don't discard the fish cooking water.
Sauté the ground spices until fragrant, add the curry spices and dry spices, then pour in the fish cooking water, add the palm sugar, kandis acid fruit, salt, mushroom stock and coconut milk. You can add Royko for more aroma. Stir until the oil rises.
Add the tuna and wait until the gulai broth boils. Taste test. The tuna gulai is ready to be served with nasi dagang.

Sauté the sliced spices. Once fragrant, add the washed rice + water according to the measure + the whole spices. COOK IT HALF-DONE (ARON) until the water is gone.
Steam the rice until cooked. Serve with anchovy sambal + fried shallots + cucumber.
strIngredient14: Water according to the rice measure

strInstructions:
Prepare the ingredients to be used.
Bring water to a boil, add the jackfruit, ground spices, galangal and bay leaves. Add the peanuts, cook until the jackfruit and peanuts are half tender. Then season with salt and add the tamarind.
Next, add the vegetables, starting with the hard ones first, beginning with the chayote and sweet corn. Then the purple eggplant and finger eggplant. Followed by the long beans, melinjo leaves and cabbage, stir evenly. Season with palm sugar and stock powder.
Cook until the vegetables are done and the flavors have come together. Don't forget to adjust the sour and salty taste, then turn off the heat.
Serve with fried fish/tempeh/tofu, salted fish and shrimp paste sambal.
strIngredient22: Cm lengkuas (1,5 jari), geprek/ iris tipis

strInstructions:
Dissolve the tamarind in warm water, strain, set aside.
Blend the shallots, garlic, candlenuts, shrimp paste and bird's eye chilies until smooth.
Sauté the ground spices together with the galangal and bay leaves until fragrant.
Put the water, tamarind solution, liquid palm sugar, granulated sugar, salt, stock powder and the sautéed spices into the pressure cooker. Stir evenly.
Add the corn, peanuts, young jackfruit and melinjo fruit. Close the pot and cook at high pressure for 6 minutes.
After the steam releases naturally, open the lid. Add the chayote, long beans, melinjo leaves and cabbage. Cook uncovered for 4 minutes.
Adjust the taste. Serve warm.
strIngredient22: (larutkan dengan 50ml air hangat, saring) asam jawa

strInstructions:
Cut up the sayur asem vegetable set. Wash clean, then drain
Boil water until boiling. Add the ground spices, bay leaves, galangal, palm sugar, and tamarind. Cook until boiling & the tamarind has dissolved
Add the vegetables, granulated sugar, salt, MSG, and stock powder. Cook again until boiling & the vegetables are soft. Adjust the taste. If it's lacking in sourness / sweetness / saltiness, you can add more to taste. (I like my sayur asem rich in the flavor of the spices, salty, sour, and sweet). Once the vegetables are tender, turn off the heat
Serve. Good luck trying it

Cut up and trim the sayur asem package. Wash clean.
Bring water to a boil. Add the cleaned sayur asem vegetables.
Once half cooked, add 1 packet of instant spice mix, flavor enhancer, and salt.
The easy, simple sayur asem is ready to serve! Good luck trying it!
strIngredient6: Packet of sayur asem spice mix

strMeal: Sayur Asem Labu Siam, Kacang Panjang, Dan Bayam 🥣✨
strInstructions:
Prepare the ingredients
Boil 800 ml of water. Add the sliced spices. Bring to a boil.
Add the hard ones first. Chayote + long beans. Cook for 5 minutes until half tender. Add the palm sugar.
Add the tamarind, tomato, salt, sugar and stock. Adjust the taste. It has to be fresh, sour-sweet-savory.
Lastly, add the spinach. Cook for only 1 minute so it doesn't wilt too much. Turn off the heat. And there you have a fresh sayur asem 🥣
strIngredient2: Long bean strands, cut into 3 cm
strIngredient4: Required extra ingredient for the 'sour' ('asem') flavor

strInstructions:
Cut the vegetables as you like, then wash clean and drain the water
Next, sauté the chicken ungkep spice mix along with the garlic and shallots until fragrant, then add the vegetables and stir-fry, while adding the sugar and the shrimp paste crumbled with your fingers, along with the Totole, the instant sayur asem spice mix, then add the water, then stir again
Next, cover and wait until the water boils and the vegetables are evenly tender, using only low heat. After that, add the salt while it's still warm. Now the shrimp paste sayur asem can be enjoyed with white rice and fried tofu as well as salted fish. Good luck trying it :)
strIngredient1: A pack of mixed vegetables (long beans
strIngredient11: Indofood instant sayur asem spice mix

strMeal: Ayam Goreng Bumbu Sayur Asem (Bumbu Racik)
strInstructions:
Wash & cut the chicken into several pieces.
Put the chicken into a medium-sized container.
Add the pepper, sayur asem spice mix, cornstarch, baking powder, and loosely beaten egg to the container with the chicken.
Mix the seasonings until evenly coated on the chicken.
Marinate for about 4-8 hours in the refrigerator's chiller.
Fry the chicken over medium heat for about 20 minutes, until golden brown. Remove.
Prepare lettuce & cucumber. The sayur asem spice mix fried chicken is ready to serve 😋.

Cut up all kinds of vegetables, wash with clean water
Peel the shallots and garlic, then prepare the bay leaves and the crushed galangal
Heat the water, then add the prepared spices, and once it boils add the vegetables
When they seem done, add the instant spice mix, salt and sugar
If the taste is right to your liking, it's ready to serve

Prepare the ingredients. Bring water to a boil, then boil the hard vegetables first. Here that's the krai cucumber, peanuts and long beans.
Once the vegetables are 3/4 cooked, add the sliced spices, instant spice mix, bay leaves, and soybean sprouts. Cook until done, taste and adjust.
Ready to enjoy.

Cut up the vegetables, wash clean and drain. (3 handfuls of water spinach means water spinach from which only the leaves and young stems have been taken.)
Prepare the sliced spices, then boil the seasonings, namely the sliced spices, bay leaves, lemongrass, spice mix, and water. Wait until it boils.
Add the cabbage, wait 2 minutes, then add the water spinach, sugar, salt and flavor enhancer. Stir evenly and adjust the taste.
Serve.
strIngredient1: Pack of sayur asem spice mix

strInstructions:
Heat the water, spices & the assorted hard vegetables, bring to a boil, until the hard vegetables soften a little
Add the tofu pieces and the leafy vegetables & those that soften easily, cook until everything is done
Don't forget to adjust the taste & serve
strIngredient1: Pack of assorted sayur asem vegetables

strInstructions:
Clean and cut up the vegetables.
Grind the shallots and chilies. You can pound them for a finer result. For a quicker way, you can use a chopper.
Bring water to a boil. Add the corn and melinjo fruit. Bring to a boil again.
Once it boils, add the ground spices.
Add the chayote pieces, young papaya and tamarind.
After a while, scoop out the tamarind, then mash it so the sour flavor comes out more.
Add the salt, sugar and flavor enhancer. Stir evenly. Adjust the taste.
Lastly, add the melinjo leaves. Cook briefly.
Ready to serve.

strMeal: Ayam Goreng Bumbu Racik Sayur Asem
strInstructions:
Season the chicken with the sayur asem spice mix and stevia sugar, stir evenly, let sit for about 5 minutes
Add the egg and cornstarch
Stir the egg and cornstarch evenly, then heat the oil
Fry until golden and the fried chicken is ready to eat 😜

🌶️Prepare the ingredients and spices. 🌶️Bring water to a boil, then add the sweet corn and soybean sprouts
🌶️Add the long beans, chayote and ground spices. Stir evenly. 🌶️Also add the galangal, lemongrass, bay leaves and sliced chilies
🌶️Add the salt, mushroom stock and Rose Brand granulated sugar. 🌶️Stir and cook until boiling and done
🌶️Lastly, add the sliced tomato. Adjust the taste. Serve warm.

Grind the shallots, candlenuts, turmeric, palm sugar, and instant spice mix together.
Take some of the peanuts and grind them coarsely.
Sauté the ground spices in a little oil until fragrant.
Boil the vegetables from the sayur asem pack until half cooked.
Add the sautéed spices and ground peanuts to the vegetable broth.
Add the remaining whole peanuts, cook until everything is done.

Prepare the ingredients and spices. Wash the in-shell peanuts clean, then drain.
Halve the chayote and young papaya and rub the cut halves in circles so the sap comes out, then peel the skin. Cut the filling ingredients as you like.
Grind the ground spices. Add the shrimp paste last so the grinding is easier.
Bring water to a boil, add the hard vegetables (melinjo, corn, peanuts, jackfruit, papaya, chayote). Add the galangal and bay leaves. Cover and cook until tender.
While it's boiling, add the soft vegetables (melinjo leaves and long beans). Add the ground spices, young tamarind, sugar, and salt. Stir evenly, cook until done.
Stir until the spices are evenly mixed. Adjust the taste. Add tamarind solution if the sourness isn't strong enough.
Turn off the heat. Let it sit for a while so the spices soak in and the vegetables are fully cooked. The Sayur Asem is ready to serve.

strMeal: Sayur Asem Pepaya Muda, Labu Siam & Buah Asam
strInstructions:
Bring the water to a boil, add the bay leaves and galangal. Add the ground spices, cook for 2–3 minutes. Add the young papaya and corn, cook for 15 minutes until starting to soften.
Add the chayote, cook for another 10–15 minutes. Add the tamarind pods.
Add salt and sugar. Adjust the taste, cook for 3–5 minutes, remove and let sit for 10–15 minutes before serving.
Ready to serve

Grind the shallots, shrimp paste, palm sugar and red chilies.
Boil water together with the galangal and bay leaves until boiling. Add the ground spices, melinjo, young papaya, young jackfruit and corn. Cook until slightly soft.
Add the chayote, tamarind, stock powder and salt. Cook until all the ingredients are done. Check the taste (you can add granulated sugar and salt), add the melinjo leaves and long beans, stir briefly, turn off the heat.
Remove and serve warm.

Prepare the white tofu, and the seasonings, namely garlic, ground coriander, salt and ROSE BRAND cooking oil, baking powder and baking soda. Cut the white tofu into squares and set aside.
Prepare the ground garlic, coriander and salt, then put them into a pot filled with water. Bring to a boil. Once boiling, turn off the stove, add the baking powder and baking soda, stir briefly to mix evenly, then pour into a container holding the tofu. The tofu must be submerged in the seasoned water. Let it sit for at least 1 hour so the seasoning soaks in.
Once the seasoning has soaked in, prepare ROSE BRAND cooking oil, pour it into a wok and fry the tofu until done. Once done, remove and drain.
Arrange on a plate and serve with bird's eye chilies or sweet soy sambal 🥰🥰🥰

Broth: the point is a fresh sweet-sour taste from the mix of palm sugar and tamarind
Pounded: shallots, bird's eye chilies, salt (it doesn't need to be very fine, it's actually nice that way)
Slice the tofu
Mix everything, and yum... delicious

Cut the tofu in 2 pieces, soak briefly in salt water and fry until half cooked so it doesn't fall apart easily
After that, prepare the ground spices and sauté the ground spices and aromatic spices until fragrant, then mix them in with the tofu bacem ingredients, add coconut water or plain water as needed
Cook the tofu until the liquid is absorbed and adjust the taste
If the liquid has reduced, turn off the heat and remove; after draining, the bacem can be fried... I don't fry mine again and serve it right away

Clean the bean sprouts and soak the tofu in hot water.
Slice the shallots and garlic.
Cut the tofu in 2 into triangle shapes.
Sauté the shallots and garlic until fragrant.
Add the bean sprouts, then add a little water.
Add the oyster sauce and a little sweet soy sauce. Once slightly wilted, add the tofu and bird's eye chilies.
Add salt, sugar, and flavor enhancer as needed. Cook until done. The stir-fry is ready to serve.

strMeal: Tahu Sumedang Kuning / Tahu Susu Kuning
strInstructions:
Boil water, add the marinade and garlic powder. Turn off the stove, then add the baking powder
Cut up the tofu and put it in a container. Add the marinade water from before. Leave it for at least 3 hours before it can be fried

Buy the tofu first okay and the ingredients, then slit only the top so the liquid soaks into the tofu. Slice the gendot chilies then wash them. Grind all the spices
Heat a wok, add 1 spoon of vegetable oil, heat it, then sauté the ground spices until cooked and fragrant, add the bay leaf, then add the tofu and water as you like, then when the heat reaches a boil add the coconut milk, stir so it doesn't split, then check the taste to your liking; after it reduces slightly, make sure it's cooked through; if it's really cooked through it can last 24 hours on the dining table

strMeal: Rice Paper + Tahu Sumedang Chili Oil
strInstructions:
Cut the rice paper as you like. Then soak it in warm water until the texture is chewy.
Here I added seasoning (bird's eye chilies, shallots, garlic, sautéed) because the chili oil wasn't plentiful enough haha
Halve the Sumedang tofu as you like, then add it to the sautéed spices. Stir until evenly mixed.
Add the rice paper, chili oil, salt and stock powder. Stir and adjust the taste. Chili Oil (Dim Sum Dipping Sauce)
Add the sliced spring onions.

Cut the green beans small, or as you like. Cut the tofu into 3 pieces, if you want it smaller cut it into 4 pieces okay.
Thinly slice the shallots/garlic, chilies, galangal, tomato, spring onion
Heat a pan, add about 7-8 tbsp of oil. More is fine if you like. Then first briefly sauté the spring onion, then add the shallots, garlic, curly chilies, galangal. Sauté until the chilies are 3/4 cooked and the shallots turn yellow
Add the green beans, stir. Add 1/2 cup of water. Then add the tomato. Stir until the green beans are 3/4 cooked, then add the Sumedang tofu
Add the salt, MSG, oyster sauce, white sugar. Stir until even, then taste test. I added the sweet soy sauce last when the stove was about to be turned off. Stir again until even. Doneee.
NOTE: The MSG can be skipped okay, it's just a matter of taste. The white sugar can be replaced with palm sugar or powdered kawung sugar. Water can also be added if you want it to have a broth. Don't overcook the green beans so there's a crunchy sensation when eating. Good luck trying it
strIngredient13: Tomato, leftover from the fridge hehe

strInstructions:
Cut the tofu into several pieces, then fry briefly just until warm
Coarsely pound the chilies and shallots, add a little salt
Heat water, dissolve the palm sugar and add the tamarind solution, adjust the taste to your liking, let it sit until done
Pour the cooking liquid over the tahu pong that has been coated with the chili sambal
strIngredient1: Tahu pong (hollow fried tofu), or 1 board also works
strIngredient3: Shallots (I like shallots so I used 3)

strInstructions:
Cut the tofu into 2 pieces
Grind the garlic and coriander
Put the ground spices, salt, and stock powder into the water
Cook until boiling, then turn off the stove
Add the baking soda and baking powder, stir until evenly mixed
Add the white tofu and soak for 1-2 hours
Fry in hot oil until the skin is dry
Yum-yummm ready to enjoy 🤤

Cut the tofu into squares (as you like) then soak in salt water for about 30 minutes
Mix all the coating ingredients, stir until evenly mixed
Put the tofu into the coating then strain with a strainer
And fry in hot oil until crispy..
Remove and serve with green bird's eye chilies or with sauce ~

Soak the tofu in water + salt + a little sugar. Mix the batter ingredients: wheat flour + tapioca flour + salt + pepper + flavor enhancer + water. Stir evenly. Add the baking powder.
Heat the oil. Dunk the tofu into the flour batter. Drain. Fry in really hot oil. Once the tofu is brownish, pour on two tablespoons of flour batter. Wait until it's slightly dry, pour over more flour batter. Do this up to 3 times.
Cook the tofu until golden brown. Once done, drain. Cook until all the tofu is used up.
While waiting for the tofu to cook. Prepare the sweet soy sambal. Slice all the sweet soy sambal ingredients. Put in a bowl, pour the sweet soy sauce over. And add the lime juice. Stir evenly.
Once the crispy Sumedang tofu is done. Serve with sweet soy sauce or chili sauce

🌷Cut the tofu into small squares (I cut one box of tofu into 4), then soak in salt water for about 30 minutes
🌷Mix all the coating ingredients, stir until evenly mixed
🌷Put the tofu into the coating then strain with a basket strainer
🌷And fry in hot oil until crispy..
🌷Remove and serve with chili sauce, sweet soy sambal, or if you're like me, just chomp on chilies on the side..

Prepare the Sumedang tofu. Mix all the flours and seasonings. Stir evenly.
Pour in water little by little, until the desired thickness. Coat the tofu with the flour batter.
Heat plenty of oil. Wait until hot. Fry the tofu until done. Remove and drain.
Serve while warm with bird's eye chilies.

Slice the shallots, chilies and tofu.
Sauté the shallots, chilies and bay leaves until wilted.
Then add the sliced tofu.
Season with sugar, salt and sweet soy sauce. Stir evenly.
Don't forget to adjust the taste, and then it's ready to serve.

Peel, trim, wash, and cut the carrots, green beans, and gembor chilies (make a slit at the tip without cutting all the way through).
Prepare the tofu and pork rind crackers. Bruise the lemongrass and galangal, then set them aside with the Indonesian bay leaves and lime leaves.
Blend all the ground spices, separate the liquid if necessary, then fry the spice mixture until fragrant and cooked. Add the lemongrass, galangal, and the remaining aromatic seasonings.
Once the spices are cooked, add the carrots and water. Bring to a boil.
Once boiling, add the green beans and cook briefly. Add the pork rind crackers and gembor chilies, then cook until tender.
Add the Sumedang tofu, season with salt and stock seasoning, and let the liquid reduce slightly so the flavors can absorb.
Finally, add FIBER CREME to make the dish richer and more delicious. I often use FIBER CREME as a substitute for coconut milk because it is rich in fiber, which is beneficial for health. Stir briefly and taste to adjust the seasoning. Remove from the heat.
Serve.

strMeal: Isi Piringku: Tahu Sumedang Masak Kuah   Ca Sawi Putih Telur
strInstructions:
Prepare the ingredients and ground spices.
Heat the cooking oil and sauté the ground spices until fragrant. Add the lemongrass, Indonesian bay leaf, and turmeric. Stir well, then add the tomato and stir again.
Add the water, salt, sweet soy sauce, coriander, and tofu. Cook until boiling. Taste and adjust the seasoning, then remove from the heat.
Serve with other side dishes. My Plate: Stir-Fried Napa Cabbage with Egg – Sumedang Tofu in Broth.
strIngredient1: Fried Sumedang tofu or brown tofu, cut into 4 pieces

strMeal: Isi Piringku: Ca Sawi Putih Telur   Tahu Sumedang Masak Kuah
strInstructions:
Prepare the ingredients. Scramble the eggs and set aside. Sauté the garlic, shallots, meatballs, and shredded beef until fragrant and the beef changes color. Add the firm parts of the napa cabbage and stir.
Add the firm parts of the napa cabbage again, stir, then add the seasonings, water, and red chili. Cook until boiling. Add the leafy parts of the napa cabbage and stir.
Add the scrambled eggs and mix well. Taste and adjust the seasoning, then remove from the heat. Serve with other dishes. I made a plate with one-third white rice, one-third Sumedang tofu in broth, and half a plate of stir-fried napa cabbage with egg. My Plate: Sumedang Tofu in Broth – Stir-Fried Napa Cabbage with Egg.
strIngredient7: Red chili, deseeded and thinly sliced

strInstructions:
Place the rice on a banana leaf, then roll it up while pressing it firmly. Secure both ends of the leaf with toothpicks. Set aside.
Next, prepare the side dishes. Grind the spices for braising, then put the cleaned chicken, tempeh, and tofu in a pot. Add coconut milk and the other seasonings. Cook until the coconut milk has reduced.
Drain and set aside.
Once drained, fry each ingredient, including the salted fish.
While preparing the fried side dishes, make the sayur asem. Prepare all the ingredients, grind the shallots and garlic with the peanuts, and bruise the galangal.
Bring the water to a boil and add the spices. Let them cook, then add the firmest vegetables first: melinjo fruit, corn, and chayote. When they are half-cooked, add the eggplant and stock seasoning.
Finally, add the melinjo leaves and long beans. Taste and adjust the seasoning, then remove from the heat and set aside.
Next, make the sambal. Prepare and wash all the ingredients, then fry them in hot oil (the same oil used to fry the chicken and other ingredients) until cooked. Transfer to a mortar and grind. Remember to add stock seasoning.
To serve, cut the banana-leaf-wrapped rice in half and arrange it on a plate with fried chicken, fried tofu, fried tempeh, and fresh vegetables. Serve with sayur asem and sambal.

✔️ Making Nasi Timbel: Prepare a sheet of banana leaf. Add 3–4 tablespoons of white rice, then roll it up like lontong. Secure with a toothpick.
✔️ Making Fried Tempeh and Tofu: Prepare the ground spices and pound them. Transfer to a container and add a little water. Coat the tempeh with the spice mixture and let it sit for 5–10 minutes.
Fry the tempeh until cooked.
Add 1 tablespoon of fried-fish seasoning and 1/2 teaspoon of salt to the remaining tempeh seasoning. Pour in a little water. Soak the tofu in the seasoning for about 10 minutes, then fry until cooked.
✔️ Prepare the fried chicken.
✔️ Making Sambal Terasi: Prepare all the sambal ingredients. Fry them in a little oil that has been preheated.
Transfer to a mortar. Add salt and palm sugar, then pound coarsely.
To serve, arrange the Nasi Timbel, side dishes, sambal, and fresh vegetables on a serving plate. Nasi Timbel is ready to serve 👍😍
strIngredient4: Block of tempeh, cut into pieces
strIngredient5: Ground spice mixture for tofu and tempeh
strIngredient26: Daun pisang utk membungkus nasi cara membersihkan daun pisang ☘️

strInstructions:
Wash the rice thoroughly. Red rice can be mixed with white rice if it turns out too dry and firm. If the red rice is naturally soft, there is no need to add white rice.
Cook the rice as usual. You can use slightly more water than you would for white rice. Let it finish cooking, then gently fluff and fold the rice so it becomes fluffier and does not stick together in a dense mass.
Take two banana leaves and place two scoops of rice, or as much as needed, on them.
Roll the leaves while pressing the rice firmly.
Press the rice firmly at both ends using a spoon or the blunt end of a spatula handle.
Neaten and close the ends of the roll.
Nasi Timbel is ready to pack for a picnic 😊 Serve with sambal, fresh vegetables, salted fish, pepes, fried jengkol, fried tofu and tempeh, and other side dishes of your choice.
For our health, let's replace synthetic 4P ingredients (sweeteners, preservatives, colorings, and flavorings) with natural alternatives. Here's how: SADARI — replace synthetic 4P ingredients with natural ones.

Wash the rice, then cook it with grated turmeric, lime juice, salt, cooking oil, pandan leaves, lemongrass, kaffir lime leaves, and Indonesian bay leaves. Cook until the rice is done, then remove from the heat. The lime juice helps the rice develop a bright, glossy color and keeps it from spoiling too quickly.
To wrap Nasi Timbel, wash the banana leaves and wipe them with a clean cloth. Warm them over a flame until pliable so they are easier to use for wrapping. Arrange the rice and side dishes on the leaves, roll them up, twist the ends, and fold them inward.
Brush the rice parcels with oil so they do not dry out while grilling. Grill until fragrant.
Sweet dried tempeh: Kering Tempe Manis.
Skipjack tuna: shredded skipjack tuna.
Serve the rice with sambal and fresh vegetables.

For the fried chicken, cut the chicken into four pieces and wash thoroughly. Grind all the spices except the whole aromatic seasonings (Indonesian bay leaves, lemongrass, and lime leaves). Sauté the ground spices, then add water and salt. Simmer the chicken in the seasoning until fully cooked. Once cooked, fry the chicken until golden brown.
For the sambal terasi, grind all the sambal ingredients except the Indonesian bay leaves and lime leaves. Sauté everything, then add the leaves and shrimp paste. Once the sambal has reduced and the liquid has evaporated, add the cooking oil. Season with flavor enhancer, sugar, and salt, then taste and adjust. Add the oil last to prevent splattering.
Heat the banana leaves over a flame until soft, but do not burn them. Fan the rice until it cools, then wrap it in banana leaves. The rice can last up to two days if it is cooked on the stove and the rice grains are washed thoroughly. Fry the tofu and tempeh, then serve the meal in a foam food container. Add fresh vegetables if desired.
strIngredient15: Red bird's eye chilies, about 10 or to taste
strIngredient17: Tomat 1 buah yg besar / sesuai selera
strIngredient20: Daun salam 3 lembat + daun jeruk 3 lembar

strMeal: Nasi Timbel Komplit Pasundan Ala Bubu
strInstructions:
Prepare the cooked white rice. Press it into a square mold, pack it firmly, then remove it onto a plate. Set aside.
Prepare the jengkol. Peel and slice it as desired, wash thoroughly, and drain. Heat oil in a pan. Once hot, add the jengkol.
Fry the jengkol until cooked, then remove.
Prepare the chicken and braise it with the ground spices until the liquid reduces and the seasoning is absorbed. Set aside.
Heat oil in a pan. Once hot, add the chicken that has been braised in yellow spices. Fry until golden.
Place the rice in the center of a plate, with the fried chicken and fried salted fish beside it.
Grind all the sambal ingredients. Taste and adjust the seasoning.
Pound the ingredients for the long-bean pencok, then combine with the sliced long beans and basil leaves. Mix well. Arrange the mixture on the plate with the rice, fried salted fish, fried chicken, sambal, and fried tofu. Place the fried jengkol and long-bean pencok around the edges. Serve with sliced cucumber. Ready to serve to your beloved family.
strIngredient8: Ground spice mixture for fried chicken

strMeal: Nasi Timbel Sambal Dadak Khas Sumedang (Sunda)
strInstructions:
Braise the chicken with water, Indonesian bay leaves, lemongrass, and the ground spices until tender. Heat the oil and fry the chicken until cooked. Remove and drain.
Braise the tofu with its ground spice mixture, then remove and drain. Fry the tofu until a skin forms. Fry the petai as well, then remove and drain.
Wash the sambal ingredients thoroughly, roast the shrimp paste, and coarsely pound the sambal.
Squeeze lime juice over it. Prepare banana leaves, place the rice on them, roll it up firmly, and secure both ends with toothpicks.
To serve, arrange the rice, fried chicken, and all the side dishes on a plate.

Wash the chicken thoroughly, coat it with lime juice, and let it sit for 15 minutes. Soak the salted fish in hot water for 10 minutes, then wash and drain it.
Braise the chicken with the ground spices until cooked, then fry it. Don't forget to fry the salted fish too; sorry, I didn't photograph that step.
To make Nasi Timbel, prepare the banana leaves and place the rice on them while it is still hot, as hot rice is easier to roll.
Twist one end of the leaf and tuck it inward, then stand the roll upright as shown in the steps. Repeat on the other side.
To serve, arrange the rice with fried chicken, salted fish, tofu, tempeh, fresh vegetables, and sambal terasi or your favorite sambal. Don't forget the sayur asem. Enjoy your meal!

Sauté the garlic and shallots until fragrant. Add enough water for the vegetables.
Add the corn and melinjo nuts first, then add the remaining vegetables to the water. Add the instant sayur asem seasoning and asam kandis. Season with salt to taste. The sayur asem is ready.
Fry the chicken, tempeh, and salted-fish crackers.
While waiting for the frying to finish, boil the chilies and tomato in a separate pan.
Once the frying and boiling are done, roast the shrimp paste until fragrant.
Drain the chilies and tomato.
Pound the chilies, tomato, and shrimp paste until slightly smooth, not too fine or too coarse.
Heat a little oil, then add the pounded sambal.
Arrange the rice, sayur asem, fried chicken, tempeh, salted-fish crackers, and sambal terasi on a plate. Nasi Timbel with chicken is ready to serve.

strMeal: Nasi Timbel, Tempe Bacem Panggang, Asin Dan Sambal Goreng Tomat
strInstructions:
First, prepare the Nasi Timbel. Clean the banana leaves and heat them over a stove flame until they become slightly glossy.
Shape the rice into a ball using a small bowl, wrap it in the prepared banana leaf, and let it sit for about an hour so the rice absorbs the leaf's aroma.
Next, prepare the tempeh bacem. Cut the tempeh into fairly thick slices so it does not break apart easily.
Grind the garlic, coriander, shallots, and candlenuts.
Heat the oil and sauté the ground spices until fragrant. Add the galangal, Indonesian bay leaves, and tamarind.
Add about 350 ml of water, then add the palm sugar and tempeh.
Add salt, pepper, and flavor enhancer. Taste and adjust the seasoning.
Cook over low heat. When the liquid starts to reduce, add sweet soy sauce to taste.
Once the seasoning thickens and the liquid has reduced, turn off the heat.
Heat a nonstick pan and brush it with a little oil. Grill the tempeh until browned.
Prepare the ingredients for the sambal.
Clean the garlic, tomato, and bird's eye chilies, then dry them with a paper towel. Cut the bird's eye chilies in half.
Heat a little oil and add the shrimp paste, tomato, and bird's eye chilies. Cook briefly, then remove and drain.
Put the garlic, shrimp paste, tomato, bird's eye chilies, and palm sugar in a mortar and pound until smooth.
Add salt, flavor enhancer, and pepper. Taste and adjust the seasoning.
Arrange the Nasi Timbel, tempeh bacem, and sambal on a plate. The meal is ready to enjoy.

Wash the rice thoroughly and add the water you would normally use to cook it. Set aside.
Sauté the anchovies until golden brown. Set aside.
Sauté the shallots, garlic, lemongrass, and Indonesian bay leaves. Set aside.
Add the sautéed anchovies and the other sautéed ingredients to the rice and water. If you want the rice to taste a little saltier, add salt to taste. However, if the anchovies are already salty, there is no need to add more salt.
Stir until evenly combined, then transfer to a rice cooker and cook as usual.
Rice-cooker Nasi Timbel is ready to enjoy.

Sambal Dadak: Pound the chilies, shallots, shrimp paste, mushroom stock powder, and granulated sugar until smooth.
Add the chopped tomato and pound again. Finally, add the juice of the lime and mix well.
Prepare the other side dishes: ✔️ Sayur Asem. ✔️ Fried tempeh, tofu, and salted fish. ✔️ Wash the fresh vegetables, including cucumber, basil leaves, and long beans. Spicy Sayur Asem.
Prepare warm white rice. Line a cone-shaped rice mold with banana leaves, then gradually fill it with rice, pressing it firmly as you go. Turn the rice out onto a serving plate and arrange the other side dishes around it.
Tumini, a traditional Sundanese Nasi Timbel dish, is ready to serve ♥️♥️.

Prepare the banana leaves and cut them to about the width of two adult handspans. Heat them over a medium stove flame until the surface becomes glossy. This softens the leaves and prevents them from tearing when rolled. Set aside and trim off the stiff parts.
Place the freshly cooked, still-hot rice on one side of a leaf. Roll it up slowly while pressing it firmly. It may be a little hot, but rolling the rice while it is hot makes it easier to shape. Once rolled, twist one end of the banana leaf.
