If the leaf is too long, trim it to about 3 cm at most. After twisting the end, tuck it inward toward the rice roll. Stand the roll upright with the tucked end at the bottom, then twist the top end as well.
Tuck the twisted top end into the rice. I make two Nasi Timbel rolls for two servings. Prepare the side dishes, especially sambal terasi, which is a must.
Also prepare assorted fresh vegetables, fried salted fish, fried tempeh, and fried chicken.

Fry the halved tomato, followed by the garlic, shallots, and chilies. Cook over medium heat until done. Remove, then pound until smooth and add salt.
Boil the spinach in the prepared water. Use about three handfuls of spinach. Add it to the boiling water and stir. Once it has softened slightly, remove and drain.
For the rice, place it in a small bowl to shape it, pressing it down a little so it holds together. Place the rice on a banana leaf and fold the leaf diagonally into a triangle until neatly wrapped. Turn it over so the smooth side faces up.
Arrange everything on a plate: rice, stir-fried wader fish, sambal terasi, and boiled spinach.
strIngredient1: Banana leaves, warmed over a flame
strIngredient2: Small bowl of stir-fried wader fish
strIngredient6: A handful of bird's eye chilies, add more for extra heat
strIngredient8: Large tomato and a little shrimp paste

strMeal: Nasi Timbel Bakar Isi Khas Sunda
strInstructions:
Put all the ingredients for the ground spice mixture into a blender or mortar and grind until smooth.
Fry the tempeh, anchovies, and petai separately.
Add a little oil to a pan and cook the ground spices. Add the galangal, Indonesian bay leaves, kaffir lime leaves, and lemongrass. Stir evenly until the sambal is cooked.
Once the sambal is cooked, add the fried tempeh, anchovies, and petai. Cook again until the seasoning is absorbed.
Before using the banana leaves, briefly heat them over a stove flame so they soften and become easier to fold.
Place the rice on the banana leaf, add the anchovy sambal on top, and wrap it.
Grill the Nasi Timbel over a stove flame or charcoal. Remove and serve while warm. Enjoy trying it 🤝 May Allah bless you.
strIngredient1: Ingredients for anchovy, tempeh, and petai sambal
strIngredient5: Ingredients for the ground spice mixture

strInstructions:
Boil the chicken, then cut it into pieces or shred it.
Slice the green chilies and mash the yellow tofu.
Sauté the chicken, yellow tofu, basil leaves, and green chilies. Add salt and flavor enhancer to taste. The more basil leaves you use, the better it tastes.
Prepare the banana leaves after drying and cleaning them. Spread the rice over the leaves, add the sautéed chicken mixture and boiled eggs, then roll the rice and fold both ends.
Steam the stuffed Nasi Timbel for about 30 minutes. It is ready to serve.

Wash the rice thoroughly, add a little water, then mix in the lemongrass, Indonesian bay leaf, and coconut milk. Cook in a rice cooker and set aside once done.
Sauté the ground spices until fragrant and their color changes, then add the toppings and sauté briefly.
Place the rice at one end of a banana leaf. Arrange the basil leaves on top, add the topping mixture, then sprinkle with crispy cleaned anchovies. Roll it up and secure with a toothpick, then grill until the leaf is slightly dry. Remove and serve.

Prepare the banana leaves, soften them, and cut them to the size of a dinner plate. Then prepare the rice. Wash the rice thoroughly, put it in the rice cooker, add water, and cook until done.
To cook the tofu, tempeh, and chicken, bring water to a boil and briefly boil the chicken, then discard the water. Grind the garlic, turmeric, and ginger until smooth. Put the chicken, tofu, tempeh, ground spices, bay leaves, lemongrass, salt, and powdered stock in a pan. Add enough water to cover everything. Cook for about 30 minutes until the water has reduced.
Fry the tofu, tempeh, and chicken until cooked.
To make the sambal, partially fry the shallots, tomatoes, bird's eye chilies, and curly red chilies. Drain them and transfer to a mortar. Add salt, sugar, shrimp paste, and aromatic ginger, then grind until smooth.
To make nasi timbel, place 2 tablespoons of rice on a banana leaf. Shape it into a firm bundle, then fold the leaf.
To serve, arrange the nasi timbel, aromatic ginger sambal, tofu, tempeh, fried chicken, and fresh vegetables on a plate. Enjoy!

strMeal: Nasi Timbel Ikan Goreng Khas Sunda
strInstructions:
Place clean banana leaves over the rice steamer until they soften.
Prepare the sambal ingredients. Wash them and briefly sauté them. Coarsely grind all the sambal ingredients.
Wrap warm, fluffy rice in banana leaves. Fry the carp, tofu, tempeh, and fresh anchovies. Wash and cut the fresh vegetables. Serve the nasi timbel with the accompaniments.
The fish, tofu, tempeh, and fresh anchovies are seasoned with salt only. I don't use shrimp paste or tomatoes in the sambal, unlike the usual Sundanese sambal, because I want the aromatic ginger and garlic flavors to stand out, like Tasikmalaya-style sambal goang.
strIngredient10: Red and green bird's eye chilies

strMeal: Nasi Timbel Teri Medan Rice Cooker
strInstructions:
Sauté the shallots, garlic, and lemongrass until the onions begin to soften.
Add the galangal, bay leaves, and Medan anchovies. Sauté until the anchovies are halfway dry.
Turn off the heat, then add the washed rice to the pan. Add salt, seasoning, and pepper, then mix well.
Transfer the seasoned rice to the rice cooker. Add water using the usual amount for cooking rice, press the cook button, and wait until done.

Prepare the ingredients. Wash the fish, coat it with salt and lime juice, and let it sit for 5 minutes, then rinse thoroughly.
Grind the spices and divide them into 3 portions: one for the fish, one for the tofu and tempeh, and one for brushing onto the grilled fish. Coat the fish with the seasoning and set aside to let the flavors absorb.
To make the sambal, fry the chilies, garlic, and shrimp paste, then grind them. Add salt and palm sugar, taste, and adjust the texture to your preference.
Fry the tofu and tempeh using the same seasoning.
Fry the fish, then grill it. I use a nonstick pan brushed with margarine. Brush the fish with the reserved third of the seasoning mixed with sweet soy sauce and cooking oil. Grill both sides, then remove from the heat.
Wrap the rice by placing it on a banana leaf, rolling it up, twisting the ends, and pushing them inward.
Arrange the rice and accompaniments on a serving plate, with the rice wrapped as shown in the photo.
strIngredient3: Yellow tofu or any type of tofu
strIngredient22: Daun kemangi (sy tdk pake diganti pete )

strInstructions:
A. Steps 1–5: Making nasi timbel. First, prepare the ingredients.
Wash the rice thoroughly, then add water to about one finger joint above the rice. Arrange the lemongrass, kaffir lime leaves, whole shallots, whole garlic cloves, and bay leaves on top.
Cook until the water has evaporated. Turn off the heat and keep the lid tightly closed for 2 minutes.
Take a banana leaf and wrap the rice like lontong.
Heat the steamer and steam until cooked, about 25 minutes.
Steps 6–10: Making anchovy and stink bean sambal. Prepare the ingredients.
Thinly slice the ingredients and keep the shallots, garlic, kaffir lime leaves, stink beans, and chilies separate.
First, fry the stink beans until crisp. Set aside.
Fry the shallots, garlic, kaffir lime leaves, and chilies until crisp. Set aside.
Finally, fry the anchovies until crisp, drain them, then mix with the shallots, garlic, stink beans, and chilies. Set aside.
Steps 11–15: Making the sambal. Prepare the ingredients.
Briefly boil all the ingredients in boiling water for just 1–2 minutes.
Drain and grind with shrimp paste, sugar, and salt. Set aside.
To serve, add various side dishes and fresh vegetables for a complete meal, as shown here.
Alternatively, for a simple meal to take on a trip, serve a whole nasi timbel with anchovies, stink beans, and sambal. To help the sambal keep longer, fry it after grinding, then store it in a sealed container.
strIngredient9: B. Anchovy and stink bean mixture

strInstructions:
Prepare warm rice and wrap it in leaves.
To make the beef semur, boil the beef until tender. While it boils, grind the coriander, candlenuts, 4 shallots, 2 garlic cloves, and red chilies. Heat a pan and sauté the ground spices. Add the beef, powdered stock, ground pepper, and salt. Add a little of the cooking broth and sweet soy sauce, then simmer until tender.
To make the fried potato sambal, wash the chopped potatoes and fry them. Grind 3 shallots, 2 garlic cloves, red chilies, and candlenuts. Sauté the ground spices and add powdered stock, ground pepper, and salt.
To make the green chili stir-fry, clean the green chilies and slit them lengthwise. Sauté ground spices made from 3 shallots and 2 garlic cloves. Add a little water, then add the chilies, a little stock powder, and salt.
To make cimlo, peel the carrots and cut them into matchsticks. Soak the rice vermicelli. Grind garlic, shallots, and candlenuts, then sauté with stock powder, ground pepper, and a little salt.
Fry the yellow tofu until dry, and slice the cucumber.
Serve the rice wrapped in leaves on a plate, arranging the cimlo, fried tofu, beef semur, fried potato sambal, green chili stir-fry, and cucumber slices alongside it.

strMeal: Lontong Cap Go Meh Versi Simple, All In 1
strInstructions:
Grind the shallots, garlic, candlenuts, turmeric, coriander, chilies, and dried shrimp.
Prepare an Asta Homeware pan. Add oil and heat it. Sauté the ground spices until fragrant. Add the lemongrass, bay leaves, and galangal.
Add the chicken and cook until its color changes.
Pour in the water and cook until the chicken is tender.
Add the chayote and cook for 3–4 minutes.
Add the tofu and long beans, then stir well.
Season with Garam Cap Kapal salt and shaved palm sugar.
Finally, pour in the Rose Brand coconut milk, stir well, cook briefly, and remove from the heat. Serve with accompaniments.
strIngredient3: Long beans, cut into 3 cm pieces
strIngredient4: Tofu, cut diagonally into 2 pieces and fried

strInstructions:
Wash the chicken and briefly fry it to remove the slippery residue from the skin.
Grind the spices and sauté until fragrant. Add the chicken briefly and stir, then add water and coconut milk. Cook until the chicken is done and the sauce thickens to make opor ayam.
Sauté the ground spices for the chayote vegetable dish until fragrant. Add coconut milk and stir until combined, then add 3 cups of water.
Wash the chayote, stink beans, and tofu, then add them to the pot.
Add sugar, salt, and stock powder. Cook until done, then serve.
Fry the potatoes and chicken liver and gizzards after soaking them in salted water. Fry until golden and cooked.
Sauté the ground spices and adjust the seasoning. Add the potatoes and liver, stir well, then add thin coconut milk and a little water. Cook until the liquid has evaporated, then serve the fried liver sambal.
Cut the lontong into pieces and serve with the chayote vegetable dish, opor, and fried liver sambal. Lontong Cap Go Meh is ready to enjoy.
strIngredient33: Bumbu sambal goreng kentang dan hati

strMeal: Bubuk Kedelai Pelengkap Lontong Cap Go Meh
strInstructions:
Prepare the fried soybeans with garlic and kaffir lime leaves.
Put them in a blender and add granulated sugar.
Blend until smooth.
Sift through a strainer.
The soybean powder is ready to serve as a topping. Store it in an airtight jar.
strIngredient1: Fried soybeans with garlic and kaffir lime leaves

strMeal: Lontong Cap Go Meh Khas Banjar
strInstructions:
Chayote vegetable dish: Heat oil in a pan. Sauté the ground spices, galangal, and bay leaves until fragrant. Add the chayote and stir well.
Pour in water and bring to a boil. Add the long beans and cook until all the ingredients are done. Pour in the coconut milk, stir well, and remove from the heat.
For the masak habang recipe, I used the attached recipe. I only cooked eggs, without fish or chicken. This is a Banjar yellow rice meal package.
Arrange the lontong in a serving bowl, add the eggs and crispy potato garnish, then pour the chayote vegetable dish over them. Sprinkle with fried shallots and serve.

strMeal: Lontong Cap Go Meh Khas Surabaya
strInstructions:
Prepare the lontong using the Lontong Praktis recipe.
If lontong is unavailable, you can use ketupat instead.
Prepare all the seasonings.
Once everything is cooked, take a plate and assemble the lontong sayur with your choice of side dishes. Enjoy!
strIngredient2: Lontong, using the Lontong Praktis recipe
strIngredient3: Large bowl of petis lading with 10 eggs, a Surabaya specialty
strIngredient4: Pot of chicken curry with 10 pieces of chicken
strIngredient5: Pot of chayote vegetable dish or sambal goreng labu siam
strIngredient6: Small pot of bamboo shoot vegetable dish, as a substitute for chayote if unavailable

strMeal: Lontong Cap Go Meh Ala Dapur Kana
strInstructions:
Lontong: Wash the rice thoroughly, then take enough to fill banana leaves. Fill each leaf about two-thirds full and secure the ends with small bamboo pins. Arrange the parcels in a pressure cooker and add plenty of water until all the uncooked lontong is submerged. Add 1 tablespoon of salt. Pressure-cook for 1 hour.
Fried liver and gizzard sambal: Boil the liver and gizzards, then briefly fry them. Slice thinly. Slice the chilies diagonally, boil until softened, drain, and roughly crush them. Grind the shallots and garlic. Bruise the galangal and crush the bay leaves by hand. Sauté the shallots, garlic, bay leaves, and galangal until fragrant. Add the chilies and stir-fry until their moisture evaporates. Add a little water, then add the liver and gizzards, thinly sliced stink beans, and coconut milk. Season with salt, seasoning, and sugar. Cook until the liquid reduces.
Fried bamboo shoot sambal: Boil the bamboo shoots until tender, then slice them into thin strips. Sauté the bay leaves, bruised galangal, ground shallots and garlic, and ground chilies. Add the bamboo shoots and stir-fry until coated with the spices. Add stink beans, shrimp, and enough water, but not too much. Season with salt, seasoning, and sugar. Cook until the spices are absorbed into the bamboo shoots. Finally, add coconut milk and cook until it boils again.
Opor ayam: Grind all the spices and sauté until fragrant. Add the chicken and stir-fry until its color changes and it is evenly coated with the spices. Pour in about 2 L of water. Add salt, sugar, seasoning, and pepper. Cook until the chicken is tender. Add more water if too much has evaporated. Add 2 sachets of coconut milk and cook until it boils again.
Vegetable lodeh: Slice the shallots, garlic, and chilies. Add the chopped long beans and eggplant, followed by the onions, chilies, galangal, and bay leaves. Add about 1 L of water and cook until the vegetables are done. Add coconut milk and wait for it to boil again. Adjust the seasoning.
Pindang eggs: Boil and peel the eggs. Cook them with sweet soy sauce, bruised galangal, bay leaves, tamarind, palm sugar, and water until the eggs turn brown and the liquid reduces.
Sate Abeng seasoning: Grind the toasted grated coconut until it releases its oil. Cook it with 1/2 glass of water or broth from the opor. Add palm sugar, lemongrass, bay leaves, and salt. Cook until thickened.
Arrange on a plate: lontong, opor ayam (cut into pieces or shredded), fried bamboo shoot sambal, fried liver and gizzard sambal, lodeh, pindang eggs, Sate Abeng seasoning, and soybean powder.
strIngredient5: Fried chicken liver and gizzard sambal
strIngredient6: Pairs of chicken liver and gizzards
strIngredient19: Rebung , rebus lalu iris korek api

strInstructions:
Heat the butter and sauté the shallots, garlic, galangal, lemongrass, bay leaves, and kaffir lime leaves until fragrant.
Add water, then add the chayote and boiled, peeled quail eggs. Season with shrimp stock, pepper, salt, palm sugar, and tomato sauce.
Once boiling, add the parsley and thick coconut milk. Stir gently until cooked.
Serve with lontong, ketupat, or compressed rice cut into pieces as desired.
strIngredient1: Chayote, peeled and grated with a vegetable grater
strIngredient3: Homemade tomato sauce for baby food

strMeal: Opor Ayam (Untuk Lontong Cap Go Meh)
strInstructions:
Sauté the ground spices in oil, then add the powdered spices and whole spices. Cook until the moisture evaporates and the oil separates, indicating that the spices are fully cooked.
Add the chicken and mix until all the pieces are coated with the spices. Add about 1 L of water, season with salt, sugar, pepper, and Toto­le to taste, and boil until the chicken is cooked. Once the chicken is done, continue simmering until the broth reaches your desired volume. For a thicker broth, leave about 500 ml.
Add the coconut milk and fried shallots. Stir to prevent the coconut milk from splitting, then bring to a boil once more. Adjust the seasoning to taste. Turn off the heat when everything tastes right. The opor is ready to serve.

Cut the tofu into cubes and fry it. Briefly fry the ground spices to remove their raw smell. Cut the chayote into julienne strips and soak briefly in salted water.
Grind the spices and sauté until fragrant. Add the bay leaves, kaffir lime leaves, galangal, ginger, and lemongrass. Add the chicken and cook until its color changes. Add half the water and simmer over low heat until the chicken is tender and the water has reduced.
Add the remaining water, tofu, chayote, and the other seasonings. Cook until the chayote is tender, then add the coconut milk.
Cook briefly and taste to adjust the seasoning.
strIngredient2: Chicken thighs, cut into small pieces

strInstructions:
Wash the beef thoroughly, then boil it in a pot for 5 minutes. Strain it or discard the water if it is too fatty. Pressure-cook the beef again with its broth, adding the whole spices: lemongrass, bay leaves, kaffir lime leaves, cinnamon, and tamarind water. Cook until the beef is done, then remove the beef and continue cooking the broth. Add more water if needed.
Heat Rose Brand cooking oil and add the ground spices, followed by the ground dry spices.
Sauté until fully cooked, then add the mixture to the beef broth. Strain in the rice water made by blending rice with water.
Once the broth boils again, season with salt, beef stock powder, Asatu Rose Brand MSG, Rose Brand granulated sugar, and sweet soy sauce.
Beat the eggs, then pour them into the broth while stirring quickly so the eggs form strands instead of clumps. Taste and adjust the seasoning, then remove from the heat.
Garnish with spring onions, celery leaves, and fried shallots. Arrange sliced beef in a bowl with rice vermicelli and potato fritters (I skipped the fritters). Sprinkle with spring onions, celery, and fried shallots, then add sweet soy sauce, sambal, and lime. Enjoy with hot rice.
strIngredient8: Rice water made by blending 50 g of rice and straining it
strIngredient15: Lemongrass, use the white part and bruise the ends
strIngredient31: Bisa juga dikukus jika ingin disimpan lama

strInstructions:
Heat the prepared Sop Saudara broth, then add the tofu skin and wait until it softens.
Add the squid-shaped tofu and kwetiau noodles. Wait until they are cooked and have expanded.
Add the enoki mushrooms, then remove from the heat.

strMeal: Sop Daging Kuah Susu Ala Sop Kaki Kambing Tiga Saudara
strInstructions:
Boil the beef ribs with 2 bay leaves, 2 kaffir lime leaves, and 1 bruised lemongrass stalk in boiling water for about 1 hour. I use a regular pot.
Once tender or cooked to your preference, remove and drain the ribs. Set aside the cooking broth in a separate container.
Sauté the ground spices. I sauté them directly in the pot to avoid transferring them between containers.
Add all the aromatic ingredients and cook until fragrant and fully cooked.
Add the milk and about 300 ml of the rib broth. Bring to a boil, then add the soup greens either to the pot or separately when serving.
To serve, cut the tomatoes, spring onions, and ribs as desired. Add ghee to taste; I use 1/2 tablespoon. Pour the hot soup over everything.
Enjoy with warm rice, sprinkled with fried shallots, lime, and melinjo crackers.
strIngredient1: Beef ribs (or a mix of 250 g beef liver and 250 g beef; other proteins such as goat, tripe, tendon, brain, tongue, or lungs can also be used)
strIngredient4: Wisman ghee for each serving, or margarine

strInstructions:
Pressure-cook the whole beef with the whole spices (bay leaves, kaffir lime leaves, cinnamon, lemongrass, and galangal) until tender. Set aside and cut into pieces.
Reheat the beef broth and add water as needed. Meanwhile, sauté the ground spices until fragrant and thoroughly cooked, then add them to the broth. Bring to a boil and cook until done. Season with sugar, salt, and Royco, then adjust to taste. Slowly pour in the eggs mixed with water while stirring, then add the spring onions. Cook briefly and turn off the heat.
Serve the beef and broth with the accompaniments.
strIngredient12: Eggs mixed with 200 ml water and beaten
strIngredient32: Sambal ( rawit & bawang putih di rebus

strInstructions:
Cut all the ingredients into spoon-sized pieces, not too large, so each spoonful can contain a little of everything.
Bring the water to a boil and add the chopped ingredients.
Add the seasonings gradually. Taste the broth to check whether it needs more salt, but be careful not to burn your tongue!
Wait until everything is cooked, and that's it! Easy, right?
strIngredient6: Fish balls and kani sticks, if available
strIngredient14: Spring onions and coriander leaves, used because celery was unavailable
strIngredient15: Optional leftover ingredient, added to avoid waste

strInstructions:
Boil the beef lungs with 2 crushed garlic cloves, 1 tbsp salt, 1 bay leaf, and 1/2 tsp ground pepper until tender. Remove, slice thinly, and fry until crispy or to your liking. Set aside.
Boil the beef liver in the remaining lung broth until tender. Remove and cut into cubes. Set aside.
Blend all the ground spices with 300 ml water, except for the fried peanuts. Strain the mixture and set aside.
Blend the fried peanuts with the remaining strained spice liquid.
Heat oil in a pan. Add the ground spices, blended peanuts, cloves, cinnamon, sliced onion, and fried shallots. Sauté until fragrant.
Prepare 6 L of water in a pot. Add the whole beef, sautéed spices, bay leaves, kaffir lime leaves, cloves, crushed galangal, 1 tbsp salt, and beaten eggs. Cook until the beef is tender.
Remove the tender beef and cut it into cubes. Set aside.
Season the broth with salt, granulated sugar, and seasoning. Taste and adjust.
To serve, arrange glass noodles, fried beef lungs, diced beef liver, diced beef, sliced spring onions, sliced celery, and potato patties in a bowl. Pour the soup over them and sprinkle with fried shallots. Serve with rice or ketupat. Enjoy!
strIngredient6: Kaffir lime leaves, remove the center veins
strIngredient24: Cabe merah besar, rebus, buang bijinya

strInstructions:
Bring water to a boil and cook the beef until tender. Skim off the floating fat and foam until the broth is clear. Leave about 750 ml of broth.
Prepare the other ingredients and grind all the ground spices.
Heat cooking oil in a nonstick pan or wok. Sauté the ground spices until fragrant. Add the sliced spices and mix well. Cook until the spices are done, then turn off the heat.
Bring the beef broth to a boil again. Add the sautéed spices and stir well. Add salt, cinnamon, granulated sugar, and powdered stock. Mix well and taste. Finally, add the tomatoes and spring onions. Cook for 1 minute, then turn off the heat.
Prepare the accompaniments.
To serve, place glass noodles in a bowl and add celery and fried shallots. Pour in the soup and beef. Add sambal and lime juice.
Serve while warm.
strIngredient27: Sesuai selera perkedel (saya 3 buah ) perkedel kentang

strInstructions:
Prepare the ingredients.
Boil the beef until tender. Do not discard the cooking water; it will be used for the soup broth.
Chop the fresh spices and fry them. Toast the dry spices.
Grind all the fresh and dry spices.
Cut the beef into pieces of your preferred size and return it to the broth.
Add the whole spices and ground spice mixture.
Season with salt, sugar, powdered stock, and tamarind water. Pour in the beaten egg and taste to adjust the seasoning. Once the flavor is right, serve with the accompaniments.
Serve with your preferred accompaniments. The video version can be found at https://youtu.be/4c8eyYIcbNQ.
strIngredient3: Egg mixed with a little water

strMeal: Sop Saudara Ayam Khas Bugis Makassar
strInstructions:
Heat oil and sauté the ground spices, bay leaves, kaffir lime leaves, cinnamon, and cloves until fragrant. Turn off the heat.
Add the egg and stir quickly until it forms fine scrambled strands. Add the chicken and let it cook briefly until its color changes.
Add the coconut milk, water, salt, powdered stock, palm sugar, and tamarind water. Stir well and continue cooking until the chicken is completely tender.
Place glass noodles in a bowl and pour the Sop Saudara soup over them.
Serve with fried shallots, chilies, lime, and optional potato patties.

Pressure-cook the beef with water, bay leaves, kaffir lime leaves, and 1 lemongrass stalk for about 30–40 minutes.
Once the beef is cooked, cut it into cubes. Use the cooking liquid as the soup broth.
Sauté the ground spices with additional bay leaves, kaffir lime leaves, and lemongrass until fragrant and the raw smell disappears.
Add the sautéed spices to the broth. Add the cinnamon and blended peanuts, then stir well.
Season with salt, beef seasoning, and powdered stock. Taste and adjust, then let the soup come to a boil.
Arrange glass noodles, spring onions, potato patties, fried beef lungs, and salted eggs in bowls. Add the beef and pour in the soup. Sprinkle with fried shallots and serve with melinjo crackers. Enjoy warm with family.
strIngredient7: Peanuts, toasted with skins on and blended

strMeal: Sop Saudara Rasa Ayam Kacang Merah
strInstructions:
Prepare the ingredients and spices. Boil the red kidney beans until tender, then drain. Boil the chicken in 1.5 L water.
Sauté the ground spices with the kaffir lime leaves, lemongrass, and ginger until cooked and fragrant. Add the mixture to the chicken broth.
Add salt, sugar, stock, and cinnamon. Taste and adjust the seasoning. Add the spring onions and tomato, then turn off the heat.
Prepare all the accompaniments. To serve, arrange glass noodles, mushrooms, red kidney beans, and chicken in a bowl, then pour the soup over them.
Serve immediately.

strMeal: Sop Kambing Tiga Saudara (Ala Abang Abang)
strInstructions:
Prepare all the ingredients. Do not discard the third batch of broth from boiling the goat meat and offal; leave it in the pot. The first and second boiling steps are described in the recipe story.
Bring the third batch of broth to a boil while grinding the spices.
Sauté the spices until fragrant, then add them to the broth along with the thin coconut milk.
Simmer the thin coconut milk for about 10 minutes, stirring occasionally. Add the thick coconut milk and stir continuously to prevent it from splitting. Taste and adjust the seasoning, then add the roughly chopped spring onions.
Ready to serve! If you love goat meat but dislike its strong smell, give this a try. It's really delicious.
strIngredient2: Goat offal, cut into small pieces
strIngredient3: Coconut for making thick and thin coconut milk
strIngredient5: Spring onion, chopped into pieces about half a finger long
strIngredient22: Margarin saat penyajian dimangkuk. (aslinya pakai samin)
strIngredient27: Acar ( ketimun + wortel + cabe rawit secukupnya) acar ketimun & wortel

strInstructions:
Place the chicken wings in a bowl and add all the seasonings. Mix until evenly coated, then marinate overnight in the refrigerator so the flavors can absorb.
After marinating overnight, steam the wings for 15–20 minutes. Do not line the steamer, so the steam can drip down.
Once cooked, let the wings cool. They can now be stored, fried, or cooked in an air fryer.
To fry, cook the wings in hot oil over medium heat so they do not burn. Alternatively, air-fry at 170°C for 10 minutes.
Spicy chicken wings are ready to serve.

strMeal: Roti Isi Ayam Teriyaki (Tanpa Ulen Tanpa Telur)
strInstructions:
Prepare the required ingredients. In a bowl, combine the milk, yeast, and granulated sugar. Mix well and let sit for 8–10 minutes until foamy.
Add half the flour. Add the salt and mix well. Pour in the melted margarine and mix.
Add the remaining flour and mix until no dry flour remains.
Cover with a clean cloth or plastic wrap and let rise for 1 hour. After 1 hour, punch down the dough, cover again, and refrigerate overnight. This is useful if you want fresh bread early in the morning: prepare the dough at night, then shape and bake it in the morning. Refrigerate for no more than 12 hours.
Grease the work surface and your hands with oil or margarine. Punch down the risen dough. Divide and shape it for your preferred bread variations. After weighing the portions, shape them into balls, cover with a clean cloth, and rest for 10–15 minutes. This is called a bench rest and makes the dough easier to shape.
Prepare the teriyaki chicken filling using the attached recipe. Flatten one portion of dough, make cuts along both sides, and place some teriyaki chicken in the center. Fold the strips over the filling in a crisscross pattern, as shown in the picture.
Brush with egg yolk and bake until cooked and golden brown. The teriyaki chicken bread is ready to serve.
strIngredient9: Chicken breast fillet for teriyaki chicken

strMeal: Gulai Ayam Kojo Khas Sumatera Selatan
strInstructions:
Wash the chicken thoroughly, squeeze lime juice over it, and let it sit for 10 minutes. Rinse again and drain. Prepare the spices and blend them until smooth.
Heat oil in a pan and sauté the ground spices until fragrant and cooked. Add the lemongrass and curry leaves, then stir-fry until the curry leaves wilt. Add the chicken and cook until it shrinks. Pour in the coconut milk and water, stirring regularly until the coconut milk boils to prevent it from splitting.
Once the chicken begins to soften, add salt, tamarind water, and mushroom stock. Continue cooking until the chicken is tender.
The chicken gulai is ready to serve.

Marinate the chicken with the packaged seasonings: coriander, mushroom stock, garlic powder, and ground pepper. Let sit until the flavors are absorbed.
Fry the chicken for about 12 minutes, or until lightly golden brown. Do not brown it too much, as it will be stir-fried again later. Remove once cooked.
Thinly slice the onions and chilies.
Add the shrimp paste first, then the garlic. Add the shallots and fry until lightly browned like fried onions, then add the chilies. Add the cooked chicken and more powdered stock.

Wash the chicken and cut it into 2 x 2 cm pieces. Mix with the marinade, ground pepper, powdered stock, palm sugar, and coconut milk until evenly combined. Refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Wash the pandan leaves. Wrap the chicken by positioning the back of the leaf facing forward, then fold it with the tip longer than the base. Insert the tip into the opening, add the chicken, then pull the leaf tip through and tuck it in. Neaten both ends. Repeat until all the chicken is wrapped.
Heat oil in a pan and fry the chicken over low to medium heat. Turn it only once. Fry for about 10 minutes until cooked. Serve hot with Bangkok chili sauce for dipping. Enjoy!

Clean the chicken, remove the skin, and cut it into 10 pieces or to your preference.
Simmer the chicken with the blended ungkep spices. Add salt and enough water to cook until tender. Drain.
Fry the chicken until golden brown, then drain.
Sauté the shallots until fragrant. Add the sliced tomatoes and spring onions, and sauté until softened. Add the coarsely ground chilies and salt to taste. Cook until done and adjust the seasoning.
Add the fried chicken and mix well. Serve.
strIngredient1: Chicken, cut into small skinless pieces

strInstructions:
Wash the chicken wings, cut them in half, soak them in salted water, then rinse thoroughly and drain. Prick the wings with a fork.
Put all the seasonings in a bowl and mix well. Pour the sauce over the wings and rub it in until evenly coated.
Arrange the seasoned wings in a container and refrigerate or freeze overnight so the flavors can fully absorb.
Cook as many wings as needed in an air fryer at 200°C for 25 minutes.
The barbecue chicken wings are ready to serve.

Wash the chicken skin and remove the fat. Coat with lime juice and let sit for 10 minutes, then rinse thoroughly.
Mix with the marinade ingredients. Refrigerate for 2 hours.
In a bowl, combine the dry coating ingredients: flour, rice flour, tapioca flour, salt, baking powder, powdered stock, and pepper. Mix evenly.
Coat the chicken skin evenly in the dry mixture. Do not make the coating too thick; just make sure it is evenly covered.
Heat a generous amount of oil in a pan over medium heat. Fry the chicken skin until golden brown, then drain.
Serve with sambal.

Thinly slice the chicken roulade and grill until dry and smoky, turning it so it does not burn.
Prepare the tortilla and fill it with lettuce.
Add cucumber, tomato, and sliced chicken roulade.
Add mayonnaise and tomato sauce, then top with a slice of quick-melt cheese.
Fold the kebab from the bottom, then fold in the right and left sides. Grill in a pan with a little margarine, turning until the entire tortilla is golden brown.
The chicken roulade kebab is ready to serve. It makes a great snack at home or a packed lunch for children.

Prepare ready-to-use wonton wrappers.
In a bowl, combine all the filling ingredients. Add the egg, tapioca flour, salt, ground pepper, seasoning, granulated sugar, sesame oil, and oyster sauce. Mix until everything is evenly combined.
Place about 1 tbsp of filling on each wonton wrapper, then pinch or fold it as desired. Repeat until the filling is used up.
Heat cooking oil and add the prepared wontons. Turn them so they cook evenly until golden brown. Remove and drain.
Serve the fried wontons with chili sauce or tomato sauce.

Wash and cut the chicken fillet, then chop it in a food processor or grind it.
Grate the carrot and add all the seasonings and other ingredients.
Prepare a steamer and heat it. Take a spoonful of the mixture, add cheese, and fold it closed.
You can also make chicken cheese bites without steaming: refrigerate them, coat with breadcrumbs, and fry.
Grease the steamer, arrange the wrapped dim sum inside, and steam for 20 minutes. Remove and fry when ready.

Heat oil and sauté the ground spices until fragrant. Add the whole spices and sauté again until cooked. Add the chicken and stir until coated with the spices and the chicken changes color and releases its juices. Add enough water to cover all the chicken.
Add the eggs and aromatic spices, then cook until boiling.
Add the Rose Brand coconut milk, salt, and Asatu MSG.
Cook until the chicken is tender and the spices have absorbed into it. Stir occasionally to prevent the coconut milk from splitting. Taste and adjust the seasoning.
Serve.

Wash the chicken thoroughly, coat it with lime juice and salt, and let it sit for 15 minutes. Rinse with clean water and drain. Grind the chicken spices, leaving out the bay leaves and lemongrass.
Coat the chicken with the spices and water, then simmer until cooked and the spices have dried. Set aside. Heat oil in a pan and fry the chicken until golden brown, not too crispy. Set aside.
For the sweet soy sauce mixture, thinly slice the garlic and fry it. Fry the peanuts until cooked, then coarsely grind them. Thinly slice the green chilies diagonally.
Finely grind the fried garlic, salt, and bird's eye chilies. Transfer to a bowl and mix with sweet soy sauce, lime juice, peanuts, and green chilies. Mix well and adjust the seasoning.
To serve, arrange the chicken on a plate and pour the sweet soy sauce mixture over it. The sweet soy chicken is ready to serve.

Blend all the dough ingredients until smooth, then shape into balls using a spoon or according to your preference.
Thinly slice the wonton wrappers. Place each dough ball on top of the sliced wrappers, then evenly cover the entire surface.
Once all the balls are coated, you can store them in the freezer or fry them immediately.
To fry, use enough oil to fully submerge the balls. Cook over low heat so the wrappers do not burn easily and the filling cooks thoroughly. Make sure the oil is hot before adding them.

Cut the chicken into pieces, then briefly boil it until foam appears. Discard the water.
Toast the pepper, cumin, cloves, and star anise.
Blend the cumin, pepper, candlenuts, garlic, shallots, red chilies, bird's eye chilies, and tomato until smooth.
Heat the oil, then add the blended spices, cloves, star anise, Indonesian bay leaves, and lemongrass.
Add the chicken and water, stir, then cover and simmer until the spices are absorbed.
Add salt, sugar, and Masako seasoning, then adjust the taste.
Next, add the coconut milk.
Serve the chicken rendang warm.

Prepare the ingredients. Mix all the seasonings and stir well.
Place a sheet of plastic wrap on a surface, add 1/2 tsp oil, and spread it evenly. Add 1 tsp of the mixture, insert a satay skewer, and shape it into a long, flat form. Wrap it with some uncooked noodles.
Fry over low heat.
Serve.

Prepare the ingredients. Chop the scallions and garlic, then sauté until softened and fragrant.
Grind the chicken in a food processor. Add the scallions and garlic, then process again until evenly combined.

Melt the butter and cook the chicken in it until all sides are fully cooked.
In a bowl, mix the mayonnaise, milk, teriyaki sauce, oyster sauce, and salt until well combined.
Once both sides of the chicken are cooked, pour in the prepared sauce.
Turn the chicken over until it is fully coated in the sauce.
Add oregano and parsley, cook briefly, and serve.

Boil the chicken until cooked. Drain, let it cool, then shred it.
Heat the oil, add the sliced aromatics, and sauté until fragrant.
Add the coarsely pounded chilies and sauté until the spices are cooked.
Add water and seasonings. Bring the broth to a boil, then add the shredded chicken and stir. Adjust the seasoning to taste.
Stir the shredded chicken until evenly coated and cook until the liquid reduces. Add the basil leaves and sliced chilies.
Stir briefly, turn off the heat, and serve with steamed white rice.

Cut the chicken into pieces and marinate with flour, salt, and ground pepper.
Fry the chicken in a little oil until golden brown, then drain.
In the same pan, add oil and sauté the minced garlic until fragrant.
Add the milk, cream cheese, pepper, seasoning powder, and salt.
Once everything is combined and seasoned to taste, add the chicken to the sauce. Cook for about 4 minutes until the sauce begins to thicken and coat the chicken.

Cut the chicken as desired and marinate with oyster sauce, brown sugar, pepper, paprika powder, and soy sauce for about 30 minutes.
Coat the chicken with flour and fry it like fried chicken (I use ready-made seasoned flour).
Fry until golden and crispy, then set aside briefly.
Chop the shallots, garlic, chilies, and scallion stalks.
Sauté until fragrant, then add salt and stock powder.
Add the torch ginger flower, fried chicken, and scallions.

Blend the chicken, shrimp, and all the other ingredients in a food processor.
Shape the mixture into small balls; do not make them too large.
Heat a little water in a non-stick pan and add the balls.
Cover each ball with a small dumpling wrapper.
Cover the pan and cook until done. Add more water if needed.
Once cooked, let the remaining water evaporate so the bottoms of the dumplings become crispy.
Remove and serve warm with chili oil.

Cut the chicken into small pieces, then marinate it with tamarind water, a little salt, and pepper. Let it sit for about 10 minutes.
Blend the spice paste. Add approximately 5 tbsp of oil to make blending easier.
Heat 1 tbsp of oil and sauté the spice paste until fragrant. Add the lemongrass and kaffir lime leaves. Continue sautéing until the paste is cooked.
Add the chicken along with its marinade.
Add the seasonings and taste to adjust.
Add water and cook for about 30 minutes until the liquid reduces.
Ready to serve.

strMeal: Ayam Goreng Kecap Dengan Selada Air
strInstructions:
Fry the chicken until cooked and the skin is crispy.
Drizzle sweet soy sauce over the fried chicken on a serving plate.
Sauté the shallots and chilies until fragrant. Add the water spinach, stir well, and season with salt.
Serve the sweet soy fried chicken, sautéed water spinach, and white rice together on one plate.

strMeal: (Sourdough Discard) Pizza Ayam Kecap   Ulen Tangan
strInstructions:
Mix the all-purpose flour, sourdough discard, instant yeast, granulated sugar, and water.
Stir until evenly combined. You can reduce or add water from the stated amount as needed.
Add the oil and salt, then knead until smooth and elastic. It does not need to pass the windowpane test; the dough should simply be flexible enough and no longer stick to the bowl. Shape into a ball and let it rest until doubled in size, about 30–60 minutes (mine took about 45 minutes).
Flatten the dough by hand (you can also use a rolling pin) and shape it into a circle of your desired size (mine was about 22 cm).
Transfer it to a baking tray. Prick the center with a fork, leaving a 1–2 cm border unpricked so it can rise.
Let the dough rest for about 30 minutes. OPTIONAL: For a thicker pizza, let the shaped dough rest for another 30 minutes or longer so it bakes up thick and soft. For a thin crust, use a little less dough and let it rest for about 15 minutes or bake it straight away. The edges will turn out crisp and will not rise as much.
Spread tomato sauce over the dough (I only had a little left, so it did not cover everything evenly, haha). Add grated cheddar and chicken in sweet soy sauce. SAUTÉED CHICKEN AND CARROTS FOR VARIOUS FILLINGS (BREAD, BAO, SAVORY BOLEN, ETC.).
Add another layer of grated cheddar on top. Drizzle with mayonnaise (and more tomato sauce if available), then sprinkle with dried oregano and parsley.
Bake in a preheated oven at 175–180°C for 20–25 minutes, depending on your oven (I use a stovetop oven for about 25–30 minutes, moving the tray to the upper rack for the last 10–15 minutes).
Remove the pizza from the oven, cut into pieces, and serve immediately while warm for the best taste.
Enjoy making it 🥰✨
strIngredient9: Chicken in sweet soy sauce and corn

strInstructions:
Wash the chicken thoroughly, then marinate it with the spice paste, egg, and cornstarch. Refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Crush the garlic and fry until halfway cooked. Remove and set aside.
Fry the chicken until halfway cooked, then add the fried garlic. Continue frying the chicken and garlic until fully cooked. Remove and drain. Serve warm 😍

Clean the chicken, then blend it together with the shrimp until smooth.
Transfer the mixture to a large bowl and add a little garlic powder and salt or mushroom stock powder. Taste the mixture first.
Place the filling inside the wonton wrappers, then fold and seal the edges with a little water.
For the sauce, blend the tomatoes and small red chilies if desired. Transfer to a bowl and mix with the sauces, fish sauce, and oyster sauce. I sauté the sauce afterward to make it last longer. You can add water while sautéing.
Fry the chicken fillets wrapped in wonton wrappers. You can fry or steam them. Enjoy!
strIngredient12: Small red chilies (more chilies make it spicier)

strInstructions:
Boil the chicken breast until cooked. Remove, drain, let cool, then finely shred.
Heat the oil and sauté the spice paste with the kaffir lime leaves, Indonesian bay leaves, and lemongrass until fragrant and cooked.
Add the shredded chicken and stir until evenly coated with the spices.
Pour in the water, then add the palm sugar, tamarind water, salt, and stock powder. Stir well and cook over medium heat until the liquid is absorbed and the seasoning mixture dries out.
The shredded chicken is ready to serve as a filling for cilok soup.
strIngredient10: Rose Brand cooking oil for sautéing

strMeal: Sayap Bakar Nisdas Em (Manis Pedas Asam)
strInstructions:
Clean the chicken wings.
Blend all the spices. Add them to the heated oil along with the Indonesian bay leaves and sauté until fragrant. Add the wings and water, then cook until done (do not overcook, or they may fall apart when removed). If the remaining seasoning sauce is too runny, sauté it briefly until thick enough to brush onto the wings.
Grill the chicken wings while brushing them with the seasoning sauce (I use a grill pan because I don't feel like making a wood fire 😆).
Enjoy with your beloved family 🥰
strIngredient11: Cooking oil for sautéing the spices

strInstructions:
Cut the chicken fillets into pieces, wash them, and drizzle with lime juice. Let sit for 30 minutes.
Rinse the chicken, then add 1/4 kg of Sajiku seasoned flour, pepper, garlic powder, and a little water until the chicken and flour are wet and submerged. Let marinate for 2 hours.
After 2 hours, coat the chicken with dry Sajiku seasoned flour and fry over medium heat until golden brown.
Sauté the onion and chilies until fragrant. Add the bottled Bangkok sauce, water, sugar, sesame oil, and scallions. Add the fried chicken, stir, then turn off the heat. Enjoy! 🙏🏻

Prepare 2 fish that have been thoroughly cleaned. Score the surface of each fish.
Coat the fish with Sajiku fried-fish seasoning and add a little water before spreading it evenly.
Let marinate for 15 minutes until the seasoning is fully absorbed.
Fry the fish in hot cooking oil until golden brown.
Remove and serve.

Marinate the fish with the seasoning and let it sit for 30 minutes, then fry until cooked.
Reserve 3 tbsp of the oil used to fry the fish. Add all the sambal ingredients, stir, and sauté briefly, just until the shallots and chilies soften.
Place the fried fish on a serving dish and pour the hot sambal over it. Enjoy!

Boil the skipjack tuna. If the tuna you bought is already cooked, simply shred it into medium-sized pieces. Then fry the tuna until cooked.
Blend all the spices, then sauté them in cooking oil.
When the spice mixture is halfway cooked, add salt, Sasa seasoning, and sugar to taste. Stir and cook until done.
Once the spices are cooked, add the fried tuna and stir well. Let it sit briefly so the flavors can absorb.
Turn off the stove and squeeze in some calamansi juice. The tuna sambal is ready to enjoy.

Clean the fish, season with salt and lime juice, and let it sit for 5 minutes.
Heat the oil, then fry the fish over medium heat. Remove and drain.
Place the fish on a plate and pour the dabu-dabu sambal over it. Serve.

Cut the tuna into medium-sized pieces, then marinate with salt and ground pepper. Mix well.
Thinly slice the white part of the lemongrass, then bruise the green stalks.
Put the garlic, candlenuts, ginger, and lemongrass in a food processor or blender and blend. Add the turmeric, shallots, and red bird's eye chilies, then blend again, but do not make the mixture too smooth.
Slice the kaffir lime leaves and pandan leaf, and cut the red tomato into pieces.
Heat the oil. Add the lemongrass stalks, pandan leaf, and kaffir lime leaves, then sauté until fragrant. Add the blended spices and sauté briefly.
Add the tuna, mushroom stock powder, and granulated sugar. Sauté briefly, then add the red tomato and stir well. Pour in the water and cook for 5–10 minutes until boiling.
Slice the scallion and add it to the pan along with the red bird's eye chilies. Cook briefly.
Turn off the heat and add the basil leaves and lime juice. Stir well and taste for seasoning.
The tuna woku is ready to serve.

First, wash the salted fish, cut it into two pieces, and fry until slightly crispy. Set aside.
Sauté the shallots and garlic until fragrant. Add the Indonesian bay leaves, galangal, kaffir lime leaves, tomato, and chilies. Sauté until slightly softened. Add a little water, palm sugar, and flavor seasoning. Then add the fried sepat fish.
Adjust the seasoning to taste and serve.
strIngredient2: Galangal, Indonesian bay leaves, and kaffir lime leaves
strIngredient7: Red bird's eye chilies and 5 green bird's eye chilies
strIngredient9: Palm sugar, flavor seasoning, MSG, and granulated sugar

strInstructions:
Cut the catfish as desired and clean it. Prepare the spice paste and the other ingredients.
Heat the oil in a pan, then sauté the spice paste until fragrant and cooked. Add the lemongrass, Indonesian bay leaves, water, and galangal. Bring to a boil, then add the fish, salt, sugar, tamarind water, and lime juice. Adjust the seasoning to taste.
Add the sliced chilies, basil leaves, and tomato. Cook briefly and taste again. The pindang is ready to serve.

Clean the fish and cut it into pieces.
Thinly slice the bilimbi.
Grind the spices until smooth, and do not forget to add salt 😁
Once the spice paste is smooth, mix in the bilimbi.
Add the fish and mix well.
Wrap everything in banana leaves.
Bring the water in a steamer to a boil, then steam the pepes until cooked.

strMeal: Model Ikan Khas Palembang Plus Mie Instan
strInstructions:
First, prepare the model fish cakes: mix the ground fish with water until smooth. Add the salt, sugar, and ground pepper dissolved in a little water. Add the egg and whisk until evenly combined.
Gradually add the sago flour and all-purpose flour. Mix just until combined so the fish cakes do not become tough. Take the tofu and coat it with the fish mixture.
Fry in preheated oil over low heat until cooked. Remove and set aside.
Sauté the ground shallots and garlic until fragrant. Add the shrimp and cook until they change color. Add the jicama, wood ear mushrooms, and dried daylily buds. Mix well. Add the sautéed mixture to a pot of boiling water. Season with salt, ground pepper, Tongchai, and flavor seasoning. Stir well and bring to a boil.
Put the instant noodles and a little of their seasoning into a bowl. Pour in the model broth, stir, and cover for 5 minutes. Add the model fish cakes to the broth and bring to a boil. Remove the fish cakes and slice them.
Put the sliced model fish cakes into a bowl with the instant noodles and broth. Sprinkle with fried shallots and sliced celery, add chopped cucumber, sambal, and calamansi juice to taste. Enjoy your meal 🤗
strIngredient18: Jamur kuping rendam air panas,dipotong kecil
strIngredient19: Bunga sedap malam rendam air panas

strInstructions:
Prepare all the ingredients. Beat the eggs, then coat the skipjack tuna pieces in the egg and fry until cooked. Drain and set aside.
Sauté the galangal, Indonesian bay leaves, lemongrass, ginger, kaffir lime leaves, and palm sugar. Add the ground spice paste, salt, flavor seasoning, and shrimp paste. Stir until fragrant.
Add the skipjack tuna and water to help the spices soak in. Stir gently and cook until the liquid has reduced. Serve.

Soak the salted peda fish in warm water for 10 minutes, then cut it into small pieces or shred it. Fry and set aside.
Crumble the tempeh by hand, then fry and set aside.
Thinly slice the shallots and garlic. Slice the chilies or roughly chop them in a food processor. Thinly slice the tomatoes as well.
Heat the oil and sauté the sliced aromatics and chilies until fragrant.
Add the tempeh and salted peda fish. Stir, add 50 ml water, then add the sliced tomatoes.
Season with sugar, salt, and stock powder. Mix well and adjust the seasoning.
Once the taste is right, turn off the heat and serve.

First, make the tekwan fish balls. Mix the ground fish and cold water in a basin until smooth and elastic. You can knead by hand or use a mixer. Add the ground pepper and salt, then knead again until thick enough that the mixture does not fall off a spatula when lifted. Add the egg white and mix until combined, then gradually add the tapioca flour and mix again.
Bring a pot of water to a boil. Scoop up a little tekwan mixture with the tip of a spoon and drop it into the boiling water using another spoon. Once the tekwan balls expand and float, remove and drain them.
Next, prepare the broth. Sauté the garlic until fragrant, then add the chopped shrimp and cook until it changes color. Add the dried daylily buds and sliced jicama. Sauté until the jicama softens, then add salt, flavor seasoning, and sliced wood ear mushrooms. Cook until done. Meanwhile, bring the water to a boil, then add the sautéed mixture.
Add the tekwan fish balls to the broth and bring to a boil.
Serve the tekwan in bowls with fried shallots, sliced celery, and chopped cucumber. Do not forget to add calamansi juice and sambal to taste 😍
strIngredient25: Secukupnya soun direndam air panas tiriskan

strInstructions:
Marinate the fish with lime juice and salt for 30 minutes. Grind the spices and mix them into the tempoyak. Stir well.
Bring the water to a boil. Add the tempoyak and the other seasonings, then cook until boiling. Add the catfish and cook until done. Adjust the seasoning to taste.
The tempoyak catfish pindang is ready to serve with warm rice, sambal, and other fresh vegetables.

Wash the fish and remove the heads, innards, and bones. Fry until lightly browned.
Wash all the spice ingredients.
Blend or pound the shallots, tomatoes, and chilies until smooth. Sauté them with the Indonesian bay leaves.
Once the water and oil have reduced, season with salt, MSG, and chicken stock powder. Taste and adjust the seasoning. When it tastes right, add the fish and stir until evenly coated.
Cook over medium heat and allow the spices to fully absorb into the fish. Once cooked, do not remove it immediately. Let it rest in the pan until slightly warm, as the cooking process will continue.
Once slightly cooled, remove and serve with vegetables or other side dishes.

Say bismillah before you start cooking.
Grind the shallots, garlic, curly red chilies, candlenuts, ginger, galangal, and turmeric until smooth.
Place the spice paste, skipjack tuna, tempeh or tofu, long beans, Indonesian bay leaves, torn turmeric leaves, bruised lemongrass, and torn kaffir lime leaves in a pot.
Add the water and salt. Stir well.
Cook over medium heat until the fish and other ingredients are cooked and the spices have absorbed, about 30 minutes.
Add the ruku-ruku leaves when the dish is nearly done. Stir briefly, then remove from the heat.
Serve warm.

strMeal: Ikan Kembung Bakar Madu Mudah Sederhana Enak
strInstructions:
Wash the fish thoroughly.
Fry briefly until half-cooked.
Prepare the seasoning ingredients.
Mix all the seasonings until evenly combined.
Coat the fish with the seasoning mixture.
Heat a non-stick pan or any type of grill. Brush the fish with more seasoning and turn it over. Once cooked to your liking, remove it from the heat.
The honey-grilled mackerel is ready to serve! Enjoy!
strIngredient9: Blue Band margarine (I used cooking oil because I ran out, haha)

strInstructions:
Mix all the ingredients except the salt and margarine. Stir until evenly combined. Add the salt and margarine, then knead briefly until the margarine is evenly incorporated into the dough.
Cover with plastic wrap and let the dough proof at room temperature for 1 hour.
While waiting, prepare the tuna sambal filling. Fry the tuna and set aside. Fry all the sambal ingredients, then grind them until smooth. Put the ground sambal in a pan, add the tuna, sugar, salt, stock powder, and water. Cook until the liquid reduces, then adjust the seasoning. Once cooled, process it in a food chopper until smooth. Set aside. Cut the mozzarella cheese into pieces.
After 1 hour, remove the dough and divide it into 56 g portions. Shape each portion into a ball, cover with a clean kitchen towel, and rest for 10 minutes.
Take one portion and flatten it. Fill with 1 tbsp tuna sambal and add a few pieces of cheese. Roll and fold the dough, sealing it tightly so the filling does not leak. Repeat until all the dough is used.
Arrange the bread rolls on a baking tray greased with margarine. Cover with plastic wrap and proof for 50 minutes or until doubled in size.
Preheat the oven for 10–20 minutes at 180°C with both top and bottom heat. Spray the dough with water, then add mayonnaise, tomato sauce, chopped mozzarella, and sesame seeds as toppings.
Bake on the middle rack at 180°C with top and bottom heat for 20–25 minutes, or adjust according to your oven.
Once baked, remove the rolls and let them cool on a cooling rack. Enjoy making them!
strIngredient16: Ikan tuna / pindang tongkol tanpa duri

strInstructions:
Pat the dory fish dry with a paper towel, then season with salt, stock powder, and pepper. Marinate for 15 minutes.
Mix the dry coating ingredients until evenly combined. Set aside.
Mix the wet batter ingredients, then pour in the soda water. Stir until evenly combined and set aside.
Coat the dory in the dry mixture, then dip it into the wet batter. Deep-fry in hot oil until fully cooked.
Heat the oil and fry the fish over medium heat, turning it until golden brown.
For the tartar sauce, sauté the chopped onion until fragrant, then transfer it to a small bowl.
Add the sweetened condensed milk and mayonnaise to the bowl with the onion.
Stir well, add salt and lemon juice, and mix until combined. Sprinkle with parsley.
Serve.

strMeal: Kue Balu/ Kue Ikan Gula Merah
strInstructions:
Beat the eggs, sugar, and vanilla with a mixer on high speed until thick and fluffy.
Preheat the oven to 185°C. Turn off the mixer. Add the flour and fold it in with a spatula. Then add the melted margarine and fold until combined.
Pour the cake batter into a fish-shaped baking pan lightly greased with margarine and dusted with flour.
Bake for 20 minutes, adjusting the time according to your oven.
Serve 👍👍.

Mix the all-purpose flour, instant yeast, and granulated sugar. Add the water and knead. Finally, add the salt and knead again. Shape the dough into a ball and let it rest for 30 minutes. I cover the dough with a cloth.
Divide the dough into 4 portions. Take one portion, roll it out, and turn it over. Roll again, then pinch the sides.
Arrange the dough on a baking tray and let it rest for 1 hour.
Before baking, brush the dough with water by dipping a pastry brush in water and brushing it over the surface. Bake for 15 minutes at 220°C using both top and bottom heat.
Heat the margarine, then sauté the garlic and onion until fragrant. Add the tuna and sauté until it changes color. Pour in the full-cream milk and add the grated cheddar cheese, salt, mushroom stock powder, and ground white pepper. Stir well and cook until bubbling.
Add the flour slurry and stir until the mixture thickens.
The baguette and creamy fish soup are ready to serve. Enjoy!

Boil the spaghetti until cooked to your preferred softness. Drain.
Prepare the remaining ingredients.
Sauté the garlic until fragrant. You can also add onion. Then add the canned tuna and diced tomato.
Stir well while breaking up the tuna. Add the tomato sauce and the other seasonings, including the soy sauces and sugar. Stir until evenly combined and thickened.
Finally, add the spaghetti and mix well. If you prefer it spicy, add sliced bird's eye chilies.
Serve the tuna spaghetti aglio olio. Enjoy! ❤️

strMeal: 493   Grilled Fish W/ Kwetiau Creamy Broccoli Sauce (25  Cp Apron 2026)
strInstructions:
Marinate the fish for approximately 15 minutes.
Grill the fish with the garlic and a little margarine over low heat until the fish changes color.
Sprinkle with parsley and cook until the fish reaches your preferred doneness. Set aside.
Sauté the onion until fragrant, then add the flour and stir quickly.
Add the broccoli that has been soaked in salted water, pour in the milk, and cook until the broccoli is halfway done.
Add the grilled fish and serve with boiled fresh kwetiau.

Wash the potatoes thoroughly, cut each into four pieces, and soak them in salted water for about 10 minutes. Fry in hot oil until cooked.
Marinate the fish with pepper and salt.
Mix the seasoned flour with ice water, then dip the fish into the batter.
Fry the fish until golden and the coating is crispy.
To make the tartar sauce, combine all the tartar sauce ingredients and stir well.
Arrange everything on a plate and serve.

Sauté the ground spices with lemongrass, galangal, bay leaves, and kaffir lime leaves until thoroughly cooked.
Add water as needed.
Add the grilled fish.
Add palm sugar, ground pepper, salt, and stock powder to taste.
Add coconut milk.
Cook until done.
Add whole bird's eye chilies and large green chilies. Cook briefly, then serve.

Rinse the fish thoroughly and drain. Add lime juice, ground pepper, minced garlic, and salt. Let marinate for 10–15 minutes.
Prepare beaten egg in one bowl and instant seasoned flour in a separate bowl. Dip the fish in the beaten egg, then coat it with the seasoned flour. Repeat twice.
Heat the cooking oil. Fry the fish over medium heat until the coating is golden, then remove and drain. Fry the potatoes too!
Serve the fish and chips with mayonnaise and a sprinkle of oregano. Best enjoyed while warm 😍

strMeal: Pesmol Ikan Nila Goreng Bumbu Merah🐟🍅🌶
strInstructions:
Prepare the ingredients.
Clean the fish thoroughly. Coat with lime juice and 1 tsp salt. Let sit for 15 minutes. Rinse briefly and drain. (Lime juice and salt are essential! They help remove the fishy smell and firm up the fish for frying.)
Heat plenty of oil over medium heat. Fry the fish until dry and golden brown. Remove and drain. (The oil must be hot, and avoid turning the fish repeatedly. Turn it just once. Set aside.)
Heat 3 tbsp of the leftover frying oil. Sauté the ground spices and whole aromatics until very fragrant, fully cooked, and the oil separates, about 5 minutes over low heat. (The spices must be thoroughly cooked! They are ready when the color darkens and the mixture looks oily.)
Add the whole bird's eye chilies and tomato. Stir briefly. Add the fried fish and gently toss until coated with the spices. Add 50 ml water to create a little sauce. Adjust the seasoning to taste, balancing sweetness, savoriness, and acidity. (Stir gently so the fried fish does not break apart. Do not add too much water; pesmol should have a thick sauce.)
Finally, add the spring onion. Stir for 1 minute, then turn off the heat.
Serve warm with white rice. So addictive! 😄

strMeal: Cefalo Al Cartoccio (Ikan Belanak Panggang Ala Italia)
strInstructions:
Remove the fish scales, innards, and gills, then rinse thoroughly. Coat with lemon juice and let sit for a few minutes, then rinse again.
Mix the tomatoes, garlic, celery leaves, and bay leaves with salt and oil. Stir well.
Stuff the fish's cavity and coat the outside with the mixture. Do not forget to add lemon slices, including some inside the fish, as shown in the picture.
Wrap the fish, place it on a baking tray, and bake for approximately 30 minutes.
Remove and serve warm. Enjoy!

Prepare the required ingredients. Chop the vegetables and set aside.
Toast the white bread until crisp and lightly golden. Remove and set aside.
Combine the mayonnaise, ground pepper, tuna, cucumber, tomato, and corn. Mix well.
Spread chili sauce on the bread and add lettuce.
Add an appropriate amount of tuna salad, then cover with another slice of white bread.
Cut in half and serve.

Mix 500 g of fatty sliced beef with the marinade (soy sauce, sesame oil, and 1/2 tsp black pepper). Let marinate for 10–15 minutes.
Heat a pan without oil, or use just a little. Stir-fry the sliced beef over high heat for 1–2 minutes until the color changes and some of the fat renders. Remove immediately along with its flavorful juices so the meat stays tender.
Heat 2 tbsp butter. Add the minced garlic and half of the sliced onion. Sauté until fragrant.
Add the remaining crushed black pepper, oyster sauce, sweet soy sauce, Worcestershire sauce, soy sauce, stock powder, sugar, salt, and 100 ml water. Stir well until the sauce bubbles and thickens naturally.
Return the beef and its juices to the pan along with the remaining onion. Toss quickly over high heat for 1 minute until all the beef is coated in the savory black pepper sauce.

Blend the dates with the coconut milk. Strain if you prefer a smooth texture without pieces of date skin.
Add the chopped potatoes and egg. Blend until smooth.
Add the flour, ground cardamom, vanilla, and salt. Mix well.
Pour in the melted beef marrow (at room temperature and already strained). Mix well.
Heat a kue lumpur cake mold. Fill the molds with batter. Cover and cook until done.
You can flip the cakes briefly to cook the tops, or remove them once they are fully cooked.
For babies, the cakes can be steamed to make them softer. My one-year-old prefers the steamed version.

Marinate the meat with salt, ground pepper, and coriander for up to 30 minutes.
Sauté the garlic, shallots, galangal, lemongrass, kaffir lime leaves, and bay leaves until fragrant.
Add the marinated meat and stir until its color changes.
Add water as needed.
Add sweet soy sauce, palm sugar, ground pepper, salt, and stock powder.
Cook until the liquid reduces, then add the tomatoes, shallots, and whole bird's eye chilies. Stir until evenly combined.
Ready to serve.

Clean the meat. I briefly boiled it first, then rinsed it.
Prepare the ground spice ingredients (I replaced ground chili with fresh chilies), then blend until smooth.
Prepare the whole aromatics as well. Sauté the spice paste in a little oil, then add the whole aromatics and stir until fragrant and cooked.
Add the meat and stir until evenly coated with the spices. Pour in the medium-thick coconut milk. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the coconut milk has reduced by half.
Add the potatoes and pour in the thick coconut milk. Add salt and mushroom stock powder.
Continue cooking while stirring so the coconut milk does not split. Cook until the meat is tender and the oil separates, then remove from the heat.
The minced beef gulai is ready to serve.
strIngredient14: Kaffir lime leaves, remove the central ribs

strInstructions:
Cut the meat into pieces and rinse thoroughly.
Blend the garlic, galangal, ginger, and turmeric. Add ground coriander, Indonesian bay leaves, and bruised lemongrass. Bring approximately 700–1000 ml water to a boil, add the spices and meat, stir well, and boil until the meat is tender.
Once tender, remove the meat and drain. Pound it gently, then fry without making it too dry.
Coarsely pound the chilies and shallots, then sauté until fragrant. Add a little water so the spices do not become too dry. Add the meat and cook until the spices are absorbed. Ready to serve 🤗

Rinse the meat thoroughly and drain.
Mix all the seasonings well. Set aside.
Heat a pan with a little oil. Sauté the meat until its color changes.
Add the seasoning mixture and water. Stir and adjust the seasoning.
Cook until the meat is tender and the liquid has reduced.
Transfer to a serving plate and sprinkle with toasted sesame seeds. The meat stir-fried with cooking wine is ready to enjoy.

Coat the steak slices with the marinade.
Heat a little oil in a nonstick pan over medium-high heat until very hot. Add the meat. Sear for 2–3 minutes, then flip. Add the butter and baste the meat with the melted butter. Remove the meat.
Using the same pan, sauté the minced garlic and onion until softened and fragrant. Add water and the remaining sauce ingredients. Stir well and bring to a boil. To thicken, gradually pour in the flour slurry while stirring quickly until the sauce thickens and bubbles. Adjust the seasoning to taste, then remove from the heat.
Serve the steak with boiled peas and French fries.
strIngredient17: Pengental: 1½ sdm tepung terigu dilarutkan dengan 3 sdm air

strInstructions:
Prepare the ingredients and cooking equipment.
Boil the spaghetti until al dente. Drain, reserving 50 ml of the pasta water. Set aside. Melt the margarine and sauté the garlic over low heat until fragrant, taking care not to burn it. Add the smoked beef, cut into small pieces.
Pour in the milk and cook until it begins to foam. Add black pepper and salt or stock powder.
Add the sliced cheese and stir until melted. Add the cooked spaghetti and mix well, then pour in the reserved pasta water. Cook until creamy.
Transfer to a serving plate and sprinkle with dried parsley. Creamy Garlic Beef Pasta is ready to serve. Enjoy, and hope you find it useful 💙

Toast the grated coconut, then pound it. Blend the spice paste ingredients. Cut the meat into pieces.
Heat the oil and sauté the spice paste until fragrant. Add the meat and stir-fry until its color changes.
Add the coconut milk, water, sweet soy sauce, and salt. Cook until the meat is tender.
Once the meat is tender, add the tamarind water, toasted coconut, and palm sugar. Adjust the seasoning. The malbi is ready to serve.
strIngredient1: Beef tenderloin, cut into thick, wide pieces

strInstructions:
Fry the potatoes and set aside.
Sauté the ground garlic in vegetable oil. Add the meat, Worcestershire sauce, black pepper sauce, sugar, and salt. Once cooked, remove and set aside.
Using the same pan, sauté the garlic and onion. Add BBQ sauce, black pepper sauce, and Worcestershire sauce. Finally, add water, salt, and sugar. Stir well and serve with the French fries and sliced beef.

strMeal: Opor Daging Sapi Bumbu Instan Plus Rempah (Empuk & Gurih!)
strInstructions:
Prepare the ingredients. Cut the beef into fairly thick pieces against the grain, similar to rendang or empal.
Sauté the ground spice paste, sliced shallots and garlic, instant seasoning, and all the whole aromatics until fragrant. Add the beef and stir until its color changes and the juices are sealed in.
Braise with plain water. First add approximately 800–1000 ml water. Cover the pan or pot and simmer over low to medium heat until the beef is very tender and the liquid has reduced by half.
Add the coconut milk last. Once the beef is tender when pierced with a fork, add the thick coconut milk. Stir continuously over low heat to prevent it from splitting. Cook until the sauce thickens and is absorbed.
strIngredient1: Beef tenderloin plus 100 g beef fat
strIngredient5: Lemongrass, use the white part and bruise it
strIngredient9: Kaffir lime leaves, remove the central ribs and tear

strInstructions:
Rinse the meat thoroughly, then pat it completely dry with kitchen paper. Pierce the meat with a fork or skewer so the marinade can penetrate and tenderize it. Mix all the marinade ingredients, coat both sides of the meat, and refrigerate for at least 1 hour to allow the flavors to absorb.
Remove the meat from the refrigerator. Heat a pan, coat it with 1 tsp olive oil, and grill the meat until cooked. I cut it into pieces to make it easier for the children to eat.
While the meat marinates, prepare the sauce. Heat 2 tbsp margarine and sauté the garlic and onion until softened. Add the sauces, then the water, and bring to a boil. Turn off the heat and blend until smooth. Return to the pan and cook until bubbling. Add the cornstarch slurry, stir, and adjust the seasoning. Turn off the heat.
Boil the corn kernels and carrots, then drain.
Take a nice photo before eating!

Prepare the meat, then pat it with a paper towel to remove any remaining blood or moisture. Season all sides evenly with salt and ground black pepper, then let it rest for about 10 minutes.
After 10 minutes, grill the meat with the crushed garlic and unsalted butter over low heat, spooning the melted butter over the meat. Flip and repeat on the other side. (I grilled it for about 10 minutes because the meat was very tender.) I also grilled the boiled potatoes. Once the meat is cooked, remove it after about 10 minutes and set aside. Set aside the potatoes as well.
Use the same pan to make the sauce. Sauté the minced garlic until fragrant, then add the onion and stir well. Add the sauce mixture and a little water so it does not become too thick. Cook until bubbling, adjusting the consistency with more water if needed.
Arrange everything on a plate. I sliced the meat to make it easier to eat, then poured the sauce over it. Mama's Western-style beef steak is ready to enjoy 😋 Don't forget the rice 🤭

strMeal: 🍲Rawon Daging Sandung Lamur 1kg 🖤 Kuah Hitam Pekat Khas Jawa Timur
strInstructions:
1. Prepare the ingredients.
2. Boil the beef: Rinse 1 kg of beef thoroughly and cut it into 3 x 3 cm cubes. Boil in 2 L of water until it reaches a boil. Skim off the foam and discard the dirty water. Replace it with 2.2 L of fresh water. Boil for another 45–60 minutes until the meat is halfway tender.
3. Tips for opening kluwek: Soak in hot water for 10 minutes. Tap along the seam with a pestle (do not slice it open). Scrape out the black flesh. Check it: oily black flesh is good; white, moldy, or rancid-smelling flesh must be discarded. Use 5–6 kluwek nuts per 1 kg of beef. Soak good-quality flesh in hot water for 5 minutes, then grind it with the rawon spice ingredients.
4. Cook the rawon broth: Heat 6 tbsp oil in a pan. Sauté the ground spice paste until very fragrant and thoroughly cooked, and the oil separates, about 10 minutes. Add the lemongrass, Indonesian bay leaves, kaffir lime leaves, and galangal. Sauté for another 3 minutes until very fragrant. Transfer the sautéed spices to the pot of beef and stir well.
5. Season with salt, palm sugar, a little granulated sugar, and stock powder. Simmer over low to medium heat for 45–60 minutes until the broth becomes thick and deep black and the beef is tender. Tip: Do not add all the salt at once; start with half and adjust at the end if needed. Once the beef is tender, add the sliced spring onion and celery leaves. Cook for 2 minutes, then turn off the heat.
6. Alhamdulillah, the family's favorite complete rawon is ready. The recipe is simple, but it tastes like a five-star dish!
strIngredient8: Kaffir lime leaves, central ribs removed

strInstructions:
Heat the cooking oil and margarine. Sauté the onion and garlic until fragrant.
Add the carrot and sauté until slightly softened.
Add the smoked beef and stir briefly until evenly combined.
Add the white rice and mix well. Add the stock powder, ground pepper, and salt. Stir again until evenly combined.
Drizzle with sesame oil and stir until everything is evenly mixed and the rice is hot.

Rinse the beef steaks, then pat dry with kitchen paper. Season with salt and ground black pepper to taste and set aside.
Heat a pan over high heat with the cooking oil and butter. Add a steak and cook for 1 minute, then flip and cook for another minute. Cook longer if you prefer it well done. Remove and wrap in aluminum foil for 5 minutes. Repeat with the other steak.
Ready to serve. Japanese wagyu steak (the longer piece) tastes more tender because it has more fat marbling. This steak is not fully cooked in the center, with about 75% doneness. It is usually served with tomato sauce and Worcestershire sauce, along with sides such as salad or tomato soup.

Grind the spices, leaving out the tomato, shallots, spring onion, and onion. Thinly slice those ingredients.

While the beef marinates, make the BBQ sauce. Melt margarine in a pan, then sauté the sliced onion and garlic. Add the BBQ sauce and tomato sauce, followed by water as needed. Add sugar, salt, and seasoning, adjusting to taste. Cook until the sauce is ready.

Slice the onion, shallots, and chilies.
Heat the margarine and sauté the shallots and onion until fragrant.

Add the oyster sauce, soy sauce, and sweet soy sauce and stir again. Add water as needed, then add the long beans. Stir and cook until the beans are slightly tender.
Add salt, sugar, and seasoning. Let the liquid reduce slightly, adjusting the cooking time until the beef and long beans are tender. Taste and serve.

Serve.

Cut the beef and beef fat into pieces, then process them in a food chopper. In a separate bowl, prepare the Pak Tani Gunung tapioca flour.
Add the red yeast rice powder, salt, garlic powder, smoke seasoning, and bratwurst seasoning. Set aside. Add the egg white to the meat, then add the tapioca flour and ground seasonings. I processed the mixture in two batches because my chopper is small. Add the ice cubes and process until everything is evenly combined and very smooth.
Transfer the mixture to a bowl, then place it in a piping bag. Prepare the sausage casings.
Pipe the meat mixture slowly into the casings to avoid trapping too much air. Do not overfill, as the sausages will expand and the casings may burst. Tie the sausages and prick them with a needle. Heat water to 60°C (warm, not hot), then simmer the sausages until they swell. Remove and drain.
Once drained, bake at 100°C until the sausage casings feel dry to the touch. Baking removes excess moisture and helps the casings adhere properly. Turn them over once one side feels dry. Do not bake for too long, or the sausages will dry out and become tough.
The sausages are ready to use. The kids will keep asking for homemade sausages every day once they know Mom makes them 😆

strInstructions:
Prepare the fresh squid: Boil the squid in boiling water for 1 minute, then drain. This helps prevent it from becoming tough when stir-fried. Fry the tofu until golden brown. Remove and drain. In the same pan, fry the squid with the lid on to prevent splattering until it changes color, then remove.

Add the beaten egg and scramble it roughly until cooked.
Add the fermented soybean paste and mix well. Add the squid, green chilies, tomato, and a little water. Cook until the liquid reduces.
Add the vegetables: Add the green beans and tofu. Mix well.
Since the fermented soybean paste is already salty, use only a little salt. Add sugar, salt, and stock seasoning. Adjust the taste, then sprinkle with spring onion.
Serve warm with hot steamed white rice. Guaranteed to be delicious!

Dip the tofu into the batter and fry until golden brown.

Stuff the tofu skins with the mixture and seal the edges.

strInstructions:
Chop the cabbage and squeeze out the liquid. I weighed 500 g of cabbage before chopping and draining; afterward, it came to approximately 250 g. Add ground pepper, ground coriander, stock powder, and salt, then mix well.
Add the minced garlic and spring onion, followed by the egg and all-purpose flour. Pour in the water gradually. About 200 ml of water is enough. The batter should not be runny.
Add the fillings, starting with the quail eggs. Mix gently, then fry. Fry each filled piece individually until crisp, then drain. Use hot oil over medium heat. After frying the quail eggs, continue with the tofu filling.
While frying, prepare the chili sauce. Boil the red chilies so they will be easier to chop finely. Combine all the sauce ingredients in a small saucepan. Simmer over low heat until boiling, then blend or chop everything until smooth. Add stock powder, sugar, and flavor enhancer. Don't forget to taste and adjust the seasoning.
Once cooked, remove and drain. Serve the tahu brontak with the chili sauce for dipping.

Heat the cooking oil and fry the tofu until crisp and golden brown.

Sauté the ground spices until fragrant.
Add the water and all the remaining ingredients.

strInstructions:
Coarsely mash the tofu and season with pepper, salt, oregano, and Chinese five-spice powder. It does not need to be completely smooth.
Heat margarine or oil in a nonstick pan. Grill the tofu while brushing it with the grilling sauce. Turn occasionally until both sides are browned.
For the brown sauce, prepare the sauce ingredients. Sauté the garlic and onion until fragrant and softened.
Add water, sweet soy sauce, oyster sauce, tomato sauce, pepper, salt, and oregano. Bring to a boil.

Serve the tofu steak with vegetables and pour the brown sauce over it.

Wash the anchovies, then fry until cooked.
