Fry the tempeh until partially crisp. Remove it. Frying it first helps it hold its shape and prevents it from breaking apart during stir-frying, while helping the seasoning stick.
Sauté the shallots and garlic until fragrant. Add the red chilies and bird's eye chilies.

Season with sweet soy sauce, oyster sauce, salt, sugar, pepper, and stock seasoning. Add 3 tbsp water. Stir quickly over high heat to keep the long beans green and crisp and give them a restaurant-style wok flavor. Don't cook too long, or they will wilt.
Adjust the seasoning, remove from the heat, and serve.

Wash and chop the spring onion. Put it in a bowl with water, salt, stock powder, and ground coriander. Mix well.
Add the flour and stir until there are no lumps. Add the sliced tempeh.
Fry the tempeh, turning it over, until golden brown. Remove and drain.

Wash the bitter melon and the other ingredients. Cut the bitter melon into four sections, then scrape out and discard the center.
Cut each section in half again, then chop into small pieces. Do not slice it too thinly, as it may break apart or become too soft during cooking.
Dice the tempeh and fry until browned.
Slice the chilies and onions, keeping the large chilies separate from the bird's eye chilies.
Sauté the seasonings with a little sesame oil for fragrance. Cook until done and the onions are slightly browned.
Add the bitter melon and stir well. Pour in enough water.
Once the water begins to simmer, add salt, sugar, MSG or mushroom stock powder, and chicken stock powder to taste. Stir well and check the seasoning. Add the tempeh and mix again.
Taste and adjust the seasonings as needed. Cover and cook over medium heat for 3–4 minutes, until the liquid reduces and the bitter melon softens. Stir again to distribute the flavors evenly.
Add the large red and green chilies as a garnish.
Serve with other side dishes. I made this for my husband's packed lunch and sprinkled sesame seeds over the bitter melon and chia seeds over the rice. Enjoy cooking!

Fry the tempeh until dry and crisp, then set aside. Fry the sliced red chilies and kaffir lime leaves, then set aside. Grind the spice mixture.
Sauté the ground spices, then add salt, granulated sugar, tamarind water, and mushroom stock powder. Cook until the mixture is thoroughly cooked and fragrant.
Once the spice mixture has cooled, add the fried tempeh and stir until evenly coated.
Add the fried shallots, followed by the fried red chilies and kaffir lime leaves.
Adjust the seasoning to taste and serve with warm rice.

Coat the tempeh with ground coriander and a pinch of salt. Fry until the outside forms a golden crust, then drain.
Heat oil and sauté the shallots and garlic until fragrant. Add the curly red chilies, bird's eye chilies, galangal, and Indonesian bay leaves. Sauté until softened and cooked.
Add the fried tempeh. Pour the sweet soy sauce, oyster sauce, and soy sauce around the hot edges of the pan so they caramelize and develop a smoky aroma. Mix well with the tempeh.
Add 120 ml water, then season with salt, stock powder, pepper, palm sugar, and MSG. Cook briefly until the flavors absorb into the tempeh.
Add the green beans last. Stir-fry over high heat for just 1–2 minutes so they cook while remaining crisp and bright green.
Adjust the seasoning, remove from the heat, and serve warm.
strIngredient2: Tempeh, cut into long strips and fried until crusted
strIngredient8: Red bird's eye chilies, sliced diagonally (optional)
strIngredient15: Ground coriander for marinating the tempeh

strInstructions:
Cut the tempeh and long beans as desired.
Heat the oil.
Fry the tempeh until partially crisp.
Fry the long beans until partially cooked.
Sauté the ground spices until fragrant.
Add the tempeh and long beans.
Add sweet soy sauce and oyster sauce to taste.
Season with Royco stock seasoning and salt.
Adjust the seasoning.

Fry the tempeh until half-cooked, then drain.
Sauté the shallots and garlic until fragrant, then add the remaining sliced seasonings, galangal, and Indonesian bay leaves. Sauté until fragrant.
Add the tempeh, anchovies, palm sugar, salt, stock powder, sweet soy sauce, and water. Stir well and cook until the liquid reduces. Serve.

Cut the tempeh into flat rectangular pieces.
Season the tempeh and let it marinate for about 30 minutes so the flavors absorb.
Thread the tempeh pieces onto skewers.
Grill the tempeh with a little oil.
Ready to serve. It tastes great with sambal matah or sweet soy chili sauce.

Prepare the ingredients. Cut the tempeh into pieces about the length of your index finger, 1/2 cm thick and 1 cm wide.
Marinate the tempeh with the marinade ingredients for 10 minutes, then drain.
For the coating batter, combine all the ingredients and whisk until smooth.
Dip the tempeh into the batter and coat evenly, then coat each piece with breadcrumbs. I use both white and yellow breadcrumbs.
Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes so the breadcrumbs adhere well.
Fry in hot oil over low heat until golden brown. Remove and drain.
Serve with your favorite sauce.
strIngredient19: Saus keju saus keju ala richees

strInstructions:
Thinly slice the tempeh and spring onion. Set aside.
Combine the Rose Brand rice flour with all the batter ingredients and mix well. Add the spring onion and stir again.
Heat the Rose Brand cooking oil until very hot.
Dip the tempeh into the batter and coat evenly. Fry in medium-high heat oil, turning occasionally until evenly cooked. Remove and drain.
Banyumas-style tempe mendoan is ready to serve. Best enjoyed warm.
strIngredient3: Rose Brand cooking oil for frying
strIngredient4: Sweet soy chili sauce for serving
strIngredient16: Bawang putih bubuk / 4 siung bawput halus

strInstructions:
Prepare the ingredients. Steam the tempeh for 15 minutes.
Sauté the sliced seasonings until fragrant.
Add the anchovies and sauté briefly, then add the tempeh.
Pour in the coconut milk and water. Stir well, then add ground pepper, mushroom stock powder, and salt. Stir until boiling.
Once boiling, add the bean sprouts. Adjust the seasoning, then remove from the heat.
The tempeh dish is ready to serve.

Prepare the ingredients. Slice the tempeh into thin, long strips.
Coat the tempeh with rice flour and fry until dry and golden. Next, fry the peanuts over low heat so they do not burn quickly.
For the sliced seasonings, fry the onions and remove them. Then fry the red chilies and kaffir lime leaves. Set aside.
Using the same oil, sauté the ground spices and galangal until cooked. Add sweet soy sauce, palm sugar, stock powder, and vinegar. Cook until caramelized, then turn off the heat. Do not let the mixture become too dry, or the seasoning will not coat the tempeh properly.
Once the sauce has cooled to room temperature, add the tempeh, peanuts, and fried sliced seasonings. Mix well without turning the heat back on.
The crispy tempeh and peanut dish is ready to serve.
strIngredient16: Daun jeruk , buang tangkai daunnya, iris memanjang

strInstructions:
Sauté the ground spices until fragrant and thoroughly cooked.
Add water as needed.
Add oyster sauce, sweet soy sauce, salt, and stock powder to taste.
Add the fried tempeh.
Add the tomato, sliced leek, and whole green bird's eye chilies.
Cook until the flavors are absorbed, then remove from the heat and serve.
strIngredient1: Tempeh, seasoned, fried, and set aside

strMeal: Sayur Santan Tempe Sawi Putih Dengan Bumbu Gulai
strInstructions:
Sauté the gulai spice mix and aromatics in a little cooking oil until fragrant.
Add the boiled eggs and stir well, then pour in the water and bring to a boil.
Add the coconut milk and fried tempeh. Season with sugar and salt, then adjust the taste.
Finally, add the napa cabbage and cook until done.
Remove from the heat and serve.
strIngredient2: Tempeh, cut into triangles and fried

strInstructions:
Steam the tempeh with the Indonesian bay leaves for 10 minutes. Remove, mash, and set aside.
Place the ground spice paste in a wok or pan. Sauté until fragrant. Add the aromatics (kaffir lime leaves, galangal, and lemongrass). Sauté again until fragrant and cooked. Remove from the heat and let the steam escape. Remove and discard the lemongrass and galangal from the sautéed spices.
Mix the sautéed spices into the mashed tempeh. Add the grated coconut, tapioca flour, salt, granulated sugar, and mushroom stock powder. Mix well and adjust the seasoning to taste.
Prepare the large lemongrass stalks that have been washed thoroughly. Take 2 tbsp of the mixture, flatten it, and place a lemongrass stalk in the center. Press the mixture firmly around the stalk. Repeat until all the mixture is used. Note: Make sure the mixture is packed tightly. From my experience, if it is not compact enough, it is more likely to crumble and fall off the lemongrass.
Prepare the steamer again. Steam the tempeh satay for another 20 minutes. Remove and set aside.
Melt 1 tbsp of margarine in a pan (I use a wok). Grill the steamed satay until the entire surface is dry and golden brown. Remove and set aside.
For the lemongrass sambal: Heat the cooking oil. Add the shallots and sauté until fragrant. Add the chilies and sauté until softened. Add the lemongrass, salt, granulated sugar, and mushroom stock powder. Mix well and adjust the seasoning to taste.
Serve the tempeh satay with the lemongrass sambal.
strIngredient12: Kaffir lime leaves, remove the central veins and finely slice
strIngredient24: Cabai rawit campur (merah dan hijau), iris
strIngredient26: Serai , ambil bagian putihnya, iris tipis

strInstructions:
Peel and wash all the ingredients thoroughly. Cut each tomato into four pieces.
Heat some oil. Fry all the ingredients except the sugar, salt, and seasoning powder until softened or cooked to your preference.
Remove and transfer everything, including the oil, to a food chopper or mortar. Grind to your preferred consistency, then season with sugar, salt, and seasoning powder. Adjust the taste.
Serve with the accompanying side dishes. Enjoy 😊
strIngredient5: Red bird's eye chilies, adjust to your preferred heat level

strInstructions:
Fry the peanuts in hot oil. Once they turn brown, remove and drain.
Next, fry the tempeh until crispy. Remove and drain.
Grind the shallots and garlic until smooth, then sauté until fragrant. Add a little water, salt, sugar, stock powder, and sweet soy sauce. Mix well.
Once the sugar has dissolved, add the peanuts and tempeh.
Turn off the stove.
Mix well while the stove is off but the pan is still hot.
Taste and adjust the seasoning. That's all—enjoy, dear! 🤤🤤
strIngredient5: Sugar, salt, stock powder, and sweet soy sauce

strInstructions:
Cut the tempeh in half and briefly grill it in a nonstick pan. Cut the tempeh into pieces (you can fry it instead, according to your preference). Prepare the spices.
Sauté all the spices until cooked. Add water, sweet soy sauce, light soy sauce, salt, and mushroom stock powder. Mix well.
Add the tempeh, scallions, and tomatoes. Mix well and cook until the liquid has reduced, checking the seasoning as you go.
Serve.

Mash the tempeh using a pestle.
Add Rose Brand rice flour, mushroom stock powder, garlic powder, and ground pepper. Mix well.
Take 1 tbsp of the mixture. Press it firmly, shape it into a ball, then flatten it. Repeat until all the mixture is used. You can place the patties in a container and store them in the freezer until ready to cook.
If you want to eat them right away, fry the patties until cooked.
The tempeh patties are ready to serve with your other favorite accompaniments.

Make the sauce: Cut the avocado and mash it coarsely. Add the cucumber and onion pickle, chili sauce, and mayonnaise. Mix until combined.
Reheat the frozen patties and burger buns with margarine.
Serve with the buns. Enjoy! 😍

Prepare the tempeh and cut it as desired.
Place the tempeh in a pan. Add the instant tempeh braising seasoning, ground pepper, and Indonesian bay leaves. Pour in the water and mix well.
Braise the tempeh until cooked with the pan covered. Let it cool first.
Add the egg, rice flour, tapioca flour, and baking powder.
Mix well.
Remove the tempeh. Strain the batter, then pour it into a plastic bottle with holes made in the cap.
Heat the cooking oil. Add the tempeh and drizzle the crispy batter over it in circular motions from about 30 cm above the pan. Let it sit briefly until the crispy coating firms up, then stir.
Fry until the tempeh is cooked and browned. Remove and drain.
Fry the remaining batter until browned and crispy, then sprinkle as much as desired over the tempeh. Serve.

Boil the melinjo skins in boiling water for about 5 minutes, then rinse thoroughly.
Cut the tempeh into pieces and fry until slightly dry. Drain.
Wash the anchovies thoroughly, then fry until crispy. Drain.
Sauté the sambal until fragrant and cooked. Add granulated sugar, palm sugar, salt, water, and stock powder. Mix well.
Add the tempeh and melinjo skins. Mix well and cook until the liquid has reduced slightly. Remember to adjust the seasoning. Finally, add the anchovies, mix well, and turn off the stove.
Serve. Enjoy making it!

Combine the all-purpose flour, rice flour, stock powder, garlic powder, coriander, scallions, and water. Mix until well combined.
Slice the tempeh and dip each piece into the flour batter until evenly coated.
Heat the oil and fry the tempeh over medium heat until cooked, turning occasionally. Remove and drain.
Serve. Enjoy making it!

Prepare the fried tofu and tempeh.
Sauté the ground spice paste with the lemongrass and Indonesian bay leaves until fragrant and fully cooked.
Add the instant gulai seasoning and mix until evenly combined. Add water, tamarind water, granulated sugar, salt, and chicken stock powder. Mix well and adjust the seasoning.
Add the coconut milk and stir again. Bring to a boil, then add the tofu, tempeh, and split green curly chilies. Stir briefly and remove from the heat.
Sprinkle with fried shallots and serve.
strIngredient1: Tofu, cut as desired, boiled, cooled, and fried
strIngredient2: Block of tempeh, cut and fried
strIngredient4: Green curly chilies, preferably split in half

strInstructions:
Cut the vegetables into pieces and place them in a bowl. Add vinegar, salt, and sugar to taste, then refrigerate.
Heat the oil and fry the eggs, scrambling them as they cook. Once done, transfer them to a bowl and set aside.
Sauté the chicken until browned, then add the chopped onion and garlic. Finally, add the chopped scallions and sauté until softened.
Add the scrambled eggs and sprinkle in curry seasoning to taste. Season with sugar, salt, and stock powder as needed.
Prepare the spring roll wrappers and add about 1–2 tbsp of filling to each. Fold into triangles if desired.
Heat the oil and fry until golden brown.
The egg martabak is ready to serve with pickles and chilies.

Fry the eggs one at a time, sunny-side up, and set aside.
Slice the shallots, garlic, large red chili, scallions, and tomato. Set aside.
Heat the cooking oil and add the sliced spices. Sauté until fragrant.
Add the palm sugar and fried eggs. Add a little water, then season with salt, oyster sauce, pepper, and granulated sugar.
Taste and adjust the seasoning. Finally, add the scallions.
Ready to serve.

Boil the eggs for 8 minutes, as I do. Remove and peel them.
Boil the garlic, shallots, and chilies.
Grind the boiled spices until smooth. I use a food chopper, but grinding them with a mortar and pestle is also delicious.
I don't fry the eggs, but if you prefer them fried first, that's fine too.
Heat a pan with a little oil. Add the blended spices and sauté until some of the liquid has evaporated.
Add the eggs and sauté briefly until they are coated with the spices. Add salt and seasoning powder to taste.
The easy and delicious egg balado is ready to serve! Enjoy!

Grind the spices.
Marinate the eggplant with the spices and let it sit for 10 minutes, then fry in hot oil. Once cooked, remove and set aside.
Sauté the ground spices and chopped aromatics until fragrant and cooked. Add salt, stock powder, and granulated sugar. Mix well.
Crack in the eggs and scramble until evenly combined.
Add the eggplant, mix well, adjust the seasoning, and remove from the heat.
strIngredient7: Garlic and a little salt, ground
strIngredient18: Cabe rawit ijo, iris, tambahan dari aku

strInstructions:
Prepare 3 chicken eggs and crack them into a bowl.
Season with salt and pepper to taste. Beat the eggs.
Pour oil into a frying pan and heat over medium heat.
Pour the beaten eggs into the pan.
Fry until cooked.
The easy omelet is ready to serve! 😋

Prepare the ingredients. Make the omelet mixture by combining the eggs, salt, pepper, stock powder, carrot, and leek. Beat until evenly mixed.
Heat a nonstick pan with a little margarine, then pour in the egg mixture. Let it cook until halfway set, cover with the tortilla, and wait until the egg is cooked before flipping it over. Spread margarine evenly over the surface of the tortilla.
Arrange the lettuce, cucumber, and tomato on one half of the egg. Add mayonnaise and tomato sauce, then place a slice of quick-melt cheese on top.
Fold the tortilla in half into a semicircle. Grill until cooked and the tortilla is golden brown, then flip and grill the other side until cooked.
The tortilla egg sandwich is ready to serve. Cut it as desired.

Put 3 tbsp of all-purpose flour into a bowl. Add salt and beef-flavored Masako seasoning.
Add enough water and stir until there are no lumps.
Add 1 egg and mix well.
Heat the oil in a pan.
Pour the batter into the pan.
Flip the omelet so it cooks evenly on both sides.
The flour omelet is ready to serve.

Make the dough: Combine all the dough ingredients and knead until smooth and elastic.
Divide into 4 portions of about 46 g each and shape into balls. Coat the dough balls with cooking oil until the surfaces are covered. Let them rest for about 2 hours; the longer they rest, the more elastic they become. I soaked mine overnight because it was already late and I forgot that the meat was still frozen, so I continued the next day.
Make the filling: Heat the margarine and sauté the garlic and onion until fragrant. Add the ground beef and cook until done. Let it cool and set aside.
After soaking overnight, take one dough ball and roll it out with a rolling pin until wide. It should be thin like in the video but not so thin that it tears easily.
Put the cooked meat mixture in a bowl. Add the eggs, scallions, sugar, salt, curry powder, and stock powder. Mix well.
Heat an oiled nonstick pan over low heat. Spread the martabak dough over the pan, then add an appropriate amount of the meat mixture and beaten egg. Fold the dough over the filling, then increase the heat to medium. Fry until the surface is browned, then flip. Fry the other side until browned as well.
Remove, drain, cut into pieces, and serve with cucumber pickles. Praise be to God 🧡 Enjoy! 👌
strIngredient7: Cooking oil, enough to submerge all the dough

strInstructions:
Prepare the ingredients. Slice the scallions and shallots, then place them in a bowl along with the corned beef.
Add the eggs, pepper, salt, stock powder, and curry powder. Mix well. Heat a little oil in a nonstick pan and arrange the spring roll wrappers over the pan.
Pour in the martabak mixture. Fold it like an envelope, then cover the top with another spring roll wrapper.
Turn on the heat and cook the martabak until browned and cooked through. Flip it over, remove from the pan, and cut as desired.
Serve. So delicious! 👍👍🥰🥰

Steam the potato and egg. Once cooked, mash them together.
Add 2 tbsp of tapioca flour, salt, and parsley leaves. Knead until evenly combined.
Shape the mixture into elongated pieces, then fry until golden brown. Serve warm.

Cut the vegetables into pieces.
Heat the cooking oil. Sauté the ground spice paste until fragrant. Push the spices to the side of the pan, add the egg, and scramble it.
Add water as needed. Add the sliced cabbage and cucumber. Then add the instant noodles along with their seasoning, and add salt.
Finally, add the bird's eye chilies and tomato. Cook until the noodles are soft. Adjust the seasoning, then remove from the heat.
strIngredient3: Cabbage (the original recipe uses mustard greens)

strInstructions:
Wash the spinach thoroughly and cut it into pieces. Pour in the oil and sauté the garlic until golden. Add the salted egg yolk and stir until foamy.
Pour in 200 ml of water and cook until the water turns yellow. Pour in the beaten chicken egg, let it sit briefly, then stir so the egg cooks and scrambles.
Add the spinach leaves and stir until wilted. Add the diced salted egg white, season, and stir well. Cook until the liquid boils, then remove from the heat.
strIngredient4: Cooked salted egg, separate the yolk and dice the white
strIngredient5: Salt, mushroom stock powder, and pepper

strInstructions:
Clean the enoki mushrooms and remove any dirt. Soak them in salted water, then drain.
Meanwhile, crush and finely chop the garlic.
Heat the oil and sauté the crushed garlic, then push it to the side of the pan.
Crack in the egg and scramble it, then mix it with the sautéed garlic.
Add the cleaned mushrooms and enough water. Add all the seasonings and adjust the taste. Cook until the liquid has reduced.
Enjoy making it!

Boil the vermicelli until cooked, then cut it into shorter lengths with scissors.
Place the vermicelli in a bowl and add the sugar, salt, and crushed garlic.
Add the chopped carrot and cabbage, then mix well.
Add the egg and tapioca flour, then mix until combined. If the mixture is too thick, add a little water.
Take a small portion (about 1 tbsp) and place it on a lightly oiled hand to prevent sticking. Put one quail egg in the center and shape the mixture into a ball. Repeat until all the mixture is used.
Prepare a steamer and steam for about 10–15 minutes. Once cooked, remove and let cool.
Once cool, prepare the flour mixed with water. Coat each ball in the flour mixture, then coat with breadcrumbs. Repeat until all the balls are coated. They are ready to fry or store for later.

Prepare all the ingredients. Beat the eggs and fry them into an omelet. Once cooked, remove and cut into pieces.
Sauté the shallots and garlic. Once fragrant, add the chilies and egg, then season with salt, ground pepper, soy sauce, and stock powder. Stir well.
Finally, add the bean sprouts and scallions. Stir-fry briefly, turn off the heat, and serve.

Bring water to a boil, then turn off the heat. Soak the oyster mushrooms that have been washed thoroughly. Once wilted, discard the water.
Prepare the seasonings. Slice the oyster mushrooms and mix them with the egg. Add the seasoned flour.
Fry spoonfuls of the mushroom mixture until all of it is used.
Drain and serve on a plate with bird's eye chilies.

strMeal: Roti Isi Kare Tomat Telur Keju Mozarela
strInstructions:
Scramble the eggs and set aside. Cut the tomatoes. You can leave them whole, but I don't like the tough skin, so I remove it.
Sauté the onion until fragrant, then add water and the tomatoes. Cover the pan and let them cook until soft. Once softened, peel off the tomato skins.
Add the curry block and stir until combined. Add the eggs and mix into the curry. Set aside.
Place the curry on a slice of crustless white bread and add mozzarella cheese. Cover with another slice and press the edges together.
Dip the sandwich in beaten egg, then coat with breadcrumbs. Fry until golden.
Done! Enjoy the remaining curry as a side dish.

Place the rice, eggs, ground spice paste, and other seasonings in a bowl. Mix well and taste to adjust the seasoning.
Brush the pan evenly with cooking oil. If you have a thick pan, use that; if using an aluminum pan, place a heat diffuser underneath to prevent burning. A nonstick pan may not give the same result. Heat the pan thoroughly over high heat, then reduce the heat and pour in the mixture. Spread it evenly.
Cover the kerak telur. When flipping it, keep the egg crust on top rather than flipping it together with the pan like street vendors do, so it doesn't fall. Cover again and cook for 3–4 minutes or until done.
Once cooked, remove and transfer to a serving plate. Sprinkle with meat floss and fried shallots, cut into pieces, and serve. It makes a good breakfast or snack with tea.
strIngredient5: Salt, slightly less or to taste

strInstructions:
Prepare all the ingredients. For the nonstick pan, I use the type shown in the photo.
Combine the eggs, scallions, celery leaves, meatballs, salt, garlic powder, and stock powder. Mix until evenly combined.
Prepare the nonstick pan and add 1–2 tbsp of cooking oil. Arrange 4 spring roll wrappers in the pan, covering the right, left, top, and bottom. Turn the stove to low heat.
Pour in the egg mixture and place another spring roll wrapper on top. Fold the wrappers toward the center, pressing gently.
Cook until one side is golden brown, then flip. Cook the other side until done. You can flip it again if needed until fully cooked. The finished martabak should look firm and puffed.
Remove the egg martabak from the pan and cut into 6 pieces or as desired.
Serve the spring roll wrapper egg martabak with bird's eye chilies or cuko dipping sauce. The sauce shown in the photo is pempek cuko; see the attached recipe for version 2.

Heat the cooking oil. Sauté the crushed garlic until fragrant, then add the egg and scramble.
Add the rice and mix well. Season with salt, stock powder, and ground pepper.
Stir-fry until cooked through. Adjust the seasoning, then remove from the heat.
Serve with the accompaniments.

Sauté the garlic and onion until fragrant. Add the ground beef and stir until it changes color. Add a little water and the seasonings, then cook until done.
Beat the eggs, then add the cooked ground beef and scallions. Mix well.
Arrange the spring roll wrappers in an oiled baking pan, layering them as needed. Pour in the egg mixture, cover the top with more wrappers, and brush with oil.
Bake at 180°C for 30–35 minutes. Remove from the oven and pan, then cut into pieces as desired.

Prepare the ingredients.
Beat the eggs with the salt, ground pepper, and chicken stock powder until evenly combined.
Add the scallions and mix again.
Heat the oil and sauté the egg mixture until half-cooked over medium heat.
Take one spring roll wrapper and place some of the egg mixture in the center.
Fold it like an envelope.
Repeat until all the mixture is used.
Heat the oil and fry the martabak over medium heat until cooked, placing the folded side down first.
Serve with green bird's eye chilies.

Lightly beat the egg with the salt, then pour it into the pan.
Place the bread, cut in half, on top and add the sausage and chili sauce.
Flip and cook until the bread and sausage are done.
Fold and cut, then enjoy.

Spread margarine or butter over the white bread. Toast both sides until golden brown.
Chop the boiled eggs, add mayonnaise, and mix well.
To serve, place the bread on a serving plate. Add curly lettuce, the egg mixture, and sliced onion.
Scoop out the avocado and cut it into pieces. Arrange it over the egg, add sliced cherry tomatoes, sprinkle with salt and pepper, and drizzle with lemon juice.

Prepare the ingredients. Cut the onion into slightly thick slices, about 0.5 cm thick. Slice the potatoes thinner than the onion, keeping the potato slices as even as possible.
Heat a generous amount of oil over medium heat. Fry the onion until softened, then add the potatoes.
Fry, stirring occasionally, until the potatoes and onions begin to change color. Remove and drain.
Beat the eggs with salt, pepper, and stock powder. Add the warm potatoes and onions, then let the mixture rest for 10–15 minutes.
Heat a nonstick pan with a little oil over low heat. Pour in the egg mixture and cook until the underside is golden brown.
Carefully flip the omelet, using a plate to help if needed. Cook until all sides are done.
Remove and serve warm for breakfast or an afternoon snack with the family.

strMeal: Tengkleng Rica Kambing Ala Pak Manto Solo
strInstructions:
Boil the goat bones with Indonesian bay leaves, kaffir lime leaves, galangal, and lemongrass until tender. Remove and set aside.
Pour in the cooking oil and sauté the ground spice paste until cooked.
Add the goat bones, water, sweet soy sauce, granulated sugar, palm sugar, salt, and stock powder.
Cook until the sauce thickens, then turn off the heat and remove from the stove.
Serve warm. Enjoy making it!

First, boil the goat meat and bones until half-cooked.
Cut the meat as desired. Blend the spices, then sauté them in oil until fragrant. Add the aromatics, followed by the meat. Stir and pour in the coconut milk.
Add water and let the meat cook completely. Once the meat is tender, add the thick coconut milk. Adjust the seasoning to taste.

Sauté the instant gulai seasoning until fragrant.
Add the goat meat and offal. Pour in the water and cook until boiling, then add the coconut milk.
The goat gulai is ready to serve.

Do not wash the goat meat, so it does not develop a strong odor. Bring water to a boil, then add all the offal along with the Indonesian bay leaves, kaffir lime leaves, lemongrass, and 1 tbsp of salt. Boil for 5–10 minutes. I also add two stainless-steel spoons to help tenderize it faster. Discard the boiling water and aromatics, then replace with fresh water. Bring the fresh water to a boil and add the goat meat and offal. I cut them into small pieces so they soften faster. Use the 5-30-7 cooking method.
Prepare the ground spices. Blend until smooth and set aside. Blend the mature coconut as well, chopping it first so it breaks down faster and releases the coconut milk. Strain the coconut milk.
I separate the first extraction of coconut milk.
Prepare a wok. Sauté the ground spices with enough oil until fragrant and thoroughly cooked. Add the instant gulai seasoning and mix well.
Pour in about 1.5 liters of coconut milk, then add the goat meat and offal. Stir well. Once boiling, taste and adjust the seasoning. When the flavor is right, turn off the stove and serve.
strIngredient9: Kaffir lime leaf, central vein removed

strInstructions:
Prepare the spices, grind them, and wash the goat bones or ribs thoroughly. Use whichever cut you prefer.
Sauté the spices until fragrant and cooked through so the dish does not spoil quickly. Lower the heat and add the goat bones and meat that have been boiled beforehand. See the link below for the boiling method.
Once the meat is evenly coated with the spices, pour in hot water, cover, and bring to a boil again over low to medium heat to let the flavors absorb. Add the coconut milk and stir until it boils, then turn off the stove.
strIngredient1: Goat bones and goat meat, without a strong odor

strInstructions:
If you don't like the strong smell of goat meat, boil the meat with bay leaves for about 5 minutes after the water starts boiling, then drain. I skipped this step yesterday. Sauté the ground spices and whole spices until fragrant, add the goat meat, and mix well.
Add water or thin coconut milk, salt, sugar, and stock powder. Cook over low heat until the meat is tender.
Once the meat is tender, adjust the seasoning and add instant coconut milk or thick coconut milk. Cook briefly, then remove from heat and serve warm.
strIngredient1: Goat meat mixture with a little offal and bones, cleaned and cut into pieces
strIngredient32: Santan instan (atau diganti santan kental asli sekitar 100 ml)

strInstructions:
Prepare all the ingredients. Sauté the Sajiku gulai seasoning mix until fragrant.
Add the boiled young goat bones and mix well.
Add water and cook until the bones are tender and the spices have infused.
Pour in the coconut milk, stir gently, and cook until the broth thickens or reaches your preferred consistency.
Season with salt, adjust the taste, remove from heat, and serve.

Wash the meat thoroughly, then briefly boil it until the water just comes to a boil to remove impurities and fat. Wash it again. Bring about 2 liters of water to a boil, add the meat, and wait for it to boil. Reduce the heat from medium to low and simmer for 30 minutes. Turn off the heat and leave the meat in the covered pot for 1 hour. Boil again until tender. If the pieces are too large, cut them into smaller pieces and return them to the broth.
Sauté the garlic, shallots, and ginger in a little oil until fragrant, then add them to the broth. Add the instant seasoning, coconut milk, salt, sugar, and seasoning powder to taste. Stir well and bring to a boil. Remember to adjust the seasoning.
Ready to serve.
strIngredient3: Small pack of instant coconut milk

strMeal: Nasi Goreng Jawa Dengan Daging Kambing Kecap
strInstructions:
Slice the shallots, garlic, and napa cabbage.
Heat Rose Brand cooking oil, then sauté the shallots and garlic until fragrant.
Add the leftover goat meat cooked in sweet soy sauce and mix well.
Add the eggs and scramble until cooked.
Add the rice and napa cabbage, then mix well.
Add sweet soy sauce, salt, Asatu seasoning powder, and pepper. Stir until everything is evenly combined and cooked through. Adjust the seasoning and serve.
strIngredient2: Leftover goat meat cooked in sweet soy sauce

strInstructions:
Boil the goat meat until half-tender. Remove it, cut it into small pieces, and set aside.
Prepare the spices and grind them into a paste. Meanwhile, heat the oil and sauté the spice paste with the bay leaves, stirring as it cooks.
Add the other whole spices as well. Once fragrant, add water and bring to a boil.
Transfer the broth to the pot containing the sliced goat meat. Add the seasonings, mix well, and cook until the meat is completely tender, keeping the pot covered.
Once tender, adjust the seasoning and serve with glass noodles, fried shallots, sliced scallions, and celery leaves.
strIngredient3: Rose Brand cooking oil for sautéing

strInstructions:
Cut the goat meat into small pieces, wash thoroughly, and boil until half-tender. Drain.
Sauté the ground spice paste until fragrant, then add the meat and mix well.
Add water, bay leaves, galangal, lemongrass, cinnamon, shrimp paste, and palm sugar.
Cook over medium-low heat until the liquid reduces and the meat becomes more tender.
Add salt, stock powder, and sweet soy sauce. Adjust the seasoning and cook until the spices are absorbed.

Prepare the spices. Briefly boil the goat meat, then set aside.
Sauté the ground spice paste until fragrant. Add the whole spices and sauté again until aromatic. Add the boiled goat meat and mix well.
Add the curry seasoning and thick coconut milk, then season with salt, sugar, and seasoning powder if desired. Cook, stirring occasionally, until done.

Prepare the goat meat and cut it into cubes as desired. Bring 2 liters of water to a boil, add the meat, and boil for 35 minutes. Strain, reserve 250 ml of the cooking water, and set aside. Blend all the ground spices.
Heat oil in a pan over medium heat and add the ground spice paste. Sauté, stirring, until fragrant. Add the aromatic spices and mix well. Add the goat meat and cook until its color changes.
Add the coconut milk and stir. Reduce the heat, cover the pan, and cook until the meat is tender and the spices have infused, stirring occasionally. Adjust the seasoning, turn off the heat, and transfer to a serving plate. Enjoy.

Wash the goat meat with salt, rinse thoroughly, and wrap it in papaya leaves for 20–30 minutes.
Wash it again and set aside.
Grind the shallots, garlic, red chilies, bird's eye chilies, ginger, turmeric, coriander, pepper, and candlenuts into a paste.
Sauté the ground spice paste in a little oil until fragrant.
Add the goat meat and stir until its color changes.
Add 250 ml water and bring to a boil. Add seasoning, salt, sugar, stock powder, and sweet soy sauce. Stir well, cover, and simmer for 5 minutes until the meat is tender and the spices have infused.
Add cabbage, bok choy, napa cabbage, tomatoes, and whole red bird's eye chilies. Mix well, cover, and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the scallions, stir, and turn off the heat. Serve on a plate. Enjoy!

strMeal: Sop Kambing Anti Bau Prengus (Empuk Tanpa Presto)
strInstructions:
Bring water to a boil in a pot. Add the goat meat and bones and cook over high heat for 10–15 minutes. Discard the cooking water, rinse thoroughly, and drain.
Bring fresh water to a boil, add the goat meat and bones, and add the aromatic spices. Cook over medium heat for another 10–15 minutes. Rinse thoroughly, discard the cooking water, and drain.
Sauté the ground spice paste in a nonstick pot without adding oil. Add the whole spices and sauté until fragrant. Add 2 liters of water and bring to a boil, then add the meat and bones that have been boiled twice. Skim off any remaining impurities. Cook over medium heat for 20–30 minutes or until the meat is tender. Cover the pot to speed up cooking.
Add the vegetables, starting with the firmest: carrots, cabbage, scallions, and celery. Season with salt, ground pepper, and stock powder. Stir well and cook until the vegetables are tender and the spices have infused. Adjust the seasoning, then remove from heat and serve.

Heat 800 ml of water, then add the meat and half of the bay leaves and kaffir lime leaves. Boil until the meat is tender, about 30 minutes.
Blend the spices into a paste. Heat the oil, then sauté the spice paste and the remaining whole spices until fragrant.
Add salt, ground coriander, and ground pepper. Add the boiled meat and stir again.
Add the remaining water (200 ml), sweet soy sauce, and granulated sugar, then taste and adjust the seasoning. Cook until the liquid has evaporated.
Transfer to a bowl. The gongso-style goat meat is ready to enjoy 🥰

strMeal: Nasi Kebuli Kambing (Campuran Beras Basmati+Beras Lokal)
strInstructions:
Grind the spices into a paste. Add the paste, whole spices, and instant kebuli seasoning to a pan, then sauté until fragrant. Add the goat meat and chicken and mix well.
Cook briefly until the spices are absorbed, then pour in the liquid milk and water. Add salt and stock powder. Cook until the broth develops a rich flavor. Taste and adjust the saltiness.
Soak the basmati rice for 10 minutes, then drain. Wash the local rice and drain. Put both types of rice into a rice cooker. Pour the broth and braised meat into the rice cooker. Add enough liquid to reach about one finger's depth above the rice, or use your usual rice-cooking measurement. Press Cook and let it cook until done.
Once cooked, fluff and mix well. Ready to serve.
strIngredient18: Sch bumbu kebuli instan untuk 1kg beras

strInstructions:
Cut the goat meat into pieces as desired and wash it.
Crush 5 shallots and the garlic, then sauté with the instant gule seasoning and other spices until fragrant.
Add the meat and enough water to cover it. Cook until it starts bubbling, then add the remaining seasonings and adjust the taste.
Add a tiny pinch of baking soda, cover, and cook until the liquid reduces and the meat is tender.
strIngredient9: A tiny pinch of baking soda

strInstructions:
Boil the goat meat until tender.
Slice the leek, bird's eye chilies, tomato, shallots, and garlic.
Sauté the spices until fragrant.
Add the goat meat and a little water. Add the cabbage, then season with sugar, salt, stock powder, and ground nutmeg. Taste and adjust as needed.
Add the sweet soy sauce when the cabbage begins to wilt. Turn off the heat.
Serve. Enjoy cooking 💜

Wash the goat meat thoroughly and slice it thinly. Coat evenly with the marinade and let it sit for 15 minutes.
Slice the other ingredients. Sauté them until fragrant. Heat oil and cook the marinated meat, adding water. Cook until the liquid has reduced somewhat and the meat can be pierced with a fork. Add the sautéed aromatics and the remaining seasonings.
Add the black pepper seasoning and ground white pepper. Stir well until the seasonings are absorbed.
Serve.
strIngredient7: Cooking oil for frying the meat

strInstructions:
🫚 Bring enough water to a boil, then add the sacrificial goat meat pieces. 🫚 Discard the first cooking water to remove impurities and the strong gamey smell. 🫚 Add fresh water and boil the meat again for about 5 minutes after the water comes to a boil. 🫚 Turn off the heat, leave the pot covered for 30 minutes, and do not open the lid. 🫚 Turn the heat back on and boil for 7 minutes, then remove and drain the meat.
🫚 Bring water to a boil again, add the goat meat cut into small pieces, and boil for about 10 minutes.
🫚 Prepare the ground spice paste by blending until smooth.
🫚 Sauté the spice paste until deeply cooked and browned, then add the whole spices. Stir until fragrant and fully cooked.
🫚 Add the meat pieces and cooking broth to the cooked spice mixture. 🫚 Add about 200 ml of extra water. 🫚 Add 3 tbsp FiberCreme and season with salt and stock powder to taste.
🫚 Let the spices infuse, taste, and turn off the heat.
The rich, spiced goat gulai is ready to serve. Happy cooking 👩‍🍳

Boil the goat liver with the aromatics until cooked.
Grind the spices into a paste, then sauté until fragrant.
Add the liver and some water.
Add sweet soy sauce, salt, sugar, and stock powder. Cook until the liquid has evaporated and the spices have infused.
Taste and serve.

Boil the goat meat and offal until tender, adding bay leaves, lemongrass, and ginger to the water. Cut into pieces as desired and set aside. I use prepared gulai kambing seasoning when boiling the meat.
Sauté the ground spice paste until fragrant. Add the goat meat and mix well.
Add the rice and stir. Season with salt, sweet soy sauce, and MSG. Mix well again and taste.
For the cucumber pickle: place the diced cucumber in a bowl. Add all the seasonings and mix well. Taste and adjust.
Serve the fried rice with the cucumber pickle.

Pressure-cook the goat leg bones for 30 minutes with bay leaves and kaffir lime leaves. Discard the first cooking water, then pressure-cook again for 1 hour with the packaged whole spices (cinnamon, cardamom, cloves, black pepper, coriander, star anise, and cumin) and aromatic leaves.
Grind the spices into a paste and sauté until fragrant, then add it to the broth and stir well.
Chop the scallions, celery leaves, and tomatoes. Add them to the broth, season with salt, stock powder, and sugar, and adjust the taste.
Boil the chilies and garlic until soft, then blend or process into a paste. Season with salt and stock powder and set aside.
Serve with warm rice, chili sauce, lime, and emping crackers if desired 💕

Prepare the goat satay.
Grind the spices into a paste.
Sauté the paste until fragrant.
Add the coconut milk and the satay meat removed from the skewers. Add sweet soy sauce, salt, and the other seasonings. Adjust the taste.
Add the cabbage and let the flavors infuse until the sauce thickens slightly. Finally, add bird's eye chilies, sliced tomatoes, fried shallots, and emping crackers. Serve.

Prepare all the ingredients. Cut the goat meat, ribs, and goat fat into medium-sized pieces. Slice the shallots and garlic, and chop the red bird's eye chilies and scallions. Set aside.
Toast the turmeric and candlenuts. Grind the shallots, garlic, coriander, toasted turmeric and candlenuts, and salt into a smooth paste. The salt helps make grinding easier, especially when using a mortar and pestle. Set aside.
Heat the oil, sauté the sliced shallots and garlic until softened and fragrant. Add the spice paste, Indonesian bay leaves, kaffir lime leaves, lemongrass, galangal, and ginger. Sauté until the spices are cooked and fragrant.
Add the chopped red bird's eye chilies and stir until slightly softened. Add the goat meat and stir until it changes color.
Add water. Cover the pan and cook over medium-low heat until the meat is tender.
When the meat is partially cooked, add ground pepper, stock powder, granulated sugar, and sweet soy sauce. Cover the pan again and continue cooking until the meat is tender and absorbs the seasoning. Adjust the taste.
Finally, add the whole green bird's eye chilies, cabbage, tomatoes, and scallions. Cook briefly, then remove from the heat.
Serve warm, topped with fried shallots.
strIngredient1: Goat meat, ribs, liver, and fat
strIngredient5: Green bird's eye chilies, left whole
strIngredient6: Red bird's eye chilies, roughly chopped
strIngredient14: Ginger, about the size of a thumb

strInstructions:
Melt the butter and sauté the garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add the shrimp and stir until they change color.
Add water as needed.
Add tomato sauce, chili sauce, oyster sauce, Worcestershire sauce, sweet soy sauce, palm sugar, ground pepper, salt, and stock powder. Stir well.
Add the sliced leek, stir, and cook briefly. Serve.

Sauté the onion until softened, then add the ground spices and kaffir lime leaves. Sauté until fragrant.
Add the water and sauce mixture, then stir.
Add salt, stock powder, sugar, and pepper. Stir and taste. Add the shrimp and cook for only 3–5 minutes so they stay juicy. The dish is ready to serve.

Heat the cooking oil. Fry the potatoes until cooked and golden on the outside. Drain.
Fry the shrimp briefly, then remove and drain.
Heat the oil left over from frying the potatoes and shrimp. Sauté the ground spice paste until fragrant and cooked. Add salt, stock powder, and granulated sugar, then stir.
Add the potatoes and shrimp, mixing well with the seasoning. Cook briefly until the flavors are absorbed, then remove from the heat and serve.
strIngredient1: Fresh shrimp, heads removed and cleaned
strIngredient2: Potatoes, peeled, diced, and soaked in water

strInstructions:
Wash the shrimp shells and heads thoroughly.
Finely chop the garlic, then dry-toast it with the shrimp shells and heads until fragrant and dry.
Blend the mixture, adding 1/2 tsp salt. After blending, dry-toast it again over low heat.
Repeat the blending and dry-toasting process three times until you get the desired texture. Store in an airtight container. I keep mine in the refrigerator.
strIngredient1: Shrimp shells and heads, thoroughly washed

strInstructions:
Sauté the garlic paste until fragrant.
Add the chicken and stir-fry until it changes color.
Add water, carrots, salt, stock powder, and a little pepper.
Once it comes to a boil, taste and adjust the seasoning.
Add the enoki mushrooms and shrimp.
Once everything is cooked, turn off the heat.
Sprinkle with celery leaves. Done! 🤤🤤
strIngredient10: Garlic paste, the secret to restaurant-style cooking

strInstructions:
Prepare the shrimp, separate them, wash thoroughly, and drain.
Prepare the cheese (use any type of cheese you like). Note: The photos of the other ingredients are for a different recipe.
Heat the oil in a pan. Add the shallots and garlic, roughly blended (or finely chopped if you prefer). Add salt and chicken stock powder, then stir. Sauté until fragrant and fully cooked, then turn off the heat. The garlic seasoning is ready to use as an accompaniment to other dishes, not just shrimp. Note: Since this dish already uses fairly salty cheese, I use only a pinch of salt and chicken stock powder for the garlic seasoning so the baked shrimp won't be too salty.
Arrange the shrimp in a baking tray. Spread the garlic seasoning in the middle of each shrimp, then add cheese. Bake in an oven using both top and bottom heat at 250°C for 30 minutes, until the cheese melts.
Transfer the dish to a plate.
Enjoy the garlic and cheese baked shrimp with all your heart 🌟✨🌞 Happy cooking 😘

Prepare the shrimp, remove the shells, wash thoroughly, and drain. Marinate the shrimp with salt and lime juice.
Prepare the sliced seasonings, wash thoroughly, and drain.
Heat the oil in a pan. Add the sliced seasonings and sauté until fragrant and softened. Add the shrimp and stir. Note: If you prefer them drier, fry, dry-fry, boil, or steam the shrimp first. Adjust to your preference.
Add oyster sauce, salt, chicken stock powder, and ground pepper. Stir until evenly combined and adjust the seasoning. Once cooked and seasoned to your liking, turn off the heat.
Transfer the dish to a plate.
Enjoy the teriyaki shrimp with all your heart 🌟✨🌞 Happy cooking 😘

Sauté the shrimp briefly until they change color. Remove and drain.
Grind the seasonings, then sauté the paste until fragrant. (Note: Use the dark green bird's eye chilies commonly eaten raw alongside fried snacks or sausages.)
Add a little water, then add oyster sauce, palm sugar, salt, and MSG.
Add the shrimp and tomato. Stir and cook briefly until done. Adjust the seasoning, then serve.

Prepare the ingredients. Wash the shrimp thoroughly, then add lime juice and salt. Let sit for 5 minutes, then rinse.
Cut the carrots, onion, and scallions into pieces.
Sauté all the seasonings except the scallions. Add water and bring to a boil. Add oyster sauce and the other seasonings. Add the shrimp and cook until done. Check the seasoning.
Serve the shrimp with oyster sauce.

Prepare the ingredients.
Combine all the ingredients and mix well.
Heat oil in a pan. Add one ladleful of batter and fry until cooked.
Serve the shrimp and corn fritters as a snack with tea.

Boil the spaghetti until cooked, then drain.
Cut the chicken into small cubes, season with salt and pepper, and let it sit for about 10 minutes. Grill it in butter until cooked and browned, then remove.
Fry the shrimp in butter until they change color and are cooked. Remove and set aside.
Make the sauce. Melt the butter, add the wheat flour, and stir until combined. Pour in the full-cream milk while stirring until the sauce thickens.
Add pepper, stock seasoning, fish sauce, salt, and a little sugar, then stir. The sauce will thicken further; if it becomes too thick, add more milk or water. Turn off the heat.
Sauté the garlic and onion until fragrant, then add them to the sauce. Stir again and turn the heat back on. Cook briefly.
Add the boiled pasta and mix well. Add the shrimp and stir again, then add grated cheese.
To serve, place the pasta on a plate, arrange the grilled chicken on top, and pour over the sauce.

Wash the shrimp thoroughly and coat them with paprika powder, salt, and ground pepper.
Bring enough water to a boil, add a little salt, then cook the pasta until al dente. Drain.
Heat the oil and sauté the shrimp until they change color. Remove and set aside.
Melt the butter, add the garlic, and sauté until fragrant. Add the bird's eye chili and sauté until softened.
Add the tomato and sauté until softened. Add a little pasta cooking water and dried oregano, then stir well.
Add the spaghetti and shrimp, mixing well with the seasonings.
Add salt and ground pepper, adjust the seasoning, and cook until the spaghetti is dry.
Transfer the spaghetti to a plate, sprinkle with Parmesan cheese and sliced fresh parsley, and serve.

Wash the tomatoes thoroughly, press them with a spoon, and set aside.
Melt the butter and cook the shrimp until they change color. Remove and set aside.
Sauté the garlic, shallots, and onion in the remaining butter until fragrant.
Add the sliced chilies and all the seasonings, then stir well.
Add the shrimp, stir, and cook briefly so the flavors are absorbed.
Finally, add the sliced chives, adjust the seasoning, and serve.
Delicious! 👍👍

Boil the pasta until al dente, then drain.
Wash the shrimp thoroughly and season with salt and ground pepper.
Heat the butter and oil, then sauté the shrimp briefly until they change color. Remove and set aside.
Sauté the garlic until fragrant, then add the cooking cream, Parmesan cheese, and sliced parsley. Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat.
Once the sauce has thickened slightly, immediately add the pasta and shrimp. Add salt and ground pepper, adjust the seasoning, and cook until the sauce thickens. Remove from the heat and serve.

Beat the eggs with salt and pepper until well combined. Add the shrimp and sliced scallions to the eggs and mix well.
Heat margarine or oil in a pan, then pour in the egg and shrimp mixture. Cook over medium heat until the bottom is set, flip, and cook the other side until done. Remove and drain.
Serve the shrimp omelet on a plate with lettuce leaves.

Clean the shrimp, then mix with lemon juice and salt. Set aside.
Bring water to a boil, add the spaghetti, and cook until done. Set aside.
Heat the butter and sauté the chopped garlic, then add the shrimp. Season with salt and pepper.
Once the seasoning tastes right, add the spaghetti and mix well. Add stock powder if needed, sprinkle with scallions, and serve.
strIngredient1: Shrimp, peeled with tails left on and thoroughly washed
strIngredient4: Garlic, chopped in a food processor

strInstructions:
Prepare the chicken, then blend the chicken and shrimp together. Add all the seasonings. Since the food processor was too full, I mixed the tapioca flour in a separate bowl.
Transfer the chicken mixture to a bowl, add the tapioca flour and cornstarch, and mix until combined.
Stack 4 spring roll wrappers to make them sturdy and wide. Spread the filling on top and roll them up. Repeat until all the mixture is used.
Steam the shrimp rolls in a steamer lined with baking paper for 35 minutes over medium heat. Remove when cooked.
Cut the shrimp rolls into pieces, dip them in the coating batter, then coat with breadcrumbs. Repeat until finished.
Arrange the shrimp rolls in an airtight container and store in the freezer. Your frozen stock is ready.

Prepare the ingredients. Blend the shrimp, chicken breast fillet, garlic, fried shallots, egg, and salt until smooth.
Transfer the mixture to a bowl and add the tapioca flour. Knead until combined.
Coat your hands with oil, then shape the sempol using popsicle sticks. Repeat until all the mixture is used, then steam for 10 minutes. Line the steamer with baking paper.
Remove the sempol and let them drain. Prepare the coating ingredients. Dip each sempol in the all-purpose flour mixture, then coat evenly with breadcrumbs. Repeat until finished.
Arrange the sempol in an airtight container and store in the freezer. Your frozen food stock is ready.

Prepare the ingredients. Marinate the shrimp with a pinch of salt, a pinch of black pepper flakes, and garlic powder. Set aside briefly.
Boil the pasta until al dente, remembering to reserve a little pasta cooking water.
Heat a pan and add the butter and olive oil. Add the shrimp and cook briefly until both sides change color. Remove and set aside.
Sauté the garlic in the same pan used for the shrimp until fragrant, then add the sun-dried tomatoes and sauté briefly.
Pour in the evaporated milk, sliced sweet basil, and Parmesan cheese. Stir well. Season with salt and black pepper flakes, and taste to adjust the seasoning. Add the shrimp and mix well. Pour in the reserved pasta water if the sauce is too thick.
Finally, add the pasta and toss until evenly coated. Transfer to a serving plate and serve warm.

Season the peeled shrimp with a little pepper and salt, then marinate.
Heat the oil and 1 tablespoon of butter. Add the shrimp and cook until they change color. Remove and set aside.
Using the same pan, add the remaining butter and garlic. Sauté until fragrant.
Add the UHT milk, grated cheese, and a little salt. Stir until a sauce forms.
Add the shrimp and stir well to coat them with the sauce. Remove from heat and sprinkle with parsley. Serve warm.
Shrimp with garlic butter sauce is ready to serve.

Rinse the shrimp waste again and remove the digestive tract near the heads. Sun-dry or air-dry it to reduce the moisture.
Toast the shrimp waste and garlic until dry without burning them. For a simpler method, use an air fryer at 100°C for 30 minutes, turning them occasionally. Repeat if they are not completely dry, as air fryer temperatures and cooking times vary by model and size.
Once fully dried and crispy, chop the shrimp waste and toasted garlic in a food processor. Add salt and ground pepper, then process until completely fine.

Process the shrimp and egg until smooth, then transfer to a bowl.
Mix with the grated carrot, garlic powder, ground pepper, salt, stock powder, and sliced leek. Stir well.
Add the tapioca flour and mix well.
Sauté the ground spice paste with the ginger until fragrant.
Add the shrimp heads and stir well.
Add enough water.
Add ground pepper, sugar, salt, and stock powder.
Shape the meatball mixture into balls and place them in the broth.
Repeat until all the mixture is used, then cook until done.
Add the tomato, celery, and leek.
Cook briefly, then serve.

Briefly cook the shrimp in a hot pan without oil until they release their liquid. Turn off the heat, discard the liquid, and set the shrimp aside. This helps remove their fishy smell.
Blend the garlic, shallots, ginger, turmeric, and onion with water until smooth. If using chilies, tomatoes, and candlenuts, add them at this stage.
Pour the spice paste into a wok or nonstick pan and cook until the liquid reduces. Add a little water gradually so the spices cook through and lose their raw smell.
Add salt, sweet soy sauce, MSG-free stock powder, pepper, and coconut aminos. Stir, add about 50 ml of water, and cook until slightly thickened.
Return the shrimp to the pan. Taste and adjust the saltiness and sweetness, then continue cooking until the liquid reduces.
Finally, add the sliced spring onion, stir briefly, and remove from heat.
Serve with lettuce for a low-carb meal, or with warm rice.

Boil the spaghetti with salt and oil until al dente.
Drain and set aside, reserving some of the cooking water.
Sauté the garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add the shrimp and stir until they change color.
Add the chopped tomatoes.
Add the tomato sauce, dried basil, salt, stock powder, and palm sugar.
Add some of the reserved spaghetti water.
Add dried oregano.
Add the cheese and cooked spaghetti, then stir well.
Add the sliced celery leaves.
Cook briefly, stir, and serve.
strIngredient2: Salt and oil for boiling the spaghetti

strInstructions:
Boil the spaghetti until tender. Add a little cooking oil to the boiling water.
Chop the garlic and cut the onion into pieces.
Sauté the garlic and onion until fragrant. Add the shrimp and cook until they change color.
Add the Bolognese sauce and cook until the shrimp are tender.
Add the spaghetti and about 2 tablespoons of the cooking water. Mix well and serve.

strMeal: Mie Jamur Enoki Kuah Tomyam (Kaldu Dari Kulit Udang)
strInstructions:
Prepare the broth first. The shrimp are used to make ebi furai, and the shells are reused for the broth so no part goes to waste. Simmer the shrimp shells with 1 liter of water and 2 cloves of garlic over low heat until the liquid reduces slightly.
Strain the broth, transfer it to another pot, and reheat with diagonally sliced lemongrass and kaffir lime leaves.
Once the shrimp broth boils, add the tom yum paste, stir well, and simmer over low heat. Briefly boil the dried noodles, then drain.
Add the meatballs and enoki mushrooms, and cook until the mushrooms are done. Adjust the seasoning. Place the yellow noodles, enoki mushrooms, and meatballs in a bowl, then pour over the shrimp-shell tom yum broth. It's delicious, refreshing, sour, and spicy, with a rich shrimp-shell flavor. Enjoy!
Take a nice photo first!
strIngredient14: Granulated sugar and mushroom stock powder

strInstructions:
Cut the water spinach into pieces, wash thoroughly, and slice the chilies, shallots, and garlic.
Heat oil in a pan. Sauté the shallots and garlic until fragrant, then add the chilies, water, salt, oyster sauce, and mushroom stock powder. Stir well.
Add the water spinach and cook until wilted, checking the seasoning as you go. Remove from heat.
Serve.

Wash all the ingredients thoroughly. Cut the long beans into pieces and slice the eggplant lengthwise into four sections.
Fry the shallots, garlic, and candlenuts, then grind them together with the bird's eye chilies. Add salt and coriander.
Bring water to a boil, add the ground spice paste, and boil for 1 minute.
Mix 10 ml of coconut milk with enough water to make it slightly thinner, then stir until combined. I dilute the coconut milk so the broth isn't too thick but still has its coconut flavor.
Add the long beans and eggplant, then pour the coconut milk mixture into the pot.
Stir well. Add salt, sugar, and chicken stock powder to taste. Taste and adjust the seasoning. Simmer until the eggplant turns brownish and the long beans are slightly wilted.
Serve with your choice of accompaniments.
strIngredient3: Use only 1/2 if the eggplant is large

strMeal: Vegetable Salad With Lemon Honey Dressing
strInstructions:
Prepare the salad ingredients. Wash thoroughly and cut into pieces.
To make the dressing, squeeze the lemon juice and add honey, extra virgin olive oil, pepper, and salt. Stir well.
Arrange the vegetables on a serving plate, pour over the dressing, and serve.

Heat the oil and sauté the chopped garlic and shallots until fragrant, then add the sliced spring onion.
Add the carrot and sauté until softened. Add the bean sprouts, salt, sugar, and pepper. Cook until the vegetables are done, then remove from heat and let cool.
Take 2 tablespoons of filling and fold it into a spring roll wrapper. Seal the edge with a paste made from flour mixed with water.
Deep-fry in oil until golden brown.

Prepare the vegetables, cut them as desired, wash thoroughly, and set aside.
Fry the shallots, garlic, and chilies. Once cooked, remove and grind them with the palm sugar.
Heat 2 tablespoons of cooking oil in a pan. Once hot, add the ground spice paste along with salt, granulated sugar, galangal, lemongrass, and kaffir lime leaves. Stir until evenly combined and fragrant, then add the coconut milk and 1,000 ml of water. Bring to a boil.
Add the washed vegetables. Stir until evenly combined, cooking over low to medium-low heat so the coconut milk doesn't split or boil over. Once the vegetables begin to wilt, taste and adjust the seasoning.
When everything is cooked to your liking, turn off the heat and serve.

Cut the eggplant as desired.
Bring water to a boil, cook the eggplant for 1 minute, then drain.
Slice the bird's eye chilies and shallots thinly. Sauté them in hot oil, frying the shrimp paste together with the chilies and shallots. Once they are half-softened, add the eggplant and sauté until fragrant. Add a little water, then season with salt, seasoning powder, and sugar to taste.

Cut the napa cabbage into pieces and wash it thoroughly.
Slice the seasonings.
Beat the egg with salt.
Sauté the shallots and garlic until fragrant, then add the sliced chilies.
Add the beaten egg and scramble it.
Add the napa cabbage, salt, and pepper.
Add water and tomato, stir well, and taste. Cook until the cabbage is tender.
The stir-fried napa cabbage with egg is ready to serve.

Boil the washed spinach stems until slightly tender.
Mix all the batter ingredients until smooth and lump-free. Strain if necessary.
Lightly oil a nonstick pan, arrange the spinach stems in it, and pour the batter over them. Cook until the underside is golden brown, then flip and cook the other side until browned, about 5–7 minutes per side.
Enjoy with a dipping sauce. Japanese soy sauce mixed with sesame seeds is commonly used; bird's eye chili can also be added.

Prepare the equipment and ingredients.
Sprinkle salt over the cleaned chayote. Squeeze it by hand, let it sit briefly, then rinse and drain.
Sauté the shallots, garlic, and dried anchovies until fragrant.
Add the galangal and Indonesian bay leaves.
Add the sliced chayote and water.
When the chayote is halfway softened, add all the chopped chilies and tomato.
Season to taste.
Once the chayote has softened sufficiently, add the long beans.
Cook until done, then remove from heat and serve. Enjoy!
strIngredient2: Long beans, cut into medium pieces

strInstructions:
For the batter, combine the wheat flour, rice flour, cornstarch, salt, and stock powder. Gradually pour in the water, stirring until slightly thick, or adjust as needed.
Add the ground spice paste and lightly beaten egg. Mix well, taste, and set aside.
Heat the oil. Dip each broad spinach leaf into the batter, then fry until golden and crispy.
Remove and drain. Serve warm.

Soak the raw cracker pieces overnight so they soften more easily during cooking.
Rinse briefly, then boil the cracker pieces in water until soft.
Prepare and grind the spices, then add them to the pot with the boiled cracker pieces. Stir well.
Add the squash and cabbage.
Add salt and mushroom stock powder. Adjust the seasoning and cook until the squash is done, then serve.

Wash the water spinach thoroughly and cut it into pieces as desired. Thinly slice the shallots and red chilies. Heat the oil and sauté the shallots and chilies until fragrant. Add the water spinach and stir well.
Add the water, cover, and cook over high heat for 2 minutes. Add salt and sugar.
Continue cooking until the seasonings are absorbed.
Remove from heat and serve.

Grind the shallots, garlic, and aromatic ginger until smooth.
Combine all the ingredients in a bowl and mix well.
If the mixture is too dry, add a little water.
Heat the oil over medium heat.
Scoop up some of the mixture and fry for 5 minutes until cooked and golden brown.
Remove, drain, and serve warm.
strIngredient9: Bird's eye chilies or curly red chilies

strInstructions:
Prepare the ingredients. Trim and wash the water spinach, then soak it in cold salted water for 10 minutes. Drain. Bring water to a boil and briefly blanch the water spinach until wilted but still crisp. Drain and set aside. Slice the garlic, red chilies, and very hot chilies.
Char the shrimp paste until fragrant, then grind it. Sauté the garlic, shrimp paste, and chilies until softened and fragrant. Add the water, oyster sauce, sugar, salt, optional seasoning powder, and ground pepper. Stir well and adjust the seasoning.
Wait until the sauce boils. Turn off the heat and pour the sautéed seasoning over the blanched water spinach (or mix everything together in the pan). Serve immediately with steamed white rice. Enjoy!

Wash the napa cabbage thoroughly and cut it into pieces as desired. Thinly slice the shallots, garlic, and chilies.
Wash the shrimp thoroughly and remove the digestive tract to prevent a bitter taste.
Once everything is washed and chopped, heat a little oil or margarine in a pan. Sauté the chilies, shallots, garlic, oyster sauce, and fish sauce until fragrant.
Add the shrimp and stir-fry until they change color and are cooked. Add the diced tofu. Once the shrimp are cooked, add a little water.
Add the washed vegetables and stir-fry until cooked through. Taste and adjust the seasoning. Enjoy!

Combine all the wrapper ingredients except the breadcrumbs. Mix until smooth and well combined. Strain if necessary.
Make thin crepes in an 18 cm nonstick pan or using a crepe pan. Make 10 wrappers and reserve a little batter for coating.
To assemble, place a wrapper on a flat surface and add the vegetable ragout filling. Fold in both sides and roll it up. Repeat with the remaining wrappers.
Dip each roll into the reserved batter, then coat evenly with breadcrumbs.
Fry in hot oil until golden brown. Remove and drain.
For the dipping sauce, boil the dried red chilies for 5 minutes. Transfer to a blender with the garlic, shallots, and some of the water. Blend until smooth.
Pour into a saucepan and add the remaining water, rice vinegar, sugar, salt, and seasoning powder. Cook over medium heat for 7 minutes until slightly thickened. Set aside.
Serve the risoles with the dipping sauce or bird's eye chilies, as desired.

Grate the carrots. Slice the cabbage, spring onion, and celery, and cut the boiled potatoes into small pieces.
Heat the oil in a pan. Add the spring onion, celery, and minced garlic, then sauté until fragrant.
Add the cabbage, carrots, and boiled potatoes. Sauté briefly, then add some of the water (about 300 ml initially). Continue cooking.
To make the roux, melt the butter in another pan. Add the flour, ground nutmeg, and pepper. Cook while stirring continuously until lightly browned, taking care not to burn it.
Add the roux to the vegetables and stir well. Add the powdered milk, sugar, salt, stock powder, and remaining water. Cook until thickened, then let cool. The vegetable ragout filling is ready to use.

Soak the oncom, then crumble it by hand.
Blend the seasonings and sauté them. Add the oncom and leunca, then add more seasoning and water. Cook until done.

Make the filling first. Prepare all the ingredients. Grate the carrots and dice the potatoes, then boil them until almost tender. Melt the margarine in a pan and sauté the garlic first. Once fragrant, add the onion.
Stir until softened, then add the flour and mix. Pour in the milk. Season with ground pepper, stock powder, salt, and sugar. This roux creates the thick paste that binds the risoles filling, known as ragout.
Once the roux starts bubbling, add the carrots, potatoes, and shredded chicken. Stir until evenly combined and cook through. Finally, add the sweetened condensed milk to enrich the flavor. Let the ragout cool, then transfer it to a covered container.
Make the risoles wrappers. Combine all the wrapper ingredients and mix well. Set aside about one-quarter of the water.
Add the cooking oil once the ingredients are combined. Strain the batter, then rinse the strainer with the reserved water. Let the batter rest for at least 30 minutes but no longer than 1 hour. Transfer it to a shallow container, ready for dipping with a crepe pan.
Dip the pan into the batter. When you hear a sizzling sound, release the wrapper onto a cutting board or wide tray. Repeat until all the batter is used. Fill each wrapper with ragout, fold in both sides, and roll it up.
Combine the coating ingredients into a thin liquid batter that is just thick enough for the breadcrumbs to stick. Dip each roll into the coating and cover with breadcrumbs. Arrange the risoles in a covered container. Freeze if you want to store them for later. If frying immediately, chill them for at least 30 minutes so the breadcrumbs adhere properly. Fry in hot oil over medium heat. Serve warm with chili sauce or bird's eye chilies. Enjoy!

Thinly slice the bitter melon, sprinkle it with salt, and massage it until it releases liquid. Soak it in plain water for about 2 minutes, rinse, then briefly boil and drain thoroughly. This helps reduce the bitterness.
Heat the oil and sauté the garlic, shallots, and chili. Once fragrant, add the dried tiny shrimp or small anchovies.
Add the bitter melon and stir-fry with salt, sugar, seasoning powder, ground pepper, and garlic powder to taste.
strIngredient5: Dried tiny shrimp or small anchovies

strInstructions:
Prepare and cut the vegetables as desired. Sauté them with shallots and garlic, then add the egg and scramble it.
Add the sauces, soy sauce, and other seasonings.
Boil the noodles until cooked. Mix them with the instant noodle seasoning packets, sauces, soy sauce, and BonCabe chili seasoning. Combine with the sautéed vegetables and serve. Enjoy!
strIngredient13: Salt, seasoning powder, and ground pepper

strInstructions:
Boil both noodle packs together.
Put the seasoning packets from both packs into a plate or bowl.
When the noodles are cooked to your liking, transfer them to the plate or bowl containing the seasonings.
Mix thoroughly and serve.
strIngredient1: Mie Sedaap Korean Cheese Buldak noodles
strIngredient2: Mie Sedaap Singapore Laksa Spicy noodles

strInstructions:
Boil the noodles, then drain.
Mix the noodles with all the ingredients, including the instant noodle seasoning packets. Stir well.
Heat oil in a nonstick pan. Pour in the noodle mixture and cook over low heat until golden brown. Flip the noodles only once. Remove and drain.
Serve.

Prepare all the ingredients. Trim, wash, and drain the vegetables. Soak the corn noodles in water until expanded, then rinse and drain. Heat oil in a pan. Add the fried-noodle seasoning and cook until fragrant and fully cooked. Add the mustard green stems and stir-fry until wilted.
Add sweet soy sauce, salt, and chicken stock powder. Stir well, then add the corn noodles and mix.
Add the mustard green leaves, celery, spring onion, tomato, and green bird's eye chilies. Mix thoroughly and adjust the seasoning. Once everything is cooked, turn off the heat.
Transfer to a plate. These delicious fried corn noodles are ready to enjoy!
strIngredient3: Choy sum stems, cut into short pieces
strIngredient5: Green bird's eye chilies, stems removed

strInstructions:
Boil the noodles until cooked, then drain.
Mix with the other ingredients and seasonings until well combined.
Scoop up a spoonful of the mixture and shape it into a long piece. Thread it onto a skewer (you can fry it briefly before skewering if it's difficult to handle). Dip it into the beaten egg, then fry in hot oil over medium heat.
Remove and drain. Serve with Bangkok-style sauce or another chili sauce of your choice.

Heat the oil in a pan and scramble the eggs until cooked. Add enough water and bring it to a boil. Add the ground spice paste, additional seasonings, instant noodles, soaked crackers, and the seasoning powder and oil from the noodle packet. Add the sausages and chicken feet if desired.
Cook until everything is done. Serve hot with cilok and pilus crackers as toppings.
strIngredient1: Raw orange crackers, soaked in water for 1 hour and drained

strInstructions:
Prepare the ingredients.
Heat water in a pot. Use a ladle to boil the egg.
Once the water boils, add the instant noodles and cook for 3 minutes. Drain the noodles and discard the water.
Mix in all the seasoning packets that came with the noodles. Add the cooked noodles and toss well.
Arrange the noodles on a plate, add the egg, bird's eye chilies, and fried shallots as toppings, then serve.

Boil the lidi noodles for 5–6 minutes. Drain and rinse with cold water, then set aside.
Sauté the ground spice paste until cooked. Add the chicken and cook until it changes color, then add the meatballs.
Add the cabbage and mustard greens, pour in the water, and cook until the vegetables are tender.
Add the lidi noodles and sweet soy sauce. Season with sugar, salt, and stock powder, then stir well.
Add the chilies, spring onion, and celery. Cook briefly and taste to adjust the seasoning.
Serve.

Boil the noodles for about 3 minutes, then drain.
Crush and mince the garlic, then chop the onion.
Heat a little oil in a pan and sauté the garlic and onion until softened. Add the ground beef and cook briefly until it changes color.
Add salt, pepper, seasoning powder, and chili and sweet soy sauces.
Stir briefly, then add the noodles. Toss until evenly coated with the seasonings. Turn off the heat.
This simple homemade fried noodle dish is ready to serve. Enjoy!

Soak or cook the instant noodles without their seasonings until half-cooked. Drain and cut them into shorter pieces. Heat the margarine and sauté the onion until fragrant. Add the carrot and meatballs, then stir well.
Pour in the milk and mix. Turn off the heat, add the noodles and all the seasoning packets, and stir well.
Add the egg and the dissolved cornstarch. Mix well and adjust the seasoning to taste. Grease a mold or baking pan with oil or margarine, then arrange some of the remaining sliced meatballs on the bottom.
Pour the noodle mixture into the mold and steam for about 12–15 minutes. Remove and let cool.
Turn it out of the mold, cut into pieces, and serve with chili sauce or your favorite dipping sauce.
strIngredient2: Meatballs, some finely diced and some sliced for the bottom of the mold

strMeal: Mie Goreng Basah Bumbu Bawang Putih Bubuk
strInstructions:
Cut the vegetables and sausages into pieces.
Thinly slice the shallots and chilies.
In a bowl, combine the sweet soy sauce, chili sauce, oyster sauce, ground pepper, garlic powder, salt, and seasoning powder. Add a little water to dissolve the seasonings.
Boil the noodles until cooked, then rinse them under running water.
Sauté the shallots and chilies. Add the eggs and scramble. Add the vegetables and sausages, then cook until partially wilted. Pour in the seasoning mixture and stir well. Add the noodles and cook until evenly coated. Taste and add more seasoning if needed.

Boil one pack of egg noodles until cooked, then set aside.
Mince the garlic and shallots, slice the chilies, cut the chicken fillet into small pieces, and slice the meatballs.
Heat the oil. Add the shallots, garlic, and chilies, then sauté until fragrant.
Add the chicken and cook through. Add the egg, followed by the meatballs.
Once everything is cooked, add the boiled noodles and toss briefly.
Add the sweet soy sauce and mix until evenly combined.
Add the soy sauce and sesame oil, then stir well.
Season with salt and mushroom stock powder.
Add the chopped vegetables and stir briefly until slightly wilted.
Taste and adjust the seasoning. Serve the fried noodles.

Prepare the ingredients and lightly beat the eggs. Combine all the ingredients and mix well. Grease a nonstick pan with Rose Brand margarine, then pour in the pizza mixture and spread evenly. Cook over low heat so it doesn't burn too quickly. Once the bottom has set, flip and cook the other side until done.
Remove from the pan and let cool before cutting into pieces.
Ready to enjoy.
strIngredient3: Dried noodles, soaked in hot water and drained
strIngredient6: Rose Brand margarine for greasing the pan

strInstructions:
Bring the water to a boil, add the instant noodles, and cook until partially done.
Add the liquid coconut milk, stir well, and reduce the heat.
Add the instant noodle seasoning, salt, chili, and egg if desired. Cook until done. Remove from the heat.
Serve warm.

Boil the instant fried noodles until partially cooked, then remove and drain. Sauté the garlic and shallots until fragrant, then add the bird's eye chilies and tomato and stir well.
Add the meatballs and stir well. Add the eggs and scramble them. Add the mustard greens.
Add the previously boiled noodles, all the seasoning from the noodle packet, ground pepper, sweet soy sauce, and about 3 tbsp of the noodle cooking water. Stir well.
Remove from the heat and serve.

Grind the spice paste, then sauté until fragrant with the lemongrass, kaffir lime leaves, and Indonesian bay leaf.
Add the chicken pieces and cook until their color changes. Add the water and fried tofu, then bring to a boil.
Add the thick coconut milk, salt, and sugar. Bring to a boil, then turn off the heat.
Boil the noodles until cooked, then drain. Pour the curry broth over the noodles and add toppings of your choice.

Heat water in a pot and boil the Sukaku dried noodles.
While waiting for the noodles to cook, crack the egg into a bowl, add the sliced sausage, and sprinkle in the chicken stock powder.
Once the noodles are cooked, drain them and mix them into the egg mixture.
Heat Rose Brand cooking oil, then pour the mixture into a nonstick pan.
Cook until the bottom is done, then flip and press down gently.
Once cooked, transfer to a plate and serve.

strMeal: Mie Instan Santan Kornet Pakcoy Telur Sederhana Enak
strInstructions:
Prepare the ingredients.
Finely chop the shallots, garlic, chilies, and spring onion. Also chop the bok choy.
Sauté the corned beef, shallots, garlic, and chilies until their color changes. Set aside.
Add the water, coconut milk, and instant noodle seasoning. Stir well. Once boiling, add the noodles.
Add the egg and bok choy.
Serve and sprinkle with spring onion. Eat while warm.

Cut the chicken into small cubes. Clean the chicken feet, then wash them and the chicken.
Prepare all the spices. Grind the shallots, garlic, pepper, coriander, turmeric, and shrimp. Bruise the ginger, galangal, and lemongrass.
Sauté all the spices until fragrant, then add the aromatics, including ginger, galangal, Indonesian bay leaves, kaffir lime leaves, and lemongrass.
Once the spices are cooked, add water as needed. Use less water for a thicker sauce or more for a soupier broth.
