Wait for the water to boil, then add salt, palm sugar, and soy sauce, followed by the chicken and chicken feet. Cook until the chicken is thoroughly done. Adjust the seasoning, add spring onion, then turn off the heat. The chicken noodles with chicken feet are ready to serve.

Cut the chicken breast into small cubes. Wash thoroughly until clean and free of any unpleasant smell. Set aside.
Clean the spring onion and slice it finely. Set aside.
Sauté the ground spice paste until fragrant and cooked. Add the aromatics (kaffir lime leaves, Indonesian bay leaves, and lemongrass), along with cinnamon, cardamom, and star anise. Stir again.
Add the chicken and cook until its color changes and the spices are evenly mixed.
Add half a liter of water. Add the seasonings: salt, MSG, Masako seasoning, palm sugar, and soy sauce. Cook until the liquid has reduced by half. Adjust the seasoning.
Add the sliced spring onion and cook until tender. Remove the chicken and set aside.
Boil the chicken feet twice. Discard the water from the first boil, then boil them again.
Sauté the ground broth spices (garlic, shallots, ginger, nutmeg, and ground pepper) until fragrant and cooked. Add them to the second pot of chicken feet. Add cardamom, star anise, and cloves. Season with salt, MSG, granulated sugar, and Masako seasoning. Adjust the taste, then remove from the heat and set aside.
Boil the egg noodles in boiling water to your preferred doneness.
Briefly blanch the mustard greens in boiling water.
Serve the noodles with the chicken topping, vegetables, and chicken feet.
strIngredient4: Curly mustard greens / sweet mustard greens
strIngredient12: Small bottle of sweet soy sauce
strIngredient13: Small block of palm sugar (the kind costing around 1,000)

strInstructions:
Prepare the spices and grind them into a paste. Heat the cooking oil.
Sauté the ground spice paste until fragrant. Add the bean sprouts and cabbage. Season with salt and stock powder, then stir well.
Pour in the beaten egg. Stir again until evenly combined and the egg is cooked.
Add the noodles and sweet soy sauce. Cook over fairly high heat until hot and steaming. Adjust the seasoning.
Add the spring onion and bird's eye chilies. Stir well and cook briefly, then turn off the heat.
Serve immediately while hot.
strIngredient1: Fresh yellow noodles, ready to cook
strIngredient3: Bean sprouts, washed, roughly chopped, and drained
strIngredient7: Large red bird's eye chilies, sliced into rounds
strIngredient15: Dried shrimp, soaked in hot water

strInstructions:
Boil the noodles until partially cooked, drain, add a little oil, then cut them into smaller pieces.
Heat the margarine and sauté the garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add the sliced sausage and corned beef, then pour in the liquid milk and add the boiled noodles.
Add the seasonings and grated cheese. Stir well and taste. Set aside and turn off the stove. Add the beaten eggs and celery, then stir well.
To make the béchamel sauce, melt the margarine, add the flour, then gradually pour in the liquid milk until smooth. Add the seasonings and spreadable cheese, stir well, and cook until thickened. Set aside.
Arrange the noodle schotel in an aluminum foil tray, spread the béchamel sauce on top, then sprinkle with grated cheese and dried oregano.
Bake at 170°C for 45 minutes, adjusting the time to suit your oven.
Serve.

Beat 2 eggs with the instant noodle seasoning.
Boil the instant noodles until cooked, then remove and drain.
Add the noodles to the eggs and stir.
Prepare a baking pan and grease it with margarine. Pour the noodle mixture into the pan.
Steam for 10 minutes.
Once cooked, remove and cut into pieces as desired.
Prepare a flour mixture by adding enough water to make it thick. Also prepare the breadcrumbs.
Dip the noodle pieces into the flour mixture, then coat them with breadcrumbs. Fry immediately until golden.
Remove the noodle nuggets and serve.

strMeal: Mie Goreng Tek Tek Brokoli Ala @Pawon.Si.Mbok
strInstructions:
Boil the noodles until cooked, then drain.
Sauté the garlic in oil until fragrant.
Add the beef or meatballs and stir briefly.
Add the broccoli, cabbage, and chilies, then stir-fry until softened.
Add the noodles, sweet soy sauce, salt, and pepper. Stir well.
Serve with sliced tomato on top.

Grind the garlic, shallots, and candlenut into a paste.
Heat some cooking oil, then sauté the ground spice paste until fragrant.
Add the sliced chilies and spring onion, then sauté briefly.
Pour in the lightly beaten eggs and scramble until cooked.
Add water according to your preference. For noodle soup, use more water; for fried noodles, use less.
Add the chicken pieces and cabbage, then stir until slightly softened.
Add the noodles, then season with salt, flavor enhancer, and sweet soy sauce to taste.
Stir until the noodles are cooked and the seasoning has been absorbed.
Finally, add the celery leaves and spring onion. Adjust the seasoning.
Remove from the heat and serve warm.
strIngredient1: Pack of Eko noodles or Burung Dara noodles, according to your needs and taste

strInstructions:
Grind the spices using a mortar and pestle or a blender.
Sauté the ground spices and whole aromatics until fragrant, add the soy sauce, then add the minced chicken.
Add water and palm sugar. Cook until the liquid has reduced and the chicken is cooked.
Chop the spring onion and add it. Let the oil separate, then collect the oil to use as seasoning for the noodles.
strIngredient15: A generous amount of cooking oil
strIngredient16: Agak banyak air sekalian untuk kuah

strInstructions:
Heat the water and add oil and salt. Boil the macaroni until tender.
Add the Bolognese sauce, salt, pepper, and mushroom stock powder to the macaroni broth.
Stir well and taste.
The Bolognese macaroni soup is ready to enjoy while still warm.

Prepare all the ingredients, peel them, wash thoroughly, and drain.
Heat oil in a pan. Add the sliced shallots and garlic, then sauté until fragrant and golden brown.
Add the water and prepared soup seasoning. Cover and wait until boiling. Add the baby blue swimming crabs, salt, and chicken stock powder. Stir.
Finally, add the carrots, long beans, and tomato. Stir until evenly combined. Adjust the seasoning. Once everything is properly cooked and seasoned, turn off the stove.
Transfer the soup to a serving bowl.
This delicious baby blue swimming crab and long bean soup is ready to enjoy. Happy cooking!
strIngredient3: Long beans, cut into 2–3 cm pieces
strIngredient4: Prepared soup seasoning, available at the market

strInstructions:
Wash the beef ribs thoroughly and boil for 20 minutes, then discard the water. Add fresh water and boil again until tender. Add the red beans and continue boiling.
Sauté the ground spice paste until fully cooked, then add it to the ribs. Add ground pepper, ground nutmeg, cloves, cinnamon, salt, and stock powder. Stir well.
Add the chopped carrots, spring onion, and celery, then stir well. Cook until the carrots are tender and taste the broth. Turn off the heat and serve.

Heat Rose Brand cooking oil. Sauté the onion, ground garlic, and nutmeg until fragrant. Add the chicken and stir well, then add water.
Add Asatu Rose Brand flavor enhancer and the other seasonings. Taste the broth. Cook over low to medium heat until boiling. Add the spring onion and celery. Cook until the spring onion softens. Turn off the heat. Remove the chicken and separate it from the broth.
Shred the chicken. Boil the macaroni and carrots separately until cooked, then drain. Soak the dried wood ear mushrooms in hot water until expanded. Wash, slice as desired, and drain. Slice some celery for the topping and set aside.
Arrange the carrots, shredded chicken, wood ear mushrooms, macaroni, celery, and fried shallots in serving bowls. Pour in the broth. Sop Manten is ready to serve. Enjoy warm with chili sauce for extra flavor.
strIngredient1: Chicken, rinsed and briefly boiled to remove impurities
strIngredient8: Rose Brand cooking oil for sautéing

strInstructions:
Prepare all the ingredients. (Boil the chicken for 2 minutes for the first boil, then remove, drain, and discard the water. For the second boil, add the chicken and 300 ml water. Once the water boils, cook until the meat is tender. Turn off the stove, drain the chicken, and keep the broth. Set aside 200 ml of the broth. Once cool, cut the chicken into cubes.) Boil the corn and carrots separately and set aside. Sauté the garlic and then the onion in margarine until fragrant.
Once fragrant, add the chicken broth and milk, stirring gently from time to time so the milk does not curdle. Cook until bubbling, then add the chicken. After the chicken has been in for 7 minutes, add the carrots, corn, and mushrooms. Cook for about 5 more minutes, stirring again.
Add the cornstarch mixture while stirring gently until the soup thickens, then add the sliced cheese. Season with salt, mushroom stock powder, and pepper, stirring gently.
Just before turning off the stove, add the oregano and cook until bubbling. Taste and turn off the heat. The soup is ready to serve as cream soup. Shape the pastry to fit the aluminum foil container, leaving extra around the edges so the filling does not spill out.
Fill the aluminum container only halfway with cream soup so it does not overflow. Cover with the pastry sheet, brush with the lightly beaten egg yolk, and sprinkle with grated cheese. Bake the cream soup for about 25 minutes, placing it in the oven after preheating the oven for 10 minutes. The zuppa soup is ready to serve.

Prepare the ingredients. Cut the tomatoes and potato.
Melt the butter, sauté the garlic and shallot until fragrant, then add the tomatoes and potato.
Add water, salt, ground pepper, and granulated sugar.
Add the powdered milk and let it warm, then blend until smooth.
Heat the soup again and add the bay leaves. Stir.
Serve the soup warm.

Mix all the ingredients.
Knead briefly, then let the dough rest for 30 minutes.
Punch down the dough, shape it into a ball, and roll it into a long strip.
Sprinkle with Italian herbs, sesame seeds, and black pepper, then add grated cheese and twist the dough.
Roll it again in the remaining toppings.
Preheat the oven to 180°C for 10 minutes, then bake for 20 minutes.
Serve with soup.

strMeal: Cream Of Mushroom Soup (Tapi Pakai Susu)
strInstructions:
Slice the mushrooms and onion. Roughly chop the garlic, since everything will be blended later.
Heat the olive oil in a pot. Add the mushrooms, onion, and garlic, and cook until fragrant and softened.
Blend until smooth (I use a chopper). If it's difficult to blend, add a little milk.
Return the mixture to the pot, then add the milk and chicken broth. Season with salt to taste. Once the flavor is right, add the flour dissolved in hot water to thicken the soup.
Serve warm. It's even better with croutons!

strMeal: Sup Bayam Creamy Dengan Jamur Krispi
strInstructions:
Prepare and clean all the ingredients.
Sauté the minced garlic until fragrant.
Add a little water to keep the mixture from becoming too dry, then add the cream or milk, salt, sugar, and pepper.
Add the cornstarch mixed with water to thicken the soup.
Add the corn kernels and stir.
Finally, add the spinach, stir again, and adjust the seasoning.
For the crispy mushrooms, clean the mushrooms in a separate bowl and coat them with wheat flour or all-purpose flour.
Fry until golden brown.
Serve the spinach soup in a bowl and top with pieces of crispy mushroom. The dish is ready to enjoy.

Prepare the ingredients.
Pour the water into a pot and add the instant mushroom cream soup mix. Stir until well combined.
Add the corn to the pot.
Turn the heat to medium and cook, stirring continuously.
Once the soup boils, continue cooking for a little while rather than turning off the heat immediately. Cook until the corn is tender.
Once the corn is cooked, the creamy corn soup is ready to serve.
strIngredient1: Packet of instant mushroom cream soup mix
strIngredient2: Corn on the cob, kernels removed

strInstructions:
Trim the tips off the tutut snails, also known as liling, then wash them thoroughly and set aside.
Grind the shallots, garlic, and other spices into a smooth paste. Sauté until fragrant and cooked through. Add enough water and bring to a boil. Add the snails, then season with salt, sugar, and flavor enhancer to taste.
Wait for the soup to boil again, then add the celery leaves and spring onion. Remove from the heat and serve. Enjoy!

Thinly slice the egg tofu, lightly coat it with cornstarch, then briefly fry in hot oil until a skin forms. Remove and set aside.
Sauté the garlic until fragrant, then add the ground chicken and cook until done. Pour in the chicken broth, then add the mushrooms and carrots.
Season with sugar, salt, ground pepper, mushroom stock powder, and chicken stock powder if using plain water. Stir until well combined and taste.
Beat the eggs with a little salt, then pour them in while stirring occasionally. Add the sliced leek, followed by the cornstarch slurry. Finally, add the fried egg tofu and sesame oil.
Serve warm.

Heat the margarine and sauté the garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add the chicken, sweet corn, and carrots. Stir until the chicken firms up and changes color.
Pour in the milk and thicken with the flour, stirring quickly until smooth.
Add the broth and season with salt, mushroom stock powder, and ground pepper.
Cook until thick and boiling, then add the oregano.
strIngredient9: Wheat flour, mixed with a little water

strMeal: Canederli Knödel (Sup Kaldu Bakso Ala Swiss, Jerman,Austria Atau Italia Utara)versi Halal
strInstructions:
To make the chicken broth, add all the broth ingredients, with the cloves inserted into the onion as shown in the picture. Cook over low heat for about 3 hours, until the chicken is cooked and the broth is rich.
Once the broth reaches the desired consistency, remove the vegetables and chicken. Set them aside to eat later or use in another dish. Melt the butter in another pot.
Dice the ham and prepare the chopped onion. Add them to the melted butter and sauté until fragrant and the onion is softened. Remove and set aside.
Meanwhile, cut the baguette into small cubes. Pour the milk over the bread and soak until completely soft. Add the eggs, ham, and sautéed onion to the bread-and-milk mixture. Mix well.
Add salt and ground black pepper and mix well. Add the parsley (I use spring onion instead) and mix again.
Shape the mixture into balls as shown in the picture. If it is too soft to shape, add enough wheat flour and mix well. Bring the broth back to a boil and add the bread balls one at a time.
Cook until the balls float to the surface. Remove and serve warm.
strIngredient6: Carrots, peeled and cut into large pieces
strIngredient12: Large, stale baguette or another firm European-style bread
strIngredient19: Daun parsley , cincang halus, aku daun bawang 3 batang cincang kasar
strIngredient20: Tepung terigu secukupnya jika dirasa adonan terlalu lembek dan tidak bisa dipulung

strInstructions:
Heat 1 tsp of oil and sauté the grated garlic and minced chicken until the chicken changes color and becomes fragrant.
Pour enough water into a pot and bring it to a boil.
Add the diced white tofu and finely chopped tomato. Cook briefly until the tofu is tender.
Lightly beat the egg in a separate bowl, then slowly pour it into the soup while stirring gently to create soft egg ribbons.
Add the sliced spring onion and celery and stir well. Adjust the flavor with a little salt or a child-friendly stock seasoning.
Remove from the heat and serve warm.
strIngredient3: White tofu, cut into small cubes
strIngredient5: Spring onion and celery, thinly sliced
strIngredient9: A little salt or natural mushroom stock seasoning, for children over 1 year old

strInstructions:
Cut all the ingredients into pieces.
Cut the tomatoes and blend them into juice, then strain.
Boil the chicken bones until the water boils. Skim off and discard the impurities from the surface.
Heat the margarine in a pan.
Sauté the onion and garlic until fragrant.
Add the chicken fillet and sauté until it changes color.
Add the water and tomato juice.
Add the carrots, sausages, and spring onion.
Add the stock, salt, pepper, and nutmeg. Cook until boiling.
Once boiling, add the peas and taste for seasoning.
Serve warm.

Prepare the ingredients.
Heat the margarine in a pan. Sauté the garlic until fragrant and lightly browned.
Add the chopped carrots and potatoes, stir, then add the water. Cook until the carrots are halfway tender. Add the chicken pieces.
Cook until the chicken is done, then add the spring onion. Add more water if needed.
Add the flour and milk. Stir well, then add salt, sugar, pepper, flavor enhancer, and cheese. Stir and adjust the seasoning. Cook until done and boiling, then turn off the heat.
Pour the soup into a heatproof bowl, leaving some space at the top. Cover with puff pastry and seal the edges with water. Brush with egg yolk and sprinkle with sesame seeds. Bake at 200°C for 15 minutes, or until the pastry has puffed up and turned golden brown. Remove and serve warm. It's delicious!

Cut the bread into pieces, spread with the topping mixture, and bake for 10 minutes.
Melt the butter, add the corn and carrots, then pour in the milk and add the grated cheese. Stir well.
Add the cornstarch slurry, salt, granulated sugar, and ground pepper. Stir until thickened.
Serve.
strIngredient10: Cornstarch mixed with a little water

strInstructions:
Prepare all the ingredients, wash them thoroughly, and cut them into cubes.
Heat the margarine and sauté the onion and garlic until softened and fragrant. Add the minced chicken and stir until halfway cooked.
Add the potatoes, carrots, and corn. Stir, then add salt, pepper, and parsley. Pour in 1 cup of water and cook until everything is thoroughly cooked.
Add the wheat flour and stir until evenly combined, then pour in the broth.
Stir again, then add the full-cream milk. Wait until the soup boils and thickens slightly, then taste and adjust the seasoning. Turn off the heat.
Toast the bread with margarine until slightly firm. The cream soup is ready to serve with the toasted bread. It's delicious!

Remove the corn kernels and dice the carrot. Boil them until tender and some of the water has evaporated.
Slice the mushrooms, spring onion, and smoked beef. Grate the cheese.
Heat the margarine and briefly sauté the garlic. Add 2 tbsp of flour and stir quickly to prevent lumps.
Add the milk and stir until hot.
Add the mushrooms, smoked beef, salt, pepper, and oregano. Add the corn, carrots, and about 100 ml of their cooking water.
Add the cheese and stir until thickened.
Taste and adjust the seasoning, then serve.

Cut the pumpkin into small pieces. Slice the onion and garlic.
Sauté the onion and garlic in butter until fragrant.
Add the pumpkin and stir well, then add the water and Indonesian bay leaf.
Boil until the pumpkin is soft, then remove from the heat and let it cool. Remove the bay leaf.
Blend until smooth, then pour the mixture back into the pot.
Add the coconut milk, nutmeg, pepper, salt, and mushroom seasoning.
Heat while stirring to prevent the coconut milk from splitting. Bring just to a gentle simmer, then turn off the heat. Adjust the seasoning and serve warm.

Prepare the ingredients. Steam the corn kernels and diced carrots, then set aside.
Put the instant cream soup powder in a pot. Pour in room-temperature water and stir until all the powder has dissolved. Turn on the heat and bring to a boil.
Add the chicken, carrots, corn, and sausages. Cook over low heat, stirring continuously, until cooked through.
Serve.
strIngredient1: Packet of instant cream soup mix

strInstructions:
Prepare the ingredients.
Sauté the minced garlic in a little oil. Once fragrant, add the onion and cook until softened.
Add the chicken and stir-fry until it changes color. Add the mushrooms and stir-fry briefly, then pour in the water. Add the corn and carrots as well.
Transfer everything to a larger pan. Add the sausages and seasonings, then pour in the milk. Stir and adjust the seasoning. Finally, add the cornstarch dissolved in water. Once the soup boils and thickens, turn off the heat. Sprinkle with Italian herbs to bring out a fragrant, Western-style aroma.
Serve.

Prepare all the ingredients.
Boil the spaghetti in boiling water mixed with a little cooking oil. Drain.
Sauté the onion in margarine until softened and fragrant, then add the corned beef. Cook until its color changes.
Add water and cook until nearly done. Add the instant rendang seasoning, a little ground pepper, and the coconut milk. Stir until evenly combined and cook until the corned beef is fully cooked.
Add the spaghetti to the rendang sauce and stir until evenly coated.
Serve.
strIngredient8: Packet of instant coconut milk, 65 ml

strInstructions:
Prepare the coconut milk. Mix the Rose Brand instant coconut milk with fresh coconut milk, then prepare the remaining ingredients.
Put the instant rendang seasoning and chicken pieces in a pan. Mix until the seasoning evenly coats the chicken.
Add the thin coconut milk and potatoes, then stir well. Add the aromatic spices, followed by beef stock powder.
Turn the heat to medium and cook for 20 minutes. Add the granulated sugar. Once the liquid has reduced, add the thick Rose Brand coconut milk.
Stir well and add Asatu flavor enhancer.
Continue cooking until the liquid has reduced and the rendang reaches the desired consistency.
Turn off the heat and serve the chicken rendang.

Boil the spaghetti in water mixed with cooking oil until al dente, then drain.
Sauté the onion in margarine until softened and fragrant. Add the ground beef and cook until it changes color.
Add water and cook until the beef is nearly done. Add the instant rendang seasoning and coconut milk. Stir well and cook until the beef is tender.
Add the spaghetti to the rendang sauce, mix well, and serve.

Soak the jengkol beans overnight in plenty of water, then peel off the thin skins. Boil for 30 minutes with 4 Indonesian bay leaves. Let them sit for another 12 hours, then replace the water and continue soaking for up to 3 more days. Change the water every 12 hours to reduce the strong smell. Finally, boil the jengkol for another 30 minutes, drain, and gently flatten each piece. Set aside.
Grind all the spice paste ingredients and prepare the aromatic spices.
Sauté the ground spice paste until very fragrant. Add the ground nutmeg, pepper, and coriander, and cook until fragrant. Add the aromatic spices and stir well. Add the instant rendang seasoning, stir, and cook until fragrant.
Add the toasted coconut, then stir well. Add the water, sugar, salt, and stock powder. Bring to a boil, then add the instant coconut milk and stir well.
Once the coconut milk boils, add the jengkol. Cook until the spices are absorbed and the liquid has reduced. Adjust the seasoning, then add the galendo and stir well.
Continue cooking over medium-low heat until the liquid has reduced significantly. Adjust the seasoning, remove from the heat, and serve.
strIngredient2: Toasted shredded coconut (serundeng), or toasted coconut

strInstructions:
Boil the beef, then drain.
Grind the spices until smooth. Sauté with the rendang seasoning mix. Add the whole spices and aromatics. Stir until evenly combined.
Add the beef and coconut milk. Stir well and cook until the liquid reduces.
The rendang is ready to serve with warm rice.

Blend the chicken with the garlic and scallions until smooth. Add the breadcrumbs and tapioca flour, then blend again until the mixture is smooth and evenly combined.
Add the oyster sauce and powdered stock to the chicken mixture. Stir until everything is well combined.
Bring water to a boil. Shape the mixture into balls, then drop them into the boiling water. Boil until the balls are cooked through and float to the surface. Remove and drain.
Heat a little oil, then add the rendang seasoning. Sauté until fragrant.
Pour in the thin coconut milk and water. Bring to a boil, stirring gently to prevent the coconut milk from splitting.
Add the boiled chicken balls and the powdered stock. Stir well and cook until the seasoning is absorbed.
Serve the rendang-seasoned chicken balls while warm.

Prepare the ingredients. Heat a little oil, then add the ground spices and all the aromatics.
Stir well, add the instant rendang seasoning, then add the beef and cook until its color changes.
Once the beef changes color, add the water and coconut milk. Stir well.
Cover the pot loosely, leaving a gap, and simmer over low heat until boiling, stirring occasionally. Once the liquid has reduced somewhat, add the beef stock and salt. Continue cooking until the liquid has reduced or dried out to your preferred consistency. Keep the pot loosely covered to help tenderize the beef.
I prefer it slightly saucy, so some of the seasoning remains visible. The beef rendang is ready to serve.

Prepare the ingredients and briefly sauté the instant seasoning.
Add the squid and stir until coated with the seasoning.
Add the instant coconut milk and cook until the sauce thickens slightly. Serve.
strIngredient4: Thick coconut milk, diluted with a little water

strInstructions:
Clean the chicken, then drizzle with lime juice and salt. Gently rub it in and let it sit for about 15 minutes. Rinse with water before cooking. I do this to remove the chicken's unpleasant smell. Prepare the Sajiku Rendang seasoning as well.
Place the chicken pieces in a pan and pour in the Sajiku rendang seasoning. Mix well, gently rubbing the seasoning into the chicken. Add all the aromatic ingredients. Marinate for about 30 minutes.
After 30 minutes, turn on the stove and stir well. Pour in the thin coconut milk. Cook over medium heat until the coconut milk boils and thickens.
Pour in the thick coconut milk and stir well. Add the boiled potatoes.
Cook until the seasoning is absorbed and the sauce reduces. I leave it in the pan overnight; I cook it at around 10 p.m., and by 6 a.m. the next day, the sauce has soaked in and the seasoning tastes wonderful.
Don't forget to taste it. Add granulated sugar and salt if needed, according to your preference.

Cut the beef into approximately 20 pieces from 1 kg of meat. Grind the spices until smooth. Place the beef and ground spices in a pan, then add the lemongrass, turmeric leaf, Indonesian bay leaves, and salt. Mix until the beef is evenly coated. Let it sit for at least 15 minutes with the stove off. After 15 minutes, turn on the stove. The beef will release liquid, and the amount will increase as it cooks.
Continue cooking until the liquid reduces, then pour in the coconut milk. Once the coconut milk boils, reduce the heat.
Toast the grated coconut until it changes color and becomes fragrant.
Add the toasted grated coconut, which has been ground, then cook while stirring until the beef is tender and the seasoning releases oil.
The rendang is ready to serve.

Rinse the beef thoroughly and add 1 pack of seasoning. Mix until evenly coated.
Add the thin coconut milk and cook for 30 minutes. Then add the thick coconut milk and cook for another 30 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Once the thick coconut milk has reduced and the rendang reaches the desired consistency, remove from the heat and serve.

Rinse the beef thoroughly and drain.
Place the beef and sliced shallots in a pan, rub them together, then turn on the stove.
Add the ground spices, aromatic roots, sweet soy sauce, salt, and seasoning powder. Sauté until the beef changes color.
Add the coconut milk and stir until fragrant. Transfer to a pressure cooker and cook under pressure for about 30 minutes (I use an electric pressure cooker).
When pressure cooking is complete, return the rendang to the pan and cook until the sauce reduces. Adjust the seasoning to taste, then turn off the heat.
Serve with warm rice.

Prepare the ingredients.
Sauté the shallots and garlic until fragrant, then add the rendang seasoning and toasted coconut seasoning. Add the aromatics and cook until fragrant.
Add the eggplant pieces and stir well.
Pour in the coconut milk, stir, then season with salt and mushroom stock powder. Taste and adjust the seasoning.
Cook until the eggplant is tender and has absorbed the seasoning.
The eggplant rendang is ready to serve.
strIngredient6: Kaffir lime leaves and Indonesian bay leaves

strInstructions:
Prepare all the ingredients.
Mix the beef with the Sajiku Rendang seasoning until evenly coated. Add the second-press coconut milk.
Stir well and cook over high heat for 20 minutes. Add the thick coconut milk, stir well, and cook over medium heat for about 10 minutes.
Cook for another 10 minutes to allow the oil to separate. Remove from the heat and serve. It goes perfectly with hot rice and can be stored for up to three days.
strIngredient1: Rendang beef, cut into 1 cm pieces

strInstructions:
Prepare the ingredients and cut the beef into 1 cm pieces.
Place the beef in a pan, add 1 pack of Sajiku Rendang seasoning, and mix well.
Add the thin coconut milk, stir well, and cook over medium heat for 20 minutes or until the liquid reduces.
Add the thick coconut milk and cook for 10 minutes, or until the rendang reaches your desired consistency. Turn off the heat and serve.
The seasoning is deliciously rich and savory.

Cut the beef into pieces about 1 cm thick so it tenderizes more easily. Briefly boil it to remove the blood.
Combine the beef with 1 pack of Sajiku rendang seasoning in a pan, stirring until the seasoning coats all sides of the meat.
Add the thin coconut milk and stir. Turn the heat to medium and cook for 20 minutes.
Once the liquid has reduced, add the thick coconut milk. Cook over medium heat for 10 minutes. Turn off the stove and let it rest for 30 minutes.
The rendang is ready to serve.

Boil or pressure-cook the jengkol until tender. Lightly crush it so it becomes even more tender when eaten.
Sauté the ground spices in enough oil, then add the instant rendang seasoning. Stir well, add a little water, and cook until the spices are fully cooked.
Add the jengkol and stir until evenly coated. Add salt, palm sugar, powdered stock, and all the supplementary aromatics. Finally, add the water and coconut milk. Stir frequently to prevent the coconut milk from splitting. Adjust the seasoning to taste.
Ready to serve.

Boil the beef until tender (a pressure cooker can also be used). Add the aromatics, salt, and ground pepper.
Add the beef, Sajiku practical rendang seasoning, and aromatics, then stir until the seasoning coats the meat evenly.
Add the thin coconut milk and stir. Cook over medium heat for 20 minutes.
Once the liquid has reduced, add the thick coconut milk. Cook over medium heat for 10 minutes, until the rendang reaches the desired consistency.
Serve.

Add the sliced beef and instant rendang seasoning. Stir until evenly coated.
Add the lemongrass and thin coconut milk. Cover and cook over medium heat for 20 minutes.
Once the sauce has reduced, add the thick coconut milk and stir. Cover again and cook for 10 minutes.
Turn off the stove. The beef rendang is ready to serve.

strMeal: Rendang Sapi Ala Padang Dengan Bumbu Praktis
strInstructions:
Prepare 500 g of beef cut into pieces about 1 cm thick. Place the beef in a pan, add 1 pack of Sajiku rendang seasoning, and stir until the meat is evenly coated.
Add 500 ml of thin coconut milk and stir. Cook over medium heat for 20 minutes, allowing it to boil and reduce.
Once the liquid has reduced, add 200 ml of thick coconut milk and cook over medium heat for another 10 minutes, until the rendang reaches the desired consistency.
The rendang is ready to serve.
strIngredient1: Beef, preferably top side or the outer part of the hind leg
strIngredient4: Water for making 500 ml thin coconut milk and 200 ml thick coconut milk

strInstructions:
Rinse the beef thoroughly, cut it into pieces, and place it in a pan. Add the instant Sajiku Rendang seasoning and stir until evenly coated.
Once the seasoning is evenly distributed, add the thin coconut milk. Stir again, cover, and cook for 20 minutes.
After 20 minutes, uncover the pan and add the thick coconut milk. Stir well, then cover and cook for another 10 minutes.
The beef rendang with convenient Sajiku Rendang seasoning is ready to serve.

Prepare the ingredients.
Put the rendang seasoning in a pan.
Add the chicken and stir until the seasoning is evenly distributed. Turn on the stove and stir for a short while.
Once the chicken and seasoning are well combined, add 1 liter of water and 1 pack of instant coconut milk. Cook over medium heat for 20 minutes.
Then add 2 more packs of instant coconut milk and cook for another 10 minutes.
strIngredient3: Instant coconut milk, 65 ml per pack

strInstructions:
Prepare the ingredients, including the Sajiku Rendang seasoning. Slice the beef thinly.
Blend the pineapple and mix it with the beef slices. Stir well and marinate for 15–20 minutes.
Add the thin coconut milk, turmeric leaf, kaffir lime leaves, lemongrass, and Sajiku Rendang seasoning.
Stir well and cook over medium heat for 20 minutes, until the sauce reduces. Add the thick coconut milk, stir well again, and cook over medium heat for another 10 minutes.
Cook until the sauce reduces, the oil separates, and the meat is cooked. Remove from the heat and transfer to a serving dish. The easy Sajiku beef rendang is ready to serve. Enjoy!

Grind the spices until smooth. Prepare the aromatics and extract the coconut milk.
Prepare the chicken and boil the eggs.
Sauté the ground spices in a little oil. When they are half-cooked, add the aromatics and cook until fragrant.
Add the chicken and stir until it is evenly coated with the seasoning. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the color changes, then add the thin coconut milk. Season and adjust the taste. Cook until the chicken is partially cooked.
Add the eggs and thick coconut milk, stirring as you pour. Let it come to a boil and cook until the chicken is done.
Ready to serve.
strIngredient1: Chicken, cleaned and cut as desired
strIngredient5: Cooking oil for sautéing the spices

strInstructions:
Bring water to a boil and boil the chicken for about 5 minutes. Remove the chicken and set it aside.
Heat the oil, add the opor seasoning, and sauté briefly until fragrant. Add the chicken, water, lemongrass, ginger, galangal, Indonesian bay leaves, and kaffir lime leaves. Bring to a boil and cook for about 5 minutes.
Add the coconut milk and seasonings. Simmer over low heat, stirring occasionally, until the seasoning is absorbed and the chicken is tender, about 20–30 minutes. Taste and adjust the seasoning. Sprinkle with fried shallots before serving.
strIngredient10: Water, enough to cover the chicken

strInstructions:
Bring the water to a boil, add the instant seasoning, and stir well.
Add the chicken and cook until tender and fully cooked. Taste the broth and add more seasonings if needed. The opor seasoning I used was already flavorful, so I didn't add anything else.
Once cooked, remove from the heat and serve. Enjoy!

Prepare the seasoning ingredients.
Clean the chicken and briefly boil it with 2 Indonesian bay leaves until the brown impurities rise to the surface. Rinse thoroughly and drain.
Grind all the spice paste ingredients until smooth, then sauté until fragrant and cooked through.
Add the Indonesian bay leaves, lemongrass, galangal, and kaffir lime leaves. Sauté until fragrant.
Add water, then add the chicken, stock cube, sugar, salt, and whole green chili. Cook until the chicken is almost done.
Add the coconut milk and cook until the chicken is fully cooked, stirring to prevent the coconut milk from splitting.
Remove from the heat and serve with fried shallots sprinkled on top.

Combine all the wrapper ingredients and mix until smooth. Strain the batter.
Heat a nonstick pan and make thin crepes. Repeat until all the batter is used.
For the filling, heat the oil and sauté the shallots and garlic until fragrant. Add the opor seasoning and mix well. Add the chicken and potatoes, then stir to combine.
Pour in the water and cook until it has reduced.
Take one wrapper and add some filling. Dip it in the flour mixture.
Coat with breadcrumbs and repeat until all the rolls are prepared. Fry over medium heat until cooked and golden brown. Remove and drain.

Fry the chicken until golden, then set aside. Grind the toasted spices until smooth and set aside.
Grind all the remaining spices except the Indonesian bay leaves and lemongrass. Combine this spice paste with the previously toasted and ground spices, then sauté until golden. Add the chicken and pour in all the coconut milk.
Add the grated pineapple, salt, and seasoning powder. Taste and adjust the seasoning. If it needs more acidity, add tamarind. Cook until the chicken is tender and the sauce reaches your preferred thickness.
The chicken opor is ready to serve. You don't have to wait for Eid to enjoy it. Serve with ketupat or lontong, as preferred.

Sauté the shallots until golden brown, then add the kaffir lime leaves and lemongrass.
Add the instant seasoning, coconut milk, and water. Stir well, then add the chicken.
Cook until the chicken is fully cooked.
Ready to serve.
strIngredient2: Small pack of instant coconut milk

strMeal: Ayam Opor Ala Mba Sari's Kitchen
strInstructions:
Clean the chicken and prepare the spice paste, aromatics, and coconut milk.
Blend the dry spices (coriander and peppercorns), then blend the wet spice paste ingredients (shallots, garlic, candlenuts, turmeric, and ginger).
Sauté the spice paste with the lemongrass, Indonesian bay leaves, kaffir lime leaves, and galangal until fragrant. Add the chicken pieces and stir until the chicken changes color.
Pour in the coconut milk and cook over medium heat, stirring gently to prevent it from splitting. Cook until the chicken is tender and the seasoning has infused the meat. Taste and adjust the seasoning.
Add the water and continue cooking over medium heat until the chicken is partially cooked. Add the palm sugar, salt, and powdered stock, then stir well.
Serve the chicken opor in a bowl and sprinkle with fried shallots if desired.
strIngredient7: Cooking oil for sautéing the spices

strInstructions:
Heat Rose Brand cooking oil in a pan and sauté the ground spice paste.
Once it is no longer raw, add all the whole aromatics.
Stir well and add the chicken. Toss until the seasoning coats the entire surface of the chicken and the chicken releases its juices.
Add the water and wait for it to boil.
Once boiling, add Rose Brand instant coconut milk, followed by the tofu and egg.
Cook until it begins to simmer, stirring occasionally. Add the seasonings and don't forget the Rose Brand Asatu MSG. Continue cooking until everything is done.
The chicken opor is ready to serve.

Peel and cut the potatoes, then fry until a skin forms. Remove and set aside. Cut the tofu as desired and fry until a skin forms, then set aside.
Briefly boil the chicken, discard the water, and set the chicken aside. Grind the spices until smooth.
Sauté the spice paste until fragrant and cooked through. Add the Indonesian bay leaves, kaffir lime leaves, and bruised lemongrass, then add the chicken and water. Bring to a boil.
Add the tofu, potatoes, coconut milk, salt, sugar, and seasoning powder. Stir well and adjust the seasoning.
Ready to serve.

Prepare all the ingredients.
Mix the coconut milk with the cleaned chicken. Sauté the sliced shallots until fragrant, then add the ground spice paste and sauté until dry. Add a little coconut milk and the whole aromatics. Finally, add the chicken and all the remaining coconut milk.
Stir well and add the seasonings. Cook until the chicken is fully cooked and the seasoning has infused the meat. Taste and adjust the seasoning. Ready to enjoy.

Prepare the ingredients. Boil the chicken until tender, discard the first batch of cooking water, then replace it with fresh water for the broth. Cut the winter melon as desired.
Sauté the ground spices and aromatics until cooked through. Add them to the chicken broth and bring to a boil. Add the winter melon and bring to a boil again.
Add the coconut milk and stir gently. Season to taste and bring to a boil once more. Adjust the seasoning as desired, then serve.

strMeal: Opor Ayam Dan Tahu Bumbu Instan
strInstructions:
Bring the water to a boil. Add the chicken and bring it back to a boil.
Add the instant opor seasoning, lemongrass, Indonesian bay leaves, ground coriander, ground pepper, salt, and Rose Brand coconut milk. Stir well and adjust the seasoning. Add the tofu and stir occasionally. Cook until the chicken is tender and fully cooked.
Serve the chicken and tofu opor with white rice.

strMeal: Opor Ayam Bumbu Instan Dengan Santan
strInstructions:
Prepare the ingredients. I only had kaffir lime leaves; I didn't have the others and was too lazy to get them! You can add Indonesian bay leaves and lemongrass if you like.
There was a misunderstanding with my husband. He thought I wanted the chicken filleted, so he deboned it. Hahaha!
Simmer the chicken over medium heat for about 15 minutes, until halfway cooked. Then add the seasoning.
Cover and continue simmering for another 10 minutes. I left it while I took a shower (oops!).
Add the coconut milk and stir over low heat for just 3 minutes.
It's ready! Four pieces of chicken were finished in one meal by my two kids. Unbelievable!

Prepare all the ingredients.
Cook the chicken for 10 minutes, then set it aside.
Grind the spice paste ingredients until smooth.
First, sauté the sliced shallots, galangal, ginger, lemongrass, Indonesian bay leaves, and kaffir lime leaves until softened. Add the ground spice paste and sauté until cooked through.
Pour in 500 ml of water and add the seasonings.
Add the chicken, carrots, potatoes, and 65 ml of coconut milk. Cook until everything is done.
Transfer to a bowl and enjoy the chicken opor with potatoes and carrots.

Toast the cumin and coriander seeds until golden brown. Blend all the spice paste ingredients until smooth, then set aside.
Coarsely slice the shallots and bruise the lemongrass and galangal. Sauté the sliced shallots with the lemongrass, galangal, Indonesian bay leaves, and kaffir lime leaves until the shallots are golden brown.
Add all the blended spices and sauté until cooked through. Turn off the heat, transfer the seasoning to a pot, and let it cool.
Add the chicken to the pot and coat it with the seasoning. Marinate for 1 hour or longer.
Once marinated, pour in the thin coconut milk. You don't need to use it all if you think there's enough. Cook until the mixture boils, then add salt, sugar, and mushroom stock powder. Stir well.
Add the medium-thick coconut milk and cook, stirring, until the chicken is tender.
Serve the white chicken opor with warm rice.

Prepare all the ingredients.
Heat the oil in a pan and sauté the ground spice paste until fragrant. Add the aromatics, then add the chicken and stir. Pour in the water and thin coconut milk. Cook using the 5-30-7 method. Add salt and powdered stock to taste.
Add the remaining coconut milk and continue cooking, tasting and adjusting the seasoning. Turn off the heat when the flavor is right.
Serve.

strMeal: Opor Ayam Fillet & Kentang Creamy, 4 Bahan Praktis
strInstructions:
Prepare the ingredients. Cut the chicken into large cubes and slice or dice the potatoes.
Sauté the ready-made opor seasoning until fragrant.
Add the chicken and sauté until it is halfway cooked or fragrant.
Add a little water.
Add the potatoes and stir well.
Pour in the coconut milk and stir.
Cook until the chicken is done, the potatoes are tender, and the sauce has thickened slightly.
Yummy!

strMeal: Opor Ayam Tahu Telur Bumbu Kari
strInstructions:
Prepare the ingredients. Rinse the chicken and cut it as desired. Peel the boiled eggs and rinse the tofu under running water, then drain. Slice the shallots and garlic, and bruise the lemongrass.
Sauté the shallots, garlic, and curry powder in oil until fragrant. Add the aromatics, then add the chicken and stir until its color changes. Pour in the water.
Season with salt, sugar, and pepper. Add the tofu and boiled eggs, then cook until the broth boils and the chicken is tender. Pour in the coconut milk and stir gently.
Cook over low heat until the chicken is fully cooked and the seasoning has infused the ingredients. Add the sliced scallion, stir briefly, then remove from the heat and serve.
Serve with warm white rice. Delicious! Enjoy your meal.

Pour the water into a pan and add the instant opor seasoning. Stir well.
Add the chicken thighs to the seasoned water and cook until tender.
Add 1 sachet of thick instant coconut milk and cook until the broth comes to a boil.
Transfer the chicken to a bowl, then pour the broth over it.
The chicken opor is ready to serve.
One, two, three—cheese!

Prepare all the ingredients for cooking. The tofu and some of the seasonings weren't photographed.
Boil the chicken with the Indonesian bay leaves and lemongrass until the chicken is halfway cooked, occasionally skimming off any impurities or fat that rise to the surface.
Add the instant opor seasoning and stir. Add the tofu and bring to a boil. Pour in the coconut milk and stir. Bring to a boil again, then taste and adjust the seasoning.

strMeal: 1319. Opor Paha Ayam Fillet Tanpa Santan
strInstructions:
🍗 Boil the chicken in 500 ml of water until partially cooked. In a separate pan, fry the tofu until cooked to serve with the opor.
🍗 Prepare all the ingredients and wash them thoroughly. Blend or grind all the spice ingredients until smooth, then sauté until fragrant.
🍗 Add galangal, lemongrass, Indonesian bay leaves, kaffir lime leaves, and palm sugar to the ground spice mixture. Add about 100 ml of water and cook thoroughly to remove the raw spice aroma.
🍗 Pour the spice mixture into the pot with the chicken broth. Add the fried tofu and bring to a boil.
🍗 Add salt, granulated sugar, and powdered stock seasoning. Finally, add coconut milk (I skipped the coconut milk). Stir continuously to prevent the coconut milk from curdling.
🍗 Once cooked, transfer to a serving dish.

Thinly slice the kaffir lime leaves and turmeric leaves, removing the tough parts.
Blend the spices until smooth.

Grind the spices for braising the meat, such as shallots, garlic, and candlenuts, then set aside. You can also buy them already ground at the market.
Grind the dry spices, including pepper, cumin, and coriander, until very fine, then set aside.
Cut the beef into pieces about half the size of your fist. Wash thoroughly and set aside.

Add salt and seasoning, then adjust to taste. Continue cooking until thickened and boiling.

strInstructions:

strInstructions:

Cut the meat as desired. Thinly slice the spices so they are easier to blend.
Fry the cashews and toast the grated coconut, then crush them.

Crushed toasted coconut.
Crushed cashews.

Grill the beef.

strInstructions:

Thread the cooked chicken onto skewers and grill it in a nonstick pan.
Add rice flour to the remaining broth and stir until thickened.
Serve with boiled bean sprouts and boiled cassava leaves, then pour the sauce over the satay.

Wash the goat meat thoroughly and cut it into fairly large pieces. Prepare the spices.
Put the orange spice paste in a pan along with the aromatic spices and turn on the heat. Once hot, add the meat and stir well.

Remove the meat and set it aside for skewering. Remove the aromatic leaves as well.
Add rice flour to the remaining broth and cook again until thickened into satay sauce.
Brush the skewered meat with satay oil.
Grill the satay on a nonstick pan or over charcoal.
Serve with rice cakes, pour over the thick satay sauce, and sprinkle with fried shallots.

Making Padang satay is so worth the effort—not only is it satisfying to eat, but honestly, it's tastier and very affordable.
Prepare the spices. Blend the garlic, shallots, red chilies, coriander, candlenuts, ginger, turmeric, and galangal until smooth, then sauté until fragrant. Set aside.
Prepare the meat and beef tongue. I boiled the lungs, intestines, and tripe separately beforehand.
Boil the tripe, intestines, and lungs separately, discard the water, then boil them again.
Heat 1 L of water and cook with the whole spices until boiling. Add the remaining ground spice paste and the reserved meat and tongue broth. Adjust the flavor; it should be slightly salty, and you can adjust the spiciness to taste. Add chopped scallions.
Add the rice flour dissolved in water and the ground toasted coconut mixture. I used 200 ml of Kara coconut milk. Stir and adjust the thickness.
Thread the meat onto skewers. This is only half of the tongue, meat, and other ingredients I cooked. Grill over charcoal or in a pan until smoky.

Padang satay is ready to serve. 🤗 Happy Eid al-Adha!

Grind the spices, then sauté until fragrant. Add the leaves and cook until done.

strInstructions:

strInstructions:

Add the beef and mix well.

Finally, add the scallions and celery, stir briefly, then remove from the heat.

Clean the eggplants, cut them as desired, and rinse thoroughly. Fry or boil until softened, then set aside.
Grind all the spice-paste ingredients. Heat the cooking oil and sauté the paste until fragrant, then add the kaffir lime leaves and cook until softened.
Add the eggplants, water, and coconut milk.
Season with salt and stock powder, stirring gently. Add the basil leaves and sliced shallots, then cook briefly until the basil wilts.
The coconut milk eggplant pecel is ready to serve.

Preheat a clay pan for about 10 minutes. Dry-roast the peanuts over low heat until cooked.
Spread the roasted peanuts on a winnowing tray and let them cool until warm. Remove the peanut skins, then winnow to separate the skins.
Prepare all the seasonings.
Dry-roast the two types of chilies and the garlic.
Combine all the seasonings with the peanuts, then take them to a grinding mill to be ground. After grinding, mix again until evenly combined and smooth.
Madiun-style pecel sambal is ready to serve.
strIngredient2: Large red chilies, cut into pieces
strIngredient7: Kaffir lime leaves, central veins removed

strInstructions:
Coarsely grind the spice-paste ingredients.
Sauté the paste in a little oil until fragrant. Pour in the water and bring to a boil. Add the banana blossom and cook for about 5–10 minutes to absorb the flavors.
Mix 65 ml of coconut milk with a little broth, then pour it back into the pot. Stir gently and cook briefly over low heat. Finally, add the salt. Check the seasoning and remove from the heat.
The banana blossom pecak with coconut milk is ready to serve.
strIngredient1: Medium banana blossom, boiled, drained, and shredded

strInstructions:
Peel the eggplants partially, leaving some skin on, then cut into pieces. Soak them in water to prevent discoloration. Set aside.
Sauté the spice paste, kaffir lime leaves, and galangal until fragrant. Add a little water and the eggplant. Stir briefly, then let the seasonings absorb into the eggplant. Once the flavors have infused, add the powdered coconut milk and basil leaves.
Stir briefly and taste. Once the flavor is right, turn off the heat. The eggplant and basil pecel is ready to accompany lunch.

Dry-roast the peanuts without oil until cooked.
Blend until smooth or to your preferred texture, then transfer to a bowl.
Heat a little oil and sauté the garlic, green chilies, curly chilies, kencur, ginger, and kaffir lime leaves until cooked.
Grind the seasonings with the palm sugar, salt, and tamarind liquid until smooth.
Add the ground seasoning mixture to the bowl of ground peanuts and mix until evenly combined. The pecel sauce is ready to use.
strIngredient7: Kaffir lime leaves, central veins removed

strInstructions:
Cut the chicken into 5 pieces.
Blend all the ingredients for the chicken braising spice paste. Braise the chicken in the paste until tender.
Fry the chicken until golden brown.
For the shrimp paste sambal: boil all the ingredients, then blend coarsely. Fry in a little oil until thoroughly cooked.
Serve with warm rice, fresh lettuce, and tempeh alongside the chicken.
strIngredient3: Spice paste for braising the chicken

strInstructions:
Prepare all the ingredients. Blend the grated coconut with 100 ml of water, then strain. Boil the eggplant with the seasonings for 20 minutes until cooked, then grind the boiled seasonings.
Put the coconut milk and ground seasonings into a pan. Add the eggplant and gently press it down a little. Add sugar and salt, then check the seasoning. Once it boils, remove from the heat immediately.
Serve with warm rice.
strIngredient10: Kaffir lime leaf, central vein removed

strInstructions:
Fry the peanuts until golden brown. Once cooled, pulse them coarsely in a food chopper or to your preferred texture, then set aside.
Fry the shallots, garlic, ginger, kencur, and chilies. Once cooled, grind them with the salt until smooth.
Add the palm sugar and grind again until soft. Add the chopped peanuts and mix well. Sprinkle with fried scallions. The mixture is ready to store or use immediately.

Heat the oil, then sauté the spice paste until fragrant and cooked.
Add the chicken and stir briefly. Add the cabbage or mustard greens, scallions, and celery. Cook until the vegetables begin to wilt.
Add the egg noodles, then season with sweet soy sauce, salt, and stock powder to taste.
Stir until everything is evenly combined and the noodles are cooked. Adjust the seasoning.
Remove from the heat and serve warm with pecel peanut sauce to taste.

Prepare all the ingredients. Soak the rice vermicelli in hot water until softened, then drain. Soak the tofu skin until soft, then drain.
Scramble the egg, then add the scallions and carrots. Stir until softened.
Sauté the spice paste until fragrant, then add the sweet soy sauce and a little water. Add the rice vermicelli and tofu skin.
Stir the vermicelli until the seasonings are absorbed. Adjust the seasoning.
Serve the fried rice vermicelli with pecel sauce, puli crackers (rice crackers), and a sprinkling of fried shallots.

Heat the oil and fry the egg and tofu until cooked on both sides. Drain.
While frying, pour boiling water over the bean sprouts until wilted, then drain.
This recipe uses ready-to-mix pecel sauce. Arrange the tofu and egg on a plate, then top with the bean sprouts.
Pour the pecel sauce over the top and sprinkle with celery and fried shallots. Serve. Add sweet soy sauce if desired.

strMeal: Tahu Goreng Sambal Pecel Ala Ibu

Marinate the tofu, then score its surface.
Prepare the other ingredients as well.
Fry the marinated tofu until golden and fairly crisp, then remove and set aside.
Arrange the vegetables and fried tofu, then pour the pecel sauce over them. This is especially delicious with salted fish and fresh petai beans.

Grate the coconut, add water, and squeeze out the coconut milk until you have 500 ml. Set aside.

Put the remaining coconut milk in a pot with the salt, granulated sugar, and pandan leaf. Bring to a boil.

To serve, peel the bananas and spoon some rice flour porridge over them.
Ready to serve.

Prepare the fried peanuts.
Heat the oil and add the red chilies, red bird's eye chilies, kencur, garlic, and kaffir lime leaves. Fry until the chilies soften. Combine the peanuts with all the seasonings and the oil used to fry the spices, then grind or blend until smooth.

strIngredient5: Kaffir lime leaves, central veins removed

Fry the garlic, shallots, bird's eye chilies, curly chilies, and kencur. Bring water to a boil and add the sliced cabbage. Once wilted, remove and drain. Add the sliced squash and cook until wilted, then remove and drain. Repeat with the water spinach. Finally, boil the eggs. Steam the potatoes separately.

Cut the rice cakes into pieces and place them on a plate with sliced cucumber.
Add sliced omelet, chopped fried tofu, and bean sprouts. Pour the pecel sauce over everything.

Roast the eggplant over low heat until soft and fully cooked. Peel off the outer skin and set aside.
Fry the chilies, garlic, sand ginger, candlenuts, and shrimp paste until softened. Remove and grind until smooth, then add salt, sugar, and MSG.
Pour the coconut milk into the sambal and mix well. Add water as needed.
Pour the sand ginger sambal over the roasted, peeled eggplant and serve. Grilled tempeh and boiled eggs can be added as accompaniments.

strInstructions:
Prepare the spinach and bean sprouts, wash thoroughly, and drain. (You can use other vegetables according to your preference or what you have available, such as mustard greens or carrots.) Place the pecel seasoning in a bowl. Gradually add hot water while stirring with a spoon until the sauce is mixed and sufficiently thick. You can add sweet soy sauce if desired.

Add the ground seasoning to the sugar syrup, stir well, and cook until slightly thickened. Remove from the heat and let cool.

Prepare all the ingredients. Peel alternating strips of the cucumber skin, then cut into small slices.

Prepare the ingredients and heat the cooking oil.

Air-fry at 180°C for 6 minutes or grill in a nonstick pan. Then serve coated with the rujak seasoning.

Mix the water and granulated sugar, bring to a boil, then let cool.

Wash the starfruit thoroughly and cut it as desired.
Put all the Bangkok seasoning ingredients in a bowl. Stir until evenly combined.

Combine the finely shaved palm sugar, salt, powdered shrimp paste, and Bon Cabe in a bowl. Mix well.
Pour the sauce mixture over the fruit. Serve it as a dipping sauce or mix it directly with the fruit.
Ready to enjoy! ☺️

strMeal: Cambodian Spiced Pineapple | Rujak Nanas Ala Kamboja

Grind the bird's eye chili, garlic, tamarind, salt, and shrimp paste until smooth.
Add the palm sugar and drinking water, then grind until smooth.
Serve the rujak sauce with pieces of fruit.

Toast the shrimp paste until cooked. Peel the semi-ripe mango, wash it thoroughly, and cut it into pieces as desired.
Place the long mango strips in a container with a lid. Add salt and palm sugar.

The flavor is a delicious mix of spicy, salty, and sweet, with a noticeable shrimp-paste taste. So good!

Briefly boil the bean sprouts, then drain.
Fry until golden brown, then drain.
Grind the garlic, chilies, palm sugar, and salt. Add freshly squeezed lime juice.
Place the boiled bean sprouts on a plate, add pieces of tofu and cucumber, then pour the sauce over them and drizzle with sweet soy sauce.

Wash the chilies thoroughly. Combine them with a pinch of salt and a pinch of shrimp paste, then grind until smooth. Add the palm sugar and grind again.
Add 1 tbsp of pomelo pulp and grind so the sugar begins to dissolve slightly.
Add the remaining pomelo pulp and mix well.

Boil the cuko sauce ingredients until the sugar dissolves, then taste and adjust the seasoning. Set aside.
Place the noodles in a serving bowl, arrange the toppings, and pour the sauce over them.

Wash the cucumbers thoroughly, then shred them using a cheese grater.
Add salt and Rose Brand granulated sugar. Mix evenly until the sugar dissolves.
Pour in cold water or drinking water and mix well. Taste and adjust as needed. If using drinking water, refrigerate it first to chill. I use ice cubes to cool it faster. 😅😀🙏🏻 Enjoyy..😘😘

Make the rujak seasoning by combining all the seasoning ingredients and grinding them until smooth.

Peel the crystal guava and cut it into pieces as desired.
Add the tamarind seasoning and sugar.
Place everything in a container or lunch box.

strMeal: Rujak Es Krim Jogja – Healthy Premium Version

Freeze the Greek yogurt, blend until smooth, then freeze it again.
Grind the chilies, palm sugar, salt, and shrimp paste until smooth. Strain.
Add drinking water and tamarind water, then mix well.
Add the shredded mango to the sauce and refrigerate for 1–2 hours.
Serve the shredded rujak in a bowl, topped with two scoops of yogurt ice cream.

Serve the fruit either by dipping it into the rujak sauce or mixing everything together. This version is served with the sauce on the side. Madura-style rujak is also often served with fried tofu, boiled krai cucumber, and crackers.

strInstructions:
Boil the peeled, chopped young jackfruit until tender. Remove and drain, then set aside.
Grind the garlic, candlenuts, aromatic ginger, and coriander. Set aside.
Boil the chicken bones and the previously boiled young jackfruit. Add the ground spices and bring to a boil.
Add galangal, bay leaves, salt, MSG, palm sugar, and instant coconut milk. Taste and adjust the seasoning.
Stir until everything is evenly combined and cook until the liquid reduces.

Clean the young jackfruit. I cut it into fairly large pieces. Prepare the spice paste and grind it until smooth.

strInstructions:

Cook the jackfruit until the liquid has reduced so the gudeg will keep longer.

Place all the seasonings in a pot. Add water, coconut sugar, and sweet soy sauce.

Line the inside of a cone-shaped rice mold with banana leaves. Add the red rice and press it firmly.

Bring the manggar (young coconut flower stalks) to a boil, rinse thoroughly, and discard the water.
Layer the ingredients in a pot in this order, from the bottom: young teak leaves, beef ribs, manggar, ground spice paste, lemongrass, bay leaves, kaffir lime leaves, thin coconut milk, sugar, and salt.
Pour in the thick coconut milk and cook until the liquid has reduced. Adjust the seasoning to taste.

Arrange the guava leaves, bay leaves, kaffir lime leaves, lemongrass, galangal, and ginger at the bottom of the pot.

Prepare the ingredients and seasonings. Grind the spices, then sauté until fragrant. Add the bay leaves, galangal, and palm sugar.

strInstructions:

Add the tofu and young jackfruit to the sautéed spices. Add the coconut milk and water, followed by the green bird's eye chilies, palm sugar, salt, pepper, and flavor enhancer. Once the mixture boils, add the krecek and cook until tender.

Boil the young jackfruit with a little salt for about 7 minutes at a rolling boil, adding young teak leaves. If unavailable, use 1/2 tsp baking soda instead; if neither is available, skip the coloring step.
Prepare the ground spices and aromatic seasonings. Blend the ground spices and bruise the aromatic ingredients.
Grind the turmeric separately with a mortar and pestle because blending it can stain the blender.
Sauté the blended spice paste in a little oil. Add the bruised aromatic ingredients, including the turmeric, and sauté until fragrant.
Pour in 2 L of water. I use the container that held the ground spices and fill it with water. Reduce the heat.
Once the water is hot, add the young jackfruit. Simmer over low heat with the lid on until it boils. Add the coconut milk, salt, powdered sugar, thinly sliced palm sugar so it dissolves easily, and flavor enhancer. Keep stirring after adding the coconut milk to prevent it from splitting. Once the coconut milk is cooked and fragrant, taste and adjust the seasoning. Cover briefly and cook until the liquid reduces slightly.
Ready to serve.
strIngredient2: Reddish young teak leaves; substitute baking soda if unavailable, or omit
strIngredient3: Turmeric as a substitute if red coloring is unavailable

strInstructions:
Wash the krecek thoroughly, then soak it in hot water until it expands. Drain. Wash the manisa squash, cut it in half, and grate it lengthwise.
Cut the tempeh as desired and cut the yardlong beans into pieces. Prepare the seasonings.
Grind the spices, then sauté them with the lemongrass and bay leaves until fragrant. Add the yardlong beans.
Add the manisa squash and stir until softened, then add the sliced tempeh.
Add water, coconut milk, salt, sugar, and stock powder.
Bring to a boil, then add the krecek that has been soaked in hot water. Cook until thoroughly done. Prepare the rice cakes.
Serve the vegetable rice cakes with egg gudeg and crackers.

Wash, cut, and boil the young jackfruit for 10 minutes.
Boil the quail eggs until cooked, then peel them.
Wash and bruise the galangal, lemongrass, bay leaves, and kaffir lime leaves.
Grind the garlic, shallots, and candlenuts into a paste.
Add the young jackfruit, quail eggs, water, coconut milk, tea bag, ground spice paste, bay leaves, kaffir lime leaves, galangal, lemongrass, chilies, palm sugar, salt, flavor enhancer, coriander, and sugar. Stir until evenly combined and boil until the liquid reduces.
Once the liquid has reduced, adjust the seasoning to taste.

Cook the gudeg a day ahead and make it fairly dry. Shred the chicken and chop the eggs. If you like it spicy, add whole or sliced chilies and cook them with the gudeg. I cook gudeg in a rice cooker; the longer it stays in the rice cooker, the drier it becomes. The recipe is attached: Easy, No-Scorch Rice Cooker Gudeg.
In a mixing bowl, combine the all-purpose flour, tang mien flour, granulated sugar, and yeast. Mix well.
Gradually add cold water. If 100 ml is enough to make the dough homogeneous, use only 100 ml. Knead until smooth and no longer sticky. Dough that is too soft can cause wrinkled steamed buns.
Add the white shortening without melting it first. Knead again until the dough is pliable. I knead by hand using a pulling motion similar to scrubbing clothes. Once pliable, shape the dough into a ball. Cover with a cloth or turn the mixing bowl upside down over it for 30 minutes, or until doubled in size.
Knead briefly again to make the dough more elastic. It does not need to pass the windowpane test; it just needs to be smooth and stretchable, about 80% elastic. Divide into 9 portions of about 45 g each. Shape into balls and arrange them in order. Keep the shaped dough and the pieces waiting to be shaped covered with a cloth to prevent them from drying out. Rest for 10 minutes.
Flatten the dough portions in the order in which they were shaped and rested. Fill each flattened piece with gudeg, shredded chicken, and chopped egg. Pinch two sides together to seal, then fold and pinch the remaining edges to form 6 pleats.
Place each filled bun on a piece of baking paper. Cover with a cloth and proof for 15–20 minutes. Do not let them proof too long, or they may wrinkle.
Heat the steamer until the water boils. Use a traditional steamer with a clean cloth wrapped around the lid.
Steam over medium-low heat for 10 minutes. Turn off the heat and leave the steamer covered for 2 minutes. Then open it and serve the buns warm.
At room temperature, the buns should be eaten within one day. Store them in a sealed container or wrap them in steamed-bun paper.
They keep for one week in the refrigerator and one month in the freezer. Steam again before serving.
strIngredient9: Easy, no-scorch rice cooker dry gudeg with chicken and eggs

strInstructions:
Boil the young jackfruit until tender, then drain.
Boil the ribs in enough water.
Grind the coriander, candlenuts, shallots, garlic, ginger, and galangal into a spice paste.
Sauté the paste in a little oil until fragrant. Add the bay leaves, kaffir lime leaves, and lemongrass.
Add the sautéed spices to the pot with the ribs and jackfruit.
Add the coconut milk and cook until done. Add sugar and salt, then adjust the seasoning to taste.
Enjoy!

Bring the water to a boil. Boil the young jackfruit with salt and baking soda for 7 minutes, then drain.
Heat a little oil and sauté the ground spice paste and aromatic seasonings.
Add the jackfruit, coconut milk, palm sugar, stock powder, salt, and pepper. Stir well and cover the pot. Cook over medium-low heat for 1 hour.
Set the eggs aside. Cook the jackfruit for another 5 minutes. Adjust the seasoning and serve.

Boil the young jackfruit for about 3 minutes and discard the water. Boil it again with bay leaves until tender, then drain. Prepare the Bamboe gudeg seasoning.
Boil the bones and meat until tender and the broth is flavorful.
Add the boiled jackfruit, tea bags, galangal, and Bamboe seasoning. Stir well.
Add the Javanese palm sugar, eggs, and coconut milk. Stir and cook, stirring occasionally.
Add salt to taste and, if desired, stock powder. Cook until the liquid reduces. Remove the tea bags just before serving.
Serve with spicy krecek sambal and chicken opor, if available.
strIngredient12: Spicy krecek sambal with cowpeas, served as a side dish

strMeal: Gudeg Daun Singkong Jogja Tanpa Daun Jati
strInstructions:
First, boil the young jackfruit with a little salt to remove its sap. Boil the eggs and cassava leaves as well.
Grind the spices. Slice and bruise the galangal and lemongrass.
Layer the ingredients in a pot in this order: some aromatic seasonings, some young jackfruit, some cassava leaves, some eggs, some ground spice paste, some palm sugar and salt, the chicken, sliced ginger, the remaining jackfruit, the remaining eggs, some more cassava leaves, the remaining aromatic seasonings, and finally the remaining ground spices, palm sugar, and salt. The key is to build several layers.
Slowly pour in the coconut milk. Cook the gudeg over medium-low heat. When the coconut milk boils and has reduced by half, taste and adjust the seasoning. Do not stir, or the ingredients may break apart. Check the flavor and liquid level regularly. Once the flavor is right and the liquid has nearly dried up, turn off the heat. This means the gudeg is ready. I cook mine for about 4–5 hours.
Serve with warm rice, spicy krecek sambal, shrimp-paste sambal, and crackers or peyek. Delicious! 🥰

strMeal: Gudeg Berkuah / Gudeg Presto / Gudeg Lengkap ▪︎ Edisi Kangen Gudeg Ibu
strInstructions:
Add the bay leaves, galangal, lemongrass, coconut milk, tea, water, and ground spice paste to a pressure cooker. Stir. Add half the jackfruit, place the chicken and eggs on top, then cover with the remaining jackfruit and add the palm sugar. Check that the jackfruit is sufficiently submerged in liquid.
Close the pressure cooker securely and cook over high heat. Once it starts hissing, reduce the heat and cook for 30 minutes. When the pressure has released, open the lid and taste. If needed, add a little palm sugar and salt, then cook briefly again. I prefer gudeg with some sauce. For a drier result, continue cooking until the liquid reduces. Ready to serve.
Optional: If using cassava leaves, wait until the steam has escaped, open the pressure cooker, add the cassava leaves to one side, making sure they are submerged in the sauce, and cook briefly again.
Optional: Pour areh, a savory coconut-milk sauce, over the gudeg for a richer, more complete dish.
strIngredient2: Young jackfruit, cut into fairly large pieces
strIngredient6: White parts of lemongrass stalks, bruised
strIngredient7: Black tea bag brewed in 200 ml water
strIngredient8: Water, or enough to cover the jackfruit
strIngredient9: Small pack of Kara coconut milk
strIngredient22: Daun singkong , rebus daun singkong rebus / lalap daun singkong▪︎

strInstructions:
Boil the eggs until cooked, then peel them.
Grind the shallots, garlic, coriander, and candlenuts into a paste.
Arrange the jackfruit, eggs, and teak leaves in a pot.
Add the palm sugar, ground spices, salt, sugar, and flavor enhancer to the pot containing the jackfruit, eggs, and teak leaves.
Pour in the thin coconut milk first, then cook for about 5 hours until the jackfruit is tender and the spices have been absorbed.
Add the thick coconut milk and cook for another 2–3 hours, allowing the liquid to reduce while leaving about three-quarters of the coconut milk.
Check the seasoning and serve. Happy Eid!

Put the bay leaves, young jackfruit, sugar, salt, tea bag, water, and eggs into a pressure cooker.
Add about 40% of the ground spice paste, or roughly half. Cook over low heat for 45 minutes after the pressure cooker starts hissing.
Sauté the remaining ground spice paste until fragrant. Add the kaffir lime leaves, lemongrass, and salt, followed by the coconut milk, chicken, and sugar. Cook until the coconut milk has reduced by about 60% and the sauce becomes oily, forming areh.
Serve the gudeg with shredded chicken and drizzle with the coconut-milk areh sauce. Serve with krecek or other side dishes.

Cut the young jackfruit into pieces and boil until tender. Drain.
Grind the spice ingredients.
Line the bottom of a pot with bay leaves and teak leaves. Add the young jackfruit, finely chopped palm sugar, ground spice paste, and coconut milk.
Add the thoroughly washed young jackfruit, finely chopped palm sugar, ground spices, and coconut milk. Cover the pot and cook over low heat until the liquid reduces.
Once the liquid has reduced, add the chicken, cover again, and cook until everything is done.
When everything is cooked and only a little liquid remains, adjust the seasoning with salt and granulated sugar.

Grind the spices. Wash the young jackfruit thoroughly, then boil it with bay leaves and salt. I use the 10-30-5 method. Boiling the jackfruit helps remove its sap.
Line the pot with banana leaves. Arrange all the ingredients in layers: I use teak leaves first, followed by bay leaves, young jackfruit, spices, eggs, chicken feet, and tea bags. Add the coconut milk and cook over medium heat until boiling.
Remember to cover the pot. Once it boils, reduce the heat to low. The teak leaves will give the dish a reddish-brown color. I added more instant coconut milk as well.
Cook until the liquid reduces and the color develops beautifully. Turn off the stove.
Serve with spicy krecek sambal. Tempeh Krecek Sambal Without Coconut Milk is a suitable side dish for gudeg.
strIngredient6: Teak leaves for lining the pot

strInstructions:
🔸️Prepare all the ingredients and seasonings.
🔸️🌿🧄🧅🥥
🔸️Blend the ingredients for the ground spice paste.
🔸️Prepare a pot and line it with banana leaves. Cover with bay leaves, lemongrass, galangal, and kaffir lime leaves. Arrange the palm sugar on top, then pour in the ground spice paste.
🔸️Add the young jackfruit, chicken, and boiled eggs. Place the tea bags on top.
🔸️Pour in the coconut milk and bring the gudeg mixture to a boil. After 1 hour, remove the tea bags.
🔸️Continue cooking over low heat for 4–8 hours.
🔸️Jogja-style chicken and egg gudeg is ready to serve! 😍👍
strIngredient12: Galangal, about 2 cm per piece, bruised

strInstructions:
Wash the jackfruit thoroughly, then boil until tender and drain. Boil the chicken until tender and drain. Peel the boiled eggs. Wash and drain the brown tofu. Set aside.
Prepare the ground spices, aromatic seasonings, and coconut milk. Blend the ground spices.
Heat a little oil and sauté the ground spices until fragrant. Add the Indonesian bay leaves, galangal, lemongrass, kaffir lime leaves, palm sugar, and salt. Stir well, then add the jackfruit, eggs, tofu, and chicken. Pour in the coconut milk. Cook until the liquid has reduced, stirring occasionally to prevent burning. Adjust the seasoning; gudeg is traditionally sweet.
Once the liquid has reduced and the jackfruit has changed color, turn off the heat. The jackfruit gudeg is ready to serve. It tastes even better with spicy krecek sambal for a sweet and spicy combination. Absolutely delicious!

Boil the chicken eggs for 10 minutes until cooked. Peel them.
Bring water to a boil and add the tea bags until the water becomes dark reddish-brown.
Add the young jackfruit to the tea water and boil for 10–15 minutes, or until it turns brownish.
Grind the shallots, garlic, candlenuts, and coriander with the salt.
Sauté the ground spices until fragrant. Add the galangal, Indonesian bay leaves, powdered stock, and chicken. Stir well, then add enough drinking water and adjust the seasoning. Let it come to a boil.
Add the boiled jackfruit, boiled eggs, and tofu. Pour in the coconut milk and stir well.
Add enough water and let it cook until the liquid reduces, taking care not to let it burn.
Serve with krecek sambal and shrimp crackers. Delicious!

Clean the young jackfruit, then boil until the water comes to a boil to remove its sap. For a darker gudeg, you can add a few teak leaves to the water. After boiling for 5 minutes, remove, drain, and cut into smaller pieces.
Blend the spices with a little water.
Arrange the jackfruit and eggs in a pot.
Add the medium-thick coconut milk, ground spices, and remaining ingredients.
Cook over medium heat until boiling, then reduce to the lowest heat and simmer for about 2 hours. Once the liquid has reduced, add the thick coconut milk. Continue cooking until only a little liquid remains.
For the coconut cream topping: place 300 ml of thick coconut milk in the freezer for 15 minutes so the liquid separates from the fatty cream, speeding up the cooking process. Remove it and scoop off the thick portion on top. Cook over medium heat, stirring continuously. Add a little salt and keep stirring until it boils and is ready to use.
After cooking for 3–4 hours, when only a little liquid remains, adjust the seasoning. If the taste is right, the gudeg and pindang eggs are ready to serve. For dry gudeg, continue cooking until all the liquid has evaporated. You can store this gudeg in the freezer for up to a month without changing its flavor.
strIngredient3: Thick coconut milk, 300 ml for the topping and 300 ml for the gudeg

strMeal: Gudeg Nangka Simple Tanpa Daun Jati
strInstructions:
Prepare all the ingredients.
Blend the ground spices and set aside. Arrange the whole spices, ground spices, and jackfruit in a pan. I use a large-diameter nonstick pan.
Pour in the coconut milk (instant coconut milk diluted with 650 ml water). Add enough white sugar, salt, and mushroom stock. Stir gently and taste. Do not make the seasoning too strong at first, as the liquid will reduce and the dish may become too salty or sweet. Adjust the seasoning once the liquid has reduced by half.
Cover and simmer for 2.5 hours, or 3 hours until the liquid has evaporated. Since I do not have a large pan lid, I used an enamel tray as a cover. After 2 hours, I added the boiled eggs and continued simmering until the liquid reduced. I then transferred everything to a medium-sized nonstick pan with a fitting lid.
This is how it looks after 3 hours of simmering.
Transfer the gudeg to a serving dish. This simple jackfruit gudeg, made without teak leaves, is ready to enjoy with warm white rice and krecek sambal. So delicious!

Clean the young jackfruit and cut it into small pieces. Mine turned out larger than intended. Briefly boil it in water with a little salt. Drain and set aside.
Grind the garlic, shallots, and candlenuts. In a bowl, combine the coconut milk, palm sugar, ground spices, tea leaves, and salt. Mix well.
Arrange the Indonesian bay leaves, kaffir lime leaves, lemongrass, and galangal at the bottom of the rice cooker pot. Add the young jackfruit and boiled eggs, if using. Pour in the coconut milk mixture. Switch the rice cooker to the cooking mode.
Cook until the rice cooker switches to warm. Remove the tea leaves. Stir well, then let it sit for at least 2 hours so the color darkens and the spices are fully absorbed. The gudeg is ready to serve.
strIngredient3: Tea bags or 1 large teak leaf
strIngredient8: Palm sugar; add more if you prefer it sweeter

strInstructions:
Coarsely grind the sambal ingredients and adjust the seasoning. Mix with the leunca and basil leaves. Squeeze lime juice over the mixture.
Serve with fried jukut leaves and salted fish. Delicious!
Hope this is helpful. Enjoy trying it!

Wash all the vegetables and cut them as desired, except for the basil leaves. Arrange everything in a bowl.
Toast all the ground spice ingredients, then grind them.
Add the ground spices, stevia as a substitute for palm sugar, salt, garlic powder, and 1/3 cup warm water to dissolve the peanut sauce ingredients. Stir until evenly combined and adjust the seasoning. Sprinkle with fried shallots and basil leaves. Enjoy cooking!

Wash and clean the roay beans, then roughly slice them. Prepare the seasonings.
Pound the seasonings, add the palm sugar, then add the roay beans and pound coarsely.
Taste and adjust the seasoning. Serve. This is especially refreshing to enjoy at midday!
