Pick the leunca berries and basil leaves, then wash thoroughly.
Grind the seasonings.
Add the leunca and pound just enough to crack the berries. Add the basil leaves.
The karedok is ready to enjoy.

Clean the vegetables. Cut the cucumber and round eggplants into small pieces, finely slice the cabbage, and cut the long beans into small pieces. Prepare the bean sprouts.
Place the garlic, chilies, kencur, salt, Rose Brand granulated sugar, and palm sugar in a mortar and grind until smooth.
Add the fried peanuts and tamarind water, then grind further. Add Rose Brand Asatu seasoning powder.
Grind until the sauce is smooth and adjust the seasoning. Add the chopped fresh vegetables and bean sprouts, then mix until evenly coated with the sauce.
Ready to serve.
strIngredient1: Long beans, cut into small pieces
strIngredient2: Bean sprouts, cleaned and rinsed with hot water
strIngredient3: Round eggplants, cut into small pieces

strInstructions:
Clean all the vegetables and cut them into small pieces.
Using a mortar and pestle, grind the salt, chilies, kencur, peanuts, and palm sugar. Once smooth, add all the vegetables and mix well. Ready to serve.

Prepare all the ingredients and wash the vegetables thoroughly. Cut the long beans, cabbage, and cucumber as desired.
Prepare the peanuts, garlic, chilies, salt, kencur, and kaffir lime leaves. Pound all the seasonings until somewhat smooth, then add the palm sugar and continue pounding until smooth. Add enough water and pound while stirring until evenly combined.
Mix the vegetables with the peanut sauce and lime juice, then stir well.
The karedok is ready to serve with crackers.

Cut the washed long beans into small pieces.
Pound the seasonings, remembering to add salt and sugar.
Once smooth, add the long beans and pound again. Ready to serve.

Coarsely chop the peanuts and set aside.
Put all the other ingredients, except the boiled potato, into a spice blender.
Add 50 g of the coarsely chopped peanuts.
Blend until completely smooth.
Pour into a bowl and mix with the remaining coarsely chopped peanuts. This gives the sauce a texture similar to one made by hand with a mortar and pestle.
Adjust the seasoning.
To make karedok, mix the sauce with raw vegetables such as cabbage, basil, long beans, small eggplants, and bean sprouts.
To make lotek, mix the sauce with mashed boiled potato, then add boiled vegetables of your choice.
The sauce can be stored in the refrigerator for 1 week or in the freezer for 1 month.
strIngredient1: Fried or roasted peanuts or cashews

strInstructions:
Finely slice the cleaned cabbage and long beans. Cut the cucumber and eggplant into somewhat larger pieces.
Pound all the sauce ingredients, including peanuts, garlic, chilies, boiled potato, and kencur, until smooth. Add the juice of the lime and mix well.
Once the sauce is ready, combine it with the chopped vegetables and stir until the peanut sauce is evenly distributed. Add fried shallots and crackers for extra savory flavor.

Prepare all the vegetables. Wash the bean sprouts, chopped long beans, sliced cabbage, and basil thoroughly, then rinse them with drinking water. Cut the cucumber and round green eggplants, then set aside.
Fry the peanuts, then blend until smooth. Prepare the other ingredients for the ground seasoning.
Grind all the seasoning ingredients except the peanuts. Mix with the ground peanuts, adding water little by little until the sauce reaches your desired consistency. Adjust the seasoning.
Add all the vegetables and mix until evenly coated.
Transfer to a serving plate and serve.

Prepare a mortar and pestle. Add all the peanut sauce ingredients and pound them together. Add enough water to achieve your preferred sauce consistency.
Add all the thoroughly washed and drained vegetables, mix well, and serve.

Put the roasted peanuts, garlic, bird's eye chilies, tamarind, and water in a blender. Blend until smooth. Add the coconut sugar and mix well.
Fry the egg until cooked. Arrange the carrot, bean sprouts, cabbage, and cucumber on a plate, then add the fried egg.
Pour the peanut sauce over the ingredients, then add crackers and sweet soy sauce. Serve.

Cut the basreng into your preferred size.
Place the basreng in cold oil, then fry until cooked.
Pound all the sambal ingredients. Add the fried basreng and mix until evenly coated.
Ready to serve.

Heat the steamer. Steam the bananas until cooked, then cut them into pieces. I split mine lengthwise before cutting them into smaller pieces.
Mix the grated coconut with salt, then steam it with the pandan leaves for 10 minutes. Mix with the bananas.
Serve warm.
strIngredient1: Ripe horn bananas, but not too soft
strIngredient2: Pandan leaves, tied in a knot

strMeal: Urap Bayam, Tauge, Dan Kacang Panjang
strInstructions:
Clean and trim the long beans, bean sprouts, and spinach. Boil until cooked, then drain.
Grind the garlic, chilies, kencur, shrimp paste, salt, and sugar until smooth.
Mix the ground spices with the grated coconut and stir well. Add a little water, cover, and cook over low heat until done.
Arrange the urap as desired and serve.

Bring a pot of water to a boil. Add the winged beans and long beans. After 2 minutes, add the bean sprouts and boil for just another 2 minutes.
Stir well, then remove the vegetables and drain.
Sauté the ground spices until fragrant. Add water, grated coconut, salt, sugar, stock seasoning, and shrimp paste.
Stir well.
Add the boiled vegetables and mix again.
Taste and adjust the seasoning.
Let it sit for a while so the spices can soak in. And it's ready! 🤤🤤🤤
strIngredient5: Water, salt, stock seasoning, and sugar
strIngredient7: A pinch of powdered shrimp paste

strInstructions:
Combine the glutinous rice, coconut milk, pandan leaves, and water. Cook until the water has been absorbed and the rice is partially cooked.
Steam the glutinous rice with the additional pandan leaves for 15 minutes. Transfer to a container, add the grated coconut, and mix well.
Steam the glutinous rice and grated coconut together again for 15 minutes, or until cooked.
Transfer to a container and let the steam escape and the mixture cool slightly. Press into plastic food containers or molds. Add more grated coconut on top.
Serve.

Sauté the ground spices until fragrant. Add water, grated coconut, salt, sugar, and stock seasoning. Stir-fry for a little while.
Add the jackfruit and stir-fry again. Taste and adjust the seasoning.
Let the spices soak in, and it's ready! 🤤🤤
strIngredient2: Salt, sugar, stock seasoning, and water
strIngredient6: A pinch of powdered shrimp paste

strInstructions:
Prepare the ingredients. Peel the taro over a clean cloth. After peeling, wipe off the sap with a tissue or dry cloth. Cut into pieces as desired.
Heat the steamer. Place the taro pieces and grated coconut in a heatproof plastic bag inside the steamer. Cover tightly and steam for about 30 minutes. After 30 minutes, open the lid, sprinkle with salt and granulated sugar, cover again, and steam for another 5 minutes. Turn off the heat.
Serve with grated coconut sprinkled on top. Thank you 🙏🥰

Cut the vegetables into pieces, wash thoroughly, and boil in boiling water until cooked. Drain.
Toast the coconut, then grate it into long shreds. Slice the shallots and garlic, then fry them with the shrimp paste. Set aside.
Grind all the spices, then fry them with the kaffir lime leaves and Indonesian bay leaves until cooked and fragrant. Turn off the heat.
Add the boiled vegetables to the cooked spices. Add the grated coconut, sambal embe, and lime juice. Mix thoroughly.
The dish is ready to enjoy. Give this recipe a try!

Clean the vegetables, then steam until cooked. Cut them into thin, long strips, except for the bean sprouts.
Grind the spices, leaving the aromatic ingredients such as galangal whole.
Heat the oil and briefly sauté all the spices with the sugar and tamarind water. Add the grated coconut and cook, stirring until evenly combined and cooked through, but not dry, crispy, or browned. Add seasoning and adjust the taste.
Once cooked, mix the coconut seasoning with the other vegetables.

Use whatever vegetables you like. I just use whatever is in the fridge so they don't end up forgotten and fossilized!
Briefly boil or steam the vegetables; don't let them become too wilted. For unripe papaya, rub it with salt to remove the sap, let it sit for 10 minutes, then rinse.
Sauté the ground spices and kaffir lime leaves in 1 tbsp oil with a little water. Cook until boiling.
Add the palm sugar, salt, and grated coconut. Stir until evenly combined. Cook a little longer so the mixture cooks through. Taste and adjust the seasoning.
Mix the vegetables with the urap seasoning and serve.

Preparing the boiled vegetables for this dish doesn't take long, but it can be a bit of a hassle. The more varieties you use, the more chaotic it gets 😅😅. The urap seasoning itself is easy—just mix and stir.
Set aside a few spoonfuls of the boiled vegetables mixed with urap seasoning and roughly chop them. Take a spoonful of cooked rice and shape it into a small bowl. Put a teaspoon of the chopped vegetables inside.
Close and shape into a ball. Repeat until all the rice is used; you should get around 12 balls.
Ready to serve. Add crackers or chips for extra fun.

strMeal: Urap Ubi Jalar Kuning  Sarapan Ala Pedesaan
strInstructions:
Wash the sweet potatoes thoroughly and steam until cooked.
Mix the grated young coconut with salt, then steam for about 10 minutes.
Remove the sweet potatoes from the steamer, peel, and cut into pieces.
Sprinkle with the grated young coconut when serving.

Grate the coconut.
Add all the ground spices and other seasonings. Mix well.
Fry or dry-roast until fragrant.
Add salt, sugar, and flavor enhancer, then continue dry-roasting until fragrant. Taste and adjust the seasoning. Once it tastes right, turn off the heat. Remove from the pan and serve.
Delicious! 👍👍 Serve with bean sprouts if desired. Time to dig in 🤭🤭.
strIngredient1: Coconut, neither too young nor too mature

strInstructions:
Boil the thoroughly washed cassava leaves in boiling water mixed with baking soda and salt. This helps keep the leaves green and makes them tender more quickly.
Once the leaves are tender, drain immediately and let them cool. Squeeze out any remaining water.
To make the serundeng seasoning, grind the spices and mix them with the grated coconut. Steam for about 15 minutes, then briefly sauté to help it keep longer.
Lightly grease a pan with oil, spread it evenly, and heat briefly. Add the urap mixture. The oil helps prevent the coconut from sticking to the pan.
Taste and adjust the seasoning. Once it tastes right, it is ready to serve.
strIngredient9: Bird's eye chilies mixed with red and curly red chilies

strMeal: Urap Sayur Jawa Bumbu Kelapa Sangrai (Gurih, Pedas, Manis)
strInstructions:
Prepare the ingredients.
Dry-roast the grated coconut in a pan without oil over low heat until dry. Keep stirring so it doesn't burn. This is the key to making it last longer. Remove and let cool.
Grind the shallots, garlic, chilies, kencur, and galangal. Add the palm sugar, salt, tamarind, and kaffir lime leaves. Stir until the mixture is dry. Sauté without oil until fragrant and the moisture has evaporated.
Mix the toasted coconut with the sautéed spices. Stir well and taste. Let it cool completely before storing in a glass jar. It keeps for 3 days in the refrigerator!
Boil the vegetables and drain, then rinse with ice water to keep them crisp. When ready to eat, mix the vegetables with 3 tbsp of the urap seasoning and toss well.
strIngredient3: Long beans, cut into 3 cm pieces
strIngredient7: Do not boil together, so the colors stay vibrant
strIngredient15: Kaffir lime leaves, central veins removed

strInstructions:
Cut the mustard greens into pieces and wash thoroughly along with the bean sprouts.
Briefly boil the mustard greens and bean sprouts.
Grind the chilies, garlic, salt, sugar, and kaffir lime leaves. Grate the coconut and mix it with the ground spices.
The coconut sambal can be eaten raw for a fresh taste. To help it keep longer, steam it wrapped in banana leaves or fry it in a little oil.
Mix the sambal with the boiled vegetables.

Grind the spices. I also grind the dried tiny shrimp, but you can leave them whole if you prefer. Grate the coconut. Boil the cassava leaves first with a little salt and oil to help preserve their color, then slice them.
Sauté the spices until fragrant. Add the coconut and stir until evenly combined.
Add the cassava leaves and sugar and salt to taste. Cook until done.

Prepare the ingredients.
Wash the sea grapes thoroughly and remove the thick stems.
Pound or process the chilies, garlic, kencur, and shrimp paste. Mix with the grated coconut, add the seasonings, and taste.
Steam for about 15 minutes.
Remove and let cool, then mix with the sea grapes. Ready to enjoy.

Dry-roast the grated coconut separately until dry. Set aside. (Preparing and cooking takes almost an hour.)
Clean and grind the spices. Dissolve the tamarind in water and remove the seeds.
Sauté the ground spices in 4 tbsp oil. Add the palm sugar, sliced kaffir lime leaves, and tamarind liquid. Stir well.
Add the grated coconut and Indonesian bay leaves. Stir until all the seasonings are evenly combined. Taste again. The seasoning is ready to use for the following dish: vegetable urap.

Steam the coconut for 15 minutes. Since mine came from the freezer, I steamed it for 15 minutes, though 5 minutes may be enough.
Pound the shallots, garlic, red chilies, kaffir lime leaves, and kencur until smooth, then add salt and flavor enhancer.
Sauté the ground spices and add the palm sugar. Add the coconut and stir until evenly combined.
The urap seasoning can be enjoyed with bean sprouts, water spinach, cabbage, or long beans.

strMeal: Sayur Urap Selada Air Tauge Jipang/Labu Siam
strInstructions:
Coarsely grate the coconut. Grind the spices finely, then sauté them in a little oil. Add the palm sugar and stir well, then add the grated coconut and salt. Stir until the spices are thoroughly combined with the coconut and cooked through. Turn off the heat, stir occasionally, and set aside.
Prepare a variety of vegetables. I used whatever we had: watercress, bean sprouts, and small chayote. Clean them, remove the tails from the bean sprouts and pick the watercress leaves. Cut the chayote into long strips, briefly boil, and drain.
Arrange neatly on a serving plate, or mix everything together directly. It's especially delicious with warm rice and unsalted dried fish. So good! 😋

Take one eggplant and cut it into 8 pieces. I leave the stems on because they make convenient handles for holding and sucking the eggplant, Moms! Repeat with the remaining eggplants, then wash thoroughly.
Heat oil in a pan and fry the eggplant until half-cooked. I like it when the texture is still crunchy, so I only fry it halfway. If you prefer a softer texture, fry it until fully cooked. Remove and drain.
Grind the shallots, garlic, chilies, shrimp paste, tomatoes, and palm sugar until smooth.
Heat 2 tbsp oil in a pan and sauté the ground spices. Add salt and granulated sugar, stirring until fragrant. Add the Indonesian bay leaves, kaffir lime leaves, and galangal. Add the flavor enhancer and stir briefly. Pour in the water and bring to a boil. Add the eggplant and gently stir until evenly coated with the spices.
Taste and adjust the seasoning. Once it tastes right, transfer to a serving plate. The eggplant balado is ready to serve. Sprinkle fried shallots on top for an extra pretty finish.
strIngredient8: Small piece of Javanese palm sugar

strInstructions:
Cut the eggplants into pieces, fry until cooked, then drain. Fry the anchovies, remove, and drain.
Grind the chilies, shallots, and garlic into a paste.
Sauté the paste in oil until fragrant. Add the fried eggplant and anchovies, and mix well. Add mushroom stock powder, salt, and sugar. Cook briefly until the seasoning is absorbed. Remove from heat.
Ready to serve.

Grind the chilies, garlic, and shallots into a paste.
Briefly fry or sauté the eggplant until partially cooked, then set aside. You can also cook it directly without frying first to reduce the amount of oil used.
Heat oil over medium heat and sauté the spice paste until fragrant.
Add the kaffir lime leaves, Indonesian bay leaves, and galangal. Stir until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes and cook until softened.
Add a little water and stir well.
Add the balado seasoning powder, pepper, palm sugar, salt, and seasoning powder.
Add the eggplant and stir until the seasoning is absorbed. Taste and adjust as needed.
Cook until the liquid has reduced, then remove from heat.
The eggplant balado stir-fry is ready to serve with warm rice.

Prepare all the ingredients below 👇
Fry the eggplant first, then sauté the ground spices. Remember to add the aromatic seasonings and flavorings, and sauté until fragrant 😄
Add the remaining seasonings and the fried eggplant 🍆. Mix well and taste to adjust the seasoning.
Simple eggplant balado is ready to serve 🤭👌

Prepare the ingredients. Cut the eggplant as desired and soak it in salted water.
Heat Rose Brand cooking oil. Fry the eggplant until golden brown, then drain.
Slice the shallots and garlic. Grind the chilies and tomato with a little shrimp paste and salt. Use a little of the leftover frying oil to sauté the sliced shallots and garlic until fragrant, then add the ground chili mixture and sauté until fragrant. Add Asatu flavor enhancer.
Add the fried eggplant and mix well. Cook briefly until the seasoning is absorbed, taste and adjust, then remove from heat.
Serve.

Prepare the ingredients. Sprinkle salt over the eggplant and let it sit for 5 minutes, then rinse thoroughly and drain. Tip: This step is essential to reduce bitterness and prevent the eggplant from absorbing too much oil.
Heat the oil. Fry the eggplant until golden. Remove and drain on paper towels. Set aside. Fry the eggplant twice: first until partially cooked, then drain. It will be added to the sambal later. This helps keep it from falling apart and absorbing too much oil.
Blend all the ingredients for the spice paste together with the tomato.
Reduce the leftover frying oil, leaving 1 tbsp. Sauté the spice paste and sliced kaffir lime leaves until fragrant, fully cooked, and the oil separates, about 5 minutes over medium heat.
Add salt, sugar, stock powder, and tamarind water. Adjust the flavor to achieve a balance of spicy, savory, sweet, and refreshing notes.
Add the fried eggplant. Gently stir for just 1–2 minutes until evenly coated with the sambal. Turn off the heat.
Sprinkle with fried shallots if desired. Enjoy while warm!

Cut the eggplant, soak it in lime juice for 10–15 minutes, then drain and pat dry.
Fry the eggplant in hot oil for 3–4 minutes, then drain.
Slice the chilies, shallots, garlic, and tomato. Sauté them with the shrimp paste, kaffir lime leaves, and lemongrass in oil until the spices are fully cooked and the oil separates, about 7–10 minutes.
Add the sugar, salt, and mushroom stock. Mix well.
Add the fried eggplant and quickly stir for 1–2 minutes until coated with the seasoning. Adjust the taste, then remove from heat.

Boil the quail eggs until cooked. Peel them and prepare the other ingredients.
Pour enough Rose Brand cooking oil into a pan. Fry the eggplant until cooked, then remove.
Leave a little of the Rose Brand cooking oil used to fry the eggplant. Sauté the ground spice paste until fragrant and fully cooked. Add salt, stock powder, and Rose Brand granulated sugar.
Add just a little water and stir to keep the spices from burning. Add the quail eggs and eggplant. Cook until the seasoning is absorbed. Taste and adjust as desired.
Remove from heat and serve.

Heat enough oil. Fry the eggplant and fry the eggs sunny-side up. Set aside.
Heat a little more oil to sauté the ground spice paste. Add the whole spices and wait until fragrant. Add salt, sugar, and stock powder, and remember to taste and adjust the seasoning. Add the eggplant and fried eggs, then stir.
Once everything is evenly mixed, taste and adjust again. Remove from heat and serve 😉
strIngredient3: Oil for frying the eggplant and eggs

strInstructions:
Prepare all the ingredients and fry the eggplant. Set aside. Grind the chilies, shallots, garlic, and shrimp paste into a paste.
Heat vegetable oil in a pan. Add the lemongrass and bruised galangal and cook until fragrant. Add the ground spice paste and cook everything together until aromatic. Add salt, flavor enhancer, and granulated sugar, then taste and adjust.
Add the previously fried purple eggplant and mix well.
Enjoy!
strIngredient1: Medium purple eggplants, washed and cut into pieces
strIngredient7: Lemongrass, use the white part and bruise it

strMeal: Olahan Putih Telur Dengan Terong Balado
strInstructions:
Mix the egg whites with salt and ground pepper, then steam for 30 minutes until cooked. Set aside; they can be stored in the refrigerator for another dish.
Dice the eggplant, briefly soak it in water, and drain. Lightly coat it with flour.
Fry the eggplant in enough oil until browned, then drain.
Cut the steamed egg whites into pieces as desired.
Coarsely grind the sambal ingredients. Sauté them over medium heat with oil, adding a little water to help the chilies soften and cook through.
Arrange the egg whites and fried eggplant, then pour the balado sambal over the top. Serve.

🍆 Wash the eggplants thoroughly and cut as desired. Cut the tofu as desired, then fry it.
🍆 Heat the cooking oil and sauté the ground spice paste with the kaffir lime leaves until fragrant and cooked. Add the eggplant, stir well, then add enough water.
🍆 Add salt and granulated sugar and mix well. Add the previously fried tofu and stir. Cook until the eggplant is done.
🍆 Taste and adjust the seasoning. Eggplant and tofu balado is ready to serve with warm rice.
🍆 Enjoy trying this recipe 😊

Cut the eggplant and tofu into pieces as desired, then fry them separately. Set aside.
Blend the shallots, garlic, tomato, bird's eye chilies, paprika powder, and enough oil into a paste.
Heat a pan, add the spice paste, and sauté until fragrant. Add the Indonesian bay leaves and galangal. Stir until the oil separates.
Add the previously fried tofu and eggplant. Pour in enough water to mostly cover them.
Season with salt, Royco chicken seasoning, Sasa seasoning, and granulated sugar. Taste and adjust, then simmer until the liquid and seasoning have been absorbed, about 10 minutes.
Sprinkle with scallions before turning off the heat. Serve.

Grind the sambal ingredients into a paste.
Wash the fish and eggplant thoroughly, then fry them.
Sauté the ground spice paste until fragrant, then add salt, sugar, and mushroom stock.
Add the fish and eggplant and mix well. Cook until the seasoning is absorbed, then remove from heat.
strIngredient6: Ingredients for the ground spice paste

strInstructions:
Fry the eggplant until partially cooked. Sauté the ground spice paste in a little oil, then add the kaffir lime leaves and lemongrass.
Add salt, Royco seasoning, sugar, lime juice, and the previously fried eggplant.
Cook until the eggplant is done.
Enjoy! :) Don't forget to support the DAPUR PARIKAH YouTube channel;

Cut each eggplant in half, then cut each half into 3 pieces. Heat the oil and fry the eggplant until lightly browned. Drain when cooked.
Soak the dried shrimp in warm or cold water for 3 minutes, then drain and roughly chop.
Prepare a mortar and pestle or blender. Grind the red chilies, shallots, and garlic until partially smooth.
Sauté the ground spices in a little oil. Remember to add the seasonings: salt, sugar, MSG, and vinegar.
Once the spices are fragrant, add the dried shrimp and stir-fry until fragrant and cooked.
Arrange the eggplant on a plate, then spread the dried-shrimp sambal evenly on top, or add about half a spoonful to each piece of eggplant.
And there you go—dried-shrimp balado is ready to serve, with less oil and little fuss!
strIngredient7: Warm or cold water for soaking the dried shrimp

strInstructions:
Heat the cooking oil and sauté the ground spice paste until fragrant. Add the shrimp and mix well.
Add the sliced eggplant and mix well. Season with salt and sugar, add water, and cook until the eggplant is done.
Taste and adjust the seasoning. Round eggplant and shrimp balado is ready to serve.
Enjoy 😊

Wash the dried squid thoroughly, then briefly boil it to reduce its saltiness. Drain.
Cut the eggplant into pieces.
Heat the oil. Fry the squid and eggplant.
Sauté the shallots until softened. Add the ground chilies. When nearly cooked, add the kaffir lime leaves. Once cooked, turn off the heat and immediately add the fried squid and eggplant. Mix well. Let cool, transfer to a bowl, and serve.

Wash the eggplant thoroughly, then fry until partially cooked. Set aside.
Blend the ground spice ingredients with a little water, then sauté until the mixture is cooked and thickened. Add the flavor enhancer and cooking oil.
Add the eggplant to the seasoning and stir. Taste and adjust. Once the flavor is right, turn off the heat. The eggplant balado is ready to serve.

Prepare all the ingredients.
Fry the fish until the outside is crisp but not burnt. A crisp exterior helps keep the seasoning from making it soggy.
Briefly fry the eggplant for 2–3 minutes per side, until softened and browned around the edges. Tip: Sprinkle with salt and leave for 10 minutes, then rinse and squeeze gently. This helps reduce oil absorption.
Drain.
Grind all the spices. Sauté over low heat with 3 tbsp of the leftover frying oil for 8–10 minutes, until the oil separates and the color turns deep red. If the spices are undercooked, the balado will taste raw and spoil more quickly. The spices are ready when they smell fragrant rather than sharp and the red color deepens.
Add the fried fish and eggplant. Stir over high heat for just 1–2 minutes. This helps the seasoning cling while keeping the fish and eggplant dry. Do not cook too long or they will become soggy.
Taste and adjust. For a fresh, tangy flavor, add 1 tsp of lime juice just before removing from heat.
A plate of fish balado and eggplant balado is ready to make lunch irresistible 😋
strIngredient1: Fish, cut into 3 pieces and washed thoroughly; coat with salt and lime juice, leave for 10 minutes, then rinse again and pat dry with paper towels before frying. Dry fish is less likely to fall apart.
strIngredient2: Large eggplant, cut diagonally into 2 cm-thick slices
strIngredient5: Curly red chilies—for balanced heat and good color
strIngredient6: Red bird's eye chilies—add more for extra heat
strIngredient11: Granulated sugar, to balance the flavor

strInstructions:
Prepare all the ingredients. Cut the eggplant, scallions, onion, red chili, and green chili as desired.
Put all the seasonings in a bowl and mix well. Heat the cooking oil.
Sauté the onion and scallions over medium heat until fragrant. Add the eggplant and seasoning mixture, then stir until evenly combined. When the eggplant is halfway cooked, add the sliced chilies and stir again until evenly mixed. Once cooked, Korean-style eggplant balado is ready to serve.

Wash the chicken wings thoroughly. Coat with salt and lime juice, then let them sit briefly. Heat the oil and briefly fry the wings until their color changes. Remove and drain.
Sauté the ground spice paste in the remaining frying oil. Add ground pepper, kaffir lime leaves, Indonesian bay leaves, lemongrass, and galangal. Cook until fragrant.
Once the spices are cooked, add 600 ml of water and bring to a boil. Add the chicken wings and stir. Cover the pan and simmer until the wings are half-cooked.
Add salt, sugar, sweet soy sauce, and stock powder. Stir and continue simmering until the liquid reduces, the seasoning is absorbed, and the chicken is cooked. Adjust the seasoning to taste, then remove from heat.
strIngredient2: Salt and lime juice for marinating

strInstructions:
Heat the oil and sauté the garlic until fragrant.
Add the onion and sauté until softened.
Add the chicken pieces and stir-fry until their color changes.
Add sweet soy sauce, oyster sauce, soy sauce, pepper, salt, and stock powder. Mix well.
Add the water and cook over medium heat until the chicken is done. Add the scallions, stir briefly, and serve.

✅ Fry the chicken until golden brown.
✅ Sauté the ground spice paste until cooked. Season with sweet soy sauce, granulated sugar, salt, and stock powder. Mix well.
✅ Add the chicken and stir to coat. Pour in the water.
✅ Cook until the liquid reduces. Taste and adjust the seasoning.
✅ Serve.
strIngredient1: Chicken that has been simmered in spices

strInstructions:
Coat the chicken with citrus juice and salt. Let it marinate for 20 minutes.
Grind the shallots and garlic. Put them in a pan with ground ginger, turmeric, and galangal. Add water, salt, Indonesian bay leaves, and lemongrass. Bring to a boil, then add the chicken pieces. Cover and simmer until the chicken is tender and the liquid has reduced.
Fry the chicken until golden.
Meanwhile, pound the fried garlic, 6 bird's eye chilies, and salt together. Transfer to a bowl. Add sweet soy sauce, coarsely crushed fried peanuts, sliced green bird's eye chilies (the remaining ones), and citrus juice. Mix well.
Arrange the fried chicken on a serving plate and pour the soy sauce mixture over it. Serve.
strIngredient15: Ingredients for the sweet soy sauce mixture
strIngredient16: Bawang putih , iris tipis , lalu goreng
strIngredient21: Secukupnya minyak goreng untuk menggoreng ayam

strInstructions:
Boil the chicken for about 5 minutes with 2 Indonesian bay leaves and 2 kaffir lime leaves. Drain, rinse thoroughly under running water, and drain again.
Add water and the seasoning mix for simmering the chicken. Add 1 Indonesian bay leaf, 3 kaffir lime leaves, and the chicken that was boiled earlier. Cook until the liquid reduces.
Briefly fry the seasoned chicken, then drain. Do not fry until crispy.
Pound the ground spice ingredients and sauté over medium heat until fragrant.
Add the sliced tomato and red chili, 2 Indonesian bay leaves, bruised ginger, bruised galangal, and nutmeg.
Add water. Once it boils, add sweet soy sauce, salt, Royco seasoning, and a little Sasa seasoning. Taste and adjust.
Add the fried chicken and sliced onion.
Stir until the seasoning is absorbed into the chicken.
Remove from heat and serve.
strIngredient2: Packet of ready-made chicken simmering spice mix

strInstructions:
Wash the chicken thoroughly.
Briefly fry it until the outside changes color.
Sauté the ground spice paste, garlic, shallots, candlenuts, pepper, and coriander.
Add the chicken and stir-fry briefly. Pour in the coconut water and simmer until the chicken releases its juices and the liquid reduces.
Add soy sauce, salt, and seasoning. Stir until evenly combined.
Simple homemade chicken in sweet soy sauce is ready to serve! Enjoy!

Sauté the onion and garlic in Rose Brand margarine until fragrant.
Add the ground chicken, water, sweet soy sauce, Worcestershire sauce, oyster sauce, and water. Cook until boiling, then taste and adjust the seasoning.
Finally, add the Rose Brand cornstarch slurry and cook until thickened. Add the scallions.
Remove from heat and serve warm.
Rose Brand margarine and cornstarch make this sweet soy chicken extra delicious.

strMeal: Ayam Kecap Manis🍗🍯Gurih, Manis, Legit. Lauk Sejuta Umat!
strInstructions:
Prepare all the ingredients. Grind the spices.
Heat the oil. Sauté the ground spice paste and onion until fragrant and cooked. Add the Indonesian bay leaves, lemongrass, and galangal.
Add the chicken and stir until its color turns pale.
Pour in 500 ml of water. Add salt, stock powder, and palm sugar. Cook over medium heat for 20 minutes until the liquid has reduced by half and the chicken is tender. Do not add the soy sauce yet.
Then add the sweet soy sauce and whole bird's eye chilies. Stir well.
Increase the heat and cook for another 15 minutes until the sauce thickens and becomes glossy, turning the chicken occasionally. Taste and adjust the seasoning.
Remove from heat. Sprinkle with fried shallots if available. Serve warm with hot steamed rice 🤤

Clean the chicken and marinate it with 2 tbsp of soy sauce. Set aside. Slice the onion, garlic, shallots, and scallions. Tie the celery into a small bundle.
Heat the cooking oil and margarine. Sauté the onion until fragrant and softened, then add the garlic, shallots, and 1 tbsp of soy sauce. Stir until fragrant.
Add the chicken and stir-fry until its color changes. Add sweet soy sauce, Raja Rasa sauce, granulated sugar, salt, seasoning, MSG, ground pepper, and star anise. Stir until evenly combined.
Add hot water, stir briefly, then cover and simmer over medium heat until the liquid has reduced by half.
Taste and adjust the seasoning. If you prefer a darker color, add more sweet soy sauce to taste. Add the scallions and celery, then continue simmering until the chicken is deep brown and the sauce thickens. Ready to serve 😍

Prepare all the ingredients.
Grind the shallots, garlic, and candlenuts, then sauté until fragrant. Add the Indonesian bay leaves, lemongrass, and kaffir lime leaves.
Add the ground turmeric, pepper, salt, stock powder, and chopped chicken. Stir until evenly combined.
Pour in 700 ml of water and add Saori sauce and palm sugar.
Add the sweet soy sauce and cook for 30 minutes. After 30 minutes, add a handful of scallions and cook for another 5 minutes, or until the liquid has reduced slightly.
The minced chicken in sweet soy sauce is ready to enjoy.

Wash the chicken thoroughly.
Slice the garlic, shallots, scallions, and tomato.
Bruise the galangal, turmeric, and ginger.
Heat a pan with margarine. Sauté the garlic, shallots, and the white parts of the scallions until fragrant and lightly browned.
Add the aromatic spices and tomato. Stir well.
Once fragrant, add the chicken and stir until evenly coated.
Add the water and seasonings.
Stir well and simmer for 30 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Taste and adjust the seasoning. The fragrant sweet soy chicken is ready to enjoy with steamed rice 🤗
strIngredient1: Chicken wings, or another cut of your choice

strInstructions:
Wash the chicken thoroughly. Coat with salt and 1 tbsp of lime juice and let it sit for 15 minutes.
Deep-fry the chicken until cooked.
Sauté the coarsely crushed shallots until translucent. Add the ground spice paste and kaffir lime leaves. Stir until fragrant and fully cooked.
Add the fried chicken and a little water. Add salt, sugar, and pepper, then stir until the chicken is coated in the seasoning.
Add the remaining lime juice.

Wash and clean the chicken, then briefly boil it and discard the boiling water. Bruise the galangal and combine it with the other whole spices.
Prepare the pepper and sweet soy sauce. Bruise the garlic and ginger. Fry the chicken until half-cooked.
Remove and drain in another container.
Fry the bruised garlic until fragrant, then add the whole spices and cook until done.
Add the tomato sauce and water. Once boiling, add the palm sugar and let it dissolve.
Add ground pepper and stock powder, then add the chicken. Let the sauce reduce slightly.
Once the sauce has thickened, add the sweet soy sauce and stir until evenly combined. Taste and adjust, then turn off the heat.

Prepare all the ingredients.
Mix all the dough ingredients and knead with a mixer for 10 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Let the dough rest for 30 minutes.
Divide the dough into 50 g portions. Shape into balls and let rest for 15 minutes.
Flatten each portion and fill with 30 g of chicken in sweet soy sauce. Use a knife to cut the edges of the dough into 6 sections.
Wrap the chicken filling, shaping the dough into flower petals.
Place in a covered container and let rest for 30 minutes.
Steam for 10 minutes, or until cooked. Serve.

Fry the chicken until golden brown.
Sauté the ground spice paste, then add the remaining aromatics. Cook until fragrant. Add the chicken and enough water to submerge it.
Add salt, pepper, stevia, MSG, and dark soy sauce. Cook until the liquid is absorbed.

Wash the chicken pieces thoroughly. Marinate with pepper and lime juice for 10 minutes, then rinse.
Heat some oil and use it to sauté the previously ground spice paste.
Add the ginger and whole bird's eye chilies. Sauté until cooked and fragrant, then add the marinated chicken.
Add sweet soy sauce and oyster sauce. Pour in enough water, then add salt, mushroom stock, and sugar. Stir well and let the seasoning absorb.
Cook over medium-low heat so the sweet soy sauce seasoning penetrates the chicken and the sauce begins to thicken. Once the chicken is cooked and the sauce has reduced and thickened, add the long beans. Stir well and cook briefly for about 2–3 minutes, until tender but still crunchy and bright green.
Remove from heat and serve immediately. Enjoy with warm steamed rice.
strIngredient1: Long beans, cut into 4–5 cm pieces
strIngredient10: Red bird's eye chilies, whole or sliced

strInstructions:
Briefly boil the chicken, but do not discard the broth.
Slice the chilies, shallots, garlic, and tomatoes diagonally.
Sauté the chilies until fragrant. Add the boiled chicken and some of the broth.
Add palm sugar, salt, soy sauce, and the other seasonings listed above. Add raisins for a slightly tangy flavor, and tomato sauce or chili sauce according to your preference.
Mix 1 tbsp of cornstarch with some chicken broth and add it to the pan to thicken the sauce slightly. Taste it—the result should be delicious!
strIngredient17: Tepung maizena dicairkan dengan air kaldu

strInstructions:
Heat a little oil. Sauté the onion and garlic until fragrant, then add the chicken and cook until done.
Add the oyster sauce (which can be omitted) and sweet soy sauce. Cook briefly, then set aside.
In a bowl, combine the sliced scallions, cooked chicken in sweet soy sauce, eggs, and stock powder. Mix well.
Heat a little oil in a pan and place a spring roll wrapper in it. Pour in the egg mixture, fold the wrapper, and cook over low heat until the outside is dry and the filling is cooked through.
strIngredient2: Chicken thigh fillet, minced or ground

strInstructions:
Coat the chicken with 3 tsp of salt and let it sit for about 30 minutes. Then wash thoroughly.
Briefly fry the chicken until just cooked.
Mix the oyster sauce and sweet soy sauce together.
Heat a little oil and sauté the garlic until fragrant. Add the chicken and stir well.
Add the water, finely ground onion, and sauce mixture. Stir well and bring to a boil, stirring occasionally.
Cook until the seasoning is absorbed and the liquid has reduced slightly. Add the scallions and mix well. Taste and adjust; add sugar, salt, or stock powder if needed.
Once the scallions have softened and the seasoning tastes right, remove from heat and serve.

strMeal: Sambal Goreng Kentang Ati Anti Gagal
strInstructions:
Clean the chicken liver and gizzards. Boil until half-cooked in salted water, then drain and fry until fully cooked. Remove, cut into small pieces, and set aside.
Peel and dice the potatoes. Wash and drain them, then fry until cooked. Set aside.
Grind the chilies, shallots, garlic, shrimp paste, tomato, and palm sugar into a smooth paste.
Heat cooking oil in a pan. Once hot, add the ground spice paste, salt, galangal, Indonesian bay leaves, and kaffir lime leaves. Stir until fragrant.
Add 50 ml of water, one packet of instant coconut milk, and seasoning. Stir well. Once boiling, add the chopped liver, gizzards, and potatoes. Stir gently and taste to adjust the seasoning. Add the scallions, stir briefly, then turn off the heat.
The spicy fried potato and chicken liver dish is ready to serve.
strIngredient14: Lemongrass, cut into 4 pieces and bruised

strMeal: Sambal Goreng Kentang Ati Enak Mudah Sederhana
strInstructions:
Peel the potatoes and cut them as desired. I cut mine into small cubes because the potatoes are quite small.
Wash the chicken livers and gizzards thoroughly. Fry the potatoes first, then fry the livers and gizzards. Once cooked, remove and cut them as desired.
Clean the garlic, shallots, tomatoes, and chilies. Chop everything in a food processor.
Heat a pan and add oil. I use a fairly generous amount. Add the blended seasoning, then add Indonesian bay leaves, galangal, and lime leaves. Continue sautéing until the oil separates.
Add the livers, gizzards, and potatoes. Stir-fry until evenly coated with the chili sauce. Add salt and seasoning powder. Stir-fry for 2 minutes.
The delicious, easy, and simple fried potato sambal with chicken livers and gizzards is ready to serve! Enjoy!

Wash the chicken livers and gizzards thoroughly, then boil until cooked and cut into cubes. Boil the quail eggs for about 8 minutes until cooked, then peel them.
Dice the potatoes and soak them in salted water. Rinse, drain, and fry in hot oil until cooked. Remove and drain.
Sauté the ground seasoning until fragrant. Add lemongrass, galangal, and kaffir lime leaves. Cook until the seasoning is fully cooked and the oil begins to separate. Add salt, sugar, and powdered stock. Stir and adjust the seasoning to taste.
Add the potatoes, quail eggs, and chicken livers and gizzards. Stir-fry until evenly combined. Remove from the heat and serve with rice cakes and your family's favorite side dishes.
strIngredient3: Pairs of chicken livers and gizzards

strInstructions:
Prepare all the ingredients. Boil the quail eggs until cooked beforehand. Dice the potatoes and fry until cooked.
Separate the chilies from the other ground-seasoning ingredients. Boil the chilies first to give the dish a vibrant red color. Once cooked, drain and grind them. Grind the remaining seasoning ingredients as well. Sauté the ground seasoning and chilies until fragrant. Then add them to a pot of boiling water along with the fried potatoes, quail eggs, and tofu. Add the sautéed seasoning and coconut milk.
Add granulated sugar, salt, and mushroom stock powder. Adjust the seasoning to taste and cook until done. Transfer to a serving dish and enjoy with warm white rice.

strMeal: Sambal Goreng Ati Ampela Tahu Kentang Dan Wortel
strInstructions:
Cut the chicken livers and gizzards, tofu, potatoes, and carrot as desired.
Heat oil and deep-fry the tofu, potatoes, and chicken livers and gizzards until golden and crisp. Drain.
Heat a little oil, add the ground seasoning, Indonesian bay leaf, and ginger, and sauté until fragrant. Add water, carrot, palm sugar, salt, mushroom stock, and coconut milk. Cook over medium heat while stirring so the coconut milk does not split.
Add the tofu, potatoes, chicken livers and gizzards, sliced chilies, and sweet soy sauce. Stir well and cook until the coconut milk sauce has reduced or evaporated. Ready to serve ❤️

strMeal: Sambal Goreng Udang Tempe & Telur Puyuh
strInstructions:
Prepare all the ingredients.
Boil the curly red chilies (10 pcs) and red bird's eye chilies (15 pcs) in boiling water to give the sambal a beautiful red color. Remove and drain. Grind the boiled chilies with the shallots, garlic, and salt.
Heat cooking oil in a pan. Fry the tempeh until partially cooked, then remove and set aside. Briefly fry the boiled quail eggs, then remove and set aside. Briefly fry the shrimp until they change color, then remove and set aside.
Use the remaining oil from frying the tempeh, quail eggs, and shrimp to sauté the ground seasoning. Add the sliced shallots and cook until fragrant and softened. Add the ground seasoning, galangal, lemongrass, and Indonesian bay leaves. Cook until the seasoning is done.
Pour the thin coconut milk into the pan and add palm sugar. Bring to a boil.
Add the quail eggs, tempeh, and shrimp. Add powdered stock, stir well, and cook until the seasoning is absorbed and the sauce reduces.
Pour in the thick coconut milk. Add the petai beans and whole red bird's eye chilies. Stir well.
Cook until the coconut milk boils, stirring continuously so it does not split. Adjust the seasoning to taste, then remove from the heat and serve.
strIngredient3: Tempeh block, diced and briefly fried
strIngredient4: Petai bean pod, each bean split in half
strIngredient5: Red bird's eye chilies, left whole

strInstructions:
Cut the tofu into pieces, then fry until the edges are crisp.
Prepare the ground seasoning. The chilies are already ground, so there is no need to grind them again.
Sauté all the seasonings until fragrant.
Add water, salt, and sugar. Cook while stirring.
Add the tofu and krecek, stir well, then add the coconut milk. Stir gently until the krecek softens.
Cook the sambal goreng until the sauce thickens.
The tofu and krecek sambal goreng is ready to serve as a side dish.

Blend the seasoning ingredients in a food processor and sauté until fragrant.
Fry the tempeh until partially cooked and still slightly moist. Remove and mix into the ground seasoning. Stir well.
Add the long beans, whole aromatics, and water. Stir until combined. Cover the nonstick pan and let the water evaporate and the seasoning soak in. Serve.

Dice the tempeh, then boil for about 15 minutes. Add sugar and salt, about a small pinch of each or roughly 1/4 teaspoon. Remove and drain.
Grind the seasoning. A tip for a smoother result: boil the Tanjung red chilies and curly red chilies first.
Sauté the ground seasoning until fragrant. Add the petai and tomato, both diced into small pieces, along with the remaining ingredients.
Once fragrant, add about 500 ml of water. When it boils, add salt, sugar, bird's eye chilies, and tempeh. Adjust the seasoning to taste.
Add the cow-skin krecek. Stir occasionally.
Add the coconut milk and stir gently. Wait until it boils. Serve sprinkled with fried shallots.
strIngredient6: Petai bean pod, peeled and cut as desired

strInstructions:
Grind all the seasonings except the red bird's eye chilies. You can use a mortar and pestle or a blender until smooth. I use only a few chilies so the children can taste it too. Hehe.
Heat oil and sauté the ground seasoning. Add the aromatics, including Indonesian bay leaves, kaffir lime leaves, and lemongrass. Once the seasoning is fully cooked, add a little water.
Add the chicken livers and gizzards that have been washed, boiled, and cut into pieces. Stir until evenly combined. Then add the potatoes and tempeh, which should have been partially fried beforehand.
Stir well, then add the coconut milk. Don't forget to season it. Add the whole red bird's eye chilies. Taste and adjust the seasoning. Cook until the sauce has reduced. If using cow-skin crackers or krecek, add them at this stage, before the sauce reduces.
The chicken liver and potato sambal goreng is ready to serve to the family.
strIngredient1: Pairs of chicken livers and gizzards, washed and boiled

strInstructions:
Dice the tofu and tempeh, then fry. Boil the cecek (beef skin) and cut it into cubes.
Prepare the seasonings.
Grind the seasoning ingredients, then sauté until fragrant.
Add the tofu, tempeh, and cecek. Stir well and add a little water. Add the whole aromatics.
Add the coconut milk and stir until combined. Add ground pepper, powdered stock, salt, and sugar. Cook until boiling. Adjust the seasoning to taste, then transfer to a pot.
The sambal goreng is ready to serve.

Prepare all the ingredients. Blend the ground-seasoning ingredients and fry the potatoes.
Boil the chicken livers and gizzards, drain, then fry them.
Sauté the ground seasoning in a pan, then add the potatoes and chicken livers and gizzards. Add water.
Add the seasonings and thick coconut milk.
The fried potato and chicken liver sambal is ready to enjoy.
strIngredient15: Oil for frying the potatoes and chicken livers

strMeal: Sambal Goreng Kentang Telur Puyuh Udang
strInstructions:
Dice the potatoes and fry until cooked. Peel the shrimp and fry briefly. Boil the quail eggs, then peel them.
Sauté the ground seasoning until fragrant. Add the Indonesian bay leaf, kaffir lime leaves, and galangal. Stir well, then add salt, granulated sugar, and sweet soy sauce. Stir to combine.
Add the fried potatoes, shrimp, and quail eggs. Stir well, remove from the heat, and serve.

Cut the tempeh into pieces and steam until cooked. Set aside. Boil the eggs until cooked and set aside. Prepare the remaining ingredients and grind the ground-seasoning ingredients.
Heat a little cooking oil and sauté the ground seasoning until fragrant. Add lemongrass, Indonesian bay leaves, galangal, and kaffir lime leaves. Stir well, then add water.
Add the chayote and stir well. Add the tempeh and stir again. Add the instant coconut milk and mix well. Season with salt, granulated sugar, and powdered stock. Stir to combine.
Add more water if needed. Add the petai, followed by the eggs and finally the whole bird's eye chilies.
Cook until the seasoning is absorbed. Taste and adjust the seasoning.
Serve with rice cakes.
strIngredient1: Chayote, peeled and cut into matchsticks
strIngredient3: Tempeh block, cut into pieces and steamed
strIngredient6: 65 ml packet of instant coconut milk

strInstructions:
Prepare the ingredients and seasonings, then grind the seasoning ingredients.
Sauté the ground seasoning and add the whole aromatics. Cook until fragrant, then add just enough water.
Add salt, sugar, and mushroom stock powder, then add the fried potatoes. Taste and adjust the seasoning.
Once the flavor is right, let the sauce reduce and the seasoning soak in. When the sauce has thickened and the seasoning is absorbed, turn off the heat and serve. 🥰🤗🙏🏻
strIngredient1: Potatoes, peeled, washed, cut as desired, and fried

strInstructions:
Boil the chicken livers until cooked, cut into pieces, and fry briefly.
Sauté the ground seasoning and aromatics until fully cooked, then pour in enough water. Stir well.
Add the livers, seasoning powder, and sugar. Cook until the seasoning is absorbed and the liquid has reduced, stirring occasionally.
strIngredient1: Pairs of chicken livers and gizzards

strInstructions:
Blend the ground seasoning, then sauté it with lemongrass, Indonesian bay leaves, and galangal until fragrant.
Add the chicken livers and gizzards and sauté briefly. Add the potatoes, quail eggs, salt, powdered stock, and sugar. Stir until evenly combined.
Add water, stir, and cook until the water has reduced and the seasoning is absorbed.
The fried potato sambal is ready to serve.
strIngredient2: Pairs of chicken livers and gizzards, boiled and diced

strInstructions:
Mix all the ingredients for the meatballs, then shape them as desired. Prepare a steamer and steam the meatballs until cooked, about 15 minutes.
Peel the potatoes and dice them. Fry until golden brown, then remove, drain, and set aside.
Prepare the ground seasoning and grind it using a mortar and pestle or blender, whichever you prefer. I use a blender to save time. Sauté the ground seasoning until fragrant, then add lemongrass, galangal, Indonesian bay leaves, and kaffir lime leaves. Continue cooking until the seasoning is done.
Add the fried potatoes and stir well. Add the meatballs and stir again until evenly combined. Add the coconut milk and water, then stir. Season with salt, palm sugar, and granulated sugar. Stir and cook until the sugar and salt dissolve.
Cook until the liquid reduces and the seasoning is absorbed by the meatballs and potatoes. Adjust the seasoning, then remove from the heat and serve. To freeze, let the dish cool, portion it into vacuum-seal bags, and freeze.

Mash the potatoes coarsely so you can still feel the potato pieces when biting into them.
Thinly slice the cabbage, spring onion, and shallot.
Lightly beat the eggs. Add salt, sugar, pepper, and powdered stock to taste. Do not make the mixture too salty because the fried potato sambal is already seasoned.
Add the potatoes, cabbage, and spring onion. Mix well and adjust the seasoning.
Prepare the spring roll wrappers. Place one spoonful of filling on each wrapper, fold it like an envelope, and fry until cooked.
strIngredient3: Small bowl of fried potato sambal

strInstructions:
Boil the chicken bones. Once the water has boiled for about 5 minutes, discard the water and rinse the bones. Add fresh water and boil the chicken bones again for about 30 minutes over medium-low heat. Set aside once done.
Sauté the finely chopped garlic in a little oil until fragrant. Add the ground chicken and cook until done.
Once the chicken is cooked, add the prepared stock and rice. Stir well.
If there is not enough chicken stock, add more water. Once it boils, add all the seasonings. Stir continuously until the rice turns into porridge. Remember to adjust the seasoning to taste.
Spoon the porridge into bowls and arrange the cakwe, wonton crackers, fried shallots, and spring onion on top. Serve warm.

Wash the chicken thoroughly. Bring water to a boil, add the chicken, and boil for 5 minutes. Remove and drain. Bring 3 liters of water to a boil, add the chicken, and simmer until it releases its stock.
Add the rice, Indonesian bay leaves, salt, and chicken stock taken from the pot. Cook over low heat until it becomes porridge. I use a rice cooker.
Prepare the ground seasoning and sauté until fragrant. Add lemongrass, Indonesian bay leaves, kaffir lime leaves, and galangal. Sauté until the seasoning is cooked.
Add the sautéed seasoning to the chicken broth. Season with granulated sugar, salt, and powdered stock, then simmer until the chicken is tender.
Remove the chicken and fry until golden brown. Remove and drain.
Set aside the yellow broth. Once the chicken has cooled, shred it.
Spoon the porridge into bowls and add the other toppings. The porridge is ready to enjoy.

Bring 500 ml of water to a boil. Add Indonesian bay leaves, kaffir lime leaves, and turmeric powder.
Add 2 pieces of yellow-seasoned chicken prepared by simmering or previously boiled, to use as shredded chicken topping for the porridge.
Rinse the rice thoroughly. Put it in a rice cooker with the water brought to a boil in the pot to speed up cooking. Add Indonesian bay leaves and salt, stir, and cook as you would rice. Partway through cooking, open the lid and stir with a rice paddle, pressing the rice to break it up. Continue stirring for about 5 minutes, then close the lid again. Repeat this process after a while. Wait until the water has reduced and the cooker switches from Cook to Warm. Stir again to prevent the porridge from sticking to the bottom.
The chicken porridge is ready to serve.

Boil the chicken and chicken feet in 2 liters of water with Indonesian bay leaves and lemongrass until tender. Remove the chicken and set the meat aside. Strain the broth and reserve 1.5 liters for the porridge.
Grind the shallots, garlic, turmeric, and ginger. Sauté them with lemongrass, kaffir lime leaves, and Indonesian bay leaves until fragrant. Add the mixture to the broth, season with salt and sugar, and cook for 15–20 minutes.
Bring 1.5 liters of the yellow chicken broth to a boil with the chicken feet. Add the rice and Indonesian bay leaves. Cook, stirring, until the rice grains open up. Add salt, pepper, and the rice-flour slurry, stirring until the porridge thickens.
Sauté the shallots and garlic until fragrant. Add the shredded chicken, sweet soy sauce, oyster sauce, pepper, and a little broth. Cook until the seasoning is absorbed.
Serve the porridge warm with chicken on top, then garnish with fried shallots, celery leaves, spring onion, crackers, sweet soy sauce, chili sauce, and calamansi or lime.
strIngredient5: Sweet soy sauce and chili sauce

strInstructions:
Rinse the rice, then soak it in boiled water for about 1 hour.
Thinly slice the shallots and garlic, then sauté until fragrant.
Put the rice in a slow cooker and add the sautéed shallots and garlic, chicken, carrot, and broccoli.
Cook for 2 hours. Once cooked, strain the porridge.
The porridge is ready to serve. Divide into 30 ml portions. If it is too thick, add boiled water when serving until it reaches the desired consistency.

Prepare all the ingredients. Finely chop the garlic and chicken.
Heat a pan with a little cooking oil. Sauté the garlic until fragrant and golden. Add the minced chicken and stir until it changes color.
Pour in the fish sauce and stir well. Add hot water. Once it boils, add the rice. When the liquid begins to reduce, season with salt, mushroom stock powder, and ground pepper. Stir well.
When the liquid begins to reduce, season again with salt, mushroom stock powder, and ground pepper. Stir well, then add sesame oil and mix.
Taste and adjust the seasoning. Once the porridge is cooked, turn off the heat and serve with love to your loved ones. 💕 If desired, add fried wontons, chopped celery or spring onion, and fried shallots.

strMeal: Bubur Ayam Untuk Diet (Menu Pagi Hari)
strInstructions:
Bring water to a boil, then add the chicken and sesame oil.
Add garlic powder and more sesame oil. Cook the chicken until done, then remove it and set aside.
Add 3 tablespoons of cooked rice. For extra fiber, add Brazilian spinach, salt, and pepper. Cook until the liquid has reduced, then turn off the heat.
Put the rice porridge in a food chopper and blend until smooth. If it is difficult to blend, add a little water.
Don't forget to boil an egg as well.
Pour the rice porridge into a plate, then add the chicken and boiled egg.
If you like it spicy, add just a little chili powder. Enjoy!

Prepare all the ingredients. Sauté the star anise in a little oil until fragrant. Add the Indonesian bay leaves, garlic, and roughly chopped ginger, and cook until softened.
Add enough water, using an approximate rice-to-water ratio of 1:3. Add the rice and salt, then lower the heat.
Continue cooking, stirring occasionally and scraping the bottom of the pot. Taste and adjust the seasoning, then add sliced spring onion. Continue cooking until the porridge thickens.
Add the egg yolk just before serving. Cook it medium or well-done according to your preference.
Serve the porridge with a soft-cooked egg, cakwe, spring onion, soy sauce, and chili powder. 🤗🤗
strIngredient1: Plates of leftover rice from the previous night

strInstructions:
Rinse the rice and soak it overnight. Bring water to a boil, then add the rice, Indonesian bay leaves, and lemongrass. Add salt and cook, stirring occasionally, until done.
Grind the seasoning ingredients. Heat oil and sauté the ground seasoning until fragrant. Add lemongrass, Indonesian bay leaves, galangal, and kaffir lime leaves. Sauté until softened.
Add water, chicken pieces, and boiled eggs. Season with salt and mushroom stock powder. Cook until done.
Prepare serving bowls and spoon in the porridge. Top with shredded chicken, fried peanuts, sliced celery and spring onion, boiled egg, omelet, and fried shallots. Add the broth.
The chicken porridge is ready to serve. Don't forget the crackers! 😁 Enjoy.

Wash the chicken and marinate it in lime juice for 10 minutes. Rinse and set aside.
Prepare a pot of drinking water and add the thoroughly washed rice, sesame oil, Indonesian bay leaves, salt, stock, and pepper.
Add the marinated chicken to the pot with the rice. Simmer over low heat, stirring continuously.
Once the porridge reaches your preferred thickness and flavor, turn off the heat. You can shred the chicken directly or fry it first before shredding.
The chicken porridge with cakwe is ready to serve with your favorite condiments. ❤️
strIngredient1: Rice measured with a 200 ml cup

strInstructions:
Put the rice, water, Indonesian bay leaves, and seasoning into a pot. Stir well and cook over medium heat, stirring occasionally.
When the liquid begins to reduce, stir continuously to prevent the porridge from sticking to the bottom of the pot. Cook until thickened, tasting and adjusting the seasoning as you go. Turn off the heat.
Spoon the porridge into bowls and add your preferred toppings. Serve.
Are you on team stirred chicken porridge or unstirred? I'm definitely on team stirred! 🤤 Enjoy trying it! 😊
strIngredient13: Practical chili sauce for meatballs or chicken noodles

strInstructions:
Toast the coriander seeds until brown, then grind them with a mortar and pestle. Set aside.
Prepare all the ingredients. Fry the ingredients in oil, then grind them together with the toasted coriander.
Grind until smooth. Prepare the aromatics and put everything into a pot.
Add 2 liters of water, then season with flavor enhancer, salt, and ground pepper.
Clean the chicken and add it to the broth. Cook until the broth is flavorful.
Once the chicken is cooked, remove it and fry briefly. Add 1 tablespoon of granulated sugar to the broth.
Put the leftover rice in a blender and add some of the broth and plain water.
Blend until smooth, then transfer to a pan and add 1 tablespoon of salt.
Cook over low heat until the porridge thickens, then set aside.
Spoon a ladleful of porridge into a bowl, pour in some broth, and add toppings as desired. Enjoy!

✅ Cook the rice and the other porridge ingredients until they become porridge.
✅ Grind the shallots, garlic, candlenuts, and coriander. Sauté the seasoning until fragrant and cooked, then add the sliced spring onion and cook until softened.
✅ Add water and season with granulated sugar, salt, and stock powder. Bring to a boil and taste to adjust the seasoning.
✅ Serve with your other favorite accompaniments.

Fry the chopped garlic and ginger until golden, then drain. Set aside the oil as well.
Heat the rice, stock, boiled chicken, and seasonings, excluding the sesame oil. Stir until the mixture thickens into porridge. Add the seaweed and stir briefly.
Serve the porridge warm with a drizzle of sesame oil, the fried garlic and ginger with their oil, and any other side dishes you like.
strIngredient2: Chicken thigh and drumstick, boiled; reserve the broth

strInstructions:
Rinse the rice thoroughly and set aside.
Bring water to a boil, add the chicken, and boil for 2 minutes. Remove the chicken and discard the water.
Bring 1200 ml of fresh water to a boil. Add the chicken, Indonesian bay leaves, and lemongrass. Cook until the chicken is done, and don't forget to add salt.
Once cooked, remove the chicken and set it aside. You don't need to fry it, but you can if you prefer.
Add the rice to the chicken broth, season with pepper, and stir. At first, you only need to stir occasionally.
Once the porridge starts to thicken, stir continuously until it is fully cooked. Adjust the texture to your preference.
Spoon the porridge into bowls and add toppings. It's ready to serve! The recipe is simple, although cooking porridge does take some time.

✅ To make the porridge: Put all the porridge ingredients except the margarine into a pot. Cook over medium heat, stirring occasionally to prevent burning.
Continue cooking until the rice becomes porridge. Add the margarine and stir well. Turn off the heat. Alternatively, you can cook everything in a rice cooker, checking and stirring occasionally.
✅ To make the soto broth: Bring water to a boil. Add the chicken and cook over medium heat until tender. Remove the chicken and shred it.
Grind the shallots, garlic, turmeric, and candlenuts. Sauté the seasoning with Indonesian bay leaves and lemongrass in a little oil until fragrant.
Add the sautéed seasoning to the pot of broth. Season with salt and stock powder, then taste. Bring it back to a boil and turn off the heat.
Spoon the porridge into bowls. Top with shredded chicken, sliced spring onion, and fried shallots. Pour in as much broth as you like. Serve with accompaniments. Alhamdulillah 🌸

Sauté the chopped garlic and spring onion in sesame oil until fragrant. Add the minced chicken and cook until done, stirring as needed.
Add the leftover rice. I usually blend the white rice with water first to speed up the process of turning it into porridge. It doesn't need to be completely smooth. If you add the rice directly, it will take longer, so choose whichever method you prefer.
Add water and bring to a boil.
Season with salt, pepper, and soy sauce. Stir well and cook until done, adjusting the softness of the porridge to your liking. Add more water if needed. Taste, adjust the seasoning, and turn off the heat.
strIngredient1: Rice scoops of leftover cooked white rice

strInstructions:
Blend the leftover rice with water.
Pour it into a pot and add Indonesian bay leaves, instant coconut milk, salt, and stock powder.
Stir and cook until it becomes porridge, adjusting the texture to your preference.
Remove from the heat and let it cool slightly. As it cools, the porridge will naturally thicken.
Spoon the porridge into a bowl. Pour soto broth over it, then sprinkle with celery leaves and spring onion. Arrange shredded chicken and a boiled egg on top.
Ready to serve. Add chili sauce, soy sauce, and crackers if desired.
strIngredient1: Plate of leftover cooked white rice

strInstructions:
Rinse the mung beans thoroughly.
Soak the mung beans for 30 minutes.
Boil the mung beans in boiled water for 10 minutes. The water should sit about 1–2 finger-widths above the beans.
Turn off the heat and leave the pot covered for 30 minutes.
Prepare a slurry with the glutinous rice flour.
Add palm sugar, ginger, pandan leaves, and a little salt. Boil for 10 minutes. Add the glutinous rice flour slurry during the final minute, then turn off the heat.
In a separate pot, bring boiled water to a simmer. Add pandan leaves and coconut milk, then season with salt to taste. Bring to a boil, stirring continuously to prevent the coconut milk from splitting.
The mung bean porridge is ready to serve.

Prepare all the ingredients: chocolate-flavored Cap Enaak sweetened condensed milk, mung beans, Javanese palm sugar, vanilla powder, fine salt, pandan leaves, coconut milk, and tapioca flour. Chop the palm sugar into small pieces so it dissolves quickly. Put it in a saucepan with the vanilla powder and salt.
Add 300 ml of water, stir, and cook over medium heat until the sugar dissolves and the mixture boils. Remove from the heat and set aside.
Rinse the mung beans until the water runs clear, then drain. Put them in a pot with the pandan leaves tied in a knot. Add the remaining 700 ml of water.
Cook over medium heat until the water boils. Cover the pot and cook for 5 minutes, then turn off the heat and leave it tightly covered for 30 minutes. After 30 minutes, turn the heat back on and cook over medium heat for another 7 minutes with the lid tightly closed.
After 7 minutes, open the lid and check whether the mung beans have softened and split open. Pour the palm sugar syrup through a strainer into the pot to keep any impurities out of the porridge. Add the chocolate-flavored sweetened condensed milk and stir well.
Put the tapioca flour in a bowl, add water, and stir until dissolved.
Pour the tapioca slurry into the mung bean porridge and stir. Taste and adjust the flavor. When it tastes right, turn off the heat and let it cool.
Put the coconut milk in a saucepan with pandan leaves and salt. Cook over medium heat, stirring continuously to prevent it from splitting. Once it boils, turn off the heat and set aside.
For warm serving, spoon some mung bean porridge into a bowl and pour coconut milk over it. Stir and enjoy.
For the popular iced version, spoon the mung bean porridge into a serving bowl, add shaved ice, and pour coconut milk over it. Finish with chocolate-flavored sweetened condensed milk.
The thick iced mung bean porridge is ready to serve and enjoy. 🙏🥰

Soak the mung beans for 3 hours, then rinse thoroughly. Boil them in water until tender.
Add ginger, pandan leaves, granulated sugar, and Cap Enaak sweetened condensed milk. Stir well.
Add salt and lower the heat. Pour in the glutinous rice flour mixed with water, stirring continuously and scraping the bottom so it doesn't stick and burn. The mung bean porridge without coconut milk is ready. Turn off the heat.
strIngredient1: Mung beans, soaked for 3 hours to help them soften faster
strIngredient7: Glutinous rice flour, dissolved in water

strMeal: Bubur Kacang Hijau Ketan Hitam Dengan Santan Matang
strInstructions:
Rinse the mung beans and black glutinous rice, then soak them for 12 hours in the lower section of the refrigerator.
Boil the mung beans and black glutinous rice with water and pandan leaves until tender. Add more water if they are not yet soft.
Add granulated sugar, palm sugar, and salt. Add one sachet of vanilla powder. Stir well and cook until the ingredients dissolve and combine into porridge.
Cook the coconut milk separately with a little salt, stirring continuously to prevent it from splitting.
Serve the porridge with the cooked coconut milk poured over the top.

strMeal: Bubur Kacang Hijau Topping Kelapa Muda
strInstructions:
Prepare the ingredients and weigh them as needed. If using round blocks of palm sugar, finely shave them. I ended up using granulated palm sugar instead (see photo). Tie the pandan leaves into knots and bruise the ginger.
Bring the water to a boil in a pot. Add the mung beans and boil for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally. Turn off the heat, cover the pot, and let it stand for 30 minutes.
Turn the heat back on, add enough water, and boil the mung beans again for 7 minutes or longer, until tender. Turn off the heat and set aside.
Pour water into another pot and add Rose Brand granulated sugar. Stir until dissolved, then add the palm sugar and pandan leaves and ginger. Bring to a boil until the sugars dissolve. Remove from the heat.
Pour the sugar syrup into the pot of mung beans and stir well. Let the syrup absorb into the beans. Turn off the heat. The mung bean porridge is ready.
Pour water and coconut milk into a pot. Add salt and pandan leaves, then stir well. Bring to a boil and turn off the heat. Let cool.
Serve the mung bean porridge with coconut milk sauce and pieces of young coconut. Don't forget to add ice cubes.
strIngredient2: Water for boiling the mung beans
strIngredient3: Granulated palm sugar or shaved palm sugar

strInstructions:
Rinse the mung beans thoroughly. Boil the mung beans and pandan leaf using the 5-30-7 method.
Boil the water with palm sugar and salt until the palm sugar dissolves.
Pour the palm sugar mixture into the pot of mung beans. Cook until boiling, then add the bananas.
Bring to a boil again, then add the coconut milk and granulated sugar. Cook until the coconut milk boils. Taste and adjust the seasoning.
Serve.
strIngredient2: Water for boiling the mung beans
strIngredient7: 65 ml sachet of instant coconut milk

strInstructions:
Make the mung bean porridge: Rinse the mung beans thoroughly, then soak for 1 hour.
Boil the mung beans in water until cooked and tender (I use the 5-30-7 method). First, boil the mung beans for 5 minutes, then turn off the heat and cover the pot for 30 minutes. Turn the heat back on and cook the mung beans with the pandan leaves and granulated sugar for 7 minutes, or until tender and the liquid has reduced.
Make the banana compote: Prepare the ingredients. Boil the palm sugar, granulated sugar, salt, and pandan leaf in water until the sugar is partly dissolved. Add the sliced bananas and cook until the bananas are tender and the sugar has dissolved.
Make the coconut milk sauce: Boil the coconut milk with the pandan leaf and salt, stirring continuously to prevent it from splitting. Just before it boils, pour in the cornstarch slurry and stir until the sauce thickens.
Place the mung bean porridge, banana compote, and coconut milk sauce in separate containers.
Serve the mung bean porridge and banana compote with coconut milk sauce poured over the top.
strIngredient7: Horn bananas, cut into small pieces
strIngredient10: Pandan leaf, tied into a knot

strInstructions:
Rinse the mung beans until the water runs clear, then drain. Transfer them to a pot and add fresh water and pandan leaves.
Add the palm sugar, vanilla powder, and salt. Cook over medium heat until boiling. Cover the pot and boil for 5 minutes. After 5 minutes, turn off the heat and leave the pot covered for 30 minutes. Do not open the lid during this time.
After 30 minutes, turn the heat back on and cook over medium heat until the water boils again, keeping the lid closed. Once boiling, cook for another 7 minutes so the mung beans become tender. After 7 minutes, open the lid, stir, then add the granulated sugar and stir again. Finally, add thick coconut milk or instant coconut milk.
Stir until the coconut milk is mixed with the mung bean cooking liquid. Cook briefly until boiling, stirring continuously to prevent the coconut milk from splitting. Once boiling, cook for about 3 more minutes, continuing to stir so it cooks through, then turn off the heat and remove the pot.
Transfer the mung beans to a serving bowl. Enjoy them warm, or serve cold with ice cubes. Enjoy making them! 🙏😍
strIngredient2: Palm sugar or palm sugar blocks, adjust to taste
strIngredient7: Thick coconut milk or 1 sachet of 65 ml instant coconut milk

strInstructions:
Rinse the mung beans thoroughly.
Bring the water to a boil. Add the mung beans and salt, then cook over high heat for 10 minutes. Cover the pot and let it stand for 30 minutes. Then turn the heat back on and cook for another 10 minutes.
Transfer to another pot. Since part of the batch is being made without ginger, boil the water with granulated sugar, ginger, and pandan leaves. Add the coconut milk.
Add the softened mung beans, stir well, and serve.
strIngredient6: Small sachet of instant coconut milk

strInstructions:
Bring the water to a boil, then add the mung beans, white glutinous rice, and pandan leaves. Cook until the mung beans begin to swell.
Once the mung beans have swollen, add the granulated sugar and salt. Cook until the beans split open and the liquid reduces.
Next, mix the instant coconut milk with the water until combined. Pour it into the mung bean pot, add the vanilla powder, and cook until boiling and the coconut milk is cooked through.
Once the mung bean porridge is cooked and has reached your preferred thickness, taste and adjust the seasoning, then turn off the heat.
Serve and enjoy.

Pour the water into a pot. Add the roasted ginger, cinnamon stick, pandan leaves, and mung beans. Bring to a boil, then cover the pot and continue cooking over low heat until the mung beans are tender. Add the salt and granulated palm sugar only after the mung beans are tender.
Once the mung beans are tender, add the FiberCreme while stirring continuously. When it has dissolved completely, turn off the heat. Serve in bowls with palm sugar syrup to taste and slices of white bread.
Happy cooking! 😀
strIngredient1: Mung beans, soaked for 2 hours and rinsed thoroughly
strIngredient2: Ginger, rinsed, briefly roasted, and bruised
strIngredient4: Pandan leaves, rinsed and tied into knots
strIngredient5: Granulated palm sugar or palm sugar
strIngredient10: White bread, cut into cubes or as desired

strInstructions:
Soak the mung beans for 1 hour, then boil them with the pandan leaves using the 5-30-7 method, or until the beans split open.
Next, add the sugar and salt. Boil until the sugar dissolves, then add the instant coconut milk and stir well.
Add the jackfruit pieces and stir briefly.
Serve the mung bean porridge warm. It should be sweet and creamy.

Rinse the mung beans thoroughly, then soak for at least 1 hour. Discard the soaking water and boil the beans until tender.
Prepare the durian flesh and blend some of it, leaving the rest in whole pieces.
Add the coconut milk, blended durian, whole durian pieces, sugar, salt, and pandan leaf. Bring to a boil and taste to adjust the flavor. Remove from the heat.
Serve warm.

strMeal: Bubur Kacang Hijau Durian (Tanpa Gula Putih)
strInstructions:
Soak the mung beans for at least 3 hours before using. Boil them in enough water to cover until tender. Set aside.
Cook the palm sugar until dissolved. Mix the coconut milk with the water and stir well, though you can also use the coconut milk without mixing it with water.
Pour the palm sugar syrup and coconut milk into the mung bean pot, straining the palm sugar syrup first. The coconut milk does not need to be strained.
For a creamy, milky flavor, add Cap Enaak sweetened condensed milk. You can also add the durian flesh at this stage. Stir well and bring to a boil, stirring continuously. Remove from the heat. Since one of my children doesn't like durian, I serve it as a topping instead. It tastes even better served cold! 😉🤤

Soak the mung beans overnight to help loosen their skins (optional).
Bring the water to a boil, then add the mung beans and 2 pandan leaves. Cook until done.
Dissolve the tapioca starch and mix it into the mung beans. Stir briefly, then turn off the heat.
For the coconut milk sauce, mix the coconut milk with salt and pandan leaves. Cook until it reduces slightly. You can also add hunkwe flour to thicken it.
The mung bean porridge is ready to serve.

Soak the mung beans overnight.
Boil the mung beans and coconut milk for 5 minutes. Add the sugar, salt, ginger, pandan leaves, and cinnamon powder.
Turn off the heat and let the pot stand for 30 minutes, then boil again for 7 minutes.
The mung bean porridge is ready to serve.

Soak the rinsed mung beans for 2–3 hours. Heat 700 ml of water and cook the mung beans using the 5-30-7 method. Don't forget to add 1 pandan leaf during the second boiling stage, after the beans have rested for 30 minutes. Cook until the mung beans are completely tender. Once tender, add the granulated sugar and stir until dissolved and evenly mixed. Reduce the sugar if you prefer it less sweet.
Grate the coconut and extract the coconut milk using 300 ml of water. Cook the coconut milk with a pinch of salt and one pandan leaf. Stir frequently to prevent the coconut milk from splitting.
Cut the white bread into cubes as desired and set aside. Prepare the ice cubes as well.
Put some mung beans into a bowl and add the bread cubes. Pour in as much coconut milk as desired.
Add ice cubes and sweetened condensed milk. The iced mung bean porridge is ready to refresh you.

Mix the grated coconut with salt, then steam for 15 minutes. Remove and set aside.
Put the starter mixture ingredients into a saucepan and stir well. Cook over the stove, stirring continuously until thickened. Turn off the heat.
In a bowl, combine the glutinous rice flour and salt. Pour in the starter mixture and stir until a smooth dough forms.
Weigh out 16 g portions of dough. Take one portion, roll it into a ball, and flatten it. Fill with 4 g of palm sugar, then seal and roll it into a ball again. Repeat until all the dough is used.
Bring 700 ml of water to a boil. Add the klepon. Once they float to the surface, remove them and roll them in the grated coconut.
Serve.
strIngredient10: Palm sugar, finely sliced and shaped into small portions
strIngredient14: Water for boiling the dough balls

strInstructions:
Steam the sweet potato, then peel it.
Prepare the ingredients. Mix the grated coconut with salt, then steam for about 15 minutes.
Mash the sweet potato, then add the salt, vanilla powder, and tapioca flour. Knead until combined, adding a little water.
Add the chili-red food coloring and knead again until evenly colored and smooth.
Take a small portion of dough and flatten it. Place palm sugar in the center, then close the dough, smooth it, and roll it into a marble-sized ball. Repeat until all the dough is used.
Bring water to a boil, then add the klepon balls. Wait until they float to the surface, then remove and drain briefly.
Immediately roll them in the grated coconut so they do not stick.
Arrange on a serving plate and serve. Enjoy making them! 😋😊

Steam the grated coconut with the pandan leaves and set aside.
Mash the steamed purple sweet potato and mix it with Rose Brand glutinous rice flour, Rose Brand tapioca flour, Rose Brand instant coconut milk, and the water, adding the water little by little.
Knead until the dough can be shaped into balls and no longer sticks to your hands.
