Take a small portion of dough, flatten it, add palm sugar, then roll it into a ball and seal it tightly.
Heat the water until warm but not boiling. Add the klepon and cook until they float to the surface.
Remove them and roll them in the steamed grated coconut. Serve.

Mix the pumpkin, salt, and flour until combined. Gradually add water while kneading. Once the dough can be shaped into balls, set aside any remaining water.
Dice the chocolate bar. Take a small portion of dough, flatten it, add chocolate, and roll it into a ball.
Boil the balls in boiling water until they float to the surface. Roll them in grated coconut mixed with a little salt. Serve.
strIngredient7: Coconut, with the brown skin removed, grated and briefly steamed

strInstructions:
Mix all the dough ingredients evenly. Gradually pour in the pandan juice, stirring until the dough can be shaped into balls.
Take a small portion of dough and fill it with palm sugar. Repeat until all the dough is used.
Boil the klepon balls until cooked, then remove them.
Steam the topping ingredients for about 15 minutes.
Roll the cooked klepon balls in the steamed grated coconut. They are ready to serve.
strIngredient9: Grated coconut with a pinch of salt

strMeal: Klepon Pandan Kenyal, Balur Kelapa Parut 💚🥥
strInstructions:
Mix the glutinous rice flour, rice flour, and salt.
Gradually pour in the warm water while kneading until the dough can be shaped into balls.
Take a small portion of dough, flatten it, add palm sugar, and seal it into a ball.
Bring the water and pandan leaves to a boil. Add the klepon.
Once they float to the surface, remove and drain them.
Roll the klepon in grated coconut that has been steamed with a little salt and pandan leaves.
The klepon is ready to serve. 💚

Prepare all the ingredients. Put the glutinous rice flour in a bowl, then pour in the Indomilk Creamy Matcha sweetened condensed milk. Add water while kneading, stopping when the dough can be shaped into balls.
Bring water to a boil. Take a small pinch of dough, roll it into a ball, then press it into a small cup shape. Fill it with Indomilk Creamy Matcha sweetened condensed milk.
Seal it tightly and roll it into a ball again. Repeat until all the dough is used, then boil the balls in boiling water.
Once they float to the surface, the klepon is cooked. Drain, then roll in grated coconut.
Serve and enjoy! ❤
strIngredient2: Indomilk Creamy Matcha sweetened condensed milk
strIngredient6: Indomilk Creamy Matcha sweetened condensed milk

strInstructions:
Steam the grated coconut for 10 minutes. Add salt and mix well.
Slice the palm sugar.
Combine the wet mixture ingredients and cook while stirring with a spatula until thickened. Add it to the glutinous rice flour and tapioca flour mixture, stirring with a spatula while still hot. Once warm, knead briefly. Let the dough rest for 15 minutes.
Take a portion of dough and shape it into a cylinder. Cut into pieces of about 12 g each. Cover the dough with plastic wrap to prevent it from drying out.
Shape each piece into a small bowl, fill with 3 g of sliced palm sugar, then seal and roll into a ball.
Place the balls into a pot of boiling water with the heat turned off. Repeat step 5.
Cook for about 3 minutes until they float, then continue cooking for another 3 minutes to ensure the klepon is cooked through.
Roll the klepon in the grated coconut.
Serve as a snack with tea or coffee.

Prepare the ingredients. Steam the grated coconut with salt and pandan leaves for 15 minutes. Slice the palm sugar and shape it into small balls. Set aside.
Place the rice flour and Rose Brand granulated sugar in a pan. Add water and pandan paste. Mix well.
Cook over low heat until thickened. Turn off the heat.
Pour the Rose Brand glutinous rice flour into a bowl. Add the klepon mixture and knead until smooth and pliable. Take some dough, fill it with palm sugar, seal it, and roll into a ball.
Boil the klepon in boiling water until cooked and floating. Drain and coat with the grated coconut mixture.
The traditional Javanese klepon is ready to serve.

Combine the cassava, potato, and tapioca starch, then set aside. Add food coloring.
Next, add the Cadbury pieces one at a time.
Bring the steamer water to a boil. Line the steamer with banana leaves, then arrange the klepon on top.
Steam for 26–30 minutes, then remove and drain.
Roll the klepon in the young grated coconut, which has also been steamed. Garnish with Cadbury and grapes.
Ready to enjoy. Give it a try!
strIngredient2: Small potato, boiled, mashed, and mixed with the cassava
strIngredient4: A few drops of green and blue food coloring
strIngredient5: A bowl of grated young coconut

strInstructions:
Prepare the Rose Brand granulated sugar, blended into a fine powder, Rose Brand cornstarch, Rose Brand margarine, and egg. Sorry, the other ingredients were not photographed.
Manually whisk the egg, Rose Brand margarine, and butter. Add the blended Rose Brand granulated sugar, powdered milk, and Rose Brand cornstarch. Mix well. Gradually add the all-purpose flour and mix again, then knead by hand until a dough forms. Add green food coloring as needed.
Take a portion of dough, roll it into a ball, flatten it, add the filling, and roll it into a ball again. Coat with desiccated coconut. Repeat until all the dough is used. Bake until cooked.
Store in a jar or enjoy immediately.

Coffee: Brew the ground coffee with hot water and stir well. Set aside.
Palm sugar syrup: Cook the granulated sugar over low heat until it caramelizes. Add the shaved palm sugar and cook until melted.
Add water and pandan leaves. Bring to a boil, then continue cooking for 15–20 minutes until slightly thickened. Let cool.
Pandan juice: Cut the pandan leaves into pieces. Blend with water until smooth, then strain. Set aside.
Dilute the instant coconut milk with warm water. Set aside.
Prepare all the ingredients for the klepon coffee. Pour in 2–3 tbsp of palm sugar syrup, add ice until the glass is almost full, then pour in about 60 ml of coconut milk, followed by 75 ml of coffee and 2 tbsp of pandan juice. Stir before drinking.

Prepare all the ingredients.
Combine all the coating ingredients in a heatproof bowl. Steam for about 15–20 minutes. Set aside and transfer to a bowl.
Filling: Shave or finely slice the palm sugar. You can shape it into balls for a neater filling.
Make the klepon dough: Place the water, Rose Brand rice flour, Rose Brand granulated sugar, and red food coloring in a pan.
Mix well and cook until the mixture thickens. Turn off the heat.
Pour the Rose Brand glutinous rice flour into a bowl, then add the klepon mixture. Knead until smooth and pliable.
Take some dough, make an indentation, and fill it with palm sugar. Seal and shape into a ball. Repeat until all the dough and filling are used. Boil in boiling water until the klepon is cooked and floats.
Drain the klepon and coat with the coconut mixture. The red-and-white klepon is ready to serve.

Combine all the flours in a bowl, add salt, and gradually add a little water while kneading.
Add food coloring and mix until evenly combined. Let the dough rest.
Divide the dough, fill each portion with shaved palm sugar, and roll into a ball. Place on a tray lightly dusted with tapioca flour.
Bring water to a boil, then add the balls and cook until they float. Roll them in grated coconut until coated.

Mash the pumpkin, then combine it with the glutinous rice flour and tapioca flour. Add salt and mix, then gradually pour in warm water until the dough can be shaped. Stop adding water once the dough is workable.
Take a small portion of dough, flatten it, and add shaved palm sugar as needed. Roll into a ball. Repeat until all the dough is used.
Bring enough water to a boil. Boil the klepon until cooked and floating. Remove and let cool until warm.
Roll the klepon in the coating mixture until covered with grated coconut. Done.

Prepare the required ingredients.
Mix the rice flour, granulated sugar, and water in a saucepan. Cook until thickened and the color changes. Set aside.
Repeat the same process for the red dough, adding red food coloring.
Prepare separate bowls for the red and white mixtures. Add glutinous rice flour to each.
Mix and knead until evenly combined and pliable enough to roll into balls.
Finely shave the palm sugar.
Take a portion of dough, flatten it, and place sugar in the center. Enclose the filling and shape into a ball. Repeat until all the dough is used.
Bring water to a boil and cook the klepon until they float. Drain.
Divide the grated coconut into two portions and add salt to each. Mix well, then add red food coloring to one portion. Steam for about 10 minutes.
Once the coconut has cooled slightly, roll the red klepon in the red coconut and the white klepon in the white coconut.
Ready to enjoy.

Steam the grated coconut with salt and pandan leaves for about 10 minutes to help it keep longer and become fragrant. Set aside.
Place the glutinous rice flour and salt in a bowl. Gradually pour in the beetroot juice while kneading. Do not add it all at once, as the amount needed may vary depending on the flour's moisture and the juice's thickness. Knead until the dough is soft, smooth, and easy to roll into balls without cracking. If too dry, add a little more beetroot juice; if too soft, add a little glutinous rice flour.
Take about 8–10 g of dough, flatten it, place palm sugar in the center, then seal tightly and roll into a ball. Make sure there are no gaps so the sugar does not leak out. Bring water to a boil and add the klepon. Once they float, continue boiling for about 1–2 minutes, then remove.
Drain briefly and immediately roll in the grated coconut.

Steam the grated coconut with 2 pandan leaves and a little salt.
Slice the palm sugar. You can melt it if you prefer, but I chose the easier option.
Bring water to a boil and add 3 pandan leaves.
Combine the glutinous rice flour, pandan paste, and enough water. Knead until the dough no longer sticks to your hands and can be shaped into balls.
Shape the dough into balls and fill them with palm sugar. Drop them directly into the boiling water. Remove them when they float to the surface, which means they are cooked.
Roll the klepon in the grated coconut until all sides are covered.
Repeat until all the dough is used. These simple klepon are ready to enjoy.

Combine the sweet potato, salt, and granulated sugar. Mash until smooth.
Add the glutinous rice flour, tapioca flour, and warm water. Mix well.
Add red food coloring and mix well. Take some dough and fill it with palm sugar.
Bring water and 2 pandan leaves to a boil. Add the klepon and cook until they float. Remove and let cool.
Combine all the custard ingredients in a saucepan. Cook until done and thickened.
Ready to serve—the red-and-white klepon are truly soft and melt in your mouth.

strMeal: Dadar Gulung Coklat Isi Unti Matcha Istimewa 💚
strInstructions:
Prepare the required ingredients.
Pour 1 sachet of Indomilk Creamy Matcha Sweetened Condensed Milk over the leftover grated coconut. Mix well and add salt. Transfer to a bowl, add one knotted pandan leaf, and steam in a hot steamer for about 10 minutes.
For a richer flavor, ideal moisture, and a brighter color, add the margarine and 1 sachet of Indomilk Creamy Matcha Sweetened Condensed Milk. Mix well. The delicious, vibrant matcha coconut filling is ready to use.
For the wrappers, combine the all-purpose flour, sugar, cocoa powder, salt, and egg. Gradually add the milk and water. Mix and strain until smooth.
Cook the wrappers in a square pan. Fill with the special matcha coconut filling, roll up, and repeat until all the mixture is used.
For an extra-special finish, dust with powdered sugar and add Indomilk Creamy Matcha Sweetened Condensed Milk.
The café-style rolled pancakes with special matcha coconut filling are ready to serve. I used the leftover filling to make filled Kue Ku as well.
strIngredient3: Indomilk Creamy Matcha Sweetened Condensed Milk

strInstructions:
Place the flour, vanilla, and coconut milk in a bowl. Mix briefly with a mixer until the batter is smooth and elastic, then add 2 tbsp of cooking oil.
Combine all the filling ingredients in a bowl and mix with a mixer until evenly combined, then pour into a pan. Cook over the lowest heat to prevent burning, and keep stirring.
Cook the rolled-pancake wrappers in a nonstick pan and remove them. While they are still warm, add the filling. Ready to serve.
strIngredient16: Santan cair bisa ditambahkan jika ingin lebih cair adonannya

strInstructions:
Place all the coconut filling ingredients in a pan and cook until evenly combined. Let cool.
Combine all the wrapper ingredients and mix well, then strain the batter.
Take 3 ladlefuls of batter, add white food coloring, and mix well. Pour into a squeeze bottle and set aside. Add chili-red food coloring to the remaining batter and mix well.
Heat a crepe pan and pour in the white batter to make a pattern of your choice. Let it cook briefly. Add the red batter and spread it over the entire surface, covering the pattern. Cook until the edges release from the pan, then remove.
Take one wrapper and add 2 tsp of coconut filling. Fold the top, right, and left sides inward, then roll forward. Repeat until all the wrappers are used.

Make the coconut filling: Put the grated coconut, Rose Brand granulated sugar, palm sugar (I also added some palm sugar syrup I had stored in the refrigerator), salt, pandan leaves, and water in a pan. Cook until the liquid has evaporated.
Set the filling aside.
In a bowl, combine the wheat flour, Rose Brand tapioca flour, granulated sugar, and pandan flavoring. Gradually add water while stirring to help everything combine.
Once evenly mixed, add the egg and stir again. Add Rose Brand cooking oil and mix well.
Let the batter rest for 30 minutes to allow the gluten to develop. Prepare a nonstick pan with a diameter of 20 cm and lightly grease it with cooking oil. Stir the batter again, then pour in one ladleful and spread it out. Cook until the edges dry, then transfer to a plate. Repeat until all the batter is used.
This made 13 pieces. Take a wrapper with the side to be filled facing up, add 1 tbsp of coconut filling, then fold it like an envelope. Repeat until all the batter is used.
Arrange on a serving plate. The rolled pancakes are ready to serve.

Prepare the coconut filling ingredients.
Cook the palm sugar, water, pandan leaves, and salt until the sugar dissolves. Add the grated coconut and cook over low heat, stirring until the liquid reduces and the filling becomes fairly dry. Set aside.
Prepare the wrapper ingredients. Mix 65 ml of Rose Brand coconut milk with water. Stir well and set aside.
Combine the wheat flour, Rose Brand tapioca flour, and salt. Add the egg and Rose Brand coconut milk mixture gradually, stirring until smooth. Strain the batter to remove lumps.
Add pandan paste and Rose Brand cooking oil. Stir until smooth.
Heat a nonstick pan over low to medium heat. Pour in one ladleful of batter and spread it thinly. Cook until the surface is set and the wrapper can be lifted easily. There is no need to flip it.
Take one wrapper and place about 1 tbsp of filling near the bottom. Fold the right and left sides inward, then roll tightly.
The rolled pancakes filled with coconut filling are ready to serve.

Mix the granulated sugar, salt, and water. Stir well.
Add the grated coconut and stir again until the liquid reduces. Add pandan leaves for extra fragrance, then set aside.
In another bowl, combine the wheat flour, tapioca flour, and egg.
Add powdered coconut milk, salt, and water. Mix until evenly combined and the consistency is neither too thin nor too thick. Add pandan paste (sorry, I forgot to photograph the batter).
Heat a nonstick pan and wipe it with a tissue lightly coated in oil. Pour in a thin layer of batter and cook until done. Remove. Tip: Make sure the pan is hot so the surface develops pores.
Take one wrapper, add the white coconut filling, and roll tightly.
Arrange on a plate and garnish with pandan leaves if desired. Yummy!

Make the coconut filling first. Add palm sugar, granulated sugar, salt, pandan leaves, and water. Cook until the sugar dissolves.
Add the grated coconut and stir well. Cook until the liquid reduces, then add the glutinous rice flour. Do not cook until completely dry.
Once the liquid has reduced, let the filling cool. Next, make the wrapper batter by combining all the ingredients and mixing with a spatula, then strain.
Heat a nonstick pan. Mine is 24 cm in diameter, although a 22 cm pan is recommended. Once hot, lightly grease it with oil using a tissue. Remember to grease the pan each time before cooking a wrapper.
You can also use an inverted pan lightly greased with oil using a tissue, which makes cooking the wrappers easier.
Pour in the chocolate batter to make a pattern of your choice, then add one ladleful of green batter. Cook until done.
Transfer to a tray to cool. Repeat until all the batter is used. Take a wrapper and add 1 tbsp of filling.
Fold and roll it up. Repeat until finished.
strIngredient8: Glutinous rice flour, without mixing with water
strIngredient10: Cakra wheat flour; Triangle-brand flour can also be used
strIngredient15: Instant coconut milk mixed with water, with a total combined weight of 1,200 g or 1,300 g for thinner wrappers
strIngredient18: Pewarna hijau muda atau hijau apel bisa di ganti dengan pewarna kuning muda 1/2 sdt
strIngredient20: Butter di lelehkan dan di dinginkan atau bisa di ganti dengan 3 sdm minyak goreng
strIngredient25: Air...semua bahan di aduk licin lalu di saring dan di masukkan ke plastik segitiga

strInstructions:
Bring the water, granulated sugar, pandan leaves, kaffir lime leaves, and vanilla essence to a boil. Add the grated coconut, stir well, and cook again until the coconut becomes somewhat dry.
Add all the wrapper ingredients and mix with a mixer until combined and no flour lumps remain. Add the water gradually.
Cook the wrappers in a nonstick pan until all the batter is used. Take one wrapper, add the filling, and roll it up.
Wrap in plastic or banana leaves, and the rolled pancakes are ready to serve.
strIngredient10: Pandan paste and green food coloring

strInstructions:
Make the coconut filling: combine water, palm sugar, granulated sugar, pandan leaves, and salt. Cook until dissolved. Add the grated coconut and stir until evenly combined and the liquid has reduced. Remove from heat and let cool.
Make butterfly pea flower water by boiling a handful of dried butterfly pea flowers in 2 cups of water. Let cool, then strain. Measure as needed.
Mix the butterfly pea flower water with coconut milk. Beat the egg until smooth, then combine it with the coconut milk and butterfly pea mixture.
Combine all the ingredients and stir until the sugar dissolves, then strain.
Heat a nonstick pan. Pour in a thin layer of batter and cook into a thin pancake. Remove and set aside.
Place a sheet of pancake on a flat surface, add the coconut filling, and roll tightly.
Serve.
Enjoy!

Cook all the coconut filling ingredients until the mixture is cooked and fairly dry. Remove from heat and set aside. Taste and add more sugar if needed. Then prepare the remaining ingredients.
Mix all the pancake ingredients and stir until smooth with no lumps. Strain if necessary. Add red food coloring to your liking.
Heat a nonstick pan over low heat and lightly grease it with margarine or oil. Pour in the batter and cook until the pancake is set, then remove it. Repeat until all the batter is used.
Add some coconut filling, then roll and fold the pancakes. Repeat until finished. The rolled pancakes are ready to serve.
The pancakes are delicious and flexible even without eggs, and the coconut filling is creamy.
Adjust the sweetness of the filling to your preference.
One definitely won't be enough!
Enjoy!
strIngredient7: Fiber cream dissolved in enough warm water

strInstructions:
Pour the water into a saucepan, add the palm sugar, and cook on the stove. Stir until the sugar dissolves. You do not need to bring it to a boil. Remove from heat and strain.
Strain the mixture, then add the grated coconut, pandan leaf, granulated sugar, and salt. Cook until the liquid has evaporated.
Once the liquid has evaporated, add the sweetened condensed milk, vanilla, and margarine. Stir until combined, then let cool.
Cut the pandan leaves into pieces, blend them with water until smooth, then strain.
Strain the mixture, then add the wheat flour, tapioca flour, salt, vanilla, and pandan paste.
Whisk until smooth, then strain again. The batter is ready to cook. Stir the batter before making each pancake.
Heat a nonstick pan and lightly brush it with oil. Pour in the batter and cook until the edges of the pancake begin to lift. Remove from the pan.
Place one pancake wrapper on a flat surface and add one heaping tablespoon of coconut filling. Fold it like an envelope, then roll it up. Repeat until finished.
Ready to serve. Easy to make, right?

Prepare the filling first. Put all the filling ingredients into a pan. Tear the pandan leaf lengthwise and tie it into a knot. Cook until the liquid has evaporated and the mixture is cooked through. Set aside.
Combine all the pancake wrapper ingredients. Gradually pour in the coconut milk and stir until evenly combined. Finally, strain to ensure the batter is smooth and free of lumps.
Combine all the ingredients for the white pattern and stir well. Strain if necessary.
Make the pancakes by spooning the white batter onto a preheated nonstick pan first. Wait briefly, then pour in the red batter.
Once the edges are dry and lift away from the pan, the pancake is cooked. Transfer it to a plate, add 1 tablespoon of coconut filling, press the filling together, and roll while still warm. The red-and-white rolled pancakes are ready to serve.

strMeal: Dar Lung Lang (Dadar Gulung Bunga Telang)
strInstructions:
1. First, make the rolled pancake wrappers. Wash the butterfly pea flowers. Bring the water to a boil, turn off the heat, and add the flowers. Let them steep until the water changes color, then set aside.
2. Combine the wheat flour, tapioca flour, salt, and margarine. Stir evenly, then add the butterfly pea flower water until the batter is not too thin. Make sure there are no flour lumps. Strain the batter if necessary.
3. Heat a flat nonstick pan or skillet. Lightly grease it with oil, then pour in about 2 tablespoons of batter. Cook over low heat until done and no longer sticking. Remove from the pan. Repeat until all the batter is used.
4. Make the filling by combining the grated coconut, granulated sugar, water, and pandan leaf. Stir until evenly combined, then cook until the liquid has reduced. Remove from heat and set aside.
5. Assemble: Take one pancake wrapper and add 1 tablespoon of filling. Fold it like an envelope, then roll it up. Repeat until finished. Ready to serve.

Combine the sugar, salt, water, and pandan leaf. Cook over low heat until the sugar dissolves, then add the grated coconut. Cook until the liquid has reduced and the mixture is dry. Divide into two portions. Add 2 drops of red food coloring to one portion and stir well. Set aside and let cool.
To make the wrappers, combine all the ingredients and stir until smooth. Divide the batter into two portions and add 3 drops of red food coloring to one portion. Set aside.
Heat a pan over medium heat and lightly grease it with oil. Pour in a little batter and spread it evenly. Cook until done, then set aside. Repeat until all the batter is used.
Shape the cooled filling into small balls. Repeat until finished.
Cut each pancake wrapper into five sections, as shown in the picture, without cutting all the way through. Place the filling in the center and fold the wrapper as shown.
The rose-shaped rolled pancakes are ready to enjoy.
strIngredient14: Pack of instant thick coconut milk

strInstructions:
Combine all the wrapper ingredients. Mix the liquid ingredients separately and stir until combined. Pour them into the flour mixture and stir until smooth with no lumps. Let rest for 15 minutes before cooking the pancakes.
Heat a pancake pan until hot. Pour in one ladleful of batter for each pancake. The pan used here has a diameter of 22 cm. Repeat until all the batter is used.
Make the filling by combining all the coconut filling ingredients. Cook until the filling is cooked and set. Let cool before using.
Place a pancake with its smooth side facing up. Add 2–3 tablespoons of coconut filling, fold, and roll. Ready to serve.

Make the chocolate custard: combine the cocoa powder, cornstarch, and salt. Stir well. Add the egg and stir again. Pour in the milk and turn on the stove.
Cook over low heat until boiling and thickened, stirring continuously. Once thick, add the dark cooking chocolate and stir until melted. Turn off the heat, let cool, and transfer to a piping bag.
Make the wrappers by combining all the ingredients and gradually adding the water. Stir well. Strain if necessary.
Heat a nonstick pan and lightly grease it with cooking oil. Once hot, pour in one ladleful of batter and spread evenly. When cooked, the wrapper will release from the pan on its own. Remove it.
Place a banana on a pancake wrapper and add enough chocolate custard. Fold the wrapper and repeat until finished.
Ready to enjoy.

Mash the bananas until mostly smooth. Put them in a nonstick pan with the sugar and margarine.
Cook the bananas over medium heat until the mixture is cooked through. Turn off the heat and let cool.
Make the wrappers by combining the wheat flour, tapioca flour, salt, vanilla, and water in a bowl. Stir well, then strain.
Divide the batter into several portions. I divided mine into white and chocolate portions using chocolate paste. Transfer to piping bags and adjust the coloring to your preference.
Heat a nonstick pan and lightly grease it with oil, spreading the oil with a tissue. Make a pattern—in this case, polka dots—and let it dry slightly. Add the white batter and cook until the top is dry and the edges lift away. Repeat until all the batter is used.
Remove each wrapper and transfer it to a flat surface. Add the filling, then fold the top and sides as shown in the picture.
The banana-filled rolled pancakes are ready to serve.

First, prepare all the pancake ingredients. Combine the wheat flour, tapioca flour, and milk. Whisk together.
Add the egg and melted margarine. Stir well, then strain to remove any lumps. Add the cocoa powder.
Stir until the batter turns brown. Heat a nonstick pan and grease it with margarine or oil, then wipe with a tissue to prevent large holes from forming in the pancakes. Pour in one ladleful of batter and spread it over the pan. Wait until bubbles appear on the surface, then remove the pancake. Repeat until all the batter is used.
Prepare the pancake wrappers, chocolate glaze, and ripe bananas. Cut each banana lengthwise into four pieces.
Take a pancake wrapper and fill it with banana and chocolate glaze. Fold it into a rolled pancake shape. Repeat until finished.
Once all the pancakes are rolled, serve with chocolate topping or another topping of your choice.

In the name of God, prepare all the necessary ingredients and equipment. In a clean saucepan, combine all the custard filling ingredients except the unsalted butter. Stir well, place on the stove, and add the butter.
Cook over low heat, stirring continuously until the custard thickens and becomes smooth. Remove from heat and transfer to another clean container. Cover with plastic wrap, pressing it directly onto the surface, and let cool. The original recipe notes that it can be chilled in the refrigerator.
Next, prepare the wrappers by combining all the wrapper ingredients in a bowl. Stir well, then gradually pour in the chocolate mixture.
Stir until there are no lumps. The batter should be somewhat thin. Heat a nonstick pan over low heat, pour in one ladleful of batter, and spread it evenly. Cook until done, then remove. Repeat until all the batter is used.
Whisk the custard filling again until smooth, then transfer it to a piping bag. Press the filling down and snip off the tip. Pipe the filling onto the wrappers in the amount you prefer; the original recipe suggests two rows. Roll each wrapper closed. Repeat until finished.
The rolled pancakes are ready to serve. Enjoy making and eating them. The original recipe notes that the flavor is well balanced.

strMeal: Dadar Gulung Cokelat Isi Unti Kelapa
strInstructions:
Prepare the ingredients. Combine the wheat flour, tapioca flour, powdered sugar, cocoa powder, and salt. Pour in the water and stir until evenly mixed.
Add the egg, melted butter, and chocolate paste. Stir until everything is thoroughly combined. Strain the batter to make it smooth and remove lumps.
The finished batter should be thin. It is ready to cook, but you can also let it rest for 5–10 minutes if you prefer.
Heat a nonstick pan. Pour in one ladleful of batter and spread it into a thin layer. Cook until done, then remove. Repeat until all the batter is used. The wrappers are ready to be filled.
For the coconut filling, combine the granulated sugar, pandan leaf, and water. Cook until the sugar dissolves. Add the grated coconut and salt, stir well, and set aside. This white-sugar coconut filling can be used for rolled pancakes, fried bread, steamed buns, and more.
To assemble, take a pancake wrapper and add the coconut filling. Fold and roll it like an envelope.
The chocolate rolled pancakes are ready to enjoy as a snack with tea or coffee.
strIngredient15: Pandan leaf, tied into a knot

strMeal: Unti Kelapa Gula Putih (Bisa Utk Isian Dadar Gulung, Roti Goreng, Bakpao, Dll.)
strInstructions:
Prepare the ingredients. Combine the granulated sugar, pandan leaf, and water in a pan. Cook, stirring, until the sugar dissolves.
Add the grated coconut and salt, then stir well. Cook over low to medium heat, stirring continuously so the bottom does not burn.
Once the coconut and sugar are evenly combined and the liquid has reduced and the mixture is fairly dry, transfer it to a bowl. The coconut filling is ready to use in rolled pancakes, fried bread, or steamed buns. This batch was made for rolled pancake filling.
strIngredient4: Pandan leaf, tied into a knot

strInstructions:
Prepare the ingredients.
Heat 1 tablespoon of Rose Brand margarine and pan-fry the bananas until cooked. Cut each banana into four pieces and set aside.
Combine all the wrapper ingredients and strain. Set aside a small portion of the batter and color it with chocolate paste.
Heat a nonstick pan and make a pattern of your choice. Pour in the remaining white batter and cook the pancakes until all the batter is used.
For the chocolate custard, bring the chocolate milk, dark cooking chocolate, and granulated sugar to a boil. Thicken with cornstarch that has been dissolved in a little water.
Take a pancake wrapper, add a spoonful of chocolate custard and a banana piece, then fold into a triangle.
Serve.

Combine all the spring roll wrapper ingredients and cook thin wrappers in a nonstick pan until all the batter is used. Set aside.
Mix the mayonnaise and sweetened condensed milk until smooth, then set aside.
Take one spring roll wrapper and spread 1 tablespoon of the mayonnaise mixture on it. Add one slice of egg and one slice of sausage, then fold and roll neatly.
Repeat until all the wrappers are filled. Set aside.
Dip each spring roll into the liquid flour batter, coat with breadcrumbs, and fry until golden. Remove from the oil.
strIngredient8: Hard-boiled eggs, each cut into 8 slices
strIngredient9: Sausages, each cut in half and then into 3 slices
strIngredient11: Wheat flour mixed with 300 ml water

strInstructions:
Heat the oil and margarine. Sauté the chopped onion and garlic until softened. Add all the vegetables and some water, then cook until boiling. Add the seasonings, check the taste, and cook until the vegetables are tender.
Add the milk powder and grated cheese. Stir well, then add the wheat flour and stir until the ragout thickens and the liquid has been absorbed.
Set the ragout aside to cool. Put all the rissole wrapper ingredients into a food processor and blend until smooth. Pour into a clean bowl and let rest for about 15 minutes.
Heat a nonstick pan and pour in one ladleful of batter. Cook until set, then add as much vegetable ragout as you like and fold in both sides.
Repeat until all the batter is used. Dip each rissole in beaten egg, then coat with breadcrumbs.
Heat enough cooking oil and fry the rissoles until cooked on both sides. Remove and drain upright on a draining rack.
Serve with bottled Bangkok chili sauce. The flavor is just right.
strIngredient9: Peeled potatoes, cut into small cubes
strIngredient26: Tepung panir putih (me di blender dl agar lebih halus)
strIngredient27: Telur ayam +2 sdm air kocok lepas

strInstructions:
Prepare the filling first. Dice the carrots and potatoes. Boil until tender, then set aside.
Heat the oil and margarine. Sauté the garlic and onion until fragrant and softened. Add the chicken and sauté until it changes color.
Add the potatoes and carrots, then stir well. Add water and the remaining seasonings: salt, pepper, and mushroom stock powder. Cook until the liquid has reduced and the seasonings have been absorbed. Add the cornstarch, wheat flour, and sweetened condensed milk. Stir well.
Finally, add the milk. Cook until everything is combined. Reduce the heat and continue stirring until the mixture bubbles and thickens.
Transfer to another container and let cool. The ragout is ready to use.
While waiting for the ragout to cool, make the rissole wrappers. Put the wheat flour, tapioca flour, salt, egg, and water into a bowl, reserving 150 ml of water. Whisk until smooth with no lumps, then add the remaining water. The total amount of water is now 750 ml. Strain, add the oil, stir well, and let the batter rest for at least 30 minutes.
Heat a nonstick pan. Pour in one ladleful of batter and tilt the pan to spread it. Cook over low heat and wait until the edges release on their own.
Transfer each wrapper to a plate and repeat until all the batter is used. You can save time by filling each finished wrapper while cooking the next one.
Take one wrapper, add the filling, and fold as shown in the picture. Seal the edge with wheat flour dissolved in water.
Repeat until all the ingredients are used.
Prepare the coating ingredients. Dip each assembled rissole into the dipping mixture, then roll it in breadcrumbs.
Repeat until finished. The rissoles can be fried immediately or stored in the refrigerator or freezer.
Heat oil in a pan. Once hot, fry the rissoles over medium heat. Use enough oil to submerge them completely. Turn each rissole only once.
Repeat until finished.
The rissoles are ready to enjoy or give as a food gift.
strIngredient3: Potatoes, diced and boiled until tender
strIngredient4: Carrots, diced and boiled until tender
strIngredient5: Cornstarch, dissolved in a little water
strIngredient6: Wheat flour, dissolved in a little water

strInstructions:
Combine the wheat flour, tapioca flour, egg, salt, and water. Stir.
Add the oil and strain the batter. Cook into thin wrappers and set aside.
Grind the garlic and finely chop the onion.
Sauté the ground spices until fragrant, then add the onion and carrots and potatoes. Add a little water.
Add seasoning, stock powder, and pepper.
Add the sugar and cook until the vegetables are tender.
Mix the wheat flour with water, pour it into the mixture, and add the milk.
Cook until the liquid has reduced. Take a wrapper, add the filling, and fold.
Mix the dipping ingredients and stir.
Dip each rissole in the mixture, then coat with breadcrumbs.
Fry until browned and serve.

Combine the wheat flour, tapioca flour, milk powder, and salt in a bowl. Stir well.
Gradually pour the water into the bowl while stirring with a whisk or mixer.
Add the egg and beat it into the batter until evenly combined. Then add the oil and stir until thoroughly mixed.
Make sure the batter is not too thick so that it can be poured and spread easily in the pan.
Heat a 22 cm nonstick pan. Pour in enough batter, then rotate the pan to spread it over the entire surface.
Once cooked, transfer the wrapper to a plate or tray. Smooth it out so that no parts are folded over. Repeat until all the batter is used.
To make the filling sauce, combine the mayonnaise, salt, sweetened condensed milk, barbecue sauce, cheese sauce, and grated cheese. Stir until thoroughly combined, then set aside.
Cut each hard-boiled egg into six pieces and set aside.
Prepare the smoked beef. If the slices are large enough, cut each into eight pieces. Set aside.
Take a rissole wrapper and spread about 1 teaspoon of cheese sauce on one side. Add the smoked beef and egg slices.
Fold and roll the wrappers until sealed. Dip them in beaten egg white, then coat evenly with breadcrumbs.
Place in a covered container and freeze until firm. The rissoles are ready to fry and serve.
Fry over medium heat, cooking one side before turning to the other side until golden brown. Remove and drain on tissue paper to absorb excess oil.
strIngredient21: Tepung panir warna orange (saya campur yang putih sebagian)

strInstructions:
Prepare the ingredients and grind the spice paste until smooth. First, make the risoles wrappers using Soft and Elastic Risoles Wrappers #536.
Sauté the spice paste until fragrant, then add the carrots and potatoes and stir.
Add water and wait until it boils. Add the chicken and mix well. Season to taste and cook until the water has reduced.
Add the liquid milk, creamer, and sweetened condensed milk. Mix well.
Cook until most of the liquid has evaporated, then add the flour slurry and mix well.
Wait until the mixture boils and thickens, then turn off the heat and let it cool.
Prepare the spring roll wrappers, filling, flour slurry, and breadcrumbs.
Take one wrapper, add the filling, and fold it like an envelope. Seal it with a little flour slurry.
Repeat until all the filling is used.
Heat the cooking oil and fry the risoles until cooked. Remove and drain.
These are great for selling or snack boxes. Put them in OPP plastic bags and add bird's eye chilies. Yummy, delicious, and creamy!
strIngredient1: Risoles wrappers, Soft and Elastic Risoles Wrappers #536
strIngredient11: Wheat flour, mix with a little water

strInstructions:
Prepare the ingredients:
In a bowl, combine the flour, egg, salt, and water to make the risol wrappers. Mix everything using a whisk or briefly with a mixer on low speed. Let the batter rest briefly, then set aside.
Boil and slice the filling ingredients, such as eggs and smoked beef. Set aside.
To make the wrappers, prepare an 18 cm nonstick pan and brush it with a little cooking oil. Let the pan heat up, then pour in one ladle of batter. Cook until the wrapper is done but not dry, then remove it.
Fill each wrapper with smoked beef, egg, mayonnaise, chili sauce, and tomato sauce.
Fold the filled wrapper into a long shape. Repeat until all the batter and filling are used.
Prepare the coating: blend the breadcrumbs until fine, and mix the flour with water in a separate bowl.
Dip each risol in the flour mixture, then coat it with breadcrumbs. Repeat until all are coated.
The risol can be fried immediately. Heat plenty of cooking oil in a pan over medium-high heat. Once the oil is hot, add the risol and fry until golden yellow, then turn each one over. Turn them only once, reduce the heat, and remove when golden yellow.
The risol can also be frozen for later use.
The smoked beef, egg, and mayonnaise risol is ready to serve 😊

Mix all the wrapper ingredients, then strain the batter.
Heat a nonstick pan and lightly grease it with oil. Pour in 1–2 ladles of batter to make a thin wrapper. Cook until the edges loosen, then remove it. Repeat until all the batter is used.
Place one wrapper on a cutting board. Add sauce, egg, and sausage. Fold in the right and left sides, then roll tightly.
Dip each risol in the flour mixture, then coat it with breadcrumbs.
Fry in hot oil over medium heat until golden yellow.

Make the wrappers first by combining all the wrapper ingredients and mixing until smooth. Cook in a nonstick pan over low heat, then let them cool.
Prepare the filling. Chop all the vegetables and meatballs. Sauté the ground spices, then add the filling ingredients. Cook until done and let cool.
Take one wrapper, add an appropriate amount of filling, fold, and roll it up. To make the coating, combine the flour, salt, and water, then mix well. Dip each risol into the wet mixture, then roll it in breadcrumbs. Repeat until all are coated.
Heat the cooking oil and fry over medium heat until the breadcrumbs become dark in color. Turn each risol only once to prevent it from becoming oily. Remove and drain.
Serve with your favorite sauce.

Prepare all the ingredients. Whisk the granulated sugar, water, egg, salt, baking soda, baking soda, and vanilla until evenly combined. Gradually add the flour, mixing until smooth, then add the yeast and stir again. Let the batter rest for 30 minutes. If using pandan essence, add a little after dividing the batter.
Heat a nonstick pan over medium heat, then pour in the batter and cook over low heat. Wait until it is half-cooked and bubbles appear, then sprinkle with granulated sugar. Cover with a pot lid and cook until done. Remove from the pan, spread with butter, sprinkle with grated cheese, and cover briefly. Cut into pieces.
Repeat the same steps without adding pandan essence.
Serve.

Mix the first group of ingredients, excluding the egg and baking powder. Stir until evenly combined, with no lumps, and until the batter becomes sticky and small bubbles begin to appear. This indicates that the gluten is starting to develop. You can also use a mixer.
Add the egg and baking powder, and mix briefly until just combined.
Let the batter rest for at least 1 hour, up to 5 hours, or store it in the refrigerator to use the next day.
After resting, many small bubbles should appear, indicating that the batter is ready to cook.
Divide the batter into 2 portions.
Mix 50 ml water with ½ tsp baking soda, then divide the mixture into 2 portions.
Add one portion of the baking soda solution and ¼ tsp vanilla or pandan flavoring to each portion of batter.
Heat a nonstick pan over medium heat. Sprinkle a little water on it; if the water evaporates immediately, the pan is hot enough. Pour in the martabak batter.
Tilt the pan toward the edges to form the martabak crust.
Wait for bubbles to rise. Move any area without bubbles toward the heat source, because insufficient heat will prevent bubbles from forming.
Once bubbles appear evenly and begin to burst, immediately lower the heat and sprinkle with granulated sugar. The sugar can also help the bubbles burst.
You can place a metal plate under the pan to prevent the martabak from burning.
Cover the pan and cook for 2–3 minutes until done. To check, touch the martabak with your index finger; if it is no longer sticky, it is cooked.
Remove the martabak from the pan. Spread margarine or butter evenly over it and cover briefly so it melts.
Cut the martabak in half and add toppings to taste, such as chocolate sprinkles or cheese.
Drizzle sweetened condensed milk over the top.
Finally, stack the two halves and cut into pieces.
The foolproof, honeycombed, chewy nonstick-pan martabak manis is ready to serve and enjoy.
The key to making martabak successfully in a nonstick pan is not the ingredients, but understanding how your stove's heat works.

Put the wheat flour, cornstarch, salt, and baking powder in a bowl and mix well.
Combine the water, egg, sugar, and vanilla and mix well. Pour into the flour mixture and stir until there are no lumps. Cover the batter and let it rest for about 1 hour.
Mix the remaining water with the baking soda, then add it to the batter and mix well.
Heat a non-stick Teflon pan over low to medium heat. Wait until the pan is hot before adding the batter, making sure to spread a little extra around the edges. Let it sit until bubbles appear and the edges are cooked. Sprinkle with a little sugar, lower the heat, then cover the pan.
Once the batter is cooked, turn off the heat and remove the martabak. Spread butter over it while hot and add toppings as desired. Enjoy!

Put the granulated sugar, wheat flour, cornstarch, egg, baking powder, soda powder, powdered milk, and salt in a bowl, then add the coconut milk and liquid milk.
Add the water, mixing some of it with warm water, then stir until evenly combined and smooth. Let the batter rest for about 3.5 hours.
Heat a nonstick pan until very hot, then pour in the batter. Let bubbles form, lower the heat, and wait until the surface dries. Sprinkle with granulated sugar. Remove from the pan, spread with margarine, and add toppings of your choice.
strIngredient13: Drops of light yellow food coloring

strInstructions:
Whisk the egg, sugar, and instant yeast until the sugar dissolves.
Gradually add the flour and water. Stir until smooth and evenly combined. Let the batter rest for 1 hour until it rises.
Stir the risen batter again and add the salt. Mix until evenly combined. Heat the mold, pour the batter into the apem mold, and press the center to create crispy edges.
Once the edges are dry and browned, remove the apem and let it cool. Add chocolate sprinkles, grated cheese, and white sweetened condensed milk as toppings.
Ready to enjoy.

Mix the batter ingredients, excluding the water, Fermipan yeast, egg, and baking soda.
Gradually add the water while stirring or beating vigorously with a whisk until smooth. Add the Fermipan yeast and mix well. Cover with a cloth and let rest for 30 minutes.
Add the beaten egg and granulated sugar to the batter, then mix well.
Finally, add the baking soda and melted margarine.
Heat a nonstick pan (I use a 20 cm pan) over medium heat. Once it is really hot, pour in about 3–4 full ladles of batter. Spread some batter around the edges to form the usual martabak crust. When bubbles appear, sprinkle with granulated sugar. Lower the heat and cover the pan.
Once cooked, remove the martabak, spread with margarine, and top with sweetened condensed milk and grated cheese. Enjoy while warm for a softer texture.

Mix all the ingredients except the water and baking soda. Use a whisk and stir until there are no lumps. Cover with a clean cloth and let rest for 30–60 minutes; I rested mine for 60 minutes.
Heat a nonstick pan or martabak mold until very hot. Add the water and baking soda mixture, then stir well. Pour the batter into the pan using a ladle and shape the edges to form the martabak crust. Let holes form, sprinkle with a little granulated sugar, then cover the pan and cook until done and the surface is dry.
Remove from the pan and cut in half. Spread with margarine or butter, sprinkle with chocolate sprinkles and grated cheese, then add white sweetened condensed milk. Fold the martabak, spread margarine or butter over the outside, and cut into pieces as desired.
Serve.
strIngredient9: Water + 1/4 tsp baking soda, mixed well

strInstructions:
Combine all the ingredients and mix until the batter dissolves evenly and becomes bubbly.
Heat the mini martabak mold until hot. This is one of the tips for getting a honeycombed texture. Grease only the bottom of each cavity with margarine, not the edges, because the batter may not stick and the edges may collapse.
Once the pan is hot, pour in one ladle of batter and press once to form the martabak edge. Do this only once so it can rise and form a honeycomb texture.
Wait until the batter has risen and developed a full honeycomb pattern, then sprinkle with sugar and cover briefly until the edges look dry and golden brown. If the edges are not dry enough, they may collapse.
When cooked, brush with margarine and remove from the pan. Add toppings of your choice, finishing with sweetened condensed milk.

Crack the egg, add the sugar, and stir until dissolved.
Add the wheat flour while sifting it in, then stir until evenly combined. Add the liquid milk and mix well.
Since I didn't have chocolate sprinkles, I mixed cocoa powder and granulated sugar together instead.
Prepare a flat pan or nonstick pan. Heat over medium-low heat and grease with a little margarine. Once melted, pour in half a ladle of batter and spread it thinly. Before the batter dries, sprinkle the chocolate-sugar topping over it.
Fold it twice to make an elongated shape. Once folded, transfer it directly to a plate.

Prepare a clean bowl and all the ingredients. Add the wheat flour, sugar, yeast, egg, baking powder, vanilla, and water to the bowl. Stir until evenly combined. Cover the bowl with a cloth and let the batter rest for 1 hour.
After 1 hour, once the batter is bubbly, add the melted margarine and baking soda. Stir until evenly combined.
Heat a mini martabak mold over low heat. Test it by sprinkling a little water on it; if it sizzles and evaporates immediately, the mold is hot enough. Pour one ladle of batter into a cavity. Wait until holes begin to form, then cover the mold and cook until done.
When the bottom is brown, remove the martabak from the mold, immediately brush with margarine, and add chocolate sprinkles and sweetened condensed milk, or other toppings of your choice.

Mix all the ingredients until the batter is smooth and free of lumps. Strain it if you are unsure.
Beat vigorously for 10 minutes until small bubbles appear. Cover with plastic wrap and refrigerate for 6 hours.
The total batter volume is approximately 400 ml. Divide it into 2 portions.
Stack the stove supports as shown in the photo or place a sheet of metal underneath to prevent direct heat from reaching the nonstick pan. Heat the pan over low heat and cover it so the heat spreads evenly. While waiting, add half of the additional ingredients to half of the batter and beat vigorously.
Test the pan's heat by sprinkling a little water on it. If the water evaporates or sizzles immediately, the pan is hot enough.
Pour in the batter, then use a spoon to press the edges into a martabak crust. Set the heat to medium. You may cover the pan to distribute the heat evenly, but wipe the lid promptly if a lot of condensation forms.
Once many bubbles have formed, sprinkle with granulated sugar. Lower the heat and cover the pan, wiping the lid occasionally if it becomes wet.
When the surface is dry, turn off the heat. Leave the pan covered for about 1 minute.
Spread with butter or margarine as needed, then add toppings of your choice.
This is how the outer crust looks—not burnt 😍 Spread the outside crust with butter or margarine as well.
Cut as desired and enjoy while warm.

Combine the wheat flour, Cap Pak Tani Gunung tapioca flour, Rose Brand granulated sugar, and water in a bowl. Whisk until the sugar dissolves and the flour is free of lumps.
Add the baking powder and black forest chocolate paste. Mix again while beating vigorously to incorporate plenty of air. Continue until bubbles appear. Cover with plastic wrap or a cloth and let rest for 30 minutes.
Add the baking soda. Stir again while beating lightly until foamy bubbles form.
Prepare a nonstick pan and heat over medium heat. Sprinkle water onto the pan; if the water moves around and evaporates quickly, the pan is ready. Pour in enough batter to fill about three-quarters of the pan. Press the batter to form the edges.
Wait until the honeycomb pattern forms, then sprinkle with Rose Brand granulated sugar.
Cover the pan and cook until the top is done. Do not cook too long; remove the sweet martabak as soon as the top begins to dry and is cooked.
While still hot, spread with Rose Brand butter and sprinkle with chocolate sprinkles.
strIngredient2: Cap Pak Tani Gunung tapioca flour
strIngredient6: Drops of black forest chocolate paste
strIngredient11: Rose Brand granulated sugar for sprinkling

strInstructions:
Mix the wheat flour, cornstarch, granulated sugar, salt, and water. Then add the egg and baking powder. Let the batter rest for 60 minutes, covered with a clean cloth.
Next, prepare the water and baking soda. Add this mixture to the batter and stir well.
Pour the batter into a nonstick pan; do not grease the pan with margarine. Wait until bubbles or holes appear on the surface of the martabak, sprinkle with sugar, and cover until cooked.
Once cooked, brush with margarine.
Sprinkle with chocolate sprinkles and sweetened condensed milk. Fold the martabak in half, then cut as desired.
The chocolate sweet martabak is ready to serve. Delicious! 👍👍
strIngredient15: Margarine for brushing the outer crust

strInstructions:
Prepare a clean bowl for the batter. Add 225 ml water, 70 g granulated sugar, L'arome, and salt. Whisk until the sugar dissolves or nearly dissolves.
Add the wheat flour and whisk until evenly combined. Add 2 tbsp cocoa powder and mix until the batter is smooth and uniform. Cover the bowl with plastic wrap or a clean cloth and let rest for 1 hour.
After 1 hour, prepare a pan and heat it over low heat. While waiting for the pan to heat, add the egg, remaining 50 ml water, and baking soda to the flour mixture. Stir until the egg is fully incorporated, beating the batter vigorously. Small bubbles will appear because of the baking soda.
Test the pan's heat by sprinkling a little water on it. A gentle sizzling sound means the pan is ready. If the sizzling is loud, turn off the heat briefly. Pour in the batter, filling the pan or martabak mold to no more than halfway. Use a ladle to spread some batter up the sides of the pan, then lower the heat.
Watch the batter as small bubbles slowly appear around the edges. When only the center remains visibly wet, sprinkle with a little granulated sugar. Cover the pan and cook until done.
Remove the cooked martabak and place it on a cutting board. Spread a mixture of butter and margarine evenly over it, pressing gently so it soaks in. I use 2 heaping tablespoons of Royal Palmia butter.
Divide the martabak in half and add toppings of your choice, followed by sweetened condensed milk. Stack the halves, spread a little butter on top, and cut as desired.
Ready to serve 👍👍.
Delicious, soft, and full of honeycomb bubbles ❤❤.
strIngredient12: Blueband margarine and Anchor/Wijsman butter, mixed 1:1
strIngredient18: Kacang dan gula pasir digiling kasar

strInstructions:
Prepare the ingredients, mix well, and add the water.
Add the baking powder and baking soda solution to the batter. Stir until bubbles appear. Then heat a nonstick pan.
Pour the batter into the pan and cook over medium heat until holes appear across the surface. Sprinkle with granulated sugar as needed, cover the pan, and cook over very low heat until done.
Once cooked, transfer the terang bulan to a plate, spread with butter while hot, and add chocolate spread. The terang bulan is ready to enjoy while hot.
strIngredient9: Water for dissolving the baking powder and baking soda

strInstructions:
Combine the wheat flour, tapioca flour, granulated sugar, and milk, then mix well. Add the instant yeast and stir again. Cover and let rest for 25 minutes.
Add the egg and melted margarine. While heating the nonstick pan, add the baking soda and baking powder to the batter. Stir quickly. Pour the batter into the pan and swirl it slightly so it reaches the edges. Use very low heat.
Once holes or bubbles appear in the batter, sprinkle with a little granulated sugar and cover the pan. Cook until done. Remove the sweet martabak from the pan and repeat until all the batter is used.
Spread with margarine and add chocolate sprinkles, grated cheese, roasted peanuts, and white sweetened condensed milk. The mini sweet martabak (mini terang bulan) is ready to enjoy 💖💕🩷

Whisk the egg and granulated sugar until the sugar dissolves.
Alternately add the liquid milk and wheat flour, stirring until evenly combined.
Finally, add the baking powder and baking soda. Stir for 1–3 minutes until bubbles appear in the batter.
Heat a nonstick pan, pour in the batter, and spread it toward the edges. Wait until the honeycomb pattern forms, sprinkle with granulated sugar, and cover until cooked. Note: Do not grease the pan with butter or margarine while heating it, as my experience has been that the martabak burns quickly. You can test the pan's heat by sprinkling a little water on it. The pan used here is 18 cm in diameter.
Remove the martabak and spread butter or margarine evenly over it. Cut it in half, add toppings of your choice, stack the halves, and cut into pieces.
The economical sweet martabak is ready to enjoy.

strMeal: Kue Terang Bulan/Martabak Manis Tanpa Telur
strInstructions:
Prepare the ingredients. Mix the all-purpose flour, Cap Pak Tani Gunung tapioca flour, sugar, and salt. Add water and stir until evenly combined. Strain the batter.
Add pandan paste. Cover the batter with a cloth and let it rest for 1 hour. Lightly grease a small nonstick pan with oil and heat it. Pour in the batter, rotating the pan so the batter coats the sides. Reduce the heat and cook until holes begin to form. Once the holes appear, cover the pan. Wait until the top starts to dry slightly.
Sprinkle with sugar. Turn off the heat and remove the batter from the pan. Serve warm.
strIngredient2: Cap Pak Tani Gunung tapioca flour

strInstructions:
Mix the first group of ingredients with a mixer until combined and smooth, with no lumps, to achieve a chewy texture. Turn off the mixer.
Add the second group of ingredients to the first mixture in a bowl. Stir in a circular motion, gently, just until evenly combined.
Let the batter rest at room temperature for at least 1 hour.
When ready to cook, mix the third group of ingredients (water and baking soda) in a glass until dissolved. Add this mixture to the rested batter and stir gently until evenly combined.
The batter is ready for the pan. If the bubbles have not fully burst, as shown in the photo, it is not ready for the sugar yet, and you should not cover it.
Once all the bubbles have burst, sprinkle with granulated sugar, reduce the heat, and cover. Wait briefly until the crispy edges turn brown.
Remove from the pan, spread butter or margarine over the surface, and add your desired toppings.
For other flavors, simply add flavoring or food coloring.

Prepare a clean bowl. Add the all-purpose flour, cocoa powder, and baking powder. Mix well and sift if needed. Add the sugar and salt, then set aside.
Add the Black Forest paste to a glass of water and stir until evenly combined. Pour it into the flour mixture, add the egg, and briefly whisk or mix until combined. Cover with a clean cloth or plastic wrap and let rest for at least 1 hour.
Add the baking soda and baking powder just before pouring the batter, then mix well. Heat a nonstick pan until very hot. Pour in the batter and cook over low heat. Wait until bubbles or holes appear on the surface of the martabak, sprinkle with sugar, and cover until cooked.
Remove from the pan and quickly spread margarine or butter over the surface and outer crust to keep it flexible. Butter tastes better. Add fillings as desired; I used cheese and chocolate sprinkles.
Add cheese and sweetened condensed milk, cut the martabak in half, then fold one half over the other. Spread butter on top.
Cut into pieces and serve warm.
Note: Do not grease the nonstick pan with oil or margarine. This helps produce a smooth, attractive martabak crust without uneven bumps.
strIngredient13: Cheese / chocolate sprinkles / milk / roasted peanuts / sesame seeds / sweet corn, as desired
strIngredient14: White sweetened condensed milk, as desired

strInstructions:
1. Prepare the ingredients and make the martabak batter. Combine the all-purpose flour, Cap Pak Tani Gunung tapioca flour, granulated sugar, and water.
2. Mix with a mixer until all the ingredients are combined.
3. Add the egg and baking powder, then mix well. Let the batter rest for at least 1 hour, until small bubbles appear.
4. Divide the batter into two portions for vanilla and pandan flavors. Also divide the baking soda and water into two portions.
5. Heat a nonstick pan over medium heat. For the vanilla batter, mix the baking soda with water and vanilla flavoring. For the pandan batter, mix the baking soda with water and pandan flavoring. Pour the vanilla batter into the pan and spread it so it coats the sides. Wait for bubbles to appear, then slightly reduce the heat and sprinkle granulated sugar on top to help the bubbles burst. Once the holes have formed, cover and cook until done and the surface is no longer sticky.
6. I added red velvet paste to the remaining vanilla batter. Pour the red velvet batter into the pan and cook as before.
7. Cook the pandan batter in the same way as the first batch.
8. Once cooked, immediately spread margarine over the entire surface of each vanilla, red velvet, and pandan martabak.
9. Cut each martabak in half and sprinkle with grated cheese. Stack the halves together and cut into pieces as desired. Repeat for the vanilla and red velvet martabak.
10. Serve warm.
strIngredient2: Cap Pak Tani Gunung tapioca flour
strIngredient16: Wijen sangrai sesuai selera. mi: margarin dan keju

strInstructions:
Combine the all-purpose flour, cornstarch, granulated sugar, salt, and water. Mix well, then add the egg and baking powder. Let the batter rest for 60 minutes, covered with a clean cloth.
After that, mix the water, green food coloring, and baking soda. Add this solution to the batter and stir well.
Heat a nonstick pan over medium heat until hot but not smoking, so the martabak develops a good honeycomb texture. Pour the batter into the pan; do not grease it with margarine. Wait until bubbles or holes appear on the surface, sprinkle with sugar, cover, reduce the heat, and cook until done.
Once cooked, remove from the pan and spread with margarine. Cut in half.
Sprinkle with chocolate sprinkles, grated cheese, and sweetened condensed milk. Fold the martabak over, then cut into pieces as desired.
The pandan sweet martabak is ready to serve. Delicious!
strIngredient14: Margarine for spreading on the outer crust
strIngredient15: Margarine for spreading on the martabak surface

strInstructions:
Mix all the ingredients until smooth and free of lumps.
Heat a nonstick pan over medium heat. Sprinkle a little water onto the pan. If it makes a sizzling sound, the pan is hot enough.
Pour in the batter and spread some along the edges. Then increase the heat. Once holes form around the edges and the batter rises, reduce the heat. Cook until done.
Remove from the pan, spread with margarine, and add any toppings you like.

Combine all the ingredients except the bananas. Add water and stir until smooth, adjusting the consistency for banana fritter batter.
Cut the bananas as desired and mix them into the batter.
Fry in hot oil over medium heat until golden brown.
Remove, drain, and enjoy.

First, make the batter by mixing all the batter ingredients in a bowl.
Heat the cooking oil. Slice each banana lengthwise into four sections without cutting all the way through, then fan the sections out. Dip the banana into the batter and fry.
Turn it only once so it does not absorb too much oil. Remove, drain, and serve.

Combine the all-purpose flour, rice flour, tapioca flour, granulated sugar, salt, baking powder, and margarine in a bowl. Gradually add water, stirring until the batter is smooth.
Add the bananas to the batter and mix well.
Add honey and stir again.
Heat the oil and fry the bananas until golden brown. I use a 10 cm ring to make them round.
Remove and drain, then brush honey over the fried bananas while they are still warm.
Ready to serve.

strMeal: Pisang Goreng Madu Ala Bu Nanik
strInstructions:
Mix all the dry coating ingredients. Add water and stir well, then add honey and mix until combined.
Cut the bananas into small pieces and add them to the flour batter.
Fry the bananas until brown, then remove and drain. Enjoy while warm.

Combine all the ingredients in a bowl.
Add the melted butter.
Add the water and sesame seeds.
Add the bananas and mix well.
Fry the bananas in hot oil until both sides are cooked.
Remove and serve.

Peel the ripe bananas and cut each in half lengthwise.
Place the Kobe crispy banana-fritter flour in a bowl and gradually add water until the mixture thickens slightly.
Heat the cooking oil. Dip the bananas into the wet batter.
Coat the bananas with the dry flour mixture, then place them in the hot oil. Fry until golden brown.
Remove the bananas and drain. Top with grated cheese and chocolate sprinkles.
strIngredient1: One comb of raja bananas, halved
strIngredient2: Kobe crispy banana-fritter flour for wet batter
strIngredient3: Kobe crispy banana-fritter flour for dry coating

strInstructions:
Combine all the batter ingredients in a bowl and mix until smooth and free of lumps.
Slice the bananas diagonally as desired and add them to the flour batter.
Heat the oil and fry the bananas over medium heat.
When the underside is golden brown, turn them only once and continue frying until both sides are cooked.
Remove, drain, and serve warm.

Mix all the ingredients except the bananas until a thick batter forms.
Add the bananas to the batter and mix well.
Fry until cooked and browned.
Arrange the bananas in cups or on a plate.
Drizzle with sweetened condensed milk, then sprinkle with chocolate sprinkles and grated cheese.
They are so easy to snack on that you lose track of how many cups you've eaten!

Prepare all the ingredients. Place the all-purpose flour, granulated sugar, salt, and cornstarch in a bowl and mix well.
Gradually pour in the ice water until the desired thickness is reached. Mix well, then add Indomilk Creamy Matcha sweetened condensed milk and stir.
Add the bananas, which have been cut in half lengthwise, and coat them evenly in the batter. Heat the oil and fry until golden brown.
Remove and drain.
While the bananas are frying, make the matcha sauce. Place the liquid milk and grated cheese in a saucepan, then add Indomilk Creamy Matcha sweetened condensed milk.
Stir until combined, place the pan on the stove, and heat. Add the cornstarch while stirring.
Stir until evenly combined and thickened.
Arrange the fried bananas on a serving plate, pour over the matcha sauce, and drizzle with a little more Indomilk Creamy Matcha sweetened condensed milk. The extra creaminess makes them irresistibly delicious!
strIngredient5: Indomilk Creamy Matcha sweetened condensed milk
strIngredient12: Indomilk Creamy Matcha sweetened condensed milk

strInstructions:
1. Make the batter by combining the flour, margarine, salt, sugar, baking powder, and water. The batter should be neither too runny nor too thick.
2. Split the kepok bananas lengthwise, then gently flatten them so the banana seeds do not get fried along with them.
3. Dip the bananas into the batter and fry until cooked.
4. Once cooked, the bananas are ready to serve.

Peel the ripe bananas and cut them in half lengthwise.
Mix the flour, coconut milk, sugar, and salt until smooth. Dip the bananas into the batter.
Heat the oil and fry the bananas until golden brown. Remove and drain.
Serve warm.

Prepare the bananas. Peel and cut them as desired.
Make the wet batter by adding the all-purpose flour, salt, and margarine to a bowl. Gradually add water while stirring until the batter is thick but not too heavy.
Dip the bananas into the wet batter, then fry in hot oil until both sides are browned. Drain.
Serve.

Peel the bananas, slice them lengthwise into three pieces, and set aside.
Combine the flour, butter, salt, sugar, and vanilla. Gradually pour in the water while stirring until the batter reaches the right consistency.
Add the bananas to the batter and coat them evenly. Fry until cooked, then remove and drain.
Arrange the bananas on a plate, drizzle with sweetened condensed milk, and sprinkle with grated cheese or chocolate sprinkles before serving.

Prepare the ingredients. Cut and split the bananas to your preferred size.
Mix all the batter ingredients.
Add the water gradually.
Add the melted margarine and mix well.
Dip the bananas into the batter until evenly coated.
Heat the cooking oil. Fry the bananas until cooked and golden brown. Remove, drain, and serve.
strIngredient2: Heaping tablespoon of Rose Brand margarine, melted
strIngredient6: Heaping tablespoons of Rose Brand rice flour
strIngredient7: Heaping tablespoons of medium-protein all-purpose flour

strInstructions:
Prepare the ingredients.
Split each banana lengthwise into three sections, making sure not to cut all the way through.
Combine all the dry ingredients.
Gradually add cold water until the batter reaches a medium consistency.
Coat the bananas with the batter.
Fry the bananas in hot oil until golden brown.
Serve ❤️

strMeal: Anak Susah Ngunyah Auto Mangap! Rahasia Pisang Goreng Meises Krispi Anti Gtm Bb Booster
strInstructions:
Mix the wheat flour, rice flour, salt, and ice water until the batter is thick, not runny.
Add the chocolate sprinkles and gently stir until evenly combined.
Coat the bananas evenly with the batter.
Fry in hot oil over medium heat until crispy and golden brown. Remove and drain.

Prepare all the ingredients. Cut the bananas in half.
Melt the margarine and let it cool. Mix the flour, melted margarine, baking soda, salt, and water until evenly combined.
Dip the bananas into the flour batter, then fry in hot oil over medium heat. Fry until cooked and golden brown. Remove and drain.
Serve.

Prepare the ingredients. The initial photo shows only one banana, but there was a lot of leftover batter, so I added another banana.
To make the batter, combine the wheat flour and Rose Brand rice flour in a bowl.
Add Rose Brand granulated sugar, instant yeast, baking powder, and salt.
Pour in the water and melted margarine. Mix well, then add the bananas cut into small pieces. Stir and let rest for 20 minutes.
Heat the Rose Brand cooking oil. Fry the bananas until puffed and browned. Remove and drain.
Arrange the fried bananas on a serving plate.
Serve with your choice of toppings.
strIngredient10: Rose Brand cooking oil / as needed

strInstructions:
1. Peel and cut the bananas. I cut each into four sections. Prepare the wet-batter ingredients.
2. Mix all the wet-batter ingredients in a bowl. Gradually add ice water until the batter is thick enough, then add the sesame seeds and finally the margarine. Mix well. Heat the cooking oil and add 1 tbsp of margarine to the oil.
3. Dip the bananas into the batter, then fry in hot oil over medium heat. Fry until golden brown, then remove and drain.
4. Transfer to a serving plate. These are especially delicious while warm with coffee or hot tea. Enjoy, and happy cooking!

Sauté the shallots and garlic until fragrant. Add the cabbage and spring onion, then stir well. Add the noodles that have been boiled with their seasoning and mix well.
Mix the seasoned flour with water until smooth. Stuff the noodles into the tofu, then dip the stuffed tofu into the seasoned flour batter.
Fry in hot oil until golden brown. The stuffed tofu is ready to serve.

strMeal: Tahu Isi Ayam Pedas Mudah Sederhana
strInstructions:
Grind the garlic, shallots, chilies, and pepper. Cut the vegetables; I use carrots, cabbage, and spring onion. As usual, I roughly chop the carrots in a food processor. Heat some oil, then sauté the ground spices.
Chop the chicken fillet to your preferred texture.
Add the chicken to the sautéed spices. Cook while stirring until combined.
Add the chopped vegetables.
Stir-fry until everything is evenly mixed, the vegetables have wilted, and the liquid has reduced. Add salt and seasoning powder.
Make a hole in each pong tofu.
Fill the tofu with the prepared filling.
Gradually add water to the coating ingredients until the desired consistency is reached.
Dip the stuffed tofu into the flour batter. Heat oil in a pan, and once hot, add the coated tofu. Fry until browned.
This easy, simple spicy chicken-stuffed tofu is ready to serve! Enjoy!

strMeal: Tahu Isi Jeletot Mudah Simpel | Makanan Rumahan Sederhana
strInstructions:
Wash the vegetables thoroughly and cut them as desired. I only use cabbage, carrots, and spring onion. I roughly chop the carrots in a food processor.
Prepare the ground spices: chilies, garlic, and shallots. I also process these in a food processor.
Sauté the ground spices until fragrant, add the vegetables, and stir-fry until cooked. There is no need to add water. Once the vegetables have wilted, add salt, pepper, and seasoning powder.
When cooked, turn off the stove. While the filling cools, make holes in the tofu to hold the vegetable filling.
Stuff the prepared tofu with the sautéed vegetables.
Put half a packet of seasoned flour in a bowl. Gradually add water until the batter is not too thin.
Coat the prepared tofu with the flour batter.
Heat the oil. Once hot, add the coated tofu to the pan. Turn occasionally until golden. When cooked, remove and drain. Repeat until all the tofu is fried. If you have tofu left to fry later, store it in the refrigerator and coat it with batter when ready to fry.
The spicy Jeletot stuffed tofu is ready to serve! Enjoy!

First, prepare the filling. To save time, use a packaged soup vegetable mix. Take the cabbage, spring onion, and carrot. Wash and slice them so they fit in a food processor, then process to your preferred texture.
Grind the garlic, shallots, and pepper. Heat a pan and sauté the ground spices. Once softened, add the processed vegetables. Season with salt and seasoning powder to taste. When cooked, remove from the heat and let cool.
While the filling cools, prepare the all-purpose seasoned flour. Empty it into a bowl and add water gradually. The batter should be neither too thin nor too thick.
Heat oil in a pan. Once hot, dip the stuffed tofu into the seasoned flour batter and fry until browned. Remove and drain.
Stuff the cooled vegetable filling into the hollowed-out pong tofu, dip into the flour batter, and fry in hot oil.
Once cooked, remove and drain. The vegetable-stuffed tofu is ready to serve! Enjoy!

Prepare all the ingredients. Cut the tofu into 12 pieces as shown in the photo or as desired.
Make a hollow in the center of each piece of tofu and mix the removed tofu with the ground beef.
Add all the remaining ingredients and mix well. Check the seasoning by taking a little of the mixture and boiling it.
Fill each tofu piece with some of the ground beef mixture. Repeat until all the tofu is filled, then steam for 20 minutes.
When ready to serve, dip the tofu in beaten egg and fry in preheated oil until browned. Remove and drain.
The ground beef-stuffed tofu is ready to serve.
strIngredient12: Egg, beaten for coating the tofu

strInstructions:
Wash the tofu skins and gently press them to remove as much excess water as possible. Make a pocket for the vegetable filling by cutting into the middle without cutting all the way through. Drain.
While the tofu drains, prepare the vegetable filling. Cut the carrots and cabbage as desired. Wash them thoroughly with the bean sprouts, then drain.
Heat a pan with a little oil and add the prepared vegetables. Add Desaku garlic powder and white pepper powder, then stir until the vegetables have wilted.
Season with salt and seasoning powder to taste. Adjust the seasoning, then set aside.
Add 8 heaping tablespoons of wheat flour and 2 heaping tablespoons of rice flour to a large bowl. Add ground coriander, salt, and seasoning powder to taste. Gradually pour in water while stirring until the batter reaches the right thickness and has no lumps.
Put 2 tablespoons of vegetable filling into each cut tofu skin. Press gently to pack the filling. Repeat until all the tofu skins are filled.
Dip each stuffed tofu skin into the batter, making sure all sides are well coated, then place it in hot oil.
Fry until golden brown. Repeat until finished, then serve with green bird's eye chilies.

Prepare the ingredients. Fry the tofu until a skin forms, then make a slit in the middle.
Sauté the garlic until it changes color. Add the spring onion.
Add the chicken and stir until it changes color. Add the bean sprouts and carrot. Season with salt, pepper, and sugar. Mix well, then remove from the heat.
You can add chilies if desired. Stuff the tofu with the sautéed vegetables.
The stuffed tofu can be stored in the refrigerator and fried later.
Mix all the coating ingredients with water until smooth.
Dip the stuffed tofu into the batter.
Fry in hot oil until golden yellow.
Remove and drain. Serve with sweet soy chili sauce.

Prepare all the ingredients.
Heat a little oil in a pan. Add the garlic, followed by the shallots, and sauté until fragrant. Add the grated carrot, sliced cabbage, and bird's eye chilies. Season with salt, granulated sugar, pepper, and powdered stock. Mix well.
When the carrots and cabbage begin to soften, add the bean sprouts and sliced spring onion. Stir briefly to combine, then remove from the heat and set aside.
Cut open the tofu and fill it with the vegetables.
For the coating batter, combine all the ingredients and gradually add water until the desired consistency is reached.
Heat plenty of oil in a pan. Coat the tofu with the batter and fry in hot oil until the coating is cooked. Remove and drain.
Enjoy the spicy stuffed tofu with green bird's eye chilies or your favorite sauce or sambal 😍
strIngredient2: Cooking oil for frying the tofu
strIngredient3: Small carrot, grated or cut into matchsticks
strIngredient4: Cabbage leaves, thinly sliced, or as desired
strIngredient9: Bird's eye chilies, thinly sliced, or as desired

strInstructions:
Cut the tofu diagonally and fry until cooked. Remove and drain. Take one piece of fried tofu and cut a slit in the middle. Repeat with all the tofu pieces.
For the filling, prepare all the ingredients and seasonings. Set aside.
Sauté the garlic, then add the shallots and continue cooking until fragrant. Add the carrot and seasonings, stir briefly, then add the cabbage and bean sprouts. Stir until the seasonings are evenly distributed.
Taste and adjust the seasoning. Once it tastes right, turn off the heat. Let the filling cool slightly before using. Fill each piece of fried tofu with the vegetables and tidy the opening. Repeat for all the tofu, then set aside.
To make the coating, combine all the ingredients. Gradually add water while stirring until a thick, porridge-like batter forms. Heat cooking oil in a pan. Coat each stuffed tofu piece in the batter and fry until golden brown. Remove and drain.
Arrange the vegetable-stuffed tofu on a serving plate and serve with fresh chilies 🥰🥰

🔸Prepare the long beans and bean sprouts after washing them thoroughly. 🔸Grind all the seasonings.
🔸Combine the long beans, bean sprouts, egg, and ground seasonings. 🔸Mix until evenly combined.
🔸Stuff the mixture into the pong tofu. 🔸Repeat until finished.
🔸Dip the stuffed tofu into the flour batter. 🔸Fry until both sides are evenly cooked.

Finely chop the cabbage and grate the carrot. Set aside. Grind the garlic and pepper. Sauté until fragrant, then add a little water. Add the vegetables and mushrooms and cook until their liquid has reduced, then add the spring onion. (I make my vegetable filling spicy.) Stuff the cooked tofu with the vegetable filling.
Prepare the wheat flour and cornstarch. Add a little turmeric powder, salt, and ground coriander. Make a thick wet batter and prepare some dry flour mixture. Coat each tofu piece in the wet batter, then the dry mixture, until all the tofu is coated.
Serve warm with fresh chilies.

Cut the tofu in half and fry in hot oil.
Set the tofu aside and let it cool (I left mine in the chiller overnight). Then prepare the sambal by sautéing all the ingredients until softened.
Grind the sambal with a mortar and pestle while preparing the flour coating.
