Prepare the ingredients and scoop out the tofu filling to make room. Mix a small amount of wet batter.
Fill the tofu with the sambal, dip it into the wet batter, then roll it in the dry coating. Fry until browned.
The tofu stuffed with sambal gami is ready to enjoy while warm! 🙌🏼🔥

Prepare the tofu. Cut each piece diagonally into two and fry until partially cooked. Make a slit or hollow in the center of each piece for the filling.
Heat 3 tbsp of cooking oil. Sauté the garlic and shallots until fragrant, then add the carrot, cabbage, salt, oyster sauce, white pepper, and granulated sugar. Mix well. Add the spring onion and bean sprouts, then cook until done. Remove from the heat and taste. Once cool, put the filling into the hollowed tofu.
Mix all the coating ingredients until smooth and free of lumps. Dip the vegetable-stuffed tofu into the batter, then fry in hot oil until golden yellow.
Remove and drain. Mix ready-made pecel seasoning with warm water as needed and slice the bird's eye chilies. Serve the stuffed fried tofu with the pecel sauce for dipping and sliced chilies.
strIngredient1: Yellow tofu, cut diagonally in half

strInstructions:
Sauté the garlic, then add the shallots and cook until fragrant.
Add the carrot and stir. Pour in the water and cook until softened.
Add the bean sprouts, powdered chicken stock, and ground pepper. Cook until the bean sprouts have wilted. Adjust the seasoning, add the spring onion, stir, and turn off the heat.
Cut open the tofu skins and fill them with the sautéed vegetables.
Combine all the coating ingredients in a bowl, except for the spring onion. Mix well, then add the spring onion and stir again.
Dip the stuffed tofu into the coating batter.
Fry in hot oil over medium heat until crisp and crunchy on the outside.
Remove, drain, and serve.
strIngredient14: Medium-protein wheat flour (I used low-protein flour)

strMeal: Bola Mie Tahu Isi Bakso Kerikil
strInstructions:
Mash the tofu with a fork. Add all the ingredients, including the noodles, wheat flour, tapioca flour, egg, carrot, spring onion, and seasonings. Mix well.
Shape into balls weighing 20 g each, filling the center with a small meatball. Roll in breadcrumbs. Refrigerate for 30 minutes to help the coating stick, then fry until golden brown. Sorry, I forgot to take a photo of the frying process.
Ready to serve.

Prepare the vegetable stir-fry filling first.
Heat cooking oil and sauté the ground spices until fragrant.
Add the vegetables: cabbage, carrot, and spring onion. Mix well. Season with salt and granulated sugar. Mix well, adjust the taste, and cook until the vegetables wilt or are half-cooked. Remove from the heat and let cool.
While waiting for the filling to cool, prepare the tofu. Cut a slit in the tofu without cutting all the way through. Prepare the coating as well.
Fill the tofu with the vegetable stir-fry, repeating until all the tofu is filled.
Heat enough cooking oil. Coat the tofu with the coating mixture.
Fry the stuffed tofu until cooked and golden brown. Turn the tofu once one side is golden brown. Remove and drain.
Tahu Susur, or vegetable-stuffed tofu, is ready to serve. Serve with bird's eye chilies or chili sauce for dipping, as desired. Enjoy!
strIngredient1: Pong tofu, I use the triangular-shaped kind
strIngredient13: Ground spices for the vegetable stir-fry filling
strIngredient16: Cabe merah besar/ cabe teropong, atau sesuai selera bisa ganti cabe rawit / cabe keriting merah

strInstructions:
Prepare the tofu, cut it diagonally, and fry until hollow inside. When it becomes hollow, the tofu usually spins around by itself. Prepare the vegetable filling.
Sauté the garlic until fragrant, add the vegetables, and mix well. Add the seasoning powder and oyster sauce. Cook until done, let cool slightly, then stuff the tofu.
Combine all the dipping-batter ingredients in one bowl and add water until the batter reaches a medium consistency. Dip the tofu into the batter, then fry in hot oil, turning it once until golden yellow and cooked through. Drain. Serve hot with green bird's eye chilies.
strIngredient4: Here is the recipe for a simple fried vermicelli filling for fried snacks

strInstructions:
Prepare the ingredients.
Sauté the ground spices until fragrant. Add the carrot, shredded chicken, spring onion, salt, pepper, and mushroom stock. Cook until the seasonings are absorbed.
Then add a little of the chicken cooking broth and cook briefly until done. Set aside.
Mix the coating ingredients until evenly combined.
Cut open the tofu and fill it with the shredded chicken mixture. Then coat it in the flour mixture.
Heat the oil. Fry the stuffed tofu until cooked.
And here is the result after frying, along with the other dishes... 🙏🏻
strIngredient10: Salt + mushroom stock + ground pepper + garlic seasoning

strInstructions:
Heat the oil and fry the white tofu until golden brown. Remove and drain. Once cool, cut a slit in the middle of each tofu piece so you can add the filling.
In a bowl, prepare the vegetables: grated carrot, sliced pak choi, sliced spring onion and celery, and bean sprouts.
Heat the oil and sauté the ground spices until fragrant. Add the carrot, then the pak choi, bean sprouts, sliced spring onion, and celery. Mix well.
For the coating, combine wheat flour, rice flour, cornstarch, ground garlic, ground white pepper, salt, and mushroom stock. Add water and mix well until there are no lumps.
Stuff the tofu with the sautéed filling. Dip it in the coating mixture, then fry until golden brown. Remove and drain.
The stuffed tofu is ready to serve. Enjoy!

Sauté the ground spices until fragrant, then add salt, sugar, and carrot. Stir until the carrot softens.
Add the shrimp and stir for 2 minutes, then add the cabbage. Mix well, cook for 5 minutes, and set aside.
Cut a slit in the side of each tofu piece to make a pocket, then fill it with the vegetable and shrimp mixture.
Mix the wheat flour, rice flour, cornstarch, salt, and water. Stir until smooth with no lumps.
Dip the stuffed tofu into the batter, then fry until golden yellow. Remove and drain.

Soak the glass noodles in hot water until softened and expanded.
Soak the dried wood ear mushrooms in hot water until rehydrated, then slice thinly.
Chop the shallots and garlic using a chopper. Sauté until fragrant, then add the chilies. Sauté again, then add the Indonesian bay leaves and galangal.
Add the wood ear mushrooms and mix well. Add salt, granulated sugar, and sweet soy sauce.
Add the glass noodles, mix well, and adjust the seasoning.
Make a slit in the tofu with a knife and stuff it with the glass noodle filling. Repeat until all are filled, then set aside.
Put the Rose Brand rice flour, Rose Brand tapioca flour, wheat flour, pepper, salt, powdered stock, and baking powder in a bowl and mix well. Pour in the water while stirring until evenly combined.
Heat the Rose Brand cooking oil. Dip the tofu stuffed with glass noodles into the coating batter, then place it in the hot oil and fry until golden brown.
It tastes best served hot.

Cook the instant noodles according to the package instructions, then remove and drain. Prepare the hollow tofu as well. Cut a lengthwise slit on one side.
Wash the vegetables thoroughly, then slice them thinly. The carrot can be grated or cut into long strips. Add the instant noodles and their seasoning, but skip the oil seasoning packet. Mix well and adjust the taste.
Stuff the hollow tofu with the noodle mixture. Repeat until finished.
Make the coating batter by mixing the wheat flour, salt, and water. Stir until smooth and reach your desired consistency. Dip the noodle-stuffed tofu into the batter and coat evenly, then...
Fry in hot oil over medium heat, turning until cooked through. Remove and drain.
Serve warm.
strIngredient2: Packets of chicken curry-flavored instant noodles

strInstructions:
Prepare the ingredients and weigh them according to the specified amounts.
Blend the leftover white rice, garlic, salt, powdered stock, and tapioca flour until smooth. Add the water and blend using a blender or food processor.
Pour the blended mixture into a nonstick pan and cook over low heat, stirring continuously until it thickens.
Prepare ingredient group B: put the tapioca flour and finely sliced spring onion in a bowl. Add mixture A while it is still hot, then stir until evenly combined with the tapioca flour and firm enough to knead or shape.
Take a small portion of the dough and shape it into a flat piece as desired. Coat your hands with flour to prevent sticking. Repeat until all the dough is used.
Heat the oil and fry the rice cireng until golden yellow and cooked through. Remove and drain.
Serve the rice cireng with chili sauce or rujak dipping sauce, as desired.

Prepare the tapioca flour and seasonings.
Bring the water to a full boil. Then immediately pour it over the flour while stirring.
Once done, place some dry tapioca flour in a separate container and roll the wet dough into balls.
Fry the cireng until cooked and golden yellow over medium heat.

Prepare the ingredients. Grind the garlic and slice the spring onion.
Bring the water to a boil, then add 2–3 tbsp of Rose Brand tapioca flour. Stir well until translucent. This is the starter dough. In a separate bowl, add the remaining tapioca flour, garlic, spring onion, salt, chicken seasoning, and ground pepper. Mix well.
Add the starter dough to the bowl containing the tapioca mixture. Mix until the dough is smooth and easy to shape. Take a portion of the dough and flatten it.
Heat the oil and fry the cireng over medium heat until cooked. Remove and serve warm.

Boil the chicken breast until cooked, then shred it. Reserve the cooking broth.
Sauté the shallots, garlic, chilies, kaffir lime leaves, Indonesian bay leaves, and lemongrass until fragrant.
Add the shredded chicken and season with sugar, salt, flavor enhancer, and a little chicken broth. Cook until the seasonings are absorbed.
Mix the sago flour and wheat flour in a bowl.
Bring the salted water to a boil.
Pour the boiling salted water into the flour mixture and stir quickly with a spatula. Knead briefly, just until the dough can be shaped.
Take some dough, flatten it, and add the spicy shredded chicken filling.
Brush the edges with egg white and seal by pinching them together. This should keep the filling from spilling out, God willing :)
Fry the cireng in hot oil until cooked and crispy.
strIngredient4: Slightly heaping tablespoons of wheat flour

strInstructions:
Mix the wheat flour and tapioca flour with the water until smooth and free of lumps, then add the seasonings. I use a chopper so I don't need to strain the mixture.
Pour the mixture into a plastic bag and tie it tightly, then place it in the pot while the heat is still off. Use medium-high heat and cook covered for approximately 15–20 minutes. Turn off the heat and let it sit for approximately 30 minutes without opening the lid.
The color is slightly green because of the coriander. Fry in hot oil.
After frying, serve with flavored powder, chili oil, or sauce. Sauce is the best option, though.

Mix the tapioca flour, water, and seasonings until smooth and lump-free. Cook until the mixture thickens and becomes somewhat translucent. Prepare the crumble and cheese.
Take some dough, press into the center, add cheese, cover with dough, and shape into a ball.
Roll it in the crumble until completely coated. You can also freeze them for later.
Heat the oil until hot, add the cireng, and fry briefly—just until the crumble coating dries. Ready to serve.

✅ Making the filling: Blend the garlic and bird's eye chilies. Sauté until fragrant, then add the intestines. Add the other seasonings and a little water. Cook until the seasonings are absorbed. Taste and adjust the seasoning. Turn off the heat and let cool.
✅ Making the dough: Combine all the flours, salt, and stock powder. Gradually add the hot water while stirring until the mixture forms clumps.
Weigh the dough into portions as desired; I weigh mine at 25 g each. Roll each portion thinly and cut into circles (I use a glass lid). Add 1 tbsp of filling, then fold and shape like a pastel pastry.
Heat enough cooking oil. Fry the cireng until golden brown and cooked. Remove and drain.
Alhamdulillah, ready to serve.
strIngredient8: Intestines, boiled and cut into small pieces
strIngredient11: A handful of bird's eye chilies

strInstructions:
Mix the tofu, Rose Brand tapioca flour, wheat flour, and all the seasonings except the spring onion and chilies. Mix well. Add the sliced spring onion and chilies, then mix again. If the mixture still feels dry, gradually add hot water until the dough holds together.
Shape portions of the dough as desired, then roll them in Rose Brand tapioca flour. Repeat until finished.
Heat enough Rose Brand cooking oil. Fry the cireng until crispy, turning only once so they do not absorb too much oil.
Place them in a container, separating layers with plastic so they do not stick together. Store in the freezer for later.
Enjoy.
strIngredient6: Ground pepper; I use black pepper
strIngredient8: Granulated sugar, ground together with the garlic
strIngredient10: Green bird's eye chilies, or to taste, sliced
strIngredient11: Rose Brand cooking oil for frying
strIngredient12: Rose Brand tapioca flour for coating

strInstructions:
Bring the water to a boil, then add the garlic, salt, coriander, and stock. Add 50 g of tapioca flour. Stir quickly until thickened, then turn off the heat.
While the mixture is still hot, add the remaining tapioca flour and sliced spring onion. Stir with a ladle until combined, but do not knead until smooth; avoid kneading so the cireng does not become hard.
Pinch off a small amount with your fingers, according to your preferred size. Flatten it and fry. Do not fry until too dark, or it will become hard. Use medium heat. Serve with rujak dipping sauce.
For the rujak sauce: grind the bird's eye chilies with salt. Gradually add palm sugar and tamarind water while grinding. Add the peanuts and grind, but do not make the mixture too smooth.
Serve the hot cireng with the dipping sauce.
strIngredient15: Tamarind pulp, diluted with drinking water

strInstructions:
Cireng filling: Clean the chicken, then boil it for about 15 minutes. Shred the chicken. Sauté the ground shallots, garlic, and chilies until fragrant. Add the chicken, salt, palm sugar, and soy sauce, then cook until done.
Cireng dough: Put the wheat flour, tapioca flour, and a little salt in a bowl. Gradually pour in the hot water while stirring, then knead until smooth.
Making the cireng: Take a small portion of dough and flatten it. Add the chicken filling and seal it again, like making a pastel pastry, or use a mold. Repeat until all the dough is used. Fry over low heat until cooked, then serve.

Combine all the cireng ingredients and pour in the hot water. Do not make the mixture too soft; it should remain slightly crumbly.
Shape into flat rounds as shown in the picture.
Fry in hot oil over medium heat until golden brown and slightly crispy.
To make the broth:
Sauté the shallots, garlic, and aromatic ginger.
Add the ground chilies and chopped tomato.
Cook until the mixture is fully cooked, then pour in 250 ml of water.
Add the egg while stirring the broth so the egg mixes in.
Add the fried cireng.
Add vinegar, flavor enhancer, and spring onion, then adjust the seasoning.
Feel free to try this recipe, and happy cooking. It is guaranteed to be delicious!

Take 1 tbsp of tapioca flour and mix it with the sliced spring onion, salt, powdered stock, garlic, and water until combined. Once mixed, cook it until the texture changes to a glue-like consistency.
Combine this mixture with the remaining tapioca flour. There is no need to knead it until smooth.
Once combined, shape it into flattened pieces. The shape is up to you; they do not need to look perfectly neat.
Fry over medium heat. They will not splatter. Fry until dry and crispy.

Mix the tapioca flour, wheat flour, salt, chicken stock powder, and garlic powder until evenly combined.
Pour the boiling water over the flour mixture. Stir well with a wooden spoon, then briefly knead by hand until evenly combined.
Take a handful of dough and flatten it. Place it in a pastel mold, add grated cheese filling, and close the mold. Repeat until all the dough is used.
Heat the oil over high heat, then lower the heat once the oil is hot. Fry the cireng over low heat until both sides are cooked. Turn only once.
Serve warm. You can also serve it with chili oil for dipping.
strIngredient1: Tapioca flour, Pak Tani Gunung brand

strInstructions:
In a bowl, combine the white tofu, grated garlic, salt, pepper, mushroom stock, and spring onion. Mix well.
Add the wheat flour and tapioca flour, then mix until combined.
Take some of the mixture and shape it into small, flat pieces. Coat each piece evenly with tapioca flour. Heat the cooking oil, then fry the cireng until dry and crispy. Remove and drain.
The tofu cireng is ready to serve with sweet soy sauce chili dip ❤️❤️.
strIngredient1: White tofu, mashed with a fork

strInstructions:
Prepare all the ingredients.
Grind the shallots, garlic, and pepper until smooth.
Place the tofu in a bowl and mash it. Add the minced chicken, salt, and stock powder, then mix well.
Add the spring onion and mix again.
Add the chili powder and mix again.
Heat the cooking oil. Take a spoonful of the mixture and fry until golden brown. Remove and drain.
Serve while warm with your favorite dipping sauce or sweet soy sauce chili dip.

Bring the water to a boil. Boil the chicken until tender, then shred it using a fork.
Prepare the ground spice ingredients and grind until smooth.
Heat the cooking oil and sauté the ground spices until fragrant and fully cooked. Add the water, kaffir lime leaves, stock powder, granulated sugar, and salt. Mix well, then add the shredded chicken and stir. Cook until the liquid has reduced. Set aside.
Prepare the cireng wrappers. Combine the wheat flour and tapioca flour. Add garlic powder, ground pepper, salt, and stock powder. Mix well, then gradually add boiling water while stirring with a spatula. Once the dough has cooled enough to handle, knead by hand until smooth.
Cover the dough with plastic wrap and let it rest for about 15 minutes. Sprinkle tapioca flour on the work surface. Take a portion of the dough and roll it out thinly.
Place the rolled dough in a cireng mold and add the spicy chicken filling. Close the mold and trim the edges. Repeat until all the dough is used.
Fry the cireng in warm oil that is not too hot, over low heat, turning occasionally until cooked and golden brown. Remove and drain.
Serve while warm.

Place the tapioca flour in a bowl. Add the stock powder and salt, then mix well.
Bring the water to a boil, then gradually add just a little of the boiling water to the tapioca flour. Stir until dry clumps form. Do not let the mixture become too soft.
Fry the cireng in hot oil, using approximately 1 tsp of mixture per piece. Fry until puffed, crispy, and cooked through. Remove and drain.
Serve the cireng with your favorite dipping sauce! Delicious, savory, crispy, and chewy, with a stretchy texture. It does not absorb much oil. Simple!

Gently press the tofu without crushing it. I use a spatula for this.
Mix all the seasoned flour ingredients, then coat the tofu evenly with the mixture.
Heat the cooking oil and fry the coated tofu until dry and crispy. Remove and set aside.
Heat a little cooking oil and sauté the garlic until softened. Add the chilies and mix well. Add the sliced kaffir lime leaves and spring onion. Season with mushroom stock, salt, granulated sugar, and ground pepper.
Add the tofu cireng and mix well. Remove from the heat and serve.
strIngredient10: Small spring onions, cut into short pieces
strIngredient11: Red bird's eye chilies, originally curly red chilies, sliced into rounds
strIngredient12: Kaffir lime leaves, remove the central veins and thinly slice

strInstructions:
Prepare the required ingredients.
Use a food chopper to finely process the tofu, chicken, the white part of the spring onion, shallots, and garlic.
Add the salt and oyster sauce, then chop again. Add the thinly sliced green part of the spring onion and mix well.
Add the tapioca flour and mix again.
Prepare the wonton wrappers and cut each into four pieces. Spread a little of the mixture on each piece. Garnish with celery leaves and slices of red chili.
Heat the oil and fry the cireng with the filling side facing down first. Once cooked, turn them over and fry until done. Use medium heat.
Enjoy immediately, with your favorite dipping sauce if desired.
ADDITIONAL NOTE: I did not fry all the mixture. I used the remaining mixture to make dumpling-style snacks and steamed them. They can be stored frozen.

Prepare the tofu and mash it. Add the garlic, spring onion, ground pepper, salt, and stock powder. Mix thoroughly.
Add the tapioca flour and mix again until evenly combined.
Heat the oil, add the cireng mixture, and shape as desired. Fry the tofu cireng until golden yellow, then drain.
Serve the tofu cireng with sweet soy sauce and sliced chilies.

Combine the tapioca flour, garlic powder, stock powder, salt, ground pepper, and sliced spring onion. Mix well.
Pour in the boiling water and stir briefly with a ladle until combined.
Once the mixture has cooled enough to handle, take a portion, shape it into a ball, and flatten it slightly. If it is sticky, dip your fingers in tapioca flour first.
Heat the oil over medium-low heat and fry until puffed and dry.
Drain and serve.

Blend the rice, salt, stock powder, pepper, garlic, and water, then transfer the mixture to a pan. Cook until thickened. Add the spring onion, tapioca flour, and wheat flour.
Knead until smooth. If the dough does not feel firm enough, gradually add more tapioca flour. Take a small portion of the dough.
Fry until golden and serve with cuko sauce.
strIngredient1: Leftover rice, about one full rice scoop

strInstructions:
Combine the tapioca flour, garlic powder, stock powder, salt, and spring onion. Mix well, then gradually pour in a little hot water, stirring only until roughly combined.
Take a small portion of the mixture, shape it into cireng, and fry until cooked. Set aside.
To make the seblak broth, grind the chilies, garlic, and aromatic ginger. Sauté the ground spices until cooked.
Pour in the water and bring to a boil. Add or crack in the eggs. Cook until the eggs are done, stirring them gently.
Add the enoki mushrooms and spring onion. Season with salt, stock powder, granulated sugar, and ground pepper. Taste and adjust the seasoning.
To serve, place the cireng in a bowl, cutting it into pieces first if desired, then pour the seblak broth over it.

strMeal: 836. Rujak Cireng Berkuah Khas Jawa Barat
strInstructions:
Grind the garlic and place it in a saucepan with the water. Add the spring onion and some of the tapioca flour, along with the salt, stock powder, and ground pepper. Mix well.
Cook over low heat until the mixture resembles glue. While it is still hot, immediately add it to the remaining tapioca flour, stirring with a spatula or ladle just until combined. Do not knead until smooth.
Pinch off portions of the dough, flatten them, and place them on a tray. Repeat until all the dough is used.
Heat the cooking oil over medium heat. Add the cireng and let them cook until they naturally rise to the surface, then turn them over and fry until done.
For the rujak dipping sauce, grind all the sauce ingredients and add water. Cook until bubbling, making sure it does not become too thick if you want a pourable sauce. Taste and adjust the seasoning, then turn off the heat. Alternatively, combine and grind everything without cooking, then add drinking water and tamarind water or vinegar. Adjust the seasoning and serve.

Sauté the spring onion until fragrant and wilted.
Prepare the flour, then pour it into the pan.
Add the water and mix well. Cook over low heat, then turn off the heat.
Add the wheat flour and tapioca flour, then mix again.
Prepare the wonton wrappers and separate the individual sheets.
Place 1 tbsp of the mixture on one wrapper, then shape it with your fingers as shown in the photo.
Repeat until finished.
Fry until yellowish in color.
Remove and drain, then arrange on a plate.
Pour the peanut sauce over the cireng. So delicious!

Peanut sauce: Use a food chopper to blend the steamed sweet potato and fried peanuts with the cooking oil. Set aside.
Chop the red chilies, shallots, and garlic. Combine them with the ground peanut mixture, then add the kaffir lime leaves and water.
Add Asatu Rose Brand flavor enhancer, Rose Brand granulated sugar, and the other ingredients.
Cook until thickened. Taste and adjust the seasoning, then turn off the heat.
Chili sauce: Blend the red bird's eye chilies and garlic.
Add the cooking vinegar and the other ingredients. Cook over low heat until the liquid reduces and the sauce thickens. Remove from the heat and set aside.
Batagor: Sauté the ground shallots and garlic until fragrant. Remove and set aside.
Combine the seasonings with the ground fish and Rose Brand granulated sugar.
Add the fish sauce and ice water, then mix well. Add the beaten egg and mix again. Add the sautéed shallots and garlic, along with the sliced spring onion, and mix well.
Gradually add Pak Tani Gunung tapioca flour and wheat flour, mixing until evenly combined.
Prepare the wonton wrappers. Spread 1/2 tsp of the mixture over each wrapper, then fold it.
Fry in moderately hot oil until cooked. Remove and drain.
Serve with the peanut sauce and accompaniments.
strIngredient26: Tepung tapioka cap pak tani gunung

strInstructions:
Grind the aromatic ginger, garlic, and chilies.
Sauté the mixture in cooking oil until fragrant and cooked through.
Add the water, batagor lidah, egg, tofu, egg, sugar, salt, and stock powder. Mix well and adjust the seasoning.
Add the water spinach and cook briefly. Turn off the heat.
The seblak is ready to serve. Enjoy!
strIngredient11: Water spinach, trimmed and washed thoroughly

strInstructions:
Prepare the ingredients and mash the tofu.
Slice the spring onion and grind the garlic. Add both to the tofu. Add the salt, stock powder, and egg, then mix until combined.
Add the tapioca flour, wheat flour, and water. Mix evenly.
Heat the oil. Scoop half a tablespoon of the tofu mixture into the hot oil and fry until golden brown. Repeat until all the mixture is used.
For the peanut sauce, mix the prepared peanut sauce seasoning with enough water. Cut the cucumber into pieces.
Arrange the batagor on a plate, add the cucumber slices and peanut sauce, then serve.
strIngredient12: Packs of ready-made peanut sauce seasoning

strInstructions:
Thinly slice and chop the garlic and spring onion, then mix them together with the tofu, egg, and all-purpose seasoned flour. Do not add water unless the mixture is too thick; if needed, add just a little so it does not spill out when placed on the wonton wrappers.
Heat the oil, then reduce the heat. Place 1 tbsp of the mixture on a wonton wrapper and flatten it evenly. Put it into the hot oil. Fry for about 1 minute per side until crispy.
Serve with peanut sauce, pecel seasoning, or sweet soy sauce chili dip. This is a great quick snack or side dish. Give it a try!

Grind the seasoning ingredients.
Combine the starter dough ingredients in a pan and cook over low heat, stirring continuously. Cook until the liquid reduces and the mixture can be kneaded.
Once the starter dough is cooked, let it cool. Add the egg and mix.
Add the tapioca flour and knead until smooth.
Shape the mixture inside the wonton wrappers.
Prepare a steamer and steam the siomay for approximately 30 minutes.

First, prepare all the required ingredients.
Mash the white tofu with a fork, then add the salt, sugar, mushroom stock, garlic powder, soy sauce, sesame oil, chopped garlic and shallots, and spring onion. Add the egg and mix well.
Once everything is evenly combined, add the tapioca flour and mix well.
The mixture is ready for frying, but at this stage I also add corned beef. Take the wonton wrappers and divide each into four triangular pieces. Place 1 tsp of the mixture on each piece, then fold the wrapper.
Heat the cooking oil and fry the tofu batagor until golden brown. Drain.
While waiting for the tofu to cool slightly, prepare the peanut sauce by mixing approximately 2 tbsp of ready-made peanut sauce seasoning with 4 tbsp of boiled water. Pour the sauce over the batagor.
Serve the batagor with boiled eggs, calamansi lime, and sweet soy sauce.

Place the chicken fillet, garlic, fried shallots, and ice water in a food chopper. Blend until smooth.
Add the fish sauce, oil, pepper, salt, stock powder, and granulated sugar. Chop again until evenly combined.
Transfer the mixture to a bowl. Add the tapioca flour, wheat flour, and baking powder, then mix well.
Fry the white tofu, cut each piece diagonally, and scoop out a little of the center. If desired, mix the scooped-out tofu into the meatball mixture.
Fill the tofu and wonton wrappers with the mixture, folding them as desired.
Heat the oil and fry the batagor and wontons over medium-low heat until cooked. Drain.
For the broth, boil the beef bones in enough water until boiling. Let simmer for about 5 minutes, turn off the heat, and discard the water.
Boil the bones again in 3 liters of fresh water. Skim off the foam, then add the whole celery stalks, ground fried garlic and shallots, and pepper.
Cook over medium heat until the broth develops flavor. Add sugar, salt, chicken stock, and mushroom stock. Taste and adjust the seasoning.
Serve the batagor and wontons in bowls, pour the broth over them, and sprinkle with celery and fried shallots. Add sweet soy sauce, sauce, chili sauce, and calamansi lime as desired.
strIngredient30: Seledri dan daun bawang iris halus

strInstructions:
Begin by saying Bismillah. Prepare the tools and ingredients.
Combine all the ingredients and seasonings, then mix well. Gradually add the hot water and knead until smooth.
Take a piece of tofu and place some of the mixture in the center. Repeat until all the tofu is filled.
Heat the oil. Fry the tofu batagor over medium heat until cooked and golden brown. Remove and drain.
Cut the batagor into pieces and serve warm with peanut sauce or chili sauce. Enjoy trying this recipe! 😊♥️
strIngredient6: Spring onion can also be used

strInstructions:
Mix all the filling ingredients together. Pour in hot water while stirring until evenly combined.
Cut open the tofu and add the filling. Repeat until all the mixture is used.
Heat cooking oil and fry the tofu until crispy, turning it over as needed. Serve with peanut sauce.

Prepare all the ingredients. Combine the tofu, garlic, scallions, pepper, salt, and Asatu Rose Brand seasoning.
Mix well, then add Pak TANI Gunung tapioca flour and stir. Add the egg.
Mix until evenly combined, then let the mixture rest for 30 minutes. Fry in Rose Brand cooking oil.
Once the oil is hot, scoop up 1 tsp of the mixture and fry until cooked. Repeat until all the mixture is used.
Remove from the oil and serve.
strIngredient7: A pinch of Asatu Rose Brand seasoning

strInstructions:
Slice the shallots and sauté until golden brown. Set aside.
Add the chicken, garlic, salt, sugar, pepper, and mushroom stock powder to a food processor and blend until smooth. Add the fried shallots along with their oil, ice water, fish sauce, egg, and scallions, then blend again.
Add the sago flour and wheat flour. Mix well and refrigerate the mixture for 20 minutes.
Prepare spring roll wrappers or wonton wrappers, and cut the tofu as desired. I cut each wonton wrapper into 4 pieces and the tofu into small pieces because these are for my child's school lunch. Place the mixture on the wrapper and fold the corners to form a flower shape. I freeze some for my child's lunch supplies. For the tofu, place the chicken mixture on top. Steam.
To make the peanut sauce, chop the red curly chilies, shallots, and garlic, then crush the candlenuts. Fry them and set aside.
Blend the peanuts with 100 ml of water, then add the fried chilies, shallots, garlic, and candlenuts. Blend until smooth.
Transfer the mixture back to the pan, then add water, palm sugar, tamarind water, salt, and rice flour. Cook until done. If the sauce is not thick enough, add a mixture of rice flour and water.
Boil the potatoes and eggs together. Once cooled, peel them and arrange them in the steamer.
Boil the cabbage until tender but not too soft, then fold each leaf like an envelope and place it in the steamer.
Fry the spring roll mixture in hot oil until golden brown. Drain. The chicken siomay and batagor are ready to enjoy with iced tea. Yum!
strIngredient7: A small amount of pepper (at the tip of a tablespoon)

strMeal: Batagor Ikan Kembung Dengan Bumbu Kacang
strInstructions:
Remove the skin from the mackerel, then finely mince the fish. Combine the fish, tapioca flour, wheat flour, chives, garlic, salt, pepper, and water.
Shape the mixture into oblong pieces as desired. Fry the batagor in hot oil until golden.
Mix the peanut sauce with boiled water and stir well. Serve the batagor with the peanut sauce.

strMeal: Kuah / Saus Kacang Batagor / Siomay / Cilok
strInstructions:
Process the steamed sweet potato and fried peanuts with the cooking oil in a food processor. Set aside.
Process the red chilies, shallots, and garlic.
Combine this with the ground peanut mixture, kaffir lime leaves, and water. Add Asatu Rose Brand seasoning, Rose Brand granulated sugar, and the remaining ingredients. Cook until thickened, taste, then turn off the heat.
The peanut sauce is ready to serve with batagor, siomay, or cilok.

Prepare the starter dough ingredients. Cook the water, rice flour, and medium-protein wheat flour, stirring continuously until a thick dough forms. Let it cool.
Pour hot oil over the scallions, add the garlic, and mix well. Add fish sauce, oyster sauce, salt, sugar, pepper, and stock powder or seasoning, then stir well.
Add Asatu Rose Brand seasoning. Gradually add the egg white and Pak Tani Gunung tapioca flour. The mixture will feel firm but soft.
Combine this with the cooled starter dough and mix evenly. Once cooled, the flour mixture should look firm but soft.
Cut the tofu in half, or into quarters if the pieces are large. Score the center of each piece with a fork so the batagor filling sticks. Some of the mixture can also be wrapped in wonton wrappers. Continue until all the mixture is used.
Heat the oil and fry the batagor over medium-low heat until golden.
To make the chili sauce, blend the garlic, red curly chilies, bird's eye chilies, and 50 ml of water until smooth. Cook the blended chilies, add the remaining water, and bring to a boil. Add the salt, sugar, and stock powder, then bring to a boil again. Add vinegar and cook until the water reduces and the sauce thickens and is cooked through. Adjust the seasoning.
Arrange the tofu batagor on a plate, pour over the sauce, squeeze in some kaffir lime juice, and add sweet soy sauce to taste. The fish-free tofu batagor is ready to serve with peanut sauce and a little chili sauce.

Prepare the ingredients. Cook the water, rice flour, and medium-protein wheat flour, stirring continuously until a dough forms. Let it cool.
Pour hot oil over the scallions, add the garlic, and mix well. Add fish sauce, oyster sauce, salt, sugar, pepper, and stock powder or seasoning, then stir well. Add Asatu Rose Brand seasoning.
Add the egg white and Pak Tani Gunung tapioca flour. Combine with the mixture until evenly mixed. Let the flour mixture cool.
Cut the tofu in half, or into quarters if the pieces are large. Score the center with a fork so the batagor mixture sticks to the tofu. Heat the oil and fry the batagor over medium-low heat until golden.
strIngredient17: Kuah / saus kacang kuah /saus kacang batagor /siomay /cilok

strInstructions:
Prepare the ingredients. Cook the water, rice flour, and medium-protein wheat flour, stirring continuously until a dough forms. Let it cool.
Pour hot oil over the scallions, add the garlic, and mix well.
Add fish sauce, oyster sauce, salt, sugar, pepper, and stock powder or seasoning, then stir well.
Add Asatu Rose Brand seasoning. Add the egg white and Pak Tani Gunung tapioca flour. Combine with the mixture until evenly mixed. Let the flour mixture cool.
Cut the tofu in half, or into quarters if the pieces are large. Score the center with a fork so the batagor mixture sticks to the tofu. Fill the tofu with the mixture and make a pattern with a fork. Repeat until finished.
Heat the oil and fry the batagor over medium-low heat until golden.
Serve with peanut sauce. The peanut sauce recipe is attached as Batagor Peanut Sauce.

Fry the peanuts and let them cool.
Steam the sweet potato and cut it into pieces. Process the steamed sweet potato and fried peanuts with the cooking oil in a food processor. Set aside.
Process the red chilies, shallots, and garlic. Combine with the ground peanut mixture and add the kaffir lime leaves and water.
Add palm sugar, Rose Brand granulated sugar, and salt. Add Asatu Rose Brand MSG.
Cook until thickened, taste, and turn off the heat.
strIngredient10: A pinch of Asatu Rose Brand MSG

strInstructions:
Prepare the ingredients. Cook the water, rice flour, and medium-protein wheat flour, stirring continuously until a dough forms. Let it cool.
Pour hot oil over the scallions, add the garlic, and mix well. Add fish sauce, oyster sauce, salt, sugar, pepper, and stock powder or seasoning, then stir until combined.
Add Asatu Rose Brand seasoning. Add the egg white and Pak Tani Gunung tapioca flour.
Combine with the mixture until evenly mixed. Let the flour mixture cool.
Cut the tofu in half, or into quarters if the pieces are large. Score the center with a fork so the batagor mixture sticks to the tofu. Some of the mixture can also be wrapped in wonton wrappers. Continue until all the mixture is used.
Heat the oil and fry the batagor over medium-low heat until golden.
To make the chili sauce, blend the garlic, bird's eye chilies, and water until smooth. Cook until boiling, then add the seasonings and bring to a boil again. Add vinegar and cook until the water reduces and the sauce thickens and is cooked through. Adjust the seasoning.
The fish-free tofu batagor is ready to serve with chili sauce.

Grind the chicken, shrimp, and garlic.
Grate the carrot and slice the scallions.
Combine all the ingredients until evenly mixed.
Fill the wonton wrappers with the mixture.
Steam for about 30 minutes. Serve with peanut sauce.

Make a hole in each tofu puff. Process the chicken, egg, garlic, and shallots in a food processor.
Add sliced scallions, sliced kaffir lime leaves, salt, sugar, pepper, stock powder, and a little sesame oil. Mix well. Add Pak Tani flour and mix again.
Fill the tofu puffs with the chicken mixture, then steam for about 25–30 minutes.
Remove and serve. You can fry them, or eat them straight after steaming, like I do while dieting. 😁😌

Mix all the ingredients until evenly combined.
Take a little of the mixture and fry or steam it to test the seasoning.
Once the flavor is right, place the mixture on siomay or gyoza wrappers, shape into siomay, and add a little grated carrot on top. Steam for about 25 minutes, depending on the size of the siomay.
For meal-prep stock for your child, let the siomay cool, then portion it into plastic bags and freeze. When ready to eat, remove the siomay from the freezer and steam until tender.

Prepare the ingredients: grated chayote and pindang skipjack tuna.
Blend the pindang skipjack tuna with the garlic and shallots until smooth.
Combine the fish mixture, wheat flour, salt, pepper, mushroom stock powder, and water. Stir well, then cook until thickened and cooked through. Turn off the heat and let it cool until warm.
Add the squeezed grated chayote and tapioca flour. Stir gently until evenly combined.
Cut open the tofu and fill it with the mixture.
Steam for 20 minutes until cooked. Remove and serve with peanut sauce.

Prepare the ingredients. Wash the chicken fillets and drain.
Place the chicken thigh fillets, salt, sugar, ice water, stock powder, and pepper in a food processor. Process until sticky.
Transfer the mixture to a bowl. Add the chayote, egg white, fish sauce, oyster sauce, minced garlic, and cooking oil. Mix well.
Add the wheat flour and tapioca flour. Mix well, then add the sliced scallions and mix again until evenly combined.
Divide the mixture into 3/4 and 1/4 portions. Shape the larger portion into round balls using a spoon and fork. Place them in boiling water and briefly boil for about 1–2 minutes. Remove and drain.
For the tofu: cut each piece in half, score the center, and remove some of the filling. Mix the removed tofu with the remaining 1/4 portion of the mixture. Fill the tofu with this mixture. Score the edges of the tofu first so the filling does not come loose easily.
For the cabbage: separate the leaves and briefly steam until slightly wilted. Remove and roll them up.
Fry the peanuts, red curly chilies, shallots, garlic, and candlenuts until cooked.
Blend the fried peanuts and boiled potato with the fried seasonings until smooth.
Transfer the blended mixture to a pan. Add water, kaffir lime leaves, palm sugar, granulated sugar, sweet soy sauce, mushroom stock powder, salt, and tamarind paste. Cook until the sauce thickens. Remember to taste it.
Steam the siomay, stuffed tofu, potatoes, cabbage, and eggs. Steam the cabbage and eggs for about 7–8 minutes, and the other items for about 20 minutes.
To serve, arrange the siomay, stuffed tofu, cabbage, potatoes, and eggs on a plate. Pour peanut sauce over them and add a little chili sauce on top. Yummy!

Finely chop the scallions and grate the carrot.
Combine the fish meat and flour, then add the seasonings, scallions, carrot, and egg. Mix all the ingredients until evenly combined. Shape the siomay as desired; you can also use dim sum wrappers.
Bring water to a boil to firm up the round siomay mixture. If using dim sum wrappers, you can steam them directly.
Finally, steam the siomay for about 15–20 minutes until fully cooked.

Combine the chicken, egg whites, garlic, shallots, scallions, and seasonings. Mix well.
Add the tofu and mix again.
Gradually add Rose Brand tapioca flour until the mixture reaches almost the desired thickness. If it feels too firm, add ice water a little at a time, such as 1 tbsp or about 15 ml each time. Mix and check again.
Shape the mixture into balls. Use some of the mixture to fill the bitter melon, tofu, and cabbage, then steam for 25–30 minutes until cooked.
To make the peanut sauce: blend the peanuts with the fried garlic and chilies until smooth. Transfer to a saucepan and gradually add water while stirring to prevent lumps. Add palm sugar, granulated sugar, salt, kaffir lime leaves, and stock powder. Cook over low heat, stirring continuously for 10–15 minutes until cooked and thickened. Finally, add tamarind water and sweet soy sauce. Adjust the seasoning.
Bandung-style siomay is ready to serve with the accompaniments, peanut sauce, and a squeeze of calamansi juice.
strIngredient2: White tofu; mash and squeeze out the water

strInstructions:
Marinate the chicken and shrimp for 15 minutes.
Rinse and drain.
Process half of the chicken and shrimp together with the other dough ingredients until the mixture becomes sticky.
Cut the remaining half of the meat into small pieces and process briefly so the filling retains some chunky texture.
Once all the dough ingredients have been processed, mix in the grated carrot.
Grease the steamer with oil.
Wrap the mixture in dim sum wrappers and top with finely grated carrot.
Steam for 3 minutes, brush with sesame oil, then steam for another 7 minutes. Voila! ☺️

Process the steamed sweet potato and fried peanuts with the cooking oil in a food processor. Set aside.
Process the red chilies, shallots, and garlic.
Combine this with the ground peanut mixture, kaffir lime leaves, and water. Add palm sugar, Rose Brand granulated sugar, salt, and Asatu Rose Brand MSG. Cook until thickened, taste, and turn off the heat. The peanut sauce is ready to serve with batagor, siomay, or cilok. Enjoy!
strIngredient10: A pinch of Asatu Rose Brand MSG

strInstructions:
Prepare the ingredients. Fry the peanuts in Rose Brand cooking oil over medium-low heat.
Process the steamed sweet potato and fried peanuts with the cooking oil in a food processor. Set aside.
Process the red chilies, shallots, and garlic. Combine with the ground peanut mixture, then add the kaffir lime leaves and water.
Add palm sugar, Rose Brand granulated sugar, salt, and seasoning or stock powder. Stir well.
Cook until thickened, taste, and turn off the heat.
The fragrant and savory peanut sauce is ready to enjoy with batagor, siomay, cilok, otak-otak, and more.
Fish-free batagor dos recipe: Batagor Dos | Fish-Free Batagor
Spanish mackerel batagor recipe: Spanish Mackerel Batagor 🐟

Prepare the ingredients. Briefly sauté the spring onions in a little oil, then let them cool. Mix the ground chicken with the seasonings until evenly combined.
Add the cooking oil, sautéed spring onions, and chayote, then mix again. Add Pak Tani Gunung tapioca flour and stir gently until combined.
Add water little by little until the mixture becomes smooth and cohesive. Heat the steamer until plenty of steam rises, then shape the siomay mixture into balls using a spoon. Steam for 30 minutes until cooked.
While steaming, I also added tofu and cabbage as optional accompaniments.
To make the peanut sauce: Wash and drain the peanuts, then fry until about three-quarters cooked. They will continue cooking after being removed from the pan. Drain them. Blend the peanuts, garlic, shallots, red chilies, bird's eye chilies, and candlenuts.
Sauté the chili mixture until cooked, then blend it with half of the fried peanuts until smooth. Once smooth, add the remaining peanuts and blend again, but do not make it too smooth.
Cook the peanut mixture again with all the sauce ingredients. Add tamarind water and stir until bubbling. Adjust the seasoning to taste. Dissolve the rice flour in 1 tbsp water, add it to the peanut sauce, stir well, and cook until thickened.
Serve the chicken siomay with peanut sauce poured over the top. So delicious! 🤤

Blend the chicken, egg, and seasonings without the tapioca flour.
Once smooth, add Pak Tani Gunung tapioca flour and blend again. You can use a blender or mix it manually in a bowl.
Once the mixture is thoroughly combined, shape it with a spoon. Arrange the pieces in a rice-cooker steamer that has been preheated, then steam for 20–25 minutes.
Once cooked, remove and serve with chili sauce or peanut sauce, according to your preference.

Prepare the ingredients.
Using a food chopper, process the fish, ice cubes, and garlic. Once smooth, add the egg, water, flour, and seasonings. Process again. Transfer to a bowl, add the chopped spring onions, and stir.
Make a small hole in the center of the tofu pieces cut into triangles. Fill the tofu and dumpling wrappers with the mixture.
Fry until half-cooked if you want to store them for later, or fry until fully cooked if serving immediately. Use medium heat, then reduce the heat once they turn golden brown and continue cooking until they become brown.
You can also steam them to make siomay.
Serve with lime and ready-made ABC peanut sauce mixed with bird's eye chilies and a little warm water so it is not too thick.

Prepare the chicken, remove the bones, and put it into a food chopper.
Add the carrots, broccoli, and chayote.
Add low-fat milk, garlic powder, and pepper.
Add salt and mix again.
Add Pak Tani Gunung tapioca flour, then process until smooth again.
Grease a baking pan with oil, then pour in the mixture.
Steam for 30 minutes.
Remove and serve.

Cut the tofu into triangles, then soak it in salted water. Cut the bitter melon into pieces as shown in the photo and remove the center. Sprinkle salt over the bitter melon and set aside.
Peel and grate the chayote, then squeeze out the liquid. Fry the shallots and garlic, then grind them into a paste.
Process the Spanish mackerel in a food chopper and slice the spring onions.
In a bowl, combine the Spanish mackerel, egg, spring onions, sautéed shallots and garlic, grated chayote, Pak Tani Gunung tapioca flour, Rose Brand granulated sugar, salt, and powdered stock. (The photo shows the Rose Brand sugar packaging in a different place because this was the second time making it; I forgot to take a photo the first time.)
Rinse the bitter melon thoroughly and make a slit in the tofu. Fill them with the siomay mixture. Bring water to a boil, shape the remaining mixture into small balls, and boil until cooked and floating.
Boil the cabbage, then boil the eggs. Roll up the cabbage leaves and peel the eggs. Peel and cut the potatoes as desired. Steam the potatoes, tofu, and bitter melon until the siomay filling inside is cooked.
Grind the shallots, garlic, candlenuts, and chilies. Shave the palm sugar into thin pieces. Sauté the ground spices with the kaffir lime leaves, add the ground peanuts and enough water. Add the palm sugar, tamarind water, sweet soy sauce, salt, and powdered stock. Cook until done. Taste and adjust the seasoning, and adjust the thickness as desired.
To serve, arrange portions of siomay and the accompaniments on a plate, then pour peanut sauce over them. Add calamansi lime and fried shallots if desired. This is great for a packed meal or to send to relatives.

Put the wheat flour, Pak Tani Gunung tapioca flour, and salt in a bowl and mix well. Pour in the water and knead just until evenly combined.
Cover the dough with a clean cloth and let it rest for 1 hour.
After an hour, roll the dough through a pasta machine, gradually setting it to the thinnest setting. Sprinkle Rose Brand cornstarch over the surface of the dough. Cut it to the desired size. Sprinkle Rose Brand cornstarch between each sheet to prevent them from sticking together.
Store the dough in a plastic bag or an airtight container.

Mix the chicken, shrimp, seasonings, chayote, and oil.
Stir until combined, then add the Pak Tani Gunung tapioca flour last.
Take one dumpling wrapper, fill it with the mixture, and arrange it neatly in the steamer. Steam for 20 minutes. Once cooked, brush each piece with oil, remove, and serve.
For crispy balls, cut the dumpling wrappers into small pieces and place some mixture in the center. Roll the mixture over the wrapper pieces. Chill for 15–30 minutes, remove and let stand briefly, then fry until cooked. Enjoy trying the recipe!
strIngredient5: Grated and squeezed chayote, yielding 100 grams after squeezing

strInstructions:
Wash the tuna thoroughly, then finely chop it (you can also use a food chopper). Mix it with Pak Tani Gunung tapioca flour.
Add granulated sugar, salt, powdered stock, ground pepper, egg white, and ice water. Stir until evenly combined and cohesive.
Shape into balls as desired, or fill tofu or dumpling wrappers with the mixture. Steam for 15 minutes or until cooked, then remove.
Tuna siomay is ready to serve with boiled eggs and peanut sauce.
strIngredient11: Accompaniments: boiled eggs and peanut sauce

strInstructions:
Cut the tofu into two triangular pieces. Wash and soak in salted water. Set aside.
Wash the fish thoroughly and blend it with the garlic. Put it in a bowl, add the egg, tapioca flour, sugar, seasoning, and spring onions. Mix well.
Drain the tofu and fill it with the siomay mixture. Continue until all the tofu is used. Boil the remaining siomay mixture in boiling water, dropping spoonfuls into the water; they do not need to be shaped neatly.
Soak the cabbage leaves in hot water, then roll them up as shown in picture 2.
Once everything is ready, arrange the eggs, potatoes, cabbage rolls, tofu siomay, and other siomay in the steamer. Steam for a few minutes.
Serve with peanut sauce, sweet soy sauce, and chili sauce.
strIngredient13: Sweet soy sauce and chili sauce

strInstructions:
Peel and grate the chayote, then squeeze it to remove excess water. Discard the liquid or use it as vegetable stock.
Cut the chicken thigh fillet into small pieces. Put half into a food chopper with the garlic. Add the remaining half along with the ice water, egg white, salt, sugar, fish sauce, and ground pepper. Process until smooth and evenly combined.
Transfer the chicken mixture to a bowl. Mix in the chayote, cilantro (or finely chopped spring onions), Pak Tani Gunung tapioca flour, and wheat flour. Stir well.
Use two spoons to shape the mixture into balls. For the tofu, scoop out a little of the center and fill it with the mixture. Heat the steamer and grease the steaming tray with oil. Arrange the balls on the tray and steam for about 20 minutes or until cooked (cut one open and taste to check).
Place in a container if you want to store them. Otherwise, serve with peanut sauce or your favorite dipping sauce.

Blend the shallots, garlic, and water. Then add the fish and egg, and process again until smooth.
Add all the seasonings, then transfer the mixture to a bowl. Add the spring onions and tapioca flour, and mix well.
Steam until cooked (35 minutes). Cut the siomay and serve with peanut sauce. Grease the pan or thin-wall container with cooking oil first so the mixture does not stick.
Serve with sweet soy sauce and sliced cucumber.

Wrappers: Combine the all-purpose wheat flour and Pak Tani Gunung tapioca flour, then sift. Add salt and mix. Add cooking oil, then gradually pour in boiling water while stirring until all the flour is mixed and no dry flour remains.
Shape the wrapper dough into a ball, cover with a clean cloth, and let it rest for 15 minutes. Divide the dough into 15-gram portions. Let them rest briefly, then roll each portion thinly.
Cut to the desired size (I used 8 cm). Continue until all the wrapper dough is used. Set aside.
Siomay filling: Clean the chicken and pat it dry with kitchen paper. Place it in the freezer until partially frozen. Remove and process in a food chopper, but do not make it too smooth. Set aside. Clean the shrimp and remove the dark intestinal tract. Add baking soda, mix well, and let sit for 10 minutes. Rinse, place in a container, and freeze until partially frozen. Then chop coarsely and set aside.
Siomay filling: Coarsely grate the chayote and set aside. In a clean bowl, combine the ground chicken, ground shrimp, and grated chayote. Mix well. Add fish sauce, sesame oil, salt, pepper, granulated sugar, and chicken stock powder. Mix until evenly combined.
Siomay filling: Crush the garlic and sauté it in a little oil until fragrant and cooked. Add it to the mixture and stir well. Add the egg and Pak Tani Gunung tapioca flour, then mix until all ingredients are evenly combined. Take a small amount and steam it until cooked to test the seasoning.
Place 15 grams of filling on one wrapper and shape it like a typical siomay. Repeat until all the filling is used. Steam in a hot steamer for 20 minutes or until cooked.
Chili sauce: Boil the garlic, bird's eye chilies, and large red chilies until softened. Remove from the pot and blend or grind until smooth. Return to the pot, add water and sugar, and bring to a boil. Add the cornstarch slurry and stir until it boils again.
After 20 minutes, remove the siomay from the steamer and place on a serving plate. Lightly brush the surface with sesame oil. Serve with chili sauce.
strIngredient7: Pak Tani tapioca flour — for dusting to prevent sticking

strInstructions:
Prepare the ingredients.
Thinly slice all the spices, then sauté until fragrant and softened. Remove and drain. Grind the sautéed spices into a paste.
Add the ground spices to the chicken. Add ground coriander, ground pepper, salt, sugar, powdered stock, thick coconut milk, and grated coconut. Mix until evenly combined. Taste-test by frying or boiling a small amount of the mixture.
Cover your hands with plastic gloves or a plastic sheet. Take 1.5 tbsp of the mixture and wrap or press it around a satay skewer or lemongrass stalk. Press firmly as you shape it. Grill in a pan over low heat so the mixture cooks through.
Serve with warm rice. Hmm... yummy! 😋🤩
strIngredient10: A thumb-sized piece of aromatic ginger

strInstructions:
Prepare the bhase gede spice paste ingredients: red chilies, shallots, garlic, ginger, turmeric, galangal, and aromatic ginger. Cut them into pieces. Heat a frying pan and fry the sliced spices, shrimp paste, and kaffir lime leaves until fragrant and softened.
Once softened, remove them from the pan. Remove and set aside the kaffir lime leaves. Grind the remaining spices into a paste. I use a blender.
Finely chop the chicken in a food chopper. Add palm sugar, coconut, instant coconut milk, coriander, pepper, salt, powdered stock, granulated sugar, and the bhase gede spice paste that was blended earlier. Mix well. Test the seasoning by grilling a little of the mixture in a nonstick pan. Once the taste is right, take a lilit satay skewer. Lightly oil your hands, take 1 tablespoon of the mixture, and press it around the skewer. Continue until all the mixture is used.
Grill over relatively low heat, turning occasionally until cooked. Remove and serve with sambal matah.
strIngredient4: Pack of instant thick coconut milk, 65 ml each
strIngredient23: Gula merah sisir (saya pake palm sugar )

strInstructions:
1. Separate the meat from the bones and skin, then process it in a food chopper. I also added carrots to make more, hehe.
2. Set the chicken mixture aside. You can toast 2 tbsp of grated coconut until it becomes slightly brown.
3. Prepare the spices. I roughly chopped each ingredient separately in a food chopper rather than processing everything together. These include shallots, garlic mixed with turmeric powder and other spices, and red spice paste mixed with kaffir lime leaves. You can process everything together if you prefer; it's up to you.
4. Sauté all the spices together in a pan.
5. Mix them into the chicken mixture along with the toasted coconut, coconut milk, tapioca flour, and other seasonings. By the way, I didn't use all the spice mixture because it turned out to be too much, so you can increase the amount of chicken.
6. Mix everything evenly. Prepare 4 lemongrass stalks and cut each into two pieces. If possible, prepare 8 stalks instead, because it is a little difficult to attach the mixture to thin stalks.
7. Press the mixture onto the lemongrass stalks as needed. Then grill in a nonstick pan. It takes a while to grill, so make sure the mixture is fully cooked.
8. That's all! It turns out delicious. Don't forget to try making it yourselves! 😙

strMeal: Sa Te Lit : Sate Lele Lilit
strInstructions:
Finely chop the catfish fillet (to remove the skin, pour hot water over it).
Mix the prepared spice paste with the grated coconut until evenly combined.
Divide the catfish mixture mixed with the spices into portions, then wrap each portion around a lemongrass stalk.
Steam for about 20 minutes, then grill until browned.
Serve.

Prepare the ingredients and grind the spices.
Mix all the ingredients and ground spices until evenly combined.
Lightly crush the white end of each lemongrass stalk, then press the mixture around the end of the stalk. Repeat until all the mixture is used.
Heat a nonstick pan or grill pan and brush with butter. Grill the satay, turning it occasionally, until cooked.
Make sweet soy dipping sauce with sliced shallots and chilies to enjoy with the lilit satay. 🤗

Prepare the ingredients.
Clean and boil the skipjack tuna. This step is important to remove the fishy smell and firm up the meat. Bring water to a boil with 1 kaffir lime leaf and 1/2 tsp salt. Add the skipjack fillet and boil for only 2–3 minutes. Remove, drain, and let cool. Shred it, then roughly chop with a knife. Do not blend it until smooth, or it will become like meatballs. Brief boiling is essential to remove the fishy smell and help the meat bind.
Grind all the spice paste ingredients with the coriander, pepper, and toasted shrimp paste. Mix the spice paste with the toasted coconut, salt, sugar, and calamansi juice. Stir well.
Add the chopped skipjack tuna, thick coconut milk, and sliced kaffir lime leaves. Knead by hand for 7 minutes until the mixture is very sticky. To test it, take a pinch and press it onto your palm. If it stays in place, the mixture is ready. If it still crumbles, add 1 tbsp toasted coconut. The mixture should be sticky; if it is too soft, add more toasted coconut.
Wrapping around lemongrass: Take 2 tbsp of the mixture and wrap it around a crushed lemongrass stalk. Press firmly until compact and even. If it is loose, it will fall off when grilled.
Charcoal option: Grill over low heat for 3–4 minutes per side. Brush lightly with coconut oil when turning.
Nonstick pan option: Heat a nonstick pan over low heat and brush with coconut oil if available. Grill for 3–4 minutes per side, then cover for 1 minute so the inside cooks. Total grilling time is 12–15 minutes. Do not grill for more than 15 minutes. Avoid high heat because skipjack tuna and coconut burn easily.
Enjoy making this at home! I hope this skipjack tuna lilit satay brings a little taste of Bali to your table. Enjoy! 🌴
strIngredient1: Skipjack tuna / fresh tuna fillet, skin and bones removed
strIngredient6: Bird's eye chilies, adjust to taste
strIngredient21: -17 batang serai , geprek 3-4 cm dari ujung bagian bawah

strInstructions:
Steam the Spanish mackerel for about 5 minutes, then remove the bones and grind the fish.
Briefly toast the grated coconut.
Sauté the ground spice paste with the sliced kaffir lime leaves until cooked and fragrant and the moisture has reduced, so the satay mixture will not be too watery. Remove and let cool.
To make the satay mixture, combine the ground fish, toasted grated coconut, thick coconut milk, tamarind water, palm sugar, salt, and powdered stock in a bowl. Add the cooled spice paste, mix well, and knead until smooth, cohesive, and well combined.
To wrap around lemongrass or bamboo skewers, take a small handful of the mixture (about 1–2 tablespoons). Press it onto the white end of the stalk, then squeeze and rotate downward until the mixture wraps neatly and sticks firmly. Repeat until all the mixture is used.
To grill, heat a grill pan or nonstick pan and brush with a little butter. Grill the lilit satay over low to medium-low heat, turning regularly so all sides cook evenly. Once golden brown and deeply fragrant, remove from the pan.
The lilit satay is ready to serve. It tastes best while warm with white rice, sambal matah, and water spinach plecing.
strIngredient8: Kaffir lime leaves, ribs removed and thinly sliced

strInstructions:
Cut the tempeh into pieces, then steam it with the coconut for about 10–15 minutes.
Blend the spices until smooth, then sauté them in cooking oil until fragrant and the oil separates.
Once the tempeh has been steamed, mash it until completely smooth (I used a fork).
Mix the tempeh, coconut, and spices together until evenly combined.
Wash the lemongrass stalks and cut them to the desired length. Crush the white ends, then press the tempeh mixture around them until it sticks, like making sempol.
Heat a nonstick pan and grill the tempeh over medium-low heat until the surface is smoky with a few charred spots. Serve with sambal.

Rinse the chicken fillet thoroughly, then cut it into pieces. Blend with all the ingredients except the scallions.
Add the scallions and mix. Im
Prepare the lemongrass stalks and shape them like clubs, then boil for 10 minutes. After draining, grill until browned. Serve.

Cut the beef, then clean it.
Finely blend the beef with the fried shallots, fried garlic, egg, cornstarch, and fine salt using a chopper.
Take some of the meat mixture, squeeze it into a ball, and wrap it around a lemongrass stalk.
Steam the meat for about 25 minutes. Once cooked, prepare sesame oil and sweet soy sauce, then brush them onto the meat.
Grill on a nonstick pan until cooked and browned.
The beef wrapped satay is ready to eat.

strMeal: Sate Lilit Daging Sapi Cocok Untuk Anak2
strInstructions:
Cut the beef into small pieces, rinse thoroughly, then chop until smooth.
Sauté the ground spices until fragrant.
Once fragrant, turn off the stove and mix the spices evenly with the chopped beef.
Add salt, ground pepper, ground coriander, and seasoning if they were not already sautéed with the ground spices. If they were, do not add them again.
Once everything is evenly mixed, take a popsicle stick or satay skewer and wrap an appropriate amount of mixture around it. Keep it from getting too thick so it cooks faster and evenly.
Repeat until all the meat mixture is used.
Bring water to a boil for steaming. Once the steamer is ready, add the wrapped satay.
Steam for only 5–10 minutes.
When it seems cooked, remove it and set aside for now.
Melt the margarine, then mix it with sweet soy sauce.
Heat a nonstick pan, brush it with some of the margarine and soy sauce mixture, and briefly grill the satay. Turn it over so it cooks evenly.
Once cooked, remove and serve the wrapped satay ☺️. Serve with tomato sauce if desired, or according to your taste 😊

Finely grind 250 g of boneless chicken thigh and 100 g of tilapia fillet.
In a bowl, combine the ground chicken and tilapia with all the ingredients and ground spices. Mix until evenly combined.
Take a little of the mixture and wrap it around a lemongrass stalk.
Brush a nonstick pan with a little oil. Grill until cooked.
Once cooked, serve with sambal matah.
The tilapia wrapped satay is ready to enjoy.

strMeal: Sate Lilit Manis (High Protein, Kids Friendly)
strInstructions:
Sauté the ground spices until cooked and fragrant.
Mix the ground spices with the chicken. Stir well.
Add the other seasonings. Mix well, then refrigerate the mixture for about 30 minutes to make it easier to wrap around the skewers.
Wrap the mixture around the satay skewers.
Grill the satay in a nonstick pan over low heat until thoroughly cooked on all sides.
The wrapped satay is ready to serve. Enjoy!

Grind all the ground-spice ingredients using a mortar and pestle or a blender until smooth.
Heat a little cooking oil, then sauté the ground spices with the finely sliced kaffir lime leaves until fragrant and thoroughly cooked.
In a bowl, mix the sautéed spices into the ground chicken. Add thick coconut milk, toasted grated coconut, and sugar and salt to taste, then mix until evenly combined.
Take some of the chicken mixture and press it around a lemongrass stalk. Make sure it sticks firmly, and do not make it too thick so the chicken cooks through when grilled.
Prepare a grill pan or nonstick pan, brush with a little oil, and heat it. Grill the wrapped satay, turning it until browned and cooked.
Remove the cooked satay and serve warm. It goes very well with sambal matah.

Pound all the spices, then mix them with the ground chicken.
Bring water to a boil in a pot for cooking the satay mixture.
Once the water boils, wrap the chicken mixture around the satay skewers. This is a little difficult because of its texture, so do your best. Once the mixture sticks somewhat, immediately place it in the hot water in the pot so it sets.
When it seems half-cooked, remove it, as it will be grilled later with soy sauce and sauce.

Chop the spices, then sauté them in a little oil until fragrant and cooked.
Chop the chicken. Put it in a bowl and mix with the sautéed spices. Add coconut milk, ground nutmeg, sugar, salt, and powdered stock. Add the sliced kaffir lime leaves. Mix well.
Take some of the mixture and press it around a lemongrass stalk to form a satay shape. Then grill in a pan until cooked.

Grind the satay spices and mix them with the chicken, coconut, and other seasonings.
Shape the mixture around satay skewers and grill until cooked.
Slice the cucumber and serve it with the satay and sambal.
Fry the bananas and sprinkle grated cheese on top.
Cut the potato and fry until crispy.

Clean the chicken and cut it as desired. Marinate it with lime juice, salt, and black pepper.
Prepare and grind the spice paste. Shave the palm sugar and grill the shrimp paste.
Heat the oil and sauté the spice paste. Add the palm sugar, shrimp paste, and whole spices. Sauté until cooked and fragrant, then add the marinated chicken.
Add the coconut milk and simmer the chicken until cooked. Add the seasoning and adjust the taste.
Once cooked and the liquid has reduced, grill the chicken in a nonstick pan or in the oven. Taliwang grilled chicken is ready to serve. Enjoy cooking!

Marinate the chicken for at least about 1 hour. Prepare the spice paste and other ingredients.
Sauté the spice paste until fragrant, then mix in the other seasonings. Stir well and adjust the taste.
Pour in the coconut milk and stir again.
Add the whole chicken or pieces, as preferred. Cook until done and the oil separates. Continue until the liquid has reduced, then set aside.
Prepare a nonstick pan and grill the chicken, turning it and brushing it with the remaining seasoning. Serve with plecing kangkung.
Serve with plecing kangkung (for plecing kangkung: put sambal over boiled water spinach, then sprinkle with fried peanuts).
Hope this is helpful. Enjoy trying it 👌

strInstructions:
Prepare the ground spices, blend them all, and put them into a pan. Add the whole spices and cooking oil (I use coconut oil).
Sauté over low heat until the oil separates and the mixture is fragrant. Then add the chicken that has been rinsed clean.
Add thin coconut milk and cook until thickened, then turn off the stove.
You can grill it in a nonstick pan if you like, but I prefer the oven. Bake the chicken at 150–200°C for 20–25 minutes.
If making it for meal prep, let it cool first, then store it in an airtight container in the refrigerator.

You can use any chicken, whole or cut into pieces. I used pieces. Rinse the chicken well and drizzle with lime juice.
Grind all the spices, then sauté them with the aromatic leaves.
Sauté until fully cooked, add the coconut milk and a little water, then add the chicken. Season and stir until evenly coated.
Cook until the liquid has reduced and the spices have fully absorbed. Remove and set aside to grill.
Grill the chicken, occasionally brushing it with the remaining chicken seasoning. Turn it until evenly cooked.
Once cooked, remove and serve with sambal matah and fresh vegetables. Sambal Matah

strMeal: Ayam Taliwang Kuning & Kecap (Pan Seared Tanpa Cabe Untuk Anak)
strInstructions:
Grind all the spice-paste ingredients, then sauté them in cooking oil.
Sauté until fragrant, add the kaffir lime leaves, chicken wings, salt, and water. Cook until the water boils and the chicken is cooked.
Once cooked, you can add soy sauce before searing in the pan. Enjoy trying it!

Coat the chicken with ground turmeric and salt to taste, massaging/squeezing until evenly covered, then set aside. While the chicken marinates, prepare all the ingredients.
Heat a pan or nonstick pan and grill the chicken until lightly browned. Remove and set aside.
Sauté the ground spices until fragrant and fully cooked. Add the coconut milk, water, and kaffir lime leaf, then stir well.
Season with salt, sugar, powdered stock, and shrimp paste. Stir well and cook until the coconut milk boils. Adjust the taste. Set aside about 2 ladlefuls for brushing onto the chicken while grilling.
Add the chicken. Stir well and cook until thoroughly cooked, the seasoning has absorbed, and the liquid has reduced. Note: if desired, add a little sweet soy sauce around the edge of the pan for extra aroma and color.
Next, grill the chicken, occasionally brushing it with the seasoning.
Arrange on a plate and serve with plecing kangkung and fresh vegetables. Alhamdulillah 🙏🏼😊
strIngredient11: A little sweet soy sauce ~ optional

strInstructions:
First marinate the chicken with the marinade ingredients. Leave for at least 1 hour. If marinating all day, put it in the refrigerator.
Sauté the ground spices until cooked and dry, then add the supplementary ingredients and sauté briefly. The seasoning will be somewhat liquid.
Take some of the seasoning for the Taliwang sambal and set aside.
Once the chicken reaches room temperature, grill it in a pan without oil until both sides are half-cooked. Remember to press the chicken a little and cover the frying pan to get a smoky aroma.
Then add the chicken to the seasoning or coat it with the seasoning. Grill it in the pan with the lid on so it cooks thoroughly. Continue until all the seasoning is used.
The chicken is ready to serve.

Clean the chicken and drizzle it with lime juice. Coat evenly and leave for 10–15 minutes. Prepare the spices and dry-roast the candlenuts.
Blend the ground-spice ingredients. Cook until fragrant and the liquid has evaporated or the oil separates.
Add the coconut milk, water, and the other dry seasonings. Cook until boiling.
Add the chicken. Cook, turning occasionally so both sides cook. Once cooked and the seasoning has reduced, remove the chicken and separate it from the seasoning.
Grill both sides until browned. I use a nonstick pan. Serve with plecing kangkung.
