strInstructions:
Prepare the ingredients. Rinse the chicken and cut open the lower breast area so it can be spread flat. Marinate with salt, pepper, and lime juice. Finally, brush the entire surface of the chicken with ROSE BRAND coconut milk until fully covered. Grill the chicken to bring out its aroma.
Grill both sides. Grind the ground-spice ingredients.
Heat ROSE BRAND cooking oil and sauté the ground spices until fragrant.
Add water and the chicken, then season with salt, powdered stock, and ROSE BRAND granulated sugar.
Cover and cook, turning occasionally.
Cook until the seasoning has absorbed and the chicken is tender. Turn off the heat.
Heat a grilling pan. Add a little ROSE BRAND margarine and grill the chicken, brushing it with the Taliwang seasoning. Cook until somewhat dry with a few charred spots 😆. Turn it over (I cover it because I use a Happy Call pan) so it becomes more tender.
Once cooked, remove it from the Happy Call pan and serve with fresh vegetables. The remaining Taliwang seasoning can be made into sambal. So delicious 😍🤤 Tender all the way through. Hehe.
Sorry, some of the chicken had already been eaten in the product photo 🤣🙏. So delicious 😍🤤
strIngredient1: Javanese free-range chicken without head and feet
strIngredient21: Secukupnya minyak goreng rose brand untuk menulis bumbu

strInstructions:
Prepare the main ingredient and rinse it thoroughly. Marinate with calamansi juice and salt, then leave for about 5 minutes.
Grind all the spices, then use them to marinate the chicken after removing it from the first marinade.
Grill in a nonstick pan until fragrant.
Sauté the remaining marinade until fragrant, then add the instant coconut milk.
Add water and the chicken. Cook until the liquid has reduced and make sure the chicken is cooked through.
Grill the chicken on a grill pan.
Serve. It is usually served with plecing kangkung, but I skipped it because I didn't have the ingredients at home.

Clean and rinse the chicken, then make shallow cuts so the seasoning can penetrate. Prepare the spice paste and blend it in a blender or grind it manually with a mortar and pestle.
Heat ROSE BRAND cooking oil, then sauté the spice paste until fragrant. Add the kaffir lime leaves and lemongrass and sauté until the spices are cooked. Season with palm sugar and salt. Pour in the coconut milk, stir well, and adjust the taste.
Add the chicken and simmer until cooked and the sauce has reduced and thickened.
Remove the chicken and transfer the remaining sauce to a bowl to use as a glaze while grilling. If desired, add sweet soy sauce to the glazing sauce. Heat a nonstick pan and grill the chicken over medium-low heat.
Brush the chicken with the remaining simmering sauce, turning it so it cooks evenly. Remove and serve. Since this is for children, I don't use bird's eye chilies. For a spicier version, the large red chilies can be replaced with curly red chilies and bird's eye chilies. Enjoyy..😘😘
strIngredient2: ROSE BRAND instant coconut milk + 150 ml water, mix
strIngredient5: Shaved palm sugar, or to taste

strInstructions:
Prepare the ingredients. Wash the chicken thoroughly. Grind or blend the spice ingredients into a paste. Bruise the lemongrass.
Heat the cooking oil, sauté the spice paste until cooked, then add water and bring to a boil.
Add the chicken, powdered chicken stock, palm sugar, and salt. Add the coconut milk. Stir until evenly combined and adjust the seasoning. Cook until the chicken is done and the liquid has reduced.
Heat a grill pan or nonstick pan and brush it with oil or margarine. Grill the chicken while brushing it with the remaining seasoning until browned. Ready to serve.

Prepare the ingredients. Cut the water spinach into long pieces and wash thoroughly. Fry all the ingredients, add salt and palm sugar, then grind them. Add freshly squeezed lime juice.
Sauté until fragrant, then add the water spinach. Add ASatu Rose Brand MSG, salt, and palm sugar, then grind the mixture. Add freshly squeezed lime juice.
Adjust the seasoning, remove from the heat, and serve.
strIngredient9: Salt, to taste, ASatu Rose Brand MSG

strInstructions:
Trim the water spinach. Take the upper 2–3 thumb-sized sections of the stems, then separate the remaining stems and set them aside. Wash thoroughly and set aside.
Heat water in a pot and add 1 tsp of salt. Wait for it to boil. Once boiling, add the cleaned water spinach stems first and cook for a few minutes until half-cooked. Then add the young leaves. Remove once cooked, approximately 5 minutes over medium heat.
Transfer the boiled water spinach into ice water to stop the cooking process and help it retain its fresh green color.
Prepare a mortar and pestle. Add all the sambal ingredients except the tomato and lime. Grind until smooth, then add the tomato and grind again until the sambal is smooth.
Once the sambal is sufficiently smooth, squeeze lime juice over it.
The water spinach plecing is ready to serve with a main dish or as a simple meal.

Dry-roast the ingredients for the pounded sambal until browned.
Bring water to a boil, add the water spinach and enough salt, stir, and cook until the water spinach is done. Remove and drain.
Once browned, transfer the roasted ingredients to a mortar and pestle. Add the seasonings, including Rose Brand granulated sugar, and grind until smooth.
Once smooth, add the previously heated Rose Brand cooking oil and mix well.
Add the boiled water spinach and mix evenly again.
Finally, squeeze in the lime juice and mix well.
Serve.

Cut the water spinach in half and wash thoroughly.
Boil the water spinach in boiling water with salt and a little baking soda to help it stay green. Remove and drain.
Grill all the seasoning ingredients except the salt, sugar, lime, and MSG.
Grind the seasonings, then add salt, sugar, MSG, and lime. Taste and adjust the seasoning.
Serve the water spinach with the pounded or blended sambal.
strIngredient1: Bunches of water spinach with roots

strInstructions:
Wash the water spinach thoroughly and cut it into pieces. Boil the water spinach in boiling water with baking soda. Cook only until done, without overcooking, then remove and drain.
Fry the peanuts together with the garlic. Prepare the sambal ingredients.
Pound all the sambal ingredients except the tomato until smooth. Add the tomato that has been sliced.
Pound again until smooth. Taste and adjust the seasoning. Arrange the water spinach on a serving plate and pour the shrimp paste sambal over it. Sprinkle with fried peanuts. The water spinach plecing is ready to serve.

Wash all the ingredients, including the water spinach cut lengthwise, red chilies, bird's eye chilies, and tomatoes.
After washing everything, boil all the ingredients until cooked. TIP: Boil the bean sprouts for only 20 seconds so they remain crunchy. Once cooked, drain.
Place the salt, sugar, seasoning powder, stock powder, and roasted shrimp paste in a mortar.
Add the tomato first and pound it. This is an important step because it makes the other ingredients easier to pound. Once mixed evenly, pound all the ingredients together.
Squeeze the kaffir lime into the sambal, then pound until evenly combined.
The plecing sambal is ready. Now prepare the seasoned grated coconut.
Pound the large red chili, aromatic ginger, sugar, salt, seasoning powder, and stock powder.
Add the coconut and mix evenly with the ground spices.
Dry-roast the coconut over low heat while adjusting the seasoning to taste. Turn off the stove once all the seasonings are well combined.
Dry-roast the peanuts until they turn brown.
Place the water spinach over the sambal, then arrange the bean sprouts, grated coconut, and roasted peanuts on top.
Serve with warm rice and your favorite side dishes.

Prepare the ingredients and seasonings. Trim, wash, and cut the water spinach into pieces. The original version uses large Lombok water spinach, with the stems split and cut lengthwise.
Boil the chilies, tomato, and shallots for 3 minutes. Then pound them coarsely with sugar and salt.
Add kaffir lime or lime juice if desired.
Boil the water spinach for approximately 3–5 minutes until wilted but still fresh-looking. Remove immediately and rinse with cold water. Drain.
To serve, place the boiled water spinach on a plate and add the plecing sambal on top. Serve with warm rice and fried tofu or tempeh. Sprinkle with fried peanuts if available.

🌿Prepare the shallots and shrimp paste for grilling by threading them onto skewers that have been soaked in water. One shallot has not been skewered yet. 🌿Wash the water spinach thoroughly, bring water to a boil, boil the water spinach, then turn off the stove. 🌿Blend all the seasonings together, adding some of the water used to boil the water spinach. Adjust the amount of water to taste; normally, only a little is needed, approximately 50 ml. Make sure the palm sugar is soft so it does not damage the chopper or blender blades.
🌿After chopping or blending the seasonings, drain the water spinach, add it to the seasoning mixture, and stir well.
🌿Ready to enjoy.

Boil the sambal ingredients until cooked, then grind or pound them to your desired texture. Add palm sugar, salt, shrimp paste, and freshly squeezed kaffir lime juice. Adjust the seasoning to taste.
Arrange the vegetables as desired.
Pour the boiled sambal over them, then sprinkle with peanuts and fried anchovies.
strIngredient1: Water spinach, trimmed and boiled as desired
strIngredient4: Powdered shrimp paste; I use 1/2 sachet of sachet shrimp paste
strIngredient13: Bird's eye chilies, adjust to taste

strInstructions:
Boil the washed chilies, shallots, and tomatoes until softened. Remove and drain. Add the shrimp paste and salt, then grind until smooth.
Add stock powder and the juice of 1–2 kaffir limes. Mix, adjust the seasoning to taste, and set aside.
Wash the water spinach after splitting its stems. Boil, then remove and drain.
Clean and wash the long bean sprouts. Briefly soak them in boiling water, then remove and drain.
Arrange the water spinach and bean sprouts on a serving plate. Add the sambal and sprinkle with fried peanuts. Ready to serve. Alhamdulillah 🧡
strIngredient1: Water spinach, stems split and thoroughly washed
strIngredient2: Long bean sprouts, trimmed and washed

strInstructions:
Prepare all the required ingredients.
Cut the water spinach into pieces as desired and soak it in salted water for approximately 10 minutes. Fry the garlic and peanuts.
Drain the peanuts and garlic. Dissolve the tamarind in warm water. Prepare a mortar for pounding the sambal, then add palm sugar, shrimp paste, salt, fried garlic, and chilies that have been briefly boiled. You can also use raw chilies.
Pound until the mixture is still slightly coarse. Add one spoonful of peanuts and crush them coarsely with the pestle, then add the strained tamarind water. Boil the water spinach with a pinch of salt.
Drain and rinse with ice water to stop the cooking process, or shock it. Arrange on a serving plate and pour the pounded sambal over the top.
Sprinkle with fried peanuts. Delicious sweet water spinach plecing is ready to enjoy with your beloved family 🥰.

Prepare the chicken thighs, separate them, wash thoroughly, drain, then marinate with lime juice and salt. Boil the chicken until cooked. Briefly fry the chicken, remove it, and drain off the oil. Next, fry the prawn crackers, remove them, and drain off the oil. Set aside.
Prepare a bowl. Crack in 1 egg and add salt. Beat until evenly mixed. Fry the egg into an omelet until cooked, remove, let cool, then slice thinly into noodle-like strips. Set aside.
Prepare several dishes for the tumpeng set, such as squid curry, fried squid noodles, pineapple and cucumber pickle, and lado sambal. For the complete recipes, please check the attachment 😉
Prepare a round tray and line it with banana leaves that have been washed and wiped dry. To make it more attractive, arrange the leaves neatly and add lettuce leaves if desired. Arrange the rice and garnish it with sliced cucumber, tomato, and omelet. Arrange the fried chicken, fried squid noodles, fried prawn crackers, and squid curry around it, with two cups containing pineapple and cucumber pickle and lado sambal.
Najah-style tumpeng rice is ready to enjoy wholeheartedly 🌟✨🌞
strIngredient3: Fried squid noodles, fried squid noodles
strIngredient6: Pineapple and cucumber pickle, pineapple and cucumber pickle

strInstructions:
Mash the steamed cassava while it is still warm.
Add granulated sugar and salt, then mash. Next, add margarine and knead until smooth and pliable.
Take a small amount of getuk dough and add red food coloring. Place it in a cone-shaped tumpeng mold. Add the white getuk dough on top of the red layer and press firmly.
Prepare a plate or large tray and decorate it with banana leaves. Place the red-and-white getuk tumpeng on top of the banana leaves.
Now make Tegal putu cakes and koe cakes: mash the steamed potatoes.
Add glutinous rice flour, salt, and sugar, then mix well. Pour in the coconut milk and knead until smooth and pliable.
For the Tegal putu cake filling, peel the plantain and cut it into 6 pieces. Divide the dough into two portions, coloring one portion red.
Take 25 g of dough and place a piece of banana in the center. Shape into a ball. Once cooked, roll it in grated coconut.
For the white dough, take 25 g, place a piece of banana in the center, and shape into a ball. Steam the dough for 10 minutes.
The Tegal putu cakes are ready to serve.
Now prepare the mung bean paste filling: steam the peeled mung beans for 20 minutes. Then blend them with water until smooth. Cook the blended mung beans with pandan leaves, granulated sugar, and salt.
Once the mung bean paste becomes smooth and pliable, remove from the heat and let cool.
Now make the koe cakes: place the red and white dough into flower-shaped molds, add the mung bean paste, then cover with more dough.
Place on banana leaves and steam for 15 minutes.
Now make the rolled pancakes: combine all the ingredients for the pancake wrappers and mix until smooth.
For the filling, cook all the ingredients for the grated coconut filling until evenly combined and set.
Divide the pancake wrapper batter into two portions. Color one red and leave the other white. Put the white batter into a sauce bottle.
Heat a nonstick pan, then pour the white batter into a circle. Once it begins to set, pour on the red batter. Remove the wrapper when the bottom is cooked.
Take a wrapper and cut it into 4 pieces. Place the grated coconut filling in the center, then fold it into a flower shape.
The flower-shaped rolled pancakes are ready to serve.
Arrange the rolled pancakes, Tegal putu cakes, and koe cakes around the getuk tumpeng.
strIngredient7: Red-and-white Tegal putu cakes and red-and-white koe cakes
strIngredient35: Am kelapa sedang diparut dan dikukus

strInstructions:
Yellow Rice: Sauté the ground spice paste with kaffir lime leaves, pandan leaves, and lemongrass until fragrant and cooked.
Add the washed rice and stir until the spices are evenly distributed.
Add coconut milk, Masako® Chicken seasoning, and salt.
Keep stirring until the seasoning is absorbed and the coconut milk has reduced.
Transfer the rice to a preheated steamer and steam until fully cooked. Turn off the stove.
Sweet Tempeh: Fry the tempeh, cut into pieces as desired, until golden brown. Remove and set aside.
Sauté the sliced shallots and garlic until fragrant and softened. Add lemongrass, bay leaves, kaffir lime leaves, kandis sour fruit, and palm sugar, then stir.
Add the fried tempeh and mix well.
Add water, salt, and Masako® Chicken seasoning. Cook until the liquid has reduced, then turn off the stove. Set aside.
Balado Tofu and Quail Eggs: Fry the quail eggs and tofu until golden brown. Remove and set aside.
Sauté the balado spice paste until fragrant and cooked.
Add the tofu and quail eggs and stir well. Turn off the stove.
Fried Noodles: Boil the noodles until cooked, then remove and drain.
Sauté the ground spice paste until fragrant and cooked, then add the cabbage. Mix well.
Add the noodles, sweet soy sauce, and SAORI® Oyster Sauce. Stir until evenly combined.
Add the mustard greens, sliced scallions, salt, and Masako® Chicken seasoning. Mix well and cook until the vegetables are done, then turn off the stove.
The mini tumpeng is ready to serve.
strIngredient14: Block of tempeh, cut as desired

strInstructions:
Prepare all the ingredients for the steamed buns. Mix the water, Rose Brand granulated sugar, and instant yeast, then stir well. Let stand for 10 minutes or until the yeast has foamed.
Combine the steamed-bun flour and baking powder in a bowl. Pour the yeast mixture into the flour and stir until clumps form.
Knead until the dough is evenly mixed. Add the cooking oil and knead until smooth and elastic. Shape the dough into a ball, cover with a cloth, and let rest for approximately 30 minutes. After 30 minutes, knead briefly until the surface is smooth and the dough is slightly elastic. Divide into two portions and color one red, kneading again until evenly colored. Divide the dough into 15 g portions, shape into balls, and let rest for 5–10 minutes. Take one portion, roll it out, add the filling, and shape as desired.
Let the dough rest for 20–30 minutes. Steam over medium-low heat for 10 minutes. Turn off the heat but do not remove the buns immediately; leave them in the steamer for another 10 minutes to prevent wrinkling. Arrange them into a cone-shaped tumpeng.
The tumpeng steamed buns for Clover's birthday are ready to serve. Happy 8th anniversary, Clover!

Wash the rice thoroughly, then put it in a pot with water, coconut milk, salt, bay leaves, and lemongrass.
Cook over medium heat, stirring until the liquid has almost completely evaporated (the rice is partially cooked).
Once the liquid has reduced, steam the rice until fully cooked and fluffy.
Prepare a round tray and line it with banana leaves. Decorate the edges with cut leaves and secure them with double-sided tape.
Shape the rice into a tumpeng using a mold or bowl and place it in the center of the tray.
Decorate the rice with tomato and cucumber garnishes as desired. Arrange the side dishes around the tumpeng.
Serve the red-and-white tumpeng for a special occasion.
strIngredient13: Sweet soy sauce fried vermicelli recipe

strInstructions:
Heat a little oil, add the onion, and stir until softened and fragrant. Add the egg, scramble it, and mix well.
Add the chives and stir until wilted, then add the rice and mix well.
Add salt, ground pepper, garlic powder, and mushroom stock. Stir until the seasonings are absorbed. Adjust the taste.
Divide the rice into two portions, one white and one red. Add the dragon fruit, mashed with a fork, to the red rice. Mix until the color is evenly distributed. Adjust the seasoning and remove from the heat.
Put the rice into a piping bag. While still warm, add the red rice first, followed by the white rice, and press firmly.
Serve with accompaniments as desired. Alhamdulillah. Happy 8th birthday, Clover! May you continue to grow, develop, and always stay united 🎊🎉🎊🎉🎂🎂🎂💐💐💐🌹🌹🌹❤❤❤❤. Aamiin 🤲.
Hope you like it ❤❤❤❤🇮🇩.
strIngredient1: Plates of leftover rice from the previous night
strIngredient8: Small dragon fruit, mash with a fork

strInstructions:
Prepare a pot and combine the granulated sugar, agar-agar powder, and jelly powder. Stir well. Gradually pour the liquid milk into the pot while stirring until evenly mixed. Note: the jelly powder can be replaced with agar-agar powder. I used one packet of jelly powder that had already had 1 tsp removed, making use of the leftover powder from a previous recipe.
Turn on the heat and cook, stirring continuously, until the milk boils and the sugar dissolves. Add salt, stir well, adjust the taste, and turn off the heat. Continue stirring until the steam subsides.
Take 750 ml of the pudding mixture and pour it into a round mold with a 16 cm diameter that has been moistened with water. Let the pudding set at room temperature.
Next, take 500 ml of the white pudding mixture and add enough red food coloring plus just a little brown coloring to make the red darker, closer to the red-and-white flag colors. Pour it into a cone-shaped tumpeng mold and let it set at room temperature. Note: without a little brown coloring, the pudding will look more pink. If using a dark red coloring, the brown coloring can be skipped.
Divide the remaining white pudding mixture into several portions and add pandan paste, taro paste, orange food coloring, red food coloring, and mocha coffee flavoring, or other colors as desired. Note: if the pudding mixture begins to thicken, add a little liquid milk or water, then reheat it.
For the talam cake molds, I poured in white mixture and layered it with red or purple. For the flower molds, I added white, layered it with green and red, then added another white layer. For the other molds, I used white and layered it with orange. I added mocha coffee paste to the small amount of remaining mixture and poured it into quail-egg-shaped molds.
To make the tumpeng base, tear banana leaves into strips 8–9 cm wide, then fold them in half to mark the center. Fold the right side twice toward the center, then do the same with the left side.
Staple the center of the folds, then cut off the excess leaf at the bottom.
Arrange the folded leaves on a plate, tray, or round woven tray. Use staples or small skewers to secure the folds together. Place a round piece of leaf in the center.
Once all the puddings have set, arrange them on the plate. First, unmold the milk pudding in the center of the plate. Arrange the small puddings around it, then unmold the tumpeng pudding on top of the round pudding. Note: the mocha coffee pudding was not included in the arrangement because it had not set when it was time to assemble everything. It was almost time to take the photo.
The red-and-white tumpeng pudding is ready to serve.
strIngredient9: Orange coloring and mocha coffee paste
strIngredient11: Banana leaves for the tumpeng base

strInstructions:
Sauté the spice paste, then add the chicken and coconut water.
Fry over low heat until golden brown.
Arrange the tumpeng rice, Ayam Goreng Pemuda chicken, and the prepared condiments.

Mix 3.5g agar-agar powder, 40g sugar, 200ml water, and cocopandan syrup. Cook until boiling.
Pour into mini cone-shaped molds and let it partially set.
Mix 3.5g agar-agar powder, 40g sugar, 200ml milk, and vanilla. Cook until boiling.
Slowly pour over the red layer and let it set completely.
Remove from the molds and serve.

Blend the dragon fruit, strain the juice, then mix the juice with the red rice and water. Cook until done. Cook the white rice as usual until done.
Prepare a cone-shaped rice mold. Add the dragon-fruit red rice as the bottom layer and press firmly. Add the white rice on top and press firmly to form a two-colored cone.
Grind the shallots, garlic, coriander, turmeric, ginger, and galangal. Sauté the spices, add the chicken, and add enough water. Add the salt and mushroom stock powder together. Simmer covered until the chicken is tender and the spices have been absorbed. Remove and drain, then fry the chicken until golden brown.
Cut the tempeh into pieces, fry until golden brown, and drain. Sauté the shallots, garlic, galangal, bay leaves, and green chilies together until fragrant. Add the fried tempeh, sweet soy sauce, palm sugar, salt, and mushroom stock powder. Mix well until the seasonings are absorbed.
Boil the noodles until cooked, drain, and set aside. Sauté the shallots and garlic until fragrant, then add the cabbage and mustard greens and stir briefly. Add the noodles, salt, sugar, mushroom stock powder, and sweet soy sauce. Mix well until everything is combined, then remove from the heat.
Fry the potatoes and chicken liver and gizzards until cooked. Grind the shallots, garlic, and red chilies. Sauté the ground spices in oil until cooked and fragrant, then add salt, sugar, bay leaves, and mushroom stock powder.
Add the chicken liver and gizzards and mix well, then add the fried potatoes and stir until the seasonings are absorbed.
Boil the eggs until cooked, peel, and set aside. Grind the shallots, garlic, and large red chilies. Sauté the ground spices until fragrant, then add salt, palm sugar, and mushroom stock powder. Cook until the spices are done.
Add the boiled eggs and mix well until the seasonings are absorbed. Remove from the heat.
Grind the shallots, garlic, shrimp paste, and kaffir lime leaves (remove the central ribs). Sauté the ground spices until fragrant, then add salt, palm sugar, and mushroom stock powder. Add the grated coconut and cook until slightly dry. Arrange the boiled spinach, bean sprouts, and long beans on a plate, then sprinkle the seasoned coconut on top.
Fry the shallots, garlic, red chilies, bird's eye chilies, tomatoes, and shrimp paste until cooked. Pound all the fried ingredients together, add salt, sugar, and seasoning powder if desired, and mix well. Set aside.
Arrange the tumpeng as desired.
strIngredient4: Pairs of chicken liver and gizzards
strIngredient30: (sekitar 400g, ambil sarinya saja) buah naga merah

strInstructions:
Heat a little oil and scramble the egg, then add the rice.
Add salt, ground pepper, garlic powder, and mushroom stock powder. Mix well. Remove some of the rice.
Add dragon fruit to the remaining rice, mix well, and remove from the heat.
Garnish as desired and serve.
strIngredient5: Ground pepper and mushroom stock powder

strInstructions:
Dissolve the salt in the water. Place the aren sago flour on a tray. Sprinkle the salted water over it little by little using your fingers while stirring until moist, crumbly granules form. Steam it on a cloth lining and add pandan leaves. Steam for 20–30 minutes, starting from when the steamer begins boiling.
Kawul process: After steaming the sago, remove it while still warm and transfer it to a tray. Separate the granules so they do not stick together, sprinkling with water until the texture is moist and crumbly.
Steam again for 30 minutes. The color will become clearer and the granules will expand. Because packaged aren sago is used, immediately wrap the cooked horog² in teak or banana leaves so it does not dry out and harden when exposed to air. If it has already hardened at room temperature, reheat it by steaming for about 10 minutes to restore its chewy texture.
Horog² is usually served with meatball soup, soto, beef-skin satay, and pecel. I served it with ayam besengek and pecel. Since (in the story) we've already arrived in Jepara, I also made R.A. Kartini's favorite dish, ayam besengek (Jepara).

Rinse the rice thoroughly, add enough water, and cook in a rice cooker. Once cooked, take one plate of warm white rice, add the nasi uduk seasoning, and mix well.
Shape it into a cone, pressing it firmly so it holds together. Set aside.
For the omelet, beat the eggs with salt until combined. Add cooking oil to a pan and fry the eggs until cooked. Set aside.
For the tempeh stir-fry, slice the tempeh as desired, fry until half-cooked, and drain. Briefly blend the chili sauce, add the fried tempeh, and mix well. Then add the other seasonings, including oyster sauce, sliced chilies, kaffir lime leaves, and so on. Cook through and remember to adjust the seasoning to taste.
For the balado eggs, grind the seasonings using a chopper, blender, or mortar and pestle. Sauté the spices until fragrant. Add the peeled boiled chicken eggs. Mix well and cook over low heat. Adjust the seasoning to taste, then remove from the heat.
Remove the nasi uduk from the mold and place it on a decorated serving plate. Neatly arrange all the tumpeng accompaniments. Enjoy!

Rinse the rice thoroughly, then parboil it until the water has evaporated.
Take one-third of the parboiled rice and add food coloring. Steam again for 30 minutes.
Add nasi uduk seasoning to the red rice, then press it into the bottom of a mold.
Add nasi uduk seasoning to the white rice.
Place the white rice on top as the first layer, then add another layer of red rice. This is how it looks when the mold is removed.
For the fried vermicelli, first boil the vermicelli, then remove and drain it. Add sweet soy sauce.
Pour a little oil into a pan, then sprinkle in garlic powder and ground pepper. Stir-fry briefly and check the seasoning.
For the galangal fried chicken, cut the chicken into pieces, add the fried-chicken seasoning, and simmer covered.
Then fry until golden.
For the tofu, add salt and water, then fry until a skin forms.
For another accompaniment, I used ready-made peanut sauce and simply thinned it with hot water.
Wash the eggs thoroughly, then steam them.
To peel them easily, place them in a container and shake until the shells loosen.
First arrange the rice, fried chicken, and other side dishes.
Add lettuce and tomatoes; this time, arrange the lettuce differently.
Happy birthday, Clover!
strIngredient3: Packets of instant nasi uduk seasoning

strInstructions:
Coat the mold with food coloring. For the tumpeng shape, I use a piece of plastic cut into a circle and shaped into a cone. Add drops of coloring to the bottom. If using one large mold, use one about 24 cm in size.
Put all the dry ingredients in a bowl. Pour in the water while stirring until no lumps remain.
Pour the mixture into a saucepan through a strainer. Cook over medium heat, stirring continuously with a wooden spatula.
The mixture is cooked when it becomes translucent and smooth.
Remove it immediately and pour it into the mold. Let it sit for about 20 minutes until the surface firms up.
Apply food coloring to the surface, then let it cool completely for about 2 hours.
Cook the brown-sugar sauce ingredients until dissolved and slightly thickened. Once the selendang cake has cooled, cut it into pieces and place them in serving bowls.
Pour in the coconut milk sauce, sugar sauce, sweetened condensed milk, and ice cubes.
Serve.

Rinse the rice thoroughly and prepare the seasonings.
Sauté the seasonings until fragrant. Add the rice, coconut milk, and other seasonings. Stir and wait until the liquid has been absorbed.
Transfer to a steamer basket. Steam for about 25 minutes or until fully cooked, then set aside.
Cook the noodles according to the package instructions, remove, and drain. Mix with the included seasoning, then set aside.
Fry the sliced tempeh until partially cooked; it does not need to become crispy.
Sauté the ground spices until cooked, add the tempeh, and mix well. Add sliced kaffir lime leaves, chilies, oyster sauce, sugar, salt, and other seasonings. Mix well and adjust the taste. Ready to serve.
Prepare the balado seasoning using a blender, mortar and pestle, or chopper, along with the peeled boiled chicken eggs.
Sauté the seasonings until fragrant. Add the chicken eggs and mix well. Cook until the liquid has evaporated. Remember to adjust the taste.
Press the red rice into a mold, leaving some space because white rice will be added. Top with white rice and press firmly again. Transfer to a decorated plate.
Serve and arrange the accompaniments around the tumpeng.

Peel and wash the cassava, then grate it lengthwise. Add vanilla.
Add salt, tapioca flour, and sugar, then mix. Divide into two portions and color one portion red.
Place the white mixture in a round mold and wrap the red mixture in leaves to form a cone. Steam for 15 minutes.
Arrange all the cakes into a tumpeng shape and serve.
strIngredient7: Red-and-white serabi, a West Javanese specialty

strInstructions:
Rinse the rice and place it in the rice cooker. Add the instant nasi uduk seasoning and salt.
Add water, lemongrass, bay leaves, and coconut milk. Stir and cook until done. Set aside.
Rinse the rice, then add red food coloring and water.
Add coconut milk, salt, and garlic powder.
Add ground coriander and sugar, then stir. Cook until the liquid has reduced.
Heat the steamer and steam the rice until cooked.
Mold the rice and garnish with the side dishes.
Serve.

strInstructions:
Divide the rice into two portions. Leave one portion white and mix the other with red food coloring.
Sauté the shallots until fragrant, then add the bay leaves and lemongrass.
Place each portion of rice in a separate pot, add water and seasoning according to the specified amounts.
Cook both portions until done as white and red nasi liwet.
Mold the white and red nasi liwet in mini tumpeng molds, arranging them so the colors remain separate.
Place the tumpeng on banana leaves.
Arrange the tempeh stir-fry, fried noodles, chicken katsu, and fried salted fish around the tumpeng.
Serve as a family meal.

Pour the water into a bowl, add the egg yolk, instant yeast, and margarine, then stir.
Add Cakra and Segitiga wheat flours, then stir.
Knead until smooth and elastic.
Divide the dough and shape into balls.
Cover and let rest for 45 minutes.
Fry until golden brown.
Dip into the glaze and melted DDC.
Arrange the doughnuts into a tower or tumpeng shape.
Serve.

First, peel and wash the cassava thoroughly, cut it into small pieces, and steam for 30 minutes until tender.
Once cooked, mash the cassava. Add sugar and salt and mash again, then add margarine and mash until evenly combined. Divide the getuk into portions and add food coloring according to the characters or shapes you want.
I first made the tumpeng by combining red and uncolored getuk for the bottom. Next, I made the dry tempeh topping by coloring 3 tablespoons of getuk brown, rolling it thin, and cutting it into small pieces like tempeh. Add red getuk shaped into thin strips for chili slices. Then take 3 tablespoons of getuk, add 2 drops of orange coloring and 1 drop of yellow coloring, mix well, and roll into noodle shapes. Add green getuk for the leaves and white getuk for the cabbage.
Next, make boiled eggs using white getuk with orange getuk in the center, along with beef rendang and cucumber slices.
Arrange on a serving plate and serve with grated coconut. Enjoy ❤

Add the rice and pink food coloring, then stir until evenly combined. Cut the beef into pieces. Sauté the spring onion, onion, and large red chili, then add the beef and enough water. Add the sauces and seasonings, then cook until the beef is tender.
Slice the meatballs and sausages. Sauté the batokok seasoning in a nonstick pan with a little oil. Add the sausages and meatballs, then stir until evenly coated. Add one salted egg as an accompaniment.

Cut the chicken into pieces and clean it. Sauté the ground spices and add the other seasonings. Add the chicken and cook until its color changes.
Gradually pour in the coconut milk and adjust the seasoning. Add the boiled eggs and potatoes. Cook until the coconut milk boils.
Place the rice, chicken, potatoes, eggs, and their sauce in the rice cooker pot. Add the long beans and eggplant. Cook in the rice cooker until done.
Once cooked, shape it into a tumpeng or serve directly. The Sundanese tumpeng rice is ready to enjoy.

Peel the cassava, wash it thoroughly, and cut it into pieces. Clean the bananas, wash them, and remove their ends.
Wash and clean the pumpkin skin and sweet potatoes, then cut them into pieces and set aside.
Wash the unpeeled peanuts thoroughly until completely clean. Cut the sweet corn into several pieces.
Prepare the steamer and arrange the ingredients inside. Group ingredients with similar cooking times together (peanuts, cassava, and corn).
Add the pumpkin, sweet potatoes, and bananas.
Steam until cooked, then remove and arrange on a decorated tray.

Prepare the ingredients.
Wash the rice thoroughly, then soak it in turmeric water for about 30 minutes.
Steam for 30–45 minutes until the rice is sticky or half-cooked. Remember to add a stalk of lemongrass, bay leaves, galangal, and kaffir lime leaves.
Boil the coconut milk with lemongrass, bay leaves, galangal, kaffir lime leaves, and salt until it comes to a boil.
Once the rice is sticky and half-cooked, remove it and transfer it to a bowl. Pour the boiling coconut milk over it until it is evenly moistened.
Let it rest for about 15 minutes so the coconut milk can be absorbed by the rice. Once sticky, steam again for 45 minutes to 1 hour until fully cooked. Stir occasionally to ensure it cooks evenly.
Make the tempeh stir-fry to accompany the tumpeng rice. Slice and fry the tempeh. Then season it with sliced garlic and shallots and add sweet soy sauce. It is not spicy because it is intended for elementary-school children.
Serve in a bento container, shaping the cooked yellow rice into a cone and adding fried noodles, tempeh stir-fry, cucumber, and fried shallots.

strMeal: Tumpeng Nasi Kuning Ulang Tahun Homemade 🌻🌝
strInstructions:
Rinse 2 liters (1.5 kg) of rice thoroughly and drain. Put the rice in a pan and add enough coconut milk, using an informal measurement—about the length of the tip of a little finger. There was more than 1000 ml of coconut milk available. Alya bought grated coconut and made fresh coconut milk rather than using packaged coconut milk, which comes in very small quantities. Add yellow food coloring, pandan leaves, and the seasonings.
Lightly beat 4 eggs with salt and seasoning powder. Add the spring onion, then pour the egg mixture little by little into a nonstick pan while rolling it. Once cooked, slice the tamago.
Fry the chicken that was marinated beforehand.
Sauté the onions and chilies, then add the tempeh that has been cut and fried beforehand. Add the sauces and seasonings.
Sauté the onions again, then add the yellow noodles that have been boiled beforehand, along with the seasonings.
Prepare a mortar and pestle, pound the ingredients, then pour hot oil over them. Remember to add salt and seasoning powder.
Mold the yellow rice (only half of the cooked rice is used). Arrange the side dishes, yellow noodles, and sambal. Ready to serve.

strInstructions:
Rinse the rice, then steam for 15 minutes. Remove and cook it in a pot with lemongrass, bay leaves, sliced shallots, stock powder, and coconut milk.
Add the turmeric juice and ground coriander. Once the liquid has evaporated, remove the rice and steam for another 30 minutes.
When the rice is cooked, remove and serve with side dishes of your choice. I served it with sweet tempeh, spicy potato sambal, chicken rendang with eggs, cucumber, crackers, and melinjo crackers.

Prepare the ingredients.
Heat the oil and sauté the garlic until fragrant. Add 100 ml of coconut milk and stir, then add the kaffir lime leaves, pandan leaves, galangal, and lemongrass.
Mix the remaining coconut milk with salt and turmeric powder, then add it to the seasoned coconut milk. Stir briefly and cook until boiling, stirring continuously. Adjust the seasoning to taste.
Add the rice and stir until it becomes partially cooked rice (aron).
Heat the steamer and line it with banana leaves so the rice does not become too mushy. Steam the parboiled rice for 40–45 minutes.
Turn off the heat and transfer the yellow rice to another container, then sprinkle with fried shallots or shape it into a tumpeng.

Prepare all the required ingredients. 1) Wash the rice thoroughly. 2) Put it in the rice cooker. 3) Blend the garlic and turmeric with a little water, then strain. 4) Add lemongrass, Indonesian bay leaves, pandan leaves, kaffir lime leaves, instant coconut milk, salt, and water. 5) Mix well and press the cook button [it usually takes 45 minutes to cook]. 6) Once the rice is cooked, let it sit for 10–15 minutes before opening the lid, then stir well.
While waiting for the rice to cook || Instant-seasoned fried chicken: 1) Squeeze lime juice over the chicken and let it sit briefly. 2) In a pan, add 200 ml of water and 1 packet of fried chicken seasoning mix. 3) Add lemongrass, Indonesian bay leaves, and kaffir lime leaves, then bring to a boil. 4) Add the chicken and mix well. 5) Cook until the braising liquid has reduced. Remove and let cool, then fry in hot oil or cook in an air fryer until done and golden brown.
Rolled omelet: 1) Combine all ingredients and whisk well in a bowl. 2) Heat a pan over low heat and add just a little oil. 3) Make thin omelets, like making risoles wrappers. 4) Repeat until all the batter is used. 5) Roll the omelets together. 6) Cut to your preferred size.
Once everything is cooked, the yellow rice is ready to serve with the other side dishes.
strIngredient14: Packet of fried chicken seasoning mix
strIngredient26: Secukupnya kering tempe kering tempe sederhana

strInstructions:
Wash the rice thoroughly.
Transfer it to a pot. Add the seasoning mix, salt, turmeric, cornstarch, and water gradually.
I usually measure the water up to the finger-mark level, adding a little extra so the rice becomes fluffy and holds its shape when molded.
Mix well and partially cook the rice by stirring it over heat.
Once the rice has been partially cooked, steam it for 25 minutes.
Continue by fluffing and stirring the rice while using a fan to cool it. Shape it in a tray as desired. Add your preferred side dishes. That's it, all done.

strInstructions:

For the potato and anchovy stir-fry, the original recipe uses tempeh and anchovies, but I used potatoes because I happened to be out of tempeh. Cut the potatoes into thin slices, then fry in hot oil until cooked. Remove and drain. Fry the anchovies until cooked as well, then remove.

strInstructions:
Wash the rice thoroughly. Prepare a stainless-steel steaming container. Add the rice, other spices, seasonings, instant coconut milk, and water. Stir until evenly combined. Turn on the heat to steam the rice.
Remember to stir the yellow rice when it is almost cooked. Cook for approximately 40 minutes.
Once the yellow rice is cooked, serve it with the accompaniments. It tastes delicious, savory, and fragrant with the aroma of spices.

strInstructions:
Grind the candlenuts, turmeric, shallots, garlic, and coriander.
Heat the oil and briefly sauté the ground spices until fragrant.
Put the sautéed spices, lemongrass, pandan leaves, ginger, Indonesian bay leaves, and star anise into the rice cooker.

Put the rice in the Magicom rice cooker pot. Add the ground spices, lemongrass, Indonesian bay leaves, galangal, and salt. Dissolve the turmeric in water.
Pour the turmeric mixture into the pot with the rice, add water, and mix well. Press the cook button and cook until the rice is done.

Cut the tempeh and fry it. Fry the peanuts as well. Then add the onions and sauces. Remember to add the seasonings.

📌 Wash the rice, then put it in the rice cooker pot. 📌 Add coconut milk and salt, then stir. Add pandan leaves if available.

Combine all the meatball ingredients in a bowl. Knead by hand until evenly mixed and smooth.
Shape the mixture into balls about the size of large marbles, or to your preference. Make sure the surface is smooth so they do not crack during cooking.
Heat oil over medium heat. Fry the meatballs until golden brown all over; they do not need to be fully cooked inside yet. Remove and drain.
Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a covered pot or pan.
Sauté the onion, shallots, garlic, ginger, cinnamon, and cloves until fragrant and the onion has softened and turned translucent. Do not let them burn, or the broth will taste bitter.
Pour in the stock and add the fried meatballs.
Add sweet soy sauce, ground nutmeg, salt, and pepper. Mix well.
Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce the heat to the lowest setting. Cover the pot tightly.
Cook for 30–40 minutes until the meatballs are very tender and the seasonings have infused. Stir gently from time to time so they do not stick to the bottom.
Taste and adjust the seasoning. Add more sweet soy sauce if it is not sweet enough, or more salt if it is not salty enough. The broth should reduce and thicken slightly on its own.
Turn off the heat. Sprinkle with spring onions before serving.

Sauté the ground spices and the bruised whole spices.
Add the beef liver.
Add water and coconut milk.
Season to taste and cook until the liquid reduces and thickens.
The beef liver malbi semur is ready to serve.

Cut the potatoes into pieces and fry until partially cooked. Grind the spices, then sauté them with the cinnamon stick and red chilies until fragrant. Add the chicken and sauté until its color changes.

Fry the carp until crispy. Soak the glass noodles beforehand.

🧄 Bring enough water to a boil, then boil the chicken livers and gizzards with Indonesian bay leaves until tender. Cut them into large pieces and set aside. 🧄 Prepare the potatoes and spices.

Fry the tofu and tempeh, then set aside. Fry the eggs sunny-side up and set aside.

strInstructions:
1.A Wash the chicken thoroughly, then soak it in 2 teaspoons of salt for 10 minutes. 1.B Discard the soaking water and rinse the chicken thoroughly. Set aside. 1.C Grind all the ingredients for the ground spice mixture using a blender or mortar and pestle. Note: You can omit the chilies. I used a little chili for some heat, so I wouldn't need to look for sambal later, haha.

Lower the heat. 2.C Add the chicken and stir until every piece is coated with the spices. 2.D Increase the heat to medium-low and braise the chicken for about 5 minutes. 2.E Add the water, sweet soy sauce, and palm sugar. Sauté the ground spices until fragrant. Add the lemongrass and galangal, then continue cooking until the spices are thoroughly cooked. Add the water, sweet soy sauce, granulated sugar, salt, and Asatu flavor enhancer. Bring to a boil.

Wait until everything is cooked and the flavors are absorbed. Taste and adjust the seasoning.
Serve with diced tomato on top, or use any topping you prefer.
strIngredient22: Tomat merah (me: iris kotak untuk topping )

strInstructions:
Sauté the ground spices with the whole spices until fragrant. Add the onion and cook until softened. Add the water, salt, palm sugar, ground pepper, and mushroom stock powder. Cover the pan and cook until the sauce boils. Add the potatoes and cook until tender.
Add the boiled eggs, sweet soy sauce, and oyster sauce. Stir and cook until the sauce reduces.
It's delicious and so fragrant with spices. I love it! 👍😋
This is my lunch meal prep 😍.
strIngredient8: Ground pepper, mushroom stock, and salt

strInstructions:
Fry the tofu until golden brown and prepare the peeled boiled eggs.
Grind the spices; using a mortar and pestle gives a better result.
Sauté the ground spices until cooked and slightly browned, then add the whole spices and cook until fragrant.
Add the water, sweet soy sauce, palm sugar, and flavor enhancer. Bring to a boil, then add the eggs and tofu. Cook over low heat until the seasonings are absorbed and everything turns brown.
Once cooked, serve with fried shallots, warm rice, and sambal.

Clean the chicken feet. Put them in a pot with water, Indonesian bay leaves, kaffir lime leaves, and lemongrass to remove any unpleasant odor. Boil for 10 minutes, then drain. Sauté the spices until fragrant.
Add water to the sautéed spices, then add sweet soy sauce, ground pepper, ground nutmeg, kaffir lime leaves, Indonesian bay leaves, and lemongrass. Mix well.
Add the meatballs and salt. Adjust the seasoning. The chicken feet and meatball semur is ready to serve. Enjoy!

Cut the Chinese tofu diagonally into triangles, then fry and set aside. Sauté the ground spices with the aromatics until thoroughly cooked and fragrant.
Add the water and bring to a boil. Add the boiled eggs, fried tofu, and chicken fillet. Cook until the chicken begins to soften.
Add the sweet soy sauce, salt, sugar, and powdered stock. Let the flavors penetrate the ingredients, then adjust the seasoning and serve warm.

Prepare the spices and cut the boiled beef liver into pieces. Set aside and grind all the spices.
Sauté the spices until fragrant, then add the salt, sugar, powdered stock, and sweet soy sauce. Stir well.
Add the beef liver and stir. Pour in a little water and cook until the flavors are absorbed. Then add 1 liter of water and continue cooking. Check the seasoning.
Remove from the heat and serve. Done!

Prepare the ingredients.
Prepare the spices. Puree the shallots, garlic, and candlenuts.
Heat a little oil, sauté the ground spices until cooked.
Add water, also add lemongrass, galangal, lime leaves, bay leaves, pepper powder, cinnamon, and star anise, wait for it to boil.
Add the quail eggs and tofu, stir well, wait for it to boil while stirring occasionally.
Add coconut milk powder and sweet soy sauce, stir well. Correct the taste. If necessary, add sugar and salt in this step.
If the taste is right, add the chives, stir briefly until the chives wilt, and it is ready to be served.

strMeal: Semur Bola Bola Ayam (Khas Sunda Betawi Peranakan Belanda)
strInstructions:
Boil the eggs, then fry the tofu and potatoes until cooked. Set aside.
Balls: mix all ingredients then form into balls with quail eggs inside. Make the rest into small balls then fry until browned.
Semur broth: sauté the onion trio with margarine until cooked and fragrant, add tomatoes, sweet soy sauce, granulated sugar, brown sugar, grated nutmeg, cinnamon, cloves, salt, and pepper.
Add water then put everything in (eggs, tofu, potatoes, and fried chicken balls). Cook until absorbed; you can add scallions, brown sugar, granulated sugar, or soy sauce if it lacks flavor. Reduce heat for 30 minutes until spices are absorbed.
Add scallions and fried shallots as a complement according to taste.

Prepare the ingredients. Previously, I squeezed lemon + garlic pepper onto the squid and let it rest in the fridge overnight.
Sauté the ground spices (I just sliced them thinly), shallots, garlic, sliced ginger, coriander powder, and nutmeg powder until fragrant.
Add the squid and water. Then add sweet soy sauce, salt, black pepper, and mushroom broth. Cook until boiling.
Add tomatoes, cook until the spices are absorbed or the water has slightly reduced. Correct the taste.
Once the taste is deliciously perfect. Turn off the stove and pour into a serving dish, ready to be served with the family alongside other vegetable menus.

Prepare all ingredients.
Puree the spices.
Boil the beef lung with White Base Spice, add Bay Leaves, Galangal, and Brown Sugar.
Add Kalasan Spice and Ground Spices.
Add soy sauce and all seasonings... cook until done.
Ready to be served.

strMeal: 🐟 Gulai Ikan Bawal Kuah Santan + Terong 🍆 Anti Amis
strInstructions:
Prepare ingredients.
Heat the oil. Sauté ground spices + lemongrass + bay leaves + lime leaves until fragrant and the oil separates. Use medium heat.
Pour in the coconut milk little by little while stirring so it doesn't curdle. Add the candis acid. Cook until almost boiling.
Once the broth boils, add the pomfret fish pieces. Do not stir, just shake the pan so the fish doesn't break apart. After 5 minutes, add purple eggplant and whole bird's eye chilies, then gently flip the fish just once.
Season with salt, broth powder, sugar. Cook over low heat for another 5 minutes until the fish is cooked and the broth thickens. Correct the taste. Turn off the heat. Do not stir after it's cooked so the coconut milk doesn't curdle.
Eat warm with white rice... so good 🔥

Wash thoroughly and cut the mackerel tuna into 5 parts. Coat with lime juice, then the marinade spices. Stir well. Let it rest for a moment.
Sauté the ground spices until fragrant. Add the aromatic leaf spices and candis acid. Stir well.
Add the fish. Stir well. Add water. Boil until it bubbles. Reduce the heat. Add coconut milk.
Add sugar, salt, broth powder. Add tomatoes & green chilies. Stir briefly then turn off the heat.
strIngredient2: Lime, squeeze the juice and coat the fish
strIngredient3: Small pack of instant coconut milk 120 ml
strIngredient25: Asam kandis atau 5 buah asam jawa

strInstructions:
Bismillah. Prepare all ingredients. Sauté ground spices until the water evaporates. Then add oil, cook while stirring. Next, add lime leaves, turmeric leaves, galangal, cikala acid, and lemongrass. Cook until fragrant.
Add thin coconut milk, cook until boiling. Add fish, long beans, salt, mushroom broth, a little sugar, and sliced sour acid.
Cook until the meat is done, then add thick coconut milk, sliced tomatoes, and batak leeks. Cook again until the broth slightly reduces and is absorbed into the meat. Correct the taste. Then turn off the stove. And the Tilapia Fish Curry is ready to be served.

strMeal: Gulai Ikan Panggang Tahu Cabe Gendot
strInstructions:
Sauté ground spices along with bay leaf, lemongrass, and lime leaves until cooked.
Add enough water.
Add fish and tofu, stir well.
Add coconut milk, sugar, salt, broth powder, and gendot chilies.
Cook until done.
Remove from heat and serve.

Coat the fish with lime and a little salt. Let it sit for 10 minutes, then rinse.
Sauté the ground spices with lemongrass, lime leaves, bay leaves, and galangal until fragrant and cooked. Add water.
Add the fish. Cook over medium-low heat until the fish is cooked.
Pour in thick coconut milk and salt.
Cook while occasionally shaking the pot—do not stir too often so the fish does not break apart.
Correct the taste. Turn off the heat.

Air fry for 15 minutes the washed fish and chicken, having made incisions on the meat, spraying cooking oil on the surface along with a sprinkle of garlic and shallots.
Also prepare the filling ingredients so they can be easily executed quickly.
Heat oil, sauté garlic and shallots until fragrant, then add tomatoes, potatoes, empal gentong spices, and coconut milk, stir well. Pour water and add the fish and chicken that were air-fried earlier, wait until it boils, then add granulated sugar, totole (mushroom broth), black pepper, and lime. Cover the pot until the fish and chicken are perfectly cooked and the distinct aroma comes out, turn off the heat, then add salt while it is still warm and stir well. Serve while warm with white rice. Good luck trying it! 😊

Prepare the ingredients. I bought freshly squeezed coconut milk for 5k. Used half a pack of the thin one, half of the thick one.
Puree the spices. Initially I wanted to crush them with a mortar but decided to just blend them.
Pour the thin coconut milk into the wok. Add the ground spices to the thin coconut milk. Stir well.
Add dry spices.
Bring to a boil, add smoked milkfish, round eggplants, melinjo leaves, and long beans.
Cook until the vegetables are tender and the fish is cooked. Don't forget to also add whole ceplak chilies.
Add thick coconut milk, stir gently, cook for just a moment.
Correct the taste, turn off the heat immediately after the thick coconut milk is added and boils so it doesn't get oily.

Prepare ingredients. Wash the fish thoroughly and drizzle with lime juice. Set aside. Puree spices with a chopper.
Heat oil, sauté ground spices until fragrant, add drop-in spices, stir well. Add water.
Add the fish, add coconut milk, salt, sugar, and mushroom broth, stir well. Cook until the fish is cooked while gently stirring.
Turn off the stove and check the taste. Trevally curry is ready to be served.

Wash the mackerel thoroughly then cut into 2 (can also be left whole), add turmeric and salt, after that coat the fish evenly with turmeric and salt, let it sit for 10-15 minutes.
Prepare the spices to be pureed then blend or mash with a mortar (I used a blender).
Fry the fish until cooked, I used an air fryer to make it healthier 🤭 but using oil is fine too.
Heat oil then add the ground spices, sauté until fragrant, add the drop-in spices, sauté again until everything is cooked. After that add the fried fish. Stir well until the spices coat all the fish.
Add water, cook until the water boils, add instant coconut milk, stir well. Add salt and granulated sugar. Cook until the curry broth boils, correct the taste, then remove.
Serve with hot rice and fresh raw vegetables 😋

Prepare spices, peel and wash thoroughly then blend until smooth.
Prepare a wok. Add bay leaves, lime leaves, and lemongrass. Add a little oil then turn on the stove. Then add the blended spices. Cook until fragrant. Then add whole bird's eye chilies.
Once the spices are fragrant, add coconut milk and give a little water.
When the coconut milk broth is almost boiling, add the mackerel tuna that has been cut and washed clean. I stirred and cooked it until it boiled again. Lastly, add salt and broth powder, taste test. Then cook for a few minutes. So it doesn't spoil quickly, lastly add sliced tomatoes. Ready to be served.

strMeal: Gulai Pedas Ikan Asap Kepala Mayung
strInstructions:
Prepare ingredients.
Blend all spices until smooth (add enough water), after blending, cook until the water slightly reduces.
Add the smoked fish, stir well until all fish are coated with spices, add tamarind water, and other spices, cook again until it slightly reduces.
Add coconut milk, cook again until all spices are absorbed into the fish, remove, transfer to a serving plate, then serve.
strIngredient1: Smoked manyung fish head and tail
strIngredient8: Tamarind, mixed with a little water

strInstructions:
Wash the fish thoroughly then fry, set aside. Fry shallots, garlic, bird's eye chilies, turmeric, and candlenuts then puree with salt, sugar, and broth powder, sauté again with crushed galangal and lime leaves until fragrant and the leaves wilt.
Boil the eggplants briefly then add into the pot that already contains coconut milk and spices. Also add the fried fish, stir gently. Don't forget to taste test, once boiling turn off the heat.
Serve 🥰🥰
strIngredient5: Liter of medium thick coconut milk

strInstructions:
Prepare the ingredients.
Sauté Sajiku gulai spices until fragrant. Add lemongrass, turmeric leaf, bay leaves, and lime leaves.
Add the cut snapper fish pieces, stir well. Add water and stir well.
Add coconut milk, stir well. Cook until boiling. Add bird's eye chilies. Check taste, turn off the heat.
Place the snapper fish curry in a serving container and serve.
strIngredient1: Snapper fish, cut into pieces and cleaned, give lime juice

strInstructions:
Fry tofu until a skin forms, remove and set aside. Wash the catfish stomach thoroughly, set aside. (Me: briefly boil the salted catfish stomach with turmeric, lemongrass, and ginger to reduce the saltiness + fishy smell).
Sauté Sajiku gulai spices with cooking oil, add leaf spices. Stir until fragrant and cooked, then add water.
Add the catfish stomach, stir. Add the fried tofu, stir. Cook over low heat.
Then pour in the coconut milk, stir so the coconut milk doesn't curdle.
Add whole red bird's eye chilies. Cook until the broth thickens. Correct the taste.
Taraaaa, it's doneee 🤗🤗👏🏻👏🏻.
Serve with warm rice, raw vegetables, and shrimp paste sambal.. delicious!! 😍😍🧡🧡
strIngredient2: White tofu, fried until skin forms
strIngredient8: Stalks of curry leaves / salam koja
strIngredient9: Sheet of turmeric leaf, tied in a knot

strInstructions:
Fry the fish briefly, so it doesn't break apart when cooked, don't let it get too dry.
Crush ginger and turmeric then roast, toast candlenuts, slice the large red chilies while the bird's eye chilies remain whole to be dropped in during cooking, don't blend them. Blend all ground spice ingredients adding vegetable oil & a little water. For the drop-in spices, crush the lemongrass then fold it, fold the pandan leaf, tear the lime leaves then crumple slightly with the bay leaves.
Sauté the ground spices and drop-in spices until fragrant, add 1 pack of coconut milk, stir well then add water. Add flavorings, soak tamarind in about 200ml hot water, stir until dissolved then strain. Correct the taste until right, then add the fish.
If the broth has thickened enough, add the sliced long beans, cook until everything is done and the oil rises, lastly add 2 more packs of coconut milk, stir briefly and serve.
strIngredient3: Packs of small instant coconut milk

strInstructions:
In a wok, add ground spices, bay leaf, lime leaves, turmeric leaf, and crushed lemongrass.
Add coconut milk, stir well. Turn on the stove, cook while continuing to stir so the coconut milk does not curdle. Once boiling, add the fish head and other parts.
Also add tempeh pieces. Add salt and flavor enhancer. Cook until the fish is done, the coconut milk gets thicker and is fully cooked. Gulai is ready to be served.
strIngredient1: Tuna fish head along with its meat pieces

strInstructions:
After knowing the authentic taste of curry from this practical Sajiku spice, let's cook snapper head curry..
Prepare the ingredients, spices, and practical Sajiku curry spice..
Slice / chop the shallots, garlic, sauté with oil/margarine until fragrant,.. Prepare the coconut milk - this is from 1 coconut for thin and thick coconut milk..
Add the practical Sajiku chicken curry spice and sauté until fragrant.
Add the other spices. Pour in the thin coconut milk, cook over medium heat until it boils..
Add the snapper fish head, stir gently so it doesn't break apart. Because my pot is only size 24, the fish must be moved around to cook evenly.
After the fish is almost cooked (15 minutes), add the thick coconut milk. Correct the taste..
Cook until the broth thickens and the fish is perfectly cooked. Correct the taste, remove from heat.
strIngredient1: Pack of practical Sajiku chicken curry spice

strInstructions:
Wash the fish thoroughly, marinate with lime juice and a little salt.
Puree the spices; chili, onion, ginger, galangal, turmeric..
In a wok, add coconut milk, ground spices, leaves, and lemongrass.
Cook until it bubbles, stirring the coconut milk continuously so it doesn't curdle.
Add the mackerel and candis acid, stir briefly, let it sit for a moment.
Add the long beans, cook until the beans are tender (according to your preferred tenderness). Add salt, mushroom broth, and a little sugar, taste test.
Reduce the heat, leave it for +- 5 minutes, then transfer to a container.

Wash the fish thoroughly then fry briefly until the skin is brownish.
Puree the ground spices then sauté with galangal, lemongrass, lime leaves, and bay leaves until fragrant.
Add water, salt, fish, and coconut milk, cook until boiling.
Add tomatoes and basil, cook until slightly wilted then remove from heat.

strMeal: Gulai Pucuk Daun Singkong Ikan Salai 🍀🐟
strInstructions:
Prepare all ingredients. Boil the cassava leaf shoots first. Cook the coconut milk, before it boils, add the complete curry spice.
Add the smoked fish, stir well so the coconut milk doesn't curdle. Sprinkle only half a sachet of Sajiku curry spice. Add the cassava leaf shoots.
Stir the curry, after it's cooked, taste test. The taste of the smoked fish is absorbed into the curry broth. The cassava leaf shoots don't taste bitter. The cassava leaf shoot curry tastes sweet.

strMeal: Gulai Ikan Tongkol Cue Tempe Kacang Panjang
strInstructions:
Cut the tempeh into cubes or according to taste.
Cut the long beans.
Heat the oil, once hot, add the curry spice, sauté until fragrant. Add the fish, tempeh, long beans, water, sugar, salt, Royco, and coconut milk powder. Stir. Let it sit until cooked, then turn off the heat.

strMeal: Gulai Asam Ikan Pilot (Gule Masam Ikan Pilot)
strInstructions:
Prepare the ingredients for making pilot fish sour curry. Clean the ingredients, wash thoroughly, and drain.
Heat water in a wok, add sour curry spices, bay leaves, lime leaves, sliced sour acid, torch ginger, salt, and chicken broth powder.
Add pilot fish, basil, belimbing wuluh (bilimbi), and long beans. Let it simmer until the broth reduces and it is cooked.
Correct the taste. If it's right and cooked, turn off the stove.
Place some of the dish onto a plate.
The incredibly delicious pilot fish sour curry is ready to be enjoyed wholeheartedly 🌟✨🌞
strIngredient2: Sour curry spices bought at the market
strIngredient9: Sour belimbing / belimbing wuluh, cut into 2

strInstructions:
Boil water, then add the ground spices.
After the spices and water boil again for about 3 minutes, add the fish.
Follow with lemongrass, tamarind, lime leaves, lemon juice, sugar, salt, MSG.
Bring to a boil, add coconut milk. Correct the taste.
Right before turning off the heat, add scallions and basil. The dish is ready to be served.
strIngredient1: Tuna fish, cut and wash clean

strInstructions:
Soak the salted jambal roti fish in hot water for 35 minutes to remove its saltiness.
Add water, salt, Royco, coriander, pepper, sugar, and the fried jambal roti fish.
Fry the fish until browned, set aside. Then sauté the ground spices with enough oil. Add bay leaves, lime leaves, galangal & lemongrass, cook until fragrant.
Pour in the coconut milk, then add sliced tomatoes & whole chilies so it's not too spicy, cook until boiling.
Good luck trying! :) Don't forget to support the DAPUR PARIKAH channel; for the full video, check the YouTube video link.

Clean the fish, wash thoroughly, set aside. (I mixed tilapia and snakehead fish).
Sauté the ground spices until fragrant, then add the leaves and crushed spices, stir well until wilted. Add water. Cook until boiling.
After boiling, add the fish, stir well, then add coconut milk, stir well. Add holy basil leaves, candis acid, and carrots as well as salt. Stir occasionally so the coconut milk doesn't curdle. Cook until done and the broth reduces.
Don't forget to correct the taste. If it's okay, remove from heat. And ready to be served.
Alhamdulillah🤲.
strIngredient3: Long beans, cut into long pieces

strInstructions:
Marinate the fish beforehand for about 15 minutes. Puree the spices. Can be blended. Put in a wok. Add lime leaves and turmeric leaves. Add thin coconut milk, sliced green chilies. Turn on the heat. Add the fish heads. Cook until boiling.
Add salt, candis acid, add the eggs. The fish must be submerged so it cooks evenly and the spices are absorbed. Note: Be careful when stirring. The fish can break apart. Just stir the broth by pouring the coconut milk over the fish.
Add thick coconut milk. Add flavor enhancer. Stir gently. Cook until boiling. Check the taste.

Sauté ground spices, bay leaves, and galangal until fragrant and cooked, after that add them into the boiled jackfruit.
After that, add long beans, sugar, salt, and broth powder to taste. Once the beans are cooked, add the melinjo leaves.
Once the melinjo leaves are cooked, add coconut milk, correct the taste. Stir, do not let the coconut milk curdle. Turn off the heat after boiling.

Sauté the white spices until cooked, add the aromatic spices.
Add the boiled young jackfruit and chicken feet.
Add coconut milk and water, then add seasonings, check the taste.
Cook until the spices are absorbed and the water reduces.
strIngredient1: Pack young jackfruit, boiled until tender
strIngredient2: Chicken feet, boiled with the 5:30:7 method

strInstructions:
Prepare the ingredients, puree the spices, and crush the ingredients to be crushed.
Boil the young jackfruit, discard the first water after boiling, cook the young jackfruit again until half cooked, remove and drain.
Sauté ground spices, crushed ginger, crushed lemongrass, crushed galangal, bay leaves with preheated oil until the fragrant aroma comes out., add pepper powder, cook until the spices change color, then add 500 ml of water, cook again.
Then add the boiled young jackfruit, add sugar, salt, coconut milk, stir and correct the taste.
Add the boiled eggs, and the remaining 250 ml of water, stir and cook again until done. Remove from heat and serve.

Wash the jackfruit thoroughly. Put the jackfruit, water, and salt into a pot then boil the jackfruit until tender. I used the 5:30:7 boiling method.
Puree the shallots, garlic, and candlenuts. Heat vegetable oil, sauté the ground spices, lemongrass, bay leaves, lime leaves, ginger, and galangal until fragrant.
Add the jackfruit, water, salt, sugar, coriander, and turmeric. Cook until boiling, then add coconut milk, cook again until boiling.

Prepare the ingredients, cut the jackfruit according to taste, cut the chicken bones.
Boil the jackfruit until tender, and boil the chicken and chicken bones for 5 minutes, set aside first.
Puree the ground spices then sauté until fragrant, add bay leaves, lemongrass, and lime leaves, then add water.
After the water boils, add the chicken, cook until the chicken is tender, then add the jackfruit, add salt, sugar, and broth powder.
Then add water, put in the instant coconut milk, taste test.
If the taste is right, remove from heat, sprinkle with fried shallots, serve.

Wash the young jackfruit thoroughly, drain, then boil until tender.
Prepare the drop-in ingredients.
Heat oil in a wok then sauté the ground and aromatic spices.
Once fragrant, add the chilies and young jackfruit.
Stir well, add water.
Add coconut milk, then stir occasionally so it doesn't curdle, then season.
Once it's slightly boiling, add petai. Then add melinjo leaves and celery.. cook until done and serve.

Boil young jackfruit until tender. Drain.
Puree the ground spice ingredients.
Heat oil. Sauté the ground spices, bay leaves, and galangal until fragrant. Add beef trimmings and its boiling broth.
Add the boiled young jackfruit, stir well. Cook briefly until the spices are absorbed.
Pour in coconut milk, salt, brown sugar, and flavor enhancer. Cook until boiling.
Add melinjo leaves. Cook until done. Don't forget to test the taste.
strIngredient2: Beef trimmings, boiled with 500ml water until tender

strMeal: 9. Sayur Nangka Kapau   Ikon Kuliner Indonesia
strInstructions:
Pairing on the table with Rendang and Snapper Head Curry.. A perfect lunch.. 🇮🇩🎉❤️
Prepare the ingredients. For the Ginger and Turmeric, I used the ones previously prepped.
Boil young jackfruit until tender, drain.
Sauté ground spices, bay leaves, lemongrass, and galangal until fragrant.
Add jackfruit, stir well with the spices.
Pour in thin coconut milk, cook until boiling, after it gets somewhat tender, add cabbage and stir well.
Add thick coconut milk, salt, and sugar. Cook over low heat until the spices are absorbed.
Correct the taste, remove from heat and serve.
strIngredient12: Curly red chilies - 2 tbsp dried red chilies

strInstructions:
Boil the cut young jackfruit until tender. Prepare ground spices, roughly chopped scallions, whole bird's eye chilies, and bay leaves.
Sauté the ground spices. Add bay leaves, chopped scallions, and whole bird's eye chilies. Sauté until fragrant.
Add the young jackfruit, stir briefly. Add a little water while stirring so the spices don't burn.
Pour in water again, cook until the jackfruit is tender. Add coconut milk and sugar, cook while stirring gently until boiling. Cook until done and the spices are absorbed.
Correct the taste, remove from heat. Serve with lontong (rice cakes) / rice and crackers.

Boil the jackfruit with a little salt, boil for 15 minutes, then discard the water.
Puree the ground spices, sauté until fragrant, add lemongrass, bay leaves, and lime leaves.
Add chicken and 3 glasses of water, wait until the water reduces to about 2 glasses.
Add coconut milk, wait until it boils, then remove from heat.
Jackfruit stew is ready to be served.

First, boil the young jackfruit with enough salt until half cooked. Remove and drain. This step must be done to remove the sap present in the young jackfruit.
Boil the beef bones until tender then discard the fat floating on the broth.
Prepare the ground spices then process in a chopper until smooth.
Prepare the other spices then sauté the shallots first.
Once the shallots are cooked, add lemongrass, bay leaves, galangal, and lime leaves. Then add the ground spices and sauté until all spices are fully cooked, fragrant, and not raw.
In the pot with the beef broth, add the young jackfruit, cooked spices, along with sugar, salt, MSG powder, etc.
Add plain water and coconut milk, then cook until perfectly done. Taste and you can add more seasoning according to taste. Cook until fully done.
Once fully cooked, remove and it is ready to be served.

Prepare the ingredients.
Sauté the ground spices until fragrant. Add the other spices, then add the jackfruit and thin coconut milk.
Once boiling, add the blondo and thick coconut milk, cook until boiling, then add the cassava leaves. Correct the taste, wait until the cassava leaves are somewhat tender, turn off the stove.
Jackfruit and cassava leaf vegetable dish is ready to be served. Served with shrimp paste sambal, it's even more delicious ❤
strIngredient1: Young jackfruit or gori, chopped, then boiled and drained

strMeal: Sayur Lodeh Nangka Muda Ikan Asin Telang
strInstructions:
Prepare the ingredients.
Clean the jackfruit and cut into pieces, wash thoroughly, drain, then boil until tender.
Heat Rose Brand cooking oil, sauté the ground spices, bay leaves, and lemongrass until fragrant and cooked, set aside.
Pour in the thin coconut milk, stir well, and add the pumpkin and young jackfruit. Cook briefly, add the sautéed ground spices, stir well.
Add the long beans, salted fish, and pour in Rose Brand thick coconut milk. Add salt, Rose Brand granulated sugar, brown sugar, and broth powder. Cook over low heat while stirring so the coconut milk doesn't curdle, cook until the vegetables are cooked and the broth thickens, check the taste, remove from heat.
Serve with white rice, enjoy.
strIngredient2: Salted telang fish, cut into pieces

strInstructions:
~ cut the jackfruit according to taste, then boil with a little oil until tender, drain
~ prepare the spices, puree, sauté the ground and aromatic spices until fragrant, add the jackfruit and whole chilies, stir well.
~ add a little water, cook until the spices are absorbed, add sugar and salt to taste, stir well.
Add coconut milk, stir continuously so it doesn't curdle, taste test. Once it's set, turn off the heat
~ serve
strIngredient4: A handful of whole bird's eye chilies

strInstructions:
Boil water, add enough salt, and add the young jackfruit. Cook until tender. Once tender, drain and shred so it's not too large. Cut the long beans. Set aside.
Prepare the spices. Heat the wok, add oil. Sauté the spices until cooked and fragrant.
Add the long beans and a little water, cook until the long beans are half tender. Add the young jackfruit, flavorings, and the remaining water. Cook until all ingredients are done. Do a taste test before the dish is served.
Transfer the cooked vegetables to a container. The dish is ready to be served.

Cut the young jackfruit according to taste, then wash thoroughly, and boil until tender. Drain and prepare the spices.
Boil water, add galangal, bay leaves, and ground spices. Once the water boils, add the tender young jackfruit. Let the spices absorb. Add sugar and salt.
After the spices are absorbed and the water slightly reduces. Add the coconut milk powder while continuously stirring. Then taste test. If the taste is right, turn off the stove.
Savory tewel/young jackfruit vegetable dish is ready to be served 🥰

🔅Wash the young jackfruit thoroughly, boil/cook until done. 🔅Remove and discard the boiling water, wash again under running water. 🔅Boil water, add the thoroughly washed chicken feet, cook until the feet are tender.
🔅Puree the spices, sauté until fully cooked and fragrant. 🔅Add the jackfruit and ground spices into the pot with boiling chicken feet. 🔅Add broth powder, granulated sugar, and salt, cook until the jackfruit and chicken feet absorb the spices 🔅
🔅Let the water boil for a moment, then add Rose Brand instant coconut milk, stirring so the coconut milk doesn't curdle. 🔅Correct the taste according to preference.
🔅Jackfruit and chicken feet lodeh is ready to be served, and don't forget to sprinkle fried shallots.

strMeal: Gulai Sayur Nangka Buat Lontong Sayur Padang
strInstructions:
Wash thoroughly and steam the jackfruit vegetable for about 30-45 minutes
Let it sit for 1-2 hours (so the sap drains), don't be surprised if the water turns orange/cloudy and sticky
Sauté the ground spices until fragrant, add various leaves. After that, add the beef trimmings
Cook until 1/2 done
Add the jackfruit vegetable gradually, stir until the spices are evenly distributed
Add coconut milk and water
Add salt and broth, cook until the spices are absorbed over medium heat
10 minutes before removing, add chayote, correct the taste
Can be served with rice/lontong (rice cakes).

Prepare the ingredients first, soak the glutinous rice, I soaked it at night before sleeping, I used it in the morning.
Wash the dried shrimp (ebi/rebon) thoroughly, soak in hot water, drain then roast until dry and mash, set aside.
Puree all the coconut serundeng spices, put the spices into a heated wok then add grated coconut, granulated sugar, salt, brown sugar, and bay leaves, roast until the coconut is dry. Set aside.
Making kerak telor: heat a wok, DO NOT use a non-stick one, then put in 2 tbsp of glutinous rice, add 4 tbsp of water, cover the wok, cook over low heat until the water reduces.
While waiting for the water in the glutinous rice to reduce, prepare the eggs, crack them into a bowl, add 1 tbsp of coconut serundeng, 1 tsp of fried shallots, 1/4 tsp of roasted dried shrimp, I added 1/4 tsp of salt and broth powder, you can skip it, beat the eggs, pour into the glutinous rice that has reduced its water, stir the eggs and glutinous rice evenly in the wok, spread it out. If using ground spices like in the ingredients, you can add it in this step, like the original recipe 🙏
Cover the wok again, keep the heat low, wait until the edges of the kerak telor dry, flip the wok while sliding the egg part that is still a bit wet, bake until the top of the kerak telor is slightly burnt, then remove the kerak telor, it is indeed sticky on the wok, scrape the edges a bit until it comes off the wok.
Arrange in a container, add coconut serundeng and fried shallots. Betawi's signature kerak telor is ready to eat, yum.... yum, delicious.... so happy to be able to make my own kerak telor at home.😆

Prepare the ingredients. Put in all ingredients except oil and grated coconut, stir until even
Fry and spread out. Cook until perfectly done and crispy, and add grated coconut on top..

Puree the shallots, garlic, and red chilies, add salt and brown sugar. Also puree the roasted dried shrimp and granulated sugar.

Pour into a mold, wait for it to set and cool. Store in the refrigerator.
Serve cold for better taste.

👉🏿Slice red chilies thinly then sauté until fragrant 👉🏿Roast coconut until yellowish brown 👉🏿Roast dried shrimp then crush roughly, crush fried shallots too

strInstructions:
Prepare turi flowers, remove the pistils (the middle part). Wash turi flowers, spinach & bean sprouts thoroughly.
Boil bean sprouts, drain. Then boil spinach, drain. Boil turi flowers with salt, don't boil them too long. Remove and drain.

Correct the taste of the sambal.
Squeeze the boiled water hyacinth/genjer so the water content reduces.
Mix the water hyacinth/genjer into the peanut sauce earlier.

Refreshing.. whether it's raining or hot, always delicious, especially with lots of crackers.. can't stop eating it..
Puree garlic, chilies, and candlenuts, etc., then sauté with oil until fragrant.

Pour into the plate containing the seasoning and bean sprouts, stir well and serve

Prepare ingredients. Mix ground spice ingredients, add enough water (medium consistency). Add scallions, stir well. Test taste if necessary.

Fry tempeh until both sides are cooked, but don't let it get too dry.

strInstructions:
Make mendoan batter, weigh flour and measure tapioca. Mix into sliced scallions. Add flavor powder spices: chicken broth, turmeric, salt, flavor enhancer. Also add the pureed duo onions (garlic and shallot). Stir well.
Pour water little by little, until the mendoan batter is neither too thick nor too runny. Submerge the sliced tempeh one by one. Heat cooking oil so they don't stick to each other.
Flip the tempeh when one side is dry. Remove and drain, alhamdulillah the mendoan batter and tempeh run out at the same time.
Fry until finished, fry all the tempeh. Serve in a serving container with bird's eye chilies. Mendoan tempeh can be a snack for drinking coffee or tea, or it can be a side dish for eating rice. Alhamdulillah..
