strInstructions:
Prepare ingredients
Mix flours, ground spices, and scallion. Also add salt, turmeric powder, and MSG
Put gembus (tofu dregs tempeh) into the batter
Fry until cooked

Prepare ingredients, thinly slice tempeh.
In a container, put in wheat flour, Rose Brand Rice Flour, enough water, and spices. Stir until evenly mixed, then add finely sliced scallions.
Pour Rose Brand Cooking Oil and heat it.
Put the sliced tempeh into the flour batter then fry.
No need to make it crispy, after one flip, remove and drain immediately.
Ready to be served while warm.

Prepare ground spice ingredients.
Grind until smooth.
Mix ground spices with wheat flour and water as well as sliced scallions

1. Prepare mendoan tempeh. Fry sausages with a little oil to make them look glowing. 2. Beat eggs until dizzy, make omelets, do until finished then slice each sheet into 2. 3. Mix all flour ingredients in a bowl. Add pepper, salt, turmeric powder, and garlic powder, stir well and thin it with boiled water, not tears, set aside. Next, place an omelet on top of the tempeh, add sausage, then roll. Secure with a toothpick so it doesn't fall apart like a heart left by the crush. 4. Coat the rolled tempeh in the flour batter that has been added with sliced scallions, fry in hot oil until 24-karat golden yellow. Remove and drain, then pull out the toothpicks, not pull teeth. 5. Ready to be eaten while warm, dipped in soy sauce or bird's eye chilies.

Prepare mendoan tempeh which is usually sold wrapped in leaves.. or if not available, just use regular tempeh, slice thinly and widely..
Puree garlic, turmeric, coriander.. Mix ground spices, flour, salt and pour water little by little until the batter is neither thick nor runny..

Prepare all ingredients
In a container, put all dry ingredients, stir briefly, then pour water little by little while stirring until it becomes a batter with the same consistency as banana fritter batter. Dip the tempeh

1. Wash soybeans thoroughly. Set aside. Boil water, then pour into the container containing the soybeans earlier. Then close the container and leave it for 8 hours. After 8 hours, open the lid and leave the soybeans in the soaking water. This is how the soak looks on day 1. 2. Continue soaking until day 3 when foam appears and ignore the unpleasant smell 😁. Discard the soaking water and wash the soybeans thoroughly until the smell is gone. Drain the soybeans by placing them on a Paris cloth (I used a clean unused headscarf) let the soybeans dry completely. 3. After the soybeans are completely dry, pour the tempeh yeast and mix it so the yeast is evenly distributed. 4. Take 1 plastic bag, fill 1/3 of the plastic bag then prick the plastic bag with a toothpick/skewer. Then tidy up the soybeans. Arrange the tempeh starters in a wide-surfaced container/tray. Then cover the tempeh starters with a dark/black cloth and in a place not exposed to sunlight. Wait for 30 - 36 hours (depending on weather) for the tempeh to become uniformly solid. 5. Alhamdulillah after waiting for 36 hours, finally the mendoan tempeh is ready to be executed.🤗

Cut beef following the grain, thinly.
Heat cooking oil. Sauté ground spices until fragrant. Add lemongrass, galangal, and bay leaves. Sauté briefly until wilted.
Add beef. Pour in apple juice and water. Add pepper, salt, and broth powder.
Cook until meat is tender. If water runs out but meat isn't tender, add water, then cook again until tender. Once cooked, let it cool.
Pound or beat the meat until thin, but not falling apart.
Heat enough oil. Fry until slightly dry. Drain.
Sambal: boil chilies and onion (shallot) until wilted. Then grind or roughly chop.
Heat enough oil. Sauté chilies and onion.
Add salt, broth, and tamarind water. Also add the meat boiling broth. Cook until the oil separates again.
Serve dendeng (jerky) with sambal. You can also mix the sambal and meat. Afiyet olsun (Enjoy your meal)!

Boil the beef lung, I added a secret spice, salt, and tamarind. After 30 minutes let the lung cool down. Slice the lung thinly according to taste.
Prepare lung spices, puree everything; garlic, turmeric, coriander, and salt. Boil water, add galangal, ginger, lemongrass, and pepper. Add the sliced lung. Add the pureed lung spices.
Boil until all water is absorbed by the lung, remove and drain. Arrange the lung on a baking sheet, bake for 15 minutes, temperature 180⁰. Take out from the oven, fry the lung over medium heat. Until dry. Fry shallots until crispy. Serve lung with a sprinkle of fried shallots.

Cut the meat into several pieces; I cut mine into thin slices.
Grind all the spices except the bay leaves. The paste is yellow because some leftover galangal paste was ground after the turmeric.

Cook over medium heat, stirring occasionally so the spices coat the meat evenly. Cover the pan to help the meat become tender faster.
Let it cook until the liquid has reduced and the meat is tender. Taste and adjust the seasoning. Once it tastes right, transfer it to a container.
The galangal beef jerky is ready to serve.

strInstructions:
Slice the meat, it's easier to slice when it's still frozen. Marinate with the secret spice, tamarind and fine salt. Put in a covered container. After marinating for quite a long time, braise the meat. Cook without adding anything until its juices come out and absorb back into the meat.
Fry the meat until brownish then chop / pound it in a chili mortar. Fry again over low heat until cooked.
Remove and drain the meat. Continue by baking the jerky in the oven, at a temperature of 150⁰ using top and bottom heat. For about 10 minutes, making the oil in the jerky come out and making it drier and crispy.
Meanwhile, fry shallots. Arrange / place the jerky on a plate then spread the fried shallots. Store the jerky in a covered container to keep it crispy and dry.

Cut the meat thinly and into small pieces against the grain. Then pound with the blunt side of a knife
Puree the ground spices except brown sugar. When it's soft, add brown sugar and mash until even. Then test taste
Separate the spices into 2 parts. Half to marinate the meat, the other half for the grated coconut. Then mix both
Heat oil over medium heat, add enough dendeng ragi (spiced meat with grated coconut), fry until cooked brownish

Puree garlic, ginger, coriander, cloves, nutmeg, and salt.
Cook the meat with the ground spices, cardamom, star anise until cooked, do not throw away the remaining water
Remove the meat, cut and crush.
Fry the potatoes and jerky just briefly.
Puree red chilies, shallots, tomatoes, and salt.
Sauté sliced shallots and garlic until fragrant, add pureed chilies, sauté until cooked.
Add coconut water, leftover meat boiling water and add the jerky, cook until the spices are absorbed.
Add potatoes and tomatoes, cook until boiling.
Serve warm.

Mix the sliced meat with coriander powder, cumin powder, sugar and salt, grated garlic.
Also add grated galangal, broth blocks, and brown sugar
Stir evenly, add cooking oil. Stir until evenly mixed. Knead using hands (don't forget to wash hands or use plastic gloves) until all spices are evenly mixed. Marinate for at least 1 hour.
Prepare aluminum foil. Then take enough meat mixture and place it inside the aluminum foil
Bake in a preheated oven for 30 minutes with top and bottom heat at 170°C or adjusted to each oven.
After it's cooked, I flip the top part of the jerky, so that the bottom part of the jerky also gets drier and I heat it again for 10 minutes until the jerky is drier.

strInstructions:
Freeze the meat for 1-2 hours, slice as thinly as possible against the grain (1-2 mm).
Mix the meat with coconut water and vinegar, squeeze gently, let it sit for 15 minutes, drain.
Puree the shallots, garlic, candlenuts, ginger, coriander, cumin, nutmeg.
Sauté the ground spices, bay leaves, lemongrass, and lime leaves until fragrant.
Add the meat, stir well. Add brown sugar, soy sauce, salt, broth.
Cook on low heat, stir continuously until the spices are absorbed and it is completely dry (20-30 minutes).
Arrange on a baking sheet, bake in the oven at 140°C for 20-30 minutes, flip every 10 minutes.
Increase the temperature to 190°C, bake for 5-10 minutes until caramelized and crispy.
Cool, cut into small pieces, store in an airtight jar.

Prepare ingredients. Peel and wash carrots and lettuce thoroughly. Finely shred then boil the carrots for 3 minutes, then pour cold water over them and drain. Cut the meat lengthwise. Set aside.
Prepare and cool the rice. Beat the eggs, make a thin omelet with a pan then roll it (no need to slice it) and set aside. Place nori on a mat/cutting board, put rice on top then flatten and compact it.
Arrange the omelet, beef pieces, carrots, and lettuce on top of the rice. Roll carefully while compacting. Moisten the end of the nori then stick it to lock it. Cut the sushi according to taste. Serve or pack for lunch. Good luck trying it.

Boil meat, crushed ginger, coriander powder until tender, drain
Crush the drained meat then fry briefly until slightly dry, drain.
Sauté the ground spices until fragrant and cooked then add the meat and stir evenly
Correct the taste and cook until done
Alhamdulillah ready to be served. 👌

Take 4 cloves of garlic, lemongrass stalk, and galangal then pound/crush. Cut the cleaned meat. Cut ALONG THE GRAIN, as thinly as possible and wide in a square shape
Pour coconut water until the meat is submerged then, add the pounded spices as well as add the tied turmeric leaf, 2 bay leaves, 1 lime leaf, 1/2 tbsp tamarind, and 1/2 tbsp salt and stir then add the cut meat, and boil with low heat until the water reduces and the spices are absorbed.
While waiting for the boiling. Take 100 gr of large chilies and red bird's eye chilies according to taste, 2 cloves of garlic and 50 grams of shallots, put them in a blender then blend them until smooth.
Remove the boiled meat and pound gently until thin (do not damage the meat). Pour enough oil into a wok then heat the oil and fry the meat for a few seconds only (until the meat is brownish). Remove then drain. Leave a little oil to sauté the tomatoes that have been cut into pieces.

Fry potatoes and jengkol then flatten the jengkol

Heat oil, add the crushed chilies, add seasoning and add the remaining water from braising the meat. After that, stir all ingredients until evenly mixed and it is ready to be served

Boil meat with lime leaves & bay leaf until tender. Remove, crush but do not let it fall apart. Fry briefly in hot oil. Remove, drain.

Mix the remaining spices into the grated coconut, then add the marinated chicken, sprinkle starch flour evenly and press the chicken so it sticks.
Fry until cooked.

Marinate and boil meat. Drain when cooked and changed color, slice thinly and crush.

Fry potatoes until golden brown, set aside.
Fry meat until crispy.
Boil curly chilies and garlic. Then crush roughly and add 5 peppercorns (or to taste; pepper makes the sambal aroma more fragrant). Slice shallots.

Prepare meat ingredients, slice to desired thickness, prepare spices and puree.
Put meat in a wok Add pureed spices

Mix all spices and meat, stir well, then let sit for 60 minutes / 1 hour.
Heat a non-stick pan, add meat, cook over low heat until tender and the water dries up. If the meat isn't tender yet, add water little by little until completely tender.
Before removing, add 3 tablespoons of cooking oil, fry briefly.
Remove and serve as a side dish for warm rice.

Wash meat thoroughly, cut following the meat fibers. Prepare and puree meat braising spices.
Coat meat with braising spices, then boil beef until tender, then remove and drain (I boiled the meat using a pressure cooker for about 45 minutes).
Take a piece of meat, then beat/crush/pound (can use a mortar or meat tenderizer) so the meat is flatter and its fibers are softened. Do this until all meat is done.
Heat oil in a wok, fry meat just briefly until brownish, remove and drain.
Prepare balado spices, then roughly grind large red chilies, curly red chilies, red bird's eye chilies, shallots and tomatoes.
Sauté sliced shallots until fragrant, add ground spices and lime leaves, sauté until cooked. Pour broth/meat boiling water, stir well.
Add tamarind water, salt, sugar, pepper and broth powder, stir well while correcting the taste. Add beef, stir well and cook until water reduces and spices are absorbed.
Pour onto a serving plate, enjoy dendeng batokok with a plate of warm rice 🍚...hhmmm yummy 😋😍

Cut beef thinly and boil or pressure cook with spices for about 30 minutes. Drain and crush
Steam spices, drain, add candlenuts, and grind.
Fry meat just briefly until its color changes
Sauté the spices from earlier, add lime leaves, stir, and season with sugar, salt, beef broth. Stir until fragrant. Correct taste. Then add the crushed meat from earlier. Lastly add water until it reduces, stir, correct taste again, and serve.

Then add tamarind water and water into the wok.
Cook until water reduces and meat is tender. I cooked it for 25-30 minutes earlier.

Jerky (wet anti-fuss) is ready to be served.

Cut meat 1 cm thick. Cut according to the meat fibers
Puree spices using a blender.
Put meat in a wok/pot. Pour ground spices and drop-in spices. Sprinkle salt, sugar, and soy sauce. Squeeze meat with spices so it absorbs and becomes tender. Let sit for 15 minutes.
Add water and coconut milk. Boil meat until tender, cooked, and spices reduce. Test taste.

Heat oil in a wok. Fry the crushed meat until brownish. Remove. Drain the oil.
Serve empal gepuk with onion sambal, rice, fresh vegetables.

Prepare ingredients. Boil meat with drop-in spices until tender. Shred the meat.
Prepare spices and other ingredients. Puree/blend spices with a little water. Heat enough cooking oil. Sauté spices until fragrant.
Add shredded meat. Stir well. Add coconut milk, brown sugar, and salt. Cook while continuing to stir until spices are absorbed. Correct taste by adding mushroom broth.
Cook while continuing to stir until the moisture level of the empal is to your liking. If you like it dry like meat floss (abon), after the spices are absorbed, the empal can be further fried. Serve.

strInstructions:
Put meat into a pot. Add enough water until submerged. Boil ±10–15 minutes until impurities rise to the surface. Discard boiling water. Re-boil meat in clean hot water, boil until half tender.
Puree all ground spices. Heat oil, sauté ground spices over medium heat until fragrant. Add all aromatic spices. Cook until spices are fully cooked (color slightly darkens and oil starts to separate).
Add powdered spices, stir briefly. Just 60 seconds. Immediately add meat, stir until the entire surface of the meat is coated with spices.
✅ Add 1200-1400 ml water, cook for about 30 minutes, then add seasoning. Stir well. Cook slowly until meat is tender and broth reduces. ✅ When meat is about 85–90% tender, remove briefly, lightly crush using a mortar.
Add coconut milk. Continue cooking until broth is almost gone and spices stick to the meat and the surface is slightly oily. Taste test. Remove and let it cool completely.
Cool Completely. Let it sit until completely cool before storing. Do not seal tightly right away while hot. Serving: Fry briefly over medium heat.

Boil buffalo meat with water until tender (45–60 minutes), save 200ml of broth.
Sauté ground spices, bay leaves, galangal, and lemongrass until fragrant.
Add boiled meat, stir well. Add soy sauce, sugar, salt, pepper, tamarind water, and 200ml broth.
Braise over low heat until spices are absorbed and broth reduces. Add coconut milk if you want a wet version.
Cool the meat, then gently crush until flat.
Fry the crushed meat briefly until brownish and dry on the outside.
Serve warm with rice, sambal, and fresh vegetables (lalapan).

Serve beef empal.
Sprinkle with fried shallots.

Pour sweet soy sauce, salt, and pepper. Stir until all mixed evenly and rice is hot.

Puree garlic, coriander, candlenuts, tamarind, Javanese sugar and salt, check taste adjust to preference

Cook until spices are absorbed, then turn off heat. Pour into a serving bowl, sprinkle with scallions and squeeze lime juice (I used lemon). Makassar style Konro Soup is ready to be served.

Cut meat into bite-size pieces and cut rib bones 10-15 cm each so they are easy to eat. Boil meat and bones with water until tender. Once tender, drain the water.
Puree the spices by grinding or blending. Soak kluwak and tamarind with hot water.
Sauté the ground spices with bay leaves and lemongrass until fragrant and cooked.
When the spices start to dry, add roasted grated coconut. Stir well.
Put the mashed kluwak and tamarind solution into the pot. Add drop-in ingredients and water.
Put the meat and bones into the pot with the spices. Cook until spices are absorbed.
Add fried shallots and scallions after spices are absorbed. Turn off the stove.
Serve warm with burasa (rice cake) or other carb foods. Enrich the taste by adding complementary ingredients like lime, fried shallots, sliced scallions and celery, soy sauce and sambal.

Boil goat meat with spices to reduce its strong smell. Pressure cook for 30 minutes.
Fry peanuts until cooked then set aside.

strInstructions:
Prepare all ingredients, wash the boiled beef ribs thoroughly then discard the water to reduce fat and impurities.
Boil beef ribs with 2000 cc of water, add directly the crushed galangal, bay leaves, cloves, cinnamon, cardamom, tamarind. Puree the ground spices: garlic, shallots, ginger, turmeric, lemongrass, cumin, coriander, pepper, candlenuts, add the kluwek that has been soaked in hot water.
Sauté until cooked and fragrant, pour the ground spices into the beef rib broth, add salt and brown sugar. Close the pressure cooker, pressure cook for 45 minutes after the pressure cooker hisses. (Depending on the respective pressure cooker) turn off the heat and let the hot steam of the pressure cooker disappear.
Serve the MAKASSAR STYLE BEEF RIB KONRO SOUP with a sprinkle of scallions and fried shallots as well as a squeeze of lime juice and sambal.

strInstructions:

While the ribs are boiling, puree the prepared spices, then sauté with enough oil until fragrant, add bay leaves and crushed galangal. Sauté until cooked
Put the sautéed spices into the cooked rib broth, add tamarind water and cinnamon, cook until the spices are absorbed, add broth powder and salt... test taste, turn off the stove
Remove and serve, add complementary ingredients

Prepare ingredients. Boil beef ribs briefly, discard the first boiling water. Put the ribs and water in a pressure cooker then cook for 30 minutes (counted from when the cooker hisses). Soak black-eyed peas overnight or at least 3 hours until tender. Drain and set aside.
Slice tofu and tempeh to taste. Puree shallots and garlic then sauté with instant rawon spices until wilted and fragrant. Add bay leaves and lime leaves, sauté briefly. Add broth from boiling ribs.
Put water, remaining broth, and sautéed spices into the pressure cooker containing the ribs. Add melinjo skin and black-eyed peas, cook until boiling. Add tofu, tempeh, and rib meat, stir well.
Add salt, flavor enhancer, pepper powder, and Javanese sugar, cook until cooked and spices are absorbed. Pour in coconut milk while continuing to stir so the coconut milk doesn't curdle. Correct taste, add very spicy bird's eye chilies and cook briefly then remove. Serve. Good luck trying.

Prepare ingredients. Soak black-eyed peas overnight. Cut chicken, boil briefly, discard the first boiling water. Reboil with salt until cooked, remove and drain. While waiting, prepare the ground spices. Crack and take the contents of the kluwak. Peel shallots and garlic then roast candlenuts until fragrant and oil comes out.
Puree spices until completely smooth. Heat a little oil then sauté ground spices until fragrant and wilted. Add drop-in spices, sauté briefly.. Add chicken and its boiling water then stir well. Sprinkle salt, granulated sugar and pepper powder. Stir again.
Add boiled peeled eggs and melinjo skin. Add 2 liters of water. Cut tofu and tempeh to taste. After brongkos boils add black-eyed peas, tempeh, white tofu, and skin tofu (magel tofu) Stir carefully so the tofu doesn't break apart.
Cook until boiling, then add coconut milk while continuing to stir so the coconut milk doesn't curdle. Reduce heat, add broth powder, flavor enhancer (optional) and Javanese sugar. Correct taste, lastly add very spicy bird's eye chilies and cook until spices are absorbed and brownish. Remove and serve. Good luck trying.

Cut all ingredients

Crack kluwak then soak in hot water and prepare all spices
Puree kluwak, raw chilies, coriander, candlenuts, pepper and turmeric, set aside, heat enough oil then sauté ground spices until fragrant and cooked (raw kluwak smell disappears), then add drop-in spices then bird's eye chilies, stir well, sauté until fragrant

Make ground spices. Blend all ingredients with a little water.

Put the pot lid on, lock until it clicks. Turn on medium heat. Cook for 30 minutes after hearing the steam sound. Turn off and let the pressure cooker cool. Then open.

strInstructions:
Mix sugar, coconut milk, and pandan leaf. Add coconut milk, stir well. Then boil until cooked. Let it cool.
Mix rice flour and tapioca flour, add the cooked coconut milk from earlier. Divide into 2 while straining. Add rose red coloring to 1 part.
Prepare the steamer, wait until it boils. Then take 1 soup ladle of batter. Pour into the mold, steam for 6 minutes. Then continue with the next layer for 6 minutes per layer. Lastly, steam for 30 minutes. Let it cool and put it in the fridge first until completely cold before removing from the mold. Lapis beras is ready to be served

strInstructions:
Prepare ingredients.
Cook coconut milk + pandan leaves over low to medium heat until boiling, while continuously stirring so the coconut milk doesn't curdle, let it cool.
In a container, mix tapioca flour, rice flour, granulated sugar, vanilla, and salt. Stir evenly.
Add the cooled coconut milk little by little while stirring until all ingredients are evenly mixed and sugar is dissolved. Strain the batter, divide the batter equally into two.
Chocolate layer: dissolve cocoa powder with 3 tbsp hot water until it forms a paste then mix into one part of the batter, strain.
Heat the steamer until there's plenty of steam, line the steamer lid with a clean cloth/napkin. Heat the mold that has been smeared with cooking oil for 5 minutes.
Pour 100 ml of chocolate batter, steam for 7 minutes (use a timer) then pour 100 ml of white batter, steam for 7 minutes. Do this until the batter is finished, lastly steam for 25 minutes.
Turn off the heat, remove the mold from the steamer, let it cool completely before removing the cake from the mold. Cut according to taste.
Serve.
strIngredient7: Pandan leaves, tied in a knot

strInstructions:
Heat Rose Brand Coconut Milk, Rose Brand Granulated Sugar, and salt in a pot. Set aside and wait until cool.
Mix Rose Brand Rice Flour, Cap Pak Tani Gunung Tapioca Flour, vanilla, and coconut milk mixture. Stir until evenly mixed.
Strain the batter mixture, so there are no lumps. Then divide into 2 equal parts. Add orange food coloring to one part of the batter.
Boil water in a pot, after boiling, insert the mold that has been smeared with cooking oil previously. Pour 15 ml of white layer batter. Then steam for 4 minutes.
Open the steamer, pour again 15 ml of the second orange layer. Steam again for 4 minutes. Do this until 5 layers are made while alternating colors. The last part is steamed for ± 10 -15 minutes to cook perfectly.
Cool down, remove from the mold and lapis is ready to be served.
strIngredient2: Cap pak tani gunung tapioca flour
strIngredient9: Cooking oil for greasing the mold

strInstructions:
Boil coconut milk with 1 sheet of pandan leaf,.. Let it cool
Mix mung bean flour (tepung hongkue), wheat flour, sugar, and salt in a container.
Pour coconut milk little by little while stirring until dissolved and not lumpy (strain if necessary)
Divide the batter into two parts, give purple food coloring to one part, leave the other part white/add a little food whitener that has been dissolved
Heat steamer, line the pan with plastic or apply a thin layer of oil.... Heat mold for 3 minutes
Pour 50 ml of purple batter... steam 5 - 7 minutes.... Before pouring the batter, it must be stirred so it doesn't settle at the bottom
After the purple batter sets, pour the white batter (50 ml) on top of it, steam for 5 minutes.
Repeat until the batter is finished, steam the last layer for 20 minutes to cook perfectly.
Let it cool, cut according to taste.
strIngredient4: Medium thick coconut milk /1 pack instant coconut milk 65 ml +335 ml water =400ml

strInstructions:
Mix Rose Brand granulated sugar, salt, water and coconut milk. Stir evenly.
Add pandan leaves, cook until boiling. Let it cool. Weigh Rose Brand rice flour and Rose Brand tapioca flour
Mix evenly. Pour the cooled coconut milk, use a strainer. Stir until the batter is even. Divide the batter into 2 equal parts.
Give white coloring to 1 batter, stir evenly. And give red coloring to 1 part. Stir evenly
Prepare a mold that has been smeared with oil, heat the steamer. Pour 1 tbsp of batter. Steam for 7 minutes. Then pour again 1 tbsp of red batter. Steam again for 7 minutes.
Then pour 1 tbsp of white batter, steam 7 minutes. Pour again 1 tbsp of white batter, steam 7 minutes. Repeat the same thing. And on the last white batter, steam for 20-25 minutes until the cake is perfectly cooked. Let it cool. Only then take the cake out of the mold.
Serve.
strIngredient8: White food coloring, solution with 1 tsp warm water

strInstructions:
Cook coconut milk, sugar, salt and pandan leaf until boiling, turn off stove and let cool.
Put both flours into a large container, pour some of the coconut milk, stir gently then pour the rest of the coconut milk, stir again until evenly mixed, add liquid vanilla.
Then strain, divide the batter into two parts, add enough chili red food coloring to one part, stir well, add white food coloring to the other part, set aside.
Heat the steamer, insert the mold that has been thinly coated with oil, put in 1 tbsp of white batter (or adjust to the mold), steam for 3 minutes, pour again half a small soup ladle of red batter, steam again for 5 minutes, every time you want to pour the batter, it must be stirred first, repeat until the batter is finished, lastly steam for 15 minutes.
Red and white lapis is ready to be enjoyed.
strIngredient9: Chili red and dark red food coloring

strInstructions:
Prepare all ingredients. Grease the pan with a little vegetable oil
Put 3 sachets of instant coconut milk, salt, water and pandan leaves into a pot. Cook over medium heat while stirring continuously until you can smell the pandan leaves. After 10 minutes / boiling turn off the stove. Wait until the coconut milk is warm then divide into 2, each 500 ml
Prepare ingredients for the red batter and white batter
Put granulated sugar, rice flour and cornstarch into a container. Stir until evenly mixed. Pour the coconut milk little by little, stir well. Pour all the remaining coconut milk. Stir until evenly mixed
Strain the batter. Add liquid vanilla. Add chili red food coloring
Stir the batter until evenly mixed. Pour into the mold that has been greased with vegetable oil earlier up to half the height of the mold
Arrange the mold containing the red batter in a steamer pot where the water is already boiling. Steam for 10 minutes over medium tending to low heat. The pot lid must be wrapped with a clean cloth/napkin
While waiting for the red layer cake to cook mix granulated sugar, cornstarch, rice flour and vanilla. Add coconut milk, stir until evenly mixed. Pour all the remaining coconut milk, stir well
Strain the batter. The batter is ready to be molded
Top the red batter with the white batter. Steam again for 20 minutes
After 20 minutes the layer cake is perfectly cooked. Remove and wait until completely cool before taking it out of the mold
Alhamdulillah Red and White Lapis Cake is ready to be served
strIngredient5: Pandan leaves, if large 1 leaf is enough
strIngredient11: Drops chili red liquid food coloring

strInstructions:
WET INGREDIENTS 1A. Put coconut milk, granulated sugar, salt, and vanilla into a pot. 1B. Stir well, then cook over low heat while stirring continuously. 1C. After the sugar dissolves and the coconut milk starts to get hot, turn off the heat. No need to boil. 1D. Let it sit until the coconut milk is cool enough/room temperature.
2A. Put rice flour and tapioca flour into a container. 2B. Pour the coconut milk little by little while continuing to stir until the batter is smooth & not lumpy. 2C. If necessary, strain the batter so the cake is smoother. 2D. Divide the batter into 2 equal parts. Add pink food coloring to one part & purple to the other part. strMeal: Onde Onde Isi Kacang Hijau (Tanpa Gula) 🌹
strInstructions:
In a container, put glutinous rice flour, steamed potatoes, stevia and baking powder, stir with a spoon/spatula while pouring boiling water. Once the heat reduces, knead with your hands until it forms a dough that can be rolled. Weigh the dough @30 gr. Set aside
Prepare the filling that has been weighed @15 gr. Then take 1 part of the skin dough, flatten it, add filling then close, tidy up. Then roll in sesame seeds until the whole surface of the onde-onde is covered in sesame seeds. Do this until all the skin dough has been filled and covered in sesame seeds.

Fry the onde-onde in cooking oil that is not too hot yet, then fry over medium heat tending to low, fry while occasionally stirring until the whole surface of the onde-onde is cooked, remove then serve.

Prepare ingredients
How to cook lupis-style fluffy glutinous rice: Half-cook (aron) the glutinous rice, mix drained glutinous rice with coconut milk, pandan leaves. Half-cook (aron) in a wok using low heat while continuously stirring for 10-12 minutes until coconut milk is absorbed and glutinous rice is half cooked.
Steam the half-cooked (aron) glutinous rice in a boiling steamer for 25 minutes. Line with banana leaves.
Open the lid, pour the remaining 100 ml coconut milk, stir well. Steam again for 10-12 minutes until glutinous rice is shiny and fully cooked (tanak). Turn off heat, let sit for 10 minutes.
How to cook chicken filling. Sauté ground spices + bay leaves + lemongrass using oil until fragrant and cooked.
Add minced chicken, stir until it changes color and is somewhat dry.
Add salt, brown sugar, granulated sugar, coriander, broth powder. Stir well.
Pour coconut milk, cook using low heat while continuously stirring until coconut milk is dry and chicken is oily. Correct taste: it must be slightly saltier than normal taste (add salt if necessary).
Remove, let it cool first before using it for filling.
Mold in a 20x20 baking pan. Grease pan thinly with oil. Line with plastic wrap so it's easy to lift.
Take 2/3 glutinous rice, press using the back of a wet spoon until dense and even.
Sprinkle all chicken filling, flatten.
Cover with the remaining 1/3 glutinous rice, press again until tight and the surface is even.
Cover the lemper surface with plastic wrap, then press using another baking pan or a box-shaped container so it's denser and even. Important note: 1)If you want to bake it in the oven at 170°C, you must open all plastic wrap. Just thinly grease the pan with oil. 2)If using the steaming method, just open the top plastic wrap. The goal is so water vapor doesn't drip onto the lemper and make it soggy.
Bake in oven 170°C for 15-20 minutes or steam for 15 minutes. This makes the lemper more set and legit (chewy and sweet). If you don't have an oven, sun drying it for 30 minutes also works.
Cool the lemper for at least 1 hour at room temperature, or 30 minutes in the fridge until completely set. Then cut using a sharp knife lined with plastic wrap or thinly greased with oil. The cut results will be neat, not sticky, and won't fall apart.
Tips for Cutting Lemper Neatly: 1) Knife must be sharp and wet/oiled. Dip knife in warm water or thinly smear oil before cutting. Wipe again every 2-3 cuts. 2) Cut with one press, don't saw. Press knife straight down in one motion so the surface isn't jagged. 3) Use a ruler/measuring stick. Place a clean ruler on the lemper surface as a guide, so all cut sizes are the same. 4) 20x20 cm pan = 16 neat pieces. Divide into 4 columns x 4 rows, each piece 5x5 cm.

Lemper can be served directly. Pack beautifully as gifts/hampers or snackbox

Mix all ingredients besides glutinous rice. Stir and boil until boiling.
Add glutinous rice to the boiling coconut milk water. Keep stirring so it doesn't stick. Wait until all water is absorbed.
Turn off the stove and move to a steamer. Cook until half cooked.
Shape lemper and wrap with banana leaves. I made them too big like arem arem size
Steam lemper for about 20-30 minutes
strIngredient12: Meat floss (abon) or beef lemper filling meat

strInstructions:
Soak glutinous rice, then steam for about 5 minutes (make sure the result is not too soft) set aside
Heat coconut milk, add salt, bay leaves, lime leaves and crushed lemongrass
After coconut milk boils add the steamed glutinous rice, let it reduce and become dry
Prepare banana leaves, take some steamed glutinous rice then fill with beef floss. Roll then arrange on the steamer
Steam for 20 minutes.
Can be eaten directly, or can also be grilled first before serving....

Boil Chicken for 15 minutes. Drain, shred / cut into small pieces.
Sauté spices, until fragrant and boiling.
Add shredded chicken, cook until spices are absorbed.
Store in a closed container in the fridge.

Prepare glutinous rice and coconut serundeng. Prepare banana leaves, cut banana leaves into small pieces, fill with glutinous rice and serundeng. Then wrap the lemper into an elongated shape after that lock with a stapler. Nb: If you have small children, avoid using a stapler to be safer. The solution is to replace it with a toothpick or if you can, fold the leaf using a certain technique so the lemper is wrapped well.
Next, heat the teflon pan. Grill all the lemper until the lemper releases a fragrant aroma and the banana leaves turn brownish. If it's done, turn off the stove.
Move the lemper to a plate.
The super delicious coconut serundeng filled lemper is ready to be enjoyed wholeheartedly🌟✨☀
Seriously, this lemper is very delicious💖💖
strIngredient2: Coconut serundeng/sarundeng super delicious coconut serundeng
strIngredient3: Banana leaves that have been boiled/wilted and washed clean

strInstructions:
Prepare ingredients. Wash glutinous rice, place into Rice Cooker, add pandan leaves, bay leaves and salt, Kara coconut milk and water. Cook like cooking rice, wait until cooked. Remove glutinous rice from Rice cooker. Place in a 20x10 Cm baking pan lined with plastic. Add beef floss topping. Cover with glutinous rice, press while flattening.
Wait until cool, place on a cutting board.. cut according to taste. Wrap with banana leaves
Serve. Thank you 🙏

Mash the purple sweet potato then mix with all ingredients except coconut milk, stir until evenly mixed, pour coconut milk little by little²
While stirring until dissolved and there are no lumps. Cover the batter and let it sit for 60 minutes. After that
Heat a concave teflon pan if available over low heat, I used a pan with four holes, smear with oil then pour the batter until full or almost full, let it be until its pores come out then cover and cook until done (the surface is dry)
Remove and cook until finished, set aside.
Make brown sugar kinca sauce, mix in a pot, shaved brown sugar, coconut milk and pandan leaves then cook until sugar dissolves and boils, then pour cornstarch solution, stir and cook until thick and bubbling², remove and let it be warm or cold
Serve purple sweet potato serabi with brown sugar kinca sauce.... Hmmm... Yummy, sweet, legit (chewy sweet) and soft

Mix all ingredients, stir briefly. Let it sit for 30 minutes
Heat teflon. Pour a little bit at a time onto the teflon. Once holes appear, flip it for just a moment.
Remove and place on a serving plate

Make brown sugar kinca sauce. Boil coconut milk, brown sugar, pandan leaves, and salt
Boil coconut milk with pandan leaves. Let it be until warm.
Rice flour, glutinous rice flour, salt, vanilla mixed together. Pour warm coconut milk gradually while stirring until getting a thick batter.
Stir batter until smooth, slick and light. Add instant yeast and remaining coconut milk
Stir until batter is evenly mixed. Cover batter and wait until it rises. Characterized by batter rising and foaming.
Open batter cover and stir to release formed gas. Move to a measuring cup to make it easier to pour batter into mold.
Heat mold and thinly smear with margarine. Pour batter into mold not completely full. Bake until cooked.
Cooked sambareh remove and ready to be enjoyed with brown sugar kinca sauce.

Make serabi batter first. Prepare ingredients. in a container put wheat flour, rice flour, sugar and salt. Stir well.
Add instant yeast. Whisk well. Add other ingredients including liquid ingredients. Whisk everything well until smooth and not lumpy. Let it be for 30 mins - 1 hr.
While waiting make kinca sauce. Mix Rose Brand Coconut Milk, plain water and salt together. Stir well.
Pour this mixture into a pot. Add brown sugar and pandan leaves. Cook while stirring until boiling.
Add cornstarch solution. Stir well until slightly thickened. Turn off stove. Move kinca sauce to another container. Set aside
After 30 minutes the batter has risen. Stir well. Divide the batter into two give coloring/paste according to taste.
Heat teflon. Use medium tending to low heat. Pour batter into teflon using a soup ladle. Cook until holes appear on the surface. Serabi doesn't need to be flipped.
Do this until batter is finished.
Serve Surabi with Kinca sauce. Really delicious.
strIngredient11: A few drops of pandan paste
strIngredient12: A few drops of strawberry paste

strInstructions:
Weigh and prepare all ingredients to be used
In a container mix All-purpose Flour, instant yeast and baking powder. Add Egg. Pour Coconut Milk little by little, stir with a whisk until smooth. Add Moringa leaf powder and Pandan flavor, stir until even.
Then rest the batter for 60 minutes
After fermentation, the batter is ready to be molded in an iron wok which has previously been heated. Cook over low heat until the batter has many pores. After the surface is dry, remove
Arrange in a wide container
Kinca Sauce: Cook water, granulated sugar, brown sugar, salt and vanilla until sugar dissolves. Add Coconut Milk, stir² don't let Coconut Milk curdle. Add Durian/ Jackfruit, cook until boiling. Turn off heat, let it cool
Serve Serabi with Kinca sauce 💚💚🌿🌿
Hmmm... Delicious amazing!! 😍😍👏🏻👏🏻

In a container, put egg, salt, Rose Brand Coconut Milk, and water. Stir until the egg is frothy. Only then add wheat flour and baking powder while sifting.
Stir the batter gently until evenly mixed and there are no lumps, if necessary it can be strained.
Then let the batter sit for at least 30 minutes, until bubbles appear in the batter. Smear the pan with a little oil, leave it until the pan or mold is really hot, I use medium heat. Only then pour 1 soup ladle of batter or more if you want it thicker, leave it until bubbles appear, cover briefly until the surface is dry. Remove then set aside.
I added pandan flavor to the remaining batter. Mold the batter until finished.
Making Brown Sugar Sauce: In a pot put Rose Brand Granulated Sugar, brown sugar, salt, pandan leaves, water, and a little coconut milk, Stir well. Cook until sugar dissolves and boils. Keep stirring until water reduces.
After water reduces, move the brown sugar sauce to a bowl or container, after cooling the brown sugar sauce will thicken if the water really reduced when cooked. If you want it more liquid, the brown sugar sauce doesn't need to be cooked until the water reduces, just until the sugar dissolves and the water boils. Serabi is ready to be eaten with a drizzle of brown sugar sauce, very delicious.
strIngredient6: White food coloring powder, dissolve with 1 tbsp water
strIngredient11: Water, can be added if you want it more liquid
strIngredient12: Rose brand coconut milk, can be added if you want the sauce to be milk chocolate colored
strIngredient13: Pandan leaves, tied in a knot

strInstructions:
Mix Wheat Flour, Rice Flour, Granulated Sugar, salt and Baking powder. Stir well.
Then add Yeast, stir again. After that, add egg.
Also add coconut milk, and stir with a whisk until everything is evenly mixed. Then let the batter sit for 30-1 hour.
While waiting for the batter to rest. Cook the kinca sauce. Mix water, coconut milk, Brown Sugar, Pandan leaves and salt.
Stir well, and cook coconut milk until boiling and sugar dissolves.
After the sauce boils, add cornstarch solution while stirring. And cook the sauce briefly just until slightly thickened.
After the batter has rested, stir the serabi batter. Then divide the batter into two parts. And give each red and white food coloring.
After that cook red and white serabi until done.

Mix together serabi ingredients except coconut milk and food coloring
Pour coconut milk little by little, until batter is evenly mixed, strain, then cover let sit for 15-30 mins
After 30 minutes stir batter then divide into two, one part is given chili red food coloring
Cook in non-stick teflon pan with low heat, until batter runs out
Mix together Kinca sauce ingredients, except cornstarch, Cook until boiling
Then add cornstarch that has been dissolved with a little water, cook until kinca sauce thickens
Merdeka Serabi with kinca sauce ready to be enjoyed😀

Mix all ingredients 1 in a blender, then blend until smooth... Pour into a container, set aside
Mix ingredients 2 in a container,.. Stir until everything is evenly mixed
Heat the takoyaki pan over low heat, grease thinly with oil... pour the batter until ¾ of the mold's height,... Let it sit until, small holes form in the batter
Then pour batter 2 until the mold is full,.....cover the mold and cook until the cake's surface is cooked ± 3 minutes
strIngredient9: Cooking oil for greasing the mold

strInstructions:
Put all ingredients A into a container, stir well, set aside
Put all ingredients B, water, grated coconut and Rose Brand Instant Coconut Milk into a pot, boil until bubbling, turn off the heat, let it cool.
Add ingredients B to the batter A, stir until evenly mixed, cover tightly, let sit for up to 1 hour
While waiting for the serabi batter, let's make oncom sambal for the topping. First, cut the oncom into pieces. Pour enough Rose Brand cooking oil into the pan, fry the oncom until cooked and brownish, remove
Roughly crush the fried oncom, set aside
Puree the chilies, duo of onions (shallots and garlic), and kencur, pour a little Rose Brand cooking oil into the pan, add the ground spices, sauté until fragrant and cooked
Add oncom, stir well, add salt, Rose Brand Granulated Sugar and Asatu Rose Brand MSG, cook until done. Set aside
Heat the mold, grease with Rose Brand Margarine.
Pour the serabi batter into the mold, wait until half cooked then add the oncom topping, cover until cooked
Serve this Bandung oncom serabi with tea or coffee, very suitable for guests, also as a business idea.
strIngredient8: Grated coconut from slightly young coconut

strInstructions:
Mix rice flour, salt, and 500 ml water, stir well.
Add 500 ml coconut milk, stir until dissolved.
Add 500 ml warm water, stir quickly until the batter is smooth.
Heat a teflon pan, grease with butter.
Pour 1 ladle of batter into the pan, cook until done.
Remove and serve on banana leaves, pierce with a toothpick if necessary.

Prepare the ingredients for making jackfruit kinca serabi. Wash the pandan leaves and drain. Next is the process of cooking the jackfruit kinca. Prepare a pot, add water, brown sugar, salt, granulated sugar and pandan leaves. Cook until it boils. Next, add the thickener solution, stir. Lastly, add the coconut milk. Stir until even. Correct the taste. If it's right and cooked, turn off the stove. Put some of the jackfruit kinca in a bowl.
Prepare a basin. Add rice flour, baking soda, coconut milk, liquid milk, salt, granulated sugar and water. Stir.
Strain the serabi batter. Then add cooking oil and green food coloring. Stir until even. Cover and let the batter sit for about 30-60 minutes.
Heat the pan until hot using medium tending to low heat. Pour the batter into the pan, wait until the batter produces bubbles and changes color. If so, remove. Do this process until finished (until the batter is all cooked).
Place the serabi on a plate.
Add the jackfruit kinca in the middle.
Serve.
The seriously delicious jackfruit kinca serabi is ready to be enjoyed wholeheartedly🌟✨🌞
strIngredient3: Baking soda (you can use fermipan / instant yeast. I only had baking soda at home, if you have it, it's better to use instant yeast)
strIngredient9: Green food coloring (about 2-3 drops. I used too little coloring, if you want more color, add more)
strIngredient10: Cooking oil (initially wanted to use melted margarine, but I replaced it with oil)

strInstructions:
Prepare Grated Dry Tempeh and activate the yeast: mix instant yeast, wheat flour and warm water, stir well. Rest for 5 minutes, until frothy.
Mix dry and wet ingredients, stir well. Add the activated yeast, stir well. Cover with plastic wrap and rest for 30 minutes.
The batter has risen and is frothy. Stir slowly
Heat the serabi mold, turn down the stove and pour 1.5 ladles of batter, just 3/4 of the mold's height. After 2 minutes, sprinkle the tempeh. Cover the mold and cook again for 3 minutes until cooked.
Serve for a savory snack.
strIngredient1: Grated dry tempeh grated dry tempeh

strInstructions:
Blend the banana and coconut milk until smooth, set aside
In a container, mix wheat flour, granulated sugar, egg and instant yeast, then pour the blended banana little by little while stirring until evenly mixed.
Add salt, stir until evenly mixed then cover and let the batter sit for ±1 hour
After 1 hour, mix baking powder and a little water, then pour into the batter, stir evenly again (for me, I mix the baking powder at once with the wheat flour)
Heat the teflon then pour the batter, cook until done. Remove
Add filling then roll
Serve 🥰

Coconut milk broth: cook the coconut milk until it boils over low heat, let it cool first
For the filling, mix rice flour, tapioca flour and wheat flour. Add the egg, then stir while pouring the coconut milk which has started to cool. Stir the batter evenly until it all dissolves, cover and let sit for about 2 hours.
Coconut milk areh: cook the coconut milk areh briefly until it boils while stirring continuously, let it cool to room temperature.
How to make serabi: after the batter has rested for 2 hours, stir well. Take 1 ladle of batter for the motif, place it in a bowl and add pandan flavor, stir well.
Prepare a round teflon mold, heat over medium heat then pour 1 ladle of the filling batter, then press slightly or rotate the teflon so a hollow edge is formed.
Put in the pandan colored batter. Add pieces of jackfruit or banana then cover the batter, cook so it's half done, then give a little drizzle of coconut milk areh on top of the batter.
Cover and cook until done, remove and arrange the serabi on a plate, serve.

Mix all ingredients, add coconut milk little by little, stir well and strain, cover and let sit for 1 hour
After 1 hour, stir the batter, then cook with a hot teflon pan over low heat, if it has formed holes, cover, and do not flip
Cook the kinca sauce, bring to a boil and strain ready to be served

In a bowl mix rice flour, wheat flour, granulated sugar, salt, Rose Brand Coconut Milk, and water. Stir until even, I beat it while stirring so there are no lumps.
After the batter is evenly mixed and smooth, add instant yeast, stir evenly again, then cover the batter with a napkin and let it sit for 30 minutes, for me it was 1 hour 25 minutes because I left it to do something else.
After letting it sit, bubbles will appear in the batter, a sign that the yeast is active. Stir with a ladle to break the bubbles. Pour one ladle onto a teflon pan that has been smeared with a thin layer of oil using a tissue.
Cook until the surface forms holes, then cover when there is only a little wet surface left. Cook until done. Remove, keep on a plate. Repeat until the batter runs out.
Kinca Sauce: before turning on the stove Mix brown sugar, granulated sugar, coconut milk, water, and salt in a pot, stir well. Then turn on the stove.
After the sugar dissolves, correct the taste. Then cook until it boils, turn off the heat. Continue stirring so the coconut milk doesn't curdle. Then pour it over the serabi.
Serabi Kocor is ready to be served. It's so delicious, the sauce seeps into the serabi's holes 😍
strIngredient5: Rose brand coconut milk mixed with 85ml water

strInstructions:
Mix starter ingredients, let it sit for 15 minutes. If after 15 minutes the yeast foams, it means it's still active.
KINCA SAUCE : Measure 100 ml of Rose Brand coconut milk then mix all ingredients, cook until boiling, set aside.
SERABI : Put dry ingredients in a container, pour 1 pack 200 ml Rose Brand Coconut Milk and warm water, stir well.
Pour the starter, stir well
Cover the batter and let it sit for at least 30 minutes
After 30 minutes stir well then divide into several parts and add coloring according to taste.
Heat the mold, pour 2 ladles (50 ml), let it form pores then cover and cook over low heat until done.
Do this until the batter runs out.
Arrange serabi on a serving plate and ready to be served with kinca sauce.
strIngredient17: Kinca (25 gr gula merah +50 ml air, masak sampai gula larut lalu saring)

strInstructions:
Prepare ingredients and a wok or serabi mold. I used a kue lumpur (mud cake) mold.
Pandan Serabi : mix all dry ingredients, stir well. Add egg and coconut milk, stir until everything is homogeneous.
Strain so there are no lumps in the batter. Add pandan paste, stir well. Let it sit covered for 1 hour.
After 1 hour, stir the batter again. Heat the pan or non-stick wok. I used a mold with 7 circles, so it finishes quickly 😁. Once the mold is hot, smear with a little oil, pour the batter.
Let it sit until the surface forms holes, then cover the mold, cook until done. Don't flip it. Remove. Continue until finished.
Kinca sauce: mix all ingredients together in a pot, stir well. Cook on the stove over medium heat until boiling. Remove and strain.
Serving: place Pandan Serabi on a serving plate, add kinca sauce. Yummyyyy…
strIngredient8: Pack of 65ml rose brand coconut milk
strIngredient11: Pack of 65ml rose brand coconut milk

strInstructions:
For petulo, cook and mix all ingredients together except tapioca and food coloring, cook until the batter is not sticky, if so sprinkle with tapioca stir well then add coloring and mold, steam for about 10 minutes
For serabi, mix all ingredients together, stir while pouring coconut milk slowly until even, after that let it sit for about 30 minutes, and mold on a teflon without any greasing wait until cooked with low heat
For the sauce, mix sugar and salt also pandan leaves, pour coconut milk and add Cap Enaak Sweetened Condensed Milk Stir well and cook over low heat until done
Serve Petulo serabi with savory creamy sauce
strIngredient8: Drops of green and yellow food coloring

strInstructions:
Mix serabi ingredients (rice flour, grated coconut and yeast, except salt). Stir evenly.
Add warm coconut milk and stir evenly. Cover the basin and let it sit for 1 hour.
Pour the batter onto a pan that has been thinly smeared with oil. Cover the pan until the serabi is cooked. Use medium heat tending to low. Do this until the batter runs out.
Cook the brown sugar sauce until it boils. Strain so there is no dirt (from the brown sugar). Serve serabi with brown sugar sauce. Hmm... yummy 😋🤩
strIngredient3: Rose brand coconut milk + 385 ml warm water
strIngredient10: Rose brand coconut milk + 685 ml water

strInstructions:
Mix wheat flour and rice flour, sugar, yeast, salt, egg, coconut milk, milk powder, and water. Stir until evenly mixed
Let the batter sit for at least 30 minutes, cover with a clean cloth (I let it sit for 1 hour). After 1 hour stir the batter
Divide the batter into 2 parts. Add purple food coloring to 1/3 part, leave 2/3 part plain. If the white batter has been cooked for 7 mold holes, add light green food coloring
Heat the serabi mold, pour the batter, put banana and jackfruit pieces on top. Cover and cook over low heat until done, arrange on a serving plate
Cook the kinca sauce by boiling coconut milk, powdered palm sugar, water, granulated sugar, pandan leaves, cornstarch, and salt until dissolved and cooked. Once cooked, pour into a serving bowl
Add Cap Enaak Chocolate Sweetened Condensed Milk, stir until evenly mixed
Serve three-colored serabi with warm kinca sauce
strIngredient11: Drops of light green food coloring

strInstructions:
Mix all dry ingredients, set aside. Add egg + Cap Enaak Sweetened Condensed Milk, and liquid ingredients. Stir evenly with a balloon whisk. Let it sit for 10-20 minutes
Heat a pan, put 1 ladle of batter into the pan. Wait until it forms holes, remove. Do this until the batter is finished (you can add food coloring as you like)
Mix coconut milk water with Cap Enaak Sweetened Condensed Milk + salt + sugar + pandan leaf. Bring to a boil and keep stirring. Test taste and ready to be enjoyed with family😘❤️👍 (you can add durian topping if you like😘)

Activate yeast, mix yeast ingredients, stir well. Rest for 5 minutes until frothy.
Mix dry ingredients and wet ingredients, stir well. Add yeast, stir well. Cover with plastic wrap and rest the batter for 30 minutes.
After the batter rises and becomes frothy, stir gently.
Heat the serabi cake mold, turn down the stove. Pour 1.5 ladles into each mold hole. Cook for 2 minutes, cover the mold and continue cooking for another 3 minutes until done.
Keep on a plate.
Make kinca sauce, mix kinca sauce ingredients, cook until sugar dissolves, add thickener, cook until boiling.
Serve.

Prepare ingredients. Activate yeast: mix yeast with warm water and sugar. Stir well, wait until frothy. Sift in ingredients: wheat flour, rice flour, salt, and baking powder. Stir well. Add yeast solution, coconut milk, water, and granulated sugar. Stir using a whisk until there are no lumps.
Divide the batter into two equal parts. Add drops of red food coloring and green pandan paste. Make sure the colors are soft because the colors will turn darker when baked. Stir well until homogeneous and the color is even.
Heat teflon, take one ladle of batter and pour carefully so the shape is nice. Wait until it's cooked and forms holes. Make sure the entire surface is porous, then carefully remove using a spatula. Do this for both colors until the batter runs out.
After finishing, arrange the serabi on a serving plate then set aside. Make the sauce: mix all sauce ingredients, cook until boiling. Add cornstarch solution, stir well. Serve serabi with palm sugar sauce. Good luck trying and happy breaking the fast.
Tips for beautiful porous serabi: use non-stick teflon, no oil, and do not cover. Keep heat at medium low. Once it forms holes, the teflon can be lifted slightly so it doesn't burn but still forms holes evenly.

Prepare ingredients.
Soak glutinous rice in warm water for at least 30 minutes (30-60 minutes) then drain. Steam for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally, then transfer to a basin.
Dissolve 1 sachet of Creamy Matcha Sweetened Condensed Milk with 150 ml of boiling water. Pour into the steamed rice while stirring until evenly mixed.
Cover and let sit for 15-30 minutes until the water is completely absorbed.
Steam again for 15-20 minutes.
Dissolve 2 sachets of Indomilk Creamy Matcha Sweetened Condensed Milk with 150 ml water in a wok, add 2 tbsp cooking oil. Turn on the heat, let it boil then add the completely steamed glutinous rice.
Stir while cooking over low heat until the liquid is gone. Mold in a baking pan lined with plastic.
Wait until cool then cut into pieces and serve.
strIngredient2: Creamy matcha sweetened condensed milk + 150 ml water for half-cooking (aron)
strIngredient3: Indomilk creamy matcha sweetened condensed milk + 150 ml water for cooking

strInstructions:
Wash white glutinous rice thoroughly, soak for 2 hours then drain and steam for about 40 minutes. At minute 15, sprinkle the glutinous rice with some hot water, then at minute 30 pour the remaining hot water (try to use just boiled water) stir well and continue steaming until cooked, turn off and set aside
Blend pandan and suji leaves with water (adjust to the pandan)
Cook thick coconut milk, granulated sugar and salt
Add pandan water and a few drops of green food coloring, stir well, do not let the coconut milk curdle, then cook until boiling
After evenly mixed, reduce stove heat then add steamed glutinous rice, keep stirring continuously until even and smooth/pliable (kalis)
After pliable (coconut milk reduced and not burnt). Prepare a baking pan lined with plastic and smeared with vegetable oil, pour wajik mixture flatten first and press until dense
After all pans are full, let it be until the hot steam disappears (3 hours) and flip the wajik and it's ready to be decorated.

Prepare all ingredients.
Break the rice vermicelli and soak with hot water. After expanding, drain.
Shave the brown sugar. Mix Kara coconut milk with water.
Boil brown sugar, coconut milk, and pandan until boiling and brown sugar dissolves.
Add corn vermicelli and stir. Cook until the water reduces.
Let it cool. Once cold, discard the pandan leaves. Add tapioca flour gradually and stir until evenly mixed.
Transfer to a baking pan that has been greased with oil or margarine. Flatten the surface while pressing. Then steam for about 20-25 minutes or until cooked.
Vermicelli wajik is cooked. Wait until it cools down and take it out of the pan and it can be cut into pieces to enjoy with warm tea or coffee.

Boil the thin coconut milk with the salt, then remove from the heat and set aside. Drain the glutinous rice and steam for 15 minutes. Pour the coconut milk over the steamed rice and mix well. Let it sit briefly until the coconut milk is absorbed. Steam again for 25 minutes, or until cooked, then set aside. Boil the thick coconut milk with the palm sugar and granulated sugar until dissolved. Remove from the heat and strain. Transfer the mixture to a nonstick pan and cook until the sugar syrup thickens. Add the steamed glutinous rice and stir continuously until the syrup is absorbed and the mixture becomes dry. Transfer to a tray lined with banana leaves or plastic. Let cool, cut as desired, and serve.

Soak the white glutinous rice for about 1 hour, then wash and drain it. Steam for about 5 minutes. Remove and mix evenly with 200 ml of coconut milk and water, then steam for another 10 minutes. Bring the remaining coconut milk to a boil with the sugar, salt, vanilla powder, and Indonesian bay leaves, stirring well. After it has boiled briefly, add the rice and mix. When the coconut milk begins to be absorbed and the mixture starts to set, add the margarine and mix until fully set. Divide the rice into two portions. Add a few drops of red food coloring to one portion. Grease a mold with margarine or cooking oil. Press the white wajik mixture into the bottom of the mold, then add the red mixture on top, leveling and pressing it down. Let cool. Cut the red-and-white wajik as desired. For snack boxes or selling, it can be packed in plastic containers or OPP bags. Serve. It can also be shaped into a cone for a tumpeng-style presentation.

Wash the glutinous rice, soak for 2 hours, and drain. Add 250 ml of coconut milk, salt, and 2 pandan leaves. Add the rice and cook, stirring, until the coconut milk has been absorbed. Stir the rice. In a separate pan, combine coconut milk, palm sugar, granulated sugar, and pandan leaves. Cook until the sugar dissolves, then strain. Pour the sugar syrup into a nonstick pan, add the glutinous rice, and cook over medium heat while stirring. Continue cooking until the mixture becomes thick and sticky, like dodol. Lightly grease a tray with oil, add the hot wajik, and press it down. Let cool and set, then cut as desired.

Soak the glutinous rice for 2 hours. Drain and steam for 30 minutes. Cook the coconut milk, palm sugar, salt, and cinnamon with the pandan leaves. Stir until the sugar dissolves and the mixture boils, then reduce the heat. Add the steamed glutinous rice and mix until evenly combined. Lightly grease a mold with cooking oil and line it with banana leaves or plastic. Press the mixture firmly into the mold. Let cool until set; refrigerating overnight is an option. Cut the wajik as desired. Enjoy!
strIngredient1: White glutinous rice, soaked for 2 hours

strInstructions: Prepare the ingredients. Wash the glutinous rice and drain it. Heat the steamer. Once steam rises, steam the rice with the pandan leaves for about 20 minutes, stirring occasionally for even cooking. Meanwhile, bring 300 ml of water to a boil. After 20 minutes, transfer the rice to a bowl, pour in the boiling water, add salt, and mix until the water is absorbed. Steam for another 20 minutes, stirring occasionally. In a nonstick pan, combine palm sugar, coconut milk, pandan leaves, and kaffir lime leaves. Heat until the sugar dissolves, then strain the syrup. Bring the syrup to a boil again, then reduce the heat. Add the rice and cook over low heat, stirring continuously to prevent burning, until the rice is fully cooked, cohesive, and no longer sticks to the pan. Transfer the mixture to a tray or mold lined with banana leaves or heat-resistant plastic. Press it down firmly and let cool. Once cool, remove from the mold, cut as desired, and serve.

Soak the glutinous rice in water for 4 hours. Wash and drain. Steam the rice on a bed of pandan leaves for 40 minutes over medium heat. Squeeze the grated coconut with water to make coconut milk, then strain. In a heatproof bowl, combine the sugar, salt, and coconut milk a little at a time. Add the steamed rice and mix until the coconut milk is evenly distributed. Steam the rice mixture again on pandan leaves for 45 minutes over medium heat. Steam the palm sugar, pandan leaves, and coconut water over low heat until the sugar melts. In a wok, add the cooked rice mixture. Strain the hot palm sugar syrup into the rice a little at a time, stirring over low heat until evenly combined. Add granulated sugar if you want it sweeter, then mix well. Line a 26 × 26 cm tray with clear plastic. Transfer the rice mixture to the tray and press it flat using hands covered with plastic. Leave for about 4 hours, or until cool. The wajik is ready to eat.

Cook the soaked, washed glutinous rice until fully cooked. Dry-roast the cleaned grated coconut, keeping it light in color. In a clean pan, combine the granulated sugar and vanilla. Add the unflavored gelatin powder and water, then cook until the sugar dissolves and the mixture thickens. Add the cooked steamed glutinous rice and mix well. Add the toasted grated coconut and stir until evenly combined. Continue cooking, stirring constantly, until the liquid evaporates and the mixture becomes thick, glossy, oily, and caramel-like. Let it cool until slightly warm, then wrap in colorful waxed paper. Allow to air-dry before packing in a container. These make nice gifts for relatives.

Wash the glutinous rice thoroughly and soak it; the longer the better. The author soaked it for 5 hours. Drain the rice and bring water to a boil in a steamer. Steam the rice for 30 minutes. Once the rice has started to expand, turn off the heat. Prepare the remaining ingredients. Heat 200 ml of coconut milk in a pot. Once it boils, add the rice and stir until the coconut milk is absorbed. The rice will be partially cooked. Add the remaining 300 ml of coconut milk, palm sugar, granulated sugar, and pandan leaves. Heat until nearly boiling, then add salt and ground cinnamon. Add the glutinous rice and cook over low heat, stirring continuously until the syrup reduces and the rice becomes fully cooked and less wet. The rice will change from light brown to dark brown as it absorbs the syrup. Remove the pandan leaves. Transfer to a tray lined with banana leaves and lightly greased with cooking oil. Press the mixture down until firm and level. Let cool, then remove from the tray. Cut into diamond shapes and serve.
strIngredient2: Palm sugar, sliced to help it dissolve
strIngredient10: Banana leaves for lining the tray
strIngredient11: Cooking oil, for greasing the leaves

strInstructions: Prepare the ingredients. Soak the glutinous rice for about 1–2 hours. Steam until cooked, then set aside. Pour 300 ml of water into a pan and add the Kara coconut milk, pandan leaf, palm sugar, and salt. Cook until the mixture forms a caramel-like syrup. Add the cooked glutinous rice and stir until thoroughly combined and cooked; it should no longer stick to the spoon. Turn off the heat. Transfer to a mold or tray lined with banana leaves. Let cool before cutting. The author used a kue lumpang mold to make serving easier. Serve with warm unsweetened tea or black coffee.

Soak the glutinous rice for at least 1 hour. Put the rice in a pan, add coconut milk, and cook while stirring to prevent burning until the liquid reduces. Steam for about 20 minutes. For the green layer, combine granulated sugar, coconut milk, and pandan paste in a pan. Cook until the sugar dissolves, then add half of the rice. Stir until the liquid reduces and the rice is fully cooked and cohesive. Transfer to a 20 × 20 cm tray lined with baking paper or plastic lightly greased with oil. Spread and press firmly. For the brown layer, combine coconut milk, palm sugar, and a pinch of salt in a pan. Cook until the sugar dissolves, add the remaining rice, and stir until the liquid reduces and the rice is fully cooked and cohesive. Spread over the green layer and press firmly. Let cool and set, then remove from the tray, cut, shape as desired, and serve.

Soak the glutinous rice for a while and prepare the jackfruit. Finely chop the palm sugar and combine it with salt and instant coconut milk. Add water and cook, stirring, until boiling. Add Fiber Creme, then remove from the heat and strain to remove any impurities from the sugar. Cut the jackfruit into small pieces. Steam the glutinous rice until cooked, about 20 minutes. While waiting for the rice, bring the palm sugar syrup back to a boil. Add the cooked rice and stir until combined. When the liquid has reduced, add the chopped jackfruit and continue stirring until the mixture is dry. Transfer to a tray lined with banana leaves and press firmly. Let cool, cut as desired, and serve.

First, clean the glutinous rice and soak it overnight. Steam the rice until half-cooked, placing a knotted pandan leaf underneath it. When the rice is halfway cooked, sprinkle it with boiling water and steam again until cooked. Remove and set aside. Cook the thin coconut milk with granulated sugar, palm sugar, salt, and pandan leaves, stirring until the mixture boils and is evenly combined. Add the steamed rice. Since the original pot was too small, transfer everything to a larger wok for easier stirring. Continue stirring until the coconut milk and palm sugar syrup have reduced and the rice no longer sticks to the wok. Lightly grease a tray with cooking oil, transfer the rice mixture, and press it neatly and firmly into the corners. Leave the wajik for a day or until completely cool. Once cool, cut as desired.

strMeal: Wajik Kemerdekaan (Wajik Gula Pasir Warna Merah Putih)
strInstructions: First, pray and wash your hands. Prepare the ingredients. Rinse the glutinous rice according to the package instructions and steam for 25 minutes, then set aside. Bring the coconut milk to a boil while stirring, then add the rice and mix evenly (a process called aron). Steam again until fully cooked, about 30 minutes. Divide the cooked rice into two portions; the author made the red portion larger. Set aside. For the red wajik, boil the red-layer ingredients until bubbling and slightly reduced. Add one portion of the rice and stir until all the liquid has evaporated and the texture is fairly dry, not mushy. Turn off the heat. Grease a pie pan with oil and press the red mixture into the base. For the white wajik, boil the white-layer ingredients until bubbling and reduced, then add the remaining rice. Stir until dry and not too soft. Place it over the red layer and smooth the surface. Decorate with any remaining mixture and leave until set. The red-and-white wajik is ready to enjoy. Notes: If the steamed rice is still only partially cooked, sprinkle it with hot water or coconut milk while steaming. Adjust the sugar to your preferred sweetness. You can add 1 tablespoon of cooking oil while mixing the rice into the coconut milk syrup.
strIngredient7: Pandan leaf, tied into a knot
strIngredient14: Pandan leaf, tied into a knot

strInstructions: Wash and soak the glutinous rice for about 1 hour, then steam for 5 minutes. Remove. Cook the coconut milk, water, salt, sugar, Indonesian bay leaf, and kaffir lime leaf. Once boiling, add the steamed rice and stir until the mixture sets. Add a little fresh cooking oil, about 1 tablespoon, and mix well. Divide the mixture into two equal portions and set one aside. Cook the portion remaining in the pan over low heat until fully cooked and smooth, then pound it with a pestle and set aside. Put the other portion into the pan, add red food coloring, and cook until smooth and fully cooked. Pound it with a pestle as well. While still warm, press the mixtures into molds lightly greased with oil to prevent sticking. Serve. This can also be made for selling. Red and white, hooray for independence!

In a pan, combine the glutinous rice, coconut milk, salt, and pandan leaves. Mix well and cook until the liquid is absorbed. Steam the rice for another 15 minutes, then set aside. In a pan, combine all the sugar-sauce ingredients except the jackfruit. Cook until the sugar thickens, then add the rice and jackfruit. Continue cooking and stirring until the rice is cohesive and no longer sticky. Transfer to a tray lined with plastic or banana leaves. Press the rice firmly. Let sit for at least 2 hours, then cut and serve.
strIngredient1: Glutinous rice, washed, soaked for 2 hours, and drained

strInstructions: Soak the glutinous rice for at least 2 hours, then steam until half-cooked. When the rice is nearly ready, boil 200 ml of coconut milk with 1/2–1 teaspoon of salt. Boil the coconut milk just before removing the rice from the steamer so it is hot when poured over the rice. Transfer the half-cooked rice to a bowl and pour the hot coconut milk over it. Let the liquid soak in; the rice will expand. Once absorbed, return the rice to the steamer and steam for another 30–45 minutes until cooked. Transfer to another container. In a nonstick pan, cook 400 ml of coconut milk with granulated sugar, pandan leaf, pandan paste, and light-green food coloring, stirring continuously until boiling. Continue cooking until the coconut milk thickens and reduces. Add the rice and cook over medium-low heat, stirring until the rice is cohesive and no longer sticks to the pan. Line a tray with banana leaves, including the sides, and grease with cooking oil. Spread the wajik evenly and press it firmly. To prevent the surface from drying out, cover it with leaves. Steam will condense on the cover; wipe it dry and cover again. Repeat whenever the cover becomes wet. If made at night, the wajik can usually be cut the next morning once fully set, or after several hours. Remove from the tray and cut as desired, using a plastic scraper to prevent sticking.

Cook the main ingredients over low heat, stirring until done; alternatively, cook them in a rice cooker until done, then stir briefly. Bring the sugar-and-pandan ingredients to a boil and strain. Combine the sugar mixture with the cooked glutinous rice. Cook over low heat for 20 minutes, stirring until the oil from the coconut milk comes out. Press into molds, let cool, and cut as desired.
strIngredient1: Glutinous rice, soaked in hot water for 15 minutes
strIngredient5: Sugar mixture / can be replaced with pandan flavoring
strIngredient9: Add 50 ml pandan paste for pandan flavor, if desired

strInstructions: Steam the sweet potatoes and young coconut for 20 minutes. Slice the palm sugar. Mash the steamed sweet potatoes. Once smooth, mix in the sliced palm sugar. Coat the getuk with the steamed young coconut. Done.

Prepare the ingredients. For the grated coconut topping, mix the grated coconut with salt, place a pandan leaf on top, and steam for 10 minutes. The author used leftover sweet potatoes from the refrigerator and steamed them briefly to make them easier to mash. Mash the Cilembu sweet potatoes while hot, then mix with margarine, salt, and granulated sugar. Do the same with the purple sweet potatoes. Lightly grease a flower-shaped mold with oil. Layer or alternate the purple and Cilembu sweet potato mixtures to create a two-color effect. Press gently, then remove from the mold. Arrange the flower-shaped getuk on a serving plate and sprinkle with savory grated coconut.

Peel the cassava, cut it into pieces, wash thoroughly, and steam until tender. About 5 minutes before the cassava is done, place the grated coconut in a bowl with salt and a pandan leaf and steam it as well. Remove everything from the steamer. Transfer the cassava to a plate, add salt, sugar, and vanilla, then mash and mix well. Divide into three portions. Add food coloring as desired; the author used red, purple, and yellow and reserved a little mixture for flower details. Shape the portions using a mold of your choice; the author used a flower-shaped pudding mold. Repeat until all the mixture is used. Arrange the getuk on the grated coconut and serve. It can also be packaged in attractive plastic containers as a gift.

Peel and wash the cassava, then steam until tender. Mash the cassava (or use a food chopper to save time). Mix the cassava with palm sugar, vanilla, and salt, then shape into small balls. Repeat until all the mixture is used. Mix the coating ingredients until smooth. Dip each cassava ball into the coating batter, covering it evenly. Heat the oil and fry the getuk over medium heat until cooked and golden brown. Remove and drain. Sokaraja-style fried getuk is ready to serve. Enjoy!

First, steam the grated coconut. Wash the kimpul (taro corm), steam it until partially cooked for about 10 minutes, then peel it. Steam again for about 20 minutes. While it is still hot and tender, mash it (I used a mortar and pestle). When it is partly mashed, add a pinch of salt and granulated sugar. Mash again, using your hands if needed to make the mixture more even. Add the grated coconut and mix well. Divide the mixture into two portions and add red food coloring to one portion; mix well. To make the colors even, press the mixture into a tray, placing the red layer on the bottom and the white layer on top. Carefully loosen the edges with a spatula and turn the tray over. Cut the getuk as desired and sprinkle with grated coconut before serving. Getuk kimpul is ready to enjoy.

Peel and wash the cassava. Mix the grated coconut with a little salt to enhance its savory flavor. Steam the cassava until cooked and tender. Steam the grated coconut as well. Once cooked, mash the cassava while it is still warm. Add 4 tablespoons of granulated sugar, a pinch of salt, and 1 tablespoon of margarine. Mix well. Divide the mixture into two portions and color one portion red. Shape the getuk using a flower-shaped silicone mold: use white getuk for the flower center and red getuk for the petals, then reverse the colors for another piece. Serve with the steamed grated coconut.
strIngredient1: Cassava (source says 'Am singkong'; likely a typo)
strIngredient6: Grated coconut (source says 'Am kelapa parut'; likely a typo)

strInstructions: Choose a starchy cassava and steam until tender. Steam the grated coconut as well. Mash the cassava while it is still hot. Mix it with the grated coconut (reserve a little for topping), granulated sugar, butter, and salt. Divide the mixture into two portions and add food coloring or flavoring paste as desired. Shape and press the mixture into a mold, or cut it into pieces as desired. Serve topped with grated coconut.

strMeal: Getuk Lindri Merah Putih Tanpa Cetakan
strInstructions: Steam the grated coconut for 10 minutes, then add salt to taste. Peel, wash, and cut the cassava into pieces. Steam for about 40–45 minutes. Turn off the heat and, while the cassava is still hot, remove any tough central fibers, then mash it. Add powdered sugar, salt, vanilla powder, and margarine. Add chili-red food coloring as desired. Mash again until smooth and adjust the taste. Take portions of the finished mixture and flatten them to the desired size. Continue until all the getuk mixture is used. Use a scraper to make grooves about 1 cm apart without cutting all the way through. Arrange the red-and-white Getuk Lindri on a serving plate. It is ready to serve with tea; grated cheese can be added as a topping if desired.
strIngredient8: Grated mature coconut, peeled and cleaned (source wording is abbreviated)

strInstructions: Prepare the ingredients. Steam the grated coconut with salt and pandan leaves for about 10 minutes. Mash the cassava using a mortar and pestle or a food chopper; it does not need to be completely smooth. Put the water, palm sugar, salt, and pandan leaves in a saucepan. Cook over low heat until the sugar melts. Mix the melted palm sugar syrup with the mashed cassava. Knead until thoroughly combined and no longer sticky, using a spatula to help if needed. Press the getuk into a container lined with plastic wrap. Remove it from the container and cut it as desired using a knife wrapped in plastic wrap to prevent sticking. Finish with grated coconut. Palm-sugar cassava getuk is ready to enjoy.

Steam the breadfruit until cooked. Steam the grated coconut too. Set aside a little salt for sprinkling and reserve the rest to mix with the breadfruit (the author uses 10 tablespoons of coconut). While still hot, mash the breadfruit with the grated coconut, salt, margarine, and granulated sugar until smooth. Divide the mixture into two portions. Add red food coloring to one portion and leave the other uncolored. Shape the getuk, placing the red and plain portions side by side in a mold, or arrange them as desired. Repeat until all the mixture is used. Coat or sprinkle with grated coconut when serving. For the red-and-white version, sprinkle coconut only over the plain portion so it remains visibly white. Serve.
strIngredient1: Steamed breadfruit (source says 'Am sukun kukus'; likely a typo)
strIngredient7: Dark red and chili-red coloring (author's note)

strInstructions: Peel and wash the cassava. Shave or finely slice the palm sugar. Steam the cassava until cooked. While it is hot, mash it and mix in the palm sugar, a little salt, and vanilla. Combine the coating ingredients and stir until smooth. Shape the cassava mixture into small portions and dip them into the coating batter. Fry in hot oil until cooked and golden brown. Remove and drain. Serve with tea or coffee.

Steam the cassava and grated coconut until tender. While they are still hot, mash them together. Add margarine, sugar, salt, and vanilla, then knead until evenly combined. Add food coloring to part of the mixture, then shape into balls and fill each with diced chocolate. Once all the balls are formed, coat them with the flour batter and then with breadcrumbs.
