Heat the oil and fry until cooked. Serve.

strMeal: Getuk Singkong Gula Aren (Kenyal, Manis, Legit)
strInstructions: Prepare the ingredients. Steam the grated coconut for 10 minutes. Place the peeled cassava on banana leaves and steam over medium heat for about 30–40 minutes, until very tender and easily crushed with a fork. Do not boil it, as the getuk may become watery. Remove the cassava and immediately mash it with a wooden pestle or in a large mortar. If using a food chopper, pulse briefly so some texture remains; do not turn it into a purée. Cook the palm sugar, water, salt, vanilla, and pandan leaves until the sugar melts and the syrup thickens slightly. Strain if there are impurities. Gradually pour the hot syrup into the mashed cassava while kneading with gloved hands, until the color is even and the mixture is smooth and no longer sticky. Line a 20 × 20 cm tray, or another tray of your choice, with plastic wrap, leaving some overhang. Lightly oil the plastic wrap. While warm, press the getuk mixture into the tray with an oiled spatula until even and compact. Let it set for 15 minutes, then lift it out using the plastic wrap and cut into pieces. Prepare the steamed grated coconut for the topping. Roll each piece in the coconut or sprinkle the coconut on top. Palm-sugar cassava getuk is ready to serve.
strIngredient2: Cassava, preferably mature and starchy; peeled, washed, and cut into small pieces
strIngredient3: Palm sugar, finely shaved (real palm sugar is recommended for its color and aroma)
strIngredient6: Pandan leaves (source wording appears truncated: 'Tapi biar wangi')
strIngredient9: Grated semi-mature coconut, using only the white flesh

strInstructions: Steam the bananas until cooked, then peel them. Slice or shave the palm sugar. Mix the palm sugar with the peeled bananas, add a little salt, and mash until smooth. Prepare a tray lined with banana leaves and lightly brush it with fresh cooking oil. Spread the mashed banana mixture evenly in the tray and refrigerate until firm. Cut into pieces and serve with coarsely grated young coconut.
strIngredient1: Ripe-but-firm bananas (source says 'Biji pisang mengkel'; likely six bananas)
strIngredient2: Shaved palm sugar (source wording is abbreviated)

strInstructions: Since I boiled the kimpul the day before, I peeled it and grated it into thin matchsticks to make mashing easier. Mix the grated kimpul with granulated sugar, vanilla powder, and salt. Transfer to a steamer tray, add grated coconut and pandan leaves, and steam for about 10 minutes after the water boils. Remove and transfer to a bowl. Use a wooden or plastic spoon to mix and mash the kimpul and coconut until evenly combined and smoother. Taste and add more sugar if needed. Press the getuk into any container or mold. I sprinkled a little toasted sesame seed on top for a nicer appearance. Cut the getuk kimpul into pieces and serve.

Boil the peeled cassava and grated young coconut. Once cooked, mash the cassava until smooth, then add the steamed young coconut and mix together. Combine all the ingredients listed under 'Ingredients 2' and stir again. Once the texture is smooth and right, shape the mixture and wrap it in plastic as shown. Enjoy, and remember to share your results!

Cut the cassava into small pieces and steam for 20 minutes. Mash the cassava using a pestle covered with plastic, then add sugar, salt, and butter. Divide the mixture into two portions: add taro paste to one and coffee-mocha paste to the other, or use any flavors you prefer. Flatten the mixture to a thickness of 1.5 cm, make long grooves, and cut into pieces as desired. Getuk Lindri can be served with grated coconut that has been steamed beforehand.

strMeal: Cara Membuat Kue Getuk Goreng Keju Yang Enak,Kenyal Dan Anti Gagal
strInstructions: The source instruction field contains website navigation text rather than recipe instructions, so it has been translated literally: Premium; Featured Recipes; Premium Weekly Menu; Most Viewed; Premium; Post Together; Send Feedback; Country.

Soak gaplek (dried cassava) or gatot that has been fermented through alternating hot and rainy weather for about a week, until it becomes somewhat dark, in water until tender. Slice it thinly. Rinse the sliced gaplek and steam for about 15 minutes, then remove and drain. Put the gatot in a bowl, add grated coconut and salt to taste, and mix well. Gatot is ready to enjoy.
strIngredient1: Gaplek (dried cassava; source wording is abbreviated)

strInstructions: Cut the cassava into pieces and wash thoroughly. Steam until tender. I steamed it together with grated young coconut mixed with salt. While hot, mash the cassava with chocolate milk powder, margarine, granulated sugar, and salt. (Because my mixture was still lumpy, I blended it again briefly in a food chopper.) Flatten the mixture on plastic wrap with a rolling pin to about 0.5 cm thick. Cut into pieces about 10 × 6 cm (length × width). Use the edge of a fork to make ridges, as shown in the picture. Carefully turn each piece over and roll it up. Repeat until all the mixture is used. Serve with steamed grated coconut.

Mash the tempeh and set aside. Sauté the ground spice paste until fragrant, then add the tempeh and stir until evenly combined. Add water, stock powder, salt, and sugar. Stir and cook briefly. Add the basil leaves and cook until both the tempeh and basil are done. Adjust the seasoning before turning off the heat, then let the filling cool. Mix the grated cassava with margarine, instant tempeh seasoning, stock powder, and salt. Take some of the cassava mixture, add filling, and shape as desired. Make the combro as large or small as you like; I shaped mine into oblong pieces about four fingers long. Heat the cooking oil over medium heat. Fry the combro until firm, then turn and fry until golden brown. Note: wait until the combro is firm before turning it so it does not fall apart.
strIngredient21: Minyak goreng rose brand untuk menggoreng

strInstructions: Prepare the ingredients. Combine all the outer-layer ingredients and mix until evenly combined. Take 1 tablespoon of the mixture, flatten it, and add the filling (see the attached recipe). Shape into oblong balls and repeat until finished. Heat the oil over medium heat and fry the comro until dry and golden brown, turning it only once to prevent it from absorbing too much oil.
strIngredient1: Peeled cassava, washed, grated, and squeezed to remove the liquid

strInstructions: Finely chop the shallots, garlic, and red bird's eye chilies in a food chopper. Crumble the oncom. Sauté the shallots, garlic, and bird's eye chilies until fragrant. Add the oncom, salt, flavor enhancer, and water. Stir and cook until the mixture is fully cooked and fairly dry, then remove from the heat and let cool. Mix the grated cassava with salt, ground pepper, and flavor enhancer. Take some cassava mixture, flatten it, and add the spicy oncom filling. Place one whole bird's eye chili in the center, then shape into an oblong. Heat the oil and fry the combro until golden brown. Remove and serve with whole bird's eye chilies.

Clean the cassava, then grate it finely. Mix the grated cassava dough with: grated coconut, minced garlic, coriander powder, sliced scallions, salt, and bouillon powder. Mix well, then adjust the seasoning. Take an adequate amount of dough, flatten it, add the basil tempeh chili filling, and wrap the cassava dough until evenly covered. Repeat until the dough is finished. Heat the oil and fry the combro until golden brown and cooked. Remove and drain.

strMeal: Combro Isi Oncom Ala Mak Ijah
strInstructions: Grate the cleaned cassava until fairly smooth. After grating, squeeze and strain the cassava until dry and free of water. Add chopped scallions to taste. Grind the garlic and bird's eye chilies or curly chilies. Sauté the previously mashed oncom. Add scallions, basil, sugar, salt, pepper, and mushroom bouillon (Totole) to taste. Take an adequate amount of the grated cassava, shape into a ball, and flatten it to hold the sautéed oncom filling. Insert the oncom into the cassava dough. It is ready to be fried. Fry the combro until cooked and serve with bird's eye chilies according to taste.
strIngredient5: Bird's eye chilies or curly chilies

strInstructions: Make the filling first (oncom chili paste): Slice the oncom, then fry until dry and browned. Grind the shallots, garlic, aromatic ginger (kencur), and chilies. Mash the fried oncom as well. Sauté the ground spices with bay leaves and lemongrass until fragrant. Add the oncom and mix well. Pour in a little water. Cook until the water boils. Add brown sugar, bouillon powder, and salt. Once the water has reduced, add the basil leaves. Check the taste. Cook until the basil leaves are wilted, then turn off the heat. For the combro skin: Mash the cassava, then add the sliced scallions, minced garlic, coriander powder, grated coconut, salt, and bouillon powder. Add the tapioca flour (Cap Pak Tani Gunung brand). Mix until evenly combined. Take an adequate amount of dough, flatten it, add the basil oncom filling, and wrap the dough until evenly closed. Repeat until finished. Fry the combro in hot oil. Once golden brown, remove and drain. Combro is ready to be served.

Slice the scallions, and process the cassava in a chopper until smooth. Mix the cassava, scallions, and salt. Add the coconut and margarine, then stir. Take 2 tbsp of the cassava dough, flatten it, fill it with tempeh, and shape it into an oval. Fry until browned. Serve.

Grind the spices and mash the tempeh. Sauté the spices until fragrant, then add the tempeh. Add brown sugar, salt, and flavor enhancer. Cook until the water reduces. The tempeh chili paste is ready to be used as combro filling.
strIngredient8: Flavor enhancer and a little water

strInstructions: Make the skin dough: Mash the cassava (can be grated/blended. If the cassava is watery, squeeze it first), then mix with coconut, scallions, and salt. Stir well and set aside. Prepare the filling: cut the tempeh, then fry it. Meanwhile, grind the chilies and garlic. Coarsely grind the tempeh and spices, then sauté. Set aside. Take 1 tbsp of the skin dough, add the filling, and shape it into a ball like an egg. Fry in hot oil until cooked and golden brown. Serve while warm.

Prepare the cleaned cassava. Soak in water for 15 minutes, then drain. Cut into small pieces and grate. (No need to squeeze as this cassava doesn't contain much water). Grind the spices for the oncom, then sauté until fragrant. Mash the oncom in a mortar, then add it to the sautéed spices. Cook until the oncom is done. Don't forget to season and check the taste. Stir well, add half of the sliced scallions, mix, and turn off the heat. The oncom is ready to be used as filling. Mix the grated cassava with margarine, cornstarch, and grated coconut. Stir well, add a little salt, and mix again. Take about 200 grams of the grated cassava dough into another container for the misro dough, add vanilla powder, mix well, and set aside. For the Combro: mix the cassava dough with enough flavor enhancer, coriander powder, and the remaining half of the sliced scallions. Stir well. The combro is ready to be shaped. Take an adequate amount of dough, add the oncom filling, and shape it neatly into an elongated oval. Fry in hot oil until golden brown, remove, and drain. Repeat until finished. For the Misro: take an adequate amount of dough, add brown sugar and 1/2 tsp of granulated sugar as filling, then shape neatly into an elongated oval. Fry in hot oil until golden brown, remove, and drain. Combro and Misro are ready to be served warm. Chewy, soft, and savory because of the grated coconut. Enjoy!
strIngredient9: Lemongrass (take the white part, slice finely)
strIngredient20: Dan penyedap untuk adonan singkong nya
strIngredient22: Secukupnya gula merah potong potong kecil untuk isian
strIngredient24: Sedikit vanili bubuk untuk adonan singkongnya

strInstructions: Grate the cassava and squeeze out the water. Collect the starch sediment from the water, and discard the liquid. Grind the bird's eye chilies, coriander, aromatic ginger, garlic, shallots, salt, and mushroom bouillon. Divide the ground spices into two parts: Use the first half to sauté the oncom filling with basil. Mix the second half into the grated cassava dough along with grated coconut, margarine, and scallions. This ensures the combro is evenly seasoned inside and out. Sauté the first part of the spices with the mashed oncom and basil until fragrant, then remove to use as filling. Mix the remaining ground spices into the grated cassava, add the grated coconut, margarine, scallions, and the cassava starch sediment, then stir well. Take the cassava dough, flatten it, add the oncom filling, and shape it into an oval. Fry the combro until golden yellow and cooked.

Peel, clean, and grate the cassava, then squeeze. Here, I blended the cassava. Let the cassava water settle for 30 minutes. Mix the grated cassava with the cassava starch sediment (discard the water, take the sediment). Add instant coconut milk. Grind the garlic and salt. Mix with the grated cassava, sliced chives, and coriander powder. Stir well. Take a little dough, fill with tempeh chili paste, seal tightly, and fry. Done.
strIngredient7: Bowl of mashed tempeh chili paste

strInstructions: Make the filling: prepare the ingredients. Boil water, cook the instant spaghetti according to package instructions, remove, and drain. Mix the boiled spaghetti with its seasoning packets. Cut the cooked aglio olio spaghetti into smaller pieces. Set aside for filling. Mix the grated cassava and salt until even. Take the cassava dough, flatten it, add the spaghetti filling, then shape into a ball and seal tightly. Heat the oil and fry the combro until golden yellow and cooked. Remove and drain. Serve warm.
strIngredient3: Packet of instant aglio olio spaghetti

strInstructions: Prepare the ingredients, then make the filling: grind the spices, mash the oncom, and add salt and MSG (A1 Rose Brand). Sauté the spices, add the oncom, and stir until slightly cooked. Add the scallions, stir until cooked, check the taste, remove, and set aside the oncom filling. After squeezing the bitter water from the cassava, discard the water but keep the starch sediment. Add Cap Gunung Agung tapioca flour, Rose Brand margarine, sugar, and salt. Mix well. Take an adequate amount of combro dough, fill with the sautéed oncom until finished (makes 9 pieces). Fry with Rose Brand cooking oil over medium heat until yellow. Remove and enjoy warm as a snack with bird's eye chilies. Yummy!

strMeal: Combro Ala Mba Melyni (Tanpa Kelapa Parut)
strInstructions: Grate the cassava; it can be fine or coarse according to taste. Grind all the filling ingredients: bird's eye chilies, garlic, salt, and bouillon. Sauté the ground spices until fragrant. Add the oncom and aromatic ginger (kencur) powder, cook until done and dry. Remove and drain from the oil. Set aside. Take a little grated cassava, flatten it, add the oncom filling, then roll it into a ball. Fry the combro until golden yellow and cooked.

strMeal: Set Jajan Pasar (Kue Talam, Combro, Klepon)
strInstructions: In a bowl, mix glutinous rice flour, rice flour, and salt. Stir well. Pour in warm water and cooking oil, then mix. Knead until smooth and moldable. Add pandan paste and knead until the color is evenly mixed. Take an adequate amount of dough, flatten it, and fill with brown sugar. Seal and roll into a ball. Repeat until the dough is finished. Boil water and cook the klepon until they float and are cooked. Remove and roll them in steamed grated coconut. Serve the Klepon together with sweet potato combro and cassava tape talam cake.
strIngredient12: Grated coconut + 1/6 tsp salt (mixed and steamed)

strInstructions: Wash the sweet potatoes clean, then steam until cooked. Peel the skin and mash while still hot. Once mashed, add tapioca flour, cornstarch, salt, and baking soda. Oncom chili paste: Mash the oncom/tempeh, blend the ground spices, then mix into the oncom. Stir well. Heat a little cooking oil, then sauté the oncom chili paste. Add all seasonings. Sauté until cooked. Check the taste and remove. Divide the sweet potato dough into several parts, flatten, and fill with the oncom chili paste. Shape into oval blocks again. Heat cooking oil, fry the combro until cooked and golden brown, remove, and drain. Sweet Potato Combro is ready to be served.
strIngredient2: Block of tempeh, steamed and mashed

strInstructions: First, cook the combro filling. Prepare the shredded chicken and ground spices. Heat oil. Add the ground spices consisting of red chilies, shallots, and garlic. Sauté until cooked. Add the shredded chicken, sugar, salt, and chicken bouillon powder. Mix thoroughly. Check the taste. Once right and cooked, turn off the stove. Transfer to a plate. Next, make the combro skin. Prepare the cassava, peel, cut into small pieces, soak in water, wash clean, and drain. Blend all the cassava until smooth, then squeeze out the water. Place the cassava in a bowl. Add the fried shallots and garlic that have been ground. Add salt and chicken bouillon powder. Mix evenly. Flatten the combro dough in the palm of your hand. Fill the dough with shredded chicken. Shape into an oval. Repeat until all the dough and filling are used up. Heat oil in a wok. Add the combro, fry until cooked, then remove and drain the oil. Jumbo combro with delicious shredded chicken filling is ready to be enjoyed wholeheartedly.
strIngredient2: Fried shallots, ground with a mortar
strIngredient3: Fried garlic, ground with a mortar

strInstructions: Process the cassava, grated coconut, garlic, salt, coriander, 1 tbsp coconut oil, and egg in a chopper. For the filling: grind chilies, aromatic ginger (kencur), salt, and brown sugar. Once smooth, mash the tempeh and mix with the grated coconut. Form into balls and flatten. Make cassava balls and add the filling. Place them on a baking tray lined with baking paper (I crumple the baking paper first, then grease it with 1 tbsp of coconut oil). Bake in the oven. I set the temperature to 250°C for 30 minutes.

Thinly slice the scallions. Prepare the grated coconut and all-purpose ragout for the filling. Squeeze the grated cassava, then add the grated coconut and scallions. Add salt and bouillon seasoning to taste, stir until evenly mixed, and check the taste. Take a rengginang mold, fill it halfway, add the ragout filling, cover with more dough, and press gently. Repeat until the dough is finished. Heat the oil. Fry the combro until golden yellow and cooked, turn it over, then remove. Drain and serve.

Prepare the ingredients, steam the purple sweet potatoes until soft, mash, and set aside. Mix the mashed purple sweet potatoes with granulated sugar, tapioca flour, vanilla, and salt, kneading until smooth. Take 1-1.5 tbsp of dough (±25-30 gr), flatten it, fill with brown sugar, roll into a ball, and shape it into an oval. Repeat until the dough is finished. Heat oil, and once hot, fry the misro until cooked and crispy on the outside. Remove and it is ready to be served.

Peel the cassava, then wash thoroughly. Grate the cassava and mix with grated coconut, instant coconut milk, and salt. Stir well. Thinly slice the brown sugar. Take a tablespoon of the cassava mixture, fill it with brown sugar, and roll it into a ball. Heat the oil and fry the cassava balls until browned. Once cooked, remove and drain. Serve warm.

Prepare all ingredients, then measure and slice the brown sugar. Squeeze the ground cassava first to remove the water content, but do not make it too dry. Add the grated coconut and stir until evenly mixed. Add the Tapioca Flour (Cap Pak Tani Gunung) and stir again. Then add granulated sugar, vanilla, and a pinch of salt, stirring once more. Shape the dough into a ball first, then flatten it, add an adequate amount of brown sugar, roll it into a ball again, and flatten it (or shape according to taste). Heat oil in a wok, fry the misro over low heat until golden brown. Once golden brown and perfectly cooked, remove the misro. Serve the misro accompanied by a cup of coffee or tea.

Grate the cassava (I used a cheese grater since I couldn't find a coconut grater), add salt and grated coconut, mix well. Prepare the finely sliced brown sugar. Take a full tablespoon of the cassava dough, place the sliced brown sugar on it, cover with a little more dough, shape into a ball, and neaten it. Heat a good amount of oil, fry the misro until cooked and golden, remove and drain. Serve the misro while warm; the melted brown sugar is delicious. Crispy on the outside, soft, sweet, and melted on the inside.

Peel and wash the cassava thoroughly, then grate it. Squeeze the cassava using a cloth base; I used a regular strainer but also squeezed it by hand so it wouldn't be too watery, but don't squeeze it too dry either, or the misro will become hard. Just squeeze it moderately so it's easy to shape. Add salt, sugar, and grated coconut (but I skipped the coconut here because I didn't have any). Mix well, then take a sufficient amount in your hand, add the filling, close, and shape into a ball. Fry the misro over medium-low heat until cooked. Ready to serve ✨ Happy trying ✨.

Grate all the cassava, then slice the brown sugar. Mix the grated cassava, grated coconut, and salt evenly. Shape the dough, add brown sugar, then roll back into a ball. Heat the cooking oil, fry the shaped dough until golden brown, remove, and drain. Serve warm as a companion for coffee/tea.

Prepare a container, place the grated cassava, add coconut, salt, and granulated sugar, and stir until evenly mixed. Shape the dough into balls and flatten them, then fill with finely sliced brown sugar according to taste (can be a little or a lot). Reshape into balls. Then fry in hot oil until browned and crispy. Remove and drain. (Note: use a stove with medium heat so the misro cooks perfectly). Misro/jemblem filled with brown sugar is ready to be enjoyed. Happy Cooking 😊.

Wash the cassava clean, then cut it into several pieces. After that, grate the cassava until smooth. Mash the oncom, then set aside. After the cassava is grated, put it into a cloth and squeeze the water out until completely gone. Prepare the filling ingredients for comro and misro: comro filling: slice enough brown sugar, scallions, and red chilies; grind the shallots, garlic, candlenuts, and aromatic ginger (kencur). Misro filling: sliced brown sugar. Add 1/2 tsp sea salt and 2 tbsp mocaf flour into the grated cassava. Prepare a frying pan to sauté the oncom. Add a little coconut cooking oil. After that, add the ground spices, red chilies, shrimp paste, bay leaves, kaffir lime leaves, brown sugar, and oncom. Then sprinkle with sea salt and ground pepper. Cook until fragrant (check the taste). After that, prepare plastic gloves to shape the misro and comro. Take a little dough, flatten it, and insert a little filling for both the oncom and misro. Repeat until the cassava dough is finished. Shape the comro into an oval, then shape the misro into a round shape. Prepare a wok, add coconut cooking oil. Wait until the oil is completely hot. Then fry the comro and misro until cooked and browned. Once cooked, remove, drain, and serve warm 🤤.

Mix the grated cassava, grated coconut, tapioca flour, and salt. Stir until even. Take the dough, flatten it, and fill with brown sugar. Roll the dough filled with brown sugar into a ball. Fry over medium heat until browned. Eat while hot.

Grate the cassava. Add grated coconut and salt, mix well. Slice the palm sugar, set aside. Take the grated cassava, adjusting the size to what you want to make. I made it about half a handful. Fill with sliced palm sugar, and shape into a ball. Then fry in hot oil over medium heat. Turn over when it is browned. Fry until cooked. Serve.

Cut the cassava, then steam until cooked. Mash the cassava until smooth and knead it, then add salt, wheat flour, and tapioca. Knead until mixed, then add margarine. Shape it and add brown sugar inside until the dough is used up. Fry the misro over low heat until cooked. Then it is ready to be served. Happy trying.

Prepare the ingredients. Grind the red chilies, bird's eye chilies, shallots, garlic, and aromatic ginger (kencur). Rinse the oncom under running water, then mash. Heat the cooking oil, sauté the ground spices until fragrant and cooked, add brown sugar, cook until the sugar dissolves, then add salt, bouillon powder, and oncom. Stir until all ingredients are evenly mixed and cooked, remove. Grate the cassava, then add Rose Brand margarine and a little salt, mix well. Divide the grated cassava in two; I divided it into a 70% portion for combro and a 30% portion for misro. Then, I added bouillon powder to the grated cassava for the combro and mixed well. Take a sufficient amount of grated cassava for the combro, add enough oncom filling, seal, and shape it into a slightly oval shape. Take a sufficient amount of grated cassava for the misro, add finely sliced brown sugar, seal into a ball, and then slightly flatten it. Do this until all the grated cassava for combro and misro is filled. Heat enough cooking oil, first fry the misro until cooked. After frying the misro, fry the combro until cooked, remove, and serve.

1. Peel, wash, and grate the cassava. Peel, wash, and grate the coconut. Mix and add salt. 2. Stir well. Divide the dough according to your desired size. I divided it into 20 pieces. Make balls and flatten them. Finely slice the brown sugar. 3. Add brown sugar. Reshape into balls. Heat oil and fry. 4. Once brown and cooked, remove and drain. 5. Plate beautifully, and it is ready to serve.

Grate the cassava and coconut. I usually just buy from the coconut vendor and ask them to grate the cassava and coconut together, hehe. Mix margarine, salt, and vanilla, stir well. Flatten the dough, add the filling, and seal. Fry over low heat until browned, remove, and serve. I also made a half-cooked version to stock in the freezer. Happy trying 😋😋
strIngredient5: Sliced brown sugar / chocolate sprinkles (meses) for filling

strInstructions: Grate the washed cassava. Add the grated coconut to the grated cassava. Add salt, add sugar, stir until even, then take the mixed cassava and shape according to taste. Prepare hot oil over low heat, add the shaped misro one by one. Fry until browned. Remove then serve.

The first step is to prepare the tools and ingredients. Then grate the cassava until smooth. Then slice the sugar, but not too big and not too powdery. Then heat the banana leaves over the fire so they can be used to wrap the grated cassava without sticking. Then place the grated cassava on the banana leaf, add sugar, and roll until covered. Wrap it, then steam over medium heat. And the misro is done. Very easy, right? Just with simple ingredients, perfect for a snack at home. Let's try it 😍🥰.

Mix the grated cassava and coconut evenly, divide into 5 parts. Oh, the purpose of squeezing the cassava juice is so the misro becomes crispy after frying. Take 1 part, flatten it, add the brown sugar filling, close it, and shape it into an oval or round shape. Do this until the dough is finished. Fry the misro in hot oil, flipping it back and forth so it cooks evenly. Serve while warm.
strIngredient1: Grated cassava, squeeze out the juice

strInstructions: Grate the cassava. Squeeze using a coconut squeezing cloth. Mix with the grated coconut that has been steamed beforehand. The purpose is so the dough doesn't spoil easily. Add salt. Stir until even. Take 1 tbsp of the misro dough. Flatten it. Add filling. Shape into a flat round (this is the signature misro shape). Fry in hot oil until cooked and browned. Serve warm.

Kernel/shave the sweet corn, then grind it by pressing gently. Set aside. Slice the scallions, set aside. Grind the garlic and shallots (I ground them coarsely so the shallot texture remains). Prepare a basin, add the shaved corn, sliced scallions, pepper, ground spices, salt, MSG, bouillon powder, wheat flour, rice flour, and a little water. Stir evenly. Set aside. Heat cooking oil over medium heat. Once hot, add the dough little by little. Stick it to the edge of the wok. Once it can be slid into the oil, fry until golden yellow. Repeat until the dough is finished. Once cooked, the corn fritters (bakwan jagung) are ready to be eaten with spicy chili sauce for dipping. Happy trying 🤗.

Shave the corn, then mix in a container with the shallots, garlic, scallions, celery, chilies, and egg. Stir well. Add Asatu Rose Brand MSG, pepper, salt, wheat flour, Rose Brand Rice Flour, and Rose Brand Tapioca Flour. Stir evenly, add water (optional, the water can be skipped). Check the taste. Fry in hot oil until cooked. Serve warm. Crispy... crunchy... great to accompany tea.
strIngredient13: Rose brand (Cap Gunung Agung) tapioca flour

strInstructions: Grind/blend the coriander, shallots, garlic, and chilies. Kernel the sweet corn, then coarsely mash and mix with the ground spices. Transfer the sweet corn to another container, mix with wheat flour, tapioca, rice flour, egg, and water. Then stir, add salt and flavor enhancer. Finely slice the scallions and celery. Heat oil. Then pour the corn batter. Cook until golden brown. Drain. The corn fritters are ready to be served and please enjoy.

Mix the corn, carrots, scallions, and instant bakwan flour in a container. Add water little by little until the batter is evenly mixed and not too runny. Cut the dumpling wrappers into 4 pieces. Heat oil, take one piece of dumpling wrapper, put 1 spoonful of batter on it, then fry until golden yellow. Remove and drain. Serve with green bird's eye chilies.

Prepare the ingredients. Kernel the sweet corn and slice the carrot, cabbage, and scallions. Set aside. Evenly mix the bakwan flour with water. Add the other ingredients. Stir well. Adjust the thickness of the batter to taste. Heat Rose Brand cooking oil. Pour the bakwan batter using a ladle. Fry over medium heat until cooked, flipping occasionally. Quick and easy corn fritters are ready to be served. It's more delicious eaten while warm.

strMeal: Resep Dadar Jagung Jawa Timur (Bakwan Jagung) Empuk, Renyah
strInstructions: Prepare the ingredients, wash the corn thoroughly, then shave it. Grind the spices, then add the sweet corn, leaving a little of the shaved corn unground. Add wheat flour, rice flour, salt, sugar, mushroom bouillon, scallions, and the remaining shaved corn. Stir evenly and it is ready to be fried.
strIngredient5: Kaffir lime leaf, remove the stalk

strInstructions: Prepare the required ingredients. Mash the tofu. Mix with flour, egg, pepper, salt, and garlic powder, stir evenly. Add the corn, stir evenly again. Next, add the scallions, stir again. Heat the oil, fry over medium heat until browned. Ready to be served.

Kernel the corn from the cob, finely chop the chilies, slice the scallions and celery. Grind the spices. Add the ground spices and egg to the corn mixture, pour ice water little by little until the desired thickness is reached, then check the taste. Heat the cooking oil, then take 1 tbsp of batter, fry until golden yellow, remove, and drain. Transfer to a serving plate and it is ready to be enjoyed while warm.

Peel the corn, wash it clean, and then kernel it. Put it in a bowl along with the sliced and washed scallions. Add the bakwan seasoning flour, cornstarch, and enough water. Then add the egg, stir until even, making sure it is not too thick and not too runny. Don't forget to taste it. Heat the cooking oil, once the oil is hot, fry the bakwan using about half a rice ladle per piece. Fry the bakwan until golden brown, flipping occasionally. Remove and drain. Corn fritters (bakwan jagung) are ready to be served for your loved ones ❤.
Peel the corn, then shave it. Add scallions, celery, and seasonings, mix in the flour, stir evenly, and add water little by little until you get the desired texture. Heat the oil, fry until cooked.

Shave the corn into a container. In another container, mix the two flours, ground pepper, garlic, salt, sugar, mushroom bouillon, and baking powder. Stir evenly. Add the shaved corn, stir evenly. Add water little by little. Stir evenly. Add scallions, celery, and grated coconut. Stir evenly again. Check the taste by frying a small amount of batter. Fry in hot oil over medium heat until cooked and golden brown. Serve with your favorite dipping sauce.

Beat the eggs. Add the seasoning flour to the beaten eggs, add kerneled corn, scallions, and grated carrots. Stir evenly. Heat the oil, I used a wide pan because I want to make the fritters thin and wide. Fry on both sides until golden and remove.

Prepare the ingredients, mix everything except water, flour, and egg, stir evenly. Add the flour, then water little by little until quite thick, but not too runny, taste it, if it's enough, add the egg and sliced celery. Stir evenly. Fry using a tablespoon measure, I used 2 tbsp, flip to cook evenly, remove, and drain. Serve warm 😍.

Prepare the thoroughly washed ingredients. After processing, arrange the shaved or kerneled sweet corn, chopped garlic, and sliced scallions, celery, and chilies. Mix all ingredients except oil, stir evenly until it becomes a batter. (I didn't use water, following the original recipe. The liquid comes only from the eggs and the water content of the corn). Heat a large amount of cooking oil until it is really hot. Take the batter with a spoon, drop it into the hot oil. Fry until the bakwan is golden yellow and crispy, remove, and drain.
strIngredient7: Curly red chilies, thinly sliced diagonally
strIngredient8: Kaffir lime leaves, remove the center stalk, slice

strInstructions: Peel the shallots and garlic, kernel the corn, and coarsely mash with the shallots and garlic. After mashing, add Royco, pepper, sugar, and crack the egg, stir evenly and add the moringa leaves. Heat the oil, fry until cooked. Corn fritters with moringa leaves are ready to be eaten.

Prepare all ingredients. Kernel the corn and mash the tempeh, but not too finely. Mix the corn, tempeh, seasonings, and all the flours, stir evenly. Add scallions, pour in water, stir evenly. Stop pouring water once the batter is cohesive and easy to shape. Heat cooking oil over medium heat. Take an adequate amount of bakwan batter, fry until cooked, remove, and drain.

Prepare the ingredients. Kernel the corn, slice the chilies. Mix with bakwan seasoning flour, salt, and pepper. Stir evenly until all the flour coats the corn. Add ice cubes and water little by little. Stir evenly. Heat the oil. Take 1 tablespoon of bakwan batter. Fry in hot oil until both sides are cooked. Remove. Drain. Ready to be served with chilies or chili sauce.

Prepare the ingredients. Heat oil, fry the potatoes until half cooked. Use medium heat. Grind the ground spices until smooth. Mash the potatoes until smooth. Mix all ingredients, stir evenly. Take 1 tbsp of dough and shape into a ball. Heat oil, fry the perkedel until cooked. Use medium heat. Serve.

Peel and wash the potatoes clean, then steam until cooked. Mash, and wait until the temperature is not too hot. Boil the meat, chop/mince into small pieces. Add to the mashed potato dough. Add chopped celery and ground spices. Stir evenly, then shape the dough. Coat in tapioca flour so it doesn't stick and is sturdier. Dip into beaten egg, then fry over medium heat until browned. Making Soy Sauce Chili Paste (Sambel Kecap): Chop bird's eye chilies into small pieces, add fried shallots and garlic, press with a spoon, then add sweet soy sauce to taste. Potato meat perkedel is ready to be served with soy sauce chili paste 😊.
strIngredient8: Soy sauce chili paste (sambel kecap) ingredients

strInstructions: A side snack that can be paired with anything. Eaten with Fried Noodles, it automatically gives a celebratory (Berkat'an) vibe; with Nori and Japanese Rice, it becomes even yummier. Prepare the ingredients: Peel and cut the potatoes, then fry until cooked and drain. Sauté garlic and shallots until fragrant. Mash the fried potatoes while warm. Mix potatoes, corned beef, sautéed onions, scallions, pepper, salt, and nutmeg. Shape the dough into flat rounds. Beat the egg with a pinch of bouillon/salt, coat the perkedel with the egg. Heat the oil, fry the perkedel until golden yellow.

strMeal: Perkedel Kentang Ala Chef Devina Hermawan
strInstructions: Cut, then fry half cooked (forgot to take a picture of the frying). Slice garlic and shallots, then fry together with the potatoes. Fry until cooked and browned. Drain and transfer to a mortar. Add salt, chicken bouillon powder, granulated sugar, and ground pepper, then mash smoothly and add sliced scallions and celery. Transfer the perkedel dough to a bowl, add cornstarch and 2 tbsp of beaten egg. Stir evenly. Shape the potatoes into balls and flatten them. Then coat in the beaten egg. Don't forget to add a little salt to the beaten egg. Fry until cooked. Drain. Serve.

strMeal: Perkedel Kentang Khas Minang (Lauk Pendamping Soto Padang)
strInstructions: Slice the potatoes, heat the steamer, steam the potatoes until cooked and soft. (Test by piercing with a fork.) While waiting, grind the garlic, nutmeg, and cloves. Heat a little cooking oil. Fry the shallots until golden brown and dry. Remove, drain. Sauté the scallions until wilted and dry. Remove, set aside. Finely mash the steamed potatoes. Add the ground spices (from step 1), fried shallots, sautéed scallions, salt, and ground pepper. Stir evenly using a spoon or spatula. Check the taste. Take the perkedel dough, about the size of a ping pong ball. Roll into a ball, flatten, neaten the edges. Repeat until finished. Then prepare the beaten egg. Heat enough cooking oil. Coat the perkedel with the beaten egg. Put into the hot cooking oil. Fill the pan. Fry until golden yellow. Flip, fry again until all parts are cooked. Remove, drain. Serve with Soto Padang.

Prepare the ingredients. Cut the potatoes into small pieces (diced), then fry until cooked. Fry the shallots and garlic until golden yellow. Mash the potatoes while hot; I use a stone mortar covered with plastic so the potatoes don't stick. Then add the fried shallots and garlic, pepper, salt, mushroom bouillon, and nutmeg powder. Once smooth, add the egg yolk, stir evenly, finally add celery. Stir evenly. Take a handful of dough, shape it into an oval. Set aside. Heat oil, coat the pergedel (perkedel) in egg white, then fry until golden yellow.

Peel the potatoes, slice them, then wash thoroughly and drain, then fry half cooked. Grind the ground spices. Then add the potatoes and mash. Transfer to a container, add broccoli, chopped carrots, and beaten egg, stir evenly, then take enough dough, roll into a ball and flatten. Beat the egg, then coat the perkedel dough with the beaten egg. Then fry until golden yellow, remove, drain, and serve.

Peel and dice the potatoes, fry, mash until smooth, then set aside. Process the chicken breast fillet in a chopper with one egg yolk (the egg white will be for dipping later), add a little Royco, salt, pepper powder, and 1 tsp sesame oil. Set aside. Mix the potatoes, ground spices, chicken breast fillet, the remaining Royco, salt, pepper powder, celery, and 1 egg, stir until even. Shape the perkedel into flat rounds, arrange them on plastic lightly greased with oil. Shape until the dough is used up. Dip the dough into the egg white, then fry until cooked and browned. Remove and serve, can be eaten as a side dish for soto.

Peel and wash the potatoes. Cut into pieces and steam until cooked. Cool the potatoes, then mash them. Fry the sliced shallots and garlic, drain. Mix the mashed potatoes, shredded chicken, fried shallots and garlic, pepper powder, garlic powder, mushroom bouillon, salt, and scallions. Stir evenly. Add the beaten egg. Stir evenly and check the taste. Shape the dough, then dip it into the beaten egg. Heat oil, fry the perkedel until cooked.

Heat a little oil, fry the shallots and garlic over medium heat until cooked and browned, set aside. Grind with salt and pepper. Fry the potatoes until browned and soft. Add the ground spices, egg yolk, curry powder, scallions, tapioca flour, minced meatballs, bouillon powder, and sugar. Stir evenly. Mash the fried potatoes with a mortar, transfer to a bowl. Heat oil, shape the perkedel into balls with the help of a fork, fry over medium-low heat until cooked, drain.

Peel and wash the potatoes clean, dice them, then fry until half cooked. Once cooked, mash the potatoes with a fork or mortar while still hot. Sauté the ground spices until fragrant, then add the chicken breast, stir evenly until perfectly cooked. Add the sautéed chicken to the potato dough, then add the crushed fried shallots, 1 egg, scallions, celery, and seasoning ingredients, stir evenly. Chill the dough in the refrigerator for 15 minutes to make it easier to shape. After 15 minutes, take the dough and shape into balls, then flatten, shape according to taste until the dough is used up. Put 1 egg in a container and beat it for dipping. Dip the shaped dough into the egg and fry until cooked, and the perkedel is ready to be served.

Peel all the potatoes, wash, and cut them. While boiling water, add the potatoes. Once it boils, remove and drain for about 20 minutes. After that, mash them. Slice the shallots and garlic, then fry until crispy. Remove and mix into the previously mashed potatoes. While adding pepper powder, Masako, and 1 tbsp tapioca flour. Then shape according to taste. Fry until slightly yellowish. Once done, remove and serve 😇.

Peel the potatoes, cut thinly so they cook quickly, and wash the potatoes clean. Drain. Steam the potatoes. Remove and mash. While waiting for the potatoes to cook, grind the garlic and salt. Mix the ground spices into the mashed potatoes. Add Asatu MSG and pepper powder. Stir evenly. Add Rose Brand Tapioca Flour, stir until all parts are mixed. Then add the egg and stir again until everything is evenly mixed. If the dough is too soft, you can add a little more Tapioca Flour. Pour a good amount of Rose Brand Cooking Oil. Turn on the heat to medium-low. Wait until hot. Take about 1 tablespoon of dough. Shape into a flat coin and fry until it floats and is browned. It can also be half-fried and stored for the next day's stock. Serve with clear soup.

Peel the potatoes, wash and cut them, then soak briefly in water. Heat oil, fry the potatoes until cooked. Once cooked, drain and mash with a mortar while hot. Wait until lukewarm, then add the seasonings, stir evenly. Check the taste, if it's good, add the egg, stir evenly. Shape the dough into balls according to taste while heating oil. Fry until cooked. Serve while warm.

Grind or mash the spices. While still hot, mash the steamed potatoes as well. Put all ingredients into a container, add sliced Brazilian spinach leaves. Check the taste. Then shape according to taste. When ready to fry, dip into the beaten egg, fry in hot oil over medium heat until evenly cooked. Remove and drain. Serve.

Bismillah,,, prepare all ingredients and equipment to be used.. Wash the oxtail clean under running water then boil it first until it changes color, then discard the boiling water... For the second boil, put it in a pressure cooker, fill with enough fresh boiled water until the oxtail is submerged, then add garlic and onion... Then cook for 45 minutes. After finishing with the pressure cooker, the oxtail looks tender and fragrant, add hot water again in a regular cooking pot, then add the potato and carrot pieces. Stir the soup evenly,,, then add spices: cloves, cinnamon, star anise, salt, granulated sugar, flavor enhancer,,, white pepper powder, nutmeg powder, cook until boiling, then check the taste. Turn off the stove heat, then add sliced celery leaves, scallions, and fried shallots. Full-spice oxtail soup is ready to be served warm ☺️ happy trying and enjoy 🙏.
strIngredient4: Dieng potatoes, peeled and cut into pieces
strIngredient5: Carrots, peeled and cut into pieces

strInstructions: Boil the meat first with 1L of water, cook over medium heat until boiling, then lower the heat, wait 10 minutes, and discard the first water. Pour 1.5 L of water into the meat pot, add the spice bundle wrapped in a sterile cloth, cook over medium heat; after the pressure cooker hisses, count 30 minutes from the hiss. Open the pressure cooker pot after the steam inside is gone, and add carrots, green beans, and potatoes, as well as salt, flavor enhancer, sugar, and flavor booster. Add scallions and celery too, cook until the vegetables are done. Check the taste and serve with accompaniments like emping (melinjo crackers) and tomatoes if you like. Check the taste and it is ready to be served.

Cut the oxtail into pieces, then wash clean. Boil until tender. Add water, add aromatics. After the water boils, add potatoes and carrots. Cook until the carrots and potatoes are tender. Sauté the ground spices until fragrant and the raw smell is gone, pour in salt and bouillon powder. Add scallions and celery. Pour 2 ladles of soup broth. Sauté until wilted. Pour the sautéed spices into the soup pot. Let it boil. A bowl of oxtail soup is ready to be served and eaten with the family.

Boil the beef oxtail for 1 hour over medium heat using a pressure cooker if you have one so it becomes tender quickly. Grind pepper, nutmeg, chop garlic, cut onion into small pieces. Heat butter then sauté garlic and onion, after fragrant add pepper and nutmeg. Sauté until evenly cooked then put into the pot containing meat add cardamom, butterfly pea flower, beef flavor enhancer, salt, granulated sugar, and tomato sauce, cook for 1/2 hour so the spices seep into the meat. Check the taste and it is ready to be served along with leftover ketupat.

Wash the beef oxtail with boiling water in a pot for about 5 minutes, add crushed ginger and bay leaves (as aromatics, its function is to remove the smell of the oxtail), after boiling discard the floating scum, aromatics, and boiling water). Put the boiled beef oxtail into a pressure cooker and add water until all the oxtail is submerged, then pressure cook for about 20 minutes. The aim is to make the oxtail tender. When the steam in the pressure cooker is gone, you can discard the oil/fat floating on the water. After that, prepare the sautéed spices, namely shallots and garlic thinly sliced (not chopped or blended, so the broth is clear) with Blue Band until it emits a fragrant smell. After that, into the oxtail and broth add about 500-700 ml of water, add the sliced carrots and potatoes, sautéed shallots and garlic, 1/2 whole onion, scallion and celery tied together, salt, pepper, granulated sugar, and nutmeg. Pressure cook briefly for about 8-10 minutes. Finally, add tomato pieces and scallions. Boil briefly, check the taste according to preference. Transfer to a container and sprinkle fried shallots on top and it is ready to be served :))).

Pressure cook the oxtail, fill with a lot of water because it will be pressure cooked for quite a long time -+ 1 hour 15 minutes. Cut the vegetables into small squares, adjust to your child's preference. Grind the ground spices. Open the pressure cooker then add the ground spices, cloves, cinnamon, and crushed garlic. Add the vegetables, add a little salt. Optional: you can add MSG or Totole. Once the vegetables are cooked, remove and serve with a little rice. If the oxtail is large, you can make 2 portions for eating.
strIngredient1: Oxtail, adjust to the size of the oxtail. I chose a center cut oxtail
strIngredient11: Peppercorns, adjust to child's taste. can be ground or left whole

strInstructions: Wash the oxtail clean then boil in boiling water until the water boils again, turn off the heat and skim the scum if any. Then add cardamom, cloves, and nutmeg, cook again until the water boils again. Prepare the ground spice ingredients, grind with a blender then sauté until fragrant. Put the sautéed spices into the oxtail boiling pot, stir evenly, add salt and granulated sugar, then add celery, scallions, and tomatoes, stir evenly. After that, add carrots and potatoes, cook until done, check the taste. Turn off the heat then remove all the cooked oxtails. Prepare the ingredients for grilled oxtail, mix all together then add the oxtail, stir evenly until all the oxtail is coated with spices. Prepare a pan for grilling the oxtail, add margarine. Put the oxtail into the pan then grill until cooked. Serve grilled oxtail with rice and a bowl of oxtail soup, provide accompaniments of lemon or calamansi and fried emping.

Prepare the necessary ingredients. Boil the oxtail until tender. Then heat oil and sauté the ground spices until fragrant and the raw smell is gone, pour into the oxtail meat boiling water. Add water. Grind the ground spice ingredients. Leave a few cloves of shallots to be sliced. Add all the aromatic spices and pour in salt and bouillon powder. Let it cook until it boils. Once boiling, add carrots and scallions. Let it boil again for 5 minutes then taste. Check the taste and correct if necessary. Ready to be served.

Clean the beef oxtail, wash thoroughly, peel potatoes and carrots and cut them, prepare the spices. Boil water until boiling, add beef oxtail, also add garlic, cloves, cardamom, cinnamon, nutmeg powder, cook until the water boils again, then I transfer it to a pressure cooker. Count the cooking time after the hissing sound, mine is 10 minutes. Then turn off the stove, open the lid after the hot steam is gone, and the beef oxtail is already tender. Then add carrot and potato pieces, add salt, bouillon powder, pepper powder, cook until tender, check the taste, once it suits your preference turn off the stove. Transfer to a serving bowl, sprinkle with scallions and celery leaves.

1. Cut the beef oxtail according to taste, wash clean. Boil water, add the beef oxtail, once it changes color and boils, discard the water. Change to clean water, do this 3x until the water is clear of dirt. 2. Boil the beef oxtail until tender, use the 7.30 method. 5. If it's not tender yet, repeat the method until it is tender to your liking. 3. Chop the garlic, put it into the broth, add nutmeg, cloves, and cinnamon. Season with pepper, sugar, and salt, check the taste. 4. Cook until the spices seep in and set. Add leeks and celery, stir well. Turn off the heat. 5. Serve with a sprinkle of fried shallots.

Boil water until boiling, add the thoroughly washed beef oxtail, boil briefly, remove, discard the water, and rinse the beef oxtail under running water. Boil fresh water again until boiling, add the beef oxtail again, boil until tender. Add potatoes, cook until half done, add all the spices, cook until done and absorbed. Remove, serve while hot.

strMeal: Sop Buntut Sapi Empuk Gurih Rempah
strInstructions: First prepare the meat and oxtail: cut the meat into pieces first if you haven't. Boil the beef oxtail and beef with enough water just until perfectly submerged. Boil for 10 minutes. Discard the boiling water, I use the method of draining by pouring everything into a strainer. Purpose: the resulting soup won't be dirty/cloudy later. Fill a large pot with 4 liters of water, cook until boiling. Once boiling, add the previously boiled and drained meat and oxtail. Cook for 3 hours over medium-low heat. Initially, a little foam and some dirt from the first boil will still come out. Not much though, it can be scooped out with a ladle. While waiting for the meat to boil, prepare the sautéed onions first. Sauté the diced onion and blended garlic until fragrant. Once the sautéed onions are fragrant, add pepper, nutmeg powder, cardamom, cloves, and cinnamon. Stir evenly. Turn off the heat. Set aside. Once it's been 3 hours, put the sautéed onions into the meat broth. Stir evenly. Add the sliced potatoes and carrots as well. Cook for about 10 minutes. Then, also add the sliced scallions and sliced celery. Cook again for about 5 minutes. Season with salt and flavor enhancer. Taste it. If it's lacking, you can adjust it again according to taste. Finally, add the tomato pieces. Only cook briefly for about 1 minute, then turn off the heat. The aim is so the tomatoes don't fall apart from being boiled too long, but you don't want them to taste like raw tomatoes either. Sprinkle with fried shallots, serve with warm white rice, emping, and sambal. Yummmm my husband even asked for more rice.
strIngredient25: Pcs jeruk limo (untuk perasan per porsi)
strIngredient29: Secukupnya sambal untuk sop sambel cair untuk sop

strInstructions: Cut the chicken breast into small pieces... then put it into a wok, add a little water... at the first boil, discard the water, then change the water and cook again. After the chicken changes color, add salt and flavor enhancer... stir well. Add pecel sauce and sweet soy sauce, cook until the water reduces and the chicken is perfectly cooked. Ready to be served and eaten... happy trying 🥰.

Dice the chicken breast fillet then marinate with the spices. Let it sit for about 1 hour. Skewer with 4 pieces per skewer. Deep fry the satay until slightly browned. Set aside. Fry the peanuts, then blend with a little water, sweet soy sauce, and a little salt. Heat a Teflon pan. Grill the fried satay and baste with the peanut sauce. Grill until browned and the spices are absorbed. Prepare the tomato, chili, and shallots. Then slice thinly and mix with 3 tsp sweet soy sauce. Serve the satay with the soy sauce chili paste. Enjoy with warm rice... awesome.

In a bowl, add the ground spices, tamarind water, sweet soy sauce, brown sugar, coriander powder, pepper powder, salt, and bouillon powder, then mix well. Marinate overnight. Skewer all the marinated meat, repeat until finished. Grill in a pan with a little margarine, flipping back and forth until all sides are cooked. Remove and serve.

Dice the chicken and its skin. Then wash clean and drain until the water is gone. Prepare the marinade. Then mix into the chicken and skin, stir evenly. Marinate for at least 30 minutes in the chiller. Prepare the peanut sauce ingredients, then blend the peanuts, chilies, candlenuts, and garlic until smooth. In a wok, mix all the remaining peanut sauce ingredients. Cook over medium-low heat. Keep stirring slowly so it doesn't burn, do this until the spices release oil, and check the taste. Wash the skewers clean. Then skewer the chicken, ± 5 pieces of chicken per skewer. Repeat until finished. Mix the basting sauce and coat every side of the chicken. Grill the chicken over medium heat while continuously flipping until every side is cooked. Chicken satay is ready to be enjoyed with an addition of chili pickle.

Dice the chicken fillet. Add lime juice. Let it sit for 10 minutes then rinse again until clean. Marinate the chicken with garlic, pepper powder, and salt. Let it sit. Fry the peanuts until browned. Once the peanuts are cooked, add garlic, chilies, candlenuts, and shallots. Sauté until wilted. Drain. Blend the peanuts and sautéed spices with water until smooth. Sauté the peanut sauce with a little oil. Season with kaffir lime leaves, soy sauce, salt, sugar, pepper powder, and bouillon powder. Keep stirring while tasting. Cook until the peanut sauce is thick and bubbling. Set aside. Take a little peanut sauce and soy sauce on a plate. Then coat the skewered chicken. Then grill. Grill until the chicken is cooked while flipping the sides. Remove and serve with peanut sauce, sliced shallots, and bird's eye chilies.

Cut the scallions (green part), thinly slice the ginger, and crush the garlic. Heat a pan over low heat. Add soy sauce, water, scallions, garlic, ginger, palm sugar, and dashi. Stir evenly. Cook for 10 minutes over low heat. So the aroma comes out. After 10 minutes, turn off the heat then wait until it cools. Once cool, remove the garlic, scallions, and ginger. The Tare sauce is ready to use. Cut the white part of the scallions. About 2 knuckle lengths. Skewer the chicken and scallions alternately. Do this until all the chicken and scallions are used up. Dip the yakitori into the Tare sauce. Marinate for about 10 minutes so it absorbs. Heat a pan over medium heat. Grill the yakitori. Occasionally baste with tare sauce while flipping so it doesn't burn. Grill the yakitori until cooked. Serve with a sprinkle of sesame seeds and chili powder.

Wash the chicken, then cut into pieces according to taste for satay. Grind the marinade with a blender/chopper/mortar. Put the chicken into the marinade, then let it sit for at least 30 minutes. I usually leave it all day in the refrigerator. Skewer the chicken onto satay sticks. Then grill until cooked. It's already very delicious up to this point, if you want to use peanut sauce it's also delicious:).

Grind the spices, wash the chicken clean. In a pot, add the ground spices, bay leaves, and the chicken that has been cut into cubes. Boil until the chicken is cooked, drain. Skewer a few pieces of chicken onto satay sticks, do this until finished. Then mix all the basting ingredients, stir evenly. Grill the satay on a Teflon pan while basting with the basting sauce, flipping back and forth until the spices are absorbed, remove, serve the satay with other accompaniments.

strMeal: Sate Ayam Rempah Manis Dan Simple
strInstructions: Cut into small pieces and clean the chicken! Make the marinade. Grind garlic, shallots, coriander, nutmeg, galangal. Mix with the chicken, then add soy sauce, salt, chicken flavor enhancer, brown sugar, pepper. After mixing evenly, skewer the chicken satay. Then grill/roast the chicken satay with your own tools. Don't forget to fan it so it cooks evenly. Then after it's done, serve with soy sauce chili paste / peanut sauce ❤️.

Coat the chicken with salt and lime juice. Set aside. Mix the marinade ingredients then stir evenly with the chicken. Let it sit for at least 1 hour or overnight. Dry roast the peanuts, garlic, and kaffir lime leaves until they change color. Blend with palm sugar and salt. When ready to use, just mix with hot water and sweet soy sauce to taste. Skewer the chicken onto satay sticks. Heat Rose Brand margarine, then grill the satay until cooked while occasionally basting with sweet soy sauce.

Mix all ingredients together. Then stir evenly. Let it sit for 30 minutes. After that, skewer with satay sticks. Grill with a little margarine. When one side is cooked, flip. Cook until both sides are cooked.
strIngredient1: Chicken thigh fillet, sliced into cubes

strInstructions: Cut the chicken lengthwise then marinate with grated galangal, grated onion, instant marinade, granulated sugar, oil, and coconut milk, stir evenly then skewer the chicken onto satay sticks while pressing it. Slice the galangal. Put the galangal, large red chilies (Tanjung), shallots, garlic, and oil into a chopper, blend until smooth and sauté until fragrant. Put the fried peanuts into the chopper, blend coarsely then put into a wok, sauté briefly. Add water, kaffir lime leaves, palm sugar, granulated sugar, salt, mushroom bouillon, and coconut milk, cook over low heat until it reduces. Brush the grill with oil, grill the satay until cooked and browned on both sides. Singapore-style chicken satay is ready to be served.

Sauté the spices until fragrant & darker, let it cool briefly then mix into the chicken fillet / boneless chicken thighs. Marinate for at least 30 minutes (overnight is tastier). Skewer the chicken one by one. Cook using a grill pan, air fryer, oven, or regular grill.

Slice the breast fillet into small, flat pieces (so they cook evenly when grilled). After that, skewer with satay sticks. Heat a wide grill/Teflon pan, then grill the satay until cooked (flip 1x). Boil enough water to dissolve the Sinti pecel sauce. After the satay is cooked, add the Sinti sauce, sweet soy sauce & fried onions. Chicken satay is ready to be served 😉.

Skin satay: boil the chicken skin with lemongrass, ginger, and a little salt. Once cooked, cut lengthwise and skewer onto sticks. Set aside. Spices: dry roast the coriander. Blend shallots, garlic, coriander, and galangal until smooth. Prepare the diced chicken, add the ground spices. Add soy sauce, tamarind water, and grated brown sugar. Add salt, pepper powder, and bouillon powder. Stir evenly. Marinate for at least 30 minutes. Skewer the marinated chicken meat and skin. Grill the satay. Because I don't have charcoal at home, I used a stone. Flip the satay and baste with peanut sauce, grill until cooked. Remove and it's ready to be served.
strIngredient1: Chicken fillet, separate skin and meat

strInstructions: Vegetable pickle (acar): mix all the pickle ingredients, stir evenly, and put in the refrigerator so it's fresher. Peanut sauce: Fry the red chilies, bird's eye chilies, shallots, and garlic with a little oil. Remove and drain. Blend the fried ingredients, fried peanuts, and water. Cook with the other ingredients until it reduces and thickens. Dice the chicken fillet according to taste. Skewer with 3-4 pieces per stick. Repeat until the chicken pieces are used up. Brush with a mixture of peanut sauce and soy sauce. Grill until cooked, don't forget to flip it back and forth so it cooks perfectly. Serve the chicken satay with peanut sauce and vegetable pickle.
strIngredient4: Red chilies and bird's eye chilies

strMeal: Sate Kelapa (Sate Ayam Kelapa) Bumbu Gulai Instan
strInstructions: Prepare all the ingredients to make coconut satay. Add the instant gulai seasoning, sauté with the chicken, add water and aromatic spices. Cook briefly, add the grated coconut. Cook over low heat until the grated coconut and chicken blend with the spices. Add oyster sauce. Set aside the coconut chicken on a plate, skewer with satay sticks. Pan-fry briefly until smoky. Serve the coconut satay with warm rice. Enjoy.

Mix the chicken with sweet soy sauce, marinade, and cooking oil. I marinated this overnight. Then skewer with satay sticks. Grill on a Teflon pan until cooked. Ready to be served with fresh vegetables (lalapan) and warm rice.
strIngredient5: Accompaniment: practical soy sauce chili paste

strMeal: Firinda Tavuk şiş (Sate Ayam Ala Turki)
strInstructions: Coat the chicken with lime juice then dice according to taste, mix all the marinade ingredients. Mix the chicken and marinade, store in the refrigerator so the spices absorb, don't forget to cover with plastic wrap. Oven-bake the chicken pieces or skewer the chicken with satay sticks, you can alternate with tomatoes (I skipped this) at 180°C for 30-40 minutes, ready to be served.

Prepare the ingredients. Grind the garlic and candlenuts. Mix the chicken and marinade ingredients, stir evenly. Then let it sit for at least 30 minutes so the spices absorb. Make the soy sauce chili paste: cut all the ingredients. Then mix all the ingredients with sweet soy sauce. Stir evenly and serve. Prepare the satay skewers, then skewer the chicken onto the satay sticks. Do this until finished. Then grill the satay until cooked. Chicken Satay with Soy Sauce is ready to be served with soy sauce chili paste.

Prepare all ingredients. Wash the chicken fillet clean, then dice it and coat with salt and lime juice. Let it sit for 15 minutes, rinse. Skewer the diced chicken fillet onto satay sticks until finished. Set aside. Grind the ground spices and fried peanuts. Blend with a little water. The peanut texture can be a bit coarse when blended. Sauté the ground spices, then add brown sugar and kaffir lime leaves. Also add sweet soy sauce, salty soy sauce or fish sauce, and a little salt. Keep stirring until the spices are cooked and bubbling. Once the spices are not too hot, coat the satay with the spices. Let it sit in the refrigerator for about 1 hour. After that, prepare a grill pan or roaster. Grill the chicken satay. While grilling, flip it back and forth while basting again with a little satay sauce. Grill until the satay is cooked. Add accompaniments (lime juice, fried onions, chili paste, and lontong/rice cake). Serve. Yummy.
strIngredient3: Or 3 small pieces of brown sugar
strIngredient4: Lime for coating the chicken fillet
strIngredient7: Salty soy sauce or fish sauce

strInstructions: Mix all the marinade spices, check the taste. Put the chicken into the marinade, stir evenly. Let it sit for ±30 minutes. Skewer the chicken, the amount according to taste. Grill while basting with the marinade. Mix all the sauce ingredients, check the taste. Let it sit for ±15 minutes; the sauce will become a little watery from the tomatoes. After 15 minutes, you can add sweet soy sauce if it feels lacking. Serve warm. Happy trying, moms 💕.
strIngredient3: Packet of Kobe fried rice seasoning

strInstructions: Marinate the chicken with lime juice, salt & bouillon for about 15 minutes. Sauté the onions until fragrant, then blend with roasted peanuts & water. Cook the peanut sauce over low heat, add soy sauce + salt + brown sugar. Cook until thickened, don't forget to check the taste. Skewer the marinated chicken, then add 1 ladle of peanut sauce, spread evenly. Heat the grill, add a little margarine. Then grill the satay until cooked. After the satay is cooked, pour peanut sauce over it & it is ready to be served.

Banjar satay: marinate the chicken with the marinade, stir. Let it sit while preparing the other spices. Heat cooking oil, fry the peanuts until cooked. Remove and set aside. Grind the satay spices. Sauté, add cinnamon, water if necessary, peanuts, salt, granulated sugar, and bouillon powder. Check the taste. Skewer the chicken onto satay sticks, add the red spice mixture. Grill in a pan until both sides are cooked. Vegetable soup: grind the spices, heat cooking oil, sauté the spices. Add lemongrass, bay leaves, kaffir lime leaves, and galangal. Sauté until fragrant. Add chayote, chicken bones, and coconut milk. Add quail eggs, add salt, sugar, pepper, and bouillon powder. Stir. Cook until done. Serving: arrange the lontong (rice cakes), add the chayote vegetable soup, satay, and its sauce.
strIngredient2: Chicken thigh fillet, cut into cubes
strIngredient22: Labu siam , potong panjang dan cuci bersih

strInstructions: Dry the meat using kitchen paper towels, cut the meat diagonally slightly wide across the grain so the meat becomes tender quickly; do not make it too thin so the meat doesn't dry out when grilled, put it in a container. Add the ground spices, add salt, pepper powder, bouillon powder, tamarind water, and sweet soy sauce, stir evenly, marinate in the refrigerator for about 1 hour so the spices are absorbed. After 1 hour, skewer the meat with satay sticks, do this until finished (if you want to grill the satay over coals, soak the satay sticks in water first so they don't burn easily). Grill the satay over coals/griller/grill pan according to taste, when the satay is half cooked, baste with the basting ingredients, grill both sides until cooked, remove. How to make tomato chili paste: coarsely grind bird's eye chilies, shallots, and tomatoes, season with sugar and salt, then add calamansi juice, stir evenly, set aside. How to make soy sauce chili paste: put the sliced ingredients into a bowl, add pepper powder, sweet soy sauce, and calamansi juice, stir evenly, set aside. Serving suggestion: serve maranggi satay with lontong/warm white rice, tomato chili paste, soy sauce chili paste, and pickles if you like || enjoy...
strIngredient22: Cabe rawit merah /sesuaikan selera pedas nya

strInstructions: In a container, mix the meat with the ground spices. Add egg, tamarind, brown sugar, sweet soy sauce, breadcrumbs, pepper powder, salt, and bouillon powder to taste, stir evenly. Squeeze and shape into balls with the help of ice cream sticks. Steam until cooked. Drain. If you want to serve it grilled, baste lightly with a mixture of soy sauce + pepper while flipping all sides. Ready to be served.
strIngredient15: Mixture of soy sauce and pepper powder

strInstructions: Cut the beef according to taste. Blend all the ground spice ingredients. Add into the meat, add soy sauce, tamarind water, and salt. Stir evenly. After it's mixed evenly, wrap with papaya leaves. Let it sit for 1 hour at room temperature. After 1 hour, skewer the meat according to taste. Then grill over low heat so it cooks evenly and becomes tender. Set aside. To make the soy sauce chili paste, slice all the ingredients then add soy sauce. Stir evenly. Maranggi satay is ready to be served 😍.

Prepare all ingredients. Grind the marinade ingredients + tamarind water. Sauté the ground spices while stirring until fragrant and cooked. After the spices are cooked, add sweet soy sauce, stir again, add the meat, stir until mixed with the spices, remove and let sit for ±30 minutes. After marinating, stir-fry the meat while stirring until the meat is cooked, tender, and slightly dry, check the taste. Once it's right, remove, sprinkle with fried onions, serve with warm white rice and soy sauce chili paste.
strIngredient15: White rice + soy sauce chili paste

strInstructions: Prepare the satay ingredients. Cut the meat rather thinly and add baking soda. Let it sit for 30 minutes so the meat becomes tender. Then rinse with water. Grind the spices with a Chopper, then marinate the meat for 2 hours. Skewer the meat with satay sticks until finished. Then grill the meat with a pan or Teflon until cooked. Occasionally baste with the remaining spices. Prepare the ingredients, mix all ingredients. Stir evenly. Arrange the goat satay and soy sauce chili paste on a serving plate. Maranggi satay is ready to be eaten 😋.

Cut the meat into pieces, then wash clean, then soak in enough vinegar water until all the meat is submerged, let it sit for 15 minutes, then rinse and drain (the function is to remove remaining blood and gamey smell). Prepare the ground spices, then mix everything together and grind. Put the ground spices into the meat container. Then mix evenly by hand while squeezing. Cover the meat container, then let it sit in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes. I did 1 hour. Wash the satay sticks under running water, then skewer the meat onto the satay sticks until all the meat is used up; some of mine have 3 pieces, some 4 because the meat cuts are uneven. Let's make the soy sauce chili paste: wash clean and cut all the ingredients into pieces, then sauté all the ingredients (except tomatoes) with a little oil. After wilting, put them into a container with the tomato pieces. Stir evenly, then add soy sauce and set aside. Prepare the charcoal, then grill the satay while continuously fanning. Once cooked, serve with soy sauce chili paste and rice.

strMeal: Sate Maranggi Mudah Membuatnya Enak Rasanya 🥰
strInstructions: Thinly slice the beef lengthwise, about a finger wide. Blend all the ground spices until completely smooth using a little water, pour onto the meat, also add the additional spices, stir evenly, marinate the meat for at least 1-2 hours. After two hours, skewer the meat using satay sticks in a zigzag direction. Grill the satay with charcoal, so the taste is more delicious. It can also be grilled on a griller, occasionally baste with the remaining ground spice marinade earlier, grill the satay to the desired doneness. Maranggi satay is ready to be eaten directly or with tomato chili paste, sliced shallots, calamansi, and sweet soy sauce.

strMeal: Sate Kambing Maranggi (Tanpa Tusuk) Dengan Sambal Kweni Kecap
strInstructions: Prepare the ground spices, and also make tamarind water, then mix the tamarind water into the spices. Thinly slice the goat meat. Squeeze the papaya leaves, rub them onto the meat, let sit for 1 hour, after that rinse the meat clean quickly, drain. Coat the meat with the ground spices, let sit for 30 minutes. Heat a wok, grill the meat until cooked and browned. Make the dipping chili paste: slice the onions and chilies, chop the kweni mango, add soy sauce. Serve the maranggi satay with its kweni chili paste.
strIngredient16: Mangga kweni , karena ga punya tomat

strMeal: Sate Maranggi Sapi Dan Sambal Tomat Matah
strInstructions: Cut the meat into small pieces, wrap with papaya leaves, let sit for 2 hours. Coat the meat with ground spices and sweet soy sauce, let sit for at least 30 minutes. Skewer using satay sticks. Grill over coals or using a grill until cooked. How to make raw tomato chili paste (sambal tomat matah): coarsely pound the onions and chilies, mix with salt, sugar, and lime juice. Thinly slice the tomatoes, mix with the chili paste. Serve the satay with the raw tomato chili paste and sweet soy sauce. Recipe for a large portion: (I once made this for 10 kg of meat) Goat Satay + Maranggi-style Raw Tomato Chili Paste.
strIngredient1: Beef tenderloin + fat if you like

strInstructions: Cut the meat into pieces. Then dry roast the coriander and cumin, then grind the meat spices before marinating, cover with cut papaya leaves for 30 minutes. Sauté the spices with oil until fragrant, add tamarind water, palm sugar, soy sauce, Saori, bouillon powder, once it has set enough, remove. Then mix the spices into the meat pieces until evenly mixed for 1 hour, then skewer with satay sticks that I previously soaked in water so they don't burn easily. Then grill the satay over charcoal briquette fire until cooked, serve with chili paste and pickles.
strIngredient1: Grams or more of sacrificial beef and goat meat

strMeal: Sate Maranggi Ala Hj. Yetti (Versi Rumahan Grill Di Pan Tanpa Tusukan)
strInstructions: Grind all the ground spices in a chopper. Cut the meat (if you want a quick marination, slice it thinly) against the grain (choose a tender part like tenderloin/shank). Mix the meat pieces with the ground spices to marinate for 1-2 hours in the chiller. After 1-2 hours of marination, heat a pan (to make it simple), there's no need to skewer it, but if you want to skewer it, that's fine too. Grill in the pan without adding oil again because the meat will release its natural oil later. Keep grilling until caramelized, then at the end you can add coarsely chopped Indian red onions or regular onions to add texture (optional). After the satay is cooked, then prepare the freshly pounded tomato chili paste (sambal dadak tomat). Pound the chilies, shallots, garlic, add salt and flavor enhancer. Once smooth, add the large pieces of tomato that have been prepared, no need to pound too much, just press slightly. Then give it a squeeze of calamansi juice and spread it evenly in the chili paste. Hj. Yetti Purwakarta style Maranggi Satay is ready to be enjoyed with freshly pounded tomato chili paste and warm fluffy rice. Happy trying too. Happy recooking! Post your recook results too :).
strIngredient13: Freshly pounded tomato chili paste (sambal dadak tomat)

strInstructions: Marinate the chicken with all the spices, let sit for 30 minutes. Grill the chicken in a pan until both sides are browned. Serve.

Prepare all the necessary ingredients, dice the chicken meat fillet, grind the chicken meat marinade spices with the ground spices, stir until evenly mixed. Add sweet soy sauce, stir evenly again, let sit for 30 minutes so the spices absorb better, skewer 3-4 pieces of marinated chicken fillet onto a satay stick, repeat until finished. Prepare a non-stick pan, spread a little margarine, grill the satay on the pan, flipping back and forth so it cooks evenly, repeat until finished. Chicken Maranggi Satay is ready to be served.

Prepare the Chicken, cut the chicken breast into cube shapes (±3x3 cm). Wash quickly, drain, then dry using a kitchen paper towel so the spices absorb better. 4️⃣ Marinate the Chicken. Put the chicken into the spices. Stir evenly, massage lightly so it absorbs. Let sit for at least 1 hour (better 4 hours or overnight in the refrigerator). 👉 Because this is chicken breast, don't exceed 24 hours so the texture doesn't become mushy. Skewer the chicken onto satay sticks (3–4 pieces per skewer). Leave a little spice mixture for basting when grilling. Baste the satay with the remaining spices. Grill while flipping until cooked and slightly caramelized. Don't take too long so it doesn't dry out. Tomato chili paste: pound the onions and chilies, add salt and sugar. Stir with thin tomato slices, add calamansi juice.

Wrap the meat pieces with squeezed papaya leaves, let sit for 30 minutes. Mix meat + ground spices + pepper + salt + bouillon powder + brown sugar + coriander + soy sauce, stir evenly, let sit for 30 minutes. Skewer 4-5 pieces of meat per satay stick. Do this until all are used up. Heat the grill using low heat only. Spread a little margarine / oil. Grill the satay until the meat is no longer watery, flipping back and forth. Baste with soy sauce then grill again, flipping back and forth until cooked and slightly charred. Remove and serve with fresh vegetables (lalap) and soy sauce chili paste.

Prepare the ingredients for goat satay curry rice. Wash all the spice aromatics: cinnamon, star anise, cardamom, cloves, curry leaves, shallots, garlic, and black peppercorns. Wash the long-grain basmati rice clean, soak for 30 minutes, drain. Heat a wok pan, add ghee (minyak samin) and vegetable oil. Add coarsely chopped shallots + garlic, cardamom, cinnamon, star anise, cloves, and whole black peppercorns, sauté until fragrant (onions turn yellowish). Add the red base spice, five-spice powder (ngohiong), and curry powder, sauté again until fragrant. Add curry leaves and goat satay meat, sauté briefly. Add the basmati rice, Himalayan salt, and beef bouillon, stir evenly. Pour in mineral water, dried lemon, and raisins, stir evenly. Cover the pot, cook over medium-low heat. Cook until the water is completely absorbed by the rice. Open the pot lid, stir the curry rice, cook for a few moments. Cover the wok pan again and turn off the stove heat. Let it sit for 10 minutes, open the wok pan lid and stir the goat satay curry rice again. Goat satay curry rice is ready to be enjoyed while warm with cucumber slices, sunny-side-up egg, and emping melinjo.
strIngredient14: Red base spice plus dried shrimp (ebi)

strInstructions: Prepare the ground spices and sauté using cooking oil, season with salt, palm sugar, MSG, stir evenly and add tamarind water. Set aside. Squeeze the papaya leaves and place them in a basin as a base. Then place the pieces of goat meat and knead the goat meat with the sautéed ground spices. Knead evenly. Then cover with the squeezed papaya leaves. Wrap the meat for up to 30 minutes. After 30 minutes, skewer the meat using satay sticks. Spread a little oil on the satay grill and grill the satay on a Teflon pan. And flip the satay back and forth, occasionally basting with the remaining ground spices mixed with soy sauce.

Cut the goat meat into small pieces. Add all the spices, stir evenly. Let sit for 15 minutes. Soak the satay sticks for 10 minutes so they don't burn easily when grilled. Heat the oven. Skewer 3-4 pieces of meat onto the satay sticks. Then arrange on a grilling rack. Put into the middle rack of the oven. On the bottom rack, place the oven's black tray lined with aluminum foil to catch the drippings from the goat meat while grilling. Grill for 20 minutes at 150°C using top and bottom heat. Or until cooked, adjust to your respective ovens. Serve.

Prepare the required ingredients. Dice the goat meat. Squeeze the papaya leaves then wrap the cut meat with the papaya leaves. Leave it for 30 minutes. Cut and grind the shallots, garlic, ginger, candlenuts, pepper, and coriander. Put all the flavor enhancers into the ground spices. Take the meat out of the papaya leaf wrapping then mix it with the ground spices. Stir evenly then add sweet soy sauce. Stir evenly. Marinate the meat for 30 minutes.
