After 30 minutes, fry the marinated meat. Then, add brown sugar, enough water, and cook until the water reduces and the meat is cooked. Cook until the water reduces. Once reduced, it is ready to be served with a topping of your choice.

Prepare ingredients. Cut the meat into cubes or according to taste. Then marinate it to make it more tender for 30 minutes to 1 hour. Sauté the spices, the two onions, and the rest. Once fragrant, add the marinated meat. Stir the meat. Then add salt, flavor enhancer, and soy sauce. Stir again until the spices are absorbed. You may add a little water. Finally, add the chilies and onion. Stir until the onion and chilies wilt. Check the taste. Serve with warm rice.

Cut the meat into cubes, not too thin as the meat will become dry. Mix the meat with blended pineapple, let sit for 15 minutes. Rinse the meat with clean water, drain. Grind the shallots and garlic. Mix the meat with the ground spices, soy sauce, salt, pepper, and oil. Skewer the meat onto satay sticks. Arrange the satay in the air fryer. Grill at 180°C for 12 minutes. Flip the satay, continue grilling for another 12 minutes until cooked.

Cut the goat meat into small cubes, then skewer, 5 pieces per stick. Marinate the skewered meat with practical seasoning. Ready to be grilled until cooked. Don't forget to watch it while flipping it back and forth so it doesn't burn. To make the soy sauce seasoning, simply mix all the ingredients in a bowl. Ready to be served.

strMeal: Sate Buntel Kambing Sambal Kecap (Khas Solo)
strInstructions: Prepare all ingredients. Chop the meat until fine. Add egg, ground spices, and other spices. Chop again until all ingredients are evenly mixed. Then transfer the dough to a container. Prepare 1 satay stick. Take the dough according to the desired amount. Mold it onto the satay stick and compact it evenly and gently. Do this until the dough is used up. Heat water in a pot. Prepare a steamer. Brush it with oil. Steam the satay until cooked, ±10-15 minutes. Set aside. Prepare the basting sauce. Stir evenly. Baste the surface of the satay evenly. Heat a wok or charcoal grill. Grill the satay until cooked, flipping it back and forth so it cooks evenly. Prepare a small bowl. Put in all the soy sauce chili paste ingredients. Stir evenly. Ready to be served. #semangatmencoba 😊.

Wash and cut the meat along with its fat. Then put it into the previously washed and squeezed papaya leaves. Let it be for about 30 minutes. While waiting for the meat, you can prepare the marinade. Blend or grind the marinade, except for the ginger and kaffir lime leaves which just need to be crushed. Next, evenly mix the marinade into the meat. Wait at least 1 hour so the spices are absorbed. While waiting for the marination, you can prepare the soy sauce. Skewer the meat and fat according to taste, then grill. Done.
strIngredient20: Tusuk sate yang sudah direndam air selama 30 menit

strInstructions: Cut the goat meat into small pieces. Grate the peeled pineapple. Grind the marinade. Coat with the grated pineapple and marinade. Squeeze lightly. Let it sit for about 15 minutes. While waiting, prepare the grill. Skewer the goat meat until finished. Prepare the basting sauce. Mix soy sauce and cooking oil. Grill a few skewers of satay. Flip it back and forth, baste with the basting sauce. Grill until cooked. Repeat step 8 until finished. Satay is ready to be enjoyed with soy sauce chili paste or peanut sauce.
strIngredient12: Packets of sweet soy sauce (2000 rupiah size)

strInstructions: Cut the goat meat into pieces. Use the fat too. Wrap with papaya leaves for 30 minutes. Blend the marinade except for ginger and kaffir lime leaves. Mix all the marinade into the meat. Wait at least 30 minutes. Skewer the meat. Mix the basting sauce. Baste onto the satay while grilling. For the chili paste. Just slice it and mix with soy sauce.
strIngredient2: A few sheets of papaya leaves

strInstructions: 🧄Clean the goat meat, coat with lime juice, let sit for 15 minutes. 🧄Prepare the basting sauce. Grind the garlic, pepper, coriander, and salt. 🧄Wash the meat under running water, drain. Cut the meat into small pieces (according to taste) then skewer with satay sticks until finished. 🧄Transfer the ground spices to a container, pour enough cooking oil and sweet soy sauce. Stir evenly. 🧄Coat the skewered meat with grated pineapple then apply the basting ingredients. 🧄Grill to the desired doneness. 🧄Do this until finished. Making soy sauce chili paste: 🧄Slice the chilies and shallots. Dice the tomato into small pieces. 🧄Put them in one container then pour enough sweet soy sauce. Stir evenly. 🧄Serve the goat satay with warm rice or ketupat (rice cake). Enjoying it together is more fun 🤩🤩🤩.

Grind the shallots, garlic, coriander, candlenuts, salt, pepper, and pineapple. Cut the goat meat, mix with the ground spices and grated pineapple. Let the meat sit for 30 minutes so the spices and pineapple are absorbed. Skewer the meat onto satay sticks, baste with sweet soy sauce and oil. Grill the satay over coals until cooked, flipping back and forth and basting with the remaining spices.

strMeal: Sate Kambing Bumbu Ketumbar Sambal Kecap
strInstructions: Wash the meat clean, cut into cubes, and add wheat flour, stirring until evenly mixed; the aim is to remove the smell of the goat meat. Next, squeeze the papaya leaves then put them into the meat, stir evenly again, and let sit for 1 hour so the meat is tender. For the ground spices, grind the shallots, garlic, coriander powder, and salt, set aside. For the soy sauce chili paste, slice the shallots, red bird's eye chilies, and red tomatoes, put them in a bowl, add sweet soy sauce, then stir evenly. After 1 hour, wash the meat clean then drain, add the ground spices, and stir evenly. After that, add soy sauce, stir evenly again, and skewer the meat. Grill the meat over charcoal until cooked, serve with soy sauce chili paste.

Wash the goat meat clean, squeeze it with betel leaves, then wash again with lime juice, then rinse with clean water. Cut the goat meat according to taste then skewer it with satay sticks. Grind all the dipping sauce ingredients. Add water & soy sauce according to taste to the dipping sauce. Soak the skewered meat in the dipping sauce. Grill the satay until it smokes and put it back into the dipping sauce for 2x. Apply the basting sauce to the satay on the final grill. Grill the satay until cooked according to taste. Serve with sweet soy sauce and a sprinkle of pepper, sliced cabbage, shallots, and chilies. Happy trying.

Wash the papaya leaves clean, squeeze them, put them in a container, add the meat, put in the refrigerator overnight. Blend the ground spices then sauté with a little oil until cooked. Add to the meat (remove the papaya leaves first) then add soy sauce to taste, then put in the refrigerator (wait about 1 hour so the marinade absorbs). Skewer the satay then grill according to taste (don't forget to baste with the remaining spices so it absorbs more when grilled). Then serve (I put the rest back in the refrigerator to grill next time). Happy trying 🥰.

strMeal: Sate Goreng Kambing Anti Bau Prenggus
strInstructions: Key to Preventing Gamey Smell: Wash the meat quickly, don't soak it for long. Coat the meat with lime juice and baking soda, let sit for ±1 hour. Without rinsing, boil briefly in boiling water for ±15 minutes with 5 kaffir lime leaves. Remove, discard the boiling water. Cut the meat according to taste (I cut it into small cubes so it cooks faster and absorbs the spices). Grind the onions, the two chilies, coriander, cumin, and pepper. Sauté the spices until cooked and fragrant with 2 tbsp oil. Add lemongrass, kaffir lime leaves, ginger, galangal. Add the meat pieces. Add soy sauce and oyster sauce, as well as salt and sugar, stir evenly. Cook over low heat until caramelized and oily. Check the taste to your liking, then remove. Serve with sliced chilies and scallions / shallots. It tastes tender, spicy, savory, and sweet 😋.

strMeal: Ikan Nila Bakar Madu Teflon Mudah Simpel
strInstructions: Wash the tilapia (nila) clean. Mix all the spice ingredients. Stir evenly with cooking oil. Coat the fish. Store in the refrigerator for about 30 minutes. Heat a Teflon pan or any grill. Grill the fish on the Teflon while occasionally basting with the spices. Honey Grilled Tilapia is ready to be served! Happy trying!
strIngredient10: Cooking oil (because Blue Band ran out, haha)

strMeal: Ikan Bakar Pedas Teflon Mudah Sederhana
strInstructions: Wash the fish clean, you can use vinegar or lime juice. Grind garlic, shallots, and chilies. Mix with all ingredients. Stir everything with Blue Band. Coat the fish evenly. Do not throw away the rest because it will be used for the basting sauce later. Marinate first for about 30 minutes in the refrigerator. Heat the Teflon or any grill being used. Baste with the spices occasionally. Once it's flipped, do the same. A suggestion: when grilling, don't flip too often or it will fall apart. Spicy grilled fish is ready to be served! Happy trying!

Prepare the cleaned fish then coat with lime juice, let it sit for a while then wash clean again. Sauté the basting ingredients until fragrant and cooked, let it cool to room temperature. Soak the fish in the basting sauce for ±20 minutes so the spices absorb. Grill the fish until cooked on both sides, don't forget to baste periodically with the basting sauce. Serve.
Marinate the fish + dried tamarind slices (asam keping) and salt to taste. Then in a separate container, mix all the ingredients, stir evenly. Grill the fish then add enough spices.

Prepare all ingredients. Wash the fish clean & grind the spices. Sauté the ground spices along with the aromatic spices until fragrant & cooked. Then add the coconut milk powder that has been dissolved in water. Add the seasonings & pepper powder while checking the taste. Once the taste is right, add the fish. Cook until the spices reduce & absorb into the fish. Then roast/grill. The grilled mackerel (ikan salem) is ready to be served. Alhamdulillah ☺.

Mix lemon juice, salt, and water. Soak the fish for 1 hour, drain, and dry. Heat a pot, grease banana leaves with a mixture of margarine and oil. Line the pot with it, arrange the fish, and cover with banana leaves. Grill the fish for 5 minutes per side over medium heat. Flip only once so it doesn't fall apart. Mix the dabu-dabu chili paste ingredients, pour hot oil over it, and stir evenly. Serve the warm fish with dabu-dabu chili paste and white rice.
strIngredient11: Red/green bird's eye chilies, thinly sliced
strIngredient12: Melted margarine + cooking oil mixture for basting

strInstructions: Mix all the spices. Marinate the fish for a few hours before grilling. Grease the pan with margarine. Grill the fish on the pan greased with margarine. Grill until all sides are cooked. Remove and serve.

Clean the fish then marinate with lime/lemon juice and salt. Prepare the candlenuts then grind them for the base basting mixture with salty soy sauce, oil, lime/lemon, and sweet soy sauce. Don't forget to shape the pandan or lemongrass leaves into a brush for basting later. After that, separately grind the garlic, chilies, lemongrass, and galangal. Slice the shallots then set aside. Heat oil and cook the ground spices until cooked but not dry. Add flavor enhancer, salt, and sesame oil. Then heat the coals, wait until they become embers/low fire, then place the fish on the grill, occasionally basting the fish with the base basting mixture. Once it's half cooked, just continue with the second basting mixture that has been cooked and flavored until the fish is perfectly cooked, then remove.

Clean the pangasius fish pieces, then coat with turmeric powder for about 15 minutes. Prepare a Teflon pan, add butter/margarine then arrange the pangasius fish pieces, cover the Teflon, flip after a few minutes, once cooked remove. Arrange on a serving plate. Serve with chili paste according to taste.

Marinate the fish with lime juice and salt. Grind the spices, I used a blender and added a little water to make it smooth. Discard the water from the marinated fish then wash it. Fry the fish first so it doesn't fall apart later, then set aside. Cook the spices with a little oil or adjust to taste, until the spices release oil and change color, remove and set aside. Coat the fish with the spices, let it sit first so the flavor absorbs, once done it can be grilled. Grill using a Teflon pan, don't forget to flip it back and forth so it doesn't burn, if it seems done you can remove it. Serve with soy sauce chili paste, mix all the ingredients then add a little water.
strIngredient21: Bawang putih di geprek lalu iris tipis

strInstructions: 1. Clean the fish, then fry half cooked with preheated oil. 2. Prepare the grilling spices. Mix all the spice ingredients, stir evenly. The white base spices, salt, flavor enhancer, sugar, pepper powder, coriander powder, margarine, and water are all mixed into 1. After that, marinate the half-cooked fish with the spices. Or brush the spices onto it. 3. After being marinated, the fish is ready to be grilled. Heat a Teflon pan, add a little margarine. Then grill the fish. 4. Once cooked, the fish is ready to be served 🤗.
strIngredient7: White base spices (garlic, shallots, ground coriander)

strInstructions:
~ clean the fish, wash thoroughly then make slits on both sides
~ grind the spices and sauté until smooth, add all the dry spices, and also the sauce, sugar, and salt, stir evenly, check the taste, turn off the heat
~ put the fish into a Teflon pan lined with leaves, brush with spices, grill both sides until cooked, remove
~ serve

strMeal: Ikan Bakar Madu Saffron Sambal Dabu Dabu
strInstructions: Coat the fish with lime juice, let sit for 10 minutes then rinse clean. Mix warm water and Herati Saffron in a glass. Stir evenly. Mix the ground spices, salt, sugar, bouillon powder, honey, and cooking oil. Stir evenly. Add half of the Herati Saffron water mixture. Stir. Coat the whole body of the fish with the honey spice mixture. Let sit in the refrigerator for at least 15 minutes to absorb. The remaining fish spices can be sautéed until fragrant for a sauce. Heat a pan or grill. Line with banana leaves. Grill the fish over medium-low heat while occasionally basting with the remaining honey spices. Flip only once so the fish meat doesn't fall apart. Grill until cooked and slightly caramelized. Remove. Mix the shallots, bird's eye chilies, and tomato pieces in a bowl. Add salt, sugar, bouillon powder, and lime juice. Stir evenly while pressing slightly so the aroma comes out. Pour thoroughly hot oil over the chili paste, stir quickly. Add the remaining Herati Saffron water. Stir. The dabu-dabu chili paste is ready to be served with the grilled fish.
strIngredient1: Fresh fish, washed clean and slit
strIngredient13: Red bird's eye chilies, to taste
strIngredient15: Green bird's eye chilies, to taste
strIngredient17: Tomat merah, buang bijinya, potong dadu kecil

strInstructions: Clean the fish, split into 2... Add salt, squeeze lime juice over it. Prepare the ground spice ingredients, blend, then sauté until fragrant. Add salt, oyster sauce, sweet soy sauce, chili sauce, stir evenly. Grill the fish on a Teflon pan, line with banana leaves, brush the spices onto the fish... Flip back and forth until cooked, serve warm to eat with the family. For the soy sauce seasoning, thinly slice tomatoes, bird's eye chilies, shallots, add soy sauce and lime juice. Serve.

Wash the fish fillet, then add lime juice, let sit for 15 minutes. Sauté the ground spices until fragrant, then add soy sauce and salt, check the taste. Sauté evenly until cooked. Coat the fish fillet with the ground spices, marinate for 30 minutes. Heat a Teflon pan, add margarine. Grill the fish fillet until cooked. Grilled fish fillet is ready to be served.

Grind the Spanish mackerel (tenggiri) meat using a chopper, pour into a large bowl. Add the egg white, stir evenly. Grind the shallots and garlic. Add the ground spices, salt, sugar, pepper powder, stir evenly. Add coconut milk, stir evenly. Add Cap Pak Tani Gunung Tapioca Flour and sliced scallions. Stir evenly, not too long, just until mixed. Prepare the leaves that have been wiped clean and cut to the required size. Take 1-1.5 tbsp of the dough, place on a leaf, then secure with a toothpick. Grill on a Teflon pan, use medium-low heat, flip occasionally so both sides cook. Serve with peanut sauce, it so happens I had pecel sauce, that's fine, it tastes good too 😁.
strIngredient9: Banana leaves for wrapping, tear to taste

strInstructions: Wash the fish clean and coat with lime juice. Set aside. Grind the shallots, garlic, ginger, turmeric, galangal, candlenuts, and chilies. Sauté the ground spices and add the lemongrass, bay leaves, and kaffir lime leaves. Add sugar and salt. Cook until the spices are cooked, don't forget to taste. Marinate the fish, let sit for at least 30 minutes. The longer the marination, the more the spices will absorb. Grill the fish until cooked. Doneness according to taste. Grilled fish is ready to be served. Perfect to enjoy with fresh vegetables (lalapan) and chili paste.

Blend all the spice ingredients, set aside. Because I used water when blending, I dry roasted the blended spices first until there was no water, then poured in all the palm oil, and sautéed the spices until cooked. Add all the kitchen spices, sauté again until cooked and fragrant, check the taste, if it's okay turn off the stove. Take a banana leaf, place a bay leaf on it, coat the bay leaf with the sautéed spices, arrange the fish on the spices. Add more spices on top of the fish, followed by basil leaves and sliced tomatoes, and secure with toothpicks at both ends of the banana leaf. Do this for all the fish until finished. After everything is done, grill the pepes (wrapped fish) on a grill pan. Flip when one side looks charred, then press the pepes being grilled with a mortar and pestle, about 10 - 15 minutes or until the pepes doesn't release water, so the grilled fish is cooked perfectly, and the small bones inside the fish become soft. After that, remove the pepes, drain, and serve while hot.
strIngredient2: Whole batu banana leaves, tear into pieces and wilt

strInstructions: Clean and make slits on the fish. Set aside. Grind all the ground spice ingredients. Then sauté with a little oil. Add salt, pepper powder, brown sugar, and soy sauce. Cook until the spices are perfectly cooked. Melt margarine in a non-stick pan. Coat the fish with the spices. Grill in the pan over low heat until cooked. Do not flip too often so the fish doesn't fall apart.

Wash the fish clean and coat with lime juice. Let sit for 15 minutes, then wash again. Grind the spices and sauté until fragrant, add soy sauce, chili sauce, and flavor enhancer. Coat the fish with the spices, and let sit for 10 minutes. Heat a Teflon pan, grease with margarine. Cook the fish until done. Don't forget to flip and brush again with spices. Serve while warm.

Cut the duck into 6 pieces. If possible, ask the seller for help to make it easier. Then coat with lime juice (or 2 tbsp apple cider vinegar). Coat it all over and let sit for 10 minutes. Wash clean. Boil the duck with 1 liter of water and add bay leaves, kaffir lime leaves, lemongrass, galangal, ginger. Boil until tender. Grind the spices, then sauté until fragrant, pour in the duck boiling water so the sticky spices release. Put the spices into the duck boil, followed by salt, sugar, and soy sauce. Cook until absorbed, the water reduces to half. Check the taste and stir occasionally. Once reduced, pour in the coconut milk, let it boil, continue cooking with the pot covered until the broth reduces and thickens. Once cooked, serve with fresh vegetables (lalapan) and shrimp paste chili sauce (sambal terasi).
strIngredient7: Lemongrass, take the white part, crush

strMeal: Opor Bebek (+ Tips Agar Tidak Amis)
strInstructions: Wash the duck clean, roast/grill until the skin is dry. I used an air fryer at 200°C for 25 minutes, flipping it over. Grind the spices. Cut the duck into pieces. Sauté the ground spices until fragrant. Add the other spices. Sauté briefly. Add the duck. Stir well. Add a glass of water, salt, and sugar. Cover the pot. Cook until the duck is cooked, add coconut milk. Bring to a boil, check the taste.

Prepare all the ingredients and spices, wash the cut duck clean under running water. Make the ground spices. Grind all the ground spices, then sauté, add bay leaves, lemongrass, and galangal. Let it be until fragrant. Add the duck, stir-fry until it changes color. Then transfer to a pot, pour in the coconut water. Stir until boiling and the water reduces. Test the tenderness, once tender, add hot water. After boiling, add the thick coconut milk from 1 mature coconut. Stir so the coconut milk doesn't break, while preparing Bu Rudy's style Onion Chili Paste. Remove and ready to eat, serve with onion chili paste 😋.
strIngredient2: Mature coconut, take the coconut water
strIngredient19: Sambal bawang sambal bawang ala bu rudy

strInstructions: Cut the duck (into 12 pieces), then wash the duck meat clean. Finally, wash with lime/lemon juice. I didn't roast the duck meat because the duck we bought at Pasar Tani was already clean and the feathers were gone. If the duck meat is obtained from a live duck, it is better to roast the duck first before cutting it so the fine feathers are removed. Prepare all the necessary spices. Then dry roast the coriander and candlenuts until fragrant, then pound the roasted coriander until smooth. Set aside. Then grind the other ground spices (candlenuts, shallots, and garlic). Prepare the coconut milk. Squeeze the grated coconut with a little water. The first two squeezes are separated as thick coconut milk, then the rest is for making thin coconut milk. Next, sauté the ground spices with oil then add the finely pounded roasted spices. Sauté until it smells fragrant, then add the sliced spices. After that, add the duck meat, sauté briefly until water comes out of the duck meat, then add the thin coconut milk. Cook the duck meat until tender and the coconut milk reduces slightly. In cooking this, just use medium heat so the duck meat becomes really tender. After the duck meat is tender, add the thick coconut milk and flavor enhancers. Cook again until the broth is just a little. At this point, the oil from the duck and coconut milk will usually come out. If there's too much oil, I usually discard a little so it's not too oily. After that, check the taste. If the savory and sweet tastes are lacking, it can be corrected by adding salt, sugar, and flavor enhancer. Once the taste is OK, Klaten Duck Opor is ready to be served.
strIngredient6: Lime / lemon to wash the duck

strInstructions: Prepare the cleaned duck. Grind the garlic and salt, then mix with lime juice. Coat the inside of the duck with the spices... Add water. Boil the duck until tender and serve with raw bird's eye chili paste and crackers.

Grind the spices and sauté until fragrant. Add duck meat, sweet soy sauce, a little water, bay leaves, and lemongrass. Stir well. Pour in coconut milk, stir, and add brown sugar, salt, and flavor enhancer. Cook until the duck is tender. Finally, add tamarind water and adjust the seasoning.
strIngredient13: Small packets of Kara coconut milk

strInstructions: Wash the duck meat then soak it in lime juice for 15 minutes, then wash it again until clean. Put all boiling ingredients into 1 liter of water. Let it boil, add the duck meat. Boil for 5 minutes. Turn off the stove for 30 minutes with the pot covered, boil the meat again for 7 minutes. Blend all spices until smooth. Prepare cooking oil, sauté the ground spices until fragrant. Add a little water from the boiling ingredients to the sautéed spices. Put the sautéed spices into the duck boiling pot. Add palm sugar, soy sauce, salt, flavor enhancer, and 1 packet of Kara coconut milk. After the water reduces, add 1 packet of Kara coconut milk until it thickens. Check the taste. Duck opor is ready to be served with a sprinkle of fried onions.

Wash the duck under running water, repeat 2x, then soak the duck in water mixed with 1-2 tsp of vinegar. Grind the spices except bay leaves, lemongrass, galangal, ginger, and kaffir lime leaves. Better to use a blender; grinding spices manually is tiring. Pressure cook the duck for about 15 minutes after the cooker hisses. Don't forget to salt the duck so it's not bland. Sauté the ground spices and add the other ingredients. Afterward, put the pressure-cooked duck into the sautéed spices, add a little water (just add a bit of the cooking broth). Then add coconut milk, check the taste... and voilà, yellow duck opor is ready... shhh, if you want to fry it, just take the duck out, it's savory.
strIngredient13: Instant coconut milk as desired (thick or thin)
strIngredient15: Salt, sugar, and a little mushroom bouillon (Totole)

strInstructions: Coat the cleaned and cut duck meat with grated pineapple to make it tender easily. Let it sit for 30 minutes. Sauté the ground spices until fragrant and wilted. Add the duck meat and other spices, stir well, and let sit for 3 minutes. Add thin coconut milk, cover. Adjust seasoning. Let the coconut milk reduce. Check the doneness; if it's somewhat tender, add thick coconut milk. Let it boil for a while, remove from heat. Serve Duck Opor with a sprinkle of Fried Onions.

Tips to prevent duck meat from smelling musty after cooking: ideally, after plucking the feathers, roast/grill the duck over hot coals until the fat renders out. Don't forget to flip it so it doesn't burn. Cut the duck into 8 pieces and wash thoroughly. Heat cooking oil, sauté the ground spices until fragrant, add brown sugar, bay leaves, and lemongrass. Add water, add duck meat, cover, and wait until the spices are absorbed and the duck is tender. Once the duck is tender, add coconut milk and enough water. Wait until cooked, taste, add Royco, and remove from heat.

To avoid odors, make sure the duck is clean from remaining feathers. Cut and discard the oil gland near the tail (brutu) and excess fat in the abdominal cavity. Wash under running water, then soak in water with lime juice for 15 minutes. Rinse. Boil the duck submerged in water (put the duck in before turning on the heat) for about 5 minutes until the dirty foam rises. Turn off the heat. Discard the dirty boiling water. Wash the duck and cooking utensils thoroughly under running water. Then boil again with 1.3 liters of fresh water, in a clean pot/wok. Add all the spices, both ground and whole. Cook until the duck is perfectly cooked and tender. To make it tender quickly, cover the wok. To reduce the water, open the lid. But, we won't reduce the water completely because we'll use it to make 'kremes' (crispy flakes). After the duck is tender, turn off the heat. Let the duck soak in the braising liquid for 30 minutes. Then drain. Strain the leftover braising liquid. We will use 500 ml to make kremes. Heat 1-2 liters of cooking oil over low heat. Making Kremes: Mix all the ingredients except baking soda. Stir until well combined with no lumps. Then mix in the baking soda and stir well. Transfer the batter into a bottle or glass covered with plastic and tied with a rubber band. Then poke many holes in the lid. After the oil is hot enough, set to medium heat. Pour the kremes batter from a height of 30-40 cm above the oil with a circular motion covering the oil surface. After the oil bubbles reduce and the batter looks firm, fold it. Flip once. Continue frying until dry. Alternatively, fry until half dry, then remove and cool. Fry again in hotter oil until crispy. Remove and drain until the remaining oil completely drips off. Store the kremesan in a jar lined with oil-absorbing kitchen towels. Seal tightly to maintain crispness. Fry the duck over high heat, sprinkle with kremes batter. Flip just once. Once the kremes is firm, remove and drain until the excess oil completely drips off. Serve the fried duck with its kremesan.
strIngredient20: Tepung tapioka cap pak tani gunung

strInstructions: Wash the duck. Coat with lime juice and salt for 30 minutes, then wash thoroughly until the water runs clear. Blend the ground spices with a little water. Put the duck, ground spices, aromatic spices, and enough water into a pressure cooker until the duck is submerged. Close the pot, cook over medium heat until it hisses. Lower the heat, cook for 30 minutes. Then let it sit until the hot steam is gone. Heat the oil until it is really hot. Fry the duck skin-side down, flip, fry until browned. Serve with cucumber slices and sambal korek (simple chili paste). Or mango chili paste for extra freshness.
strIngredient1: Muscovy duck (entok), cut into 12 or 14 pieces, discard the tail (tunggir) and excess fat

strInstructions: Prepare the required ingredients. Coat the duck with lime juice, let sit for 30 minutes, then wash again until clean. Grind all ground spice ingredients. I blended them with a chopper using some of the boiling water. Once smooth, pour into the pressure cooker. Add the ground spices and stir. Then add salt. Stir again until even. Add all the lemongrass and kaffir lime leaves, then arrange the duck meat in the pressure cooker. Pressure cook for 30 minutes (depending on your respective pressure cooker). Once cooked, open and let it cool, then take out the duck pieces. Fry until dry. Set aside. Take the remaining spices, boil until the water evaporates, then grind all the Mango Chili Paste ingredients. Once smooth, pour the hot oil left over from frying the duck over it. Add sliced mango. Mango Chili Paste is ready to serve. Surabaya Fried Duck with Mango Chili Paste and Braised Spices is ready to be served.
strIngredient2: Duck, cut into pieces, washed clean

strInstructions: Coat the duck with lime juice & salt, let sit for 10 minutes, then wash thoroughly & cut to taste (I cut it into 8). Blend the spices until smooth, sauté with a little oil until fragrant & cooked, add kaffir lime leaves, lemongrass & bay leaves, add coconut water, put in the duck pieces, salt, sugar & mushroom bouillon, cook until tender & check the taste. Remove, drain & let it cool. Fry the braised duck until slightly dry, serve with sambal matah (raw shallot & lemongrass relish).
Prepare the ingredients. Grind the ground spices. Pour the ground spices over the duck, add water then cook (pressure cook) until tender. Remove, fry. Serve.

Prepare the boiled duck and discard the water. Add the spices: coriander powder, Selera Ayam Goreng Lengkuas seasoning, and water. Boil until the water reduces, check the taste beforehand. Fry in hot oil over medium heat until evenly cooked. Don't let it get too dry so it's more delicious. Remove and drain. Wash the vegetables clean, peel the cucumber skin, cut. For the cabbage, fry first until crispy or just wilted. The stink beans (petai) can be fried or raw. Arrange on a plate before serving.
strIngredient2: Packet of Selera Ayam Goreng Lengkuas (galangal fried chicken seasoning)

strInstructions: Prepare the ingredients. Blend the ground spices then sauté with enough cooking oil. Then add turmeric powder, coriander powder, and pepper powder. Next, add the whole spices. Stir until the water reduces and the spices are fully cooked (the aroma comes out). Then add the duck. Stir until the duck is coated with spices. Add enough water. Boil/braise the duck until tender (if the water reduces but the duck isn't tender yet, you can add more water and braise until tender). Once the duck is tender, it's ready to be fried and served with other accompaniments (here I pair it with young mango chili paste, Madura-style black chili paste, the remaining braising liquid that I thickened, fried tofu and eggplant, and fresh vegetables/lalapan).
strIngredient21: Air (bisa ditambah jika bebek kurang empuk)

strInstructions: To prevent the duck from smelling fishy, discard the oil gland (brutu). After cleaning, you can add lime juice. Put in the pressure cooker: the duck meat and all the spices. Add water, salt, coriander powder, and other accompaniments. Usually, the braising liquid needs to be saltier so it absorbs better. But again, it depends on taste. Cook until the desired doneness & tenderness. If it's not tender enough & the spices haven't absorbed enough, just boil it again but no need to pressure cook. Just boil normally. Check the taste first. If it's not salty enough etc., add more according to taste. After checking the taste & desired tenderness, just drain & cool the duck then fry it. Don't forget to use crushed garlic to drop into the hot oil so the duck is more fragrant when fried.
strIngredient2: Water or more for braising the duck. Estimate the amount
strIngredient3: Packet of braising spice. Bought from the spice grinder at the market
strIngredient5: Large lemongrass. If unavailable, use small ones but many

strInstructions: Cut the Duck into sizes according to taste, pour Lemon juice over it and sprinkle enough Salt. Let sit for about 10 minutes, then wash clean and drain. Blend Shallots, Garlic, Ginger, Turmeric, and Coriander until smooth. Mix the ground spices into the cleaned duck, add Salt, Flavor Enhancer, and Brown Sugar. Let sit for about 15 minutes. Braise the duck that has been coated with ground spices, add crushed Galangal (Laos), and add enough water. Use a pressure cooker to get tender duck meat. Braise for approximately 30 minutes. The duck is ready to be fried and eaten 😘.

Wash the Duck clean and coat with lime juice. Cut into 4-6 pieces. Wash again. Put it in the pressure cooker along with the braising spices, add water and cook for approximately 30 minutes. Remove and drain the Duck from the pressure cooker then fry in hot oil until cooked. Use a chopper for the green chili paste ingredients. Heat a wok then sauté. Put the fried Duck into the sautéed green chili paste. Add a little water, salt, sugar, and flavor enhancer. Sauté until the spices are absorbed. Serve the green chili Duck on a plate while hot.

Wash the duck, drizzle with lime juice and salt to remove the fishy smell. Let sit for 15 minutes. Grind spice mixture A along with the aromatic spices except bay leaves (I used a Chopper), add a little water. Once smooth, set aside. Grind spice mixture B (chilies) by adding a little oil (oil, guys, not water). Wash the duck that was marinated with lime and salt, arrange it in a wok, add ground spice mixture A along with bay leaves, pepper powder, coriander powder, bouillon powder, salt, and tamarind water. Then braise. Once the duck is considered tender and cooked, remove and drain. The remaining braising spices are cooked again until the water evaporates; once the oil comes out, add the ground chilies and sugar, stir the spices so they don't burn to process into black spices. Use very low heat. After the spices turn black, lower the heat even more (like it's about to die) while stirring. Fry the duck. For serving, you can add green chili paste. Green chili paste ingredients: fry green bird's eye chilies and green tomatoes. Crush raw garlic, add the fried chilies and tomatoes, salt, and sugar. Crush until smooth then pour hot oil over it.

Wash the duck clean. Give it a squeeze of lemon juice, let sit for 30 minutes, then wash again. Mix and stir the duck evenly with the ground spices, then pour in water. Add salt and bouillon powder, cook over medium heat until the water evaporates. Fry.

Grind the ingredients for the ground spices and sauté until cooked, add water, then add lemongrass, bay leaves, galangal, and kaffir lime leaves. Add the duck, wait until cooked and tender, then fry / you can also use a pressure cooker. Add chilies and garlic, add a little salt and flavor enhancer, then pound. Once smooth, add 3 spoons of hot oil. Once cooked, serve together.

strMeal: Bebek Goreng Surabaya (Kremesan Kayak Bebek Sinjay)
strInstructions: Coat the duck with lime juice and salt, leave it for 30 minutes (so it doesn't smell fishy), after that wash it clean. Prepare a pressure cooker, add the duck, ground spices, lemongrass, bay leaves, kaffir lime leaves, add water until it covers all the duck (not too much), add 2 tbsp salt and 1/2 tbsp MSG (the amount of salt can be reduced or added, so the spices absorb even though using a pressure cooker, the water needs to be a bit salty), do not add sugar so that when the duck and spices are fried, they do not burn. Close the pressure cooker, cook for 15-30 minutes counted from when the pressure cooker hisses. The cooking time is adjusted to your respective pressure cooker, the desired result is a duck that is tender but still firm and doesn't fall apart; in my pressure cooker, it takes 30 minutes. After 15-30 minutes, turn off the pressure cooker, release the steam, open the pressure cooker and take the duck, cool it first then fry the duck until the skin is crispy. Set aside. Divide the leftover duck braising liquid into 2, one for the yellow sauce on the rice, one for braising the spice topping. Yellow sauce for rice: add 1 ladle of cooking oil, 1 tsp turmeric powder to the leftover braising liquid, boil until it thickens and is slightly salty (needs to be slightly salty because if it is poured on the rice it won't taste too salty). Once done, set aside. Spice topping: add grated galangal, coarsely chopped candlenuts, and coriander to the leftover braising liquid. Boil until the water evaporates and the spices are yellowish. Strain and take only the spices then fry until browned using medium-hot heat. Once done, set aside. Shrimp paste chili sauce (Sambal terasi): fry all ingredients except brown sugar. Pound or use a chopper on all ingredients together with the brown sugar and add salt and MSG. Once done, fry the pounded chili sauce again, add 3 tbsp of yellow sauce for rice, cook until fully cooked. Once done, set aside. Mango chili sauce (Sambal pencit): pound garlic, bird's eye chilies, salt, and sugar. Add grated young mango, mix evenly, pour hot leftover oil from frying the duck and shrimp paste chili sauce ingredients. Set aside. Serving method: prepare white rice and duck on a plate, pour 3-4 tbsp of yellow sauce on the rice, sprinkle the duck with the spice topping, add shrimp paste chili sauce and mango chili sauce on the side of the plate. Surabaya duck is ready to be served. Done.
strIngredient1: Ducks, cut into 4-8 pieces each, discard the tail so it doesn't smell gamey
strIngredient10: Young galangal, grated/chopped with a chopper

strInstructions: Cut and wash the duck clean. Coat with lime juice then let sit for 15 minutes. Rinse until clean. Grind the spices. Heat the oil then sauté the spices until fully cooked. Add the duck then add coconut water until all is submerged. Boil for 15 minutes. Turn off the heat. Let sit for 30 minutes. Add salt and bouillon powder. Cook again for 15 minutes. Fry over high heat just briefly until browned. Cover the wok so the oil doesn't splatter. Remove and drain. Ready to be eaten with warm rice.

Clean the duck, remove the fat from its tail, coat with lime juice, let sit for 10 minutes then rinse. Boil water, put in the duck, stir and cook until it boils again, turn off the heat, let the duck sit in the pot for 5 minutes then remove and drain (discard the first boiling water). This is done to remove dirt, remaining blood, and fat. Prepare the spices and grind them. Sauté the ground spices until fragrant, add the whole spices. Add the drained duck, stir evenly, add 500 ml of water, salt, sugar, braise over low heat until the duck is tender and the water reduces, and the duck is ready to be fried or grilled.

First, clean the duck, cut it according to taste, then marinate it with 3 tbsp of vinegar. Let it sit for 30 minutes, then wash thoroughly and set aside. Grind or use a chopper for all the spices. Then pour all the ground spices and the duck into a wok, add coconut water, and braise for 1 hour; don't forget to cover it. Add the bay leaves, kaffir lime leaves, lemongrass, ginger, and galangal that have been crushed. Once the liquid has reduced, remove the duck. Then divide the remaining braising spices into two: one for the spicy black seasoning, and the other for the savory seasoning. To make the black seasoning, add pounded bird's eye chilies to some of the spices, along with 1 tbsp of rawon seasoning. Sauté, adding a little leftover oil from frying the duck until fragrant and the oil separates; you can optionally add a little sugar. For the savory seasoning, just add oil and sauté until the oil separates. No need to add any more spices, it's already very delicious, savory, and salty.
strIngredient21: Bumbu rawon instan boleh merk apa aja

strInstructions: Prepare all the ingredients to be used. Wash the duck and its liver thoroughly. Cut into pieces according to taste. Then drizzle with lime juice, let sit for about 30 minutes, rinse again. Prepare the ground spices. Then grind the spices. Dry roast the grated coconut mixed with 2 tbsp of ground spices & salt. Roast over low heat and add a little cooking oil so the serundeng (roasted coconut) will be more savory later. Keep stirring until the grated coconut is cooked and turns brown. Sauté the ground spices until fragrant with a little cooking oil. Then add the duck meat, stir evenly until the meat turns pale. Then pour in water, add salt, flavor enhancer, and sugar. Also add the tamarind water. Cook the duck meat for about ±40 minutes, then add the liver. Cook again for about ±15-20 minutes or until tender and the water reduces. Stir occasionally. After that, separate the meat and liver from the spices. Fry the duck briefly, remove and drain. Then grind the serundeng until all the oil comes out. For the black seasoning, add the remaining braising spices with the leftover oil from frying. Cook over low heat while continuously stirring for about ±30 minutes until it turns black. Be careful not to burn it. Don't forget to check the taste. If it's right, remove from heat. Black Spice Fried Duck (Madura style) is ready to be served.
strIngredient9: For frying the duck and frying the black seasoning

strInstructions: Cut the duck according to taste, then coat with lime juice. Let sit for 15 minutes. Prepare the other ingredients, & the ground spices. Put the duck, ground spices, other ingredients, and water into a wok. Cook until it boils. Add sugar, salt, bouillon, and pepper powder. Stir evenly, cook again until the water reduces. Don't forget to check the taste. Then remove from heat. Fry the duck, and it is ready to be eaten 🥳.

Grind all spices except kaffir lime leaves, bay leaves, and lemongrass. Sauté all spices, kaffir lime leaves, bay leaves, and lemongrass until cooked. Add the cleaned duck (discard the tail so it doesn't smell). Stir the duck until evenly coated with spices. Add seasoning: salt and flavor enhancer. Pour in all the coconut water. Cover the pot then lower the heat after the coconut water boils. Braise until the duck is tender and the water reduces (I braised it for 1 hour). You may also use the 5-30-7 method but it must be repeated up to 3 times. Check the taste, if it's not salty enough add salt. Fried duck tastes better if it's salty. Fry the duck in hot oil. Serve with fresh vegetables (lalapan) and chili paste.

Wash the duck thoroughly, add enough water, put in bay leaves, ginger, salt, and flavor enhancer. Blend / pound shallots, garlic, coriander, turmeric powder, and candlenuts (miri). Add the spices, boil for 30 minutes over low heat, turn off and let sit for 1 hour, boil again for 20 minutes, turn off and wait 30 minutes, open and test the tenderness with a fork. Fry and serve with chili paste according to taste. Happy trying 🦆.
strIngredient1: Duck, cut into pieces for side dish

strInstructions: Clean the duck, cut it into pieces. (Optional: The tail/parson's nose (brutu) part can be discarded, or scraped out and all the fat in that area discarded) Then marinate with salt and lime juice for about 15 minutes. Rinse clean. Prepare the ground spices. Put the duck, ground spices, lemongrass, kaffir lime leaves, water, and salt into a wok. Cook for about 35 minutes. Then remove the duck and set aside first. (Optional) because the result of this braising has a lot of oil, I set aside some of the oil to add to cooking fried rice/noodles. 😁 The remaining braising liquid can be used to braise tofu and tempeh. Or used to cook savory rice. Put the coconut into the remaining braising broth, and cook while stirring until the liquid evaporates. When ready to serve, fry the duck, and then the coconut. Ready to be served.
strIngredient2: Lime juice and salt for marinating chicken
strIngredient8: Grated coconut, half young half old

strInstructions: Wash the duck thoroughly. Dip into vinegar or lime juice or mirin just to remove the fishy smell. Wash again. Set aside. Boil all the ingredients. Dip the duck in. Stir. Braise over medium heat until the water reduces and the duck is tender. Leave it overnight in the refrigerator. Heat oil. Add kaffir lime leaves. Fry the duck over medium-high heat until browned. Remove. Caution: it might splatter when frying. I usually use a frying pan cover. Be careful not to burn it.
strIngredient1: Duck, cut into 4, washed clean. Feet, tail (brutu), head not used
strIngredient16: Helai daun jeruk purut untuk menggoreng

strInstructions: After the duck is cleaned, put it into the rice cooker pot. Mix the duck, water, fried chicken seasoning, and aromatic spices. Add 1 tsp of salt if necessary. Cook in the rice cooker just like cooking rice, let it be until cooked. Making the black seasoning: sauté the white base spices with bird's eye chilies, lemongrass, kaffir lime leaves, and bay leaves. Add broth water, instant soto seasoning, and instant rawon seasoning. Stir evenly and check the taste. After the duck is cooked, separate it from its broth then fry/air fry the duck until browned. Serving: serve the black seasoning fried duck with rice and fresh vegetables (lalapan).
strIngredient13: Orange bird's eye chilies, sliced / ground

strInstructions: Cut the duck roughly the size of the duck thigh. Put it into the pressure cooker. Add the spices and water. The water should submerge the duck. Stir evenly. Pressure cook for 35 minutes (calculated from when it starts hissing). Wait for the temperature to drop before opening. Drain the duck. Fry in plenty of oil until browned. Drain. Chili paste (Sambal): grind the chilies, onion, and garlic. I used a chopper. Heat oil. Fry the chili paste until cooked. Don't forget to add salt and bouillon. Serve the fried duck with rice, chili paste, and fresh vegetables (lalapan). Afiyet olsun!
strIngredient1: Bone-in duck meat, cut into pieces
strIngredient11: Red bird's eye chilies, or to taste

strMeal: Ikan Nila Kukus Saus Manis Thailand (Versi Asam Jawa)
strInstructions: Steam the fish for 15 minutes in boiling water until cooked. Stir the sauce ingredients until even, if you don't like it raw you can cook it briefly. Heat 3 tbsp of cooking oil, fry the scallions until fragrant, mix into the sauce. Serve the fish on a plate, pour the sauce evenly over it, the fish is ready to be enjoyed.
strIngredient4: Tamarind, actually using calamansi is fresher, but I didn't have any, so I replaced it with tamarind

strInstructions: Prepare all ingredients. Clean the fish, then fillet the meat, leaving the head to the tail intact, coat with lime juice. In the photo I didn't fillet it. Make the marinade, grind the garlic, add mushroom bouillon, pepper powder, and salt. Coat the fish with the spices, egg, then marinate +/- 30 minutes. While waiting for the marination to finish. Prepare the sweet and sour ingredients. Cut the pineapple. Carrots are cut lengthwise thinly, tomatoes are finely diced. Cucumbers do not need to be peeled, split and remove the seeds, cut in a zigzag pattern (triangles). Prepare the sauce. Crush the garlic, then finely chop. Chop the red chilies. Then sauté with a little oil. Once fragrant and wilted, add tomato sauce, a little salt, mushroom bouillon, sugar, & water, cook briefly 1-2 minutes. Dissolve cornstarch with a little water, then pour it in. Stir until it bubbles. Then add the pineapple, tomato, carrot, and cucumber pieces, stir briefly, then remove. Arrange the fish on a plate, then pour the hot sweet and sour sauce over it. Enjoy 🤗.

Put into the pot: tamarind, salt, turmeric, ginger, raw onion, and fragrant oil. Cook until done and the water reduces (so the broth is thick). Sauté the shallots and chilies, add lemongrass, scallions, and tomatoes into the oil. Add the spices to the fish then cook for 1 minute. Add palm sugar. Serve.

Prepare the ingredients. Here I use fish fillet, mix it with egg white, cornstarch, oyster sauce, salt, and pepper. Fry in hot oil until golden and cooked. For the sauce, sauté garlic, onion, bell pepper, and cucumber. Add tomato sauce, oyster sauce, salty soy sauce, and water. Add seasoning and vinegar. Check the taste. Cut the fish then pour the sweet and sour sauce over it. And it is ready to be served.

strMeal: Escabeshe Ikan Asam Manis Khas Filipina
strInstructions: Fry the fish that has been drizzled with salt and lemon juice, until a crust forms. Remove and set aside. Prepare the vegetables and onions that have been cut. Heat oil, sauté ginger until fragrant then add garlic and onion, sauté until fragrant. Add carrots and bell pepper. Add water, sweet soy sauce, oyster sauce, and vinegar, stir evenly. Add salt, pepper powder, and granulated sugar, stir evenly. Prepare the cornstarch solution. Pour the cornstarch solution. Stir until thickened. Remove. Pour over the fried fish. Serve with warm rice.

Prepare ingredients, wash the fish fillet clean then slice into cubes, marinate with pepper powder, salt, and bouillon powder to taste, let sit for at least 10 minutes. Take 7 tbsp of seasoning flour, then mix with ±14 tbsp ice water, the texture shouldn't be too runny or too thick, put the remaining flour on a plate. Dip the fish into the wet batter, then coat with dry flour, I only did it 1x because I don't want a thick flour texture, heat enough cooking oil in a pan over medium heat, then fry the fish until yellowish, do this until finished, I fried it 2 times. Prepare a wok, put in 1 tbsp cooking oil, then sauté the onion until fragrant, then add the cucumber, sauté for about 1 minute only then remove, pour the liquid seasoning into the wok (use low heat) stir, then add the cornstarch solution, stir evenly, check the taste first, the texture of the seasoning is rather thick, if it feels right, turn up the heat then put the fried fish fillet in, stir evenly, then put the onion and cucumber back in, stir evenly again, turn off the heat. Ready to be served.

Wash the fish clean then coat with lime juice, salt, and bouillon powder, let sit for a while. Cut all the sauce ingredients, set aside. Heat cooking oil, fry the fish until cooked but not dry. Sauté garlic until fragrant, then add onion, red chilies, and carrots. Stir evenly. Add a little water, cook until carrots are tender. Add tomato sauce and chili sauce, also add salt, granulated sugar, and bouillon powder. Stir evenly. Finally, add the cornstarch solution and pineapple, cook briefly until thickened, check the taste, turn off the heat. Place the fish on a serving plate then pour the sauce over it (I deliberately separated the sauce so it remains fresh when my husband comes home later). Happy trying 😊.
strIngredient10: Cornstarch, dissolve with a little water

strMeal: Ikan Gabus Goreng Tepung Saus Asam Manis
strInstructions: Prepare Ingredients. Marinate the Fish with salt and mushroom bouillon, set aside. Mix Wheat Flour and Rose Brand Cornstarch, set aside. Put the marinated fish into the flour mixture, stir evenly while pressing. Heat Oil, add the marinated snakehead (gabus) fish fillet. Fry until cooked or golden brown. Remove and drain from oil. Making Sweet and Sour Sauce; Heat oil briefly then add garlic, sauté until fragrant. Add carrots, tomato sauce, oyster sauce, and water, stir evenly. Add onion, scallion, and Rose Brand cornstarch solution, stir evenly. Add salt, mushroom bouillon, and sugar, stir evenly. Check the taste. Arrange the flour-fried fish on a serving plate, pour the sweet and sour sauce over it. Sweet and Sour Flour Fried Snakehead Fish is ready to be served.

strMeal: Ikan Nila Saus Asam Manis Dengan Taburan Udang Rebon
strInstructions: Clean the tilapia (ikan nila) and make slits in its flesh. Marinate the fish with 1/2 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp pepper powder, marinate for 10 minutes. While waiting for the marination, finely chop 3 red chilies, 2 cloves of shallots, 2 cloves of garlic, and 1/2 a tomato. Dissolve 8 grams of tamarind in 100ml of water. Fry the marinated tilapia over medium heat until slightly browned and crispy on the skin, once cooked remove and drain. Sauté the finely chopped shallots and garlic with a little oil over low heat, sauté until fragrant. Once fragrant, pour in the tamarind water, then add the chopped red chilies, tomatoes, and add 10 grams of palm sugar. Add 1/2 tsp bouillon powder and 1/2 tsp salt. For aroma, also add 1 crushed lemongrass stalk and cook over low heat until the sauce thickens. While waiting for the sauce to cook, toast/roast 5 grams of small shrimp (udang rebon) until the color turns golden then remove. The sauce is done, plate the fish and pour enough cooked sweet and sour sauce over it, then sprinkle with the toasted small shrimp. Add garnishes to make it beautiful and attractive. Sweet and sour tilapia fish with small shrimp sprinkle is ready to be enjoyed.

Fry the salted fish until half cooked, drain. Heat oil, sauté sliced shallots, garlic, chilies, and tomatoes until fragrant. Add salt, sugar, flavor enhancer, oyster sauce, sweet soy sauce, and Worcestershire sauce , stir evenly. Add water little by little, put in the salted fish, cook over medium heat until the water reduces a bit and the spices are absorbed.

Fry the pindang fish, set aside.
Sauté the shallots, garlic, red chilies, and tomatoes.
Add tamarind water, soy sauce, pepper powder, salt, mushroom bouillon, and sugar. Stir well, add the pindang fish, cook for 10 minutes, and check the taste. Turn off the stove, transfer to a bowl, and serve.
strIngredient10: Large red chili / 3 curly chilies ➡️ even more delicious if you add pieces of green chili

strInstructions:
Wash the tuna fish clean, cut it into small pieces or according to taste, then coat the tuna with lime juice while squeezing gently, and let it sit for ± 3 minutes. After 3 minutes, wash the tuna clean again, then boil the tuna, add enough salt, and boil for 5 minutes. (Do not boil too long so the tuna does not fall apart). Once 5 minutes have passed, remove and drain. Set aside.
Peel the shallots, garlic, and ginger. Wash clean: shallots, garlic, ginger, curly red chilies, and devil's bird's eye chilies. Then grind the shallots, garlic, curly red chilies, devil's bird's eye chilies, and ginger, adding a little salt and water. Set aside.
Prepare a container/plate/bowl, add Kentucky crispy instant chicken seasoning flour, then coat the previously boiled tuna, fry the tuna until cooked and golden brown, and repeat until finished. Once finished, set aside.
Heat cooking oil, sauté the ground spices, add kaffir lime leaves, and sauté until fragrant and paste-like. Then add tamarind water, enough flavor enhancer, and brown sugar; check the taste, and if it is not salty enough, you can add salt. If it is not spicy enough, you can add chili powder (optional). Then add the tuna, stir evenly, and cook until half dry (cook until the tamarind water reduces) while stirring constantly so it doesn't burn.
Once cooked, turn off the stove; the spicy sweet and sour tuna is ready to be eaten with warm rice or as a side dish for ketupat. Happy trying.
strIngredient6: Kentucky crispy instant chicken seasoning flour (about 10 - 15 tbsp or to taste)
strIngredient13: A thumb-sized piece of brown sugar

strMeal: Ikan Gabus Asin Masak Asam Manis
strInstructions:
Cut the salted snakehead fish according to taste, then rinse clean. Slice the two types of chilies diagonally and thinly slice the two types of onions. Set aside.
Fry until cooked using a Deep Fryer Pot from Asta, remove, and drain.
Sauté the sliced ingredients until wilted and fragrant.
Add the previously fried snakehead fish along with tomatoes, stir evenly.
Pour in the tamarind solution and brown sugar, add bouillon powder and Cap Kapal Salt, stir evenly, check the taste, and let it sit until the water reduces slightly and the spices are absorbed.
Pour onto a serving plate and enjoy.

strMeal: Ikan Nila Saus Asam Manis Simpel
strInstructions:
Grind the marinade ingredients, then coat the cleaned fish.
After the marinade is evenly coated on the fish, also add tapioca flour and cornstarch to the fish.
Fry the fish until golden and somewhat dry.
Coarsely chop the garlic for the sauce and slice the onion rather thinly.
Sauté the garlic with a little margarine and add the onion. After the onion wilts, add the other sauce ingredients and cook until boiling.
If you feel it is not thick enough, you can add cornstarch. After cooking, you can sprinkle roasted sesame seeds if you like.

Marinate the cleaned queenfish (ikan talang) with salt. Fry in hot oil sprinkled with flour so it doesn't pop until cooked/dry.
Make tamarind water, pour hot water over the tamarind while stirring.
Thickly slice all ingredients.
Sauté the garlic and shallots with oil until almost wilted. Add chilies, tomatoes, brown sugar, granulated sugar, MSG, salt, and water. Check the taste and adjust. The taste should be sweet, sour, and savory.
Once wilted, add the fried fish and cook until the water reduces.
Happy cooking 😊.

strMeal: Filet Ikan Dori Saos Asam Manis
strInstructions:
Wash the fish, then cut into several pieces. Soak the fish pieces in salted water for 5 minutes.
Prepare the dry flour mixture. Roll the fish pieces in the flour mixture.
Fry the flour-coated fish until browned, then remove and drain.
Wash the peeled carrot and onion, then slice thinly.
Sauté the sliced onion and carrot, then add water, and wait until it boils. Add granulated sugar and tomato sauce, stir evenly. Add the dissolved sago/cornstarch. Stir gently.
Serve the cooked dory fish fillets, then pour the sauce over them. The dish is ready to be enjoyed.
strIngredient16: Tepung sagu / maizena , dilarutkan dengan sedikit air

strInstructions:
Wash the carp (ikan mas) clean, add salt and lime juice, let it sit for a while, fry until dry, remove, and drain. Prepare all ingredients.
Prepare the garlic and salt, grind them. Sauté the onion and ground garlic until fragrant.
Add grated carrots, stir, add water, pour in tomato sauce and chili sauce, stir evenly, and add granulated sugar.
Finally, add the cornstarch solution, stir evenly, check the taste, and turn off the heat. Arrange the fried carp on a plate and pour the sauce over it. Ready to be served 😋.
strIngredient12: Cornstarch dissolved with a little water

strInstructions:
Clean the tilapia, marinate with the marinade and lime juice for 1 hour, clean, and fry in hot oil that has been sprinkled with flour. Flip the fish and sprinkle the surface of the fish with flour. Fry the tilapia until golden yellow.
While frying, prepare the sliced spices and sweet and sour sauce. Mix in one container: sliced tomatoes, oyster sauce, tomato sauce, chili sauce, sweet soy sauce, sugar, cornstarch, vinegar, chicken Royco, and water. Stir evenly. It's even more delicious if you add pineapple slices.
Add a little cooking oil (I used vegetable oil) into a wok; once hot, add the garlic and onion. After they wilt, add the sliced chilies, and sauté until fragrant. Then pour in the sauce mixture. Stir evenly and cook until bubbling. Remove from heat.
Prepare a serving plate, arrange the fried tilapia on it. And pour the spicy sweet and sour sauce over it until all parts of the fish are covered. Serve hot with freshly scooped rice. Hmmm...
strIngredient5: Cooking oil for frying and a little for sautéing

strInstructions:
Dissolve the all-purpose flour and water, stir evenly, and coat the cleaned fish. Proceed to fry, don't forget to flip it back and forth, and drain.
Peel and dice: cucumber, pineapple, carrot, and tomato (but the tomato doesn't need to be peeled), and cut the large red chili.
Finely chop the garlic and onion.
Prepare the oyster sauce and chili sauce in a container; because I like it spicy, I don't use tomato sauce.
Heat margarine, sauté the garlic and onion until fragrant. Add a little sesame oil. Add carrots and red chilies. Once wilted, add water and the sauces from the container.
Season with salt, sugar, pepper powder, and bouillon powder, check the taste. Once it's right and boiling, add the pineapple, tomato, and cucumber pieces, then pour in the water + cornstarch solution.
Once cooked, pour it over the fried fish. Ready to be served.

Cut the dory fish according to taste, then marinate with bouillon powder and pepper powder, stir evenly, and let sit for at least 15 minutes. Prepare wheat flour and Rose Brand cornstarch.
Put the wheat flour and cornstarch into a container, then add bouillon powder and pepper powder, stir until even. Put the fish pieces into the flour mixture, stir until the fish is coated with flour, then dip into ice water.
Put the fish pieces back into the flour, stir while squeezing gently so it becomes curly. Fry in hot oil using low heat until cooked.
Sweet and Sour Sauce: chop the garlic, slice the onion. Sauté the garlic until fragrant, add the onion, and sauté briefly until the onion wilts.
Pour in water, add tomato sauce, sweet soy sauce, bouillon powder, pepper powder, and granulated sugar. Stir evenly and cook until it boils and the broth reduces slightly. Check the taste, and if it's right, pour in the dissolved cornstarch, and stir quickly until the sauce thickens.
Add the fried dory fish, stir quickly until coated with the sauce, and it is ready to be served.
strIngredient19: Tepung maizena rose brand , larutkan dengan sedikit air

strInstructions:
Prepare the ingredients. Deep fry the bilis fish until dry. Set aside.
Sauté the ground ingredients until fragrant, add all other ingredients except the fish. Stir until even and slightly thick. Check the taste. Add the fish, and stir until the spices evenly coat the fish.
Serve!

Cut and clean the salted fish according to taste first. Do the same for the onions, chilies, and tomatoes.
Then fry the telang fish until cooked, remove, and drain.
Next, sauté the onions, chilies, and tomatoes until wilted. After that, add the telang fish. Stir evenly.
Add a little salt, but if it is already too salty, it can be skipped. Also add brown sugar and granulated sugar. Stir evenly. Check the taste.
If everything is cooked, remove and serve.

Wash the fish fillet clean and cut according to taste.
Mix the all-purpose seasoning flour with a little water. Coat the fish with the flour mixture, then fry until cooked. Set aside.
Make the sauce ingredients: sauté garlic until fragrant, then add all the sauce ingredients. Check the taste. Cook until done and thickened.
Serve the fish with sweet and sour sauce.
strIngredient10: A little vinegar or lime juice

strInstructions:
Grill the fish that has been marinated for 15 minutes.
Remove its bones, and slice all the spices.
Sauté the spices until fragrant, add water, add the fish meat, and sprinkle with seasoning powder.
Ready to be eaten.

Blend all the ground spices (don't forget to add a little salt when blending). Slice shallots, garlic, onion, and scallions.
First, sauté the sliced onion, shallots, and garlic until fragrant. Then add the ground spices, lemongrass, and bay leaves, and sauté again until everything is evenly mixed, cooked, and fragrant.
Add the chicken, stir, and sauté briefly. After that, add enough water (not too much) and stir evenly. Check the taste with salt, flavor enhancer, and pepper. Let it be until the chicken is fully cooked.
5 minutes before the chicken is removed, add chopped bird's eye chilies, scallions, and basil. Stir again and wait a moment until perfectly cooked. The food is ready to be served.

Coat the chicken with lime juice and salt, let it sit for about 15 minutes, grind the chilies, shallots, garlic, candlenuts, ginger, and turmeric powder, then sauté.
Sauté the ground spices, add lemongrass, bay leaves, and kaffir lime leaves, and cook until fragrant and done.
Add the chicken, then add water and cook over medium heat; because the drumsticks are whole, cook for about 20 minutes or until cooked and the spices are absorbed.
Add granulated sugar, salt, and mushroom bouillon, then check the taste and adjust to your liking.
Add scallions and basil leaves right before removing from heat.
Ready to be served with warm white rice.

Boil the free-range chicken until half tender. Grind the spices with a blender.
Sauté the spices until fragrant, add the boiled chicken, pour in water and chicken broth, and cook until boiling.
Add salt, brown sugar, and flavor enhancer. Cook until the spices are absorbed and the broth reduces; don't forget to check the taste, then turn off the stove.
strIngredient1: Free-range chicken, cut into small pieces

strInstructions:
Prepare the ingredients.
Heat oil, sauté chilies and tomatoes until wilted.
Add the Bamboe seasoning, lemongrass, and kaffir lime leaves, then stir evenly.
Add the chicken and water, then stir, cook until the spices are absorbed.
Add basil leaves, stir evenly, then serve!

Wash the chicken and the spices clean.
Grind the shallots, garlic, turmeric, ginger, large chilies, and candlenuts. Sauté all the spices without oil until the water content reduces. Pour in cooking oil.
Continue sautéing until the spices are fragrant, cooked, and oily. Add the chicken, stir evenly.
Pour in water, and after it boils, add salt and pepper. Check the taste. Once the taste is right, continue cooking until the broth reduces and the spices are absorbed.
Ready to be served.

Clean the chicken, then marinate with the marinade.
Grind the ground spices.
Then the marinated chicken can be fried first.
Boil the quail eggs.
Heat oil, add the ground spices, bay leaves, kaffir lime leaves, and crushed lemongrass. Cook until fragrant.
Add the chicken, then add a little water, salt, chicken bouillon, and sugar. Cook and taste until the flavor is right.
Once the taste is right, turn off the heat, then serve.

strMeal: Rica Rica Ayam Lombok Ijo Simpel
strInstructions:
Boil the chicken feet until tender, drain.
Cut the chicken to taste, clean it.
Blend the shallots, garlic, ginger, turmeric, chilies, salt, sugar, mushroom bouillon, and a little oil until smooth.
Prepare a wok, add the ground spices, bay leaves, crushed lemongrass, and crushed galangal, add 1 spoon of oil.
Turn on low heat, sauté until fragrant, the spices are thick and clumped.
Add the chicken feet and chicken, stir evenly.
Add enough water, wait until the water boils, stir, check the taste.
Cook until the water is absorbed and the chicken is cooked.

Boil the chicken thighs with bay leaves, salt, and a little bouillon powder for about 10 minutes so the chicken is more savory and not fishy.
Remove then fry briefly until the outside of the chicken is slightly browned. No need to be too dry.
Blend the shallots, garlic, candlenuts, curly chilies, and bird's eye chilies until smooth.
Heat a good amount of oil, then sauté the ground spices until fully cooked, fragrant, and the red oil starts to come out.
Add a little brown sugar, chili sauce, sweet soy sauce, salt, and flavor enhancer. Stir evenly then check the taste.
Put the fried chicken into the chili paste, stir until all parts are coated with the spices.
Cook over low heat until the spices are absorbed and slightly thickened. If you like it slightly wet and oily like in the photo, leave a little of the chili oil broth.

Wash the chicken clean until the water boils.
Grind the spices, crush the ginger, galangal, and lemongrass, then sauté with enough cooking oil, no need for much (3 tbsp), until fragrant.
Add water and the other spices. Add the chicken, soak until tender and the spices are absorbed. Don't forget to check the taste to see if it's lacking anything or is already just right.
For the tofu and tempeh, they are added last for me. The important thing is the chicken is tender first. Because tempeh and tofu also absorb quickly and these have also been fried beforehand. Just add water if the broth runs out.
Ulalaa, alhamdulillah the chicken rica-rica is done. Easy, right? ☺️👌🏻

Prepare all ingredients. Mix everything evenly, except basil and lemongrass. Let sit for 15 minutes. I modified the recipe by blending all the spices except basil and lemongrass.
Heat oil, sauté the ground spices until fully cooked, add lemongrass, kaffir lime leaves, when about to be removed add basil, remove the spices.
Take a sheet of banana leaf, arrange the chicken, pour the ground spices over it, again add basil.
Wrap the banana leaf and secure with a stick. Steam.
Remove and serve warm with rice.
strIngredient12: Banana leaves and sticks as needed for wrapping

strInstructions:
Grind all the ground spice ingredients, set aside. Clean the fish, wash and coat with the juice of 1 calamansi and salt, stir evenly and set aside. The fish can be cut in two if the size is too large (according to taste).
Heat oil in a wok, sauté the ground spices, kaffir lime leaves, pandan leaves & lemongrass until fragrant and changes color. Add the fish, stir evenly. Add water. Cook until the fish is cooked.
Add flavor enhancer, salt, and the juice of 1 calamansi. Stir, check the taste. Remove and serve with hot rice 👍😘
strIngredient5: Pandan leaf, tied in a knot

strInstructions:
Take the fish out of the can, wash by draining under running water, coat with flour.
Fry the fish until dry.
Grind the shallots, garlic, bird's eye chilies, candlenuts, ginger, turmeric, and lemongrass with a blender.
Set aside the sauce from the can.
Sauté all the ground spices until fragrant, add sliced tomatoes, basil leaves, and kaffir lime leaves, add the remaining canned sardine sauce, lastly add the fried sardines, stir briefly, serve.
strIngredient9: Lemongrass, take the white part, slice

strInstructions:
Prepare the fish. Coat the fish with seasonings until evenly mixed.
Prepare the spices, blend until smooth. Then sauté the spices together with lemongrass and kaffir lime leaves, cook the spices until fully cooked, add water, granulated sugar, tamarind water, salt, and chicken bouillon, cook until the water reduces by half, check the taste.
Add the fish, stir, cook briefly until the spices are absorbed into the fish.
Serve.

Bismillah. Prepare all ingredients. Heat the oil, then sauté the sliced shallots, cook until fragrant and wilted. Then add the ground spices. Cook until fragrant.
Add tomatoes, torch ginger, scallions, galangal, kaffir lime leaves, and lemongrass. Cook again until fragrant and wilted. Then add the basil leaves, stir evenly, then add the fish, stir evenly. Add a little water, salt, and a little sugar, stir evenly.
Cook until the broth reduces, check the taste. Once it's right, turn off the stove heat and it is ready to be served. Happy trying and hope you like the recipe, friends. Thank you.
strIngredient1: Fresh pangasius fish, cut according to taste
strIngredient11: Basil leaves, take only the leaves

strInstructions:
Sauté the ground spices with a little oil.
Add lemongrass, galangal, and bay leaves. Cook until the spices are fully cooked and the oil separates.
Add water. Seasoning.
Add the fish. Cook until the fish is cooked and the spices are absorbed.
Add tomatoes and basil leaves. Stir evenly.
Remove and serve.

Clean the fish, cut according to taste, coat with lime juice, wash again.
Sauté the ground spices with lemongrass and kaffir lime leaves, pour in water, let it boil.
Add the fish, add salt, sugar, and flavor enhancer, stir evenly.
Add the leeks, cook until done, check the taste.

Thinly slice all ingredients: shallots, garlic, kaffir lime leaves, bird's eye chilies, and lemongrass.
Boil the chicken breast until tender, remove, drain, then shred.
Sauté all sliced ingredients using classic olive oil (except bird's eye chilies), then add the shredded chicken.
Then add the red bird's eye chilies. Add sugar, salt, and mushroom bouillon, stir evenly.
Shredded chicken is ready to be enjoyed with warm white rice.

strMeal: Soto Ayam Kuah Bening Bali + Sambal Matah Nya 🍲🔥
strInstructions:
Prepare ingredients.
Boil the chicken with 2.5L of water. At the first boil, ± 8-10 minutes. Discard the water + change to new water + boil again until boiling ± 5 minutes, to discard the dirty water. To keep the broth clear, don't cover it tightly and don't stir it while boiling. Just use medium heat.
Sauté the ground spices until very fragrant and fully cooked ± 5-7 minutes. Add lemongrass, kaffir lime leaves, bay leaves, galangal, sauté again for ± 2-3 minutes. Sauté until the oil comes out. This is the key so the soto is fragrant and doesn't have a raw smell.
Put the sautéed spices into the broth pot. Add salt, sugar, bouillon powder. Cook for 30 minutes until the chicken is tender. Remove the chicken, shred it. Put the chicken bones back into the broth for 10 minutes to make the broth more savory.
Make Sambal Matah: Mix all the sliced ingredients. Pour hot coconut oil over it. Stir evenly. The oil must be really hot so the sambal matah wilts but remains fresh.
Arrange glass noodles, shredded chicken, egg, scallions in a bowl. Pour hot broth over it. Sprinkle with fried shallots. Serve with sambal matah + lime. The broth must be steaming hot when poured so all the aromas come out.

Prepare the ingredients above.
Crush the lemongrass, then chop finely. Slice the chilies, shallots, and kaffir lime leaves. Slice the shallots rather finely.
After all ingredients are sliced, mix them in a bowl. Add salt, mushroom bouillon, and shrimp paste. Stir evenly. Test the taste. Once it's right, pour in the oil and stir again. Sambal matah is ready to be eaten 😋
strIngredient4: Adjusted to the amount of chili
strIngredient6: Kaffir lime leaves, remove the center stalk

strInstructions:
Prepare the chicken ingredients and crispy flour.
Heat Rose Brand cooking oil over medium heat, and start the crispy chicken flouring process.
Put the chicken pieces into the flour, squeeze until the entire surface is covered with flour, then dip briefly into the water, remove and coat again in the flour, dip again into the water and flour for the last time, squeeze until it becomes curly.
Fry immediately after the last flouring. Do not flip back and forth; if the bottom of the chicken is yellowish or brown, flip the chicken. If both sides are golden yellow, the crispy chicken can be removed and drained. Fry over medium-low heat.
Finally, arrange the crispy chicken on a plate then pour the sambal matah over it. Crispy chicken with sambal matah is ready to accompany your hungry stomach.
strIngredient1: Pieces of chicken marinated with garlic and bouillon powder

strInstructions:
Prepare ingredients. Slice everything and put into one container. Add bouillon powder and flavor enhancer.
Heat Rose Brand cooking oil until it is really hot. Then pour it into the sambal matah container. Stir.
Sambal matah is ready to be served, can be with fried chicken or other side dishes.
strIngredient1: Handful of japlak bird's eye chilies
strIngredient4: Small kaffir lime leaves, thinly sliced

strInstructions:
Wash the fish clean then drizzle with lime juice and coat with salt. Marinate for 5 minutes
Steam the tuna for 20 minutes
Once cool, shred it
Prepare the sambal matah ingredients and thinly slice the shallots, garlic, chilies, lemongrass, and kaffir lime leaves
Heat oil over low heat, add shrimp paste, stir to crush, followed by chilies, onions, kaffir lime leaves, and lemongrass
Add Cap Kapal Salt, Granulated Sugar, and Bouillon Powder. Stir evenly
Finally, add lime juice, stir until slightly dry
Serve with warm rice

Wash and cut the eggplant, soak in saltwater for 10 minutes to remove the sap. Squeeze and rinse with water until clean
Drain the eggplant and coat with rice flour or glutinous rice flour, then fry until browned. Remove and set aside.
Prepare the chili paste ingredients, thinly slice the shallots, finely chop the chilies. Take the white part of the lemongrass and slice finely. Remove the center vein of the kaffir lime leaves, snip the leaves finely. Transfer all ingredients to a heat-resistant container, add shrimp paste and salt.
Heat cooking oil, pour it over the chili paste
The chili paste is ready to be poured over the fried eggplant

Prepare the ingredients
Cut the main ingredients, then put them together in a heat-resistant bowl, heat oil in a wok then pour it over the main ingredients, add salt and lime juice then stir evenly.
Prepare a container then serve. Later on, water will come out from the tomatoes, Moms, so the chili paste will become watery. If you don't want it watery, when cutting the tomatoes, discard the seeds.
strIngredient1: Large red tomatoes, cut into medium squares
strIngredient3: Green bird's eye chilies, cut into rounds

strInstructions:
Thinly slice the shallots, bird's eye chilies, kaffir lime leaves, and lemongrass.
Mix all sliced ingredients, salt, sugar, mushroom bouillon, and flavor enhancer.
Stir until evenly mixed and the juices come out.
Heat coconut oil, pour it over the mixed ingredients.
Stir briefly just to keep it fresh and crunchy.
Add calamansi juice and virgin coconut oil, stir again.
Check the taste, serve.

Mix shallots, kaffir lime leaves, lemongrass, bird's eye chilies, salt, sugar, and shrimp paste in a bowl.
Pour hot oil over it, stir evenly. Add coconut oil if available.
Boil instant noodles until cooked, drain.
Mix the noodles with the fried noodle seasoning. Stir evenly with the sambal matah.
strIngredient5: White part of lemongrass, thinly sliced

strInstructions:
Boil water, garlic, coriander, and baking soda.
Add the tofu, boil briefly then let sit for 2 hours.
While waiting for the tofu, let's make the sambal matah by cutting all the ingredients.
Pour hot oil over it, then add lime juice, then stir evenly. Let's go back to the tofu.
After sitting, fry the tofu until browned. Remove and pour the sambal matah over it. Ready to be served.

Grill the chicken until cooked, sprinkle with salt. Cook to the desired doneness.
Slice the shallots and chilies. Add salt then crush/mash lightly. Add hot oil and calamansi (jeruk limo) juice.
Arrange the rice in a bowl, add the chicken and top with sambal matah. Enjoy your meal 🥰.
strIngredient2: Chicken thigh fillet, cut into pieces

strInstructions:
Prepare the ingredients.
Slice the shallots, all chilies, lemongrass, and kaffir lime leaves, put them in one container.
Add salt, MSG (vetsin), sugar, and shrimp paste (terasi), and mix evenly.
Heat cooking oil, then pour it over the sliced ingredients.
strIngredient6: Lime, 1/2 if it's somewhat small, 1/4 if the lime is large

strInstructions:
Clean the chicken fillet meat then cut lengthwise, then dry roast the coriander until fragrant.
Coarsely pound the roasted coriander, grind the shallots and garlic.
Marinate the chicken with the ground spices, coriander, pepper, turmeric powder, bouillon powder, and salt, add Rose Brand Tapioca Flour and Rose Brand Cornstarch.
Stir evenly, let sit for 15 minutes, then fry until cooked.
Slice the shallots, bird's eye chilies, lemongrass, and kaffir lime leaves, place in a bowl.
