strInstructions: Finely chop the chicken fillet and grind the spices. In a bowl, combine the minced chicken, tapioca starch, cornstarch, all-purpose flour, egg, ground spices, and sliced spring onion. Add ice water and mix well. Take a small spoonful of the mixture using two forks and drop it into simmering water. Repeat with the remaining mixture and cook until the chicken tekwan pieces are done. Prepare the broth by sautéing the garlic and shallot, adding water and seasonings, then simmering until fragrant. Serve the chicken tekwan in the broth.

Prepare the ingredients. I use garlic that is already ground (it's fine if it has some cooking oil mixed in).
Mix the dough evenly. Bring water to a boil and add a little of the mixture to test the taste. If it tastes right, shape the rest and boil it. It doesn't stick, perhaps because there is a little oil mixed into the ground garlic.
I shaped them into small, long pieces for sushi filling, but they puffed up and got chubby, haha. It made so many! That's it—the process is really simple, right? A little mess doesn't matter.
Put a small portion in the freezer. Cut most of the rest into small pieces and freeze them too. Later, you can make tekwan soup, siomay or Madura satay seasoning, or pempek soup with them. They go well with all of them; the flavor is light.

Cook the dried shrimp and leftover rice with enough water until soft. Continue cooking until boiling and the liquid has reduced, then blend or process until smooth. Add salt, stock powder, garlic powder, all-purpose flour, and tapioca starch. Mix in one egg. Shape the mixture and boil until the pieces float; remove and drain.
Bring water to a boil in a pot. Grind the shallots and garlic, then add them to the boiling water. Season with salt, stock powder, granulated sugar, shrimp powder, and ground pepper. Stir, then add the tekwan fish balls.
Place boiled glass noodles and bean sprouts in a serving bowl. Add the tekwan fish balls and pour over the broth. Serve.

Grind the Spanish mackerel, then add the egg white, ice water, and garlic. Grind again. Add salt, mushroom stock powder, and sugar; mix well.
Add the tapioca starch and mix. Check the seasoning by boiling a small amount of the mixture. Once the flavor is right, pinch off small portions and boil them until cooked; repeat until all the mixture is used.
For the broth, sauté all the broth seasonings, then add them to the water used to boil the Spanish mackerel bones and head. Season with salt, sugar, and mushroom stock powder. Adjust the seasoning to taste.
Serve the tekwan with the broth and accompaniments.
strIngredient14: Spanish mackerel bone and head stock

strInstructions:
Prepare all the ingredients.
Sauté the ground spice paste in 1–2 tablespoons of oil in a pan over medium heat until cooked through. Push it to one side of the pan, add the eggs, and scramble.
Add water and bring to a boil. Add the tekwan fish balls. Season with salt, stock powder, sugar, and ground pepper; taste and adjust the seasoning. Add the bok choy and cabbage and cook briefly until the vegetables are done.
Finally, add the scallions and turn off the heat. The spicy tekwan fish-ball soup is ready to serve hot.
strIngredient14: Bok choy stems, cut into pieces

strInstructions:
Blend the Spanish mackerel until smooth. Mix with sago flour and ice water until the mixture can be shaped. Form small balls and boil them in boiling water until they float; remove and drain.
Sauté the garlic until fragrant, then add the shrimp and stir. Pour in the shrimp stock and bring to a boil. Add the fish balls, wood ear mushrooms, and quail eggs.
Season with MSG, salt, and pepper. Cook until everything is done.
Serve topped with scallions and fried shallots.

Soak the wood ear mushrooms first.
Prepare the spice paste by grinding the shallots, garlic, and pepper together.
Blend the shrimp heads, then sauté them and set aside.
Bring about 800 ml of water, or enough to taste, to a boil with the thoroughly washed wood ear mushrooms.
Sauté the ground spices and mix them with the packaged tekwan seasoning. Add this mixture to the pot with the water and mushrooms.
Add the sautéed shrimp heads and stir well.
Cook until boiling, then season with salt and flavor enhancer. Adjust to taste.
Once boiling, add the tekwan fish balls. Finish with scallions and celery.
Serve the tekwan topped with fried shallots.
strIngredient6: Packet of medium wood ear mushrooms

strInstructions:
Bring about 2 liters of water to a boil for cooking the tekwan.
Blend or mix the ground Spanish mackerel, egg white, and garlic powder until evenly combined.
Add salt and flavor enhancer, then mix well. Gradually add the sago flour.
Shape the mixture using a spatula and fork, if desired, and place the pieces into the boiling water.
Once they float, remove and drain.

For the tekwan spice paste, grind all the shallots and garlic for the broth. Sauté the whole spices—cloves, star anise, cinnamon, and nutmeg—until fragrant and darker in color. Remove and set aside.
Chop or blend the dried shrimp/rebon and set aside.
Fry the shrimp heads and bodies until they change color. Set aside.
Combine the tekwan ingredients with the ground dried shrimp: all-purpose flour, tapioca starch, stock powder, salt, pepper, and ground garlic. Gradually pour in boiling water until the mixture is soft but can still be shaped.
Bring water to a boil for cooking the tekwan. Add 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil if desired to keep the pieces from sticking together. Add the mixture little by little. Once some pieces float, remove and drain them. If they have not floated, gently stir and let them cook a little longer. Repeat until all the mixture is used.
For the broth, bring 1,500 ml of water to a boil. Add the sautéed spice paste, shrimp heads and bodies, sugar, salt, pepper, and garlic powder. Taste and adjust. Add the cooked tekwan balls, wood ear mushrooms, and dried lily flowers. Boil briefly, then turn off the heat.
Place glass noodles soaked in warm water in a bowl, if available. Add tekwan and broth, then garnish with sliced scallions, celery, and fried shallots. You may also add green bird's-eye chili sauce, calamansi, or sweet soy sauce. Enjoy the savory shrimp broth with a sweet, sour, and spicy flavor, or serve it as is.
strIngredient10: Water used to boil the tekwan
strIngredient19: Kepala udang boleh juga ditambah beberapa badan udang nya
strIngredient21: Garam (kalo kurang boleh tambah sesuai selera)
strIngredient22: Gula (kalo kurang boleh tambah sesuai selera)
strIngredient27: Jamur kuping , rendam air hangat tiriskan
strIngredient29: Secukupnya irisan daun bawang & seledri (jika ada)
strIngredient30: Note : boleh juga ditambah dgn soun
strIngredient32: Jeruk limau dan bawang goreng. (jika ada)

strInstructions:
Mix the fish, egg white, salt, sugar, pepper, and ice water. Add the sago flour and mix well.
Shape the mixture into small balls and boil them in boiling water until they float. Remove and drain.
Sauté the garlic in oil until fragrant. Add the shrimp and other accompaniments and stir briefly. Add the scallions and celery, then adjust the seasoning.
Serve the tekwan broth in bowls with glass noodles. Sprinkle with fried shallots if available.

Prepare the tekwan fish balls, shrimp stock, and other ingredients.
Grind the garlic, then sauté it with the scallions and shrimp until fragrant.
Add water and shrimp stock, then add the tekwan fish balls. Cook until boiling, and season with salt, mushroom stock powder, and sugar. Adjust to taste.
Serve the tekwan with rice vermicelli, scallions, soy sauce, and chili sauce.

Mix the Spanish mackerel meat and ice water until homogeneous. Add the ground garlic, salt, and stock powder, then mix until evenly combined.
Add the sago flour and mix just until combined. Adjust the seasoning.
Bring water to a boil with 2 tablespoons of oil.
The mixture can be chilled for several hours. Use two spoons, dipped in hot water first to prevent sticking, to transfer portions of the mixture into the hot water.
Let the pieces float, cook for another minute until fully done, then remove and drain.
The fish balls can be stored or used for tekwan.
For the broth, bring water to a boil and add fried garlic. Season with salt, sugar, pepper, and stock powder; stir and adjust to taste.
Add the fish balls to the broth.
Serve with accompaniments.

If the ground fish is frozen, thaw it by gradually adding a little water.
Add salt, MSG, and ground garlic.
Gradually add the sago flour, mixing until combined. Do not knead the mixture until too firm, as this may make the tekwan balls hard.
Bring water to a boil and add 2 tablespoons of cooking oil. Once boiling, pinch small portions of the mixture into the water.
Cook until the pieces float, then remove and drain.

Blend the Spanish mackerel and peeled shrimp until smooth. Transfer to a bowl.
Add salt, pepper, and mushroom stock powder to the fish mixture and mix well. Gradually add the tapioca starch.
Add water little by little, mixing until the consistency is right.
Bring water to a boil. Drop portions of the mixture into the boiling water using a spoon and cook until done; floating indicates that they are cooked.
For the broth, blend the dried shrimp and garlic. Sauté them without letting them burn. Add the shrimp shells and sauté until they turn orange and smell fragrant.
Once the dried shrimp, garlic, and shells are fragrant and cooked, add boiled water, jicama, and wood ear mushrooms.
Season with salt, pepper, and mushroom stock powder. Sugar is not needed because the jicama provides sweetness.
Enjoy!

Bring the water to a boil. Add the uncooked onion crackers and cook until softened.
Add the ground aromatic ginger, extra-spicy fried-rice seasoning, and tekwan fish balls. Stir well and taste. Turn off the heat.
The extra-spicy seblak tekwan is ready to serve hot, garnished with scallions.
strIngredient3: Packet of Poll Pedas fried-rice seasoning
strIngredient4: A piece of aromatic ginger, ground

strInstructions:
Take the tekwan balls out of the refrigerator. Grind the garlic with salt and pepper and set aside. Grind the softened dried shrimp as well.
Sauté the ground garlic over low heat until fragrant, then add the dried shrimp.
Pour the garlic and dried shrimp mixture into the previously strained shrimp stock. Bring to a boil, then add the scallions and celery. Add the sliced wood ear mushrooms and tekwan balls, then adjust the seasoning.
Place boiled glass noodles in a bowl and top with boiled shrimp. Pour in the tekwan and broth, sprinkle with fried shallots, and serve hot.
strIngredient12: Wood ear mushrooms, soaked until soft and sliced

strMeal: Model Ikan Gabus Isi Tahu (Khas Palembang)
strInstructions:
First, make the fish cakes (model). Blend the ground fish, water, egg, salt, and MSG for 2 minutes. Stop the mixer, add the tapioca starch, then blend again, increasing the speed from 1 to 5 over 3 minutes.
Heat the cooking oil. Put some tapioca starch on a flat plate and coat your palms with it. Take 100 g of the mixture, shape it into a ball, flatten it, fill it with tofu, then seal and round it. Fry over low heat until golden brown. Remove and drain.
Now make the broth. Soak the wood ear mushrooms and dried lily flowers in hot water, then rinse thoroughly. Sauté the garlic, ground pepper, and ground nutmeg until fragrant. Add the sliced jicama, shrimp heads, wood ear mushrooms, and dried lily flowers. Cook until well sautéed, then add water and bring to a boil. Season with salt and MSG.
For the chili sauce, pound the bird's-eye chilies and mix with a little broth.
To serve, simmer some fish cakes in the boiling broth for 2 minutes. Remove and cut into pieces, then place in a bowl. Add glass noodles and broth, and garnish with sliced celery, fried shallots, and sliced cucumber. Serve with the chili sauce.

strMeal: Model Ikan Gabus Isi Telur (Khas Palembang)
strInstructions:
First, make the fish cakes (model). Blend the ground fish, water, eggs, salt, and MSG for 2 minutes. Stop the mixer, add the tapioca starch, then blend again, increasing the speed from 1 to 5 over 3 minutes.
Heat cooking oil in a pan. Take 100 g of the mixture, coating your hands with tapioca starch from a plate first. Shape the mixture into a ball, flatten it, fill it with a boiled egg, then seal it tightly and shape it into a ball. Fry over low heat until golden brown, then remove and drain.
Next, make the broth. Soak the dried lily flowers and mushrooms in hot water, then rinse thoroughly. Heat oil and sauté the ground garlic, pepper, and nutmeg until fragrant. Add the sliced jicama, shrimp heads, mushrooms, and dried lily flowers. Sauté briefly, then pour in the water. Once boiling, add salt and MSG.
Simmer a few fish cakes in the boiling broth for about 2 minutes. Remove and slice them, place on a plate, add glass noodles, and pour over the broth. Garnish with celery leaves, fried shallots, and chopped cucumber. Serve with chili sauce for extra flavor.

To make the tofu pempek, mix the fish meat with salt, mushroom stock powder, egg white, and water until the mixture thickens and becomes cohesive.
Add the tapioca starch and mix well. Set the tofu pieces and extra tapioca starch aside; the extra starch is for coating, not for mixing into the batter.
Take some mixture, coat it with tapioca starch, flatten it, fill it with tofu, fold the mixture over the tofu, and shape as desired. Fry until golden brown and set aside. The tofu pempek will be larger than usual.
For the broth, boil the fresh shrimp to make shrimp stock. Remove the shrimp once they change color.
Sauté the ground garlic until fragrant, then add the dried shrimp (or homemade stock powder made from shrimp shells/heads) and sauté again. Add this to the shrimp stock and bring to a boil.
Add sliced jicama, wood ear mushrooms, and dried lily flowers. Cook until boiling, stirring occasionally. Add scallions, celery, salt, pepper, and mushroom stock powder. Return the shrimp to the pot after chopping them into small or coarse pieces.
Once the broth boils, add the tofu pempek and cook until everything floats and the fish cakes soften slightly.
To serve, place glass noodles in a bowl, add sliced fish cakes and broth, and include some jicama, wood ear mushrooms, and dried lily flowers. Garnish with sliced cucumber, scallions, celery, and fried shallots. Serve with ground bird's-eye chili, calamansi, and soy sauce to taste.
strIngredient2: White tofu, each cut into 6 pieces
strIngredient14: Wood ear mushrooms and dried lily flowers

strInstructions:
In a bowl, combine the ground Spanish mackerel, egg white, ground garlic, mushroom stock powder, salt, and water. Mix well (you can use a mixer for about 4–5 minutes) until the mixture becomes thick and somewhat firm.
Gradually add the tapioca starch, stopping when the mixture is firm enough to shape by hand.
Keep extra tapioca starch ready to prevent the mixture from sticking to your hands; do not mix this extra starch into the batter. Dust your hands with starch. Take about 70–80 g of mixture, flatten it, add a piece of white tofu, cover the tofu, and shape into a ball.
Heat a generous amount of cooking oil. Fry the tofu pempek over medium-low heat, preferably in a deep pan or pot so the pieces can be mostly submerged.
Fry until the pieces float and rotate, indicating they are cooked. Drain.
strIngredient6: Rose Brand Pak Tani Gunung tapioca starch
strIngredient8: Rose Brand cooking oil for frying

strInstructions:
Prepare all the ingredients.
Process the fish until smooth. Add the water and mix evenly. Add the oil and salt, then the egg, and mix well.
Add the flour and mix only until combined. Cut the tofu into two or four pieces as desired, then fry until the surface firms up. Remove and drain.
Take some fish mixture and wrap it around the fried tofu. Shape into balls or ovals. To prevent sticking, coat your hands with oil or starch.
Fry over medium-low heat, turning the pieces so they cook evenly. Once they expand and float, remove and drain. Repeat until all are cooked.
Sauté the broth seasonings until fragrant, add the shrimp, and cook briefly until they change color.
Bring the broth to a boil, add the sautéed seasonings and remaining seasonings, and adjust to taste. Add the fish cakes and cook until they float. Remove and cut into pieces as desired.
Place the sliced fish cakes in serving bowls, add broth and the other accompaniments, and serve hot. Enjoy!
strIngredient8: Rose Brand cooking oil for frying

strInstructions:
Prepare the ingredients. Mix the ground fish, garlic, salt, stock powder, granulated sugar, and the water-and-egg mixture. Stir until the batter thickens.
Add the tapioca starch and mix until evenly combined and firm enough to shape with a wooden spoon. Divide the mixture into 8 portions.
Take one portion, fill it with tofu, and seal it tightly. Repeat until all the mixture and tofu are used.
Heat the cooking oil. Fry the pempek until cooked and golden brown, turning occasionally so both sides cook evenly. Remove, drain, and set aside.
For the model broth, heat the cooking oil and sauté the garlic, ground pepper, and dried shrimp until fragrant. Add the fresh shrimp and cook, stirring, until done. Turn off the heat.
Add the sautéed mixture to a pot of shrimp stock and bring to a boil.
Add the wood ear mushrooms and jicama. Season with salt, stock powder, and granulated sugar. Bring to a brief boil again.
Add the tofu pempek and simmer for about 5 minutes so the flavors absorb. Taste and adjust the seasoning, adding more salt or sugar if needed. Turn off the heat.
Serve the tofu pempek model with its accompaniments.
strIngredient8: Rose Brand Gunung Agung tapioca starch
strIngredient9: White tofu, each cut in half
strIngredient10: Rose Brand cooking oil for frying
strIngredient12: Fresh peeled shrimp, washed and cut into pieces
strIngredient19: Air kaldu udang tips membuat kaldu udang
strIngredient24: Bengkoang ukuran sedang, kupas lalu cuci bersih dan potong korek api memanjang
strIngredient27: Timun , cuci bersih lalu cacah atau potong kecil

strInstructions:
Heat the water, then add the sliced palm sugar, granulated sugar, and pandan leaf.
Add the kolang-kaling (sugar palm fruit) and the sliced nangka banana. Cover the pot and cook until the water boils and the kolang-kaling is tender.
Once the water boils, add the coconut milk and the vanilla powder. Stir well.
Serve once the kolak has cooled.

Wash the mung beans, then put them in a pot with 1 liter of water, the pandan leaves, and the ginger. Cook until the mung beans are tender and some of the skins start to split. (I use the 5:30:7 method)
Add 500 ml of water. Add the palm sugar, granulated sugar, and salt. Stir until the sugar dissolves and the broth comes back to a boil. Add the kepok bananas. Cook over medium heat for about 5–7 minutes, until the bananas are cooked but not too mushy.
Lower the heat, then add the coconut milk. Stir gently and constantly so the coconut milk doesn't split. Turn off the heat as soon as the kolak reaches a gentle simmer and the coconut milk is evenly mixed in. Taste. Adjust the sugar or salt if needed.
The Mung Bean and Banana Kolak is ready to serve.

strMeal: Kolak Sagu Mutiara Dengan Ubi Dan Pisang
strInstructions:
Bring the water to a boil. Boil the tapioca pearls for 5 minutes, turn off the heat, cover the pot for 30 minutes, then boil again for 7 minutes.
While the pearls cook, peel and cut the sweet potato and bananas as you like. Shave the palm sugar.
Add the sweet potato and palm sugar to the pot of cooked pearls. Cook until the sweet potato is tender and the palm sugar dissolves. Add the bananas and cook briefly until they soften. Add the salt.
Pour in the coconut milk and cook over low heat, stirring, until it boils. Remove from the heat.
Ready to enjoy.

Boil the water, palm sugar, and pandan leaf until the sugar dissolves.
Add the cut bananas and cook until tender.
Turn off the heat, pour in the sachet coconut milk, and stir well.
Serve the banana kolak warm.

Prepare the ingredients: cut the bananas into pieces, cut the sweet potatoes as you like and wash them clean, then prepare the other ingredients.
Bring the water to a boil in a pot, add the sweet potatoes, and boil for about 10 minutes until tender. Then add the pandan leaves and palm sugar, stirring until the palm sugar dissolves.
Also add the vanilla powder, salt, and granulated sugar, and stir briefly.
Then add the bananas, followed by the instant coconut milk, and stir again until the coconut milk is evenly mixed. Don't forget to adjust the taste; once it tastes right, turn off the heat.
The banana and sweet potato kolak is ready to serve, warm or cold. So delicious 👌.

strMeal: Kolak Pisang Ulin Campur Kolang Kaling
strInstructions: 1. Prepare the ingredients. Slice the kolang-kaling thinly; I cut each kolang-kaling piece in half. 2. Bring the water to a boil, then add the salt and pandan leaves. 3. Add the kolang-kaling and cook until slightly tender. 4. Add the palm sugar and stir until dissolved. 5. Add the cut Ulin bananas and cook until the bananas start to soften. 6. Pour in the instant coconut milk and stir gently. 7. Add granulated sugar if needed and cook until boiling, stirring gently the whole time. 8. Remove from the heat and serve. It tastes just as good served warm or chilled from the fridge.

Peel and cut the kepok bananas as you like.
Boil the water, palm sugar, granulated sugar, and pandan leaves until the sugar dissolves.
Add the bananas and cook until they are slightly tender.
Pour in the coconut milk and salt, stirring gently so the coconut milk doesn't split.
Cook over low heat until it boils and smells fragrant, then remove from the heat.

Bring the water to a boil, then add the cassava and purple sweet potato pieces. Cook until tender.
Add the salt, granulated sugar, pandan, and banana pieces and cook them together with the cassava.
Add the coconut milk. Cook again until everything is fully cooked and the coconut milk broth thickens slightly.
Prepare serving bowls and ladle in the kolak as needed.
strIngredient2: Purple sweet potato, peeled and diced

strInstructions:
Wash the mung beans, then soak them in hot water for 1 hour so they soften faster.
Boil the mung beans with 1 liter of water, the pandan leaves, and the ginger until tender.
Add the diagonally sliced kepok bananas, along with the granulated sugar and salt.
Pour in the thick coconut milk, stir well, and cook over low heat until it boils and everything is cooked.
Remove from the heat and serve warm.

Wash the kolang-kaling thoroughly and drain. Cut the kepok bananas as you like and put them in a pot.
Add the water, sugar, and salt, and cook until boiling.
Add the coconut milk, stir well, and adjust the taste. Bring to a boil again, then remove from the heat, add the liquid vanilla, and stir well.
Serve.

strMeal: Kolak Ketela + Pisang + Nangka🍌🥥 Kuah Santan Kental Manis Legit
strInstructions:
Prepare the ingredients.
Boil the white cassava with 2000 ml of water + 1 pandan leaf + 1/2 tsp salt. Boil for 15 minutes until half-tender. Discard the boiling water. This is done to get rid of the cassava's sap and raw smell, so the kolak smells fragrant.
Put the cassava back into a clean pot. Pour in 1500 ml of fresh water. Add the palm sugar, granulated sugar, ginger, and the remaining pandan leaf. Add the kepok bananas. Cook over medium heat for 5 minutes until the sugar blends in and the bananas start to soften.
Turn the heat down to the lowest setting. Pour in the thick coconut milk + salt + vanilla. Stir slowly in one direction. Cook for 5–7 minutes until it simmers gently and the broth thickens. Low heat + constant stirring. If the heat is high, the coconut milk will definitely split.
In the last 2 minutes, add the jackfruit, then turn off the heat. The jackfruit goes in last so its aroma doesn't fade and its color stays pretty.
Turn off the heat. Adjust the taste: rich sweetness, savoriness, and the fragrance of pandan, ginger, and jackfruit. Serve warm or cold.
strIngredient1: White cassava (ketela putih / singkong), peeled, cut into 3 cm pieces
strIngredient2: Kepok bananas, just-ripe, cut into 2–3 pieces
strIngredient3: Ripe jackfruit, cut up, seeds removed
strIngredient7: Thick coconut milk from 1 mature coconut
strIngredient8: Foolproof thick palm sugar syrup 🤎 glossy, pandan-scented
strIngredient9: (or use 400 g palm sugar, finely shaved)

strInstructions:
Cut the bananas into pieces and put them in a pot. Set aside.
Also cut the boiled cassava, then add it to the pot with the bananas.
Grate the coconut, add water, and squeeze out the milk. Add the coconut milk to the pot.
Add the pandan leaf, granulated sugar, and salt. Stir well and cook until boiling, then adjust the taste.
Ready to serve.

Cut up the cassava and bananas.
Cook the water and cassava until half-tender.
Add the bananas, sugar, salt, and pandan leaves. Cook until tender.
Add thick instant coconut milk as needed, stir well, and cook briefly.
Ready to serve.

Slice the palm sugar and soak it in 100 ml of boiling water until it dissolves, then strain. Cook the sugar water with the remaining water (400 ml) until boiling, then add the granulated sugar, salt, and pandan leaves.
Slice the sweet potato and bananas 1/2 cm thick, add them to the broth, and cook until done.
Add the Rose Brand coconut milk. Cook until boiling. Turn off the heat and serve.

strMeal: Kolak Pisang Awa Dan Ubi Cilembu
strInstructions:
Cut the ripe Awa bananas diagonally (I cut each banana into 3 so they don't fall apart when cooked).
Dice the Cilembu sweet potato and wash it clean (cut it however you like).
Put the coconut milk in a pot, then add the bananas and sweet potato, then the pandan leaf, salt, milk, and palm sugar. Cook until everything is done, adjust the taste, and it's ready to serve. (I like to add everything straight in with the coconut milk, so the coconut milk flavor soaks into the sweet potato and bananas.)

Peel the sweet potatoes, cassava, and bananas. Cut as you like.
Heat the water, palm sugar, and pandan, stirring until the palm sugar dissolves and it boils.
Add the cassava. Cook for about 10 minutes. Turn off the heat and wait 30 minutes. Then cook again and add the sweet potatoes. Wait until tender.
Add the salt and granulated sugar. Stir well. Add 3 packs of thick coconut milk (Kara). Stir again until evenly mixed. Taste, and when it's right, add the Raja Nangka bananas. Wait until it boils, stirring constantly so the coconut milk doesn't split.
The cooked kolak is ready to serve.
strIngredient7: Water, or 1/2 of a medium-sized pot
strIngredient8: Kara coconut milk, 65 ml size / 1 box of Kara, 200 ml size

strInstructions:
Cut up the sweet potato and bananas.
Bring the thin coconut milk to a boil. Add the sweet potato, sugar, salt, and pandan leaf. Boil until tender.
Add the bananas and the thick coconut milk. Add the vanilla too. Stir constantly until boiling so the coconut milk doesn't split. Then taste.

Boil the tapioca pearls in enough water using the 5:30:7 method. Once translucent, set aside. Boil water, then add the palm sugar, granulated sugar, and salt. Stir well. Add the cut bananas.
Pour in the Rose Brand instant coconut milk. Stir well. Cook until done. Adjust the taste.
Assemble in a bowl: banana kolak first, then add the pearls. Stir well. Serve warm 🤩

Peel and cut the orange sweet potato, then steam until tender.
Mash the cooked sweet potato, then add the tapioca flour, granulated sugar, and salt. Mix well, then shape as you like (keep them small, since they will expand later).
Boil enough water to cook the biji salak (the sweet potato balls). Add them in batches and remove once they float. Set aside.
Cook 1½ L of water. Add the pandan leaves, palm sugar, granulated sugar, and salt. While the water heats, cut up the bananas. Once it boils, add the bananas and biji salak.
Add the coconut milk and adjust the taste. Cook until the kolak boils again, then turn off the heat. The banana and biji salak kolak is ready to serve.

Cut up the boiled taro. Clean the bananas and pumpkin, then cut them up.
Bring water to a boil. Then add the pandan leaves, palm sugar, granulated sugar, and pumpkin. Boil until the sugar dissolves and the pumpkin is half-cooked.
Then add the coconut milk, salt, vanilla powder, bananas, and taro. Stir until boiling and the bananas are soft.
Then remove from the heat and serve.
strIngredient2: Hand of ripe kepok / raja bananas

strInstructions:
Steam the grated coconut for about 10 minutes.
Combine the Rose Brand coconut milk, water, and pieces of pandan leaf. Blend until smooth. Then strain and set aside.
Prepare a bowl and add the Rose Brand granulated sugar, eggs, and salt. Mix on high speed for about 10 minutes until the sugar dissolves and the batter turns pale white.
Then add the SP/emulsifier and mix again until the batter is thick, white, and leaves a trail.
Add the wheat flour a little at a time while stirring. Also add the coconut milk–water mixture and the food coloring. Stir until combined and there are no lumps of flour.
Put ¼ of the steamed coconut into the mold that has been greased with oil beforehand. Then pour the batter into the mold.
Steam for 15–20 minutes over medium heat. Line the pot lid with a cloth.
The putu ayu is ready to serve.

Combine all the coconut ingredients, then steam for 10 minutes. Turn off the stove and let it cool until warm.
Put 2 tbsp of the steamed coconut into a mold lightly greased with oil, press, level, and set aside.
Puree the purple sweet potato with the salt and coconut milk until completely smooth, set aside.
Beat the eggs, sugar, vanilla, and SP on high speed until the sugar dissolves and the mixture is white and fluffy.
Add the pureed purple sweet potato mixture and mix again until even.
Add the wheat flour, milk powder, cornstarch, and baking powder and stir again until even; lastly add the food coloring and fold with a spatula until evenly mixed.
Pour the batter into the molds containing the coconut until full, then steam in a preheated steamer for 20 minutes.
Turn off the stove, remove from the steamer and molds, and it's ready to enjoy.

Prepare the ingredients for the putu ayu cake.
Mix the grated coconut with the cornstarch, salt, and pandan leaf and stir well. Steam the grated coconut for 10 minutes, remove and set aside.
Beat the eggs, sugar, and salt on medium speed until the sugar dissolves (about 2 minutes). Then add the SP and mix again on high speed until fluffy, thick, and leaving a trail.
Pour in the coconut milk and mix on low speed only. Then add the wheat flour a little at a time while mixing slowly.
Add the chili-red coloring to the batter and mix well.

strMeal: Putu Ayu Bambu Cokelat Tanpa Bambu
strInstructions:
Steam the grated coconut with salt for 15 minutes, then remove and set aside.
Prepare the Rose Brand rice flour in a container.
Steam the Rose Brand rice flour for 15 minutes, then remove and set aside.
Pour the pandan paste water into the Rose Brand rice flour while still warm and stir well, then strain, pressing down on any lumps that remain.
Place 1/4 of the mixture in a pan, add sprinkles, cover with another 1/4 of the mixture, add sprinkles again, and finally cover with the remaining mixture.

strInstructions:
Mix and stir all the dry ingredients, then pour in the pandan juice gradually while stirring until the dough comes together.
Then heat the stove and cook the dough until it thickens and the color slowly turns bright or translucent.
While still hot, shape the dough and pour it into water containing ice cubes.
Next, to make the sugar sauce, boil water and palm sugar until half-liquid. Then add the pandan leaf and granulated sugar, stir until dissolved.

Serve and enjoy.

Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients,
Stir with a whisk until just combined, don't take too long or it will come out dense. If you want to add Ceres sprinkles inside the batter, go ahead. If steaming, pour the batter into a pan greased with butter/oil, and dust it thinly with flour.
For those using a steamer, wait until there's plenty of steam before putting the cake in. Steam for 30 minutes without opening the lid.
Once cooked, wait 5 minutes in the pan before removing. Once cooled, cut as you like.

Divide the batter in two, prepare a bowl, pour in the batter and add chili-red coloring, and leave the other bowl as white (original) batter, then put it into a triangle plastic bag. I like this all-in-one beating method, where the emulsifier is added after 5 minutes of beating 😍 So happy, the color turned out as I hoped 😍 *The coconut milk flavor isn't very strong, but this steamed sponge is better made yourself than bought; next time I make it I'll add more coconut milk 😊

Once cooked, take out of the steamer and out of the molds. The red-and-white steamed sponge is ready to serve.

Boil 400 ml of pandan paste, 400 ml of coconut milk and 800 g of granulated sugar. Set aside, wait until cool.
Mix 8 egg yolks and 200 g of granulated sugar, beat until the color changes.
Add alternately the boiled pandan paste solution and the wheat flour. Stir little by little.
Add the baking powder, baking soda, salt and vanilla
Finally add the cooking oil. Stir with a spatula so the oil doesn't settle at the bottom, okay.
Heat the steamer, wait until the water boils and there is plenty of steam.
Add the batter, steam for 30 minutes.
The cake is ready to serve.

strMeal: Bolu Kukus Gula Merah (Dengan Tepung Protein Tinggi)
strInstructions:
Prepare the ingredients
Boil the palm sugar, water, pandan leaf, and salt until dissolved, then strain and cool.
Beat the eggs and granulated sugar until dissolved.
Add the palm sugar solution, stir well.
Add the wheat flour, baking powder, baking soda, and vanilla, stir well.
Add the coconut milk and oil, stir until evenly mixed.
Pour the batter into steamed sponge molds.
Steam for 20 minutes over high heat until cooked.

strMeal: Bolu Kukus Apel Blender Tanpa Sp
strInstructions:
Heat the steamer over high heat and wrap its lid with a clean cloth.
Prepare steamed sponge molds and add paper cups.
Blend the eggs, sugar, and apple for 3–5 minutes until pale and foamy.
Pour the batter into a bowl, sift in the flour, baking powder, cinnamon, vanilla powder and salt, and stir gently.
Add the soda water, fold quickly and gently until even.
Take some of the batter, add dark red coloring, mix well, and set aside
Pour the batter into the molds until full, then add 1 tbsp of the red batter on top. Make a plus sign on top with a chopstick or toothpick
Steam over high heat for 15–20 minutes, don't open the steamer lid. (😭 Some bloomed, some were shy, but still worth the effort 💪)
Remove, take out of the molds, serve.

Prepare the ingredients. Beat all the ingredients (except the liquid margarine) in a mixer for 15 minutes on high speed,
Add the liquid margarine, fold until even down to the bottom of the bowl. Pour the batter into a snack maker that has been heated and lightly greased with margarine. Fill to 3/4 of the height of the snack maker because the batter will rise. Sprinkle with grated cheese
Use low heat, cook until evenly cooked. Remove and serve

In a bowl, put the wheat flour, granulated sugar, Indomilk Creamy Matcha sweetened condensed milk, water, and egg. Mix until even.
Only then add the baking powder, mix well, then add the cooking oil. Mix well again; no need to mix for too long, just until combined. Then let the batter rest for 15 minutes. Cover the bowl with a cloth.
While waiting, heat the mold over low heat, then thinly grease with margarine. After 15 minutes, pour the batter to 3/4 of the mold
Wait until bubbles appear, then add the topping. Close the mold, then add more topping to the cakes that have just bubbled. Close the mold again and cook until done, until the top is dry, or if you like a slightly wet surface you can remove it right away.
The matcha kue cubit is ready to serve
strIngredient3: Granulated sugar, can be increased to 50 g
strIngredient4: Indomilk Creamy Matcha sweetened condensed milk

strInstructions:
Add the egg, sugar, flour, baking powder, baking soda, and vanilla. Pour in the milk.
Stir evenly, add the vegetable oil/cooking oil.
Let rest for at least 15 minutes.
Heat the mold, thinly grease with oil. Wait until hot, then fill with the batter. Wait until steam rises so that cavities appear in the batter. Add the topping, then remove.
Serve.

Mix the sourdough discard with the egg, Rose Brand granulated sugar and vanilla.
Add the flour, baking powder and baking soda while sifting. Mix well. Add the oil, mix well.
Divide the batter in two, add the pandan-suji sediment or pandan paste to one portion. Cover and let the batter rest for 20–30 minutes.
Heat the mold for 3 minutes on low heat, grease with margarine. Pour in to 3/4 of the mold's volume. Close the mold, and once half-cooked, sprinkle with the topping. Cover and wait again until the desired doneness.
Remove, cool and serve.
strIngredient12: For topping (I, grated cheese and chocolate chips )

strInstructions:
Put the banana, sugar and egg into a bowl, then stir with a whisk. Then add the flour, baking powder and baking soda, stir well again.
Pour in the mixture of water and sweetened condensed milk, stir well again. Pour in the melted Rose Brand margarine and stir well again.
Heat the mold, grease with Rose Brand margarine. Pour in the batter, cook until done, remove.
Ready to enjoy.
strIngredient10: Rose Brand margarine for greasing the mold

strInstructions:
Prepare the ingredients, then beat the eggs and sugar until pale and slightly foamy
Combine all the dry ingredients in a bowl, plus add the Nutrisari, stir until even
Add the dry ingredients little by little to the beaten egg and sugar, stir well. Then add the coconut milk and water mixture to the batter while stirring well. Let the batter rest for at least 15 minutes.
After 15 minutes, heat the mold first on the stove over medium-to-low heat. Add enough butter for greasing
Fill the mold with batter to 3/4 of each hole because it will rise, and close it. When it's 1/2 cooked, open the lid to add sprinkles on top. Then close it again until fully cooked. Then it's ready to serve. Happy trying.
strIngredient3: Pack of instant coconut milk, 65 ml

strInstructions:
Crack the egg into the batter bowl. Beat with the sugar for 2–3 minutes until the batter is pale, slightly foamy, and the sugar dissolves
Sift the wheat flour, baking powder and salt into the bowl of egg and sugar batter.
Add the milk and vanilla extract. Stir until all the flour is evenly mixed, with no lumps
Add the melted margarine, stir until smooth
Let the batter rest for 15–20 minutes
Grease a frying pan with oil, then heat on LOW heat.
Pour in the batter. Add the topping when the batter is 1/2 cooked (there are bubbles).
Cover the pan, cook until the top is firm and a toothpick comes out clean when inserted.
Cool, then the kue cubit is ready to eat 👍🏻

Make the starter: mix and stir the starter ingredients until dissolved. Let sit for 10–15 minutes, until foamy.
Boil the coconut milk & sweetened condensed milk until boiling, stirring constantly so the coconut milk doesn't split. Remove. Let cool. Melt the margarine; once it's hot turn off the heat, swirl to melt it completely. Cool.
Beat the eggs, sugar & salt with a whisk until the sugar dissolves.
Add the cooled boiled coconut milk, mix well. Add the flour little by little while stirring until even, while slamming/kneading the batter. Add the Fermipan, mix well. Add the melted butter, fold while slamming/kneading. Don't mix for long so it doesn't turn out dense. Cover with a clean cloth, let rest for 1 hour
Grease the mold with oil, using a brush. Heat the mold (line the mold). Pour in the batter until almost full. Let it sit until the top of the batter is slightly set & has cavities, sprinkle with cheese / sprinkles, cover (approx. 2 min) so it cooks evenly. Use low heat. Continue until the batter is used up.
strIngredient6: Wheat flour, leveled in a belimbing (star-fruit) glass
strIngredient8: White sweetened condensed milk + 200 ml Kara coconut milk + water = 300 ml

strInstructions:
Beat the eggs and sugar with a mixer until pale and fluffy, then add the pandan paste.
Add the dry ingredients alternating with the liquid milk, mix well.
Add the melted margarine, fold gently. Mix in some of the jackfruit, mix well. Let rest for 20 minutes.
Pour the batter into the hot mold (low heat). When it starts to form pores, sprinkle on the remaining jackfruit.
Remove when cooked and serve.

strMeal: Kue Cubit Coklat Keju Cuma 1 Telur
strInstructions:
Beat the eggs and Rose Brand granulated sugar until the sugar dissolves.
Add all the batter ingredients except the margarine. Mix well
Add the margarine, mix well again.
Divide the batter into 2 portions. To one portion add cocoa powder that has been dissolved in warm water beforehand. Mix well. Cover with plastic wrap and let the batter rest for 30 minutes.
Heat the mold, grease with margarine. Pour in the batter, add the topping and cook until done.
The kue cubit is ready to serve. Happy trying

Lightly beat the egg and Rose Brand granulated sugar with a whisk or mixer until even and the sugar dissolves; add the flour and baking powder gradually, alternating with the liquid milk, while stirring.
Pour in the melted margarine and add the vanilla powder, stirring constantly until evenly mixed. Cover the batter with a clean cloth and let it rest for 20–30 minutes.
Heat the mold and grease it with margarine, pour in the batter until almost full, then cover and cook until half-done. Open the mold lid, add chocolate sprinkles as topping or as you like, close again, and cook until done.
Remove and serve

Crack the egg and add the sugar, then whisk until the sugar dissolves. Mix well with the water
Mix the wheat flour, salt, milk powder, baking powder, baking soda and cocoa powder.
Combine the beaten egg and water
Mix with the flour, stir until no lumps remain
Add the melted margarine, stir well
Heat a kue cubit mold that has been greased with oil/butter, fill with batter to about one-third; some of mine were overfilled too
Wait until it has cavities, add the topping. For molten kue cubit, remove it as soon as it has cavities so there is still wet/molten batter.
Wait about 2 minutes until the batter is fully cooked, lift out by scooping/pinching. Transfer to a serving dish. Serve.
strIngredient13: As desired: marshmallows, cut up, etc.

strInstructions:
Put all the ingredients into a bowl, stir until evenly combined
Prepare Rose Brand cooking oil in a container for greasing the mold
Add the milk and Rose Brand cooking oil, stir until the batter is smooth.
Grease the mold with margarine so it doesn't stick.
Pour the batter into the mold, bake until the surface is half-cooked.
Add topping if you like, continue baking until done.

👩‍🍳Mix all the batter ingredients until even. Cover the batter and let it rest for at least 30 minutes so it doesn't get lumpy.
👩‍🍳Heat the mold. Pour in 1 ladle of batter; when it is half-cooked, sprinkle with grated cheese and sprinkles. Close the mold so it cooks evenly.
👩‍🍳Remove and serve...

Mix the eggs, sugar & vanilla paste with a mixer, just until the sugar dissolves. Add the wheat flour, baking powder & cocoa powder, mix until even
Add the UHT milk & melted margarine, stir until evenly mixed. Cover & let rest for 15 minutes
Heat the kue cubit mold, grease with margarine & pour in the batter. Put sprinkles on top as topping & cover. Cook over low heat until done
Ready to enjoy warm

Mix the dry ingredients, stir briefly until even.
Add the vanilla, egg, and liquid milk. Stir until even with no lumps
Add the liquid margarine, stir until even. After that, it's best to let it rest for about 15 minutes.
Heat the mold, grease with margarine. Pour the batter into the mold, sprinkle with topping. Cook over medium 🔥 until cooked to your liking (half-done / fully done)

Mix the flour, sugar, salt, baking soda and baking powder together, stir well. Add the eggs, stir well.
Add the milk little by little while stirring so it doesn't get lumpy. Add the melted butter, stir well again
Heat the mold, grease with butter, pour in the batter to 3/4 of the mold, add the mozzarella filling, cover and wait until it bubbles, then add the chocolate, wait until cooked, remove
Serve with additional sprinkled cheese

In a bowl, mix the wheat flour, granulated sugar, baking soda, baking powder, vanilla, and salt, stir well.
Add the egg and liquid milk, stir well.
Add the melted margarine, stir well, until thick.
Cover the batter, let it rest for ± 15 minutes.
Heat the mold, pour in the batter without filling it fully, because it will rise. Once half-cooked, add the topping of sprinkles or raisins or whatever you like. Cover, wait briefly until a crust forms on the bottom.
Remove. Ready to serve.

Mix the flour, baking powder, baking soda, granulated sugar & salt. Stir.
Pour the liquid milk into the flour mixture, stir well. Pour in the melted margarine, stir well.
Heat the kue cubit mold. Grease with margarine. Pour the batter into the mold, wait until ¾ cooked. Add topping as you like. Let it sit until dry & cooked. Serve.

strMeal: Poffertjes / Kue Cubit Belanda By Chef Devina Hermawan
strInstructions:
Combine the wheat flour, cornstarch, sugar, salt, baking powder, yeast, egg, milk, and liquid margarine into one. > stir until even with no lumps
Let the batter rest for 1 hour. > If using flavoring, the batter can be divided into 2 or the whole batch can be flavored. (stir well)
Heat the mold, then grease with butter > Pour the batter into the mold, cook over medium heat > Cook until all sides are slightly browned. > Repeat until the batter is used up
Arrange on a serving plate and sprinkle with powdered sugar and the jam you like (put the jam in a separate container). Note: Even without powdered sugar, the cake already tastes a little sweet, so adjust to taste <3
The kue cubit is ready to serve <3

strMeal: Kue Cubit Anti Gagal Anti Bantet🤏🏻 #Idebekalsekolah
strInstructions:
Mix all the ingredients, stir using a whisk
Let the batter rest for 15 minutes
Pour into the mold; I used a takoyaki mold. Fill it 1/2 full because it will rise. Cover the mold
Once it has risen and has holes, add the topping as you like. It can be fully cooked or half-cooked.
If you want it half-cooked, remove it right away; if you want it fully cooked, cover again until done. Enjoy

Wash the rice until clean, drain. Fry the Medan anchovies until cooked, set aside. Slice the shallots, garlic, and curly red chilies.
Sauté the sliced spices until fragrant. Add the lemongrass, bay leaves, kaffir lime leaves, ginger, and galangal, sauté briefly, then add the fried anchovies, stir well.
Add the rice, stir well with the spices. Pour in the water, add the salt and stock powder, then cook while stirring until it becomes nasi aron (partially cooked rice).
Transfer the nasi aron to a steamer pot and steam until the rice is fully cooked, about 30–45 minutes.
Serve the nasi liwet with favorite side dishes such as fried chicken, tempeh, tofu, sambal, raw vegetables (lalapan), and crackers.
strIngredient16: Porsi ayam goreng ayam goreng lengkuas
strIngredient17: Porsi sambal bawang sambal bawang ala dapur mama_at

strInstructions:
Pressure-cook Ingredients A for 45 minutes, or 2 hours if using a slow cooker, remove, drain, and cut as you like.
Sauté Ingredients B and Ingredients C until fragrant, add water and then the pressure-cooked tendon/kokot; once boiling, add the coconut milk, salt and mushroom stock, cook until the seasoning is absorbed, serve.

Prepare all the ingredients needed. Clean the beef tendon, then cut as you like. Boil the tendon with ginger and bay leaves until the tendon is a bit tender and its characteristic smell is reduced. Once cooked, discard the boiling water and drain the tendon.
Prepare a wok, heat the oil and sauté the ground spice paste with the lemongrass, galangal, bay leaves, and kaffir lime leaves until fragrant and cooked. Add the boiled tendon, stir until the seasoning is evenly distributed and absorbed. Add enough water, then cook until boiling and the seasoning is absorbed.
Dissolve 50 g of Fiber Creme in 150 ml of water, then pour it into the dish. Stir gently until evenly mixed. Add the instant stock, granulated sugar, salt, and tamarind solution. Stir and adjust the taste.
Add the long beans, cook briefly until the sauce thickens and the seasoning is absorbed into the tendon
Remove and serve warm with steamed white rice
strIngredient2: Strands of long beans, cut as you like
strIngredient3: Fiber Creme, dissolved in 150 ml water

strInstructions:
Sauté the ground spice paste and ground red chili, cook until done
Add the extras
Add the tendon, water and young jackfruit, stir well
Add the long beans
Add the salt, chicken stock powder and coconut milk, adjust the taste
Serve

strMeal: Gulai Tunjang (Kaki Sapi) Ala Warung Padang
strInstructions:
Clean the cow's feet by burning them first, then scrape off the thin outer skin. Cut up, wash clean, then boil them in a pressure cooker. Add water, bay leaves, ginger, kaffir lime leaves and lemongrass. Pressure-cook for 1 hour.
Prepare the spices. Grind the ground spice ingredients.
Sauté the ground spices until cooked.
Add a little water then add the lemongrass, bay leaves, galangal, kaffir lime leaves, and turmeric leaf. Add the ground pepper, then cook again until the spices are absorbed.
Add the tamarind water. Add 3 liters of water. Add the coconut milk and sweetened condensed milk.
Strain the pressure-cooked cow's feet. Add the tender cow's feet to the broth. Add the seasoning salt and stock powder. You can get creative to your own taste.
Cook until done and boiling, stirring occasionally so the coconut milk doesn't split.
Serve with rice and other accompaniments.
strIngredient23: Biji cabai merah keriting (sesuai selera,bisa ditambah rawit kalau suka pedas )

strInstructions:
Boil the cow skin and young jackfruit separately, drain. Grind the roasted coconut.
Grind all the spices, then sauté with all the dump-in spices (bumbu cemplung), including the ambu-ambu, until cooked and fragrant; add the whole bird's-eye chilies if you like it spicy.
Pour in the water, then add the cow skin and young jackfruit. Boil with the spices until boiling and the spices are absorbed.
Pour in the coconut milk, don't forget to check the taste. Once it boils again, turn off the heat and serve 😋

Boil the tendon with bruised ginger and bay leaf until boiling, drain.
Grind the red chili, shallots, garlic, candlenuts, ginger, and turmeric. Add a little water for grinding. *I ground it in 2 batches
Add the ground spices, cook until the water is gone, then add cooking oil. Sauté until fragrant. Then add the turmeric leaf, kaffir lime leaves, bruised lemongrass, star anise, and cardamom, and stir well. Add the curry spices, add the granulated sugar,
Add the thin coconut milk. Add Kapal brand salt
Add the tendon, stir well with the spices. Cook until the tendon is tender, add the thick coconut milk from the first pressing of the coconut. Cook until the spices are absorbed and it thickens.
Adjust the taste, remove and serve.

strMeal: Gulai Kikil Kuping Sapi (Sy Pakai Tunjang Dan Usus)
strInstructions:
Bring water to a boil, add the tendon, and cook for 30 minutes or until tender. Remove and set aside.
Grind the spices, then sauté with the dump-in spices (bumbu cemplung) until fragrant. Then add the coconut milk. Don't forget to stir occasionally so the coconut milk doesn't split.
Once it boils, add the tendon. Cook until the sauce reduces or the tendon is tender.
Then add the intestines. Cook while stirring occasionally; don't use too high a heat, because it will make the intestines burst. Cook until boiling (no need to cook too long since the intestines are already cooked). Add the whole bird's-eye chilies, stir well. Adjust the taste. When it's good, remove.
Ready to serve 👍👍.

Sambal kecap: mix Indofood sweet soy sauce, sliced shallots, and red bird's-eye chilies for the sambal kecap.
Tempeh satay: cut the tempeh into cubes, not too small so it doesn't break apart easily.
Grind the spices.
Mix the ground spices with Indofood sweet soy sauce and cooking oil into one seasoning.
Put the tempeh into the seasoning, stir well and gently squeeze so the seasoning is absorbed. Let the seasoned tempeh sit for 20 minutes in the fridge to firm up.
Grill the tempeh in a non-stick pan until the surface is browned. (Tip: use medium heat and turn it over so it doesn't burn)
Once cooked, skewer the tempeh with aluminum skewers. Serve the tempeh satay with the sambal kecap, sliced onion and chilies.

Cut the goat meat into satay-sized pieces. In a bowl, season the goat meat with the ground spices. Add the limo lime juice and salt to taste, and leave it in the refrigerator for a while before skewering (preferably use iron/stainless steel skewers). Grill over coals, occasionally brushing with the basting ingredients, until cooked. Serve with gulai broth. How to make it: Sauté the ground spices, lemongrass and kaffir lime leaves until slightly fragrant, then add the sliced meat trimmings and continue sautéing until the trimmings are slightly cooked. Add the dry (powdered) spices, add thin coconut milk and cook until slightly thickened and the spices taste cooked. Add thick coconut milk and continue cooking over medium heat. Ready to serve to accompany the Klatak satay.

Cut the chicken into satay-sized pieces,
Cut the onion into squares the same size as the chicken pieces
Grind the garlic + coriander + salt + stock powder
Mix the chicken pieces with the ground spices, taste (it should taste salty and savory)... let sit for 30 minutes
Thread the marinated chicken onto satay skewers, alternating with the onion
Heat a fairly wide non-stick pan so the skewers fit, add a little margarine, grill the satay in it, turning until cooked (golden brown)
Serve the satay with sambal kecap (a mixture of red bird's-eye chili + sweet soy sauce + diced raw tomato)

Prepare the beef and liver, cut into cubes, and thread onto satay skewers. Add grated pineapple. Coat the satay with it.
Prepare the grilling sauce: grind the garlic, coriander and salt, add the sweet soy sauce and cooking oil.
Prepare a non-stick pan for grilling the satay after coating it with the grilling sauce. Grill the satay until cooked.
Prepare the dipping chili sauce. And the satay is ready to enjoy, even more complete with gulai broth.

Blend the pineapple. Prepare the meat. Cut the meat into cubes. Soak in the blended pineapple for about 30 minutes.
After 30 minutes, discard the pineapple used for soaking. Then prepare the ground spices. Grind the marinade spices, then mix with the meat pieces that have been soaked in pineapple. Let sit again for about 30 minutes.
Thread the meat pieces onto skewers (sujen/satay skewers). Ready to grill. Grill the satay until cooked.
Serve the satay with the accompaniments... Mmm, yummy... Tender and the seasoning is absorbed

Cover the goat meat with papaya leaves for 30 minutes – 1 hour. Then cut the goat meat into pieces.
Prepare the marinade spices, grind the marinade spices
Mix the meat with the spices evenly, let sit for 30 minutes. Then skewer the meat (originally done with iron rods, but since I don't have any I just used regular satay skewers)
Grill until the meat is tender. Then set aside
Making the goat gulai: cut the goat meat into pieces then wrap the goat meat in papaya leaves.
Prepare the gulai spices, grind until smooth (or not, it's okay, ma'am, like mine 🤭)
Sauté the ground spices until fragrant, then the dump-in spices, add water, once it boils add the coconut milk, add sugar and salt, then add the goat meat, cook until the meat is tender and cooked, then remove
Serve the satay klatak with the gulai broth. Yogyakarta-style satay klatak is ready to serve
strIngredient1: Goat meat with some fat still on
strIngredient8: Broth taken from the goat gulai

strInstructions:
Cut the meat as you like. Mix the meat with the ground spices. Stir well. Let sit until the spices are absorbed. I wrapped the meat in papaya leaves and then let it sit for 30 minutes.
Skewer the meat with satay skewers.
Grill the meat over charcoal until the meat is cooked.
Arrange the satay klatak on a plate then sprinkle with pepper. Serve with the accompaniments. Mine was sweet soy sauce mixed with chili, tomato and sliced shallots.

Skewer the cut-up goat meat, then coat with ground garlic
Then grill the satay; when it's about half-cooked, dip it into a mixture of sweet soy sauce & salty soy sauce, then grill again and dip in soy sauce again... grill until cooked, and it's ready to serve
For serving, put cabbage and tomato on a plate, add sweet soy sauce, then place the satay, then sprinkle ground pepper over the satay

1. Cut the goat meat into dice, clean it of sinews. Then thread onto satay skewers, 3 pieces each. 2. Grind the garlic and salt, then add water, mix well 3. Prepare the grill; I used a gas grill. 4. Grill the goat satay skewers until the meat changes color, remove the skewers and dip them into the dipping mixture, grill again until cooked, don't let it burn. 5. Serve the klatak-style goat satay with its accompaniments. Ta-da, done 👌

Slice the goat meat as you like * thread 3–4 slices per skewer * soak in the soaking marinade
Grill the satay until cooked. Note: it's usually served with gulai broth for those not yet used to eating sate klathak

Prepare the ingredients needed.
Grind the garlic, pepper and salt. Add water to make grinding easier. Set aside. Cut the carrot into small cubes. Set aside.
Boil the vermicelli until soft, then drain and cut into pieces. Set aside.
Heat oil then sauté the shallots and onion until wilted and fragrant. Add the carrot and the ground spices. Add a little water. Cook until the carrot is cooked.
Add the ground spices, stir well. Then add the boiled vermicelli. Stir well. Then cook the vermicelli until done. Finally add the chopped spring onion.
Stir well then taste. Adjust the taste if needed. If the taste is okay, turn off the heat and let it cool slightly. Once cool, crack the eggs into a container and beat lightly.
Put the fried vermicelli into the container, then stir well. Set aside.
Take 1 spring roll wrapper, then add the vermicelli and egg mixture, then fold into a square. Do this until the ingredients are used up.
Heat a little oil then fry the martabak until both sides are dry and browned. Fry with just a little oil. If the oil starts to run out, add a little at the edge of the pan. Once both sides are dry, drain.
Serve with green bird's-eye chilies.
strIngredient8: Cooking oil for sautéing the spices and frying the martabak
strIngredient15: Seasoning sachets from the instant vermicelli packs

strMeal: Martabak Telur Kornet Kulit Lumpia Pedas
strInstructions:
Prepare the ingredients needed such as eggs, leek, fine salt, ground pepper, stock powder, instant curry seasoning powder, bird's-eye chilies if using, and also corned beef. Wash the spring onion clean then cut into small pieces and set aside. Also prepare the spring roll wrappers and set aside.
Crack the eggs into a large clean bowl then add the corned beef and the seasonings used such as fine salt, ground pepper, stock powder and instant curry seasoning powder.
Beat the seasoned eggs with the corned beef until everything is combined. Finally add the leek pieces and bird's-eye chilies into the seasoned corned beef egg mixture.
Beat the eggs again until all the ingredients are evenly mixed. Pour 2–3 tablespoons of cooking oil into a non-stick pan. Place 1 spring roll wrapper in the middle.
Then place 4 more wrappers around the surface of the non-stick pan so the whole pan is covered with spring roll wrappers (as in the photo). After that pour the seasoned egg mixture into the pan and level it. Cover the egg surface again with 1 spring roll wrapper.
Fold the spring roll wrappers over the egg surface so that they cover all parts of the egg and form a square (as in the photo). Turn on medium-to-low heat and let it cook until the bottom is dry, cooked and turns brown, then flip. If the oil seems insufficient, you can add another 2–3 tablespoons. Cook again until the whole surface of the martabak is dry, cooked and turns brown, then remove and drain.
After that, cut the egg martabak into pieces of your preferred size. Add cucumber pickle or cucumber-carrot-onion pickle or any other pickle to taste.
The corned beef spring roll wrapper egg martabak is ready to enjoy as a snack with tea or coffee, or as a side dish with rice. Happy trying 🙏🥰.
strIngredient9: Bird's-eye chilies, can be skipped if you don't want it spicy

strInstructions:
Mince the meat and spring onion. Heat a little oil, sauté the minced meat until it changes color. Add all the seasonings, stir well.
Cook until done and the liquid reduces. Turn off the heat, let the steam dissipate and cool slightly. Mix the sautéed meat, eggs and spring onion, beat well.
Heat oil, arrange the spring roll wrappers around the edges and center of the pan. Add the mixture and level it.
Let the bottom set a bit, then cover the top. Fry each side until golden brown, remove and set aside.
Put all the sauce ingredients into the pan (you can use the same pan used for sautéing the meat), stir and sauté briefly, then add water.
Cook until boiling and slightly reduced, taste. Cut the cucumber small, mix with vinegar, sugar and salt, stir well (keep in the fridge first so it's tastier).
Cut the egg martabak into several pieces, serve with the sauce and pickle (the sauce can be served separately or mixed with the cucumber pickle).

Put the duck egg, the cut spring onion, grated carrot, instant rendang seasoning, and enough flavor enhancer into a bowl.
Stir well with a fork.
Heat a pan, add enough cooking oil. When it's hot, place 2 spring roll wrappers in the pan, followed by the beaten egg. Level it and cover with the remaining 2 spring roll wrappers. (I totally forgot to take a photo when the egg mixture was leveled 🥲 I only remembered after placing the last 2 wrappers).
Once the bottom layer is brown, flip. Then remove and serve once both sides are evenly browned.

Prepare all the ingredients, slice the spring onion, crush the tofu
In a bowl put the tofu, spring onion, eggs, salt, pepper and mushroom stock
Take a spring roll wrapper, put in 1 tbsp of the mixture and close it like an envelope; before folding the wrappers, prepare the pan and oil and turn on the stove, so that once you finish folding you can fry right away because the mixture is wet
Do this until all the ingredients are used up, serve with cabe ceplus.

Prepare the ingredients. Cook the filling: sauté the onion until fragrant. Add the ground beef. Stir well. Add Sasa curry seasoning, pepper and sugar. Stir. Cook until done.
Cook the filling meat. Once cooked, mix with eggs, spring onion, and sugar, salt, pepper. Stir well. Wrap with spring roll wrappers. Fry in hot oil. Flip the sides. Remove when cooked
Serve with bird's-eye chilies
strIngredient4: Filling ingredients (cook a large batch, put the rest in the freezer)

strInstructions:
Prepare the tofu that has been washed clean, then place it in a bowl and mash it. Once smooth, add the spring onion, carrot and eggs
Also the minced chicken that has been stir-fried (you can replace it with beef too). Then add all the seasonings as well.
Stir all the mixture until evenly mixed. You can taste it first to make sure the flavor is right. Then take 1 spoonful of the mixture and place it on a spring roll wrapper.
Then fold it like an envelope; to prevent leaking, my suggestion is to double the wrapper. And fry over medium heat until cooked/golden brown. The tofu martabak is ready to serve with pickled chili / your favorite sauce. Let's try it ❤️
strIngredient2: Pack of Pisang Aroma / spring roll wrappers

strInstructions:
Clean the leek and bird's-eye chilies then cut as you like along with the sausage, then set aside. Crack the eggs and place them in a bowl, add the chopped bird's-eye chilies, leek, sausage, salt, pepper, stock powder if using, and curry powder.
Then beat until the seasonings and all ingredients are evenly mixed. Prepare the spring roll wrapper then add enough filling (I used 2 tablespoons).
Then fold the left and right sides inward, then fold the bottom and top inward as well.
So that it forms a square, then set aside. Repeat filling the martabak until the filling is used up. After that heat cooking oil over medium heat, then fry the martabak until the bottom is dry and cooked.
Flip the martabak so all sides cook evenly. Once it turns golden brown, remove and drain.
Sausage martabak is ready to enjoy and even better when accompanied by cucumber pickle, or you can also use chili sauce, tomato sauce, mayonnaise or another fritter sambal. Happy trying 🙏🤗.

strInstructions:
Mash the tofu, thinly slice the cabbage and spring onion.
Mix the tofu, egg, cabbage, spring onion, garlic powder, mushroom stock, salt, and pepper.
Heat a little oil in a pan, place a sheet of spring roll wrapper. Pour the mixture over the wrapper, level it. Cover the mixture with another sheet of wrapper.
Fry over medium heat until both sides are browned and cooked. Remove, drain.
Ready to serve.

Prepare the ingredients
Mash the tofu, then add the eggs, mushroom stock, pepper, salt, turmeric powder, then stir until evenly mixed.
I added oyster mushrooms that I shredded, stir well.
Wet the rice paper with water, then fill with the tofu filling, then fold or wrap as you like. Then heat a non-stick pan with a little oil, then pan-fry until cooked (leave a little space so they don't stick to the others).
And here's the result... plus other vegetable dishes.

1. Prepare all the ingredients, clean and wash the fish, then cut 2. Marinate the fish with lime juice, let sit for about 15 minutes. Rinse and set aside. 3. Grind the ground spices (shallots, garlic, red chili, bird's-eye chili, ginger and candlenuts), then add oil to make blending easier. 4. Sauté the ground spices; since there was already oil when blending, I didn't add more oil. Sauté until the spices are cooked down. Add the kaffir lime leaves, galangal, lemongrass, salt, stock and MSG. Taste. 5. Place the fish on a banana leaf, brush the fish on both sides with the sautéed spices, add tomato and basil, then wrap the fish, securing the top and bottom of the leaf with toothpicks. Then steam for about 25 minutes in a preheated steamer. The pepes is ready to serve with warm rice.

Pound the red chilies, shallots, garlic, turmeric, ginger, salt, sugar, and mushroom stock powder until smooth.
Coat the entire surface of the mackerel with the seasoning paste.
Add curry leaves on top of the fish (if using).
Wrap the fish in fresh banana leaves and secure the ends. (I just wrapped it and folded it closed.)
Cook on a hot nonstick pan, turning after a few minutes.
Brush the banana leaves with margarine and continue cooking until fragrant.
Ready to serve. This combination of side dishes is so delicious. Masya Allah, I can still remember the wonderful taste of the pepes fish.

strMeal: Pepes Ikan Nila Ala Kanjeng Mami
strInstructions:
Clean the tilapia using lime juice.
Once clean, you can marinate it with salt.
Pound the chilies, garlic, shallots, ginger, turmeric, coriander, galangal, lemongrass base, and tamarind. I blend mine instead.
Add cooking oil as needed.
Add 1 spoonful of white sugar, 1.5 teaspoons of salt, and mushroom stock powder. Adjust the seasoning to taste. Adjust the saltiness and sweetness according to your preference.
After marinating the fish, coat the fish that will be wrapped with the ground seasoning paste.
Prepare banana leaves, lemon basil, lime leaves, Indonesian bay leaves, lemongrass cut into small pieces, and bird's eye chilies.
Then wrap the fish.
Steam for 30 minutes.

strMeal: Pepes Ikan Mas Tulang Lunak Praktis (Presto)
strInstructions:
Prepare all the seasonings and ingredients. The carp should be scaled and gutted. You can marinate it in lime juice for 15 minutes, then rinse and drain.
Sauté the Sajiku gulai seasoning mix in a little cooking oil until fragrant.
Add 800 ml of water and stir evenly. Then add the kandis tamarind fruit.
Add the coconut milk and stir evenly. Turn off the heat and set aside.
Place banana leaves at the bottom of the pressure cooker, arrange one layer of fish, then pour in the seasoning mixture until the fish is submerged.
Arrange the fish and banana leaves in alternating layers so the fish do not stick together.
Place banana leaves and the pressure cooker rack on top to keep the fish in place during cooking.
Turn the heat to high until the pressure regulator spins rapidly. Then lower the heat while keeping the regulator spinning steadily. Pressure-cook for 45 minutes, starting when the regulator spins steadily.
After 45 minutes, turn off the heat and wait until all steam pressure has been released and the cooker is safe to open.
Carefully remove the fish so it does not fall apart.
The soft-boned carp is ready to serve.

Coat the cleaned fish pieces. I used fillets bought directly from the market. Coat with lime juice and a little salt. Let sit for 10–15 minutes, then rinse lightly.
Blend all the ingredients for the seasoning paste. Mix the paste with sliced lime leaves, Indonesian bay leaves, lemongrass, and galangal. Stir well and taste (the seasoning should be slightly more savory and salty so it flavors the fish properly). Sauté until fragrant, then sauté the seasoning with the fish fillets. Cover briefly to let the seasoning absorb, then remove from the heat.
Take 2 banana leaves and stack them to prevent leaks. Put a little seasoning and herbs at the bottom. Place the fish on top, then cover with the remaining seasoning and add lemon basil. Roll neatly and secure both ends with toothpicks or small skewers.
Heat the steamer. Steam the fish pepes for 25–30 minutes until evenly cooked and fragrant.
After steaming, briefly grill the pepes until the banana leaves are slightly charred and browned. Serve.
strIngredient1: Fresh fish, cut into pieces and cleaned
strIngredient11: Curly red chilies and 3 bird's eye chilies
strIngredient14: Lemon basil leaves for garnishing the fish pepes

strInstructions:
Coat the cleaned tilapia evenly with lime juice and a little salt. Let sit for 15 minutes.
Pound all the seasoning ingredients, including shallots, garlic, toasted candlenuts, bird's eye chilies, curly chilies, ginger, lemongrass, and galangal.
Heat coconut oil, then pour it over the ground seasoning.
Dice the tomatoes, slice the spring onions, lemon basil, and bilimbi, then mix them with the ground seasoning, Indonesian bay leaves, and torn lime leaves. Add ground pepper and stir again. You may add powdered stock if you like (I skipped it).
Take a banana leaf and place the tilapia on top. Coat it with the ground seasoning mixed with the chopped tomatoes and herbs.
Wrap tightly and secure both ends with small skewers. Heat the steamer, then steam the tilapia pepes for about 30 minutes until cooked and flavorful.

strMeal: Pepes Ikan Asin / Linting Gerih Abang
strInstructions:
Prepare wilted banana leaves, wipe them with a clean cloth, and prepare half-mature coconut. Rinse the lemon basil and salted fish under running water.
Grate the coconut, then pound the garlic, shallots, and chilies. You can add turmeric if you like.
Mix the ground seasoning and chopped leek with the grated coconut in a bowl.
Prepare the banana leaves. Arrange the seasoned grated coconut on them, place the salted fish on top, and remember to add lemon basil leaves.
Roll or fold the banana leaves tightly at the ends and secure with toothpicks or pieces of broomstick, repeating until all the salted fish is used.
Prepare a preheated steamer, arrange the parcels inside, and steam for 20 minutes. Turn off the stove. The rolled gerih parcels are ready to enjoy with warm rice.
strIngredient8: A handful of lemon basil leaves

strInstructions:
Clean the fish, coat with lime juice, and let sit for about 10 minutes. Rinse again. Prepare the ground seasoning ingredients and blend until smooth.
Put the ground seasoning in a bowl with the fish and coat evenly. Add sliced tomatoes and diagonally sliced large red chilies. Take a banana leaf, place the fish on it, add one Indonesian bay leaf, and secure both ends.
Place the parcels in a preheated steamer and steam until cooked, about 30 minutes. Remove and grill on a nonstick pan, turning occasionally until fragrant.
Serve the scad fish pepes with warm rice and fresh vegetables.
strIngredient3: Red tomato, cut into neat slices

strInstructions:
Grind the seasoning ingredients until smooth.
Mash the tofu with a mortar and pestle, then mix it into the ground seasoning.
Add the fish eggs to the tofu and stir until evenly combined, then wrap.
Steam for about 40 minutes over medium heat.
strIngredient3: Lemon basil leaves, skipped because I forgot to buy them

strInstructions:
Grind all the ingredients for the seasoning paste until smooth.
Dice the tomatoes and bilimbi.
Add the egg and stir well.
Add the fish pieces prepared earlier and stir until combined. Let sit for 10 minutes so the seasoning can absorb.
Add the ground seasoning to the bowl containing the tomatoes and bilimbi, then add salt, sugar, and mushroom stock powder. Taste and adjust the seasoning.
Wrap the fish mixture in banana leaves.
Steam the pepes for 30 minutes until cooked.
Remove and serve.

Clean the fish, rinse thoroughly, then marinate and let sit for 10 minutes.
~ Grind the seasonings, then sauté the ground seasoning and aromatics until fragrant. Add sugar and salt as needed, stir well, and taste. Add the tomatoes, stir until softened, then turn off the heat.
~ Arrange banana leaves in the steamer, add some lemon basil and seasoning, then place the fish on top.
~ Cover the fish with seasoning, lemon basil, bilimbi, and chilies, then cover with another banana leaf.

Marinate the fish with lime juice and 1 tsp of salt. Let sit for 15 minutes.
Toast the seasonings, then blend with a little water. Sauté the ground seasoning in a little cooking oil. Cook until the raw aroma disappears (do not let the oil separate or the seasoning turn brown). Turn off the stove, add salt to the seasoning, and stir well. Set aside.
Coat the fish evenly with the sautéed seasoning paste.
Arrange 2 banana leaves in the steamer. Add galangal, lemongrass, and a little seasoning paste. Arrange the fish, tomatoes, bird's eye chilies, and lemon basil on top.
Cover the fish with 2 banana leaves and steam for 30 minutes from the time the water boils.
The fish pepes is ready to serve 😊

Grind all the ingredients for the seasoning paste until smooth. Add sliced lemongrass and pound briefly until combined with the paste. Add salt, sugar, powdered stock, and flavor enhancer, then mix well.
Take a banana leaf, add 1 tbsp of seasoning paste, then place lemon basil and cue fish on top.
Add another tablespoon of seasoning over the cue fish and spread it over the entire surface. Add a little more lemon basil, then roll and secure both ends with skewers or toothpicks.
Steam the pepes for about 30 minutes or until the seasoning is cooked. Grill the pepes over charcoal (or use an old nonstick pan like I did) until the seasoning smells fragrant. Ready to serve.

Prepare the ingredients.
Grind the seasonings, then marinate the fish for 30 minutes.
Take the banana leaves and double them in the middle. Place the fish and seasoning on top, then add Indonesian bay leaves, lemon basil, bilimbi, and lemongrass. Fold neatly and secure.
Steam for 1 hour, then grill in a nonstick pan until the leaves are slightly charred.
Ready to serve.

Blend the ground seasoning with water, then pour it into a pan. Add lime leaves, Indonesian bay leaves, and bird's eye chilies. Add salt, sugar, and powdered stock, then stir well. Cook until the water reduces slightly (do not let it dry out) and the leaves wilt.
Turn off the stove and add the tomatoes. Stir well, taste, and set aside. Arrange banana leaves, place the fish on top, then add the ground seasoning and lemon basil. Wrap and secure with toothpicks or skewers (I used staples), then set aside.
Heat the steamer and steam for about 45 minutes or until cooked.
The pindang fish and lemon basil pepes is ready to serve. Enjoy 😊
strIngredient3: A handful of lemon basil leaves

strInstructions:
Chop all the ingredients: shallots, garlic, lemongrass, curly red chilies, green chilies, bird's eye chilies, spring onions, green tomatoes, and bilimbi. Mix everything together (set aside some melinjo leaves, tomatoes, bilimbi, and lemon basil). Rub the mixture together with 2 tbsp of used cooking oil.
Place the melinjo leaves and lemon basil at the bottom, add the tomatoes, then place the salted peda fish that has been soaked in water. Coat with Sasa seasoning and add all the prepared seasoning mixture.
Cover and secure with toothpicks. Steam for 20 minutes, then grill in a nonstick pan until cooked.
The salted peda fish pepes is ready to serve.

strMeal: Pepes Ikan Kacang Kacang Mangga Muda
strInstructions:
Prepare the pepes ingredients. Wash the fish, mango, chilies, garlic, lemon basil, bilimbi, and lime leaves thoroughly. Heat the banana leaves over the stove until wilted.
Wash each banana leaf with soap, rinse under running water, and drain. Fry the fish in 5 tbsp of oil until golden (it does not need to be fully cooked; just fry until the skin forms).
Chop the mango and set aside. Pound all the ingredients for the ground seasoning.
Add the red basic seasoning paste and pound until evenly combined (sorry, I forgot to take a photo when adding the red basic seasoning paste to the mortar). Add sliced green chilies, bilimbi, and some lemon basil. Take 2 banana leaves and place the seasoning mixture along the leaves.
Place the fish and fish eggs on top, then cover with more seasoning mixture and lemon basil. Roll gently and secure both ends with toothpicks.
Grill the pepes on a grill pan over medium-low heat. Turn occasionally so it cooks evenly.
Once cooked, remove the pepes. Continue grilling the remaining parcels. The young mango fish pepes is ready to enjoy while warm.

strInstructions:

Wash the fish with lime juice and make shallow cuts in the flesh.
Coat the fish with the ground seasoning mixed with salt and granulated sugar [me: this step was skipped because I forgot to coat the fish with the ground seasoning first] 🤦🏻‍♀️

Heat the steamer and bring the water to a boil. Steam the pepes for 30 minutes until cooked.

Serve.

strInstructions:
Prepare the ingredients.
Mash the tofu and slice the chilies and onions.
Mix the white tofu, grated coconut, melinjo leaves, chilies, shallots and garlic, granulated sugar, ground pepper, and mushroom stock powder. Pour in the coconut milk and stir well.
Crack the raw salted eggs, chop the yolks, and add them to the tofu mixture. Taste the mixture. If it is not salty enough, add salt.

Mix the eggs with the onion, chilies, spring onion, seasonings, and botok. Stir until evenly combined.
Add the glass noodles and mix again. Heat the oil, then pour in the egg mixture and cook until set. Flip it over so it does not burn.
Serve.

Mash the tofu with a fork, then add the egg, ground seasoning, oyster mushrooms, grated coconut, palm sugar, lemon basil, salt, and flavor enhancer. For a spicier version, add red chilies and sliced green chilies.
