strInstructions:
Wash the bitter melon, cut it lengthwise along the top without cutting all the way through. Remove all the seeds. Soak and rub the bitter melon with salt water for 15 minutes. Slice the shrimp and kaffir lime leaves. Boil the macaroni until soft.
Filling: Combine all the ground spices, grated coconut, shrimp, and coconut milk. Mix well.

Mix all the ingredients in a bowl and stir well.

Wrap into a tum shape and secure with a small wooden skewer.

strInstructions:
Prepare all the spices, then grind or blend them in a chopper until smooth.
Add the grated coconut, mlanding / Chinese petai / leucaena seeds, tofu, and fish p (optional).
Mix well and adjust the seasoning to taste. Once the flavor is right, wrap the mixture in banana leaves.
Steam for 20–30 minutes until cooked.

strInstructions:
Mix all the spices and stir well.
Add the chicken liver and gizzard and tofu. Mix well, and don't forget to taste and adjust the seasoning.
Take a banana leaf, add the botok mixture, then fold it.
Steam for 30 minutes.

Combine the grated coconut, Chinese petai, Medan anchovies, ground ingredients, salt, and powdered stock. Mix thoroughly by hand until evenly combined.

strInstructions:
Steep the saffron in warm water for 15 minutes.
Grind all the spices until smooth.
Chop the beef in a food processor, then add the ground spices, kaffir lime leaves, egg, and coconut milk. Process until evenly combined.
Add the Herati Saffron water and mix well.
Prepare banana leaves, place an Indonesian bay leaf on each, add 2 tbsp of the meat mixture and a bird's eye chili. Wrap tightly.

Serve the botok with saffron sauce.

Prepare the ingredients. Wash the bananas thoroughly and drain. Marinate the shrimp with lime juice and salt.
Prepare a large bowl. Add the shrimp, grated coconut, white tofu, cooking oil, ground spices, sliced spices, and seasoning powder. Mix everything until evenly combined. Wrap the pepes in banana leaves and secure with toothpicks. Bake in an oven at 150°C for 60 minutes using both top and bottom heat. Once cooked, remove from the oven.
Place some of the pepes on a plate.
Delicious shrimp and tofu pepes are ready to enjoy with all your heart 🌟✨🌞
This was my first time making shrimp and tofu pepes/botok because my mother used to prefer mackerel pepes (old photo from 2020). Both are delicious, depending on your taste. If you want to make mackerel pepes, the ingredients and method are the same. However, steam the fish first, then grill it on a nonstick pan or over a flame. In my opinion, baking in the oven is more practical. Adjust to your preference. Enjoy trying it 💖

Remove the heads and bones from the anchovies, wash them, and set aside.
Grind the ground spices until smooth.
Mix the spices with the young coconut and melinjo (Chinese petai).

Combine the tofu, tempeh, grated coconut, and ground spices in a medium bowl. Mix evenly and taste for seasoning.
Wrap the botok mixture in the prepared banana leaves. Secure with toothpicks or small pieces of bamboo skewer. Repeat until finished.

Mash the tempeh, then mix it with the grated coconut, petai, and ground spices. Also add salt, stock powder, and granulated sugar. Mix well.
Prepare banana leaves, place an Indonesian bay leaf and 1 1/2 tbsp of the botok mixture on each. Wrap and secure with a small bamboo skewer. Repeat until all the mixture is used.
Steam for 30 minutes until the botok is cooked. Remove and drain.
Serve the tempeh botok warm. Enjoy!

Cut the tofu and tempeh.
Mash the tempeh and tofu.
In a separate container, mix the grated coconut with the ground spices. Add salt to taste.
Mix the ground spices into the tempeh and tofu. Add the basil leaves and Indonesian bay leaves.
Wrap in banana leaves. (Psst, some are long-shaped because I ran out of toothpicks 😁)
Finally, steam until cooked, about 20 minutes.

Cut the tofu and tempeh into cubes, along with the softened cow skin.
Grind or blend the spices, then sauté them.
Once the spices are cooked, add water (about 1 liter), then add salt, sugar, and stock powder.
Add the tempeh, tofu, and cow skin, then cook for 10 minutes or until the liquid has reduced.
Chop the chilies and Ale, then add them to the dish along with the grated coconut.
Cook briefly until the tomatoes and chilies soften slightly. Taste and adjust the seasoning, then serve.

Cut the tempeh into cubes and steam for 10 minutes.
Grind the spices, except for the Indonesian bay leaves.
Mix the spices with the grated coconut, then combine with all the ingredients.
Prepare banana leaves, cut them to a size suitable for wrapping the botok, and warm them over a stove flame. Place an Indonesian bay leaf, some botok mixture, and one bird's eye chili on each leaf. Wrap and secure with a toothpick.
Steam for about 20 minutes, then serve.

Steam the chopped tempeh and coconut for 10 minutes to remove their raw aroma. After steaming, transfer them to a bowl and let cool.
Sauté the ground spices until fragrant, then mix them with the coconut, Chinese petai, chilies, tempeh, and anchovies in the bowl. Mix well and check the seasoning.
Arrange on banana leaves: place an Indonesian bay leaf, galangal, and a bird's eye chili on each leaf, then add 1–2 tbsp of the botok mixture. Fold and secure with a toothpick. Repeat until all the mixture is used.
Steam for 20 minutes until fully cooked.

strInstructions:
Prepare all the ingredients. Place the grated coconut in a bowl and add the crushed tempeh. Set aside.
Grind the garlic, large red chilies, bird's eye chilies, spring onion, and tomato until smooth. Set aside.
In another bowl, clean the meat and slice it into small pieces, or according to your preference.
In another bowl, cut the banana blossom as desired and wash it thoroughly.
Once everything is ready, add it to the bowl containing the grated coconut and crushed tempeh. Add the seasonings and mix evenly. Adjust the taste. Once the flavor is right, wrap in banana leaves and steam until cooked.
Once cooked, serve and enjoy with warm rice.

Prepare the main ingredients. Bring water to a boil, then add the jackfruit. Boil until tender but not mushy, drain, and let cool. Squeeze out the water until dry, then finely chop.
Cut the long beans into index-finger-length pieces and boil until moderately tender. Set aside. Finely chop the boiled jackfruit; squeeze it dry first so it does not become wet and mushy. Set aside. Char the coconut with the inner skin on, then grate it. Set aside.
Prepare the complete spice mix. 🖍️ Grind the candlenuts, pepper, coriander, and nutmeg until smooth. 🖍️ Coarsely chop the remaining spices: shallots, garlic, red bird's eye chilies, aromatic ginger, galangal, turmeric, and ginger. Add the chopped spices to the ground mixture and grind briefly to release their aroma.
Add ground coriander and ground pepper, then mix well. Heat a generous amount of oil and sauté the complete spice mixture.
Add Indonesian bay leaves and sauté until fragrant. Add salt and sugar, taste, and set aside. The complete set is shown in slide 3.
Now prepare the sambal embe. Prepare the ingredients. 🖍️ Roast the shrimp paste until fragrant. Fry the remaining ingredients separately: 🖍️ shallots for fried shallots; 🖍️ garlic for fried garlic; 🖍️ red chilies and bird's eye chilies together until fried. Combine everything except the juice of the limo lime, and mash by hand (make sure your hands are clean). Drizzle with the limo lime juice.
To serve, combine all the ingredients (boiled vegetables, sambal embe, coconut, and the complete spice mix). Mash together by hand with clean hands. This is characteristic of Balinese lawar preparation, which is traditionally mixed by hand rather than with a spoon, so using your hands is essential for the best result ☺️ Balinese vegetable lawar is ready to enjoy with rice cooked with sweet potato, shredded chicken, and torch ginger sambal—a complete Balinese meal.
strIngredient1: Young jackfruit, boiled until moderately tender

strInstructions:
Prepare the main and other ingredients.
Peel the papaya and remove the seeds. Cut it into pieces and boil in water with a little salt to help it soften quickly.
Once cooked, drain. Let it cool until warm, then cut into pieces as desired. Set aside.
Soak the grated coconut in hot water first, then squeeze out the coconut milk. Set aside.
Grind all the ingredients for the ground spice paste and sauté until cooked and fragrant. Also fry all the thinly sliced ingredients for the embe seasoning. Set aside.
Prepare the duck spice mixture and grind all the ingredients. Set aside.
Prepare the uyah sere seasoning by combining everything and setting it aside.
Once all the ingredients are ready, combine all the seasonings and the grated coconut, then mix well. Adjust the quantities to your taste. The important thing is that the flavor is right. Finally, drizzle with lime juice as needed.
Mix the lawar seasoning evenly with the boiled papaya. Ready to serve.
strIngredient4: Small kaffir lime leaf, thinly sliced

strInstructions:
Prepare the ingredients and wash them thoroughly. To make the base sune cekuh, cut the spices into small pieces to make them easier to grind. Grind the spices, then sauté until cooked. Set aside.
To make sambal embe, slice the shallots, garlic, and chilies. Sauté until cooked.
To make uyah sere, crush the shrimp paste and salt together by hand. Heat a pan, turn off the heat, then dry-roast the shrimp paste and salt. Set aside.
Char the coconut, scrape off the charred outer layer, leaving a little charred area for color and smoky aroma. Grate the coconut and set aside.
Clean the anchovies and soak them in warm water. Drain, then fry until cooked. Drain and set aside.
To assemble, prepare the grated coconut and coarsely pound the anchovies. Take some of the seasoning and mix it with the pounded anchovies. Add sambal embe and mix well. Sprinkle with uyah sere as needed and mix until evenly combined. Taste and add lime juice. Serve 💛
strIngredient22: Sesuai selera jeruk nipis / jeruk limau

strInstructions:
Say a prayer and wash your hands. Char the coconut after removing its inner skin until browned to give it a smoky taste (mine got too charred, so I scraped some off 😅). Coarsely grate it vertically and set aside. Briefly fry the "fish" until browned, then set aside.
Next, make the base suna cekuh. Blend all the ingredients until smooth, then sauté until fully cooked. Set aside.
Make sambal embe: sauté the garlic until softened and fragrant, add the bird's eye chilies and cook until mostly cooked, then add the fried shallots and mix well. Set aside.
Finally, make the uyah sere seasoning. Rub the ingredients together until combined, then sauté until cooked. Set aside.
To serve, pound or finely chop the "fish". Combine the fish, coconut, base suna cekuh, sambal embe, and uyah sere in a bowl, then mix well.
strIngredient1: Grated coconut that has been charred
strIngredient9: Oil + water for blending and sautéing
strIngredient10: Sambal embe ingredients without shrimp paste + salt

strInstructions:
Wash the vegetables thoroughly and drain. Boil the vegetables, then drain and set aside.
Sauté the ground spices until fragrant, then take half out. Leave the other half in the pan and mix it with the grated coconut. Cook until golden. Remove and set aside.
Cook the remaining half of the spice mixture with the vegetables until evenly combined, then add the seasoned coconut. Add salt, sugar, and mushroom stock powder. Mix well and taste.
Once the flavor is right, remove from the heat and serve.

Prepare water in a pot, add a pinch of granulated sugar and salt, and stir well. Boil the long beans in the mixture until half-cooked to help retain their bright color. Drain, cut into short pieces, and set aside in a bowl.
Heat a little oil and fry the shallots until crispy. Set aside. You can also use ready-made fried shallots.
Heat oil in a nonstick pan and fry the sliced bird's eye chilies until partly dry. Meanwhile, combine the shrimp paste and salt in a small bowl, then mash until evenly mixed and no lumps remain. Add this mixture to the pan and fry briefly. Transfer it to the bowl containing the boiled long beans.
Add the fried shallots and mix well. Add the calamansi juice and stir until thoroughly combined. Taste and adjust the seasoning. Serve with scrambled eggs and warm rice. Enjoy 😊
strIngredient4: Small packet of ready-to-use shrimp paste
strIngredient7: A pinch of granulated sugar and salt

strMeal: Lawar Sayuran Khas Bali (Kacang Panjang + Gori)
strInstructions:
Toast the grated coconut until fragrant and slightly browned to help it keep longer.
Prepare the other ingredients: ground spices, briefly boiled long beans, and boiled young jackfruit that has been shredded.
Sauté the ground spices, salt, Masako seasoning, granulated sugar, kaffir lime leaves, and Indonesian bay leaves until fragrant and cooked through. Adjust the seasoning, then turn off the heat.
Combine all the ingredients. Mix thoroughly with hands covered in plastic gloves. Serve.
strIngredient1: Long beans, wash thoroughly, cut into small pieces, and boil
strIngredient2: Young jackfruit, boil until tender and shred
strIngredient4: Kaffir lime leaves, remove the central veins
strIngredient7: Packet/9 g Masako or stock powder

strMeal: Lawar Ayam Kacang Panjang Khas Bali
strInstructions:
Toast the minced chicken and skin until cooked, but do not let them dry out. If liquid comes out, you can discard it first. A nonstick pan works best to prevent sticking. Remove and set aside. After toasting, mince the skin as well.
Cut the long beans into small pieces and boil until cooked but still crunchy, about three-quarters done. Remove and drain.
Toast the grated coconut until almost dry. Set aside. The original recipe uses an ungrated coconut that is roasted and then scraped to remove the blackened parts. Roasting the coconut first gives it a distinctive aroma.
Prepare all the ingredients and seasonings, placing each in a separate container. Also prepare a large bowl for mixing.
In the large bowl, combine the chicken, minced skin, embe seasoning, base genep spice paste, ground coriander, ground nutmeg, black pepper, and salt. Mix and press together by hand. Wear plastic gloves to prevent irritation from the chilies.
Add the long beans and grated coconut. Mix well again. Finally, add both types of fried onions, sliced kaffir lime leaves, and a squeeze of calamansi. Mix well and adjust the seasoning. Serve.
strIngredient7: See here: 170. chicken and jackfruit lawar
strIngredient11: Bird's eye chili seeds, to taste, sliced and fried
strIngredient19: Jeruk limau , belah, utk kucuran terakhir

strMeal: Lawar Gerang (Ikan Teri) Kacang Panjang Khas Bali
strInstructions:
Prepare all the ingredients and seasonings.
Gently squeeze the fried anchovies, but do not crush them.
Combine the anchovies, salt, palm sugar, chilies, and shrimp paste. Mix and press together by hand, remembering to wear plastic gloves. Add the shallots, garlic, and kaffir lime leaves, then briefly press them together.
Finally, add the long beans and coconut. Mix well and taste. If the seasoning is right, squeeze calamansi juice over the mixture and stir well.
Serve with warm rice.

Clean and wash the long beans thoroughly. Bring water to a boil, then cook the long beans until tender but not mushy. Remove and drain. Once slightly cooled, cut into small pieces and set aside.
Wash the shallots and bird's eye chilies, then slice thinly. Mash the roasted shrimp paste with the salt until evenly combined and no lumps remain. Cover your hand with plastic or wear plastic gloves.
Fry the shallots until golden brown, then remove and drain. Next, fry the chilies until partly dry and add the shrimp paste. Mix well and remove from the heat.
Place the sliced boiled long beans in a bowl with the fried shallots and chilies. Mix well while gently pressing the ingredients together. Use plastic to cover your hands so the chilies do not irritate your skin.
Adjust the seasoning, then add lemon lemo juice and mix well. Sprinkle a little fried shallot on top. Serve 🤩

Boil the long beans, remove, and rinse with cold water. Drain. Toast the grated coconut until slightly browned. I did not grate it myself, so I toasted it to help it keep longer.
Grill or fry the tempeh until browned.
Combine the long beans, tempeh, and base genep spice paste. Mix well, then add the grated coconut and mix again. Sprinkle with toasted peanuts. Enjoy 😋 (Note: serve with warm rice, embe/onion sambal, and crackers.)
strIngredient1: Long beans, cut into small pieces

strMeal: Nasi Campur Bali (Ayam Sisit, Lawar Sayuran, Tempe Sambal Matah)
strInstructions:
BALI BASIC SPICE PASTE (base gede meulig): Blend or process all ingredients until smooth. Heat 150 ml cooking oil and sauté the ground paste until cooked and fragrant. Set aside.
SAUTÉED CHILI: Blend all ingredients, but do not make the mixture too smooth. Heat 50 ml cooking oil and sauté until cooked and fragrant. Set aside.
SHREDDED CHICKEN: In a pan, combine the sautéed Bali basic spice paste and sautéed chili. Sauté briefly with 5 tbsp cooking oil, kaffir lime leaves, and Indonesian bay leaves until fragrant, then add the shredded chicken. Mix well.
Pour in the water. Add salt, Masako seasoning, and granulated sugar. Cook until the liquid has reduced and the seasoning has absorbed into the chicken. Adjust the taste and serve.
VEGETABLE LAWAR: Heat 3 tbsp cooking oil. Sauté the Bali basic spice paste with salt, Masako seasoning, granulated sugar, kaffir lime leaves, and Indonesian bay leaves until fragrant. Prepare the toasted coconut and boiled vegetables.
Combine all ingredients and mix evenly with hands covered in plastic. Adjust the seasoning and serve.
TEMPEH WITH SAMBAL MATAH: Combine the chilies, shallots, salt, Masako seasoning, granulated sugar, shrimp paste, lemongrass, and kaffir lime leaves, then gently squeeze together by hand. Pour in hot oil, mix well, and add the juice of key lime or sambal lime.
Coarsely chop or mash the tempeh. Transfer it to a large bowl, pour the sambal matah over it, and mix well with hands protected by plastic. Serve.
Serve the rice with the side dishes.
strIngredient3: Ingredients for sautéed Bali basic spice paste

strIngredient33: Nangka muda , rebus hingga matang dan suwir
strIngredient34: Kelapa parut , sangrai hingga harum dan kecoklatan
strIngredient35: Penuh bumbu dasar bali tumis siap pakai

strInstructions:
Blend the ingredients for the spice paste until smooth, then sauté until fragrant.
In a bowl, combine the spice paste, jackfruit, long beans, chicken, half of the fried shallots, fried garlic, shrimp paste, chilies, salt, sugar, stock powder, and lime juice. Mix well and taste as you go.
Serve with the remaining fried shallots sprinkled on top.
strIngredient1: Young jackfruit, coarsely chopped and boiled
strIngredient2: Long bean stalks, cut into pieces and boiled
strIngredient7: Red bird's eye chilies, sliced and fried

strInstructions:
Wash the papaya thoroughly and boil it in water with a little salt. Soak the grated coconut in hot water, then squeeze or drain it.
Fry the sliced aromatics, including both types of onions. Toast the shrimp paste and sliced chilies until dry.
Sauté the ground spice paste, then mix it evenly with the grated coconut.
Combine the seasoned coconut with the boiled papaya, then add fried onions, sliced chilies, and shrimp paste. Add sliced limo lime and serve.
Serve as a side dish with mixed rice or as a dish on its own.
strIngredient13: A pinch of ground pepper and ground coriander
strIngredient14: Indonesian bay leaves, for adding to the pot

strInstructions:
Prepare and wash all the ingredients. Combine all the spice paste ingredients.
Blend until smooth. Pour the ground paste over the grated coconut. Add the other seasonings. Fry the anchovies after rinsing them.
Mix well, then add the anchovies and mix again.
Steam for 30 minutes until cooked.
Boil all the vegetables.
Combine the boiled vegetables with the coconut and anchovy mixture. Mix well.
Serve with hot rice.

strMeal: Lawar Bali Simpel (Kacang Panjang Sambal Sere Mbe)
strInstructions:
Cut the long beans into short pieces. Boil briefly so they remain fresh, then remove and immediately place them in cold water. Leave for a few moments and drain.
Fry the shallots in a little oil until almost dry. Add the chilies, then the shrimp paste. Stir to break up the shrimp paste. Cook briefly until fragrant, then turn off the heat.
Place the long beans in a bowl. Mix with the fried shallots, chilies, and shrimp paste. Taste and add salt if needed. Squeeze in the lemon lemo juice. Serve with warm rice.

strMeal: Rice Bowl Ayam Popcorn Sambal Iris Tumis Dan Lawar Bali Simpel
strInstructions:
Cut the chicken breast into small pieces, then mix with chicken stock powder and ground pepper. Marinate for 1 hour.
Combine the seasoning flour, medium-protein wheat flour, and sifted baking soda. Mix well. Prepare the dipping liquid by mixing 500 ml water with 2 tbsp of the dry flour mixture.
Add the marinated chicken and press so the flour sticks. Dip it into the liquid mixture.
Coat the chicken again with the dry flour mixture. Set aside.
Deep-fry the chicken in hot oil until golden brown. Remove and drain.
Now prepare the Balinese lawar. Boil the long beans in boiling water for 5 minutes, then remove and soak in cold water.
Pound the shrimp paste and fine salt together, then set aside. Heat oil and sauté the red bird's eye chilies until partly dry. Add the shrimp paste and fine salt. Add the fried shallots, mix well, and turn off the heat.
Add the long beans cut into small pieces and mix well.
Prepare the ingredients for the sautéed sliced sambal.
Heat oil and sauté the shallots and red bird's eye chilies until fragrant. Add the lemongrass and tomato. Season with fish sauce, fine salt, and granulated sugar. Cook until the sambal is done and fragrant. Remove from the heat.
Beat the eggs with chicken stock powder, then scramble them.
Arrange all the cooked components. Put the rice in a bowl.
Arrange the side dishes on top and serve. Delicious crispy popcorn chicken with spicy sautéed sliced sambal, refreshing Balinese lawar, and savory scrambled eggs.
strIngredient11: Red bird's eye chilies, thinly sliced

strInstructions:
Prepare the ground spice paste, then sauté until fragrant.
Add the chicken pieces and mix well.
Add the sliced kaffir lime leaves and mix again.
Pour in the coconut water and stir. Cover the pot and cook until the chicken is half-cooked, then add the grated coconut and mix well.
Add the lime juice, salt, sugar, and mushroom stock powder. Cook until the coconut is dry.
Serve.
strIngredient9: Stalks of lemongrass, use the white parts

strInstructions:
🍗Blend the base genep spices until smooth. Sauté the ground paste until thoroughly cooked and fragrant. Mix well.
Add the minced chicken to the fragrant spice paste and stir until the chicken is cooked. Set aside.
🌶Make the sere mbe sambal. Finely chop the garlic, shallots, and chilies. Heat a pan and fry the garlic until golden, then set aside.
Next, fry the shallots until golden and set aside. Reduce the amount of oil, then fry the chilies until somewhat dry. Turn off the heat, add the shrimp paste, and stir well. Add sugar and salt, then combine with both types of fried onions. Mix well. Leave in the pan or transfer to another container.
🥒Bring water to a boil in a pot, add the green beans, and turn off the heat. Drain the beans and set aside.
To finish, combine the three components: chicken with base genep seasoning, sere mbe sambal, and green beans.
Mix until evenly combined, then squeeze limo lime juice over the mixture.
The green bean lawar is ready to serve.
Enjoy!
strIngredient1: Green beans, cut into small pieces

strInstructions:
Prepare the ingredients.
Sauté the ground spice paste until fragrant. Add the aromatic seasonings and sauté until softened.
Add a little water. Add the chicken and cook until its color changes. Season with salt, mushroom stock powder, and Rose Brand granulated sugar. Mix well and cook until done.
Add the juice of Chinese lemon. Add the sliced green tomatoes, basil leaves, and scallions.
The chicken woku is ready to serve. Enjoy!

Wash the chicken thoroughly, coat it with lime juice, and leave for 10 minutes. Wash it again until clean. Prepare the required ingredients and pick the basil leaves.
Prepare the ingredients for the spice paste. Grind them with a mortar and pestle or blend them.
Heat a pan. Sauté the ground spice paste with lemongrass, kaffir lime leaves, Indonesian bay leaves, and galangal until fragrant and thoroughly cooked.
Once the sautéed spices are fragrant, add the water, chicken, scallions, pandan leaves, turmeric leaves, and basil leaves. (Sorry the photo is blurry 🤭🙏)
Cook until the chicken and leaves are done, then add the chopped tomato and whole bird's eye chilies. Cook until the liquid has reduced slightly and the seasoning has penetrated the chicken. The basil chicken woku is ready to serve.
strIngredient16: Cabe rawit merah dan hijau utuh

strInstructions:
Fry the tofu until a skin forms.
Heat oil and sauté the ground spice paste with lemongrass and kaffir lime leaves until fragrant. Add 1 cup of water.
Add the chicken, sugar, and salt. Cook until the chicken changes color, then add the tofu and sliced bilimbi. Cook until the flavors are absorbed.
Add the basil leaves, stir, and turn off the heat. Serve warm.

Blend all the spice paste ingredients with enough oil until smooth.
Sauté the ground spice paste and aromatic seasonings until fragrant and cooked through.
Add the chicken and mix well. Add water and season with sugar and salt. Cook until the chicken is done and the seasoning has absorbed.
Finally, add the basil leaves, stir briefly, adjust the seasoning, remove from the heat, and serve.

Wash the chicken thoroughly and boil it in 800 ml water for 10 minutes, counting from when the water begins to boil. Discard the water and wash the chicken again.
Sauté the ground spice paste and aromatic seasonings until cooked through, then add the chicken and water. Cook until boiling.
Add the seasonings, tomatoes, and scallions. Adjust the flavor to taste and cook until the liquid boils again, reduces slightly, and the chicken is tender and fully cooked.
Add the basil leaves and stir until evenly combined.

Cut the chicken as desired and coat it with lime juice. Set aside.
Grind the shallots, garlic, and candlenuts.
Sauté the ground spices with bay leaves, lemongrass, and kaffir lime leaves until fragrant.
Rinse the chicken and mix it with the sautéed spices.
When half-cooked, add a little water.
Once the liquid has reduced somewhat, add salt and basil. Adjust the seasoning.

Cut the chicken into pieces and marinate with lemon juice for 15 minutes. Grind the spices.
Sauté the ground spices until fragrant, add the chicken and stir until its color changes. Add the sliced kaffir lime leaves, bruised lemongrass, pandan leaves, mushroom stock, sugar, and salt. Add 1300 liters of water.
Cook until the liquid has reduced. Taste again; add anything needed.

Sauté the ground spices, lemongrass, pandan leaves, and kaffir lime leaves until fragrant.
Add the chicken and stir until its color changes.
Add water, tomato, salt, sugar, and mushroom stock. Simmer covered over low heat for 15 minutes.
Add the oyster mushrooms and cook until wilted, about 5 minutes.
Turn off the heat, take out the child's portion, and sprinkle with basil and scallions.
For adults, add the bird's eye chilies, remaining basil, and scallions; cook briefly, about 1 minute.

Wash the chicken thoroughly, add a little salt and lime juice, and let sit for 3–5 minutes. Rinse again.
Sauté the washed chicken until all the liquid released from it has evaporated. You can save the liquid for another dish because it is pure chicken stock.
Prepare the whole aromatics and ground spices. Blend the ground spices.
Sauté the ground spices in cooking oil until fragrant, then add lemongrass, bay leaves, and kaffir lime leaves.
Add the chicken and stir gently. Add sugar, salt, seasoning, and pepper, then add basil and tomato.
Stir until evenly combined and check the taste. Once the savory and salty flavor is right, turn off the stove. The basil chicken woku is ready to serve.

Wash the chicken thoroughly, add lime juice, and let sit for 15 minutes. Rinse again and set aside. Prepare the spices and other ingredients.
Heat cooking oil and sauté the ground spices until fragrant. Add lemongrass, galangal, kaffir lime leaves, bay leaves, pandan leaves, and turmeric leaves.
Add the chicken, powdered stock, Sasa seasoning, and sugar, then stir well and add enough water.
Cook until the liquid has reduced slightly and the spices have thickened. Add sliced scallions and basil. Taste; if well-seasoned, remove from the heat and serve. Enjoy the chicken woku 👍

strMeal: 411. Ayam Woku Khas Minahasa, Sulawesi Utara
strInstructions:
Prepare the ingredients. Slice the tomato and leek, then set aside.
Blend the spices and pour them into a pan. Wait until the liquid has reduced. Add all the aromatic seasonings and stir until fragrant.
Add the chicken and mix until evenly coated with the spices. Add water and wait until it reduces, then add the tomato and leek. Add salt and stock seasoning. When the chicken is cooked, add the basil and stir until wilted.

Wash the chicken thoroughly, place it in a nonstick pan, and cook until all the liquid comes out and evaporates. Turn off the heat and set aside.
Heat about 100 ml of cooking oil. Add the ground spices and accompanying aromatics; cook until fragrant and the oil separates.
Add the chicken and water, then season with salt, pepper, sugar, and powdered stock. Cook until the liquid reduces.
Once the liquid has reduced, add basil, tomato, and scallions. Stir well and turn off the heat.

Prepare the chicken, wash thoroughly, and drizzle with lime juice to remove any unpleasant smell.
Finely chop the shallots, garlic, bird’s eye chilies, red chilies, and candlenuts in a chopper.
Fry the chicken that has been coated with lime juice until half-cooked.
Sauté the ground spices in the oil used to fry the chicken until fragrant so they do not smell raw.
Once fragrant, add galangal, lemongrass, and kaffir lime leaves, then add the chicken.
Sauté briefly, add water as desired, and add seasoning to taste. Cook until the chicken is completely cooked.
Once the chicken is cooked, add sliced tomato and basil.
The chicken woku is ready to serve.

Wash the chicken thoroughly, add lime juice, and let sit for a while. Rinse again with clean water and drain.
Heat cooking oil and sauté the ground spices, lemongrass, kaffir lime leaves, turmeric leaves, and pandan leaves until fragrant.
Add the chicken and salt; cook until the chicken changes color. Add granulated sugar for extra flavor.
Once the chicken changes color, add water and cook covered so the chicken softens faster and absorbs the spices. Occasionally uncover and stir so it cooks evenly. Remember to add mushroom stock. Stir well and cook until tender.
Once the chicken is tender and the sauce has reduced, add tomato, scallions, whole bird’s eye chilies, and basil. Stir well, adjust the seasoning, cook briefly, and turn off the heat. Ready to serve.
strIngredient3: Lemongrass, bruised and tied in a knot
strIngredient6: Kaffir lime leaves, central veins removed
strIngredient10: Kecil basil, pick leaves and wash thoroughly

strMeal: Ayam Woku/ Ayam Rica Rica Kemangi
strInstructions:
Marinate the chicken and let it sit for about 10 minutes, then fry until half-cooked and slightly browned.
Sauté the ground spices, then add the aromatics (bruised lemongrass, bay leaves, and kaffir lime leaves). Cook until fragrant and the spices are fully cooked; the oil should separate and the spices should look slightly dry.
Add the half-fried chicken and stir so it is evenly coated. Add a little water, which can be taken from the leftover ground-spice mixture.
Add sliced green chilies and leek. Wait until the liquid has reduced somewhat, then add basil and stir briefly. Lower the heat. Note: once the basil is added, do not cook it for too long so its distinctive aroma remains.
Adjust the seasoning. If it tastes right, serve.
strIngredient13: Bird’s eye chilies mixed with curly and large red chilies

strMeal: Simply Food Series : Ayam Woku Satset
strInstructions:
Cut the chicken into 7–8 pieces, then clean it.
Heat the oil and sauté the ground spices, lemongrass, scallions, and bay leaves until cooked and fragrant and the oil comes out.
Add the chicken and stir until evenly coated and its color changes.
Pour in water and add salt, sugar, and powdered stock. Cover the pan and cook over medium heat until the chicken is tender and the spices have infused, and the liquid has reduced.
Once cooked and the sauce has thickened, add basil and scallions. Stir briefly until wilted, then turn off the heat.
The chicken woku is ready to serve.

Marinate the Spanish mackerel with salt and pepper, mix well, and set aside.
Slice the white part of the lemongrass and bruise the green stalk. Remove the central veins from the kaffir lime leaves, then finely slice them.
Heat oil, add the lemongrass stalk, pandan leaves, turmeric leaves, and kaffir lime leaves, and sauté until fragrant.
Add the ground spices and sauté until fragrant, then add the Spanish mackerel and powdered stock; sauté briefly. Add water and cook until the fish is half-cooked.
Add red tomato and scallions, stir well, and cook until the fish is done. Taste and adjust the seasoning.
Turn off the heat and add basil and lime juice; stir well.
The Spanish mackerel woku is ready to serve.

Sauté the ground spices, kaffir lime leaves, bay leaves, pandan leaves, turmeric leaves, galangal, and lemongrass until cooked.
Add the fish and sauté briefly until cooked, then add water, tofu, and green bird’s eye chilies.
Adjust the seasoning and cook until the spices have infused. Add tomato, cook briefly, and serve warm sprinkled with fried shallots.
strIngredient2: Tofu, cut in half and fry until browned, drain and set aside
strIngredient7: Pandan leaves, cut into 4 pieces and tied
strIngredient11: Tomato, halved then cut into pieces

strMeal: 40. Ikan Kakap Merah Woku Kuah Pedas Manis
strInstructions:
Clean and wash the fish, then marinate it with citrus juice.
Grind all the spices, such as garlic, turmeric, candlenuts, and others, then set aside.
Heat oil and sauté the ground spices with the aromatics, such as bruised lemongrass and galangal. Cook until fragrant. Add the fish and stir until evenly coated with the spices and its color changes.
Add water and wait until it boils and reduces, then add citrus juice, tamarind water, sugar, salt, Ladaku seasoning, basil, and diagonally sliced leek.
Adjust the seasoning, then set aside.

Prepare the required ingredients and clean the fish with lemon to remove the fishy smell.
Prepare all the seasonings and pound the ingredients for the ground spice paste.
Sauté the ground spices, add ground chili, and cook until fragrant and fully cooked. Add the cleaned fish. Add water and cook until the fish is done and the liquid has reduced. Add basil and sliced scallions, stir, and turn off the heat. Remember to adjust the seasoning.
The Spanish mackerel woku is ready to serve. It is spicy and delicious, with a wonderful fragrant aroma of spices...👍
strIngredient2: Lemongrass, tied in a knot and bruised
strIngredient3: Pandan leaves, tied in a knot
strIngredient9: Ready-to-use ground chili, ready-to-use ground chili ❤

strInstructions:
Wash the mackerel thoroughly, cut each fish into 2 pieces, add salt and lime juice, and let sit for 15 minutes. Prepare all the ingredients.
Sauté the ground spices with the leafy aromatics until wilted and fragrant, except for the basil, which is added at the end.
Add water and wait until it boils, then add the mackerel, salt, sugar, and seasoning. Stir well and add tamarind.
When the liquid has reduced and soaked into the fish, add sliced tomato and basil. Check the seasoning; once cooked, it is ready to serve.

Prepare the ingredients.
Coat the barracuda with lime juice and salt and let sit for 10–15 minutes. Rinse lightly, then fry until cooked but not dry. Remove and set aside.
Grind the spices with a mortar and pestle or blender.
Sauté the ground spices until fragrant and cooked. Add lemongrass, kaffir lime leaves, and pandan leaves.
Add water and bring to a boil, then add tomato.
Add the barracuda and cook over medium heat for about 8–12 minutes; do not cook too long or it will become tough.
Add salt, sugar, and pepper. Add scallions and basil at the end, adjust the seasoning, and cook until the fish is done and the spices have infused.
Remove and serve warm.

Fry the marinated fish until half-cooked.
Heat oil for sautéing the ground spices. Sauté until fragrant and cooked. Add the roughly prepared aromatics (lemongrass and kaffir lime leaves). Sauté until fragrant and wilted.
Once the spices are fragrant and cooked, add water to make the woku sauce. Once it boils, add the fried fish.
Finally, once everything has boiled, add tomato, whole large bird’s eye chilies, and basil. The fish woku is ready to serve.

Grind the garlic, ginger, turmeric, candlenuts, and large red chilies.
Sauté the shallots in oil until fragrant.
Add the ground spice paste and sauté until cooked and fragrant.
Add lemongrass and kaffir lime leaves, and stir well.
Add the lemuru fish heads and stir gently.
Pour in water, add salt and sugar, and cook until the fish is half-cooked.
Add tomato, bird’s eye chilies, and basil.
Cook until the fish is done and the spices have infused; adjust the seasoning.

Cut the fish into pieces and wash thoroughly. Briefly marinate with lime. Set aside.
Blend all the ingredients for the ground spice paste (the picture is only decorative).
Sauté the ground spices until fragrant, then add the whole aromatics.
Add the fish and stir briefly, then add water, salt, and stock seasoning.
Let it cook until the liquid has reduced and the spices are fully cooked, then add basil.
Adjust the seasoning and serve with your beloved family.
strIngredient7: A handful of red bird’s eye chilies

strInstructions:
Clean the fish thoroughly, then marinate with lime juice, pepper, and salt. Let sit for 15 minutes.
Heat oil and fry the fish until crispy.
Grind the seasoning ingredients and slice the ingredients for the sliced seasoning.
Heat 2 tbsp oil and sauté the ground spices, Indonesian bay leaves, lemongrass, kaffir lime leaves, and galangal until fragrant.
Add a little water, then add the fish, sliced seasoning, whole bird's eye chilies, sugar, salt, pepper, and powdered stock. Taste and adjust the seasoning.
Once the seasoning has infused into the fish, remove from heat. Serve warm for the best flavor.

Prepare all the ingredients. Clean the catfish thoroughly and coat it with lime juice.
Bruise the lemongrass. Cut the turmeric leaf into 5 cm pieces. Tear the kaffir lime leaves. Cut the leek into 1 cm pieces. Separate the basil leaves from their stems. Chop the ingredients for the ground seasoning and put them in a blender. Blend until smooth.
Sauté the ground seasoning until fragrant and partially cooked.
Add the lemongrass, turmeric leaves, and kaffir lime leaves. Stir well and cook briefly.
Add water and bring to a boil.
Add the fish and cook until almost done.
Add salt and mushroom stock. Cook until the fish is done.
Add the leek and basil leaves.
Stir well until the basil wilts.
The catfish woku is ready to serve.

Clean and wash the fish, then marinate it with a little salt and lime juice. Set aside.
Grind the ground seasoning. Prepare the additional ingredients.
Heat ROSE BRAND cooking oil in a pan. Sauté the ground seasoning, kaffir lime leaves, lemongrass, turmeric leaves, and pandan leaf until fragrant.
Add the fish and stir well. Add water and cover the pan. Cook until the fish is done.
Add salt, seasoning powder, and calamansi juice. Adjust the seasoning, remove from heat, and serve 😋
strIngredient10: Pandan leaf, tied in a knot

strInstructions:
Cut the fish into pieces, wash thoroughly, and coat with citrus juice.
Pound all the ground seasoning ingredients.
Slice the scallions and tomatoes, and pick the basil leaves.
Sauté the ground seasoning in enough oil, then add the aromatic ingredients such as pandan leaf, kaffir lime leaves, lemongrass, and turmeric leaf.
Once fragrant, add the tomatoes and stir.
Add the fish and stir. Add enough water, then season with salt, pepper, and seasoning powder.
Wait until the fish is cooked, then add the basil and cook briefly until evenly mixed.
Once the fish is cooked, it is ready to serve.
strIngredient9: Citrus for squeezing over the fish to remove its fishy smell
strIngredient10: (lemon for fish, as called in Manado)

strInstructions:
Marinate the skipjack tuna with enough salt, lime juice, and turmeric powder. Let sit for 20–30 minutes.
Heat enough cooking oil and sauté the shallots until fragrant. Add the pounded seasoning and sauté again until fragrant.
Add the skipjack tuna and cook for about 1–2 minutes over low heat so the seasoning can penetrate the fish (Note: turn the fish only once so both sides absorb the seasoning. Do not keep flipping it, or the fish may break apart).
Add enough water, sliced tomatoes, kaffir lime leaves, lemongrass, pandan leaf, some sliced scallions, and basil leaves. Cover the pan or pot and cook the fish until done.
Once the fish is cooked, add enough salt and flavor enhancer or mushroom stock. Adjust the seasoning. When it tastes right, add the remaining basil and sliced scallions. Stir well and cook until the leaves wilt. Finally, add calamansi juice. Turn off the heat and transfer the fish to a serving plate. The skipjack tuna woku is ready to serve.
strIngredient15: Tomatoes, sliced lengthwise into fairly thick pieces
strIngredient18: Daun jeruk purut , buang tangkai daunnya
strIngredient20: Kecil kemangi , ambil bagian daunnya saja
strIngredient21: Daun pandan ukuran kecil, diikat simpul
strIngredient22: Lemon chui, ambil air lemon nya saja

strInstructions:
Wash the skipjack tuna bones thoroughly and marinate with 1 tsp salt and lime juice. Set aside. Pound the ground seasoning.
Prepare the other ingredients.
Heat oil. Sauté the ground seasoning, pandan leaf, lemongrass, and kaffir lime leaves until fragrant and their color changes. Add the tomatoes and stir.
Add the fish bones and stir well. Add water. Cook until the water boils, stirring occasionally.
Add scallions, basil, salt, seasoning powder, and calamansi juice. Stir and cook briefly. Adjust the seasoning, remove from heat, and serve 😘
strIngredient12: Pandan leaf, cut in half and tied in a knot

strInstructions:
Prepare the fish by cleaning, gutting, cutting into pieces, and washing thoroughly. Squeeze lime juice over it, let sit for 10 minutes, then wash again.
Sauté the ground seasoning, adding Indonesian bay leaves, lemongrass, kaffir lime leaves, galangal, turmeric leaf, and pandan leaf. Sauté until fragrant and cooked. Add water, salt, sugar, and mushroom stock, then cook until the water boils.
Add the skipjack tuna and cook until the seasoning is absorbed and the liquid has reduced. Add basil leaves, scallions, and tomatoes, and cook briefly.
Remember to adjust the seasoning. Remove from heat and serve. Enjoy 🥰
strIngredient8: Medium turmeric leaf, tied in a knot

strMeal: Woku Ikan Kembung, Masakan Rumah Rasa Manado
strInstructions:
Clean the fish and remove the gills and innards. Cut it in half if you want to make 6 servings. Coat with lemon or lime juice and salt. Marinate for 10–15 minutes while preparing the other ingredients.
Grill or fry the fish until partially cooked (or cook it to your preferred doneness; you can also cook it directly in the sauce).
💡Tip for frying fish without splattering: Sprinkle a little flour into the oil while frying, as the flour absorbs moisture that would otherwise cause the hot oil to splatter.
Coarsely grind or blend the ground seasoning, then sauté it with the aromatic ingredients until cooked.
Pour in the water, salt, and seasoning powder. Stir well and bring to a boil. Add the fish and stir carefully. Cook until the liquid has reduced by half.
Just before turning off the heat, add the basil, stir briefly, then turn off the stove.
Serve 🥰

Bring the water to a boil, then add the rice, corn, pumpkin, Indonesian bay leaves, and lemongrass.
Boil until the water has reduced. Once reduced, add water spinach, basil, sugar, salt, pepper, and mushroom stock.
Once cooked, serve with fried anchovies or salted fish and roa chili sauce.

Wash all the main ingredients and vegetables, then cut them into pieces as desired.
Bring water to a boil, then add the rice, corn, sweet potato, pumpkin, and all the aromatic seasonings.
Check the pumpkin and mash it with a fork. Once the mixture boils and becomes porridge, set aside.
Next, prepare the shrimp paste sambal.
Then heat oil and add the sliced onions.
Add the prepared porridge. Stir and add a little water.
Once it boils, add the water spinach, spinach, and finally the basil. Season with pepper, salt, and seasoning powder.
Serve with the accompaniments.
strIngredient31: Pisang goreng sepatu ( pisang kepok crispy)

strInstructions:
Sauté the garlic, shallots, pepper, and scallions until fragrant.
Add the rice, pumpkin, corn, potatoes, lemongrass, and water. Cook in a rice cooker until the vegetables are tender.
Add powdered stock and the sautéed onion mixture. Stir well and wait until the liquid has reduced slightly.
Add the water spinach and stir well. Once wilted, add the basil and stir. The porridge is ready when its texture has thickened.
Top with salted fish or Medan anchovies and shrimp paste sambal.

Prepare the ingredients. Wash the salted fish thoroughly and drain. Prepare the vegetables: pick and wash the water spinach, then slice it; wash and slice the gedi leaves; wash and drain the basil.
Peel the taro (wear gloves to prevent itching), dice it, then soak it in salted water for 30 minutes. Peel and clean the cassava, then cut it into pieces. Peel and dice the pumpkin.
Wash the rice thoroughly. Bring water to a boil, add the cassava, and cook for 15 minutes. Then add the rice, taro, corn, and some of the pumpkin. Let it come to a boil.
Add the lemongrass stalks, kaffir lime leaves, and turmeric leaf. Stir occasionally so the rice does not stick to the pan. Slice the garlic and scallions, sauté until fragrant, then add them to the porridge.
Add salt and taste, then add all the vegetables. Finally, add the basil and turn off the heat.
Fry the tofu and salted fish.
Put the porridge in serving bowls and add the fried tofu, salted fish, fried shallots, and sambal. Ready to serve.

Prepare all the ingredients. Bring the water to a boil, add the rice and Indonesian bay leaves, and cook over medium heat, stirring until the rice expands.
Add the cassava and sweet potato pieces. Stir again until the roots are tender and the porridge thickens. Add salt and powdered stock. Finally, add the water spinach and corn.
Stir briefly so the water spinach remains crisp. Adjust the seasoning, then remove from heat and serve warm with salted fish and shrimp paste sambal.

HOW TO MAKE THE PORRIDGE: Put the rice and water in a pot. Add lemongrass, pandan leaves, kaffir lime leaves, turmeric leaf, and Indonesian bay leaves.
Add the pumpkin, cassava, and sliced corn. Cook until done.
Grind the garlic and pepper. Heat oil, sauté the ground seasoning, then pour it into the Tinutuan porridge.
Add powdered stock and stir well.
Add water spinach and basil leaves. Stir well and cook until the leaves wilt.
Adjust the seasoning.
HOW TO MAKE FRIED TOFU: Take 1 piece of tofu, cut it in half, season it with the spices and a little water, and marinate briefly.
Fry the tofu until cooked.
HOW TO MAKE SHRIMP PASTE SAMBAL: Prepare the sambal ingredients. Pound until smooth, then adjust the seasoning.
Wash the salted fish, add a little seasoning powder and rice flour.
Fry the salted fish until cooked.
Arrange all the components of Manado porridge / Tinutuan for serving.
strIngredient19: Sendok makan minyak goreng untuk menumis

strInstructions:
Prepare the rice, vegetables, and seasonings.
Sauté the ground seasoning until fragrant. Add the rice and water. Add the pumpkin pieces and corn. Stir until evenly mixed and cook for about 30 minutes until done.
Add the spinach, basil, and water spinach. Stir until combined and adjust the seasoning.
Manado porridge is ready to serve with fried fish and tomato sambal.

strMeal: Tinutuan (Bubur Manado) Dan Sambal Ikan Roa
strInstructions:
Bring water to a boil in a medium-sized pot, filling it halfway. Add the thoroughly washed rice.
Cook the rice, stirring occasionally. Add the lemongrass and kaffir lime leaves, then add the scraped corn kernels. Cook until boiling.
Stir occasionally, then add the peeled, washed, and chopped pumpkin and root vegetables.
Stir well until boiling, then add the thinly sliced shallots.
Stir gently over medium heat, then add the washed, coarsely chopped gedi leaves. Stir well.
Add the basil and stir again. Season with salt to taste.
Next, add the spinach, water spinach, and long beans. Stir until combined. Once cooked, turn off the heat.
For the sambal, prepare all the ingredients and blend the smoked roa fish until fine.
After blending, coarsely pound the sambal ingredients.
Once ready, add the roa fish and lime juice, then stir well.
Once everything is ready, serve on a plate while warm.

Boil the rice with water. Boil the red sweet potato or cassava until tender. When the rice is half-cooked, add the steamed pumpkin and corn. Stir until cooked.
Adjust the seasoning with salt and stock.
Once the porridge is cooked, add the water spinach, spinach, and basil leaves.
Serve with roa sambal and shredded skipjack tuna.
strIngredient5: Cassava: steam and cut as desired
strIngredient6: Pumpkin: steam and cut as desired
strIngredient7: Sweet corn: scrape off kernels and boil
strIngredient18: Sambal roa , masukkan ikan ke dalam tumisan sambal)

strInstructions:
Add the rice and aromatic seasonings (lemongrass and Indonesian bay leaves) to boiling water. Cook for a while until the rice becomes soft and porridge-like.
Then add salt, chicken oil, chicken stock, and the crushed garlic.
Add the corn kernels, sweet potato, and carrot. Boil until tender.
Once the carrot and sweet potato are soft, taste the porridge. Add salt if needed. When the seasoning is right, add the green vegetables (water spinach and katuk leaves).
Stir for one minute, then turn off the stove.
Simple Tinutuan porridge is ready to serve.
For the chicken oil recipe, please see the cooking gallery. Thank you. *_^

Clean the vegetables. Peel the pumpkin and cut it into small cubes. Prepare the water spinach and spinach.
Slice the shallots and garlic. Bruise the lemongrass. Tie the pandan leaf.
Heat a little oil and sauté the sliced onions, Indonesian bay leaves, and lemongrass until fragrant and slightly browned.
Put the washed rice and pandan leaf in a pot, add water and pumpkin, and simmer over medium-low heat.
Cook until the liquid reduces and the rice becomes partially cooked and porridge-like. Add powdered stock, salt, sugar, and pepper. Stir well and taste as you go.
Fry the salted fish until cooked and set aside.
Add the water spinach first and cook until it wilts slightly, then add the spinach. Stir well. Cook until the porridge is done and reaches your preferred thickness. Taste and adjust the seasoning, then turn off the heat.
Serve the porridge topped with fried shallots and salted fish.

Cook the rice and lemongrass in water until it becomes porridge.
Add the pumpkin and corn, stir well, then add salt, mushroom stock, and ground pepper.
Once the pumpkin is tender, add the water spinach.
Finally, add the basil, stir briefly, then remove from heat.
Serve topped with fried shallots, salted fish, and sambal.

Wash the rice and bring the water to a boil. Add the rice, bay leaves, salt, water, and lemongrass. Cook over low heat until it becomes porridge, stirring occasionally to prevent burning.
Add the chopped sweet potato, pumpkin, and corn. Cook again until everything is soft.
Add the water spinach and gedi leaves/spinach/Japanese papaya leaves. If using Japanese papaya leaves, boil them separately first. Discard the boiling water, then add the leaves to the porridge. Cook until the leaves are soft. Finally, add the basil leaves. Stir and turn off the heat.
Make the corn fritters. Remove the kernels from the cob. Grind the garlic and shallots.
Mix with all the other ingredients.
Heat the oil and fry the batter in thin, wide portions until crispy.
Serve tinutuan with corn fritters, fried salted fish, and shrimp paste sambal. ❤
strIngredient11: Gedi leaves / spinach / Japanese papaya leaves

strInstructions:
Cook the rice with enough water, lemongrass, and bay leaves until boiling. Add the diced pumpkin and stir. Add more water if it seems too thick.
Once the pumpkin starts to soften, add the corn kernels and stir evenly. Add the sautéed garlic along with its oil, season to taste, and adjust the seasoning. Finally, add the water spinach and basil, stir briefly, then turn off the heat.
Fry the salted fish until cooked, remove, and drain. Serve with sambal and salted fish.
Note: I used sambal that I already had in stock, so I didn't make it fresh.

Cut the vegetables into pieces. Dice the pumpkin, sweet potato, and cassava as well.
Bring the water to a boil. Add the pumpkin, cassava, and sweet potato pieces. The pumpkin should go in first and cook until it dissolves, followed by the cassava, then the sweet potato. Once everything is very soft, add the rice, followed by the corn kernels.
Boil everything for about 1 hour until it becomes porridge. Don't forget to add salt.
When ready to eat, add the basil, gedi leaves, spinach, water spinach, and sliced spring onions. Sprinkle with fried shallots (optional).
Serve with fried tofu, boiled eggs, and cakalang sambal, roa sambal, or bakasang sambal.

Prepare the ingredients.
Add the rice, water, bay leaves, and lemongrass. Turn on the stove and cook while stirring.
Once the rice grains split and the water reduces, add the pumpkin and sweet corn. Cook until done. Then add the spinach, basil, and spring onions. Finally, add salt and adjust the seasoning to taste.
The tinutuan porridge is ready to serve. If there is any porridge left in the pan, you can add hot water and reheat it. Enjoy!

strMeal: Bubur Manado Tinutuan Ala Mbak Nayla
strInstructions:
Peel and cut the pumpkin and potatoes into pieces.
Wash the rice and cook it with water until boiling, stirring occasionally. If there isn't enough water, add hot water. In a separate pan, sauté the ground spices until fragrant.
When the rice grains have started to split, add the sweet potato, pumpkin, corn, and pandan leaf. Cook until done. Add the seasoning mixture to the porridge and stir well. Add the spinach and basil; do not cook them for too long. Adjust the seasoning to taste. Remove from the heat and serve with anchovies, fried shallots, and sambal.
strIngredient4: Sweet potato; I didn't use it and replaced it with 100 g of potatoes
strIngredient18: Daun bawang iris halus secukupnya tambahan dari saya

strMeal: Bubur Tinutuan Dari Nasi Beras Merah
strInstructions:
Prepare all the ingredients. Remove the corn kernels from the cob, then dice the pumpkin and sweet potato. Set aside. Prepare the sautéing spices as well.
In a pot, sauté the shallots, garlic, bruised lemongrass, and bruised ginger until fragrant. Add the sweet potato, pumpkin, and corn, and sauté briefly. Add 500 ml of water and cook over medium-low heat until the sweet potato and pumpkin are soft.
Add the brown rice (regular white rice can also be used). Cook over low heat, stirring continuously until the rice turns into porridge. Season with mushroom stock powder, salt, and pepper. Adjust the seasoning to taste. You can also add more water if the porridge becomes too dry.
Once the rice has become porridge and the pumpkin and sweet potato are cooked, add the water spinach and stir. Cook until wilted, then add the basil and stir well. Turn off the heat. Serve with fried salted fish and sambal.

Blend all the ingredients until smooth.
Add the celery and mix well.
Heat the mold, fill it about three-quarters full, then cover and cook until half done.
Add shredded meat on top, then bake again until fully cooked.
Once cooked, remove and serve.

strMeal: 🥔 Kue Lumpur Kentang Kismis | Lembut Lumer Di Mulut ✨
strInstructions:
Prepare the ingredients.
Steam the potatoes until tender. Remove them and wait for the steam to dissipate before mashing. Don't mash them while they're still hot, or they may become watery. Add the mashed potatoes, coconut milk, sugar, egg, melted margarine, salt, and vanilla. Blend until very smooth. Pour into a bowl. Add the flour, sweetened condensed milk, and food coloring. Whisk until there are no lumps.
Preheat the mold for 2 minutes. Use the LOWEST heat. Lightly grease with margarine. Pour in the batter, filling only three-quarters of each mold because it will rise. Add the topping. Place a raisin in the center and cover immediately. (Line the lid with a cloth so steam doesn't drip onto the cakes.) Cook for 8–10 minutes. Don't keep opening the lid. The cakes are done when the tops have set and the bottoms are golden brown. Note: Insert a toothpick into the center at the 8-minute mark. If no batter sticks to it, they're done.
Wait 5 minutes until they cool slightly. Gently loosen them with a skewer. Note: Don't remove them from the mold while they're very hot. Wait until they're lukewarm. They may break if you force them out.

Prepare all the ingredients.
Bring the Rosebrand coconut milk and pandan leaf to a boil. Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly so the coconut milk doesn't split. Once it boils, turn off the heat and let it cool. Don't forget to melt the margarine as well.
Once the coconut milk has cooled, combine all the crust ingredients and mix well. Pour in the melted Rosebrand margarine and stir again, then strain the batter.
After straining, add the pandan paste. Prepare the mold and grease it with margarine, then pour in the crust batter. 💎 My tip: Fill two cavities at a time, then add the batter using a piping bag or spoon. If you fill all the cavities at once, the crust batter will become too thick at the bottom. 💎 Continue until all the molds are filled. Remove once cooked and let cool.
For the filling or custard, combine the Rosebrand coconut milk, Rosebrand cornstarch, sugar, salt, and vanilla in a saucepan. Mix well before turning on the heat. Cook until bubbling.
While still hot, immediately fill the crusts with the custard. Lapindo mud cakes are ready to serve.

Steam the sweet potatoes until tender. Peel and mash them.
Add the sugar, coconut milk, and eggs. Mix well. Add the flour and mix again.
Add the melted margarine and mix well. Preheat the kue lumpur mold and grease it with a little margarine. Pour in the batter until full. Add the topping and cook until done. Remove and serve.

Peel the potatoes, wash them thoroughly, cut them into pieces, and steam until cooked. Once cooked, mash the potatoes while still hot until smooth. Set aside and prepare the other ingredients.
Put the potatoes, sugar, eggs, cooking oil, sweetened condensed milk, coconut milk, and water into a blender. Blend until smooth.
Put the flour in a bowl and gradually pour in the blended potato mixture, alternating between adding flour and potato mixture.
Whisk until evenly combined. Take 1 tablespoon of batter and add purple food coloring to use later as a topping.
Preheat the mold or pan and lightly grease it with margarine. Pour in batter until three-quarters full, then use a fork to add the purple topping.
Cover the pan and cook until the cakes rise and the bottoms turn brown.
Remove and serve 👌

Boil the potatoes until tender, then remove and drain. Prepare the other kue lumpur ingredients. Boil the coconut milk, 120 ml mineral water, and 1 pandan leaf until boiling, then strain. Let the coconut milk mixture cool until warm.
Put the mashed potatoes and pumpkin purée in a bowl and mix well. Add the cassava sugar and eggs, then mix well.
Gradually add the flour, Himalayan salt, and coconut milk, alternating between them.
Finally, add the melted margarine and mix until thoroughly combined. Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and refrigerate overnight.
Put all the thick coconut milk mixture ingredients in a saucepan and cook until boiling and thickened. The mixture will look oily; remove from the heat and let cool. Preheat the kue lumpur mold and grease it with margarine. Fill each mold three-quarters full with the kue lumpur batter.
Add the thick coconut milk mixture on top. Cover the mold and cook for 15 minutes, or until done, over medium-low heat.
The potato and pumpkin kue lumpur is ready to enjoy with afternoon tea. The texture is very soft and savory—absolutely delicious!

Beat the sugar and eggs until combined; they don't need to become fluffy. Add the steamed and mashed sweet potato, then mix on low speed until combined.
Add the dry ingredients alternately with the liquid ingredient (coconut milk). Mix well, then add the melted margarine and mix again.
Prepare a pukis mold or similar mold, grease it with margarine, and pour in the batter until full. Add the toppings, cover the mold, and cook until evenly done.
Serve.

Prepare the ingredients.
Blend the boiled potatoes, eggs, sugar, pandan water, and salt until smooth. Pour into a bowl, add the coconut milk, and mix well. Add the flour and mix again until combined.
I added pandan paste so the color wouldn't look pale; you can skip it if you like. Add the margarine and mix well.
Put the coconut milk, salt, flour, and pandan leaf for the custard into a saucepan. Stir until combined, then turn on the heat. Keep stirring until the custard thickens.
Put the coconut custard into a piping bag and pour the kue lumpur batter into a measuring cup. Preheat the mold, pour in the batter, then pipe the custard into the center until the mold is almost full.
Cover the mold and cook over low to medium heat for 10–15 minutes. Remove with a small spatula, using a spoon to help lift the cakes out. Repeat until all the batter is used.
🍀Happy baking🌷
strIngredient7: Steamed potatoes, mashed with a fork

strInstructions:
Put the water, granulated sugar, salt, and butter in a saucepan and cook until the butter melts. Add the flour and stir quickly until the dough comes together and is smooth.
Let the dough rest briefly, then add the coconut milk and water. Mix with a mixer until combined.
Add the eggs and mix again until combined. Preheat the kue lumpur mold and lightly grease it with a little oil. Pour in the batter and cover the mold. Cook until half done, then add raisins as a topping.
Cook again until the cakes are done. Remove and serve once warm. They taste delicious, with a soft, melt-in-your-mouth texture that still holds its shape.

strMeal: Kue Lumpur Labu Parang Legit & Lembut
strInstructions:
Cut the pumpkin into small pieces and boil or steam until cooked. Drain.
Blend the pumpkin with the coconut milk until smooth. Set aside.
Mix the sugar, eggs, and vanilla until combined; there's no need to beat them until fluffy. Sift the flour over the mixture, add the powdered milk and salt, then pour in the blended pumpkin and mix well.
Add the melted margarine and mix again.
Preheat the mold and lightly grease the surface with margarine. Pour in the batter and add the toppings when the batter is almost cooked. Wait until done, then remove.
The pumpkin kue lumpur is ready to serve 🎃💛🧡

Beat the egg with a whisk.
Add the granulated sugar and beat until the sugar dissolves.
Next, add the flour, salt, vanilla, melted margarine, and coconut milk.
Mix until there are no lumps. Finally, add the food coloring and mix well. Strain if necessary. Pour into a measuring cup to make it easier to fill the molds.
Preheat the kue lumpur mold. If possible, place a heat diffuser underneath so the cakes don't burn too quickly (I didn't use one). Once hot, grease with margarine and fill the molds with batter. Use low heat. When the edges begin to cook, scoop out the still-liquid batter from the center with a spoon so the cake forms a bowl shape. Once cooked, remove. Repeat until all the batter is used.
To make the custard: Combine the granulated sugar, cornstarch, and salt, and stir. Gradually pour in the coconut milk, stirring until smooth and lump-free. Cook the custard over medium heat, stirring continuously until it bubbles and is cooked through.
While still hot, pour enough custard into each bowl-shaped cake. Add a little strawberry jam and a pandan leaf as topping, according to taste. Let cool. Once cooled, they're ready to serve. Enjoyy..😘😘
strIngredient9: Dark red food coloring, to taste

strInstructions:
Soak the rice vermicelli in hot water until soft, then drain and cut into shorter pieces.
Beat the chicken eggs with the chicken stock powder, garlic powder, and ground pepper. Add the carrot and spring onion.
Add the vermicelli, wheat flour, and margarine, then mix until evenly combined.
Heat the kue lumpur mold and add 1 tablespoon of oil. Pour the batter into the mold. Once the bottom is cooked, flip and cook until done.
Remove, top with sliced chili and celery, and serve warm.
strIngredient2: Carrot, grated and cut into small cubes
strIngredient10: Thinly sliced red chili, for topping

strInstructions:
Blend the potatoes with the coconut milk and eggs until smooth. Pour into a bowl containing the flour, salt, stock powder, and yellow food coloring, then mix well. (Sorry, I forgot to photograph the step-by-step process and only realized after the batter was ready.) Add the sweetened condensed milk and mix well, then add the melted margarine and stir until the batter is smooth.
Preheat the kue lumpur mold and grease it with margarine. Pour in the batter, cover the mold, and cook until half done. Add the shredded meat and sliced red chili on top. Cover and cook again until the cakes are done. Use low heat so they cook evenly without burning.
Serve the savory beef floss kue lumpur with sliced celery leaves.

~ Steam the pumpkin until cooked, then mash it and set aside.
~ Prepare the ingredients. Beat the eggs and sugar until the sugar dissolves and the mixture becomes fluffy. Add the flour, vanilla, and salt, then stir until combined.
~ Add the pumpkin, water, coconut milk, and oil. Mix well.
~ Preheat the snack maker and lightly grease it with oil. Pour in the batter until full, add raisins, and cook until done. Remove.
~ Serve warm.

Beat the eggs and sugar until the sugar dissolves. Add the warm potatoes and mix well.
Add the coconut milk, vanilla, and salt. Mix well.
Sift the wheat flour into the batter and stir gently. Add the melted margarine and mix until combined.
Let the batter rest at room temperature for 15–20 minutes.
Grease the molds with margarine and preheat briefly. Pour in the batter until three-quarters full and add the toppings.
Steam over medium heat for 12–15 minutes until cooked.
Remove from the heat, take the cakes out of the molds while warm, and serve.
strIngredient9: (soak in warm water for 10 minutes, drain) raisins

strInstructions:
First, blend the steamed pumpkin with the granulated sugar and coconut milk. Then add the egg, melted margarine, vanilla powder, salt, and flour. (I added the flour little by little so the blender could run more easily.)
Heat the kue lumpur mold after lightly greasing it with cooking oil or margarine. Pour in the batter (don't fill it too much, or it may overflow), then add jackfruit pieces and raisins. Use low heat to prevent burning. Cover the mold and wait until the surface of the cakes is no longer wet and the edges turn brown. Remove from the mold.
The fragrant, rich, and sweet pumpkin and jackfruit kue lumpur is ready to enjoy 💛🧡😋
strIngredient9: Jackfruit pieces and a few raisins, if desired

strInstructions:
Combine the coconut milk, salt, and pandan leaf. Stir well and cook until boiling, then remove from the heat and let cool. Combine the banana, papaya, and water, then blend until smooth. Pour into a bowl, add the egg and sugar, and mix well.
Pour in the coconut milk and melted margarine, and mix well. Add the flour, powdered milk, and vanilla.
Mix until evenly combined, then let the batter rest for about 20 minutes. Heat the mold and grease it with margarine or oil. Stir the batter, pour it into the mold until almost full, then cover and cook until half done.
Open the lid and add raisins or other toppings as desired. Cover again and cook until done, then remove.
Repeat until all the batter is used. The banana and papaya kue lumpur is ready to serve.

Blend the jackfruit with enough coconut milk until smooth.
Combine the wheat flour, granulated sugar, salt, vanilla, blended jackfruit, and remaining coconut milk. Whisk until evenly combined and no lumps remain.
Add the egg and yellow food coloring, then mix again.
Finally, pour in the melted margarine and mix again.
Heat the mold, grease it with margarine, and pour in the kue lumpur batter. Cover the mold and cook until three-quarters done. Add the raisins, then continue cooking until fully done.
Serve the kue lumpur warm; it also tastes delicious when cold.

Put the coconut milk, salt, and vanilla in a saucepan and heat until lukewarm.
In a bowl, add the sugar and egg, then beat with a mixer until the sugar dissolves.
Add the wheat flour and the warm coconut milk, then stir until combined. Add the powdered milk and Fermipan yeast, and mix briefly.
Finally, add the margarine and stir until combined. Let the batter rest for about 45 minutes.
Heat the pukis mold over low to medium-low heat, pour in the batter, and cook until done.
Once cooked, brush with margarine and serve.

Beat the eggs and granulated sugar until fluffy. You can use a mixer to speed up the process. Add the active sourdough starter and mix evenly with a spatula.
Sift the dry ingredients (flour and powdered milk) into the mixture.
Add the wet ingredients EXCEPT THE MELTED MARGARINE. Stir until smooth and no lumps remain.
Let the batter rest at room temperature in a covered container for 3–5 hours, depending on the room temperature, until the active starter ferments the batter. Usually, the batter will double in volume and develop many bubbles.
While waiting for the batter to ferment, melt the margarine or butter and let it cool to room temperature.
Add the melted butter and baking soda to the batter, mix well, and let rest for 30 minutes before cooking.
Cook the pukis over low heat, add toppings as desired, and remove once done.
Brush the cooked pukis with margarine while hot, then serve.
For a richer sourdough flavor, you can refrigerate the batter overnight for cold fermentation after step 4. The next morning, remove it from the refrigerator, let it reach room temperature, and continue from step 6.

Melt the margarine and set aside.
Beat the eggs and granulated sugar until the sugar dissolves.
Add the coconut milk, wheat flour, and instant yeast, then beat on low speed until evenly combined.
Add the melted margarine and salt, then beat until combined. Cover and let the batter rest for about 45–60 minutes or until risen.
Heat the pukis mold, pour in the batter until the molds are three-quarters full, and cook over low heat.
Add chocolate sprinkles as desired, cover the mold, and cook until the cakes are done. Remove from the molds and serve.

strMeal: Kue Pukis Lembut Dan Empuk (Tanpa Mixer Dan Santan)
strInstructions:
First, make the yeast starter: combine the instant yeast and granulated sugar, stir well, and let sit for 15 minutes.
After 15 minutes, prepare the pukis batter.
Add the eggs and granulated sugar, then whisk until the sugar dissolves.
Sift in the wheat flour.
Add the melted butter.
Finally, add the liquid milk.
Mix all the ingredients well and let the batter rest for 30 minutes.
After 30 minutes, heat a nonstick pan over low heat.
Grease the pan with butter before adding the batter. Fill each mold three-quarters full, leaving room for the batter to rise.
When half cooked, add chocolate sprinkles or cheese as a topping.
Ready to serve.

Mix the eggs, granulated sugar, and vanilla until the sugar dissolves.
Add the yeast, wheat flour, salt, and sweetened condensed milk. Mix again until combined.
Gradually add the coconut milk to the mixture, stirring until smooth and free of lumps.
Add the melted margarine and stir until evenly combined.
To make different varieties of pukis, divide the batter into two portions and add different flavorings or food coloring.
Let the batter rest for 60 minutes.
After resting, heat the mold after lightly greasing it with margarine. Add the batter once the mold is fully hot. Cook with the mold covered.
When the tops are still half cooked, add toppings as desired. Cover again and cook until the pukis are fully done.

Prepare the yeast starter ingredients, mix them together, and wait about 8 minutes for the yeast to foam.
Prepare the other ingredients. Melt the margarine and set aside. Combine the thick coconut milk with warm water to make 300 g total, then set aside.
Beat the granulated sugar, eggs, and vanilla with a mixer until thick.
Alternately add the sifted wheat flour and warm coconut milk. Once all the flour and coconut milk have been added, add the foamy yeast starter and mix well. Add the melted margarine and mix briefly with the mixer.
Cover with a clean cloth and let the batter rise for about 30–45 minutes. Once risen, the batter is ready to cook in the pukis pan.
Heat the pukis pan and lightly grease it with margarine. Pour in the batter when the pan is very hot. When bubbles appear, cover the pan. Briefly open it and sprinkle with chocolate sprinkles, then cover again and cook until fully done. Some of the batter can be mixed with pandan paste.
Once cooked, turn off the stove and gently remove the pukis with the tip of a spoon.
Good luck trying it 💕
strIngredient9: Instant thick coconut milk + warm water; total 300 g

strInstructions:
Combine all the ingredients for Dough A and knead until smooth and elastic.
Combine the ingredients for Dough B until evenly mixed.
Divide Dough A and Dough B, flatten them, place Dough B on top of Dough A, and shape into a ball.
Steam the pumpkin and mash it. Mix with the sugar and salt to make the filling.
Take a portion of dough, flatten it, add the pumpkin filling, seal and shape into a ball, then roll it out and roll it up lengthwise.
Roll it out again and roll it into a smaller shape. Flatten once more, add the pumpkin filling, seal, and shape into a ball.
Cook in a nonstick pan or oven over low heat until the surface turns brown.
Once cooked, remove and serve warm.

Prepare all the ingredients. Beat the ingredients for Part A with a mixer until thick and ribbon-like. Add the flour and beat briefly, then add the remaining ingredients for Part B. Mix briefly until combined.
Divide the batter into two portions, one red and one plain/white. Prepare a preheated steamer and lightly grease the molds with vegetable oil. Pour in one-quarter of the batter and steam for 5 minutes with the lid covered by a cloth.
Open the steamer and add jam or spreadable cheese as desired. Pour in the remaining batter to cover the filling. Steam for another 15 minutes. Once cooked, turn off the stove, remove the bakpia from the steamer, and take them out of the molds. The red-and-white steamed bakpia are ready to celebrate Indonesia's Independence Day 🇲🇨

Put the wheat flour, Rose Brand granulated sugar, water, Rose Brand cooking oil, and salt in a bowl. Knead until smooth and elastic.
Cover the dough with plastic wrap and let it rest for 30 minutes to make it more elastic.
In a bowl, combine the ingredients for Dough B, the Rose Brand margarine and wheat flour. Mix and knead until smooth, then shape into a ball. Set aside.
Divide Dough A into 12 portions. Take one portion, flatten it, place a ball of Dough B on top, then fold and seal tightly.
Once sealed, flatten again, fill with mung bean paste, seal tightly, shape into a ball, and neaten the edges.
After filling all the dough with mung bean paste, heat a nonstick pan. Cook the bakpia with the pan covered. Once the bottoms are browned, flip and cook until fully done.
Serve the soft bakpia with warm tea.
strIngredient11: Mung bean paste for onde-onde, bakpia, and kue ku filling

strMeal: Pasta Kacang Hijau Isian Onde Onde, Bakpia, Kue Ku
strInstructions:
Soak the peeled mung beans in water for at least 2 hours.
Drain, then steam the mung beans until tender, about 20 minutes.
Put the mung beans in a food chopper, add the water, Rose Brand instant coconut milk, and Rose Brand cooking oil, then blend until very smooth.
Cook the blended mung beans in a pan over low heat.
Once the mixture starts bubbling, add the salt and Rose Brand margarine. Stir continuously over low heat until the mixture becomes smooth and can be shaped by hand.
Remove from the heat and let cool. The paste is ready to use as a filling for bakpia, onde-onde, or kue ku.

Beat the granulated sugar, Ovalet, and eggs on high speed until the mixture is pale, thick, and leaves ribbons.
Add the sifted flour and mix on the lowest speed, then add the milk and mix again.
Once the milk and flour are combined, add the chocolate paste and mix on low speed until evenly incorporated. Pour in the melted margarine or butter and fold it in, making sure no butter settles at the bottom.
Grease the molds with oil or the remaining melted butter. Fill each mold one-quarter full and steam for 5 minutes over medium-low heat.
After 5 minutes, add the chocolate spread filling and cover it with more batter. Steam again for 20 minutes.
MasyaAllah, it's so delicious, perfectly sweet, and incredibly soft. Give it a try!

strMeal: Resep Kue Bakpia Kukus Cokelat Lumer Anti Gagal
strInstructions:
Prepare all the ingredients.
Beat the eggs, sugar, vanilla, and SP for 10 minutes on high speed until the mixture leaves ribbons.
Add the sifted wheat flour, cocoa powder, and powdered milk. Add the chocolate paste and mix briefly until just combined. Finally, add the oil and fold it in with a spatula.
Prepare the molds by greasing them with vegetable oil. Fill each mold halfway and steam for 7 minutes. Remember to cover the steamer lid with a cloth so water doesn't drip onto the cakes. Remove the lid.
Add the chocolate bar pieces and cover with more batter until the molds are full. Steam for another 15 minutes.
The chocolate steamed bakpia cakes are ready to serve 👍👌

Beat the eggs, granulated sugar, and SP on high speed until thick and ribbon-like.
Add the sifted flour, cocoa powder, and baking powder, then mix on low speed. Add the cooking oil and mix until combined.
Preheat the steamer. If you're not using a special steamer lid, cover the lid with a clean cloth. Lightly grease the talam molds with oil and fill each mold halfway with batter.
Steam for 10 minutes. Open the steamer, add the filling to the center of each mold, then cover with more batter until almost full. Steam for another 10 minutes.
Once cooked, remove the cakes from the molds. The chocolate steamed bakpia are ready to serve. They disappeared in no time, without a single one left 😆
strIngredient8: Chocolate spread for steamed buns / chocolate spread filling

strInstructions:
1. Filling: Wash the mung beans thoroughly. Boil them until tender using the 5-30-7 method. Mash while still hot, then add the salt, sugar, and sweetened condensed milk. Mix well.
