Cook again until the filling becomes somewhat dry. Gradually add a little flour, mixing until the filling is even, fairly dry, and no longer sticky. Once cooled, shape the filling into balls until all the mixture is used. Set aside.
2. Bakpia pastry, Dough 1: Combine all the ingredients and knead until smooth and elastic. Set aside for 15 minutes, covered with a cloth to prevent the dough from drying out.
3. Bakpia pastry, Dough 2: Combine all the ingredients and mix evenly.
4. Take a portion of Dough 1, flatten it, and wrap it around Dough 2. Shape into a ball. Adjust the size as desired; Dough 2 should be slightly smaller than Dough 1. Repeat until all the dough is used. Let rest for 10 minutes, covered with a cloth so it doesn't dry out.
5. Flatten the dough, then fold it as many times as desired to create layers (I folded mine three times). Add the prepared filling and seal. Repeat until all the dough is used.
6. Cook in a preheated nonstick pan until fully cooked over low heat. It's best to use a pan with a lid so the heat is distributed evenly.
7. Remove and serve.

● Red bean filling: Boil the red beans with the water and salt until soft. Remove from the heat and drain.
Mash the red beans, then add the thick coconut milk and granulated sugar. Cook over medium-low heat until thick and firm. Let cool to room temperature, then portion into approximately 10 g pieces or to your preference. Set aside.
● Dough I: Combine all the ingredients and knead until smooth and elastic. Cover with plastic wrap and let rest for about 30 minutes. Set aside.
● Dough II: Combine all the ingredients and knead until evenly mixed. Let rest for about 30 minutes. Set aside.
After about 30 minutes, divide Dough I and Dough II into 30 portions each, or as desired. Note: Dough I should be larger than Dough II.
Roll out Dough I, place Dough II on top, shape into a ball, and let rest for about 20 minutes.
Take one portion, roll it into a circle, then roll it up from right to left. Roll it out lengthwise and roll it up again. Finally, roll it into a circle, add the red bean filling, seal into a ball, and flatten slightly.
Arrange the bakpia on a baking tray and bake both sides until golden brown.
The red bean bakpia are ready to enjoy.

strMeal: Pasta Kacang Hijau Isian Onde Onde, Bakpao, Bakpia, Roti Dll
strInstructions:
Soak the peeled mung beans for 8 hours (at least 2 hours). Drain and rinse under running water. Steam with the pandan leaf for 20 minutes.
Prepare the coconut milk mixture by combining 100 ml of Rose Brand coconut milk with 300 ml of water. Put the mung beans in a blender jug, pour in the coconut milk mixture, and blend until smooth.
🔸️Pour into a pan. Add the vanilla paste, salt, and Rose Brand granulated sugar.
🔸️Turn on the stove and cook until the mixture becomes smooth and no longer sticky. Let cool.
Shape into 10 g balls. Repeat until finished. Set aside.
The mung bean paste is ready to use as a filling for onde-onde, steamed buns, bakpia, and more.

strMeal: Pasta Kacang Merah (Untuk Isian Bakpao, Bakpia, Dorayaki Dsbnya)
strInstructions:
Soak the red beans overnight or for at least 6 hours. Wash them thoroughly and drain.
Boil the red beans in water until very tender, then drain. Blend with a little water until smooth. Combine the mashed red beans with Rose Brand granulated sugar, Rose Brand cooking oil, and the Rose Brand glutinous rice flour mixture. Stir until evenly combined and cook over medium heat until bubbling and thickened. Let cool to room temperature, transfer to a sealed container, and refrigerate.
Shape into balls for use as steamed bun filling, adjusting the size to fit the buns for easier filling.

Soak the mung beans in enough water for at least 2 hours (I soaked mine overnight). Pour 500 ml of clean water into a pot and bring to a boil. Add the mung beans and cook until they swell, their interiors become visible, and the water begins to evaporate. Drain.
Blend the mung beans until smooth.
Cook the blended mung beans with the sugar and coconut milk in a nonstick pan, stirring continuously until the mixture has a paste-like consistency.

strMeal: Pasta Kacang Merah Super Legit (Untuk Bakpao Dan Bakpia)
strInstructions:
Prepare the ingredients.
Wash the red beans and boil them with the pandan leaves using the 5-30-7 method until they can be crushed easily. If they are still firm, repeat using the 7-15-7 method with boiling water. Use plenty of water and cook until very tender. Drain and set aside the pandan leaves.
While still warm, blend the red beans with a little water at a time until smooth and paste-like. Do not make the mixture too thin.
Cook the red bean paste in a pan over low heat. Add Rose Brand sugar and salt, stirring continuously for about 5 minutes.
Once the paste begins to dry out slightly, add the Rose Brand cooking oil in three additions. Stir after each addition until the oil is incorporated and the paste becomes glossy, about 5 minutes.
Add the glutinous rice flour mixture, pouring it in while stirring very quickly. Continue cooking over low heat until the paste is smooth, pliable, and no longer sticks to the spatula. Total cooking time is about 20 minutes.
Take a little paste and try rolling it into a ball. If it holds its shape without being too soft, it is ready.
The rich red bean paste is ready to use as a filling for steamed buns and bakpia. 😍
strIngredient4: Heaping tablespoon of Rose Brand glutinous rice flour

strInstructions:
Using a mixer, gradually increase the speed while beating the eggs, sugar, SP emulsifier, salt, and vanilla until the mixture is thick, pale, and leaves ribbons.
Alternately add the dry ingredients (flour, cornstarch, and powdered milk) and the thin coconut milk. Mix again at the lowest speed until evenly combined.
Lightly grease the talam cake molds with vegetable oil and sprinkle with a little sesame seed. Pour in the red batter first and steam for 5 minutes. Pour the white batter over the steamed red layer and steam for another 5 minutes. At this stage, you can add a little jam if desired, taking care not to overfill. Finally, add the green batter and steam for 15 minutes. Remove and serve.

Prepare the mung bean filling.
🌸 Soak the mung beans for 2 hours, then steam until tender. 🌸 Blend all the filling ingredients until smooth.
🌸 Pour the mixture into a pan and cook over low heat, stirring continuously until firm enough to shape. 🌸 Shape the filling into balls.
Make the bakpia pastry: Put the ingredients for Dough A in a bowl and knead until smooth. Shape into a ball and set aside.
Knead the ingredients for Dough B until evenly combined.
🌸 Add food coloring as desired, then divide Dough A and Dough B into 20 portions each.
Take one portion of Dough A, roll it out, add a portion of Dough B, and shape into a ball.
Roll it out lengthwise, roll it up, then roll and roll it up again. Repeat until all the dough is used.
🌸 Take one portion of dough and flatten it. 🌸 Place the filling in the center and shape into a ball. 🌸 Press gently to flatten slightly. 🌸 Cut around the edges to create petals. 🌸 Pinch the tips to form flower petals, then make a small slit in the middle of each petal. 🌸 Moisten the center, sprinkle with sesame seeds, and press gently so they stick.
🌸 Arrange on a baking tray greased with margarine or oil. 🌸 Bake at 180°C for 30 minutes, or adjust according to your oven.
Serve. 🥰

Combine the flour, Cap Enaak Original sweetened condensed milk, margarine, water, oil, and salt. Knead until evenly combined. Submerge the dough in oil and let rest for 30 minutes. Divide into balls of about 15 g each.
Combine all the ingredients for Dough B and shape into balls of about 5 g each.
To make the filling, toast the flour, salt, and pandan leaf until the mixture feels light. Divide it equally into two portions. Mix one portion with Cap Enaak Original sweetened condensed milk and grated cheese. Stir well, then add the margarine and mix. Add the water and combine thoroughly. Shape into balls and set aside. Make the chocolate filling using the same method. Set both fillings aside.
Flatten one portion of Dough A, place a portion of Dough B on top, and fold like an envelope. Roll it out, roll it up, and roll it out again. Repeat this process three times, then add the filling and shape into a ball.
Arrange on a baking tray lined with baking paper. Bake at 180°C with both top and bottom heat for 25 minutes, then flip and bake for another 15 minutes, or adjust to your oven. Remember to preheat the oven for 10 minutes. Once cooled, store in an airtight container.
strIngredient4: Cap Enaak Original sweetened condensed milk
strIngredient14: Segitiga Biru wheat flour, divided into two portions

strInstructions:
Prepare the ingredients.
Cut the sweet potatoes into pieces, steam until tender, and mash.
Dissolve the sugar and salt in the water, then pour into the pan with the mashed sweet potato. Cook until the water has evaporated and the mixture can be shaped by hand.
In separate bowls, combine the ingredients for the flour dough and oil dough. Knead each until it forms a dough. Let rest for 15–30 minutes.
Shape the flour dough and oil dough into balls. I made 23 portions.
Take one oil dough ball and wrap it with a portion of flour dough. Repeat until all the oil dough is used.
Roll out the dough, fold it into thirds, roll it out again, and fold it into thirds once more. Roll it thinly and add the sweet potato filling. This creates crispy, flaky layers in the bakpia.
I shaped some into rounds and others into squares, but you can shape them however you like. 😁
Bake at 150°C for 20–25 minutes, then flip the bakpia and bake for another 15–20 minutes. You can also cook them in a nonstick pan.
Here is the result. 😊🙏🏻

Dough A: Add the water and sugar (powdered sugar should ideally be used, but I didn't have any). Stir until the sugar dissolves.
Add the flour, cooking oil, and water. Knead until combined and no longer sticky to the touch.
Weigh the dough into 10 g portions. Let rest for about 15–30 minutes to become elastic.
While Dough A rests, combine all the ingredients for Dough B.
Mix until the dough is no longer sticky to the touch.
Weigh Dough B into 4–5 g portions.
Once both doughs have been portioned, take one portion of Dough A and flatten it. Flatten one portion of Dough B on top of Dough A.
Fold the dough like an envelope.
Flatten it again.
Then fold it as shown in the reference.
Once all portions are prepared, let them rest for about 15–30 minutes so they become elastic and pliable.
Wrap the filling completely in the dough.
Flatten a portion of dough and add the filling from the previous recipe, Meses Bakpia Filling.
Heat a nonstick pan over the lowest heat. Arrange the bakpia in the pan and cover. Check the bottoms occasionally; when browned, flip and cook until the other side is browned too. Remove and serve as a snack with coffee or tea.
strIngredient10: Filling made with chocolate sprinkles for meses bakpia

strInstructions:
Combine the flour, chocolate sprinkles, margarine, sweetened condensed milk, and salt. Stir until evenly mixed.
Add ice water until the mixture can be shaped.
Weigh into 15 g portions and shape into flat balls.
Once all portions are shaped, store them in a container in the refrigerator, or use them immediately as bakpia filling.

strMeal: Lapis Legit Ketan / Engkak Ketan Khas Palembang
strInstructions:
Toast the grated coconut until golden brown, then grind until it releases its oil. Set aside. Toast the glutinous rice flour until it feels lighter, then add the salt and vanilla powder. Mix well and let cool.
In a bowl, add the eggs and granulated sugar. Whisk until the sugar dissolves, then add the white sweetened condensed milk. Mix again and set aside.
Sift the glutinous rice flour into the coconut milk to prevent lumps. Stir well, then add the coconut milk mixture to the egg mixture and mix again.
Add a little batter to the ground toasted coconut. Add the melted margarine and mix evenly, then pour this mixture back into the layered cake batter. Stir until everything is combined.
Prepare a traditional cake oven. I use a Bima oven for traditional cakes, heated with charcoal on top. Prepare a measuring cup, margarine for greasing the layers, and a cake press if available. Line a 20 × 20 cm pan with baking paper and grease the entire pan with margarine. Preheat the oven, placing the empty pan inside for 10 minutes. Pour in the first layer, about 350 ml, and bake for 10–15 minutes, checking occasionally to prevent burning.
Remove from the oven. If bubbles appear, prick them with a clean toothpick, then press and smooth the layer with a spoon and margarine. A square traditional cake press can also be used. Pour in the second layer, about 300 ml, and bake for another 10–15 minutes. Repeat until all the batter is used.
After the final layer is cooked, place the pan over the charcoal embers with another pan underneath, as shown. Cook for about 15 minutes. Remove and let the cake cool completely.
Remove from the pan, slice, and serve. Masyaa Allah, this is delicious!
strIngredient7: Can of white sweetened condensed milk

strInstructions:
Prepare all the ingredients.
First, beat the ingredients for Part A until pale and fluffy. Set aside. Since I used margarine, I beat it for about 15 minutes.
Beat the ingredients for Part B for about 10 minutes until pale, thick, and ribbon-like. Set aside.
Gradually sift the ingredients for Part C into Part B, folding with a spatula until evenly combined. Make sure there are no flour lumps.
Gradually fold the mixture of Parts B and C into Part A with a spatula. Continue until all the mixture is incorporated, making sure everything is evenly combined.
Prepare a 22 × 10 × 7 cm pan lined with baking paper and heat the steamer.
Weigh 40 g of batter, pour it into the pan, and smooth the surface. Steam over medium heat for 5 minutes.
Combine the topping ingredients and mix well.
After 5 minutes, pour another 40 g of batter over the first layer and sprinkle with the topping. Steam for another 5 minutes. Repeat until all the batter and topping are used.
Steam the final layer for 10 minutes until cooked. Remove the pan from the steamer immediately.
Once slightly cooled, remove the cake from the pan, slice, and serve.

1. Beat the butter and sweetened condensed milk until pale and creamy.
2. Beat the eggs and sugar until thick, fluffy, and ribbon-like. Mix in the powdered milk and spekkoek spice.
3. Combine the two mixtures until evenly mixed, using a mixer at medium speed.
4. Turn on the oven's top heat. I use a grill oven set to medium heat (level 5). Preheat for about 10 minutes.
5. Grease the pan with margarine, line it with baking paper, then grease the paper again.
6. For the first layer, weigh out 85 g of batter and bake for 3.5 minutes, until browned. Let it become fairly dark so the layers are clearly visible. Repeat until all the batter is used, adding prunes every fourth layer.
7. Continue repeating step 6 until all the batter is used.
8. Once baked, remove from the oven and loosen the edges with a blunt knife. Turn the pan over, first covering the top with baking paper.

Put the coconut milk, salt, and pandan leaves in a saucepan. Bring to a boil over heat, stirring continuously, then remove from the heat and let cool slightly. Bring water to a boil in the steamer. Grease an 8-inch square pan (20 × 20 × 5 cm) with oil and set aside.
Combine the rice flour, tapioca starch, and granulated sugar. Gradually pour in the coconut milk while stirring until smooth.
Divide the batter into two portions. Mix one portion with pandan green coloring and leave the other plain. You can also divide it into three portions and use colors of your choice.
Bring the steamer water to a boil. Pour about 100 ml of green batter into the pan and steam for 5 minutes until set. Pour in 100 ml of white batter and spread evenly. Continue alternating layers until all the batter is used.
Once cooked, remove the pan from the steamer and let cool.
Remove the cake from the pan and cut into about 24 pieces, or as desired.
Give it a try. We're all learning together here. Thank you!
strIngredient6: Pandan leaves, torn and tied into a knot

strInstructions:
Separate the egg whites and yolks into different bowls. Beat the sugar, butter, and vanilla until fluffy and slightly pale, then gradually add the egg yolks, mixing until combined.
Add the sifted flour and powdered milk, fold with a spatula, then add the sweetened condensed milk and mix well. Prepare a pan lined with baking paper and preheat the oven to 200°C, adjusting to your oven.
Weigh 120 g of batter for the first layer, pour it into the pan, and spread evenly. Bake for about 8 minutes, adjusting to your oven. Once cooked, press the layer with a cake press lightly greased with butter.
Add the second layer and subsequent layers, using 90 g of batter each. Once browned, press with the butter-greased cake press and bake using top heat only. For every third layer, add halved prunes arranged over the cake, bake until browned, then press with butter. Repeat until all the batter is used.
For the final layer, add more prunes on top and bake until cooked. Remove from the oven and let cool completely at room temperature.
Once completely cool, slice the prune lapis legit, arrange on a serving plate, and enjoy.

Beat the egg yolks and sugar until fluffy. Set aside.
Beat the cold butter and vanilla until pale.
Add the flour, powdered milk, and spekkoek spice. Mix again.
Add the butter mixture to the egg and flour mixture. Stir until combined. Prepare a double pan or Happy Call pan and grease it with butter using a tissue or brush.
Take one portion of batter and pour it into the double pan, spreading it evenly. Make sure the stove is off while pouring and spreading, and that the pan is cool. Cover and cook over very low heat for about 5–7 minutes so the top does not dry out.
After 5 minutes, check whether it is cooked. If done, brush the surface evenly with the topping mixture. Roll it from one side while still hot.
Place the rolled lapis legit on a plate and wrap it in plastic or baking paper to keep it from drying out.
Continue cooking the remaining batter as before. Make sure the double pan has cooled before pouring in more batter so it spreads evenly and does not stick. Once cooked, brush the surface with the topping mixture, place the first roll on the brushed surface, and roll it up gently. Repeat until all the batter is used. Wrap in plastic or baking paper and let rest for about 1 hour. After 1 hour, slice and serve.

1. Beat the egg yolks and powdered sugar until thick and fluffy. Set aside.
2. Beat the butter and liquid vanilla until pale, fluffy, and light. Turn off the mixer, add the flour, powdered milk, and spekkoek spice, then mix on low speed until combined.
3. Add the butter mixture to the egg mixture and mix until evenly combined. Weigh the batter and divide into two portions of about 172 g for a 22 × 28 cm pan. I used one large 30 × 40 cm pan instead.
4. Pour into a pan lined with baking paper, spread evenly, and sprinkle with candied fruit. Preheat the oven for at least 10 minutes on high heat. Bake the first portion on the middle rack for 5 minutes, then move it to the top rack for another 5 minutes. Check frequently, and if possible rotate the pan every 2–3 minutes for even baking. Once cooked, remove and bake the second portion.
5. Mix the topping ingredients together and set aside. While waiting, remove the first cake layer from the pan, spread with the topping mixture, trim off the hard edges, and roll tightly. Once the second layer is cooked, remove it from the pan and peel off the baking paper. Spread with the topping mixture and roll it around the first layer, pressing firmly. Refrigerate until set, then remove, slice, and serve. Enjoy! ❤

Beat the butter-margarine mixture and sweetened condensed milk on high speed until pale and smooth. Add the powdered milk and beat again until the mixture is pale, fluffy, and light. Set aside.
In another bowl, beat the duck eggs, egg yolks, and granulated sugar on high speed.
Beat until pale, fluffy, and ribbon-like. Gradually pour the egg mixture into the butter mixture while mixing on low speed. Mix only until combined, then turn off the mixer. The batter should be thick and ribbon-like.
Take 60 g of batter (I used about 1.5 ladles) and pour it into a 24 × 10 × 7 cm pan lined with baking paper. Spread evenly with a spoon. Bake in a preheated oven at 180°C using TOP HEAT ONLY for 15 minutes. Check the color; if it is not browned enough, rotate the pan for even heat. Bake for about 5 more minutes.
Remove from the oven. Prick the surface with a skewer or toothpick, spread with a little margarine, and press the layer with a lapis legit press. Pour in another 60 g of batter (about 1.5 ladles) and bake for 15–20 minutes. As the cake gets taller, pay attention to the baking time. Once the batter reaches about halfway up the pan, place the pan on the middle rack near the top heating element. Make sure every layer is cooked through.
Repeat until all the batter is used. For the final layer, change the temperature to 150°C with both top and bottom heat and move the pan to the lower rack. Bake for 10–15 minutes or until the surface is golden brown. Remove from the oven. The cake will initially rise high, then settle slightly as it cools to room temperature. Remove it from the pan only after it has cooled completely, then slice.

Beat the Wijsman butter and sweetened condensed milk until pale and fluffy.
In a separate bowl, beat the egg yolks, powdered sugar, and vanilla until thick. Add the powdered milk and beat briefly again.
Combine the Wijsman butter mixture with the egg yolk mixture and stir until evenly mixed.
Preheat the oven. Pour 4 tablespoons of batter into a pan lined with baking paper and bake at 160°C for 5 minutes or until browned. Remove from the oven.
Prick any bubbles with a toothpick and flatten the cake surface with a lapis cake press. Pour in another 4 tablespoons of batter and bake again. Repeat until all the batter is used.
Once the cake is baked, let it rest for 10 minutes before removing it from the pan.

✅ Beat the egg whites at medium speed. Once foamy, gradually add the sugar and increase the speed to the highest setting. Beat until white, fluffy, and stiff enough to leave ribbons.
✅ Add the flour and mix at medium speed.
✅ Add the powdered milk and gently stir until evenly combined. Add the sweetened condensed milk and mix at low speed.
✅ Finally, add the melted margarine and stir until evenly combined. ✅ Divide the batter into two portions and mix pandan paste into one portion.
✅ Prepare an 18 × 18 × 7 cm pan lined with baking paper. Pour in about 2 medium ladles of batter, adjusting to the size of your pan. ✅ Place in a gas oven or whichever oven you have at home, on the upper rack. Bake until the batter no longer jiggles when moved, then transfer it to the lower rack and use top heat. Once slightly browned, remove and add another layer of green batter. Alternate the layers until all the batter is used.
✅ Once cooked, remove from the oven and let cool before taking the cake out of the mold. Alhamdulillah. Happy baking!

Meringue: Beat the egg whites on high speed while gradually adding one-third of the Rose Brand granulated sugar. Beat until stiff peaks form. Set aside.
Egg yolk batter: In another bowl, add the butter, Rose Brand margarine, and remaining sugar. Mix at the lowest speed. Gradually add the egg yolks, followed by the vanilla essence.
Add the powdered milk, then sift in the flour while mixing on low speed. Add the sweetened condensed milk and fold with a spatula. Add the meringue and fold until evenly combined.
Prepare a baking pan lined with baking paper and greased with margarine. Pour in 130 g of batter and spread evenly. Tap the pan three times to release air bubbles. Bake on the lower rack with both top and bottom heat at 200°C for 12 minutes, or until the top is browned. Brush with butter and press the surface with a lapis legit press. For the second layer, use 100 g of batter and bake on the middle rack using top heat at 180°C for 13 minutes. Repeat for the following layers.
If any bubbles appear, prick them with a skewer. Use about 130 g for the final layer and bake on the lower rack with both top and bottom heat for 12 minutes. Once cooked, immediately loosen the edges of the pan to prevent the cake from curving. Leave the cake in the pan until cool before removing it.

Beat Ingredient C until pale.
Reduce the mixer speed, then gradually add Ingredient B until fully incorporated. Set aside.
In another bowl, beat Ingredient A on high speed until thick and ribbon-like. Gradually add the sugar.
Add the mixture of Ingredients C and B little by little. Fold with a spatula until evenly combined.
Preheat the oven to 180°C. Prepare a 20 × 20 × 8 cm baking pan and line it with baking paper.
Weigh 120 g of batter for the first layer. Stir the batter, pour it into the pan, and spread evenly. Bake until browned. Bake the first layer at 180°C using both top and bottom heat for 15 minutes. Once browned, brush the surface with butter. If air bubbles appear, prick them with a skewer or toothpick, then gently press the surface with a cake press until flat.
For the second layer and subsequent layers, weigh 90 g of batter, stir, pour into the pan, and spread evenly. Bake at 200°C using top heat for 8 minutes.
For the final layer, after pouring and spreading the batter, arrange the flattened prunes on the surface. Bake at 180°C using both top and bottom heat for 15 minutes. Once cooked, remove from the oven and let cool until warm, then refrigerate to help it set. Remove the cake from the pan, cut as desired, and serve.

Beat the butter and sweetened condensed milk until fluffy and pale, about 12–15 minutes. Set aside.
Beat the sugar and egg yolks until thick and ribbon-like.
Add the previously beaten butter mixture and mix on low speed until combined. Add the flour and powdered milk, then mix well. Add the pandan paste and fold until evenly combined.
Preheat the oven. Line a baking pan with baking paper and grease the underside of the paper with margarine. Pour in one ladleful of batter (90–100 g). Bake using bottom heat until the edges turn brown. Switch to top heat and bake until browned. Pour in another ladleful, spread evenly, and bake again until browned.
Put the Nutella in a piping bag. Add Nutella to the fourth layer and bake again until browned. Add another ladleful of batter and repeat until all the batter is used. Let cool completely. Remove from the pan and peel off the baking paper. I used a gas oven.
Store in an airtight container.

Prepare the ingredients.
Grease a baking pan with margarine and line it with baking paper.
Beat the margarine for about 5 minutes. Add Cap Enaak sweetened condensed milk and continue beating until pale and fluffy. Set aside.
Beat the egg yolks and powdered sugar until thick, pale, and ribbon-like. Set aside.
Add the beaten margarine mixture to the egg yolk mixture and mix evenly with a whisk or spatula.
Take about 270–300 g of batter, add the pandan paste, and stir until the color is evenly distributed. Set aside.
Layer 1: Take the yellow batter (about 110–120 g), pour it into the pan, and spread evenly. Bake at 150°C using both top and bottom heat until golden brown, adjusting to your oven. Gently press the layer with a lapis cake press.
Layer 2 and every second layer: Pour in the yellow batter (about 95 g), spread evenly, add red syrup, and bake using top heat only at 160–170°C, adjusting to your oven.
Layer 3 and every third layer: Pour in the green batter (about 95 g), spread evenly, then add green bananas and dates. Bake using top heat only at 160–170°C, adjusting to your oven. Repeat steps 7–9 until all the batter is used.
Once baking is complete, let the Green Banana and Date Lapis Legit cool to room temperature. Remove it from the pan and slice.
The Green Banana and Date Lapis Legit is ready to enjoy and can also make a modern gift idea for Eid.

The method is the same as in my previous recipe, Premium Bangka Lapis Legit.
This is a comparison of lapis legit made from the same recipe using different butter blends. The version made with margarine looks more yellow, while the version made with the special lapis legit butter mix looks paler. The butter-mix version tastes similar to Baumkuchen.
Note: The last image (second step) was taken by my mother using a Xiaomi phone, while the thumbnail and first step were taken by me and my sibling-in-law using iPhones. The difference is quite noticeable, possibly because of the lighting. My sibling-in-law and I both use 1200-lumen, 4000K lights.
strIngredient2: Special lapis legit butter mix, special lapis legit butter mix

strInstructions:
In a bowl, beat Ingredient A on high speed until pale and fluffy.
In another bowl, beat Ingredient B until the butter becomes creamy. Add Ingredient B to Ingredient A and mix with a spatula. Add Ingredient C and gently mix until combined.
Preheat the oven. Prepare a 24 × 30 × 3 cm baking pan and line it with baking paper. Divide the batter into two equal portions, weighing them if desired. Pour one portion into the pan.
Bake at 175°C using both top and bottom heat for 7 minutes, then continue for 3 minutes using top heat only. Remove from the oven, take the cake out of the pan, and place it on baking paper. Lightly brush the top with white sweetened condensed milk, then roll it up. Refrigerate the rolled lapis legit for 30 minutes.
Repeat with the remaining batter. Once baked, place it on baking paper, brush with white sweetened condensed milk, then place the first chilled roll on top and roll them together tightly.
Let rest for at least 30 minutes. The soft rolled lapis legit is ready to eat. It may taste even better if left overnight before serving. Thank you, and happy baking!

For the lapis legit butter mix, see my previous recipe. Combine Ingredient A except for the egg yolks, and beat until creamy. Add the egg yolks in several additions and beat until evenly combined.
Beat Ingredient B in a separate bowl until stiff peaks form.
Add Ingredient C to Ingredient A and mix on low speed until combined.
Fold Ingredient B into the mixture in two additions using a spatula.
Line a 20 × 20 × 7 cm pan with baking paper. Do not grease the sides of the pan. Bake the first layer in a preheated oven at 180–200°C using both top and bottom heat, with no fan, on the lower rack.
Bake the second and subsequent layers using top heat only at 180–200°C, without the fan, on the middle rack. Each layer must not bake for more than 6 minutes, or the cake will become dry and hard.
Remember to prick any bubbles with a toothpick and gently flatten each layer with a lapis legit press. Do not press too hard.
Bake the final layer using both top and bottom heat, with the pan on the highest rack and another tray underneath. Continue baking until the cake is evenly cooked. Once done, leave it in the pan until cool before turning it over, removing it, and slicing.
Note: I weigh each layer at 100 g. Adjust the oven temperature to suit your oven.
strIngredient2: Special lapis legit butter mix, chilled but not frozen; see my previous recipe
strIngredient6: St vanilla extract (original recipe uses 1/2 tsp vanilla powder)

strMeal: Lapis Prancis Premium / Lapis Sabun / Lapis Legit Prancis
strInstructions:
For the yellow layer, combine the egg yolks and powdered sugar until evenly mixed.
Add the sweetened condensed milk and mix well. Add the flour and Dancow powdered milk, then stir until combined.
Add the melted, cooled butter and mix until evenly incorporated.
Line a baking pan with baking paper. Strain the batter into the pan.
Steam over medium heat for about 30 minutes or until cooked. Cover the top of the pan with plastic wrap to prevent water from dripping onto the cake.
For the lapis legit, beat the butter and sugar until pale and fluffy.
Gradually add the egg yolks while continuing to beat.
Once combined, add the Dancow powdered milk and sweetened condensed milk. Mix well.
Once the steamed yellow layer is cooked, place it in the oven at 210°C using top heat for about 5 minutes.
When the surface is slightly dry, remove it from the oven and bake the lapis legit batter in layers of 80 g each.
Each layer takes about 5–6 minutes, depending on your oven. Once browned, remove it and gently press with a lapis cake press. Continue until all the batter is used.
Happy baking!

Combine all the ingredients and stir gently, using a spoon or whisk. Do not beat until creamy or fluffy. Store in a covered, airtight container in the refrigerator until needed.
I think this mixture not only smells wonderful but also gives the cake a stronger butter flavor and structure, and it does not melt as easily while waiting for the batter to bake. Since it is made entirely from butter, however, room temperature and preparation technique still matter.
For the butter mix I usually use for cookies, see my previous recipe, Homemade Buttermix.
Note: Compared with the premium lapis legit recipe that uses a ratio of two-thirds butter to one-third margarine, this butter mix costs only 3,000 rupiah more per 100 g, which is not a significant difference (30 rupiah per gram).

Prepare all the ingredients.
Beat the butter until pale and thick.
Beat the egg yolks, sugar, and vanilla until thick, pale, and ribbon-like.
Add the powdered milk and fold evenly with a spatula. Gradually add the butter in two additions, folding until combined.
Pour in 3 tablespoons of batter and spread evenly. Bake at 150°C using both top and bottom heat for about 5 minutes.
Pour in another 3 tablespoons of batter and spread evenly. Bake at 175°C using top heat only for about 5 minutes.
Repeat until all the batter is used.
Once cooked, remove the cake from the pan immediately. Let cool before slicing.

First, prepare the ingredients. Lightly grease the baking pan with butter, line it with baking paper, then grease the paper again.
Beat the egg yolks and powdered sugar on high speed until pale, fluffy, and ribbon-like.
Add the butter and mix on low speed until evenly combined.
Add the powdered milk, sweetened condensed milk, and vanilla. Mix again until combined.
Add the wheat flour and mix until evenly incorporated.
In another bowl, beat the egg whites until foamy.
Once foamy, add the powdered sugar and continue beating until stiff and the mixture does not fall when the bowl is turned upside down.
Combine the yolk mixture and egg white mixture, making sure everything is mixed evenly down to the bottom of the bowl.
Make sure the oven is preheated.
Pour the batter into the pan, adjusting the amount to the size of the pan.
Bake until browned. If bubbles appear, press them down to flatten them.
Pour in another measured portion of batter and bake again. Repeat with the same amount each time until all the batter is used.
Once finished, remove from the oven and let cool until warm. Remove from the pan and slice as desired.
The cake is ready to enjoy!

Beat the eggs, granulated sugar, and vanilla until fluffy.
Add the wheat flour and powdered milk, then mix well.
Finally, gradually add the coconut milk and stir until evenly combined.
Bake in layers, using 3 soup spoons of batter for each layer. Continue until all the batter is used. Happy baking!

Beat Ingredient A and Ingredient B separately in different bowls for 15 minutes, until pale, thick, and fluffy.
Add Ingredient A to Ingredient B. Fold with a spatula until evenly combined. Add the additional ingredients and mix again until combined.
Prepare a 20 × 20 × 7 cm baking pan, grease it with butter, and line it with baking paper. Briefly preheat the pan in the oven. Weigh 90 g of batter for each layer, spread it evenly in the pan, and bake at 170°C using both top and bottom heat until the surface is browned.
Remove the pan and gently press the cake surface with a lapis cake press. Add another 90 g of batter, spread evenly, and bake at 190°C using top heat only. Repeat until all the batter is used. If bubbles appear before pressing, prick them with a toothpick to release the air.
Bake the final layer until slightly pale at 190°C, then continue at 170°C using both top and bottom heat for 5 minutes or until the pale surface turns brown. Loosen the edges of the pan and let the cake cool before removing it. Happy baking!

Combine ROSE BRAND rice flour, ROSE BRAND tapioca starch, salt, and vanilla cream. Mix well. Gradually pour in the warmed ROSE BRAND coconut milk and ROSE BRAND granulated sugar mixture while stirring continuously until smooth.
Divide the batter into five portions, depending on the desired food colors: one portion colored rose red, one light green, one purple, one brown, and one left white.
Grease the talam molds with ROSE BRAND cooking oil, then heat them in the steamer.
Pour 1 tablespoon of batter into each mold for each layer. Example layer order: brown, light green, purple, white, and rose red last.
Steam each layer for 2 minutes. Steam the final layer over low heat for 10–15 minutes.
Remove from the steamer, take the cakes out of the molds, and serve.
strIngredient8: Food coloring: rose red, light green, purple, and brown

strInstructions:
Beat the eggs, sugar, and butter until evenly combined. Add the powdered milk and food coloring, then beat until evenly mixed. Gradually add the cornstarch and wheat flour, stirring with a spatula until the dough can be shaped.
Take a portion of dough as desired, fill it with pineapple jam, and shape it like a leaf. Bake until partially cooked, then remove from the oven and brush the surface with egg yolk. Return to the oven and bake over medium heat until fully cooked.

Beat the eggs and sugar until fluffy, then add all the remaining ingredients except the pineapple jam and cheese. Beat again until combined.
Pour half of the batter into a baking pan lightly greased with margarine.
Add the pineapple jam, then pour in the remaining batter and spread it to cover the jam.
Finally, sprinkle with cheese and bake in a preheated oven at 170°C until cooked.
Remove from the oven, let cool to room temperature, then slice as desired and serve.

Prepare all the ingredients.
Press the boiled egg yolk through a sieve, then combine it with the raw egg yolk, powdered sugar, salt, and vanilla essence. Whisk until evenly combined. Add the butter and margarine and whisk until mixed, but do not overmix.
Add the mocaf flour, cornstarch, and powdered milk. Mix until a dough forms.
Weigh the dough and pineapple jam according to your preferred portions. Repeat until everything is portioned.
Take one ball of dough, fill it with pineapple jam, and roll it into a ball. Place it on a baking tray lined with parchment paper. Repeat until all the dough is used. Bake at 140–150°C using bottom heat for 15 minutes.
After 15 minutes, remove from the oven and let the hot steam dissipate until the cookies reach room temperature. Brush with the glaze mixture. Wait 5 minutes, then apply a second coat.
Bake again for about 20 minutes or until cooked, adjusting to your oven. For a darker color, turn on the top heat. Remove and let cool. Store the nastar cookies in an airtight container.

First, make the pineapple jam filling. Grate the pineapple and heat a pan. Add the pineapple, granulated sugar, and cloves. Stir until some of the liquid has evaporated, then add the salted and unsalted butter. Adjust the taste as needed. Continue stirring until the mixture thickens and becomes relatively dry, but do not dry it out completely or it will become hard like candy and impossible to shape. Turn off the heat and let it cool slightly. Shape the filling using a 1/4 tsp measuring spoon. Set aside.
Next, make the nastar dough. While preparing it, preheat the oven to 150°C using both top and bottom heat for 20 minutes. Put the Wijsman and Anchor butter in the mixer bowl and beat until thoroughly combined. Add the powdered sugar and briefly mix again, then gradually add the egg yolks. Beat until combined and slightly fluffy.
Gradually add the dry ingredients (wheat flour, cornstarch, powdered milk, and salt), sifting them first. Mix using a spatula only. Add the grated cheddar cheese and stir again. The dough is ready to shape. Line a baking tray with baking paper and shape the nastar using a 1 tsp measuring spoon.
Bake in two stages. First, before glazing, bake at 135°C using both top and bottom heat for 25 minutes. Remove from the oven and let the cookies adjust to room temperature. Prepare the glaze by mixing the omega egg yolk, full-cream milk, and vegetable oil. If the color is not orange enough, you can add yellow egg-yolk food coloring. Brush on a thin layer using a soft brush. Return to the oven for just 5 minutes at 130°C using both top and bottom heat, checking occasionally to adjust for your oven's heat and temperature.

strMeal: Selai Nanas Manis Legit (Untuk Isian Nastar/Roti)
strInstructions:
Place the grated pineapple in a nonstick pan.
Cook until the liquid in the pineapple has reduced. Add the salt, cinnamon, and granulated sugar.
Continue cooking until the liquid has reduced further and the mixture becomes thick and dark in color.
Cook to your preferred consistency. I like it thick but not too dry. Once it looks glossy, immediately turn off the heat and remove from the stove.
strIngredient2: Granulated sugar / adjust sweetness to taste

strInstructions:
Make the jam: Cook the grated pineapple from 1 fruit until the liquid has reduced. Add 2 cloves, 1 cinnamon stick, and 150 g granulated sugar. Stir until dry, then add 1/2 tbsp lemon juice and mix well. Remove from the heat.
Let the pineapple jam cool and set aside.
Beat the butter and margarine until combined. Add the egg yolk, powdered sugar, and cornstarch, then mix well. Gradually add the flour, stirring until evenly combined. Take 12 g of dough and 6 g of jam for each cookie. Shape like a leaf. I do not have a leaf-shaped cookie mold, so I make marks on the surface of the nastar with a spoon.
Bake at 150°C using both top and bottom heat for 20 minutes.
Mix the glaze ingredients. After 20 minutes, brush the cookies with three coats of glaze, then bake for another 10 minutes. Do not bake for too long, or the cookies may develop bubbles.
Remove from the oven, let cool, and serve.

Grate the pineapple; do not blend it.
Cook the pineapple over medium heat. Leave it alone and do not stir it, or your arm will get tired.
Once the liquid has reduced, add the sugar and salt. At this stage, lower the heat and stir continuously so the mixture does not burn after the sugar is added.
Keep stirring until the pineapple jam becomes dry and dark brown. Remove from the heat and let cool, then shape it into small balls to make filling the nastar cookies easier later.

Combine the egg yolks and sugar until evenly mixed, without using a mixer. Then add the margarine and stir until evenly combined.
Gradually add the Dancow powdered milk and wheat flour, sifting them as you go. Mix by hand until the dough is smooth and pliable.
Done.

Blend the pineapple, but do not make it too smooth. Add the cloves and boil until the liquid has reduced by half.
Add the salt and sugar. Stir until brown. Let cool.
Test the consistency by rolling some into a ball. If it holds its shape, it is ready. This pineapple jam can be used for duck-shaped nastar cookies.

strMeal: Nastar Lumer Rasa Premium Untuk Jualan
strInstructions:
Say bismillah, and set your intention in your heart for the cookies to turn out beautiful and glossy, made with a million acts of love and prayers.
Combine the butter, margarine, and powdered sugar. Mix on low speed for 1 minute until combined and fluffy.
Turn off the mixer, add the egg yolks and vanilla, then mix again briefly. Do not mix for too long, or the nastar may spread and turn out badly when baked.
Add the flour, powdered milk, and cornstarch. Stir with a spatula until the dough can be shaped.
Take 3 g of jam and 7 g of dough for each cookie. Each nastar should weigh 10 g in total.
Seal the dough without leaving any cracks. Roll it into a ball by hand or use a bento mold lightly dusted with flour. Place on a baking tray; the tray does not need to be lined or dusted with flour.
Preheat the oven to 150°C for 15 minutes using both top and bottom heat.
Add the nastar and bake at 150°C for 20 minutes until partially cooked.
Wait until the nastar has cooled completely, then brush with the glaze twice.
Once the glaze has dried, bake again at 110°C for 30–40 minutes until the bottoms turn golden brown. If the bottoms are still pale, continue baking until fully cooked.
Cool the nastar completely on a cooling rack before placing them in jars. Gently brush the tops with a soft brush to bring out their glossy finish.
Once cooled, store them in airtight jars. Do not forget to add an oxygen absorber to help extend their shelf life.

Combine the Royal Palmia, egg yolks, and powdered sugar.
Once evenly mixed, add the wheat flour, cornstarch, and powdered milk. Mix until evenly combined.
Take 7 g of dough and fill it with 3 g of pineapple jam. Shape as desired.
Bake in a preheated oven.
When the nastar is partially cooked, brush with a mixture of egg yolk and oil, then bake again until fully cooked.

Combine the margarine and powdered sugar, stirring until evenly mixed with a whisk or spatula. Do not overmix, or the nastar may spread in the oven.
Add 2 egg yolks and mix evenly. Add the vanilla, cornstarch, and powdered milk, sifting them in, then stir until combined.
Add the low-protein wheat flour and mix just until combined.
Shape the dough into 8 g balls, with 4 g of pineapple jam for each cookie. Once everything is portioned, flatten each dough ball, add the pineapple jam, and roll neatly until smooth. Repeat until finished.
Take a little dough and add red and yellow food coloring. Mix well, form a small ball, then flatten it. Place it on top of each nastar and draw lines.
Bake at 120°C using both top and bottom heat for 20 minutes.
Let cool for about 5 minutes, then brush with the glaze twice.
Bake again at 120°C for 15 minutes.
Let cool, then store in an airtight container. 👍👍

Combine the butter, margarine, eggs, vanilla, and sifted sugar. Stir or mix until evenly combined.
Add the cornstarch, powdered milk, and flour. Mix until the dough is not sticky or hard and can be rolled easily.
Weigh the dough or use a measuring spoon to portion it into balls. Fill each with a ball of pineapple jam; I use ready-made Royal jam.
Bake the dough at 150°C for 20–25 minutes, placing the tray on the lower rack so the cookies cook through first.
Remove the nastar from the oven and brush while still warm. For the glaze, use 2 egg yolks, a little cooking oil, and a little sweetened condensed milk.
After glazing, bake again at 120°C for 15 minutes on the top rack.

Mix the eggs, butter, margarine, powdered sugar, vanilla, and powdered milk on the lowest mixer speed, just until combined.
Divide the dough into two portions for yellow and green coloring. Take one-quarter of the dough and color it green.
Gradually add the remaining wheat flour to the dough.
Shape the nastar jam filling into balls.
Shape the nastar as usual, then use the back of a knife to make carrot-like lines. Attach the leaves. Bake at a temperature suited to your oven. 😊
Here is how they turned out! 😍😘
The taste is just right, they are crisp, and they do not spread in the oven.

By hand, beat the margarine, butter, and powdered sugar until combined. Add the egg yolks and beat again until evenly mixed. Do not beat for too long, so the mixture does not become pale.
Add the powdered milk, cornstarch, and sifted wheat flour. Knead until the dough is smooth and pliable. Portion the dough using a 5 g measuring spoon.
Portion and roll the pineapple jam using a 2.5 g measuring spoon.
Take some dough, flatten it, fill it with pineapple jam, and roll it into a ball. Repeat until all the dough is used. Arrange on a baking tray lined with baking paper. Bake over low heat until the nastar surfaces are dry.
Once the surfaces are dry but the cookies are not fully cooked, remove them from the oven and brush with egg yolk. Return them to the oven until fully cooked. You can apply the egg yolk directly without waiting for the cookies to cool.
Once cooked, remove from the oven and let cool before arranging in airtight jars.

Beat the butter, margarine, and powdered sugar until smooth, but do not whip until fluffy. Use only low speed.
Add the egg yolks and powdered milk, and stir gently.
Add the flour, powdered milk, and vanilla. Mix with a spatula until combined.
Take a little dough, using a measuring spoon to keep the portions neat. Flatten it, fill with pineapple jam, roll into a ball, and arrange neatly on a baking tray. Repeat until finished.
Bake at approximately 150°C for 15–20 minutes.
Once all the cookies are cooked, let them cool before brushing with the egg yolk mixture.
Then bake again using top heat only for 10 minutes, until the glaze turns golden brown.
Let cool completely before storing in jars.

strMeal: Nastar Premium Lembut Dan Lumer (Plus Tips Agar Glowing)
strInstructions:
Mix the margarine, butter, and powdered sugar until fluffy, about 1–2 minutes. I used a balloon whisk because the power went out. 🥲
Add the eggs and mix evenly. Turn off the mixer. Do not mix for too long, as this can cause the nastar to spread during baking.
Add the powdered milk and flour ingredients. Mix evenly and knead briefly until the dough can be shaped.
Shape the nastar as desired. You can weigh the dough to make the portions even. Fill with pineapple jam.
Arrange on a baking tray greased with margarine and lined with baking paper. I made two shapes: plain round cookies and guava-shaped ones.
Bake at 150°C using both top and bottom heat for 15–20 minutes. Brush with the glaze mixture. Brush all the cookies once and let the glaze set, then brush them all a second time, starting with the first ones. Bake again for 15–20 minutes or until cooked.
Don't they look beautiful? 😍
My best-selling product! 😍
Note: Use omega egg yolks for a nice yellow glaze. If unavailable, add a little yellow egg-yolk food coloring.

To make the pineapple jam, peel and grate the pineapple. Cook until the liquid has evaporated, then add the granulated sugar and cinnamon. Simmer over low heat until thick. Add the butter and stir until evenly combined. Turn off the heat and let cool.
Weigh portions of 3–4 g, roll them into balls, and set aside. The pineapple jam is ready to use.
To make the nastar dough, prepare all the ingredients. Sift the wheat flour, cornstarch, and powdered milk.
Combine the margarine, butter, and powdered sugar, then mix until evenly combined. Add the egg yolk.
Mix briefly again, then gradually add the sifted wheat flour, cornstarch, and powdered milk. Once evenly combined, cover with plastic wrap so the dough does not dry out. Take a portion of dough and mix it with food coloring.
Take the uncolored dough, weigh 8 g portions, and roll them into balls. Flatten each one, add the jam filling, and roll it back into a ball, shaping it into a duck's body.
Place on a baking tray lined with baking paper. Weigh 2 g portions for the heads and roll them into balls. Add a little orange dough for the beak and black sesame seeds for the eyes. Gently press the duck's body with the smallest cocktail spoon.
Brush the body with a little egg white, then attach the head on top.
Preheat the oven to 130–150°C. Bake for 20 minutes, then remove and let cool. I left mine until the next day before glazing, and that worked fine.
Brush with the glaze once and let it set, then brush a second time. Preheat the oven to 130–150°C and bake for another 10 minutes until golden.
Remove and let cool. They can be packed in boxes as gift hampers. I sampled some right away and brought some to a religious gathering.
strIngredient17: Pewarna makanan merah dan kuning untuk paruh

strInstructions:
1. Combine the butter, margarine, and powdered sugar, stirring with a whisk until evenly mixed. Add the egg yolk and stir until combined. Gradually add the wheat flour, powdered milk, and cornstarch. Mix evenly with a spatula. Cover all the dough with plastic so it does not dry out.
2. Take 8 g portions of dough. Flatten each one, add the jam, and roll into a ball. Shape it like a duck's body. Place on a baking tray lined with baking paper. Press the center of the duck's body with the tip of a spoon to create an indentation.
3. Make the head using about 2 g of dough. Roll it into a ball and shape the head and beak with a small spoon. Attach the head to the duck's body. The head should be centered so it stays upright rather than falling sideways during baking. Make a small indentation in the duck's back with the tip of a spoon so the head sits securely and does not shift during baking.
4. If needed, preheat the oven to 140°C for 20 minutes, depending on your oven. Remove the cookies and let them cool.
5. Draw the duck's eyes with a black or brown edible pen. For the beak, mix a little egg yolk with a little red and yellow food coloring, then brush it onto the beak. Brush the rest of the cookies with the first coat of glaze and bake for another 10 minutes. Remove and let cool. Apply the second coat of glaze and bake for another 10 minutes. Remove the nastar from the oven, let cool, and pack in a container. Ready to serve.

Prepare the ingredients. Place the butter, margarine, and powdered sugar in a bowl.
Mix only until evenly combined. Add the egg yolk and mix briefly until combined.
Gradually add the wheat flour, powdered milk, and cornstarch, mixing on low speed until combined. Cover with plastic so the dough does not dry out.
Take a small amount of dough and color it orange, or mix red and yellow coloring for the beak. Take another small amount and color it black for the eyes if you do not have black sesame seeds.
Weigh 8–9.5 g of dough for each body, flatten it, and add about 1.5 g of jam. Shape it into a slightly elongated duck.
Take about 2.5 g of dough for each head and roll into a ball. Use orange dough for the beak and black dough for the eyes. Brush the body and head with egg white, then attach the head slightly into the body so it does not droop when baked.
Preheat the oven for 15 minutes. Bake the cookies over medium-low heat for about 20 minutes at approximately 130–150°C. Remove and let cool to room temperature.
Brush evenly with the glaze. Bake again for about 15 minutes, or until golden and cooked. Let cool to room temperature and store in an airtight container.
strIngredient16: Selai nanas bulat bulatkan selai nanas isian nastar

strInstructions:
Blanch the beef ribs and beef trimmings in boiling water for about 3 minutes. Discard the water, rinse the ribs and trimmings, and drain. Cut the trimmings into bite-sized pieces.
Place the ribs and trimmings in a pot, add water, and pressure-cook for 30 minutes. I use an electric pressure cooker.
While the meat cooks, dry-toast the spices until fragrant, then place them in a spice infuser. I use a round stainless-steel one.
Heat a little cooking oil in a pan and sauté the seasoning paste until softened and fragrant.
In a larger pot, bring water to a boil. Add the sautéed seasoning and spices, then simmer until fragrant and the spices have infused fully.
Add the pressure-cooked trimmings and ribs along with their broth, potatoes, and carrots. Season with salt, granulated sugar, and seasoning powder. Bring back to a boil and cook until the vegetables are done.
Just before turning off the heat, taste and adjust the seasoning. Add the sliced green onions and celery leaves, stir, and turn off the stove. Sprinkle the soup with fried shallots.
Serve with chili sauce, your favorite side dishes, and crackers.
MashaAllah, this soup is delicious, savory, fragrant, and warming.
strIngredient10: Green parts of green onions, sliced
strIngredient20: Daun bawang bagian putih, iris-iris 1 cm

strInstructions:
1. Bring water to a boil. Add the meat and boil for 5 minutes to remove impurities. Discard the water and drain. Return the meat to the pot and add fresh water until fully submerged. Cook using the 5:30:7 method or until tender. Cut the meat into small pieces. Boil the potatoes and carrots separately, then set aside.
2. Meanwhile, prepare the seasonings. Heat 1–2 tbsp of cooking oil in a pan and sauté the crushed garlic until halfway cooked. Add it to the pot with the meat.
3. Add the spices: star anise, cloves, nutmeg, crushed ginger, cardamom, and cinnamon. Season with salt, sugar, pepper, and stock powder. Cook over medium heat until boiling, then taste. Add the celery leaves and green onions. Cook briefly, then remove from the heat.
4. To serve, arrange the boiled potatoes, boiled carrots, and tomato slices in a bowl. Sprinkle with green onions and celery. Pour the hot soup and meat over them. Top with fried shallots. Add a squeeze of lime if desired. Serve.

Prepare all the ingredients. Boil the red beans until tender, then set aside.
Pressure-cook the beef ribs for 30 minutes, depending on your pressure cooker. Set aside.
Heat the oil and sauté the onion with all the spices except the curry leaves. Sauté until fragrant, then add the broth left from cooking the beef ribs. If the liquid has reduced, add more until there is about 500 ml.
Bring to a boil and let it boil for about 3 minutes, then add the carrots. Bring to a boil again.
Add all the seasonings, curry leaves, and red beans. Cook until boiling, then taste and adjust the seasoning if needed.
Ready to serve.

Boil the ribs with the bay leaves for 5 minutes to remove the smell.
Blend the garlic and shallots, then sauté them in hot oil until fragrant.
Bring water to a boil, add the ribs that were boiled earlier, and cook until tender.
Once the ribs are tender, add the blended seasoning.
Next, add the cardamom, cloves, and cinnamon.
Add the carrots, cut into pieces as desired.
Add the seasonings: salt, stock powder, flavor enhancer, and pepper.
Add the whole bird's eye chilies, then the sliced green onions, celery leaves, tomatoes, and cabbage.
Wait until everything is cooked.
Remember to taste and adjust the seasoning.
The family's favorite beef rib soup is ready to serve.
strIngredient14: Pepper powder sachets, or to taste

strInstructions:
Sauté the onion in margarine until softened. Add the ground seasoning and sauté until fragrant.
Add about 500 ml of water and the beef ribs. Season with salt, granulated sugar, and stock powder. Taste and adjust to your preference. Cook over low heat until the ribs are tender.
Once the ribs are tender, add the sliced carrots, snow peas, and sliced green onions. Cook until the vegetables are soft. Ready to serve.

Prepare the ingredients. Boil the beef ribs in boiling water until tender, then discard the water. Heat the oil and sauté the seasoning until fragrant. Add the ribs and stir briefly, then pour in the water.
Wait until the water boils, then add the potatoes. After 5 minutes, add the carrots. Cook briefly until the carrots are done, then turn off the heat.
Serve.

Bring the water to a boil. Prepare the ingredients and sauté the seasonings together with the whole spices until fragrant and cooked.
Add the ribs, ground seasoning, potatoes, and carrots.
Once the soup boils again, add the pangi. Season with salt and stock powder, then taste and adjust. Cook until done.
Finally, add the tomatoes, green onions, and celery.
Serve.
strIngredient1: Beef ribs, already boiled until cooked
strIngredient4: Carrots, cut into fairly thick rounds
strIngredient6: Green onions or leeks, cut into pieces

strInstructions:
Cut the beef ribs to your preferred size, wash thoroughly, then pressure-cook for 30 minutes.
Slice 3 cloves of shallots and garlic, fry them, then grind until smooth. Set aside.
Prepare the spices, grind until smooth, then fry until cooked and fragrant. Cut the potatoes to your preferred size.
Once the ribs are tender, add the potatoes and spices, then mix well.
Next, add the finely ground fried shallots and garlic, celery, salt, and seasoning. Cook until done.

Preheat the oven at 180 C / Gas 4. Line a baking tray with greaseproof paper.
In a bowl, mix the cashews and icing sugar. Add the egg yolks and orange blossom water and mix to a smooth homogeneous paste.
Take lumps of the cashew paste and shape into small balls. Roll the balls in icing sugar and transfer to the baking tray. Push an almond in the centre of each ghribia.
Bake until the biscuits are lightly golden, about 20 minutes. Keep an eye on them, they burn quickly.

strMeal: Tavë Kosi Baked Lamb and Yogurt
strInstructions:
1
Baking the Lamb
In a large pan (with a lid) melt the butter and olive oil together then add the diced lamb. Brown the lamb on a medium heat, this will take around 5 minutes.
2
Add the garlic, oregano, 300ml of water and season with salt and pepper. Mix well before covering with the lid. Leave to simmer for 50 minutes mixing a couple of times ensuring the lamb doesn’t start to burn.
3
The juices should have nearly all boiled away so another 150ml of water should be added along with the rice. Mix altogether, bring to the boil, place the lid on and leave for just 10 minutes. It’s advised to check at around 8 minutes – you want the liquid to be evaporated with just moist coating of oily water left over the lamb and rice.
4
Place the lamb and rice into a casserole dish, the mixture should fully cover the base and have at least 2 inches spare for the yogurt. Alternatively you can split into four ceramic bowls.
5
Making a Roux
In a small saucepan melt the butter over a medium heat and then add two tablespoons of flour while continuously stirring for two minutes (add a little extra flour if needed). The roux should not be thick but not too runny, the colour will darken slightly. Pour the roux into a bowl and keep to one side.
6
Making the Yogurt Mixture
In a mixing bowl add the yogurt, eggs and season with salt and pepper. Mix together then add the roux continuing to mix fast for a minute to ensure the roux and yogurt are thoroughly combined.
7
Pour the yogurt mixture over the baked lamb and rice and sprinkle on a little oregano.
8
Cooking
Place on the bottom shelf of the oven on 180 degrees for 35 minutes then move it up to the middle for a further 10 minutes. The Tavë kosi is ready when the yogurt has risen up high and a golden crust formed.
9
Leave to cool for 5 – 10 minutes before serving.

step 1
Heat the oil in a deep frying pan, then soften the leek for 5 mins without browning. Add the chorizo and fry until it releases its oils. Stir in the turmeric and rice until coated by the oils, then pour in the stock. Bring to the boil, then simmer for 15 mins, stirring occasionally.

step 2
Tip in the peas and cook for 5 mins, then stir in the seafood to heat through for a final 1-2 mins cooking or until rice is cooked. Check for seasoning and serve immediately with lemon wedges.
Bring water with salt to a boil then add grits; reduce heat and cover. occasionally stirring. Cook approximately 15 minutes or until grits have desired consistency. Cool then serve

Soak glutinous rice with water for at least 1 ½ hours prior to using. Drain.
Prepare a 9-inch round or square cake pan and spray with cooking spray or line with plastic wrap.
Mix coconut milk, water, salt and the rice. Pour it into cake pan, topped with the pandan knots.
Steam for 30 minutes.
After 30 minutes, fluff up the rice and remove pandan knots. Then, using a greased spatula, flatten the steamed rice. Make sure there are no holes/air bubbles and gaps in the rice, especially the sides.
Steam for another 10 minutes.

Combine pandan juice, coconut milk, all purpose flour, cornflour, and sugar. Mix well.
Add eggs and whisk well then strain into a medium sized metal bowl or pot.
Place pandan mixture over simmering water (double boiler or bain-marie)
Stir continuously and cook till custard starts to thicken. (15 minutes)
Pour pandan custard into glutinous rice layer, give it a little tap (for air bubbles) and continue to steam for 30 minutes.
Remove kuih seri muka from the steamer and allow to cool completely before cutting into rectangles or diamond shapes.

Heat the oil in a large saucepan. Use kitchen scissors to snip the bacon into small pieces, or use a sharp knife to chop it on a chopping board. Add the bacon to the pan and cook for just a few mins until starting to turn golden. Add the onion, celery and carrot, and cook over a medium heat for 5 mins, stirring occasionally, until softened.
Add the garlic and cook for 1 min, then tip in the mince and cook, stirring and breaking it up with a wooden spoon, for about 6 mins until browned all over.
Stir in the tomato purée and cook for 1 min, mixing in well with the beef and vegetables. Tip in the chopped tomatoes. Fill each can half full with water to rinse out any tomatoes left in the can, and add to the pan. Add the honey and season to taste. Simmer for 20 mins.
Heat oven to 200C/180C fan/gas 6. To assemble the lasagne, ladle a little of the ragu sauce into the bottom of the roasting tin or casserole dish, spreading the sauce all over the base. Place 2 sheets of lasagne on top of the sauce overlapping to make it fit, then repeat with more sauce and another layer of pasta. Repeat with a further 2 layers of sauce and pasta, finishing with a layer of pasta.
Put the crème fraîche in a bowl and mix with 2 tbsp water to loosen it and make a smooth pourable sauce. Pour this over the top of the pasta, then top with the mozzarella. Sprinkle Parmesan over the top and bake for 25–30 mins until golden and bubbling. Serve scattered with basil, if you like.

Peel and clean apples/rhubarb, cut in to a slices
beat eggs and sugar together into a light foam
Mix together flour, salt and baking powder
Add  the dry ingredients to the egg mixture and add sour milk gradually while stirring,  Add berries.
Pour dough in to a butter greased pan. Sprinkle over sugar (and cinnamon). Bake at 180 C for 30 minute

Boil some water in a large saucepan. Add 250ml cold water and the udon noodles. (As they are so thick, adding cold water helps them to cook a little bit slower so the middle cooks through). If using frozen or fresh noodles, cook for 2 mins or until al dente; dried will take longer, about 5-6 mins. Drain and leave in the colander.
Heat 1 tbsp of the oil, add the onion and cabbage and sauté for 5 mins until softened. Add the mushrooms and some spring onions, and sauté for 1 more min. Pour in the remaining sesame oil and the noodles. If using cold noodles, let them heat through before adding the ingredients for the sauce – otherwise tip in straight away and keep stir-frying until sticky and piping hot. Sprinkle with the remaining spring onions.

step 1
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large pan, then fry the onion and garlic over a low heat for 5 mins until softened. Tip into a large mixing bowl with the chickpeas and spices, then mash together with a fork or potato masher until the chickpeas are totally broken down. Stir in the parsley or dried herbs, with seasoning to taste. Add the egg, then squish the mixture together with your hands.

step 2
Mould the mix into 6 balls, then flatten into patties. Heat the remaining oil in the pan, then fry the falafels on a medium heat for 3 mins on each side, until golden brown and firm. Serve hot or cold with couscous, pitta bread or salad.

Place the pumpkin in a large saucepan, cover with water and bring to the boil. Cover with a lid and simmer for 15 mins or until tender. Drain pumpkin; let cool.
Heat oven to 180C/160C fan/gas 4. Roll out the pastry on a lightly floured surface and use it to line a 22cm loose-bottomed tart tin. Chill for 15 mins. Line the pastry with baking parchment and baking beans, then bake for 15 mins. Remove the beans and paper, and cook for a further 10 mins until the base is pale golden and biscuity. Remove from the oven and allow to cool slightly.
Increase oven to 220C/200C fan/gas 7. Push the cooled pumpkin through a sieve into a large bowl. In a separate bowl, combine the sugar, salt, nutmeg and half the cinnamon. Mix in the beaten eggs, melted butter and milk, then add to the pumpkin purée and stir to combine. Pour into the tart shell and cook for 10 mins, then reduce the temperature to 180C/160C fan/gas 4. Continue to bake for 35-40 mins until the filling has just set.
Leave to cool, then remove the pie from the tin. Mix the remaining cinnamon with the icing sugar and dust over the pie. Serve chilled.

Boil the kettle. Empty the mussels into a colander and run under cold water. Throw away any with broken shells. Pick through the shells, tapping each one on the side of the sink – they should be closed or should slowly close when tapped – if they stay open, throw them away. If any of the shells still have barnacles or stringy beards attached, pull them off with a cutlery knife and rinse the shells well. Keep in the colander, covered with a cold, damp cloth, until you’re ready to cook. Peel the prawn shells on the body section only – leave the heads and tails intact. Score down the backs and pull out any gritty entrails. Chill until you’re ready to cook.
Put the saffron in a small cup, cover with 50ml kettle-hot water and set aside for 10 mins. If using vermicelli, put in a bowl and crush to little pieces (about 1cm long) with your hands.
Heat the oil in a large frying pan with at least a 3cm lip, or a 40cm paella pan. Add the onion and stir around the pan for 5 mins until soft. Add the garlic and cook for 1 min more, then tip in the vermicelli and cook for 5 mins, stirring from time to time, until the vermicelli is toasted brown. Stir in the paprika.
Keeping the heat moderate, stir through the monkfish, squid and saffron with its water, seasoning well. Spread the ingredients out in an even layer, then pour over the hot stock and scatter the tomatoes on top. Bring to a simmer, then cover the whole dish with a tight-fitting lid (or foil). Turn the heat to medium and cook for 6 mins.
Uncover and stir to incorporate the dry top layer of pasta. Push the mussels into the pasta so the hinges are buried in the bottom of the dish, and they stand straight up. Arrange the prawns on top, cover tightly and cook for another 6 mins or until the mussels are open, the prawns are pink and the pasta is cooked through. Leave to simmer for another 2-3 mins to cook off most of the remaining liquid (leave a little in the pan to prevent the pasta from sticking together). Allow to sit for 2-3 mins, then squeeze over the lemon juice and arrange the wedges on top. Scatter with parsley before serving.
Chop the beetroot, add water and stock cube and cook for 15mins. Add the other ingredients and boil until soft. Finally add the beans and cook for 5mins. Serve in the soup pot.

step 1
Heat the lard in a saucepan over a medium heat and fry the finely chopped onion until golden, around 5-8 mins. Tip in the cumin and pork, and fry for 10 mins all over until browned. Add the garlic, season well and scatter over the flour. Cook for about a minute, then add the paprika and cook for 1 min more.

step 2
Pour in half of the stock, add the bay leaves, and simmer with the lid on over a low heat for 30 mins.

step 3
Add the sauerkraut, remaining stock and a drizzle of the sauerkraut pickling juices. Simmer with the lid for 30 mins, stirring occasionally, until the meat is tender. Stir in the cream and simmer for 5 mins to combine the flavours. Season to taste, the serve garnished with a spoonful of soured cream.

This recipe has been provided by Apetit Online and not been re-tested by us.

Put the flour and salt in a bowl. Add the suet, currants, sugar, lemon and orange zest.
Pour in 150ml milk and mix to a firm but moist dough, adding the extra milk if necessary.
Shape into a fat roll about 20cm long. Place on a large rectangle of baking parchment. Wrap loosely to allow for the pudding to rise and tie the ends with string like a Christmas cracker.
Place a steamer over a large pan of boiling water, add the pudding to the steamer, cover and steam for 1 1/2 hours. Top up the pan with water from time to time.
Remove from the steamer and allow to cool slightly before unwrapping. Serve sliced with custard.

Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a large, heavy-based saucepan or flameproof dish. Tip in the bacon and fry until crisp. Remove and drain on kitchen paper. Add the shallots to the pan and fry, stirring or shaking the pan often, for 5-8 mins until well browned all over. Remove and set aside with the bacon.
Pat the chicken pieces dry with kitchen paper. Pour the remaining oil into the pan, then fry half the chicken pieces, turning regularly, for 5-8 mins until well browned. Remove, then repeat with the remaining chicken. Remove and set aside.
Scatter in the garlic and fry briefly, then, with the heat medium-high, pour in the brandy or Cognac, stirring the bottom of the pan to deglaze. The alcohol should sizzle and start to evaporate so there is not much left.
Return the chicken legs and thighs to the pan along with any juices, then pour in a little of the wine, stirring the bottom of the pan again. Stir in the rest of the wine, the stock and tomato purée, drop in the bouquet garni, season with pepper and a pinch of salt, then return the bacon and shallots to the pan. Cover, lower the heat to a gentle simmer, add the chicken breasts and cook for 50 mins-1hr.
Just before ready to serve, heat the oil for the mushrooms in a large non-stick frying pan. Add the mushrooms and fry over a high heat for a few mins until golden. Remove and keep warm.
Lift the chicken, shallots and bacon from the pan and transfer to a warmed serving dish. Remove the bouquet garni. To make the thickener, mix the flour, olive oil and butter in a small bowl using the back of a teaspoon. Bring the wine mixture to a gentle boil, then gradually drop in small pieces of the thickener, whisking each piece in using a wire whisk. Simmer for 1-2 mins. Scatter the mushrooms over the chicken, then pour over the wine sauce. Garnish with chopped parsley.

Cut the aubergines in half lengthways. Place them on the board, cut side down, slice in half lengthways again and then across into 1.5cm chunks. Cut off the courgettes ends, then across into 1.5cm slices. Peel the peppers from stalk to bottom. Hold upright, cut around the stalk, then cut into 3 pieces. Cut away any membrane, then chop into bite-size chunks.
Score a small cross on the base of each tomato, then put them into a heatproof bowl. Pour boiling water over the tomatoes, leave for 20 secs, then remove. Pour the water away, replace the tomatoes and cover with cold water. Leave to cool, then peel the skin away. Quarter the tomatoes, scrape away the seeds with a spoon, then roughly chop the flesh.
Set a sauté pan over medium heat and when hot, pour in 2 tbsp olive oil. Brown the aubergines for 5 mins on each side until the pieces are soft. Set them aside and fry the courgettes in another tbsp oil for 5 mins, until golden on both sides. Repeat with the peppers. Don’t overcook the vegetables at this stage, as they have some more cooking left in the next step.
Tear up the basil leaves and set aside. Cook the onion in the pan for 5 mins. Add the garlic and fry for a further min. Stir in the vinegar and sugar, then tip in the tomatoes and half the basil. Return the vegetables to the pan with some salt and pepper and cook for 5 mins. Serve with basil.

Pound the garlic with sea salt in a pestle and mortar (or use a small food processor), until the garlic forms a paste. Whisk together the oil, lemon juice, zest, dill and garlic. Mix in the lamb and combine well. Cover and marinate for at least 2 hrs or overnight in the fridge. If you’re going to use bamboo skewers, soak them in cold water.

If you’ve prepared the lamb the previous day, take it out of the fridge 30 mins before cooking. Thread the meat onto the soaked or metal skewers. Heat the grill to high or have a hot griddle pan or barbecue ready. Cook the skewers for 2-3 mins on each side, basting with the remaining marinade. Heat the pitta or flatbreads briefly, then stuff with the souvlaki. Add Greek salad (see 'Goes well with', right) and Tzatziki (below), if you like.

Preheat fryer to 350°F. Thoroughly mix together all the spice mix ingredients.
Combine spice mix with flour, brown sugar and salt.
Dip chicken pieces in egg white to lightly coat them, then transfer to flour mixture. Turn a few times and make sure the flour mix is really stuck to the chicken. Repeat with all the chicken pieces.
Let chicken pieces rest for 5 minutes so crust has a chance to dry a bit.
Fry chicken in batches. Breasts and wings should take 12-14 minutes, and legs and thighs will need a few more minutes. Chicken pieces are done when a meat thermometer inserted into the thickest part reads 165°F.
Let chicken drain on a few paper towels when it comes out of the fryer. Serve hot.

Heat the olive oil in a large frying pan and cook the onion for 1-2 mins just until softened. Add the chicken and fry for 7-10 mins until cooked through and the onions have turned golden. Grate over the ginger, stir through the harissa to coat everything and cook for 1 min more.

Tip in the apricots, chickpeas and couscous, then pour over the stock and stir once. Cover with a lid or tightly cover the pan with foil and leave for about 5 mins until the couscous has soaked up all the stock and is soft. Fluff up the couscous with a fork and scatter over the coriander to serve. Serve with extra harissa, if you like.

Heat oven to 180C/160C fan/gas 4. Heat the oil in a large frying pan and cook the onion for 8-10 mins until softened. Add the garlic, Worcestershire sauce and 2 tsp tomato purée, and stir until combined. Set aside to cool.

Put the turkey mince, egg, breadcrumbs and cooled onion mix in a large bowl and season well. Mix everything to combine, then shape into a rectangular loaf and place in a large roasting tin. Spread 2 tbsp barbecue sauce over the meatloaf and bake for 30 mins.

Meanwhile, drain 1 can of beans only, then pour both cans into a large bowl. Add the remaining barbecue sauce and tomato purée. Season and set aside.

When the meatloaf has had its initial cooking time, scatter the beans around the outside and bake for 15 mins more until the meatloaf is cooked through and the beans are piping hot. Scatter over the parsley and serve the meatloaf in slices.

step 1
To make the leaven, mix the yeast with the sugar and flour, and stir in the warm milk. Set aside in a warm place for 30 minutes.

step 2
For the dough, put egg yolks into a heatproof bowl and add the sugar and vanilla sugar. Set the bowl over a pan of simmering water and whisk until smooth and thick.

step 3
Sift the flour into the bowl of a stand mixer, add the beaten yolks and the warm cream, mix thoroughly, then add a pinch of salt and the leaven. Bring together to make a dough and knead for 10 minutes (or 15-20 if doing this by hand).

step 4
When the dough stops sticking to your hands, pour in the cooled melted butter and knead for a few more minutes. Cover with a cloth and leave in a warm place to rise for at least 1 hr-1 hr 30 mins.

step 5
Mix the jam with the ground almonds and spoon into a piping bag or jam syringe. Divide the dough into 16 pieces and shape them into doughnuts. Cover and leave to rise for 30 mins.

step 6
Fill a deep pan or a deep fat fryer one third full of oil or melted lard and heat it until it is 180C – if you don’t have a thermometer, drop in a small chunk of bread.
